body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): For five-sign support with repeated planar types $A,A,B$, let $G$ be the graph on the five supported columns with $ij\in E$ when $u_i+u_j=2T$, $T\in\{\pm B,\pm2A\pm B\}$. Each edge contributes at most two solutions, so a total of at least fourteen implies $|E(G)|\ge7$; Mantel gives a triangle, and a disconnected graph on five vertices has at most six edges, so $G$ is connected. Relabelling a triangle $0,1,2$ with edge labels $a,b,c$ determines $u_0=a+b-c$, $u_1=a+c-b$, $u_2=b+c-a$ uniquely; a spanning tree to vertices $3,4$ has exactly two forms, giving the count $6^3\bigl((3\cdot6)^2+3\cdot6\cdot6\bigr)=93{,}312$. Notes: VERIFIED: $216\cdot(324+108)=216\cdot432=93312$. There is no remaining continuous parameter -- the triangle determines $u_0,u_1,u_2$ and every attachment equation determines the next $u_i$. Sorting the five $u_i$ quotients only by an allowed $S_5$-symmetry, so the reduction to $2{,}934$ multisets is LOSSLESS. This is the argument that upgrades a finite enumeration into a complete classification.

body:
[Definition 38 of arXiv:2608.29157, 'Dilator-based analysis of $\KP$'] A sentence in the language of $\RS$ is \emph{axiomatic} if it is one of the following: 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Extensionality:
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \neg\left(
            \forall z\in x\, z\in y
            \wedge
            \forall z\in y\, z\in x
          \right)
          \vee x=y
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Pairing:
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \exists z\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left(
          x\in z\wedge y\in z
        \right).
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Union:
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \exists y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall z\in x\,
        \forall w\in z\,
        w\in y.
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Set Induction:
        \begin{equation*}
        \neg
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left(
          \neg\forall y\in x\,A(y)\vee A(x)
        \right)
        \vee
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega A(x).
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item Infinity:
        \begin{equation*}
        \exists x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \exists y\in x\, y\in x
          \wedge
          \forall y\in x\,\exists z\in x\,y\in z
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item $\Delta_0$-Separation:
        For every $\Delta_0$-formula $A(x,\vec a)$,
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall b\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall \vec a\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \exists c\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall x\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \left(x\notin c\vee
            \left(x\in b\wedge A(x,\vec a)\right)
          \right)
          \wedge
          \left(
            \neg\left(x\in b\wedge A(x,\vec a)\right)
            \vee x\in c
          \right)
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
        
        \item $\Delta_0$-Collection:
        For every $\Delta_0$-formula $A(x,y,\vec a)$,
        \begin{equation*}
        \forall b\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega\,
        \forall \vec a\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
        \left[
          \neg\forall x\in b\,\exists y\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega A(x,y,\vec a)
          \vee
          \exists c\in \ttL(u)_\ttOmega
          \forall x\in b\,\exists y\in c\,A(x,y,\vec a)
        \right].
        \end{equation*}
    \end{enumerate}

    A sequent $\Gamma$ in the language of $\RS$ is \emph{axiomatic} if $\Gamma$ contains one of the following subsequent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item An axiomatic sentence.
        \item $A,\lnot A$ for some formula $A$.
        \item $s\notin s$ for some set term $s$.
        \item $s\subseteq s$ for some set term $s$.
        \item $s\neq t, \lnot A(s),A(t)$ for some set term $s$, $t$, and some formula $A$.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Definition 38 of arXiv:2608.29157

[Proposition 101 (Second-chaos factorization and the point-evaluation gap) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For $i<j$, let
\[
 \Xi_{ij}(t)=t^{-1}\left(
  \int_0^tW_s^i\,\mathrm dW_s^j-
  \int_0^tW_s^j\,\mathrm dW_s^i\right).
\]
The active family $(\Xi_{ij}(t))_{c_ic_j>0}$ is orthonormal in
$L^2(\Omega)$, and second-chaos radonification defines an isometry
\[
 \operatorname{Rad}^{(2)}_{\Xi,t}:
 \mathcal S_2(\mathfrak h_{2,C},E)\longrightarrow L^2(\Omega;E).
\]
Moreover
\begin{equation}
 \alpha_{A_t^C}
 =\operatorname{Rad}^{(2)}_{\Xi,t}(K_{C,t}),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(\alpha_{A_t^C})
 =K_{C,t}K_{C,t}^*=\frac{t^2}{4}\Lambda^2C.
 
\end{equation}
If $C$ has infinite rank, then almost surely algebraic point evaluation on
the active chaos space has no bounded extension to its $L^2$ closure.
Thus \eqref{eq:compact-second-chaos-factorization} is an $L^2$
radonification identity, not a bounded samplewise contraction.

[Corollary cor:appliedtoSK of arXiv:2607.06813, 'Mixing of Glauber Dynamics on High Overlap Gibbs Measures'] For any inverse temperature $\beta$, and $n$ large enough, there exists $\theta\geq 0$, which may depend on $\beta$ but not on $n$, such that lazy Glauber Dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Gibbs measure at inverse temperature $\beta$ and with external field $\theta\mathbf{1}$ 
        \[
    \nu(x) \propto \exp\left(\frac{\beta}2x^\top W x + \theta \mathbf{1}^\top x\right),
        \]
    where $W\sim\mathrm{GOE}$ (symmetric, $W_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1/n)$ for $i\neq j$ and $W_{ii}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,2/n)$), mixes, in total variation distance, in time polynomial in $n$ with high probability. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:main-intro of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] Under Assumption~(ass:kernels of the paper),
the bivariate renormalized intensity process $(V^{T,1},V^{T,2})_{T\geq 1}$
converges weakly in $C([0,1];\mathbb{R}^2)$
to the unique triangular weak solution $(V^1,V^2)$
(Definition~(def:triangular-solution of the paper)) of the coupled stochastic Volterra system.
Set
\[
\nu_i=(m_i\lambda_i)^{-1/2},\qquad
\gamma_{12}=\frac{m_1}{m_2\lambda_1},
\qquad
L_{12}:=b_\infty^{12}\|\psi^{12}\|_1(K_1*K_2).
\]
Then
\begin{align}
V_t^1 &= b_1(t)
  + \nu_1\int_0^t K_1(t-s)\sqrt{V_s^1}\,d\beta_s^1,
\\
V_t^2 &= b_2(t)
  + \nu_2\int_0^t K_2(t-s)\sqrt{V_s^2}\,d\beta_s^2
  + \gamma_{12}\nu_1
    \int_0^t L_{12}(t-s)\sqrt{V_s^1}\,d\beta_s^1,

\end{align}
where $\beta^1,\beta^2$ are independent standard Brownian motions,
$b_1$ is defined by~(equation eq:b1-def of the paper), and $b_2$ is defined by~(equation eq:b2-full of the paper).

The limiting process has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] \textbf{Heterogeneous roughness.}
Set $H_i:=\alpha_i-\tfrac12\in(0,\tfrac12)$.  Almost surely, $V^i$ is
H\"older continuous of every order $\gamma<H_i$, and the exponent is
sharp: away from the time origin, the mean-square increments satisfy
$\mathbb{E}[(V^i_t-V^i_s)^2]\asymp(t-s)^{2H_i}$
(Proposition~(prop:regularity of the paper)).  In this sense each $V^i$ has Hurst
parameter $H_i$, and $H_1<H_2$: the components carry distinct
roughnesses.

\item[\textup{(ii)}] \textbf{Covariance formula.}
The exact covariance of the limit process is
\[
\mathrm{Cov}(V_t^1,V_t^2)
= \gamma_{12}\nu_1^2
  \int_0^t K_1(t-s)\,L_{12}(t-s)\,b_1(s)\,ds,
\]
where $b_1(s)=\mathbb{E}[V_s^1]$.
In the stationary regime $b_1(s)\equiv\bar V^1$, this simplifies to
$\gamma_{12}\nu_1^2\bar V^1\int_0^t K_1(u)L_{12}(u)\,du$.
The effective cross-kernel is $L_{12}:=b_\infty^{12}\|\psi^{12}\|_1\cdot(K_1*K_2)$,
with $(K_1*K_2)(t)\sim C_{12}\,t^{\alpha_1+\alpha_2-1}$ as $t\downarrow 0$
(Proposition~(prop:main of the paper)).
\end{enumerate}

A self-contained statement with all explicit constants appears as
Theorem~(thm:main-final of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 22 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $n,d,k\in\mathbb N$ and assume that $n\ge k$. There exist two functions
\[
\alpha_{n,d,k}\colon(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\beta_{n,d,k}\colon(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty),
\]
with the following property.

Let $\mu$ be an isotropic log-concave measure on $\mathbb R^n$,
and let
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\in \mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^k)$
be such that
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\mu(f_j)>0,
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Then, for every $a>0$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \Delta_{\hat{f}}\,d\mu\ge a
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge \beta_{n,d,k}(a),
\]
and, for every $b>0$,
\[
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge b
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \Delta_{\hat{f}}\,d\mu\ge \alpha_{n,d,k}(b).
\]

[Definition eq:def:reg of arXiv:2602.04673, 'Brownian paths as loop-decorated SLEs'] The loop $\ell$ is said to be {\bf regular for $\gamma$} if it intersects $\gamma$ and the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}[i)]
    \item  The set of temporal roots $\Theta_\ell$ is reduced to a single element $\theta_\ell$. Furthermore, $\sigma_\ell\notin \{0,t_\gamma\}$.
     Remark this prevents $\theta^-_\ell=0$, since then $\theta^+_\ell=t_\ell$.
    \item  The intersection at $\theta_\ell$ is bilateral: for any $\epsilon>0$, there exists $\theta^L,\theta^R\in [\theta_\ell-\epsilon,\theta_\ell+\epsilon]$ such that
    $\ell(\theta^L)\in L(x_\ell)$ and $\ell(\theta^R)\in R(x_\ell)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    The subset of $\mathscr{L}_\gamma$ of loops which are regular for $\gamma$ is denoted $\mathscr{L}_{reg,\gamma}$. We define
		\[ \mathscr{L}_{reg}\coloneqq \bigcup_{\gamma\in \mathscr{S}} (\{\gamma\} \times \mathscr{L}_{reg,\gamma}) \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad
		\mathscr{L}_0\coloneqq\bigcup_{\gamma\in \mathscr{S}} (\{\gamma\} \times \mathscr{L}_{\gamma}).\]

Let 0<p<=1, m,n be positive integers, and x_1,...,x_n be real vectors in R^m. Write ||x||_p=(sum_j |x_j|^p)^(1/p), a quasi-norm when p<1. Let sigma_1,...,sigma_n be independent signs, each uniform on {-1,1}. If A_p>0 is any scalar Khintchine lower constant, then E||sum_i sigma_i*x_i||_p >= A_p*(sum_i ||x_i||_p^2)^(1/2). The same A_p works for every m,n. This is the first-moment convention of Yang Definition7.2, not a second-moment inequality. No triangle inequality for ||.||_p is assumed.

    For \(\ell > 0\), set 
    \begin{equation}
        \alpha_\ell = 2 \arctan\left(\sinh\left(\frac{\ell}{2}\right)\right).
    \end{equation}
    Let us consider \(u_0,\,\ldots,\,u_n\) and \(v_0,\,\ldots,\,v_n\) points of \(\Hyp{2}\).
    Let us suppose that for all \(i\in\llbracket 0, n-1\rrbracket\), \(\hyperbolicDistance{u_i}{u_{i+1}} = \hyperbolicDistance{v_i}{v_{i+1}} = \ell\).
    Let us suppose that for all \(i\in\llbracket 1, n-1\rrbracket\), if we denote \(\theta_i = \angle(u_{i-1}, u_i, u_{i+1})\in[-\pi, \pi]\), then \(\angle(v_{i-1}, v_i, v_{i+1}) = \abs{\theta_i}\).
    If for all \(i\in\llbracket 1, n-1\rrbracket\), \(\abs{\theta_i} \ge \pi - \alpha_\ell\), we have
    \begin{equation}
        \hyperbolicDistance{v_0}{v_n}
        \le
        \hyperbolicDistance{u_0}{u_n}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary corr:covariances of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $X_1, \dots, X_n \in \mathbb{R}(d)$ be independent random vectors, such that $U_i \coloneqq \norm*{\norm{X_i}}_{\psi_{\alpha}} < \infty$ for some $\alpha \ge 2$. Denote 
    \[
    \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \E X_i X^T_i, \quad
    \sigma^2 \coloneqq \norm*{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}, 
    \quad
    U^2 \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n U_i^2, \quad
    K \coloneqq \max_{i \in [n]} U_i ,\quad
    z \coloneqq z\lr{U, \sigma; \frac{\alpha}{2}}.
    \]
    Then, with probability at least $1 - d e^{-\mathrm{x}}$, it holds
    \[
    \lambda_{\max}\lr{\sum^n_{i=1} X_i X^T_i - \boldsymbol{\Sigma}} \le 2 \sigma K z \sqrt{\mathrm{x}} + \frac{4 K^2 z}{\min\lrc{2 \alpha z^{\alpha}, \hspace{0.2em}\underline{\log}\hspace{0.2em} \lr{\lr{ \frac{K }{\sqrt{2}\sigma }}^2 \mathrm{x}} }} \mathrm{x} .
    \]

[Def pi-realizable of arXiv:2607.19511, 'A Conditional Probability Hierarchy for Stochastic Choice\footnote{We thank Samson Abramsk'] A stochastic choice rule $G \mapsto c_G(\cdot)$ is \textbf{realizable as a $\Pi$-based probability mixture} if there is a finitely additive probability measure $Q$ on $(\Pi, {\cal D}_\Pi)$ such that for all $E \in \cal F$ and $G \in \cal G$:
\begin{equation}~
c_G(E) = Q([E, G]_\Pi).
\end{equation}

body:
[Proposition prop:VDC_conseq of arXiv:2609.04045, 'Heat content and spectrum for subordinated sub-Laplacians'] Suppose that $\Omega$ is an open set in $\mathbb{G}$.
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
    \item If $\Omega$ satisfies the volume density condition then $\operatorname{Vol}(\partial\Omega)=0$.
    \item If $\Omega$ satisfies the intrinsic exterior cone condition and $\overline{\Omega}$ has finite volume, then it also satisfies the volume density condition. In particular, if $\Omega$ is open, bounded with $C^1$ boundary having no characteristic points, it satisfies the volume density condition.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Proposition prop:VDC_conseq of arXiv:2609.04045

[Definition of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] A probability measure $\mu\in \mathcal{P}(G)$ is {\em $\Phi$-symmetrization resistant relative to $\mathcal{P}$ with constant $c>0$} if  
$$
A_{\Phi, \mathcal{P}}(\mu) \geq c\Phi(\mu) .
$$
If this holds with $c=1$, we simply say that $\mu$ is {\it $\Phi$-symmetrization resistant} in $\mathcal{P}$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'

[Theorem 14 (Frequency-envelope variant) of arXiv:2606.16662, '2606.16662'] Fix \(0<T\le T_0\) and a finite family \(\mathcal M\) of mixed labels.
Assume the Fourier-diagonal covariance model \eqref{eq:conv-cov} together with the envelope coefficient bounds \eqref{eq:env-K}--\eqref{eq:env-A-increment}.  Let \((\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau,\sigma)\) be such that, for every \(\tau\in\mathcal M\), the two quantities \(\mathfrak S_{\tau,H}^{\eps}(\beta_\tau,\sigma)\) and \(\mathfrak S_{\tau,B}^{\eps}(\zeta_\tau,\sigma)\) in \eqref{eq:env-SH}--\eqref{eq:env-SB} are finite, with \(\eps>0\) leaving room for the time-lift absorption \eqref{eq:time-lift-absorb}.  Then, for every finite \(p\ge2\), the centered cutoff operators satisfy
\begin{equation}
        B_\Lambda^\tau\longrightarrow B^\tau
        \quad\hbox{in}\quad
        L^p\bigl(\Omega;\mathcal L(X_T^\sigma,Y_T^{\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau})\bigr)
\end{equation}
and almost surely in the corresponding operator norm.  If, in addition, a deterministic diagonal resolution has been chosen so that the retained branches satisfy \eqref{eq:env-retained-bound}, the localized source-tail bound \eqref{eq:env-X-localized}, and fixed-block convergence in \(Y_T^{\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau}\), then
\begin{equation}
        T_\Lambda^{\tau,\mathfrak P}=T_\Lambda^\tau-\Ctr^\tau_\Lambda
        \longrightarrow \Ret^\tau+B^\tau
        \quad\hbox{in}\quad
        \mathcal L(X_T^\sigma\cap\mathcal X_T,Y_T^{\beta_\tau,\zeta_\tau})
\end{equation}
almost surely and in \(L^p(\Omega)\).  Fully Wick-subtracted branches are obtained by setting \(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda=0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The exponential criteria used to close the simplicity argument are the following.

\textup{(i)} Assume the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{thm:growth}. Let $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$ and choose $\beta>\gamma_H$. If
\[
\limsup_{|x|\to\infty}\left[a(x)+\lambda_p+d\big(M_J(\beta)-1\big)+q_1\beta\right]<0,
\]
where $M_J(\beta)=\int_\R J(z)e^{\beta|z|}\,dz$, then $W(x)=e^{\beta\sqrt{1+x^2}}$ satisfies $(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)W\le-\delta W$
outside a compact interval for some $\delta>0$. Every positive eigenfunction associated with $\lambda_p$ is $o(W)$. Consequently $\lambda_p$ is simple in the positive cone.

\textup{(ii)} Let $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$. Assume that every positive principal eigenfunction satisfies the exponential Harnack bound of Lemma~\ref{thm:growth} with exponent $\gamma_H$. Suppose there exist $\beta_+,\beta_->\gamma_H$ such that
\[
\limsup_{x\to+\infty}\left[a(x)+\lambda_p+d(M(\beta_+)-1)+q(x)\beta_+\right]<0
\]
and
\[
\limsup_{x\to-\infty}\left[a(x)+\lambda_p+d(M(\beta_-)-1)-q(x)\beta_-\right]<0,
\]
where $M(\beta)=\int_\R J(z)e^{\beta z}\,dz$; symmetry makes $M$ even. Then $\lambda_p$ is simple in the positive cone.

[Lemma do of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] For any $G$-invariant $2$-form $\sigma=\sigma_\ag+\sigma_\qg$, $\sigma_\qg=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Delta_\qg}$ as in (equation s of the paper) (i.e., $\sigma_\qg(E_\alpha,E_{-\alpha})=y_\alpha$), the only possibly nonzero components of $d\sigma$ are given by 
$$
d\sigma(E_\alpha,E_\beta,E_\gamma)= N_{\alpha,\beta}(y_\alpha+y_\beta+y_\gamma), \qquad \alpha+\beta+\gamma=0, 
$$
$$
d\sigma(A,E_\alpha,E_{-\alpha}) =\sigma_\ag(A,A_\alpha), \qquad \forall A\in\ag^c, \;\alpha\in\Delta_\qg.    
$$ 
Furthermore, as a real form on $\pg$,  
$$
d\sigma(A,e_\alpha,f_\alpha) = \sigma_\ag(A,(\im H_\alpha)_\ag) 
\qquad\forall A\in\ag,\; \alpha\in\Delta_\qg^+, 
$$
where the subscript $\ag$ denotes $Q$-orthogonal projection on $\ag$ (i.e., $(\im H_\alpha)_\ag=\im A_\alpha$).

body: [SYNTHESIS 09-08 09:5x] Bernoulli 2/3: the three obstructions found separately - the CRT free window at 0.369m, the automaton floor of log 2, and the two-entropies gap log 3 versus log(3/2) - are ONE arithmetic deficit. Everything is a function of (A_m, x_m); the bit is A_m mod 2 and the depth-k history is fixed by A_m mod 3^k, so the coupling is governed by whether A_m equidistributes mod 2x3^k - and A_m ranges over only about (3/2)^m consecutive integers. Hence the free window is exactly k < m log(3/2)/log 3 = 0.36907m (where 3^k still fits), and the full history needs 3^m residues against (3/2)^m available, a shortfall of 2^m = log 2 per step. Same number three ways, and log 2/log(4/3) = 2.4094 is the same 2.41 reported independently. ONE WALL, not three: the integer A_m is too small a register for the information the phase history carries. It bounds only arguments that DECOUPLE bit from history; an argument estimating the actual correlation (measured defect 0.048, far below log 2) is untouched

[Corollary cor:step-two-consequences of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~(thm:main of the paper), the family $(A_h)$ is
locally bounded on test functions, and
\[
  A_hf\longrightarrow\mathcal A_\mu f
  \quad\text{in }L^p_{\mathrm{loc}}(M,\mu),
  \qquad 1\le p<\infty.
\]
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
  \widehat V\,\mathcal A_\mu f
  =\frac12\operatorname{div}_{\mu}\bigl(M^\sharp(df)\bigr)
  =\frac12\operatorname{div}_{\mu}\left(
    \sum_{i,j=1}^kM_{ij}(X_jf)X_i
  \right)
\end{equation}
in distributions and on every privileged-coordinate patch,
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma_j
  =\frac12\sum_{i=1}^k
  \bigl(X_iM_{ij}+M_{ij}\operatorname{div}_\mu X_i\bigr)
  \quad\text{almost everywhere}.
\end{equation}

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): Let E_1,...,E_k be the selected witness rows in deletion order; choose one pivot coordinate p_s from each witness pair. The pivots are distinct and E_s contains no later pivot p_t (t>s), so the matrix (h_s(p_t))_{s,t=1..k} is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Consequently {h_1,...,h_k} united with {e_i : i not in {p_1,...,p_k}} is a coordinate basis, and k <= ell/log2(4/3). All selected dense witnesses can be inserted simultaneously after O(ell) exchanges. If an old selector used a removed pivot Q_{p_s}, select the witness Y_s and add the discrepancy e_s = Q_{p_s} - Y_s: at most one new direction per exchange. Under bounded congestion the exchanged-basis quotient rank remains linear. Notes: ell = entropy defect ell(A). What fails is the stronger hope that ALL remaining rows are paid solely by the number of selected witnesses - ruled out by the Walsh crosspolytope (p.43).

[Lemma lem:loc_t of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] The quotient category $\cE=\cD/F(\cC)$ coincides with the localization along the components of the natural transformation $\tau\colon 1_{\cD}\to S$. Furthermore, any morphism $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{h}\cE}(X,Y)$ can be represented by a cospan in $\mathrm h\cD$ of the form
\[
X \xrightarrow{g} S^nY\xleftarrow{\tau^n_Y}Y, \qquad \tau^n_Y\coloneqq  \tau_{S^{n-1}Y}\cdots\tau_{SY}\tau_Y
\]
for some $n\geq 0$, in the sense that $f=(\tau_Y^n)^{-1}g$ in $\mathrm{h}\cE$.

body:
[Theorem 1 (Descent--Hochster decomposition; informal form) of arXiv:2609.01882, '\textbf{Coxeter Descents and Parabolic Homotopy Colimits}\\[2mm] \large A Hochster-type de'] For every finite Coxeter system $(W,S)$ and every simplicial complex $\mathcal K\subseteq 2^S$ there is a based chain decomposition
\[
  \BK_{\mathcal K}(W)
  \cong
  \bigoplus_{w\in W}
  \Sigma^{2\ell(w)} C_*(A_{\mathcal K},L_{\mathcal K,\DesR(w)};\Z),
\]
and each relative summand admits an explicit unit Morse reduction
\[
  C_*(A_{\mathcal K},L_{\mathcal K,D};\Z)
  \simeq
  \Sigma\wtC_*(\sd\mathcal K_D;\Z).
\]
Consequently
\[
  H_n(\BK_{\mathcal K}(W);\Z)
  \cong
  \bigoplus_{w\in W}
  \wtH_{n-2\ell(w)-1}(\mathcal K_{\DesR(w)};\Z).
\]
For Weyl groups, $\BK_{\mathcal K}(W)$ is the cellular chain complex of $\XK(G)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Descent--Hochster decomposition; informal form

For every integer N >= 2 let X be uniform on H_N = {x in {-1,1}^N : x_1 x_2 ... x_N = 1}. Then every family of at most N - 1 coordinates of X is mutually independent, each coordinate an unbiased sign: P(X_i = s_i for i in I) = 2^(-|I|) for every proper subset I of {1, ..., N} and all signs s_i. The whole family is not independent: X_1 X_2 ... X_N = 1 almost surely, whereas for N independent unbiased signs the product is itself an unbiased sign. In bits b_i = (1 - X_i)/2 this is the uniform law on the words of even parity; N = 3 gives the classical three pairwise independent but not mutually independent events.
N is an integer, N >= 2
X is uniform on the sign vectors whose product is 1

body:
[Defn of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] Let $0 \le \Delta < \infty$. A graph $G = (V,E)$ is called \emph{$\Delta$-simply connected}
   if for any edge cycle $C \subset E$, there exist edge cycles $C_1,...,C_N$ with each $\mathrm{diam} C_i \le \Delta$
   such that $C = C_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus C_N$,
   where $A \oplus B$ denotes the symmetric difference of sets $(A \setminus B) \sqcup (B \setminus A)$.
   That is, every cycle of $G$ is generated (under symmetric difference) by cycles of diameter at most $\Delta$.
   If $G$ is $\Delta$-simply connected for some $\Delta < \infty$, then we call $G$ \emph{coarsely simply connected}.
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'

body:
[Defstar def:boundary of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Let $\Delta \in \{0,\infty\}$.

\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
	\item
	$\Delta$ is \textbf{instantaneous} if
	\[
	\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}(T_\Delta=0)=1,
	\qquad 
	T_\Delta:=\inf\{t>0: X_t\neq \Delta\}.
	\]
	Equivalently,
	\[
	\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}\big(\forall t>0,\ \exists s\in(0,t): X_s\neq \Delta\big)=1.
	\]

\item   
$\Delta$ is \textbf{continuous} if, under $\mathbb{P}_\Delta$, the process is either identically equal to $\Delta$ (absorbing case) or leaves $\Delta$ without a jump, that is, the jump measure of the process vanishes at~$\Delta$.

Equivalently, in the non-absorbing case, if one denotes by $G$ the set of strictly positive left-end points of excursion intervals away from $\Delta$, then
\[\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}\left( \forall s\in G, \ X_s=\Delta \right)=1.\]
\item  $\Delta$ is \textbf{non-sticky} if
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}_x(X_t=\Delta)=0,\ \forall t\in (0,\infty), \ x\in [0,\infty].\end{equation}
Equivalently, the Lebesgue measure of the $\Delta$-level set $\{t\geq 0: X_t\in \Delta\}$ is zero. 
\item $\Delta$ is \textbf{regular-for-itself} if 
\begin{equation}\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}(R^{\Delta}=0)=1, \text{ with } R^\Delta:=\inf\{t>0: X_{t-}=\Delta \text{ or } X_t=\Delta\}.
\end{equation}
In words, the process started from $\Delta$, returns immediately to $\Delta$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Defstar def:boundary of arXiv:2605.06488

body:
[Proposition 4 (LDP for $R_n$) of arXiv:2605.22445, 'Generalized specific entropy on Wiener space with application to Martingale Optimal Transp'] Under the $1$-dimensional Wiener measure $\mathbb P$, the sequence $(R_n)_{n\ge1}$ satisfies a large deviation principle on $\mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d))$ with speed $n$ and good rate function $I$, i.e. 
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (i)}] For every open set $G \subset \mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d))$, $$ \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \mathbb W ( R_n \in G)  \geq - \inf_{P \in G} I(P).$$
\item[{\rm (ii)}] For every closed set $F \subset \mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d))$, $$ \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \mathbb W ( R_n \in F)  \leq - \inf_{P \in F} I(P).$$
\item[{\rm (iii)}] For any $k \in \mathbb R_+$, $\{P \in \mathcal M_1(D([0,1],\mathbb R^d)): \, I(P) \leq k\}$ is compact in weak topology. 
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: LDP for $R_n$

[Lemma lem:subordination-semicircular of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] As in [jekel2024pha], let $\mathcal{B} = L^\infty[-2,2]$, let $\tau_{\mathcal{B}}(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_{-2}^2 f(x)\sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx$, and let $S \in \mathcal{B}$ be the identity function, so that $S$ is a standard semicircular element. Let $(\mathcal{M}_n,\tau_n)$ be the free product of $(M_n(\mathbb{C}),\operatorname{tr}_n)$ with $(\mathcal{B},\tau_{\mathcal{B}})$, so that $\mathcal{M}_n$ is generated by its subalgebra $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and a freely independent semicircular element $S$.

Fix $0<\beta<\tfrac12$ and let $D \in M_n(\mathbb{R})$ satisfy $D\succeq I_n$. 
Let $F_{\beta,-D}:\mathbb H\to\mathbb H$
be the subordination function of $G_{\beta S-D}$ subordinate to $G_{-D}$ from \pref{thm: subordination}, i.e.
$G_{\beta S-D}(z)=G_{-D}(F_{\beta,-D}(z))$.

Then the following properties are true of $F_{\beta,-D}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*), ref=\thetheorem(\alph*)]
    \item 
    $F_{\beta,-D}$ extends analytically onto the non-negative real ray, i.e. $F_{\beta,-D}(a)$ exists and is differentiable for $a \in \mathbb R$ satisfying $a \geqslant 0$.
    \item 
    \[F_{\beta,-D}\left(\beta^2\operatorname{tr}_n(D^{-1})\right) = 0.\]
    \item 
    \[F_{\beta,-D}'\left(\beta^2\operatorname{tr}_n(D^{-1})\right) = \frac{1}{1-\beta^2\operatorname{tr}_n(D^{-2})}.\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition D:prelandscapes of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] A random function $\mathcal{M}^\rho: \mathbb{Q}^4 \cap \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R}$ is a \textbf{(half-space) pre-landscape} with parameter $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$ if the following three conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item (Triangle inequality) For any $o = (x, s)$, $p = (y, r)$, $q = (z, t) \in \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0} \times \mathbb{Q}$ with $s<r<t$, we have
				$\mathcal{M}^\rho(o; p) + \mathcal{M}^\rho(p; q) \le \mathcal{M}^\rho(o; q)$.
				\item (Independent increments) For any $s_1<s_2<\cdots<s_k \in \mathbb{Q}$, the increments $\mathcal{M}^\rho(\cdot, s_i; \cdot, s_{i+1}):\mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}^2 \to \mathbb{R}, i\in\llbracket1, k-1 \rrbracket$ are independent.
                \item (KPZ fixed point marginals) Recall that $\NW_{+}$ is the set of all $f \in \operatorname{UC}_+$ such that $\text{supp}(f) = \{x : f(x) > -\infty\}$ is finite. Consider any function $f \in \NW_{+}$ with $\text{supp}(f) \subset \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}$ and $f(\mathbb{R})\subset\mathbb{Q}\cup\{-\infty\}$.  Then for any $t, s \in \mathbb{Q}$, $s > 0$ and any finite set $Y \subset \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}$ we have that
				\[
				 (f \diamond \mathcal{M}^\rho(\cdot, t; y, t + s) : y \in Y)
				\stackrel{d}{=} (\mathfrak{h}^\rho (t, y; f) : y \in Y).
				\]
                Here the right-hand side above is given by Theorem (T:half-space-fixed-point of the paper).
\end{enumerate}
Moving forward, we will use the notation $\mathcal{M}^\rho_{s, t}(\cdot, \cdot) = \mathcal{M}^\rho(\cdot, s; \cdot, t)$ for the increment in a pre-landscape from time $s$ to time $t$, and the notation $\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f = \mathfrak{h}^\rho (t, \cdot; f)$, which will help emphasize the semigroup structure under metric composition.
title: Definition D:prelandscapes of arXiv:2604.10020

[Lem 38 of arXiv:2510.22783, 'Universality of Cutoff for Riffle Shuffling'] With all assumptions in Proposition \ref{prop:new-firstmoment}, we have for all $y\in \tal,z\in \tar$ and $x \in A_{y,z}^{\stable}$, the following holds.
        \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
            \item 
            
            If $c_L(x)\geq 2\delta$, we have
        \begin{equation}
            \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathbb P[(i,i+1)\in E(G_{B_x})]^2\leq C N^{4 c_L(x)- c_F(x)+2c_E( x)+O(\delta)} + e^{-\Omega(N^{\delta-o(1)})}.
        \end{equation}
            \item
             
            If $ c_L(x)< 2\delta$, $ c_F\geq\delta-(\log N)^{-1/2}$ and $A_{y,z}^{\stable}\neq\{y\vee z\}$, we have
              \begin{equation}
                  \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathbb P[(i,i+1)\in E(G_{B_x})]^2\leq C N^{- c_F(x)+2c_E( x)+O(\delta)} + e^{-\Omega(N^{\delta-o(1)})}.
              \end{equation}
            \item 
            
            If $c_L(x)<2\delta$ and $ c_F(x)<\delta-(\log N)^{-1/2}$, then $x=y\vee z$ and $A_{y,z}^{\stable}=\{y\vee z\}$.
            \item 
            
            If $A_{y,z}^{\stable}=\{y \vee z\}$ and $c_L(y \vee z)<2\delta$, 
            we have $x=y\vee z$ and
            \begin{equation}
                \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathbb P[(i,i+1)\in E(G_{B_{x}})]^2\leq C N^{2c_L(x)+2c_E(x)+O(\delta)} + e^{-\Omega(N^{\delta-o(1)})}.
            \end{equation}
        \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition SI_subshift_cocycle of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] Let $ X \subset \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ be a strongly irreducible subshift for $ d \geq 2$. Let $G$ be a finitely generated group and $c:X\times \mathbb{Z}^d\to G$ be a continuous cocycle. For all $x\in X$, consider the map $c_x:\mathbb{Z}^d\to G$ given by $c_x(v)=c(x,v)$. Then there exists a constant $K$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}
            \item For all $x,y\in X$ and $u\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, there are group elements $g_1, g_2\in G$ such that $|g_1|, |g_2|<K$ and $c_x(u)=g_1c_y(u)g_2$.
        \item For all $x\in X$ and $v,w\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, there are group elements $g_1, g_2\in G$ such that $|g_1|, |g_2|<K$ such that $c_x(v+w)=c_x(v)g_1c_x(w)g_2$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition SI_subshift_cocycle of arXiv:2605.02226

[Definition 38 (Cemetery extension) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Given $(\mathcal T,K) \in \Omega$,  for every vertex $u$ with $K(u)=1$, we attach a unique child $u^\dagger=(u1)$ and declare recursively that
\[
    \delta(u) = 1\,\, (\text{instead of }0),\qquad K(u^\dagger)=1,
\qquad
X(u\to u^\dagger)=0.
\]
Every cemetery vertex again has a unique cemetery child with the same properties. In this way, every leaf is prolonged into an infinite ray of mass $1$ vertices with zero displacement.
We write $\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}_n$ for the extended tree constructed from
$\mathcal{T}_n \sim \Pp^{(n, \theta)}$. For convenience, we also set
\[
\kappa_1(t):=0.
\]
By construction, $\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}_n$ belongs to the space $\widetilde\Omega$ of
cemetery-extended trees defined
in Subsection \ref{subsec:spaces}.
title: Cemetery extension

[Theorem Thm.StrongUniqueness of arXiv:2411.15485, '\bf\Large Stochastic Volterra Equations for Local Times of Spectrally Positive L\'evy Proc'] If $\bar{\bar{\nu}}(0+)<\infty$, the stochastic Volterra equation (equation MainThm.SVE of the paper) has a unique strong solution. Moreover, the solution is a semimartingale with the following representation
 	\begin{eqnarray}
 	\left\{ \begin{split}
 	X_\zeta(t) 
 	&= \zeta \cdot c\cdot W'(t)  
 	+  \int_0^\zeta\int_0^\infty \big( W(t) -W(t-y)\big) \, N_0(dz, dy) \cr
 	&\quad + \int_0^t \Big( W''(0+) \cdot M(s) +  \int_0^s W'''(s-r)M(r)\,dr \Big) \, ds + \frac{1}{c}\cdot M(t),\cr
 	M(t) &= \int_0^t   \int_0^r \int_0^{X_\zeta(s)} \int_{r-s}^\infty    \widetilde{N}_\nu(ds,dz,dy)\,dr + \int_0^t \int_0^{X_\zeta(s)} \, B_c(ds,dz).
 	\end{split}
 	\right.
 	\end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Thm.StrongUniqueness of arXiv:2411.15485

body:
[Lemma lem:threshold of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Suppose that $f\colon B_1(0)\to [0,\infty)$ is an $L$-Lipschitz threshold-admissible  landscape for $\{\bm{x}_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^s$ with parameters $(\varepsilon,\rho,\tau_0,\tau_1)$. Let $G\subset B_1(\bm{0})$ be a finite set satisfying
		\[
		{\rm mesh}_{B_1}(G)
	<
		\min\left\{
		\rho-\varepsilon,\,
		\frac{\tau_1-\tau_0}{L}
		\right\}.
		\]
		Define the thresholded set
		\begin{eqnarray}
		G_{\tau_1}
		:=
		\{\boldsymbol\omega\in G:f(\boldsymbol\omega)<\tau_1\}.
		\end{eqnarray}
		By (equation eq:2.2 of the paper), 	
		$$	
		G_{\tau_1}
		\subseteq
		\bigcup_{\ell=1}^s B_\rho(\bm{x}_\ell).
		$$
In addition,
		\[
		B_\rho(\bm{x}_\ell)\cap G_{\tau_1} \neq \emptyset,\quad  \forall \ell\in\{1,\dots,s\}. 
		\]

[Theorem 5 (Fixed-kernel comparison before grazing) of arXiv:2608.16701, 'Order-Sensitive Fast-Synapse Limits in Sparse Excitatory--Inhibitory Threshold--Reset Netw'] Fix the kernels and class data above and let $T$ be a regular horizon.  There
is $C_{T,\mathrm{data}}<\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large $N$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\left[
 \mathfrak d_{q_i^N,T}(I_i^N,I)
 +\|I_i^N-I\|_{L^1(0,T)}
 \right]
 \le C_{T,\mathrm{data}}\left(
 \Delta_N+\sum_{q=1}^Q|\pi_q^N-\pi_q|
 \right).
 
\end{equation}
No smallness condition on $\alpha_\E+\alpha_\I$ is required.

As the sets of vertices and edges remain the same,  we still use the notation $\underline{G}=(V,E)$. body:
[Lemma lem:cancellations of arXiv:2411.08018, 'Last passage percolation in hierarchical environments'] The following is true for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$.

    Fix real numbers $x,y>0$.
    Fix also an integer $m\ge1$ and real numbers $x_1,\dots,x_m,y_1,\dots,y_m>0$ satisfying
    \[
        x=\sum_{j=1}^m x_j,\qquad y=\sum_{j=1}^m y_j.
    \]
    Suppose that for all $j\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$,
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{1+\delta}\cdot \frac{y}{x}\le  \frac{y_j}{x_j} \le (1+\delta)\frac{y}{x}.
    \end{align*}
    Then we have
    \begin{align*}
        \sum_{j=1}^m\sqrt{x_j y_j}\ge  (1- \delta^2) \sqrt{xy}.
    \end{align*}
title: Slope cancellations

body:
[Proposition 27 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $X\rightarrow X/G$ is an HKG cover. Let
$$l_1<\cdots<l_s$$
be the lower jumps of the wild cyclic subgroup $H=C_{p^s}$ at the wild branch point. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
\smallskip
{\bf (1) (Bleher--Chinburg--Kontogeorgis)} For each $b\in\llbracket0,p^s-1\rrbracket$, with the notation of Proposition \ref{P3}(4), we have
\begin{equation}
d_b=\left\lfloor \frac{N_{s,b}}{p^s}\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor \frac{\sum_{i=1}^s p^{s-i}[p-1+(p-1-\delta_{i,b})l_i]}{p^s}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}

{\bf (2)} The set $\{x^idx|i\in\llbracket0,d_b-2\rrbracket\}$ is a $k$-basis of $H^0\bigl(\mathbb P_k^1,\Omega_{\mathbb P_k^1}(D_b)\bigr)$. In particular, if $d_b\le 1$, then this $k$-vector space is $\{0\}$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} For $b\in\llbracket0,p^s-1\rrbracket$, we have $d_b=0$ if and only if $b=p^s-1$.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} The sequence $(d_b)_{b\in\llbracket0,p^s\rrbracket}$ is non-increasing.

[Theorem label_multiple_vertices_conditional_degrees of arXiv:2606.09386, 'High-degree vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs with freezing'] Fix $m,k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $(b_v)_{v\in [k]}\in[0,m+1)^k$. Let $V_1,\ldots,V_k\in\mathbb{A}_n$ be distinct active vertices selected uniformly at random. Let $(d_v(n))_{v\in[k]}$ be $k$ integer-valued sequences diverging to infinity such that, for all $v\in[k]$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}d_v(n)/h_n^+ = b_v$. Fix a choice sequence $\mathbf x$ such that Assumption~$\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}$(item:geq1 of the paper) and~$\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}$(item:lb of the paper) are satisfied  with $I_{\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}}=\mathcal{O}((h_n^+)^{\gamma_0(1/2-\delta)})$, where $\gamma_0\in(1,\min\{(1/2+\delta)^{-1},(1-2\delta)^{-1}\})$ and $\delta$ is as in Part~(item:lb of the paper).
Let $(M_i)_{i\in[k]}$ and $(N_i)_{i\in[k]}$ be i.i.d.\ standard normal random variables. Then, conditionally on the event $\{\deg_n(V_v)\geq d_v\text{ for all }v\in[k]\}$,
\begin{equation} \begin{aligned} 
\bigg({}&\frac{u_n(V_v)-(mh_n^+-\frac{m}{m+1}d_v)}{\sqrt{mh_n^+-\frac{m}{(m+1)^2}d_v}}, \frac{h_{V_v}^+-(h_n^+-\frac{1}{m+1}d_v)}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{(m+1)^2}d_v}}\bigg)_{v\in [k]}\\
&\buildrel {\mathrm{d}}\over{\longrightarrow} \bigg(M_i\sqrt{\frac{mb_v}{(m+1)^2-b_v}}+N_i\sqrt{1-\frac{mb_v}{(m+1)^2-b_v}},M_i\bigg)_{i\in[k]}.
\end{aligned} \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 143 (Exterior Chen representation of the geometric state) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] For $x\in H$ and $A\in\mathcal S_2(H)_{\rm sk}$, define
\begin{equation}
 
 \mathscr E(x,A):=\exp_\wedge(x+2\alpha_A).
\end{equation}
Then the following hold.

\textup{(i)} The series belongs to $\mathscr F^\wedge(H)$ and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 
 \|\mathscr E(x,A)\|_{\mathscr F^\wedge}^2
 \le(1+\|x\|^2)\exp(4\|\alpha_A\|^2).
\end{equation}

\textup{(ii)} If
\[
 (x,A)\star(y,B)
 =\bigl(x+y,A+B+\Anti(x\otimes y)\bigr),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 
 \mathscr E\bigl((x,A)\star(y,B)\bigr)
 =\mathscr E(x,A)\wedge\mathscr E(y,B).
\end{equation}
Thus the exterior product is closed on $\mathscr G_2^\wedge(H)$ and
$\mathscr E$ is a topological group isomorphism from the geometric step-two
state group onto its exterior Chen image, with the transported topology in
\eqref{eq:exterior-Chen-image-group}.  Its degree-one and degree-two coordinates
recover $x$ and $A$.

\textup{(iii)} Writing
$\mathscr E(x,A)=\sum_{k\ge0}\Xi_k(x,A)$ by homogeneous degree,
\begin{equation}
 
 \Xi_{2N}(x,A)=\frac{2^N}{N!}\alpha_A^{\wedge N},
 \qquad
 \Xi_{2N+1}(x,A)=\frac{2^N}{N!}
 x\wedge\alpha_A^{\wedge N}.
\end{equation}
For a state $z=(x,A,q)$, the joint map
\[
 z\longmapsto(\mathscr E(x,A),q)
\]
is a continuous lossless group isomorphism onto
$\mathscr G_2^\wedge(H)\times\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}$, where the second
factor is additive.  The covariance channel is exactly the information
forgotten by the exterior factor alone.

[Proposition prop:tropp_bound of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $\mathbf{X}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_n \in \mathbb{H}(d)$ be a sequence adapted to a filtration $\mathscr{F}_1 \subset \mathscr{F}_2 \subset \dots \subset \mathscr{F}_n $. 
    Let $\mathbf{X}_k$ satisfy for all $k = 1, \dots, n$
    \[
    \E[\mathbf{X}_k | \mathscr{F}_{k-1}] = 0, 
    \quad
    \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{X}_k) \le K~\text{a.s.}
    \]
    Set for all $k = 1, \dots, n$
    \[
    \mathbf{S}_k  \coloneqq \sum^k_{i=1} \mathbf{X}_i, 
    \quad
    \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k \coloneqq \sum^k_{i=1}  \E\left[\mathbf{X}^2_i \middle| \mathscr{F}_{i-1}\right].
    \]

[Definition def:uniform-generating of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] The family $W^\lambda$ is \emph{uniformly two-generating} on a set $A$ if,
for every $(\lambda,x)\in\Theta\times A$, the linear map
\[
  \mathcal B_{\lambda,x}(a,b)
  :=\sum_i a_iW_i^\lambda(x)
  +\sum_{i<j}b_{ij}[W_i^\lambda,W_j^\lambda](x)
\]
is onto and admits a right inverse whose norm is bounded independently of
$(\lambda,x)$.

[Thm 40 of arXiv:2603.05174, 'Regularization of the superposition principle: Potential theory meets Fokker-Planck equati'] Assume that $\beta,D,b$ satisfy conditions (i)-(iv), let $0\leq u_0\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}u_0(x)\;dx=1$, and let $u(\cdot,\cdot;u_0),\; \mu_t(dx):=u(t,x;u_0)dx, t\geq 0$ be the solution to \eqref{eq:BR-FP}/\eqref{eq:NL-ab}.
Then the "linearized" conditions
\begin{equation*}
\mathbf{H_{a^u,b^u}^{\sqrt{u}}},\quad \mathbf{H_{\sf \lesssim u}}({\sf L^u}), \quad \mathbf{H^{\sf TV}_0}({\sf L^u})
\end{equation*}
are fulfilled, where $a^u, b^u,$ and ${\sf L^u}$ are given in \eqref{eq:a^ub^u}.
Consequently, the conclusions of \Cref{thm:MVE} and \Cref{coro: capacity} are valid in this situation.

[Lemma meanfieldspectralgap of arXiv:2606.01937, 'Stationary fluctuations for an exclusion process with mass and energy conservation'] For $\alpha\in [0,1]$, define the binomial product measure $\varpi_\alpha = \mathrm{Bin}(\kappa ,\alpha )^{\otimes\mathbb{Z}}$. There exists a universal constant $C_{11}=C_{11}(\kappa )>0$ such that for any local function $f:\Omega\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}$ supported in $\{0,\hdots ,\ell -1\}$ for some $\ell\ge 1$, and such that~$\varpi_\alpha(f)=0$ for any $\alpha\in [0,1]$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{Var}_{\varpi_\alpha}(f) \le \frac{C_{11}}{\ell}\sum_{x,y=0}^{\ell -1}\int_{\Omega}\eta_x(\kappa -\eta_y)\big[ f(\eta^{x\to y})-f(\eta )\big]^2\,\mathrm{d}\varpi_\alpha(\eta ).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    \end{equation}

body:
[Definition def:discrete_process of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $L$ be a positive integer,
  $y^L_0 \in \{ 1, \ldots, L \}$  and
  $\sigma^1_0, \sigma^2_0 \in \{-1, 1\}$ (resp.
  $\sigma^1_0, \sigma^2_0 \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$) . Let $\sigma^1$ and $\sigma^2$ be two
  independent Markov jump processes with the transition rates of
  figure (fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2016 of the paper)
  (resp. (fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2017 of the paper)) and respective initial states \( \sigma^1_0 \) and \( \sigma^2_0 \). Further let
  $N_1$ and $N_2$ be two independent Poisson clocks with rate $\gamma$
  independent of the $\sigma^i$. Recursively define $y^L(t)$ by $y^L(0) = y^L_0$ and,
\begin{itemize}
\item when $N_1$ rings at time $t$, $y^L(t)=\max(1,\min(L, y^L(t-) - \sigma^1(t-)))$.
\item when $N_2$ rings at time $t$, $y^L(t)=\max(1,\min(L, y^L(t-) + \sigma^2(t-)))$
\end{itemize}
title: Discrete process

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, split B, full calibration, paired). The two-vertex blend of the transductive covariance penalty keeps the simplex's gain on EMIT and closes three quarters of its deficit to the pool's hand-tuned heuristic on OCO-2 (-0.27 there); the heuristic is itself label-free, so it was added as a third vertex with barycentric weights chosen by the same criterion. P26 (a) REFUTED: on OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads -0.09 vs the pool best and +0.18 vs the two-vertex blend; (b) HELD: on EMIT it reads +4.78 vs the pool best and +0.05 vs the two-vertex blend; (c) HELD: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool) are (0.09, 0.44, 0.47) on OCO-2 and (0.59, 0.24, 0.17) on EMIT; falsifier (three-vertex worse than two-vertex by more than 0.5 on either corpus) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P27, split C, pre-registered before the split-B result was read): P27 (a) HELD: on split C OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads -0.12 vs the pool best and +0.20 vs the two-vertex blend; (b) HELD: on EMIT +4.83 vs the pool best and +0.18 vs the two-vertex blend; (c) HELD: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool) (0.11, 0.42, 0.48) on OCO-2 and (0.57, 0.26, 0.17) on EMIT; falsifier (three-vertex worse than two-vertex by more than 0.5 on either corpus) not triggered. A fourth vertex (P33, the CV-shrunk long-only stack that the calibration-only selector picks on most EMIT cells): P33 (a) REFUTED: on EMIT the four-vertex blend reads +0.06 vs the three-vertex blend and +4.84 vs the pool best (candidate B alone +5.23, the three-vertex blend +4.78); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 +0.00 vs the three-vertex blend (-0.09 vs the pool best); (c) REFUTED: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool, B) are (0.48, 0.26, 0.14, 0.12) on EMIT and (0.01, 0.48, 0.40, 0.11) on OCO-2; falsifier (four-vertex worse than three-vertex by more than 0.3 on either corpus) not triggered. P42: the held-out split D (P42): P42 (a) HELD: on split D OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads +0.06 (registered) / +0.10 (R_1) vs the pool's heuristic, its best vertex there (within 0.3); (b) HELD: on split D EMIT +4.31 / +5.33 vs the pool's heuristic (at least +4.0; P26 / P27 read +4.78 / +4.83) - on this split the simplex is the best single vertex and the blends read +0.13 / +1.27 against it; (c) REFUTED: R_1 vs the registered blend +1.08 on EMIT, +0.04 on OCO-2 (within 0.2); (d) HELD: the prediction-norm variant of the registered criterion vs the registered blend +0.00 / +0.00 (within 0.1); (e) HELD: the same for R_1 -0.05 / +0.00; falsifier (EMIT gain over the pool's heuristic below +3.0 or OCO-2 worse than it by more than 0.5, either criterion) not triggered; the (d)/(e) falsifier (a difference beyond 0.3) not triggered.
the three bases are fitted on the calibration rows only (simplex = long-only relative-metric stack; least squares = per-output ridge 1e-6; pool heuristic = per-output ridge with a GCV lambda shrunk toward the pooled convex weights by a 5-fold-CV amount); barycentric weights on the 0.1 grid (66 points); the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows; the two-vertex blend is the face with zero pool weight, so its comparison is exact

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2606.24584, '2606.24584'] Let $(D_\ell)_{\ell\geq 1}$ be a sequence of doubly stochastic matrices in $\Omega_n$. If
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^\infty \big(1-\sigma_2(D_\ell)\big) = +\infty,
\]
where $\sigma_2(D_\ell)$ denotes the second largest singular value of $D_\ell$, then
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} D_1D_2\cdots D_m = J_n.
\]
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2606.24584

Then, letting $\tau^{\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}_r = \tau_{(x_0,s)}^{\xi,-}(r)$, we have

[Cor cor;non of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$ be a probability space, and $T:\Omega\to\Omega$ be a measurable transformation. If there exists an upper probability $V$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ such that $V$ is ergodic with respect to $T$, and $P\in\operatorname{core}(V)$, then there exists a unique ergodic probability $Q\in\mathcal{ M}^e(T)\cap \operatorname{core}(V)$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ such that  for any $f\in L^1(\Omega,\mathcal{F},Q)$,
	$$
	\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} f(T^{i} \omega)=\int f dQ,\text{ for }P\text{-a.s. }\omega\in\Omega.
	$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor cor;non of arXiv:2411.00663

$h$-multiplication-table types of rank $r$ is
\[
 \Theta_{k,r}\!\left(h^{(k-1)r}\right).
\]
The total number of weak multiplication types, the total number of ordered
multiplication types, and the total number of generic multiplication types
are all
\begin{equation}
 \Theta_k\!\left(h^{(k-1)(k-2)}\right).
\end{equation}

Fix a unit vector x_star in R^n. Draw a_1,...,a_m independently from N(0,I_n), observe y_i=(a_i^T x_star)^2, and set f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-y_i)^2. Initialize x_0 independently from N(0,I_n/n), and iterate x_{t+1}=x_t-eta grad f(x_t), reusing the same samples, with eta=c for a sufficiently small positive absolute constant c. There is a sufficiently large absolute constant C such that m >= C n (log m)^13 suffices for the following event to have probability 1-o(1) as n tends to infinity: for some absolute constants gamma,rho in (0,1), there is an integer T_gamma=O(log n) with min(||x_t-x_star||_2,||x_t+x_star||_2) <= gamma(1-rho)^(t-T_gamma) for every t>=T_gamma. Thus the iteration count to error epsilon is O(log n+log(1/epsilon)). The exponent 13 is the sufficient sample condition explicitly recorded after Theorem 2, rather than an unspecified polylogarithm in Theorem 1.

$K\subset\overline\calD\setminus\Sigma$ be compact.  Then
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{b\downarrow0}
    \sup_{z\in K}
    \Pbb_z\left(|r_{\tau_\Sigma}|\le b,\ \tau_\Sigma\le M\right)=0 .
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every $\lambda\in(0,1/2)$ and every fixed $K_0>0$, with
$b_\delta=\delta^{\lambda/4}$,
\[
    \sup_{z\in K}
    \Pbb_z^\delta\left(
        |r^\delta_{\tau_\Sigma^\delta}|\le K_0b_\delta,\ 
        \tau_\Sigma^\delta\le M
    \right)\longrightarrow0
    \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0 .
\]
The same statements hold for the adjoint processes.

body: Let C and D be categories and F: C -> D, G: D -> C be functors. F is left adjoint to G (equivalently G is right adjoint to F), written F -| G, if for all objects c in C and d in D there is a bijection Hom_D(F(c), d) <-> Hom_C(c, G(d)) that is natural in both c and d, meaning it is compatible with morphisms c -> c' in C and d -> d' in D via the actions of F and G on morphisms. Equivalently, an adjunction can be specified by a unit natural transformation eta: 1_C => G o F and a counit natural transformation epsilon: F o G => 1_D (where 'o' denotes composition of functors), satisfying the triangle identities: epsilon_{F(c)} o F(eta_c) = 1_{F(c)} for every object c of C, and G(epsilon_d) o eta_{G(d)} = 1_{G(d)} for every object d of D.
title: Adjoint Functors

body:
[Theorem zeros_quartic_exp_main of arXiv:2606.29622, 'Affine Structure of the Brownian Signature'] Let $X \sim \mathcal N(0, \sigma^2)\,$, with $\sigma > 0\,$. Then,
    $$
    I(x) := \mathbb E \left[\exp(-(ix + X)^4) \right] = \frac{4^{1/3}}{\sqrt{3}\sigma^{1/3}x^{1/3}}\,\exp({\Psi(x)})\,(\cos(\Phi(x)) + o(1))
    $$
    in the limit $x \to + \infty\,$, where 
    $$
    \Psi(x) := \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}x^2-\frac{3}{2^{11/3}\sigma^{8/3}}x^{4/3} - \frac{1}{4^{5/3}\sigma^{10/3}}x^{2/3} + \frac{1}{24 \sigma^4}
    $$
    and
    $$
    \Phi(x) := -\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2^{11/3}\sigma^{8/3}}x^{4/3} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4^{5/3}\sigma^{10/3}}x^{2/3} + \frac{\pi}{6} \,.
    $$

body:
[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX, d)$ be a quasi-metric space.
  Let $\emptyset \ne \SC \subset \XX$ be bounded.
  Then, writing $\CR^\ast := \bigl(\umd(\SC)\bigr)^{-1}$, the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item \emph{(A suitable codec sequence achieves every rate below $\CR^\ast$)}
          There exists a codec sequence ${\mathscr{S}^\ast = ( (E_n^\ast, D_n^\ast) )_{n \in \N}}$
          for $\SC$ such that for every $0 \leq \CR < \CR^\ast$,
          there exists $C(\CR) > 0$ satisfying
          \[
            \delta (E_n^\ast, D_n^\ast) \leq C(\CR) \cdot n^{-\CR}
            \qquad \forall \, n \in \N
            .
          \]
          In particular, $\mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}^\ast, \SC, \XX) = \SC$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Now, assume that $\mu$ is a probability measure on $\XX$ that is critical for $\SC$,
  and set
  \[
    \CR^\sharp
    := \bigl(\lmd(\SC)\bigr)^{-1}
    .
  \]
  Then the following hold:
  \begin{enumerate}[resume,label=(\roman*)]
    \item \emph{(quantitative bound relating approximation error and number of bits)}
          Let $\CR \in (\CR^\sharp, \infty)$.
          Then there exist $c = c(\CR) > 0$ and $\eps_0 = \eps_0 (\CR) > 0$
          such that for every $n \in \N$ and every $n$-bit codec $(E_n, D_n)$ for $\SC$,
          we have
          \[
            \mu^\ast
            \Bigl(
              \bigl\{
                x \in \SC
                \,\,:\,\,
                d\bigl(x, D_n(E_n(x))\bigr) \leq \eps
              \bigr\}
            \Bigr)
            \leq 2^{n - c \cdot \eps^{-1/\CR}}
            \qquad \forall \, \eps \in (0, \eps_0)
            .
          \]

    \item \emph{(any rate above $\CR^\sharp$ is only achievable on a $\mu$-null set)}
          For every $t \in (\CR^\sharp, \infty)$ and every codec sequence
          $\mathscr{S} = \bigl( (E_n, D_n) \bigr)_{n \in \N}$,
          the set $\mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}, \SC, \XX)$ is a $\mu$-null set:
          \[
            \mu^\ast \Bigl(\mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}, \SC, \XX)\Bigr)
            = 0
            \quad \text{ for every $\CR\in (\CR^{\sharp},\infty)$.}
          \]
          In fact, even
          \[
            \mu^\ast
            \biggl(\,\,
              \bigcup_{\CR \in (\CR^\sharp, \infty)}
                \mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}, \SC, \XX)
            \biggr)
            = 0
            .
          \]
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.30549

body:
[Definition def_triangle of arXiv:2608.09105, 'Longest convex chains with i.i.d.\ points'] Let $f\colon[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous and convex.
Let us write $\mathsf{A} = (a,f(a))$ and $\mathsf{B} = (b,f(b))$.
\begin{itemize}

\item (Typical case) 
If $\partial^+f(a) < \partial^-f(b)$ and at least one of these two derivatives is finite, then we denote by $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ the triangle bounded by the following three lines: the tangent line of $f$ at $a$ with slope $\partial^+f(a)$, the tangent line of $f$ at $b$ with slope $\partial^-f(b)$, and the secant line of $f$ between $a$ and $b$.
The vertices of $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ are thus $\mathsf{A}$, $\mathsf{B}$, and the unique intersection point of the two tangent lines.
See Figure~(fig_tangency_triangle of the paper) (left).

\item (Degenerate case 1: flat)
If $\partial^+f(a)=\partial^-f(b)<\infty$, then we let $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ denote the line segment between $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$.

\item (Degenerate case 2: doubly infinite)
If $\partial^+f(a)=-\infty$ and $\partial^-f(b)=\infty$, then we let $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ denote the infinite region below the secant line, defined in (equation below_secant of the paper).
\hfill\ensuremath{\square}

\end{itemize}
title: Tangency triangles

[Proposition 7 (Intrinsic projection for spans \(m\ge 3\)) of arXiv:2607.25949, 'Block-hierarchical covariance decompositions for finite-block additive functionals'] Let \(m\ge 3\), and let $\psi\in\mathcal H_m= L^2_0(\pi_m)$. Define
\[
L_m\psi
=
E(\psi\mid X_1,\ldots,X_{m-1}),
\qquad
R_m\psi
=
E(\psi\mid X_2,\ldots,X_m),
\]
and
\[
C_m\psi
=
E(\psi\mid X_2,\ldots,X_{m-1}).
\]
Then the orthogonal projection of \(\psi\) onto \(\mathcal I_m\) is
\[
\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathcal I_m}\psi
=
\psi-L_m\psi-R_m\psi+C_m\psi .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Intrinsic projection for spans \(m\ge 3\)

[Proposition prop:BP of arXiv:2411.19163, '\bfseries Random polytopes in convex bodies:\\ Bridging the gap between extremal container'] Let $f:(\mathbb{R}^d)^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a non-negative measurable function. Then,
\begin{align*}
&\int_{(\mathbb{R}^d)^{d}}f(\mathbf{x}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{x}_d)\,\textup{d}(\mathbf{x}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{x}_d) \\
    &\quad = {(d-1)!\over 2}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}\int_\mathbb{R}\int_{H(\mathbf{w},s)^{d}}f(\mathbf{y}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{y}_d)
        \operatorname{Vol}_{d-1}({\rm co}\, \{\mathbf{y}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{y}_d\})\,\textup{d}_{H(\mathbf{w},s)}(\mathbf{y}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{y}_d)\,\textup{d} s\,\sigma_{d-1}(\textup{d}\mathbf{w}),
\end{align*}
where $\textup{d}_{H(\mathbf{w},s)}\mathbf{x}$ indicates integration with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $H(\mathbf{w},s)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma tech cond of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $f : X \to Z$ is a birational contraction morphism between two smooth separated schemes where $Z$ is quasi-projective. 
Suppose further that there is a smooth closed subscheme $Y \subseteq Z$ where $f$ defines an isomorphism away from $Y$. 
Let $\bar{Z}$ and $\bar{Y}$ be projective schemes containing $Z$ and $Y$ as schematically-dense open subschemes respectively where $\bar{Y} \subseteq \bar{Z}$ is closed.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a very ample line bundle on $\bar{Z}$, and let $f^*\mathcal{L}$ denote the pullback of the line bundle under the composition $X \xrightarrow{f} Z \hookrightarrow \bar{Z}.$

Then,
there exists $d \gg 0$ such that for $L := \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ the finite-dimensional vector space $V := \operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L)$ satisfies the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(a)] The restriction map $\operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L) \to \operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Y}, L|_{\bar{Y}})$ is surjective.
    \item[(b)] If $V_Y := \operatorname{im}(\operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L) \to \operatorname{H}^0(Y, L|_Y))$, then $V_Y$ is naturally identified with $\operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Y}, L|_{\bar{Y}}).$ 
    In particular, for $d \gg 0$, $\dim V_Y > r:= \dim Y.$
    \item[(c)] The sections of $V := \operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L)$ generate $L|_Z$, and the image sections $V_Y$ generate $L|_Y$.
    Consequently, the pulled-back sections generate $f^*L$ on $X$ and generate $f^* L |_E$ on $E$.
\end{itemize}

[Thm 13 (Girsanov's theorem; see, e.g.,~\cite{KS-BM}) of arXiv:2606.18877, 'Ergodic Properties of Non-Linear Density-Dependent Perturbations of the Ornstein--Uhlenbec'] Let \((\Omega, \{\F_t\}_{t\geq 0},\PP)\) be a probability space, and let \(\{\beta_t\}_{t\geq 0}\), be an \(\F_t\)-adapted stochastic process with values in \(\R^d\) such that
    \[
    \PP\left(
    \int_0 ^T \Vert \beta_s\Vert_2^2\,ds
    <\infty
    \right)
    =1, 
    \quad \forall\, 0<T<\infty.
    \]
    Then, if the process
    \[
    \mathcal{E}_t:=\exp\left\{
    \int_0 ^t \beta_s\,dW_s
    -\frac{1}{2}\int_0 ^t \Vert \beta_s\Vert_2^2\,ds
    \right\},
    \quad t\geq 0,
    \]
    is an \(\F_t\)-martingale under \(\PP\), then for any fixed \(0<T<\infty\) the process
    \[
    \widetilde{W}_t:= -\int_0 ^t \beta_s\,ds+ W_t, 
    \quad 0\leq t\leq T,
    \]
    is an \(\F_t\)-Brownian motion on \((\Omega,\{\F_t\}_{0\leq t\leq T},\widetilde{\PP})\) with \(\widetilde{\PP}\) a probability measure such that \(\frac{d\widetilde{\PP}}{d\PP}\Bigr|_{\F_T}=\mathcal{E}_T\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] Consider the Ising model on a graph $G\sim G_{n,d}$ (for $d\ge3$) at the critical temperature, $\beta_c=\tanh^{-1}((d-1)^{-1})$. Let $\mu_{n,\text{reg}}\in\mathcal{M}_1(\R)$ be the random measure defined as
$$\mu_{n,\text{reg}}(A):=\PR_{n,\text{reg}}(m\cdot n^{-3/4}\in A\ |\ G),\ \text{with}\ G\sim G_{n,d}.$$
Then, there exists a measure $\mu_{\text{reg}}\in\mathcal{M}_1(\R)$ such that $\mu_{n,\text{reg}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\mu_{\text{reg}}$ in the 1-Wasserstein distance associated to $\text{d}_{\text{KS}}$. This measure $\mu_{\text{reg}}$ has density $$f_{\text{reg}}(y)\varpropto \exp\left(-\frac{(d-2)(d-1)}{12d^2}y^4\right).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition theorem_size_bias_coupling of arXiv:2606.03442, 'Stein's method in network analysis'] Let $X = \sum_{j=1}^m Y_j$ be a sum of non-negative random variables, with $0 < \mathbb{E} [X] < \infty$,
   and let $F_j(\cdot;y) = \mathcal{L}\bigl(\sum_{i, i \neq j} Y_i \,|\, Y_j = y\bigr)$. Let $J$ be a random index with values in $1, \ldots, m$, with $\mathbb{P}(J = j) = \mathbb{E}[Y_j] / \mathbb{E}[X]$.
   Given $J=j$, let~$Y_j^{(s)}$ be sampled from the size biased distribution of~$Y_j$; then, if $Y_j^{(s)} = y$,
    sample~$X_j^{\star}$ from $F_j(\cdot;y)$. Then $X^{(s)} = X_J^{\star} + Y_J^{(s)}$ has the size bias distribution of~$X$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition theorem_size_bias_coupling of arXiv:2606.03442

[Proposition 14 (A general upper bound on \(\EE{\Svar}\)) of arXiv:2604.13149, 'The Distributional Tail of Worst--Case Quickselect'] Let \(A>2\), and let \(L:\R\to[0,1]\) satisfy
\[
L(x)\le F(x),
\qquad x\in(2,A).
\]
Then
\[
\EE{\Svar}
\le
2+\int_2^A \bigl(1-L(x)\bigr)\,\dd x
+\frac{\exp\!\bigl(-A\log(A/2)+A\bigr)}{\log(A/2)}.
\]

body: A topological space X is path-connected if for every pair of points x and y in X there is a path from x to y, that is, a continuous map gamma from the interval [0,1] (with its standard topology) to X such that gamma(0) = x and gamma(1) = y. Every path-connected space is connected; the converse fails in general (the topologist's sine curve is connected but not path-connected).
title: Path-connected space
Lemma lem_extra_path3 of arXiv:2506.06559
Cor frag-nonexplosive of arXiv:2511.10223

body:
[Definition Gluing of arXiv:2608.13716, 'Graph Causal Optimal Transport \\ and Wasserstein Distances'] Let $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C}$ be Polish spaces and let $\pi_1 \in \probabilities{\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}}$, $\pi_2 \in \probabilities{\mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{C}}$ such that $\pushforward{\proj{\mathcal{B}}}{\pi_1} = \pushforward{\proj{\mathcal{B}}}{\pi_2} \eqqcolon \nu \in \probabilities{\mathcal{B}}$. Let $\pi_2$ be disintegrated as $\pi_2(db, dc) = \nu(db) \otimes \kappa(dc \mid b)$ for a stochastic kernel $\kappa$.

    Then $\bigglue{\pi_1}{\pi_2}$ is defined as the measure 
    $$\bigglue{\pi_1}{\pi_2}(da, db, dc) \coloneqq \pi_1(da, db) \otimes \kappa(dc \mid b) \in \probabilities{\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{C}},$$ 
    and is called the \emph{conditional independent product} of $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$. Its $\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{C}$ marginal, $\pi_1 \mathbin{\mathop{\circ}\limits_{\raisebox{1ex}{$\scriptstyle \mathfrak{g}$}}} \pi_2 \coloneqq \pushforward{\proj{\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{C}}}{\bigglue{\pi_1}{\pi_2}}$ is called the \emph{gluing} of $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$.
title: Gluing

body:
[Corollary co:close_geodesic_small_parts of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] There exist $c>0$ and $\zeta>0$ (not depending on $M,a,a_1,a_0$) such that the following is true. Fix $M,a,a_1 > 0$ such that $a,a_1$ are sufficiently small (depending on $a_0$). 
Let $\widehat{G}_{M,a}$ be the event that for every $0 \le s < t \le \infty$, the domain $D \setminus \eta([0,s]\cup[t,\infty))$ is $(M,a)$-good. Let $U \subseteq D_\eta$ be the $\delta_1^{1+a_1}$-neighborhood of $\eta$.

For $0 < \delta_1 < \delta$, let $G_{\delta_1,\delta}$ denote the event that there exists a finite collection of intervals $[s_i,t_i] \subseteq [0,\infty]$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item if $\mathrm{dist}(\eta(t),\partial D) \le \delta_1$, then $t \in \bigcup_i [s_i,t_i]$,
\item $\bigcap_i G^U_{s_i,t_i}(r_i)$ holds for some $(r_i)$ with
\[
\sum_i r_i \le M(\delta_1/\delta)^{\zetaa_0} .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[ G_{\delta_1,\delta}^c \cap \widehat{G}_{M,a} ] = O(M\delta^{{\alpha_{\mathrm{apr}}}-c(1+a_0^{-1})(a+a_1)}(\delta_1/\delta)^{\zeta{\alpha_{\mathrm{apr}}}}) \quad\text{as}\quad \delta \to 0.\]

body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For two independent centered Gaussian fields X, Y indexed by a common finite (or suitably truncated) set T with covariance functions C_X, C_Y, Kahane's interpolation forms Z(t,u) = sqrt(u) X(t) + sqrt(1-u) Y(t) for u in [0,1] and computes d/du E[F(Z(.,u))] for a smooth test function F, obtaining, since Z(.,u) has covariance u C_X + (1-u) C_Y, d/du E[F(Z(.,u))] = (1/2) sum_{s,t in T} (C_X(s,t) - C_Y(s,t)) E[d_s d_t F(Z(.,u))]. When C_X <= C_Y pointwise (or the relevant difference has a consistent sign) and F is chosen with matching sign of mixed partials, this yields a comparison inequality between functionals of X and Y, an approach that both generalizes Slepian-type comparisons and, in the Gaussian multiplicative chaos literature, is used to show that different regularizations of a log-correlated field, such as the two-dimensional Gaussian free field, converge to the same limiting chaos measure regardless of the approximation scheme, a key technical step in constructing Liouville quantum gravity measures. It does not apply to non-Gaussian fields, the interpolation is built from independent copies of the two fields (always available, since only their laws are compared; a dependent coupling adds cross-covariance terms to the derivative), and the sign or convexity conditions on F needed to obtain a clean inequality must be verified case by case rather than assumed. Typical failure: Running the interpolation on a dependent coupling of the two fields while dropping the cross-covariance terms, or to a family of regularizations whose covariance difference does not have a consistent sign across the whole index set, which is common when comparing regularizations of a log-correlated field near its singular set; either error breaks the monotonicity the interpolation is meant to exploit, and the resulting comparison can go in the wrong direction with no explicit error term to control it. Canonical reference: Kahane, 1986, Annales des Sciences Mathematiques du Quebec; Robert and Vargas, 2010, Comptes Rendus Mathematique; Berestycki, 2017, Electronic Communications in Probability.
two independent centered Gaussian fields on a common finite or suitably truncated index set
existence and enough regularity of the covariance functions to differentiate the interpolated expectation under the integral
a consistent-sign comparison, or specific structural relation, between the two covariance kernels
the test functional F smooth with the correct sign of mixed partial derivatives for the interpolation identity to yield a useful inequality rather than an uncontrolled remainder

[Lemma lem:hetero_reference_realization of arXiv:2609.00193, 'Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and'] For any agent $m\in[M]$, policy $\pi$, and step $h\in[H]$, define
\[
w_{m,h}^{\pi}
:=
\theta_h+\int_{\mathcal X}V_{m,h+1}^{\pi}(x')\,\mu_h(\mathrm d x').
\]
Then, for every $(x,a)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal A$,
\[
\bigl|Q_{m,h}^{\pi}(x,a)-\phi(x,a)^\top w_{m,h}^{\pi}\bigr|
\le H\xi.
\]
Moreover, $\|w_{m,h}^{\pi}\|_2\le 2H\sqrt d$.

\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition The variables $\mathcal T_{x_1,x_2}$, $\tau_{x_1,x_2}$ and  $N_{x_1,x_2,t}$ of arXiv:2512.12902, 'Non-equilibrium fluctuations for the \\stirring process with births and deaths'] Given the initial position  $x_1$ and $x_2$ of particles $1$ and $2$
define in $\Omega$ the random multi-interval $\mathcal
T_{x_1,x_2}=\{s\geq 0: |x_1(s)-x_2(s)|=1\}$,  calling $\mathcal
T_{x_1,x_2,t}:=\mathcal T_{x_1,x_2}\cap [0,t]$ and $I_{x_1,x_2,t}=
\{ (s,y_1,y_2): s \in \mathcal T_{x_1,x_2,t}, y_i=x_i(s)$ and a mark
appears at $s$ between $y_1$ and $y_2$$\} $, we define the stopping
time $\tau_{x_1,x_2}$ as the smallest $s$ in $I_{x_1,x_2,\infty}$
and    $N_{x_1,x_2,t}$   the total number of elements in
$I_{x_1,x_2,t}$. Notice that the presence of other particles does
not affect the values  of $\mathcal T_{x_1,x_2}$, $\tau_{x_1,x_2}$
and  $N_{x_1,x_2,t}$.

body: [Theorem 1.3 of arXiv:2512.17823, 'van den Berg-Kesten--type correlation inequalities for disjoint polymers in the KPZ univer'] There exist $C,c,L_{0}>0$ such that the following holds. Let $y\in\mathbb R$, $K\geq 0$, and $\mathsf{A}\subseteq\mathcal{C}([0,K],\mathbb R)$ be an increasing Borel measurable set. For any $t>0$, $L\geq L_{0}(t^{-1/6}\vee 1)$, and $M>C(L+y^{2})^{3/4}$, $\displaystyle\mathbb P\Bigl(\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,2}|_{[y,y+K]}-Ct^{-1/3}\log M\in\mathsf{A}\ \Big|\ \hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}(y)=L\Bigr)$ $\displaystyle\leq\mathbb P\left(\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}|_{[y,y+K]}\in\mathsf{A}\right)+3(K+1)t^{2/3}\exp(-cM^{2}).$ The same also holds when the conditioning is replaced by $\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}(y)\geq L$. The same also holds under both conditionings when the processes are considered on $[y-K,y]$ rather than $[y,y+K]$.

[Proposition 10 (Slepian's lemma) of arXiv:2605.22146, 'Poisson approximation of the largest gaps between zeros of a stationary Gaussian process'] Let $(X_i)_{i\le n}$ and $(Y_i)_{i \le n}$ be centred Gaussian vectors satisfying, for all $1 \le i,j \le n$,
\[ \E[X_i^2] = \E[Y_i^2] \qquad \text{and} \qquad  \E[X_i X_j] \le \E[Y_i Y_j] . \]
Then for every $\ell \in \R$
\[\P \big[ X_i < \ell \ \forall i\big] \le \P \big[ Y_i < \ell  \ \forall i\big] .\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
The basic household reproduction number R_* is the expected number of global infectious contacts emanating from a single typically infected household during its entire within-household epidemic outbreak in an otherwise completely susceptible population: R_* = mu_G * mu_{out}(h), where mu_G = E[X_G] and mu_{out}(h) is the expected total number of individuals infected in the household (including the primary case). A major epidemic outbreak is possible if and only if R_* > 1.

body:
CAUTION ON THE NAME: 'Rosenblum's argument' is used for at least two different results of M. Rosenblum; this entry is the scattering-theory one, the Plancherel estimate that drives the Kato-Rosenblum theorem on trace class perturbations and the standard existence proofs for wave operators. STATEMENT: let A be a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space H with spectral measure E, let psi in H be a vector whose spectral measure mu_psi(S) = <psi, E(S) psi> is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure with density bounded by a constant M (that is, d mu_psi / d lambda <= M almost everywhere), and let K be a Hilbert-Schmidt operator on H. Then the map t -> K exp(-i t A) psi is square integrable on R as an H-valued function and the integral over R of the squared norm of K exp(-i t A) psi dt is at most 2 pi M times the square of the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of K. Consequently the quantity tends to 0 along a sequence of times, and combined with Cook's criterion this is what produces existence of wave operators for perturbations that factor through Hilbert-Schmidt operators; note that the bound is UNIFORM over all vectors psi with the same density bound M, which is how the estimate is bootstrapped from a dense set of vectors to the whole absolutely continuous subspace. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) the bounded density is essential. If psi has any point mass, for instance if psi is an eigenvector of A, then the norm of K exp(-i t A) psi equals the norm of K psi for all t and the time integral is infinite unless K psi = 0. The lemma is a statement about the absolutely continuous subspace with a locally bounded density, not about arbitrary vectors. (ii) 'Hilbert-Schmidt' cannot be relaxed to 'bounded': taking K the identity makes the left-hand side the integral of a positive constant over R, which diverges. (iii) The constant 2 pi is tied to the Fourier convention; with the kernel exp(-2 pi i t lambda) the constant is 1. (iv) Nothing is claimed about the pointwise decay of the norm of K exp(-i t A) psi in t; only its square integrability.
H is a complex Hilbert space and A is self-adjoint on it
psi lies in the absolutely continuous subspace of A and its spectral density is bounded by M almost everywhere
K is Hilbert-Schmidt (in particular compact); boundedness alone is not enough
the Fourier convention is exp(-i t lambda), which fixes the constant 2 pi
the estimate is uniform in psi given the density bound and in K given its Hilbert-Schmidt norm

Fix a vector u and consider the complex measure S -> <u, E(S) psi>. Cauchy-Schwarz applied to the spectral projections gives |<u, E(S) psi>| <= mu_u(S)^(1/2) mu_psi(S)^(1/2) for every Borel S, so this complex measure is absolutely continuous (mu_psi is) with density f_u satisfying |f_u(lambda)|^2 <= (d mu_u / d lambda)(lambda) times (d mu_psi / d lambda)(lambda) <= M (d mu_u / d lambda)(lambda) almost everywhere, where the singular part of mu_u contributes nothing because mu_psi is absolutely continuous. By the spectral theorem, <u, exp(-i t A) psi> is the Fourier transform of f_u, a function in L^1 and in L^2, so Plancherel's theorem gives the integral over t of |<u, exp(-i t A) psi>|^2 dt = 2 pi times the integral of |f_u(lambda)|^2 d lambda, which is at most 2 pi M times mu_u(R) = 2 pi M times the squared norm of u. Apply this with u = K* e_j, sum over j and interchange sum and integral by monotone convergence: the integral over R of the squared norm of K exp(-i t A) psi dt is at most 2 pi M times the sum over j of the squared norm of K* e_j, which is 2 pi M times the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm of K* , equal to that of K.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:49aa2fdb48667afb4f193c04e10bfaea0de19bb6ab7c7be02e33607436bee279","revision_digest":"sha256:5fbe9483d9083c1e18b3ec600c653d4f2d8f70dfbfef14f47a1428b1b63ecc4f","source_id":"wikipedia:Scattering_theory","source_revision":"as-read-2026-09-12","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Thm phase_transition_321 of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] For $\beta >0,$ we let
\[ f^{321}_\beta(x) := \frac12 + \frac1\beta \log\left( \frac{\textup{e}^{\beta x} + \textup{e}^{\beta/2}}{1 + \textup{e}^{\beta/2} + \textup{e}^{\beta} - \textup{e}^{\beta x}} \right) \,.\]
Then, the random permutations $\tau^{\beta,321}_{n}$ converge almost surely in the sense of permutons to the deterministic permuton
\[ \mu^{321}_\beta := \big( (X,f^{321}_\beta(X))_\# + (f^{321}_\beta(X),X)_\#  \big) \frac{\textup{d} x}{1+\exp\left(\beta(\frac12-x) \right)} 
\]
if $\beta>0$,
and to the diagonal permuton if $\beta\le 0.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition defn:closen of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Take $D>0$.
For any discrete blocks $(\vec p, \vec\upsilon, \mathcal H)$ of $(\hat{\mathfrak D}_{m}^{N_m})^{k_m} \cdots (\hat{\mathfrak D}_{1}^{N_1})^{k_1}$ which are valid in parity, and any blocks $(\vec \mathbf p, \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon},\mathbf H)$ (with times $\vec \mathbf k\in \mathbb R_+^m$, and $\mathbf Q_\ell=\sum_{\ell'=1}^\ell \mathbf k_{\ell'}$ for each $\ell \in \llbracket 0, m\rrbracket$),
they are \emph{$D$-close}, or simply \emph{close} if the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
    \item $u=\mathbf u$.
    \item For each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$, we have
$|k_\ell- \mathbf k_\ell N^{2/3}|<D$.
    \item For each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$, either $\upsilon_\ell=\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell=\varnothing$, or
$|\upsilon_\ell-\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell N^{2/3}|<D$ with $\upsilon_\ell\neq\varnothing$.
    \item For each $\ell \in \llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$ and $j\in \llbracket \ell, m+\mathbf u\rrbracket$, we have $\delta_{j,\ell}=\boldsymbol{\delta}_{j,\ell}$.
    Besides, if we denote the numbers in $\Delta_{j,\ell}$ and $\mathbf \Delta_{j,\ell}$ by $t_1<\cdots < t_{\delta_{j,\ell}}$ and $x_1<\cdots<x_{\delta_{j,\ell}}$ respectively, we have for each $i\in\llbracket 1, \delta_{j,\ell}\rrbracket$,
    \[
    |t_i - N^{2/3}x_i|,\quad |p^0(t_i)-N^{1/3}\mathbf p^0(x_i)|, \quad |\mathcal H(t_i) - N^{1/3}\mathbf H(x_i)| < D,
    \]
    and
\[
 (\mathbf p^0(x_i)-\mathbf p^0({x_i}-))(p^0(t_i)-p^0(t_i-1))>0,
\]
    and $p_j=0$ on $\llbracket Q_\ell, Q_m \rrbracket$ if and only if $\mathbf p_j=0$ on $[\mathbf Q_\ell,\mathbf Q_m]$.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Let $(X_N=I_p(f_N), N\geq 1)$, where $p\geq 2$ and $f_N\in H^{\odot p}$ 
	for each $N\geq 1$. Assume that $X_N$ satisfies \eqref{c1}. Consider a 
	$d$-dimensional random sequence $(\mathbb{Y}_N, N\geq 1)=((Y_{1,N},\ldots,
	Y_{d,N}), N\geq 1)$ such that for all $i=1,\ldots,d$,
	\begin{equation*}
		Y_{i,N} = \sum_{k=1}^\infty I_k(g_{k,N}^{(i)}), 
		\qquad g_{k,N}^{(i)}\in H^{\odot k} 
		\text{ for all } N,k\geq 1,\ i=1,\ldots,d.
	\end{equation*}
	Suppose that:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item There exists $\mathbb{Y}\in L^2(\Omega)$ such that 
		$\mathbb{Y}_N\to_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{Y}$ in $L^2(\Omega)$.
		\item For every $i=1,\ldots,d$, 
		$\mathbf{E}[X_NY_{i,N}]\to_{N\to\infty}\rho_i$.
		\item For every $i=1,\ldots,d$,
		\begin{equation}
			\sup_{N\geq 1}\sum_{k=M+1}^\infty k!\,
			\|g_{k,N}^{(i)}\|^2_{H^{\otimes k}} \to_{M\to\infty} 0.
		\end{equation}
	\end{enumerate}
	Then $(X_N,\mathbb{Y}_N)\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)}(Z,\mathbb{Y})$, 
	where $Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ and the characteristic function of 
	$(Z,\mathbb{Y})$ is given by \eqref{phi}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 9 of arXiv:2606.14812

body: A parametric family of distributions {f(x;theta): theta in Theta subset R^k}, given as densities or pmfs with respect to a common sigma-finite dominating measure, is an exponential family if it can be written in the form f(x;theta) = h(x) * exp( sum_{i=1}^k eta_i(theta) * T_i(x) - A(theta) ), where h(x) >= 0 does not depend on theta, T_1,...,T_k are real-valued statistics not depending on theta, eta_1,...,eta_k are real-valued functions of theta called the natural parameters, and A(theta) = log( integral h(x) * exp( sum_{i=1}^k eta_i(theta) T_i(x) ) dx ) is the log-normalizing function that makes f integrate to 1. When theta is taken directly as the natural parameter (eta_i(theta) = theta_i), the family is said to be in canonical form.
title: Exponential Family

body:
[Corollary 14 (Polynomial-size complements) of arXiv:2606.29530, 'Cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles with growing bl'] Fix an integer $r\ge2$ and a number $a>0$. Suppose
\[
       n-m_n\sim a n^{1-1/r},
        \qquad
        k_n=r.
\]
Then
\[
        E_r^{(m_n)}\Rightarrow \Poisson(a^r),
\]
and for every fixed $p\ge1$,
\[
        \normTV{(Q_{n,p}^{(m_n)})^{*r}-U_{n,p}}\to f_p(-r\log a),
\]
while
\[
        \sepd\!\left((Q_{n,p}^{(m_n)})^{*r},U_{n,p}\right)\to
        \begin{cases}
