[Proposition 14 (Endpoint-safe phase-bin package) of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] For every \(\xi\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}\), the following conclusions hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Partition of unity.  The functions above satisfy
\[
    \chi_{\xi,0}(t)
    +
    \chi_{\xi,1}(t)
    +
    \chi_{\xi,\mathrm{sd}}(t)
    +
    \sum_{d\in\mathfrak D_\xi}\chi_{\xi,d}(t)
    =
    1
    \qquad (0\le t\le1).
\]

\item Size of the safe region.  Let
\[
    E_\xi
    =
    \operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,0}
    \cup
    \operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,1}
    \cup
    \operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,\mathrm{sd}}.
\]
Then
\[
    |E_\xi|\le C_\gamma|\xi|^{-1/2}.
\]

\item Localization of each derivative band.  For each
\(d\in\mathfrak D_\xi\), set
\(
    S_{\xi,d}=\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,d}.
\)
Then
\[
    S_{\xi,d}
    \subset
    \left\{
        t\in[0,1]:
        C_\gamma^{-1}d
        \le
        h_\xi(t)^{1/2}
        \le
        C_\gamma d
    \right\}.
\]

\item Phase-derivative bounds on each band.  For each
\(d\in\mathfrak D_\xi\), one has
\[
    c_\gamma|\xi|d
    \le
    |\varphi_\xi'(t)|
    \le
    C_\gamma|\xi|d
    \qquad (t\in S_{\xi,d}).
\]

\item Range and number of active dyadic scales.  The active dyadic scales
satisfy
\[
    C_\gamma^{-1}|\xi|^{-1/2}\le d\le C_\gamma
    \qquad (d\in\mathfrak D_\xi),
\]
and
\[
    \#\mathfrak D_\xi
    \le
    C_\gamma(1+\log(2+|\xi|)).
\]

\item Thickening estimate for each band.  For every \(d\in\mathfrak D_\xi\)
and every integer \(\ell\ge0\),
\[
    \left|
    \left\{
        t\in[0,1]:
        \operatorname{dist}(t,S_{\xi,d})\le2^{-\ell}
    \right\}
    \right|
    \le
    C_\gamma(d+2^{-\ell}).
\]

\item Bounded-variation integration-by-parts estimate.  For every
\(d\in\mathfrak D_\xi\),
\[
    \int_0^1
    \frac{|\chi_{\xi,d}'(t)|}{|\varphi_\xi'(t)|}\,dt
    \le
    C_\gamma(|\xi|d)^{-1}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:riemann-backward-convergence of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Suppose Assumptions~(assump:data of the paper) and~(assump:uniform-graph of the paper) hold, and define $t_0$ as the largest index such that $\sigma_{t_0}\le \bar\sigma$. Assume that $\mathrm{dist}(x_{t_0},\mathcal{M})\le \frac{r}{2}$. Consider the backward denoising scheme with gradient guidance as in (equation eq:projected-gradient-guidance-relaxed of the paper)
with
$\eta
\le
\min\left\{
    \frac{1}{50L},
    \frac{r}{4G}
\right\},~
\epsilon
\le
\min\left\{
    \frac{1}{2},
    \frac{1}{512\eta(G\kappa+L)},
    \frac{r}{4C\sigma_{t_0}|\log\sigma_{t_0}|}
\right\}.$
Let $p_t:=\pi_\mathcal{M}(x_t)$ and $n_t:=x_t-p_t$. Define
\begin{align*}
\textstyle \Delta_{t_0}
:=
V(x_{t_0})-\min_{x\in\mathcal{M}}f(x)
+
\frac{6C^2\sigma_{t_0}^2}{\eta}
\left(
    |\log\sigma_{t_0}|^2
    +
    4|\log\sigma_{t_0}|
    +
    8
\right),
\end{align*}
where $V$ is defined in Lemma~(lemma:Lyapunov-descent-riemann of the paper) and $C$ is defined in Lemma~(lem:stein-projection-c2 of the paper). Then
\begin{align*}
  \textstyle  \sum_{t=1}^{t_0}
    \left(
        \frac{\epsilon\eta}{480}\|\mathrm{grad}_\mathcal{M} f(p_t)\|^2
        +
        \frac{\epsilon}{2000\eta}\|n_t\|^2
    \right)
    \le
    \Delta_{t_0}.
\end{align*}
Consequently,
\vspace{-15pt}
\begin{align*}
 \textstyle    \min_{1\le t\le t_0}
    \left(
        \frac{\epsilon\eta}{480}\|\mathrm{grad}_\mathcal{M} f(p_t)\|^2
        +
        \frac{\epsilon}{2000\eta}\|n_t\|^2
    \right)
    \le
    \frac{\Delta_{t_0}}{t_0}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:riemann-backward-convergence of arXiv:2608.29507

[Theorem thm.2d of arXiv:2609.01189, 'The lower mean curvature bound in Gromov's mean-of-the-mean-curvature conjecture'] Let $(X,g)$ be a compact connected Riemannian surface with boundary of length $L$.
Assume that
\[
  K_g\geq -c^2
\]
with a constant $c\ge0$.
Then
\begin{equation}
  \int_{\partial X} \kappa_g
  \leq
  \begin{cases}
    \sqrt{4\pi^2+c^2L^2},& \text{if $X$ is homeomorphic to a 2-disk,}\\
    cL,& \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def_Martingale_solution of arXiv:2604.07497, 'The Three-Dimensional Stochastic EMHD System: Local Well-Posedness and Maximal Pathwise So'] For $T > 0$, let $B_0 \in L^2(\Omega; H^s)$ be an ${\mathcal F}_0$-measurable $H^s$-valued random variable. We call a quadruple $\bigl(\widetilde{B}_0, \widetilde{B}, \widetilde{{\mathbb W}}, \widetilde{{\mathcal S}} \bigr)$ a martingale solution to the system (equation eq:EMHD_cutoff_Ito_1 of the paper)-(equation eq:EMHD_cutoff_Ito_3 of the paper) on $[0,T]$ if:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\widetilde{{\mathcal S}} = \bigl(\widetilde{\Omega}, \widetilde{{\mathcal F}}, \widetilde{{\mathbb F}}, \widetilde{{\mathbb P}} \bigr)$ is a stochastic basis such that $\widetilde{{\mathbb W}}$ is an $\widetilde{{\mathbb F}}$-adapted cylindrical Brownian motion with components $\{\widetilde{W}^k\}_{k \ge 1}$, \\
\item $\widetilde{B}_0 \in L^2(\widetilde{\Omega},H^s)$ has the same law as $B_0$, \\
\item $\widetilde{B}$ is a progressively measurable process such that 
\[
\widetilde{B} \in L^2\bigl(\widetilde{\Omega}; C([0,T];H^s)\bigr), \ \ \ \widetilde{{\mathbb P}}\text{-a.s.},
\]
and for every $t\in [0,T]$ the following identity holds: 
\begin{align*}
&\Ltwoinner{\widetilde{B}(t),\phi} + \int_0^t \Ltwoinner{\chi^2_r \nabla \times \bigl( (\nabla \times \widetilde{B} ) \times \widetilde{B} \bigr) + \varLambda^\alpha \widetilde{B}, \phi} ds \\
=\ &\Ltwoinner{\widetilde{B}(0),\phi} + {\frac{1}{2}} \sum_{k=1}^\infty \int_0^t \Ltwoinner{{\mathcal T}^2_k \widetilde{B},\phi} ds + \sum_{k=1}^\infty \int_0^t \Ltwoinner{{\mathcal T}_k \widetilde{B}, \phi} d\widetilde{W}^k_s ,
\end{align*}
for all $\phi \in H$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Martingale solution

[Definition 3 (Exponential tightness) of arXiv:2607.12666, 'Sample-path Large deviations for \\Scheduled Arrival Processes with Unpunctuality'] A sequence of random elements $\{X^{(n)}\}$ in $D([0,T])$ is said to be exponentially tight with speed $n$ if for every $M<\infty$, there exists a compact set $K_M \subset D([0,T])$ such that
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \Pbb(X^{(n)} \notin K_M)
\le -M.
\]

[Theorem 164 of arXiv:2605.03236, 'Stochastic It\^o Equations and Parabolic Second-Order Equations with singular Drift'] Suppose that for each $n=1,2,...$ we are given
bounded continuous $\bS_{\delta}$-valued $a^{(n)}(t,x)$
and $\bR^{d}$-valued $b^{(n)}(t,x)$,
which satisfy the assumptions of
Theorem \ref{theorem 11.29,1}
(with fixed $\beta,p,q,\rho_{a},\rho_{b}$).
Then, as we know from Theorem \ref{theorem 12.6.02}
and Remark \ref{remark 11.28,1}, for each $n$
there exists a strong Markov, strong Feller, 
 regular
diffusion process $X^{(n)}$ corresponding to
  $a(n),b(n)$, for which
estimate \eqref{11.22,4} holds
and its finite-dimensional distributions
are completely determined by $a(n),b(n)$ (Theorem 
\ref{theorem 12.12.3}). For $s\geq t$ introduce
$$
T^{n}_{t,s}f(x)=E^{(n)}_{t,x}f(x_{s-t}).
$$
Suppose that $a^{(n)}\to a$ (a.s.)
and $b^{(n)}\to b$ in $L_{p_{0}}(C)$
for any   $C\in\bC$.  

Then  
for any $f\in \EO_{p,\beta}$, $s\in\bR$,  and $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ we have  
\begin{equation}
                        
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{t\in(s-\varepsilon^{-1},s-\varepsilon)}\sup_{\bR^{d}} |T^{(n)}_{t,s}f-T _{t,s}f
|(x)
=0,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
                        
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{t\in(s-\varepsilon^{-1},
s-\varepsilon)}\|DT^{(n)}_{t,s}f-DT _{t,s}f
\|_{E _{p,\beta}(\bR^{d}) }=0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
E_N(s)=\mathbb{E}_s\!\big[\min(T,\omega_N)\big].

E(s)-E_N(s)

body:
[Definition def:restrictedtraceoperators of arXiv:2609.03980, 'Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant H'] Let $\Gamma$ be a relatively open subset of the boundary $\partial \Omega$ of some bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$.
 
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item  The restriction of ${\operatorname{tr}}(f)$ to $\Gamma$ for $f\in H^1(\Omega)$ induces the restricted trace operator 
    $${\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}:H^1(\Omega)\to H^{1/2}(\Gamma), f\mapsto {\operatorname{tr}}(f)|_{\Gamma},$$
    which is again bounded and surjective, see e.g.  Proposition 1.2.60 in [Meinlschmidt].
    \item We define the Lions-Magenes space $H^{1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)$ as the subspace of functions $f\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$, for which the extension by zero $\Tilde{f}$ to $\partial\Omega$ is again an element of $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$. If $n=1$, one clearly has $H^{1/2}_{0}(\Gamma) = H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. If $n\geq 2$, then $H^{1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)$ is an intrinsic, i.e., independent of $\partial\Omega$, Hilbert space when equipped with the norm
    \begin{align*}
        \|f\|_{H^{1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)}  \coloneq  \left(\|f\|_{H^{1/2}(\Gamma)} +\int_\Gamma  \frac{|u(x)|^2}{\dist(x,\partial \Gamma)} \;\mathrm{d} x\right)^{1/2},
    \end{align*} see e.g.\ Chapter~33 in [tartar2007introduction].
    This norm is equivalent to the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$-norm of the zero extension $\Tilde{f}$.
    Additionally, denote by $H^{-1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)$ the dual space of $H^{1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)$.
    \item We define the restricted normal trace operator
    $${\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}_N:H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\to H^{-1/2}_{0}(\Gamma), f\mapsto \left( H^{1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)\to \mathbb{C}, g\mapsto
    \duality{{\operatorname{tr}}_N(f)}{\Tilde{g}}\right),$$ where 
    $\Tilde{g}$ denotes the extension by zero to $\partial\Omega$ of an element $g\in H^{1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)$.
    
    The restricted normal trace operator ${\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}_N:H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\to H^{-1/2}_{0}(\Gamma)$ is well-defined, bounded and surjective, see Lemma~(lem:normaltracesurj of the paper).
    \end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:restrictedtraceoperators of arXiv:2609.03980

body:
[Lemma lem:first-exit of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $V\subset\mathbb R^m$ be bounded and open, and suppose that
$w\in C(\overline V)$ has a unique minimum point
$\mathbf p_*\in V$ on $\overline V$.  Let
$d:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, and let $S$ be a set-valued
map from $\mathbb R$ to $\mathbb R^m$ with nonempty compact values.  Fix
$\delta>0$.  Then there exist $\eta_*,r_*>0$, depending only on $V,w,\delta$,
with the following property.

Assume that $S$ is upper semicontinuous\footnote{As in
(lem:centers of the paper)(vi), this means that, for every $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and every open
set $O\subset\mathbb R^m$ with $S(t_0)\subset O$, there exists $\sigma>0$ such that
$S(t)\subset O$ whenever $|t-t_0|<\sigma$.} and that
\[
  \operatorname{diam}S(t)\leq r_*
  \quad\text{whenever }d(t)\leq\delta,
\]
and that
\begin{equation}
  d(t)+\sup_{\mathbf b\in S(t)}[w(\mathbf b)-w(\mathbf p_*)]
  \leq\eta_*
\end{equation}
whenever $S(t)\subset\overline V$ and $d(t)\leq\delta$.
Then $S(0)\subset V$ and $d(0)<\delta$ imply that
$S(t)\subset V$ and $d(t)<\delta$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.

[Definition def.weaksolNINCN of arXiv:2605.11785, 'Regularization of a mean-field SDE by an additive common noise: the conditional expectatio'] A weak solution to (equation eq.barXsigma=0BISCN of the paper) consists of a tuple $(\Omega, (\mathcal F_t), \mathbb{F},{\mathbb P}, W, W^0,X^0,X)$, where  $(\Omega, (\mathcal F_t), \mathbb{F},{\mathbb P})$ is a filtered probability space with a complete filtration supporting $(W, W^0,X^0,X)$, such that  
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] Under ${\mathbb P}$, $W$ and $W^0$ are independent $d-$dimensional $(\mathcal F_t)-$Brownian motions,  the processes $X$ and $X^0$ are $(\mathcal F_t)-$adapted with values in $\mathbb{R}^d$, with $X_0$ distributed according to $\mu_0$, 

\item[(ii)] $X_0$, $W$ and $(W^0, X^0)$ are independent, 

\item[(iii)] The state equation holds: 
$$
 X_t = X_0+ \int_0^t b(X_s, X^0_s) ds + \sigma W_t+\sigma^0 W^0_t.
 $$

\item[(iv)]  $W^0$ is adapted to the filtration generated by $X^0$, and  $X^0_t= \mathbb{E}\left[X_t\ |\ X^0\right]$ for any $t\in [0,T]$. 
\end{itemize}

[Proposition prop:rate of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Under the hypotheses of Proposition~(prop:opmatch of the paper), and assuming in addition that
$b,f$ are bounded with bounded derivatives, there is $C=C(T,b,f)$ such that for every
$t\in[0,T]$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{E}\big[W_{2}(L_{N}(t),\mu_{t})\big]\le C\,N^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
where $L_{N}(t)$ is the empirical spectral distribution of (equation eq:opmatrix of the paper).
Consequently, if the reverse-time dynamics of \S(sec:tweedie of the paper) are simulated at
dimension $N$ by an Euler--Maruyama scheme with $n$ steps on the eigenvalue system
(equation eq:opeigen of the paper), using a score $\widehat\xi$ satisfying
$\sup_{t}\mathbb{E}[\mathcal S_{t}(\theta)]\le\epsilon^{2}$ (Corollary~(cor:stein of the paper)), the
generated law $\widehat L_{N,n}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{E}\big[W_{2}(\widehat L_{N,n},\mu_{0})\big]
  \le C_{1}N^{-1/2}+C_{2}n^{-1/2}+C_{3}\,\epsilon,
\end{equation}
with $C_{1},C_{2},C_{3}$ depending on $T,\beta,b,f$ but not on $N,n,\epsilon$.

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2606.10313, '\textbf{Invariance principles for additive functionals of voter models}'] (Holley and Liggett, 1975). Let $p\in (0, 1)$. When $\eta_0$ is distributed with $\mu_p$, as $t\rightarrow +\infty$, $\eta_t$ converges weakly to an invariant distribution $\nu_p$ which satisfies that
\[
\mathbb{E}_{\nu_p}\eta_0(x)=p
\]
and
\[
\mathbb{E}_{\nu_p}\left(\eta_0(x)\eta_0(y)\right)=p\tilde{\mathbb{P}}\left(\tau_{x, y}<+\infty\right)+p^2\tilde{\mathbb{P}}\left(\tau_{x, y}=+\infty\right)
\]
for any $x, y\in G$, where
\[
\tau_{x, y}=\inf\{t\geq 0:~X_t^{x}=\hat{X}_t^y\}
\]
and $\{X_t^x\}_{t\geq 0}, \{\hat{X}_t^y\}_{t\geq 0}$ are independent copies of the random walk $X_t$ defined as in Section \ref{section one} with $X_0^x=x, \hat{X}_0^y=y$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 1 of arXiv:2606.10313

body:
[Lem 56 of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Let $d\ge 2$.
Suppose that $F:\mathbb [0,\infty)\to [0,\infty)$ 
    is a decreasing function of exponential decay at infinity. 
    Let $K > 0$. Then there exists some $\epsilon>0$ and a constant $C = C(K, F) >0$ such that uniformly over $|\varsigma|<\epsilon$, $   a_1,   a_2\in I$, and all $0 = r_0 < r_1 \leq \cdots \leq r_m$, we have  \begin{align*}
    \mathbf E^{(\varsigma,2)}_{(   a_1,   a_2)} \bigg[ \prod_{j=1}^{m} F(|   R^1_{r_j}-   R^2_{r_j}|)\bigg] \leq C \left( 1+ r_1^{-1/2} |   a_1 -    a_2|\right)^{-K} \prod_{j=1}^{m} 1 \wedge (r_j - r_{j-1})^{-d/2}. 
\end{align*}
In particular, for fixed $r\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ we have that \begin{equation}\sum_{1\le s_1\le ...\le s_{m-1} \le r}\mathbf E^{(\varsigma,2)}_{(   a_1,   a_2)} \bigg[ F(|R^1_r -R^2_r|) \prod_{j=1}^{m} F(|   R^1_{r_j}-   R^2_{r_j}|)\bigg] \leq \frac{C^m}{\omega_r(d)^{m-1} } r^{-d/2} (1+r^{-1/2} |   a_1-   a_2| \big)^{-K} .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 56 of arXiv:2510.22155

[Theorem Theo2 of arXiv:2507.07923, 'Optimal Sets and Quantization Errors under Geometric Constraints for Discrete Distribution'] Let $\gamma_n$ be a constrained optimal set of $n$-points for any $n\in \mathbb{N}$ with $n$th constrained quantization error $Q_n^{(c)}$. Then,
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item $\gamma_1=\Big\{(\frac{2-c m}{m^2+1},\frac{c+2 m}{m^2+1})\Big\} \text{ with } Q_1^{(c)}=\frac{c^2+4 c m+6 m^2+2}{m^2+1}$.
 \item $\gamma_2=\Big\{(\frac{4-3 c m}{3 m^2+3},\frac{c+\frac{4 m}{3}}{m^2+1}),  (\frac{4-c m}{m^2+1},\frac{c+4 m}{m^2+1})\Big\} \text{ with } Q_2^{(c)}=\frac{3 c^2+12 c m+18 m^2+2}{3 m^2+3}$.
     \item $\gamma_3=\Big\{(\frac{1-c m}{m^2+1},\frac{c+m}{m^2+1}),(\frac{7-3 c m}{3 m^2+3},\frac{c+\frac{7 m}{3}}{m^2+1}),(\frac{5-c m}{m^2+1},\frac{c+5 m}{m^2+1})\Big\} \\
         \text{ or }  \Big\{ (\frac{4-3 c m}{3 m^2+3},\frac{c+\frac{4 m}{3}}{m^2+1}),(\frac{10-3 c m}{3 m^2+3},\frac{c+\frac{10 m}{3}}{m^2+1}),(\frac{6-c m}{m^2+1},\frac{c+6 m}{m^2+1})\Big\} \text{ with } Q_3^{(c)}=\frac{3 c^2+12 c m+18 m^2+1}{3 m^2+3}$.

\item For $n\geq 4$, \\
$\gamma_n=\Big\{(\frac{j-c m}{m^2+1},\frac{c+j m}{m^2+1}) : 1\leq j\leq n-2\Big\}\bigcup \Big\{(-\frac{3 c m-3 n+2}{3 m^2+3},\frac{3 c+3 m n-2 m}{3 m^2+3})\Big\}
\bigcup\Big\{(\frac{-c m+n+2}{m^2+1},\frac{c+m (n+2)}{m^2+1})\Big\} \\
\quad \text{ or }\\
\gamma_n=\Big\{(\frac{j-c m}{m^2+1},\frac{c+j m}{m^2+1}) : 1\leq j\leq n-3\Big\}\bigcup \Big\{(-\frac{3 c m-3 n+5}{3 m^2+3},\frac{3 c+3 m n-5 m}{3 m^2+3})\Big\}\bigcup\Big\{(\frac{-3 c m+3 n+1}{3 m^2+3},\frac{3 c+3 m n+m}{3 m^2+3})\Big\}\\
\hspace{ 1 in} \bigcup \Big\{(\frac{-c m+n+3}{m^2+1},\frac{c+m (n+3)}{m^2+1})\Big\} \\
\text{ with } Q_n^{(c)}=\frac{3 c^2+12 c m+18 m^2+2^{3-n}}{3 m^2+3}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:location_of_max of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] For $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, consider the function $F_{c,\theta}:[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by 
    \[
    F_{c,\theta}(\xi) = \theta \xi + \rho_{c}(1- \xi),
    \]
    where $ \rho_{c}$ is the function defined in (equation eq:mu_k_def of the paper). Then, the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
\item  If $c \le 1$ or $\theta \neq \frac{qc}{1-qc}$, then $F_{c,\theta}$ has a unique maximizer at $\xi = 1 - X_c(\theta)$.
\item  If $c > 1$ and $\theta = \frac{qc}{1-qc}$, then $\xi$ is a maximizer of $F_{c,\theta}$ if and only if $
\xi \in [0,1 - X_c(\theta)]$.
In particular, $F_{c,\theta}$ is constant on the interval $[0,1 - X_c(\theta)]$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:location_of_max of arXiv:2605.22787

[Lem convergence of coding functions and pointset for ER of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{[Berry_Broutin_Goldschmidt_12_The_continuum]}] 
  Assume that a sequence $(m_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ satisfies $n^{-2/3} m_{n} \to \sigma \in (0,\infty)$.
  Let $\mathcal{Q}^{p_{n}}$ be a binomial pointset of intensity $p_{n}$, independent of $\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}$,
  and define $\mathcal{P}_{n} \coloneqq  \{ ( (\sigma/m_{n}) i, (\sigma/m_{n})^{1/2} j ) \mid (i,j) \in \mathcal{Q}^{p_{n}} \}$.
  Then, it holds that
  \begin{align}
     & \left(
    \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{m_{n}}} H_{\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}} \left( \left\lfloor \frac{m_{n}}{\sigma} \cdot \right\rfloor \right),
    \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{m_{n}}} X_{\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}} \left( \left\lfloor \frac{m_{n}}{\sigma} \cdot \right\rfloor \right),
    \mathcal{P}_{n} \cap \left( \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{m_{n}}} X_{\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}} \left( \left\lfloor \frac{m_{n}}{\sigma} \cdot \right\rfloor \right) \right)
    \right) \notag                            \\
     & \xrightarrow[n \to \infty]{\mathrm{d}}
    (2 \tilde{e}^{(\sigma)}, \tilde{e}^{(\sigma)}, \mathcal{P} \cap \tilde{e}^{(\sigma)}),
    
  \end{align}
  where the convergence of the first and second coordinate takes place in $D([0,\sigma], \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})$

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let h be a (discrete or continuum) Gaussian free field on a domain D with Dirichlet boundary conditions, and let U be a deterministic subdomain of D. The Gibbs-Markov (domain Markov) property states that h decomposes as h = h_U + phi_U, where h_U is a zero-boundary Gaussian free field on U, phi_U is the harmonic extension into U of the values of h on the boundary of U, h_U and phi_U are independent of each other, and phi_U is measurable with respect to the sigma-field generated by h restricted to the complement of U. This is the discrete and continuum analogue of the strong Markov property for Brownian motion and harmonic functions, and it is the fundamental tool enabling induction-on-scale arguments, the theory of local sets, and the construction of conformally invariant objects such as Liouville quantum gravity from the field. It does not hold for general non-Gibbsian or non-Gaussian log-correlated fields without separate verification, and it requires exact specification of the domain and boundary conditions, since the decomposition depends on the harmonic extension operator for the particular pair (D,U) being used. Typical failure: Applying the plain Gibbs-Markov decomposition with U chosen depending on the field h itself, such as a random subdomain determined by a level set or an exploration process, without checking that U is a valid stopping domain for the field's filtration; naively random domains destroy the independence between h_U and phi_U, and the correct fix requires the more delicate theory of local sets developed by Schramm and Sheffield, not the plain domain Markov property. Canonical reference: Sheffield, 2007, Probability Theory and Related Fields; Schramm and Sheffield, 2013, Probability Theory and Related Fields.
h is a Gaussian free field with Dirichlet (or otherwise precisely specified) boundary conditions on domain D
U is a deterministic, or at least suitably measurable stopping-domain, subdomain of D
the Green's function and harmonic measure for D and U are well defined, requiring sufficient domain regularity
correct identification of phi_U as harmonic in U with boundary values equal to h on the boundary of U
title: Technique: Gibbs-Markov Property of the Gaussian Free Field

An absence theorem restricted to bigeodesic tails in deterministic thin horizontal or vertical tubes requires a further confinement theorem, or an obstruction for wider and adaptive wandering, before it can establish unrestricted absence. Countable intersections over fixed finite widths do not cover a path whose transverse displacement is unbounded. A directional limit permits unbounded sublinear transverse displacement. The separate compactness route, taking limits of geodesics between opposite distant endpoints, likewise needs anchoring near a bounded region; endpoints on opposite sides alone allow the connecting paths to escape every fixed ball. These are missing bridge premises, not refutations of absence for nonatomic iid planar FPP.

[Corollary cor:almost-sure of arXiv:2608.07410, 'Extreme least singular values of random row submatrices\\ with bounded-density subgaussian'] Let $(\xi_{ij})_{i,j\ge1}$ be an infinite array of independent copies of $\xi$. For $\gamma>1$, set
\[
\begin{aligned}
N_m(\gamma)&:=\lceil\gamma m\rceil-1,\\
A_m(\gamma)&:=(\xi_{ij})_{1\le i\le N_m(\gamma),\,1\le j\le m},\\
\mathcal M_m(\gamma)&:=M_m(A_m(\gamma)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Then, for every compact interval $K\subset(1,\infty)$,
\[
\sup_{\gamma\in K}
\left|\frac1m\log\mathcal M_m(\gamma)+h(\gamma)\right|
\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]
In particular, the exponential law holds simultaneously for every $\gamma>1$ on one
full-probability event.

At the critical real phase-retrieval threshold, $A_m(2)\in\mathbb R^{(2m-1)\times m}$. If
$R_m:=\max_{1\le i\le2m-1}\|(\xi_{ij})_{j=1}^m\|_2$, then almost surely
\[
\omega(A_m(2))^{1/m}\longrightarrow\frac14,
\qquad
R_m^{1/m}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Consequently, for every $b>1/4$, the inequality $\omega(A_m(2))\le R_m b^m$ holds for all
sufficiently large $m$ almost surely; for every $0<b<1/4$ and every fixed $C>0$, the reverse
inequality $\omega(A_m(2))>C R_m b^m$ holds for all sufficiently large $m$ almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 51 (Finite-order uniform form of the chain density estimate) of arXiv:2607.20882, 'An Eyring--Kramers Law for the Hypoelliptic Third-Order\\ Langevin Diffusion'] Fix the chain length $n=3$, the block dimension $d$, and $T<\infty$.
Fix also $p>2$ and an inverse-moment order $q<\infty$.  There is an integer
$N=N(d,p,q)$ with the following property.  Consider a family of smooth
third-order chain diffusions in the block order
$X^1,X^2,X^3$, centered at the deterministic trajectory as in
\cite[(D2)]{Pigato2022}.  Suppose uniformly over the family that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.6em]
\item the initial points and initial drift values are bounded;
\item the weak H\"ormander matrix in hypothesis \textup{(H1)} of
\cite{Pigato2022} has smallest singular value at least $\lambda_0>0$;
\item all positive-order spatial derivatives of orders $1,\ldots,N$, together
with their first time derivatives, are bounded on
$[0,T]\times\R^{3d}$;
\item the diffusion coefficient is bounded together with the derivatives
through the same order.
\end{enumerate}
Let
\[
\mathsf T_t
:=\operatorname{diag}\left(t^{1/2}I_d,t^{3/2}I_d,t^{5/2}I_d\right)
\]
and let $\Gamma_t^{\rm sc}$ be the Malliavin covariance of the centered,
scaled variable $\mathsf T_t^{-1}(X_t-\vartheta_t)$, where
$\vartheta_t$ is the deterministic trajectory from \cite[(D2)]{Pigato2022}.
Then
\begin{equation}

\sup_{0<t\le T}\E\!\left[
\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_t^{\rm sc})^{-q}\right]\le C_q,
\end{equation}
where, for a symmetric non-negative matrix $M$,
$\lambda_{\min}(M):=\inf_{|v|=1}v^\top Mv$
denotes its smallest eigenvalue.
For the same statement, after taking $N$ to be the maximum of the finitely
many orders used in the two conclusions, the transition density
$q(t,\xi,y)$
satisfies
\begin{equation}

q(t,\xi,y)
\le
\frac{C_p t^{-9d/2}}
{1+|\mathsf T_t^{-1}(y-\vartheta_t)|^p},
\qquad 0<t\le T,\quad y\in\R^{3d}.
\end{equation}
The constants depend only on
$d,T,p,q,\lambda_0$ and the finitely many coefficient bounds above.

[Lemma LEM:BD of arXiv:2512.23957, 'Concentration and fluctuations of sine-Gordon measure around topological multi-soliton man'] Let $Q\in \mathbb{Z}$ and let $\varepsilon>0$. Suppose that  $F$ is a measurable real-valued functional such that
$\mathbb{E}\big[|F(Y(1))|^p\big] < \infty$ and $\mathbb{E}\big[|e^{-F(Y(1))}|^q \big] < \infty$ for some $1 < p, q < \infty$ with $\frac 1p + \frac 1q = 1$.
Then, we have
\begin{align*}
-\log \mathbb{E}_{\mu^Q_\varepsilon}\Big[ e^{-F(\phi)}   \Big]=\inf_{\theta \in \mathbb{H}_a}  \mathbb{E}\bigg[ F\big(
\ell^Q +  \sqrt{\varepsilon}Y(1)
+\sqrt{\varepsilon}\Theta(1) \big)  +\frac 12 \int_0^1 \| \theta(t) \|_{L^2_x}^2 dt  \bigg], 
\end{align*}

\noindent
where  $\ell^Q(x)=\frac{\pi Q}{L_\varepsilon}(x+L_\varepsilon)$ is the line connecting $0$ and $2\pi Q$ in (equation BB1 of the paper), and
\begin{align}
\Theta(t):=\int_0^t (-\partial_x^2)^{-\frac 12} \theta(s) ds.

\end{align}

\noindent 
Here the expectation $\mathbb{E} = \mathbb{E}_\mathbb{P}$ is an  expectation with respect to the underlying probability measure~$\mathbb{P}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop up-to-constants_volume-tail of arXiv:2508.18807, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation I: High effective dimension}'] Suppose that $\mathbb E_{\beta_c,r}|K| \asymp r^\alpha$ as $r\to \infty$ and let $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be an increasing function whose inverse $f^{-1}$ is doubling.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item If there exist positive constants $c$ and $C$ such that $\hat \mathbb P_{\beta_c,r}(cf(r) \leq |K| \leq Cf(r))\geq c$ for every $r\geq 1$ then
  \[
\mathbb P_{\beta_c}(|K|\geq n) \succeq \frac{f^{-1}(n)^\alpha}{n}
  \]
  for every $n\geq 1$.
  \item If for each $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that $\hat \mathbb P_{\beta_c,r}(|K| \leq \delta f(r)) \leq \varepsilon$ for every $r\geq 1$ then
  \[
\mathbb P_{\beta_c}(|K|\geq n) \preceq  \frac{f^{-1}(n)^\alpha}{n}
\]
for every $n\geq 1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm2_3 of arXiv:2607.26169, 'Scaling and partial universality of the height zero probability in the 2D Abelian sandpile'] Let $U\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded connected region satisfying Assumption (a:U of the paper)(i). Let \(g : W\rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) be a $C^1$ function on an open set \(W\) containing \(\partial U_\epsilon\) for all \(\epsilon > 0\) sufficiently small. Let \(u : U \cup \partial U \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) denote the solution to the Laplace equation on \(U\) with Dirichlet boundary condition \(g\). For \(\epsilon > 0\) such that \(\partial U_\epsilon \subset W\), let \(u_\epsilon : U_\epsilon \cup \partial U_\epsilon \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) denote the solution to the discrete Laplace equation on \(U_\epsilon\) with Dirichlet boundary condition \(u_\epsilon = g\) on \(\partial U_\epsilon\). \\
    (i) The family of functions \((u_\epsilon)\) satisfy
    \[
        u_\epsilon = u + \mathcal{O}(\varepsilon) \; \text{ as } \epsilon \downarrow 0,
    \]
    where the error term is locally uniform. Moreover, the error term is also uniform 
    in $U$, as long as $|g|$ remains under a fixed bound, and the distance from 
    $\partial U$ is bounded away from $0$.\\
    (ii) Furthermore, for \(z \in U\) and \(e \in \varepsilon \mathcal{E}\) an edge incident 
    with $z_\varepsilon$, we have 
    \[
        \partial_e u_\epsilon(z_\epsilon) 
        = u_\epsilon(z_\epsilon + e)-u_\epsilon(z_\epsilon)
        = \varepsilon \tilde{e} \cdot \nabla u (x) + O(\varepsilon^2), \; \text{as } \epsilon \downarrow 0,
    \]
    where $\tilde{e} = e/\varepsilon$ is the corresponding vector in $\mathcal{E}$. 
    The error term satisfies the same uniformity statement as in part (i). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition thm:localgoodforball of arXiv:2509.21253, '\bf Capacity in high dimensional percolation'] For all $K$ sufficiently large, there exists a constant $\alpha(K)>0$, so that for all $  1\le M \le Kr^{d-1}$, and all $ r\leq \|z\|/2$, we have 
		\[
		\pr{X_r\ge  M, X_r^{K-\textrm{line-good}}\leq \alpha(K) \cdot X_r}\leq \tau(z) \cdot r^{2d-2}\cdot \exp(-\alpha(K)\cdot (\log M)^4).
		\]

body:
Let (X, Y, Z) be jointly Gaussian in R^a x R^b x R^c with covariance blocks A = Cov(X), C = Cov(Y), G = Cov(Z), B = Cov(X, Y), E = Cov(X, Z), F = Cov(Y, Z), possibly singular, and put A_c = A - E G^+ E^T, C_c = C - F G^+ F^T, B_c = B - E G^+ F^T and K = [[A_c, B_c], [B_c^T, C_c]]. Let rho_1, rho_2, ... be the singular values of R_c = A_c^(+1/2) B_c C_c^(+1/2), where A_c^(+1/2) is the Moore-Penrose inverse of the positive semidefinite square root (the partial canonical correlations). Then every rho_j <= 1; I(X; Y | Z) is finite exactly when every rho_j < 1; and then I(X; Y | Z) = -(1/2) sum_j log(1 - rho_j^2).
(X, Y, Z) is jointly Gaussian

[Lem lemma:left-convergence-locally-tree-like of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Let $G_N=(\text{\boldmath $A$}_N,\text{\boldmath $h$}_N)$ be a sequence of weighted $k$-regular graphs
which converge locally to the $k$-regular tree. Let the edge weights
$(A_{ij}:\{i,j\}\in E(G_N))$ be i.i.d. random variables with common
distribution $Q_A$, and independent of the vertex weights $(h_{i}:i\in
[N])$ which are i.i.d. random variables with common distribution
$Q_h$. Assume that $Q_A,Q_h$ are independent of $N$ and have bounded
support. For a constant $c\in\text{\boldmath $R$}$, define
$G_N(c)=(\text{\boldmath $A$}_N(c),\text{\boldmath $h$}_N(c))$, where
$\text{\boldmath $A$}(c)=\text{\boldmath $A$}_N-c{\boldsymbol 1}{\boldsymbol 1}^{{\sf T}}/N$, $\text{\boldmath $h$}_N(c)=\text{\boldmath $h$}_N$.

Then, the sequence $(G_N(c): N\ge 1)$ is almost surely
left-convergent.

body:
[Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] A \emph{first-order differential calculus} (FODC) \((\Omega^1_A,d)\) on \(A\) consists of an \(A\)\nobreakdash–\(A\)-bimodule \(\Omega_A^1\) together with a \(\Bbbk\)-linear \emph{exterior derivative}
\( d\colon A \rightarrow \Omega^1_A\), satisfying the \emph{Leibniz rule}
\[d(fg)=(df)g + f(dg),
\quad \forall f,g\in A,\] and the \emph{surjectivity condition}, which states that \(\Omega_A^1\) is spanned by elements of the form \( f dg\), for \(f,g\in A\). A \emph{morphism of first-order differential calculi}
\((A, \Omega^1_A,d_A)
\rightarrow
(B, \Omega^1_B,d_B)\)
is given by an algebra morphism \(\varphi\colon A\rightarrow B\) together with an \(A\)\nobreakdash–\(A\)-bimodule map \( \varphi^* : \Omega^1_A \rightarrow\Omega^1_B\)
such that \(\varphi^* \circ d_A= d_B \circ \varphi.\) Here \(\Omega^1_B\) is seen as an \(A\)\nobreakdash–\(A\)-bimodule via \(\varphi\). Additionally, a FODC \(\Omega^1_A\) is called \emph{inner} if there exists an element \(\theta\in\Omega^1_A\) such that
\(d a  =  [\theta,a] = \theta a - a\theta, 
\text{ for any }a \in A\). It is called \emph{connected} if
\(\ker(d) = \Bbbk\cdot 1_A\).
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.26953

For separately bias-corrected scalar Adam beta1=.9,beta2=.999 with epsilon outside sqrt, standard m0=v0=0 and eta*lambda/epsilon=38, every initialization with 0<|x0|<=10^(-57)*eta has nonzero sign-alternating positions, converges to its origin, and has x_(t+1)/x_t tending to -1 rather than -.9. The invariant normalized raw-momentum cone is 0<=-m_t/(lambda*x_t)<=2/37. In particular this is an open standard-start interval at epsilon=eta,lambda=38 for every eta>0. The sufficient radius is extremely small; no generic root selection outside it is asserted.

Kind:special; target2. Status: proof (unaudited). No literature priority
or new frontier score claimed. This answers the reviewer's open-set
root-selection subquestion on an explicitly tiny interval.

STATEMENT. Let eta,epsilon,lambda>0 satisfy eta*lambda/epsilon=38.
Run separately bias-corrected scalar Adam with b=9/10,d=999/1000,
epsilon outside sqrt, and m_0=v_0=0. If
             0<|x_0|<=10^(-57)*eta,
then every position is nonzero, signs alternate from time0, x_t->0,
and x_(t+1)/x_t ->-1. The alternative limit -b=-.9 does not occur on
this interval. In particular this holds for epsilon=eta,lambda=38,
for every eta>0. This is not a generic-root or global-basin theorem.
The constant is a sufficient tiny radius, not a practical-scale basin.

NORMALIZATION AND EXACT IDENTITIES. Set X=x/eta,M=m/(eta*lambda),
V=v/(eta*lambda)^2,rho=epsilon/(eta*lambda)=1/38, ell=1-b=1/10.
With U_(t+1)=sqrt(V_(t+1)/(1-d^(t+1))), define
 a_t=38/[(1-b^(t+1))*(1+U_(t+1)/rho)].
Then V_(t+1)=d*V_t+(1-d)*X_t^2, M_(t+1)=b*M_t+ell*X_t,
X_(t+1)=X_t-a_t*M_(t+1). By odd symmetry assume X_0>0.
Whenever X_t!=0 put z_t=-M_t/X_t and N(z)=ell-b*z. Then
 H_t=a_t*N(z_t)-1,
 X_(t+1)=-H_t*X_t, z_(t+1)=N(z_t)/H_t.              (1)
Put Z_t=X_t+18*M_t and W_t=(-1)^t*Z_t. Direct substitution gives
 Z_(t+1)+Z_t=(38-a_t)*M_(t+1).                       (2)
These are exact actual corrected updates, not frozen-preconditioner steps.

1. A FORWARD-INVARIANT MOMENTUM CONE WHEN VARIANCE IS SMALL
Set Q=2/37, a_min=1443/38, h=1/54834. Exact arithmetic gives
 N(Q)=19/370, a_min=1/Q+1/N(Q),
 a_min*N(Q)-1=19/20, 1-18*Q=1/37.
For0<=z<=Q and a>=a_min, H=a*N(z)-1>=19/20>0.
The map f(z)=N(z)/(a*N(z)-1) has derivative b/(a*N(z)-1)^2>0
and decreases in a. Its maximum is f(Q) at a=a_min, equal to Q.
Thus0<f(z)<=Q: signs flip, the next position is nonzero, and the
cone0<=z<=Q is preserved whenever a>=a_min.

Inside this cone Z_t/X_t=1-18*z_t is between1/37 and1, so W_t>0
when signs have alternated and X_0>0. Also
 R(z)=N(z)/(1-18*z), R'(z)=(18*ell-b)/(1-18*z)^2>0,
             ell<=R(z)<=19/10.                    (3)
Equation(2) now reads
 W_(t+1)=W_t*[1-(38-a_t)*R(z_t)].                    (4)
The bracket is positive by cone preservation; no sign of38-a_t is assumed.

2. FINITE BIAS-CLOCK AMPLIFICATION, WITH A CERTIFIED INFINITE TAIL
For actual Adam, a_t<=38/(1-b^(t+1)). Equations(3),(4) therefore give
 W_(t+1)<=W_t*[1+c*b^(t+1)/(1-b^(t+1))], c=361/5.
Define P_T=product_(n=1)^T[1+c*b^n/(1-b^n)]. The exact certificate
scripts/check_critical_momentum_cone.py verifies P_100<10^50 and
 S=c*b^101/[(1-b)*(1-b^101)]<1.
For n>=101,1-b^n>=1-b^101, so the sum of the remaining nonnegative
clock terms is at most S. The elementary inequality log(1+u)<=u for
u>=0 bounds their infinite product by exp(S)<e<3. The last bound also
follows directly from the exponential series using n!>=2^(n-1),
strictly for n>=3. Hence
                P_infinity<3*10^50.               (5)
The100-factor product is computed exactly with rational arithmetic;
there is no floating logarithm, unbounded truncation, or numerical orbit.

3. CLOSE THE SMALL-VARIANCE BOOTSTRAP
Set K=111*10^50=37*(3*10^50), delta=h/K.
The same exact certificate verifies10^(-57)<=delta. We may prove the
slightly stronger assertion for0<X_0<=delta.
At time0,z_0=0,W_0=X_0. Inductively, suppose the preceding positions
have alternated,0<=z_j<=Q, and |X_j|<=37*P_j*X_0 for j<=t.
By(5), every such position is at most K*X_0<=h in absolute value.
Since V_0=0, the corrected variance V_(t+1)/(1-d^(t+1)) is a convex
combination of X_0^2,...,X_t^2. Thus U_(t+1)<=h and
 a_t>=38/(1+h/rho)=1443/38=a_min.
Section1 preserves the cone and gives a nonzero next position of the
opposite sign. Section2 gives W_(t+1)<=P_(t+1)*X_0, whence
|X_(t+1)|=W_(t+1)/(1-18*z_(t+1))<=37*P_(t+1)*X_0.
This closes induction for every finite time. The global product bound
is fixed in advance, so no future orbit bound is assumed in the bootstrap.

4. ORIGIN CONVERGENCE WITHIN THE CONE
By the preceding one-step bound, W_t/P_t is positive and nonincreasing.
Since P_t has a finite positive limit, W_t has a nonnegative finite limit.
If that limit were positive, then |X_t|>=W_t would be bounded below at
late times. The raw variance convolution, with d<1, would make U_(t+1)
bounded below by a positive constant. Since b^(t+1)->0, the exact a_t
would eventually satisfy a_t<=38-kappa for some kappa>0 (take kappa<1).
Then(3),(4) give W_(t+1)<=(1-kappa*ell)*W_t, contradicting a positive
limit. Therefore W_t->0. The cone bounds imply X_t->0,M_t->0 and the
stable variance recursion gives V_t->0, hence a_t->38.
This convergence argument does not need the global low-cap theorem012v2.

5. SELECT THE ROOT
Eliminate raw momentum as in independently PASSED028v1 Section1:
 X_(t+1)=[1+b*a_t/a_(t-1)-ell*a_t]*X_t
                          -b*a_t/a_(t-1)*X_(t-1), t>=1.
Its coefficients converge to the critical ones and its characteristic
polynomial is (r+1)*(r+b), with distinct root moduli1 and.9. The last
coefficient is nonzero at every finite time, and the solution never
vanishes, so Poincare's ratio theorem gives a limit of-1 or-b.
This uses exactly the classical ratio implication, not Perron's
root-attainment addition and not a convergence-rate assertion.
If the limit were-b, X_(t+1)=X_t-a_t*M_(t+1) would imply
 z_(t+1)=-(1-X_(t+1)/X_t)/(a_t*(X_(t+1)/X_t))
                      ->(1+b)/(38*b)=1/18.
But z_t<=2/37<1/18 at every time. This is a contradiction. Hence the
ratio tends to-1. The same identity then gives z_t->1/19 and Z_t/X_t->1/19,
so the exponentially small center direction in081 is excluded here.

SCOPE AND VALIDATION. This is an open punctured interval (and its closed
outer endpoints) of standard starts at every critical scaling. It does
not cover starts of order eta, nor rule out exceptional fast starts
outside the interval, nor establish a null supercritical origin basin.
The scalar critical curvature tends to38 here; this alone does not
settle the full two-eigenvalue problem. No frontier score is asserted.

The exact script checks rational cone endpoints, derivative numerators,
variance ceiling,100 clock factors, and an explicit bound on the entire
infinite clock tail. It certifies those arithmetic steps, not the
written induction and infinite-time argument. Independent audit pending.

# Unit-norm nonlinear ReLU teacher with paired initialization

T267 / Target 1 / C010 / proof draft (unaudited); novelty unestablished.

This removes the diverging teacher norm in C009, at the price of paired
initialization and noise that shrinks with the signal. It is a restricted
four-point, stratified-design, noise-averaged theorem. It does not establish
the generic iid Gaussian-input target or a fixed-positive-noise result.
The hardest remaining target step is sign-level population-risk control
for a genuinely sampled nonlinear model beyond this finite-support
infinite-width construction.

## Statement

Fix nu in (0,1]. For 0<e<1/4 let D=1+e^2+e^4 and use the same four inputs
x_(s,t)=(1,e s,e^2 t)/sqrt(D), s,t in {-1,1}. Training contains each once;
the test law is uniform on these four points. Let

u_e=(0,e,1)/sqrt(1+e^2),
c_e=e^2/[sqrt(D)*sqrt(1+e^2)], alpha_e=c_e/2,
g_e(x)=ReLU(u_e.x)-E_X ReLU(u_e.X).

The vector u_e has norm one. On this support u_e.x=c_e(s+t), so

g_e(x_(s,t))=alpha_e(s+t+st).

Thus the teacher is genuinely nonlinear even when restricted to the
support: no affine function of x has a nonzero st Walsh coefficient.
The centering constant is the population mean c_e/2. Labels are g_e(x_i)
plus independent equiprobable noise +/-c_e, so the noise standard deviation
is c_e, not a fixed positive constant as e decreases.

Take even width m=2N and initialize each independent pair by
w_(2j-1)=w_(2j)=W_j iid N(0,I_3),
a_(2j-1)=nu, a_(2j)=-nu.
Pairs are independent; the individual neurons are NOT iid. Initially f=0
exactly. Train both layers of every neuron by simultaneous GD at step 1/2,
loss ||f(X)-y||^2/(2n), n=4, with f=m^(-1/2) sum a ReLU(w.x) and gate
convention 1_{z>0}. No symmetry is imposed after initialization.

Let Q_(m,e)(k) be clean population squared risk, averaged over the sixteen
training-label-noise patterns, conditional on initialization. Let b_h be
C009's rates for the full initial tangent kernel h_nu=k+nu^2 g1, with mode
indices 0,1,2,12. Set

k0=ceil(e^(-1/2)), k1=floor(log(2)/b1),
k2=ceil(e^(-3/2)), k3=floor(log(2)/b2),
B=log[b1/(b2+b12)].

In the iterated limit m=2N->infinity first, then e->0, the probability of
failure of the strict witnesses

Q(k0)>Q(k1)<Q(k2)>Q(k3)

tends to zero. More precisely the four risks divided by alpha_e^2 converge
in probability, in that iterated sense, to 4,7/2,4,3.
For every fixed delta>0, every maximizer k_peak on the integer interval
I_e=[floor((B-1)/b1),ceil((B+1)/b1)] is interior and satisfies
|b1 k_peak-B|<delta with probability tending to one in the same iterated
sense. Consequently

k_peak ~ (4*pi/nu^2) e^(-1) log(1/e).

This localizes a central local peak, not a global maximum or all extrema.

## 1. Teacher identity and exact initialization

ReLU(s+t) takes values 2,0,0,0, whose mean is 1/2. Its centered version is
(s+t+st)/2. The unit norm and displayed teacher identity follow directly.
The nonzero interaction coefficient rules out an affine teacher on the
four inputs, even though two projections lie exactly at the teacher's
ReLU kink. No differentiability of the teacher is used in training.

Each pair has exactly cancelling outputs. Its two readout-Jacobian Gram
summands are identical. Its two hidden-Jacobian Gram summands are also
identical because their readout factors are squared. Dividing by m=2N
therefore gives the same expected full kernel as in C009:

C_(nu,e)(i,l)=[k(x_i.x_l)+nu^2 g1(x_i.x_l)]/4.

Strong laws apply to the N independent pairs. No independent-neuron
concentration or centered independent readout-sign argument is needed.

## 2. Transfer from the actual nonlinear GD

Here we specify why C009 Section 3 applies despite correlated pairs.
For e<1/4, c_e<e^2<1/16. The largest absolute teacher value is 3c_e/2;
the largest label magnitude is at most 5c_e/2<5/32. Thus ||y||<5/16<2.
The actual initial output is identically zero; use M=0 and R_0=2 in the
deterministic finite-horizon recurrences of C009 Section 3. Those bounds
are neuronwise and use no independence. They hold separately for both
members of every pair, even after their hidden weights separate.

The empirical mean of initial squared hidden norms converges almost surely
to 3 by the pairwise strong law. The weighted initial gate-band mass is
now exactly the mean over N independent W_j of
(1+||W_j||)^2 1{min_i|W_j.x_i| <= D_* (1+||W_j||)/sqrt(2N)}.
It tends to zero by the same rational-band strong-law and dominated-
convergence argument as C009. The initial kernel converges entrywise to
C by the pairwise strong law. These are the only probabilistic inputs to
the instantaneous-kernel and exact discrete-step remainder bounds in C009.
Their finite-horizon telescoping proof therefore gives

max_(k<=T) ||f_actual(k)-f_frozen(k)|| -> 0 in probability

for every fixed e,nu,T, uniformly over all sixteen noise patterns. The
frozen iteration starts at zero exactly. Here and below T may depend on e;
width tends to infinity separately for each fixed e. This does not claim a
uniform feature-scale rate or a feasible numerical width.

## 3. Risk margins

All three nonconstant teacher Walsh coefficients are alpha=alpha_e.
Independent +/-c_e label noise has Walsh variances c_e^2/4=alpha^2.
Parseval and the zero initial prediction give the exact frozen risk

Q_e^0(k)/alpha^2 = (1-q0^k)^2
                 + sum_(h=1,2,12) [q_h^(2k)+(1-q_h^k)^2],
q_h=exp(-b_h).

C009 Section 2 supplies b1~nu^2 e/(4pi), b2~nu^2 e^2/(8pi),
b12/b2->1, and b0 bounded away from zero. At k0 all nonconstant modes
remain unlearned, giving 1+1+1+1=4. At k1 the fast component has q1->1/2
and the two slow components remain at one, giving 1+1/2+1+1=7/2.
At k2 the fast component has q1->0 while slow components remain at one,
giving 4. At k3 both slow components have q->1/2, giving 1+1+1/2+1/2=3.
The three strict limiting margins are 1/2,1/2,1. For fixed e, alpha>0 and
the finite-horizon transfer changes risk by o_P(1), hence by o_P(alpha^2)
as width grows; division by a fixed positive alpha^2 is legitimate.
Then let e decrease. This proves the four strict actual-risk witnesses.

## 4. Central peak

Interpolate the frozen curve continuously and put z=(B+s)/b1 with
B=log[b1/(b2+b12)]. Uniformly for s in compact intervals,

(Q_e^0)'(z)/[2 alpha^2 (b2+b12)] -> exp(-s)-1,
(Q_e^0)''(z)/[2 alpha^2 b1 (b2+b12)] -> -exp(-s).

Indeed each nonconstant mode contributes 2 alpha^2 b_h q_h(1-2q_h).
The fast term contributes exp(-s); its quadratic correction is
O((b2+b12)/b1). The two slow terms contribute -b2/(b2+b12) and
-b12/(b2+b12), up to errors O(((b2+b12)/b1) B). The constant-mode
term and its derivatives vanish faster than any polynomial of e.
The same estimates after one further differentiation give the stated
second derivative. Thus the frozen central peak has scaled coordinate
s_e->0 and a strict value gap away from any fixed delta neighborhood,
of order alpha^2 (b2+b12)/b1, by integrating the derivative on [-1,1].
The grid spacing b1 tends to zero, so discrete maximizers obey the same
localization. When delta>=1, the conclusion follows from any smaller
positive delta, and interval endpoints are excluded as well.

For each fixed e the interval is finite and its positive peak gap is a
fixed positive number. Section 2 therefore transfers the maximizer
localization to the actual risk with probability tending to one as width
grows. No random initial-output perturbation occurs. Finally
b1/(b2+b12)~1/e and b1~nu^2 e/(4pi) give the peak asymptotic.

## Scope and dependencies

This proof depends on the unaudited deterministic bounds and Gaussian
kernel asymptotics in C009, not on an independent audit or a floating-point
fit. Pair cancellation is only an initial condition, not frozen weights.
The centering offset is part of the single-index link ReLU(z)-c_e/2.
The teacher has uniformly unit norm and is nonlinear on the support;
its variation and the label-noise standard deviation both vanish as e^2.
The design remains stratified, finite support, with every test input in
training, and risk averages over labels. No fixed-noise, iid-design,
macroscopic feature-learning, full-target or novelty claim is made.
Primary kernel source: Heckel--Yilmaz arXiv:2007.10099v2 Section 3 K1/K2.
The existence of two noise thresholds in Stephenson--Lee 2108.12006 is not
used to infer that this model has the same noise window.
All explicit definitions in proofs/BOUNDED_RELU_PAIRED.md
Even width; independent Gaussian hidden-weight pairs with equal hidden weights and opposite heads +/-nu, nu fixed in (0,1]; neurons are not iid
Unit-norm centered ReLU teacher with a nonzero interaction Walsh coefficient on the support
Noise standard deviation c_e=e^2/sqrt((1+e^2+e^4)(1+e^2)) tends to zero; n=4 stratified training and uniform test support
Risk averaged over sixteen independent label-noise sign patterns; GD step 1/2; width limit precedes feature-scale limit

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Variation of nearest-unvisited walk length under a random start structural calculation Result: Let m and M be the minimum and maximum start-dependent lengths, R=M/m. The elementary bound Var(X)<=(M-E X)*(E X-m) implies sd(X)/E X<=(R-1)/(2*sqrt(R)) for any X in[m,M]. Classical nearest-neighbor-tour comparison gives R=O(log n), since every walk length is at least MST length and its length is at most O(log n) times a TSP tour, at most twice MST length. Hence a rigorous O(sqrt(log n)) coefficient-of-variation bound follows, short of an absolute constant. Check: The variance inequality follows by averaging(X-m)*(M-X)>=0. Maximizing(M-u)*(u-m)/u^2 over u in[m,M] gives u=2Mm/(M+m) and the displayed exact ratio. This is sharper than simply bounding standard deviation by the range. Obstruction: The deterministic logarithmic approximation examples do not automatically give a large random-start coefficient of variation. One must also control how many starting vertices exhibit the long route.

Method: Energy plus entropy conductance bound Result: Let G have odd n and edge expansion |boundary S|>=h|S| for all |S|<=n/2. Use H(sigma)=-J sum_edges sigma_u sigma_v-B sum_v sigma_v with J>0,B>=0,Jh>B, and Gibbs law pi proportional to exp(-beta H). Consider any reversible single-spin continuous-time chain with each individual spin-flip rate at most1. Put A={number of plus spins< n/2}. Global spin reversal maps A bijectively onto its complement and does not decrease Gibbs weight, so pi(A)<=1/2. An A-to-complement jump must start with(n-1)/2 plus spins, whose energy exceeds the all-minus energy by at least(Jh-B)(n-1). There are at most2^n such states and total exit rate at most n per state. Since pi(A) is at least the all-minus weight, the conductance Phi=Q(A,A-complement)/pi(A) is at most n*2^n*exp[-beta(Jh-B)(n-1)]. Starting with pi conditioned on A, the time-s law is bounded above by pi/pi(A), by Markov-kernel positivity and stationarity. Consequently the expected number of A-to-complement jumps by time t is at most t*Phi. The probability of still being in A at time t is at least1-t*Phi, giving total variation distance at least1/2-t*Phi. Convexity of total variation implies the same lower bound for the worst starting state. Therefore t_mix(1/4)>=1/(4*Phi), at least exp[beta(Jh-B)(n-1)]/(4*n*2^n). This is exponential in n when beta(Jh-B)>log2. The calculation accounts explicitly for entropy. It is a deterministic expansion-based mixing lower bound; it does not prove a metastable exit-time distribution, or expansion for every configuration-model degree law. Check: Boundary-layer counting and stationary domination give separate energy and time estimates. Obstruction: No general random-graph expansion theorem or metastable exit-time distribution is proved.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03946, 'The groups $\SL_2(\F_{13})$ and $\SL_2(\F_{19})$ are Galois over $\Q$'] Let $L/\Q$ be a finite Galois extension whose group $G$ acts faithfully and
transitively on a finite set $\Omega$, let $B$ be a point stabilizer, and put
$K=L^B$.  Fix a prime of $L$ above $q$ and let $I\trianglelefteq D\leq G$ be
its inertia and decomposition groups.  Then the primes of $K$ above $q$
correspond to the $D$-orbits on $\Omega$. An orbit $\mathcal O\ni\omega$ corresponds to a prime with
\begin{equation}
 e(\mathcal O)=|I\omega|,
 \qquad
 f(\mathcal O)=\frac{|D\omega|}{|I\omega|} .
\end{equation}

[Corollary cor:main of arXiv:2608.20537, 'Persistent anisotropy in multi-dimensional\\ branching Brownian motion'] Let $d \geq 2$.
  Almost surely, for each $L,\varepsilon > 0$ and nonempty open $U \subset S^{d-1}$, there exist $\theta_1,\theta_2 \in U$ such that

body:
[Theorem 5 (Breuer-Major in rough Hölder topology) of arXiv:2606.04179, 'Functional Scaling Limits of Interpolated Correlated Random Walks in Hölder Topology'] Assume the correlation \(\rho\) satisfies
    \[
        \tag{summable ``thin tail''}
        \sum_{k\in \Z} |\rho(k)|^{\hermRank} < \infty
    \]
    and \(\feature \in L^p(\gamma)\) for some \(p > 6\).
    Then the scaled \textbf{interpolated} random walk lifted into the space of Hölder
    rough paths converges in distribution against the enhanced Brownian motion, where the
    second level is given by the Stratonovich integral. Specifically define the scaled
    interpolated random walk
    \(\hat\interpF^n \coloneq\tfrac1{\sqrt{n}}\interpF^n\).
    Let \(\bm\) be the Brownian motion with Stratonovich integral \(\mathbb{\bm}^{\mathrm{Strat}}\). Then we have
    \[
        \mathbf{\hat\interpF}^n = (\hat\interpF^n, \tfrac12(\hat\interpF^n)^2)
        \xrightarrow{d} (\sigma\bm, \sigma^2\mathbb{\bm}^{\mathrm{Strat}})
        \qquad \text{in } \mathscr C^{\beta}([0,T]) \text{ for any } \beta \in (\tfrac13, \tfrac12 - \tfrac1p),
    \]
    with \(\mathscr C^{\beta}([0,T])\) the space of \(\beta\)-Hölder rough paths \citep[Def.~2.1]{frizCourseRoughPaths2020}
    and \(c_k\) the  Hermite coefficients of \(\feature\), cf.~\eqref{eq: Hermite expansion}.
    The variance \(\sigma^2 \coloneq \sum_{k \ge q} c_k^2 k! \sum_{m\in \integer} \rho(m)^k\)
    is well defined and finite. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Breuer-Major in rough Hölder topology

body: For every set A, there is no surjection from A onto its power set P(A) (the set of all subsets of A). Since a -> {a} is an injection from A into P(A), it follows that |A| < |P(A)| for every set A: every set is strictly smaller than its power set. In particular there is no largest cardinality, and iterating the power set on an infinite set produces an unbounded increasing hierarchy of infinite cardinalities.

body: A normed vector space (X, ||.||) is uniformly convex if for every epsilon in (0, 2] there exists delta > 0 such that, for all x, y in X with ||x|| <= 1, ||y|| <= 1, and ||x - y|| >= epsilon, we have ||(x+y)/2|| <= 1 - delta. Uniform convexity is a quantitative strengthening of strict convexity (which only requires ||(x+y)/2|| < 1 whenever x not equal to y, ||x||=||y||=1) and holds for every Hilbert space, via the parallelogram law, and for every L^p space with 1 < p < infinity. [standard, e.g. Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDEs]
title: Uniformly Convex Banach Space

[Coro 20 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (normal approximation of the count statistics $(N_\la)_{\la \geq 1}$)

dx d\mu(h) = dx h^{\beta}\ind{h>0}dh$ for some $  \beta > -1$. Then for each $t>0$, the count statistic $(N_\la)_{\la \geq 1}$ satisfies the normal approximation bounds
\[
\mathbf{d}_K \left(  \frac{N_\la - \E N_\la} {\sqrt{\Var N_\la}}, N \right) \leq C_K \cdot  \frac{\la^{1/2}}{\Var N_\la}

and

\mathbf{d}_W \left(  \frac{N_\la - \E N_\la} {\sqrt{\Var N_\la}}, N \right) \leq C_K  \frac{\la^{1/2}}{\Var N_\la} + C_W  \frac{\la}{(\Var N_\la)^{3/2}},
\]
where $C_K,C_W$  are  constants depending only on $d,\beta$ and $t$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:chernoff of arXiv:2608.24087, 'Knowing When to Ask for Help: Bayesian Self-Escalation in Hierarchical LLM Agents'] Assume a finite signal alphabet and let
\begin{equation}
  C \;=\; -\log\ \min_{s\in[0,1]}\ \sum_{k} f_0(k)^{s} f_1(k)^{1-s}
\end{equation}
be the Chernoff information of $(f_0,f_1)$, with $C>0$ iff $f_0\neq f_1$. Then
for every fixed $\tau\in(0,1)$ there is a constant $A_\tau<\infty$, independent
of $t$, such that
\[
  \mathbb{P}\big(B_t\le\tau \mid Y=1\big)\;\le\;A_\tau\,e^{-tC},
  \qquad
  \mathbb{P}\big(B_t\ge\tau \mid Y=0\big)\;\le\;A_\tau\,e^{-tC}.
\]
Consequently $B_t\to\mathbf{1}\{Y=1\}$ almost surely, and the oracle's step-$t$
thresholded decision errs with probability at most $A_\tau e^{-tC}$.

[Defn planar-map-with-missing-edges of arXiv:2510.26123, 'Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations:\\ exact exponents and scaling limit'] A \textbf{planar map with missing edges} is a planar map $\mathfrak m$ with two types of edges: \textbf{missing} and \textbf{non-missing} edges (we often refer to non-missing edges simply as edges). The missing edges are always on the boundary of the external face of $\mathfrak m$ and are \emph{not} considered to be part of $\mathcal E(\mathfrak m)$. 
    
    A \textbf{directed planar map with missing edges}  is a planar map $\mathfrak m$ with missing edges equipped with an orientation of the edges in $\mathcal E(\mathfrak m)$ that is acyclic. In particular, missing-edges are \emph{not} oriented.
    See the left-hand side of Figure~(fig-bipolar-boundaries of the paper) for an example.

[Theorem Riesz of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Any positive functional $I:C_c(X)\to\mathbb R$ comes by integrating with respect to a certain measure on $X$,
$$I(f)=\int_Xf(x)d\mu(x)$$
which is unique, modulo null sets. In addition, the following happen:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mu(K)<\infty$, for any $K\subset X$ compact.

\item $\mu(E)=\inf\{\mu(U)|E\subset U\ {\rm open}\}$, for any $E$ measurable.

\item $\mu(E)=\sup\{\mu(K)|K\subset E\ {\rm compact}\}$, for any $E$ open, or of finite measure.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition def:consistency of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] We say $P\in\Delta(\Omega)$ and measurable $Z:\Omega\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ are \emph{consistent} if $\mathbb{E}_P Z \leq 0$.
  Similarly, a set $\mathcal{P} \subseteq \Delta(\Omega)$ is \emph{consistent with} $\mathcal{Z}$ if $\mathbb{E}_P Z \leq 0$ for all $P\in\mathcal{P}, Z\in\mathcal{Z}$.
  For gamble space $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$, we define
  \begin{align}
    
    \Delta_0(\mathcal{Z}) &:= \{P\in\Delta(\Omega) \mid \mathbb{E}_P Z \leq 0 \;\forall Z\in\mathrm{mdcl}(\mathcal{Z})\}~,
  \end{align}
  to be the set of all consistent probability measures.

body:
[Lem 250 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Suppose the random vector $\bX$ in $\R^N$ is \emph{subgaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$}, meaning that $(\theta,\bX)$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$ for all $\theta$ in the unit ball $B_N\subset\R^N$. Then
    \[
    \P\bigg(\frac{\|\bX\|}{N^{1/2}} \ge t\bigg)
    \le \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{16\sigma^2} \bigg\}
    \]
provided $t\ge 6\sigma$. It follows that
$\E(\|\bX\|^p) \le  C_p \sigma^p N^{p/2}$
where $C_p$ is a constant depending only on $p$.

\begin{proof}
To bound the norm of a random vector $\bX$ in $\R^N$, the standard argument is to let $N_{1/2}$ be a $1/2$-net of the unit ball $B\subset \R^N$, and note that
    \begin{align*}
    \|\bX\|
    &= \sup \Big\{
    (\theta,\bX) : \theta\in B\Big\}
    \le 
    \sup\bigg\{
    (\theta_1+\theta_2,\bX):
    \theta_1\in N_{1/2},
    \theta_2\in \frac12 B\bigg\} \\
    &\le
    \sup\Big\{(\theta,\bX) :\theta\in N_{1/2}\Big\}
    + \frac{\|\bX\|}{2}
    \equiv S + \frac{\|\bX\|}{2} \,.
    \end{align*}
Rearranging the above gives
    \[\|\bX\|
    \le 2\sup\Big\{(\theta,\bX) :\theta\in N_{1/2}\Big\}
    = 2S\,.
    \]
We can arrange for $|N_{1/2}| \le 6^N$. If $(\theta,\bX)$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$ for all $\theta\in B_N$, then a union bound over the net $N_{1/2}$ gives
    \beq
    \P\bigg(\frac{\|\bX\|}{N^{1/2}} \ge 2t\bigg)
    \le \P(S \ge N^{1/2} t)
    \le 6^N 
    \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{2\sigma^2}\bigg\}
    \le \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{4\sigma^2}\bigg\}\,,
    \eeq
where the last bound holds provided
$t\ge 3\sigma$. Integrating (similarly to \eqref{e:subgaus.mmt}) gives the moment bound
    \beq
    \frac{\E[ \|\bX\|^p]}{N^{p/2}}
    \le
    \frac{2^p \E(S^p)}{N^{p/2}}
    \le (6\sigma)^p
    +2^p \int_{3\sigma}^\infty
    pt^{p-1}
    \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{4\sigma^2}\bigg\}\, dt
    \le C_p \sigma^p
    \eeq
for a constant $C_p$ depending only on $p$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 6 (Threshold Isolation Principle) of arXiv:2605.11783, 'Stability of Compensated Jump Integrals under Quadratic Variation Convergence'] Let $X$ and $\{X^n\}_{n\ge1}$ be c\`adl\`ag processes on $[0,t]$ such that
\[
[X^n-X]_t \to 0
\qquad \text{in probability}.
\]
Fix $r>0$, and for each $k\ge1$ define
\[
\delta(k,r):=\frac{r}{2^{k+2}},
\qquad
L(r,k):=r\Bigl(1-\frac{3}{2^{k+2}}\Bigr),
\]
and
\[
A_k(r)
:=
\Bigl\{
\omega:
\bigl||\Delta X_s(\omega)|-L(r,k)\bigr|>\delta(k,r)
\text{ for all } s\le t
\Bigr\}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb P\Bigl(\bigcup_{k\ge1}A_k(r)\Bigr)=1.
\]

Moreover, for each fixed $k\ge1$, if we define
\[
B_n(k,r)
:=
\Bigl\{
\sup_{s\le t}|\Delta(X^n-X)_s|<\delta(k,r)
\Bigr\},
\]
then
$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P\bigl(B_n(k,r)\bigr)=1.
$
On the event $A_k(r)\cap B_n(k,r)$, the classification of jumps relative to the threshold
$L(r,k)$ is preserved, i.e.
\[
|\Delta X_s|\le L(r,k)-\delta(k,r)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
|\Delta X^n_s|<L(r,k),
\]
and
\[
|\Delta X_s|\ge L(r,k)+\delta(k,r)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
|\Delta X^n_s|>L(r,k),
\]
for all $s\le t$.

In particular, on $A_k(r)\cap B_n(k,r)$,
\[
1_{\{|\Delta X^n_s|\le L(r,k)\}}
\le
1_{\{|\Delta X_s|\le L(r,k)\}}
\qquad \text{for all } s\le t,
\]
and therefore
\[
\sum_{s\le t} (\Delta X^n_s)^2 1_{\{|\Delta X^n_s|\le L(r,k)\}}
\le
2[X^n-X]_t
+
2\sum_{s\le t} (\Delta X_s)^2 1_{\{|\Delta X_s|\le L(r,k)\}}.
\]

body: The Euler-Maclaurin formula relates the sum of a sufficiently smooth function f over consecutive integers a, a+1, ..., b to the integral of f over [a,b]. It states this sum equals the integral of f from a to b, plus (f(a)+f(b))/2, plus a finite sum for k=1 to m of B_{2k}/(2k)! times [f^{(2k-1)}(b) - f^{(2k-1)}(a)], where B_{2k} are Bernoulli numbers and f^{(2k-1)} denotes the (2k-1)-th derivative, plus an explicit, boundable remainder term. It is used to approximate sums by integrals, accelerate numerical summation of slowly convergent series, and derive Stirling's approximation. Found independently by Euler and Maclaurin in the 1730s.
title: Euler-Maclaurin formula

body:
Fix positive input/output dimensions n_in,q, a nonzero deterministic input x in R^n_in, and positive constants alpha,lambda. Let n be the hidden width and d the number of residual blocks. All entries of W_0 (n by n_in), W_l (n by n), and W_out (q by n) are mutually independent N(0,1). Independently draw iid uniform signs s_lj in {-1,+1}, one per block and coordinate, and freeze them at initialization. Define z_0=W_0 x/sqrt(n_in), z_l=alpha z_(l-1)+lambda sqrt(2/n) W_l ReLU(s_l multiplied coordinatewise by z_(l-1)), and z_out=W_out z_d/sqrt(n). Write kappa=(5lambda^4+4alpha^2 lambda^2)/(alpha^2+lambda^2)^2 and beta_n=2/n+kappa d/n. There is an exact distributional representation z_out=(||x||_2/sqrt(n_in))(alpha^2+lambda^2)^(d/2) exp(G_n/2) Z, where Z is standard Gaussian in R^q independent of G_n. Its radial variable can be chosen as G_n=log(n_in ||z_d||_2^2/[n ||x||_2^2 (alpha^2+lambda^2)^d]). If n,d tend to infinity with d/n tending to a positive finite r, Theorem4 gives E[G_n]=-beta_n/2+O(d/n^2), Var(G_n)=beta_n+O(d/n^2), and G_n converges in distribution to H~N(-kappa r/2,kappa r). Thus the output normalized by its deterministic prefactor converges to exp(H/2)Z with H and Z independent. Constants in the error terms may depend on alpha,lambda and fixed lower/upper positive bounds on d/n. This is the marginal law for one fixed input, not a joint multiple-input process. The balanced result does not assume the vanilla model’s Conjecture5. The positivity restriction alpha>0 retains a nonzero skip connection and avoids finite-width extinction in the logarithm.
Fixed finite input/output dimensions and one fixed nonzero input
alpha>0 and lambda>0 are fixed (explicit restriction of the source)
All Gaussian weights independent across layers and entries
Independent fair signs per layer and coordinate, frozen at initialization
d/n tends to a positive finite constant; errors stated uniformly within a compact interval of positive depth/width ratios

\[

\forall S\subset[n]\text{ with }|S|\le \eta n:\ 
e_{\widetilde G_n}(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)|S|

\]

[Lemma 23 (A deterministic common reset partition) of arXiv:2608.06393, 'Intrinsic Tangential Hadamard Differentiability of Rough-BSDE Solution Maps'] Fix $R,B<\infty$.  There are $\varepsilon_0>0$, a deterministic
partition
\begin{equation}
 \Pi=\{0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T\},
 \qquad N\leq N_*<\infty,
\end{equation}
and constants $r_A>1$, $K_A<\infty$ such that the following assertions
hold simultaneously for every
\[
 \tau\in\mathbb T_{\mathbf x}^p,\qquad
 \|\tau\|_{\mathbb T_{\mathbf x}^p}\leq R,
\]
every $(\mathbf Z,a)\in\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf x}(\tau)$ with
$\mathfrak b(\mathbf Z,a)\leq B$, and every
$0<|\varepsilon|\leq\varepsilon_0$.

\begin{enumerate}
 \item On each $I_i=[t_i,t_{i+1}]$, the base flow and the flow driven by
 $\mathbf x^{\varepsilon;\mathbf Z,a}$ remain in the common reset regime.
 In particular, their first spatial derivatives are bounded away from
 zero, and all flow-jet estimates used in
 Propositions~\ref{prop:uniform-full-jet-expansion} and
 \ref{prop:weighted-full-tangent-generator} hold with constants independent of
 $i,\varepsilon,\tau,\mathbf Z$, and $a$.

 \item Let $\mathbb Q_i^\varepsilon$ be the local Girsanov measure generated
 by the mean $z$-coefficient in the transformed difference equation.  The
 corresponding stochastic exponentials satisfy common reverse-H\"older
 bounds, and the base and perturbed martingale integrands have
 $\mathbb Q_i^\varepsilon$-BMO norm at most a deterministic constant
 $b_{\mathbb Q}$.

 \item The positive part of the mean $y$-coefficient satisfies
 \begin{equation}
  (\alpha_s^{\varepsilon,i})^+
  \leq a_s^i+\delta_*
  \bigl(
    |\widetilde Z_s^i|^2
    +|\widetilde Z_s^{\varepsilon,i}|^2
  \bigr),
  \qquad
  \int_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}}a_s^i\,ds\leq A_*,
 \end{equation}
 where $A_*<\infty$ is deterministic and
 \begin{equation}
  2r_A\delta_*b_{\mathbb Q}^2<1.
 \end{equation}
 Consequently,
 \begin{equation}
  \sup_{\sigma\in\mathcal T_{I_i}}
  \left\|
   \mathbb E_{\sigma}^{\mathbb Q_i^\varepsilon}
   \exp\left(
    r_A\int_\sigma^{t_{i+1}}
       (\alpha_s^{\varepsilon,i})^+\,ds
   \right)
  \right\|_\infty
  \leq
  K_A:=\frac{e^{r_AA_*}}
             {1-2r_A\delta_*b_{\mathbb Q}^2}.
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The partition and $N_*$ depend on the base driver, the coefficient bounds,
$R$, and $B$, but not on the particular tangent, its representative, or
$\varepsilon$.

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2604.07275, 'Some probabilistic properties and time-changed versions of a renewal process based on Mitt'] Let $N$ be an integer valued random variable with $\mathbb{E}(u^N) < \infty$ for some $u > 1$ and it is independent with a sequence of i.i.d. random variables $\{Y_i\}_{i\ge 1}$ with common subexponential distribution $\bar{F}_{Y_1}(t)= \mathrm{Pr}\{Y_1 > t\}$ . Then,  
		$$
		\mathrm{Pr}\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i > t\Big\} \sim \mathbb{E}(N) \bar{F}_{Y_1}(t), \ \ \text{as $t \to \infty$}.
		$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 11 of arXiv:2604.07275

body:
[Proposition 20 (Exact form and zero set of $F_3$) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] Assume the spectral scalars are square-integrable,
$f_\nu\in L^2(0,1)$. \textup{(}This is automatic in any resolvent
realisation, where they are bounded --- for the biased walk
$f_\nu(\gamma)=(1-\gamma)/(1-\lambda_\nu(1-\gamma))$ with
$|\lambda_\nu|<1$ --- but it does not follow from \textup{(S2)},
which gives analyticity only on the \emph{open} interval and so
does not by itself make $F_3$ finite.\textup{)}
Let $\pi^\ast\in\Sigma$ be the fixed reference distribution of
Section~\ref{subsec:orientation} --- reset-neutrality of $\pi^\ast$ is
what gives $\langle\pi^\ast,\mathbf n_\nu\rangle=0$, and without it the
zero set below is a translate of $\Sigma$ rather than $\Sigma$
itself. Let $a_\nu(\pi)=\langle\pi-\pi^\ast,\mathbf n_\nu\rangle$ and let
$G_{\nu\nu'}=\int_0^1 f_\nu(\gamma)f_{\nu'}(\gamma)\,d\gamma$ be
the Gram matrix of the spectral scalars. Then
\[
F_3(\pi)=\mathbf a(\pi)^{\!\top} G\,\mathbf a(\pi),
\]
a quadratic form in the affine coordinates $\mathbf a(\pi)$, with
$G$ positive definite by the linear independence of the $f_\nu$
\textup{(S2)}. Consequently
\[
F_3(\pi)\ge0,\qquad F_3(\pi)=0\iff\pi\in\Sigma:
\]
the functional detects the separatrix exactly.

body:
[Proposition 23 (Middle side of a double hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{prop:middle}
Let
\[
        \alpha=\spec(A),\qquad
        \beta=\spec(B),\qquad
        \eta=\spec(E),\qquad
        \phi=\spec(F)
\]
belong to \(\Spec_n^\circ\), and assume the trace compatibility condition
\[
        \sum_i\alpha_i+\sum_i\beta_i+\sum_i\eta_i - \sum_i\phi_i=0 .
\]
Let \(U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4\) be independent Haar-distributed unitary matrices and set
\[
        S=U_1AU_1^*+U_2BU_2^*,
        \qquad
        T=U_3EU_3^*-U_4FU_4^* .
\]
For \(\nu\in\Spec_n\), write
\[
        \nu^\vee=(-\nu_n,\ldots,-\nu_1),
\]
so that \(\nu^\vee=\spec(-X)\) whenever \(\nu=\spec(X)\).
Suppose that the double hive polytope
\[
        \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi^\vee)
        :=
        \bigcup_{\nu\in\Spec_n}
        H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu)
        \times
        H_n(\eta,\phi^\vee;\nu^\vee)
\]
is full dimensional, where the two hives are glued along the common side with values
\(\nu\) on the first hive and \(\nu^\vee\) on the second. 
 If a double hive is
sampled from normalized Lebesgue measure on
\(\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi^\vee)\), then its middle side has the same
distribution as the regular conditional distribution of
\[
        \spec(S)
        =
        \spec(U_1AU_1^*+U_2BU_2^*)
\]
given the matrix equation
\[
        S+T=0 .
\]
Equivalently,
\[
        \spec(\text{middle side})
        \stackrel{d}{=}
        \spec(U_1AU_1^*+U_2BU_2^*)
        \,\big|\,
        U_1AU_1^*+U_2BU_2^*
        +U_3EU_3^*-U_4FU_4^*=0 .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Middle side of a double hive

[Prop 4 of arXiv:2604.10395, 'A remark on the comparison of the sum and the maximum of positive random variables'] Let $a_n \coloneqq \frac{h(n \alpha) -h(\alpha)}{\log n}$ for $n \ge 2$. 
Then \\
(i) $a_n < 1$ for every $n$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = 1$.\\
(ii) $(a_n)_n$ is strictly increasing. \\
(iii) There exists $N(\alpha,\beta) \ge 2$ such that \eqref{eq:beta-n-relation} holds if and only if  $n \ge N(\alpha,\beta)$.

[Lemma le:good_scales_merging_refl of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $D$ with some bounded boundary values. For any $b>0$ and $q \in (0,1)$ there exist $M,p>0$ so that the following is true. 
Let $z \in D$ and $r>0$ such that $B(z,r) \subseteq D$. Let $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$ be as defined in Section~(se:gff of the paper) with the same boundary values as $\widetilde{h}$ above (after scaling and translation). Let $G_{z,r}$ be the event that
\begin{itemize}
 \item the scale $(z,r)$ is $M$-good for $h$, and
 \item the event $G$ above occurs for the (scaled and translated) field $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$ let $E$ be the event that the fraction of $1 \leq j \leq k$ so that $G_{z,2^{-j}r}$ occurs is at least $q$. Then $\mathbf{P}[E^c] = O(e^{-bk})$.

body:
[Prop prop-critdens of arXiv:2604.14318, '\large The free energy of the interacting Bose gas:\\\medskip a variational description \\'] Fix $\beta\in(0,\infty)$. 
The map $\rho\mapsto\chi^{\ssup=}(\beta,\rho)$ is convex, and $\chi^{\ssup=}(\beta,\rho)\geq \chi^{\ssup\leq}(\beta,\rho)$.
There is a {\it critical particle density} $\rho_{\rm c}(\beta)\in(0,\infty]$ such that 
$$
\chi^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({=}})}}}(\beta,\rho)\begin{cases}=\chi^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\le}})}}}(\beta,\rho)&\mbox{for }\rho\leq \rho_{\rm c}(\beta),\\
>\chi^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\le}})}}}(\beta,\rho)&\mbox{for }\rho> \rho_{\rm c}(\beta).
\end{cases}
$$
In particular, for any $\rho\in (0,\rho_{\rm c}(\beta)]$, the free energy is given by the formula
\begin{equation}
-\beta f(\beta,\rho)= \overline q-\chi^{\ssup=}(\beta,\rho).
\end{equation}
Furthermore, there is another critical point $\widetilde\rho_{\rm c}(\beta)\in(0,\rho_{\rm c}(\beta)]$ such that the map $\rho\mapsto\chi^{\ssup =}(\beta,\rho)$ is strictly decreasing in $(0,\widetilde\rho_{\rm c}(\beta)]$ and constant  in $[\widetilde\rho_{\rm c}(\beta), \rho_{\rm c}(\beta)]$.
Moreover, for $\rho=\rho_{\rm c}(\beta)$ (if it is finite), there is an unconstrained minimizer $P\in{\mathcal P }_\theta$ of the map $P\mapsto {\rm h}(P\mid {{\tt Q}} )+\langle P,\Phi_\beta\rangle$ with $\langle P,{\mathfrak N}_U^{\ssup\ell}\rangle=\rho$, but not for any $\rho>\rho_{\rm c}(\beta)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Critical particle density, \cite{JK17}

body:
Own-work draft, status proof (unaudited): this is a proposed correction to the coefficient in arXiv2506.06501v2 Theorem E.2, not the theorem as printed. Let J>=2 and M>=1 be finite integers. Let f_m:R^d->R be convex differentiable functions with beta-Lipschitz gradients, beta>0, sharing a minimizer w_star. For each t=1,...,J and m, let g_(t,m):R^d->R be a deterministic convex differentiable surrogate. Suppose nu_t>=0 and, for every w,m,t, 0<=g_(t,m)(w)-g_(t,m)(w_star)<=f_m(w)-f_m(w_star)<=(1+nu_t*beta)*[g_(t,m)(w)-g_(t,m)(w_star)]. Take independent uniform task indices tau_1,...,tau_J in {1,...,M}, deterministic w_1, and deterministic finite steps eta_t>=nu_t. Let w_(t+1)=w_t-eta_t*grad g_(t,tau_t)(w_t), gbar_t=M^(-1)*sum_m g_(t,m), and choose deterministic weights 0<v_0<=v_1<=...<=v_J. Assume the expectations of the displayed gaps, gradient squares and iterate squared distances are finite. Define cplus_t=eta_t*v_t^2-(1+eta_t*beta)*(v_t-v_(t-1))*sum_(s=t)^J eta_s*v_s. Then sum_(t=1)^J cplus_t*E[gbar_t(w_t)-gbar_t(w_star)] <=v_0^2*||w_1-w_star||^2/2 +(1/2)*sum_(t=1)^J eta_t^2*v_t^2*E||grad g_(t,tau_t)(w_t)||^2. The plus sign is essential under these unrestricted-step hypotheses; the printed minus-sign version is false.
Finite-dimensional deterministic convex differentiable base and surrogate families with common minimizing gap comparisons as displayed.
Fixed iid uniform task law, deterministic monotone positive weights, steps eta_t>=nu_t>=0, finite expectations.

[Theorem 36 (Composite random-time peeking, upper-expectation form) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $\cP_0$ be a set of measures and $E=(E_t)$ a nonnegative process that is a $P$-supermartingale for every $P\in\cP_0$ with $E_0\le1$.
For a random time $\tau$, let $\Amart{\tau,P}$ and $\widehat P_P$ be the anticipation martingale and clock measure of $\tau$ under $P$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:surv-factor}). Writing $\overline{\E}_{\cP_0}[\cdot]:=\sup_{P\in\cP_0}\E_P[\cdot]$,
the composite peeking penalty $\overline{\cP}_\tau:=\log\overline{\E}_{\cP_0}[E_\tau]$ is the upper envelope $\overline{\cP}_\tau=\sup_{P\in\cP_0}\cP^P_\tau$ of the simple penalties $\cP^P_\tau:=\log\E_P[E_\tau]$, each of which is itself an identity: for every $P\in\cP_0$ with $0<\E_P[E_\tau]<\infty$ and every $Q\ll\widehat P_P$ with $Q(\{\Amart{\tau,P}_tE_t=0\})=0$,
\begin{equation}
  \cP^P_\tau=\E_Q[\log E_t]+\E_Q[\log \Amart{\tau,P}_t]-\KL(Q\|\widehat P_P)+\KL(Q\|Q^\star_P),
\end{equation}
with $\dd Q^\star_P/\dd\widehat P_P\propto \Amart{\tau,P}_t\,E_t$.
Hence $\overline{\E}_{\cP_0}[E_\tau]\le\exp\!\big(\sup_{P\in\cP_0}\cP^P_\tau\big)$, each simple penalty with its own correction $\E_Q[\log \Amart{\tau,P}_t]$ that vanishes iff $\tau$ is a (pseudo-)stopping time under $P$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:vanish}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Composite random-time peeking, upper-expectation form

[Thm thm2.2 of arXiv:2411.09407, 'Continuous flows driving Markov processes and multiplicative $L^p$-semigroups'] Let $\Phi=(\Phi_t)_{t\geqslant 0}$ be a semi-dynamical system on a Lusin measurable space $(E, {\mathcal B})$.
Then there exists a Luzin topology ${\mathcal T}$ on $E$ such that ${\mathcal B}={\mathcal B}(E)$ is the  Borel $\sigma$-algebra and $\Phi$ is a continuous flow with respect to this topology, 
such that  the map $x\longmapsto \Phi_t(x)$ is continuous on $E$ for all $t\geqslant 0$. 
For every finite measure $\lambda$ on $E$ and $\beta >0$ the capacity $c^\beta_\lambda$ is tight.

Let $Z$ and $Z_1,Z_2$ be stochastic processes taking values in $\mbb R^2$.

\[\al^\eps_A(Z_1,Z_2)=\int_{A}p_\eps\big(Z_1(r_1)-Z_2(r_2)\big)\d r.\]

body: In linear algebra, the singular value decomposition (SVD) is a factorization of a real or complex matrix into a rotation, followed by a scaling, followed by another rotation. It generalizes the eigendecomposition of a square normal matrix with an orthonormal eigenbasis to any $m\times n$ matrix. It is related to the polar decomposition, and is a common means for implementing low-rank approximation for matrices.

[Theorem th:fgl of arXiv:2411.03955, 'Large Deviations Inequalities for Unequal Probability Sampling Without Replacement\thanks{'] The procedures $\mathfrak{X}^{\ast }$ satisfy $\mathbb{P}\left[
i\in S\right] =kw^{i}$ for every $i$ in $[n]$, and
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb{P}\left[ \frac{1}{k}\left\vert S\cap A\right\vert \geq \alpha
+\delta \right] &\leq &\pi ^{\ast }(\eta ,\delta ,k)\text{\ \ and} \\
\mathbb{P}\left[ \frac{1}{k}\left\vert S\cap A\right\vert \leq \alpha
-\delta \right] &\leq &\pi ^{\ast }(\eta ,\delta ,k)
\end{eqnarray*}
for every set $A\subset \lbrack n]$ and $\delta \geq 0$, where $\alpha
:=\sum_{i\in A}w^{i}$ is the relative weight of $A$, and $\eta :=\alpha
-k\sum_{i\in A}(w^{i})^{2}\leq \alpha .$

[Lem partial_continuous of arXiv:2606.15339, 'Uniform integrability of the distance to the nearest leaf in random trees'] Let $\mathbf{P}$ denote the law of the local limit $\hat{\mathcal{T}}$ of $\mathcal{T}_n$ on the Polish space
$(\mathbb{T }_{\infty},\delta_{\infty})$, for a weight sequence of type~I, II or~III. Then
\[
\mathbf{P}\bigl(\{T\in\mathbb{T }_{\infty} : \partial \text{ is discontinuous at } T \}\bigr)=0,
\]
that is, $T\mapsto\partial(T)$ is $\mathbf{P}$-almost surely continuous.
