{"artifact_digest":"sha256:795b618bab79ffa26752a7159c4a514a6b84a9f0f8daa4357ff3ce683e0817bb","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/79/795b618bab79ffa26752a7159c4a514a6b84a9f0f8daa4357ff3ce683e0817bb.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:918cd3c546d66c2f7525a6b902166f5b62c3ae08f13f6c01f9aaccf300b49373","bundle_entry_key":"all-scale-flat","bundle_id":"population.t419-julia-dilation-operator-contraction-all-scale-flat-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA convergence and Julia operator dilation","draft":"w705/bundle_013.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-all-ranks-aspect-ratios-all-gaussian-scales-flat-spectrum-gd","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C025 v1: every Gaussian scale, every rank and aspect ratio, flat spectrum

Kind:narrowed. Target:1. Status:proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.

This application depends on the new unaudited C024 operator-norm contraction proof and the unaudited explicit C014 discrete boundedness proof. Both are included in full in the queued card. The single hardest dependency is C024's exact nonlinear orthogonal-dilation compression; this application does not replace it by an assumption of spectral monotonicity from loss descent. Known output-span invariance is credited to Zhang-Liu-Chen, arXiv:2502.01235, Theorem3.1/C.10. The sufficient-margin idea for continuous flow is attributed to Min-Tarmoun-Vidal-Mallada, arXiv:2105.06351, Corollary5. The discrete imbalance method is due to Du-Hu-Lee, arXiv:1806.00900, AppendixB ClaimB.1. None of those citations alone proves the present zero/Gaussian GD statement; novelty remains unresolved.

## Statement

Let r>=1, m,p>=r be arbitrary integers and Delta any real m-by-p matrix of rank exactly r, with all nonzero singular values equal to1. Let any s>0 and 0<rho<1. Define

 d=rho/2, a=d/(10r^(3/2)), b=sqrt(rp/d),
 Kbar=sqrt(r)(s^2 b^2+1+4sqrt(r)).

Initialize B0=0 and A0=sG where G is r-by-p with independent standard Gaussian entries. For any one fixed eta with

 0<eta<=1/(6Kbar+1),

ordinary simultaneous GD on ||BA-Delta||F^2/2 satisfies, with probability at least1-rho, for every integer t>=1,

 ||B_t A_t-Delta||F <=sqrt(r) exp[-eta^3 s^4 a^4(t-1)/(8Kbar)].

For every 0<eps<sqrt(r), a sufficient time is

 1+ceil[(8Kbar/(eta^3 s^4 a^4))log(sqrt(r)/eps)].

The success event and the fixed step are independent of requested accuracy. This covers every positive Gaussian scale, every rank and every input/output aspect ratio, including all proper bottlenecks m,p>r. It covers condition number1, not arbitrary target spectra. No expected-risk or finite-sample claim is included. The rate is deliberately conservative; independent proof audit and any novelty judgment remain pending.

## 1. Gaussian event

Write Delta=U V^T with orthonormal columns in U m-by-r and V p-by-r. By Gaussian rotation invariance H=G V has independent standard Gaussian entries. The event

 sigma_min(H)>=a, ||G||F<=b

has probability at least1-rho. For completeness, H is nonsingular almost surely. If sigma_min(H)<a then ||H^{-1}||F>1/a; at least one row has norm >1/(a sqrt(r)). Its reciprocal is the distance of the corresponding Gaussian column from the span of the remaining r-1 columns. Conditional on those columns that distance has distribution |N(0,1)|. A union bound and the normal density bound give probability at most r sqrt(2/pi)a sqrt(r)<d. Markov gives Pr[||G||F>b]<=rp/b^2=d. A union bound, without assuming the two events independent, proves the stated success probability. Fix any G on this event below.

## 2. Descent, bounded factors, and applicability of C024

Apply C014 with C=I, D=W=Delta, q0=r/2, J=||A0 A0^T||F+1<=s^2 b^2+1, R=2sqrt(r), K=sqrt(r)(J+2R)<=Kbar. The step condition in the statement implies eta<=1/(6K+1) and eta<=1/(1+r), since Kbar>=4r. Hence C014 proves, before invoking C024,

 q_next<=q-(eta/2)||grad q||F^2,
 ||B_t||F^2+||A_t||F^2<=Kbar,
 ||E_t||F<=sqrt(r), E_t=B_t A_t-Delta.

At every iterate, h_t=||B_t||op^2+||A_t||op^2<=Kbar and e_t=||E_t||op<=sqrt(r)<=Kbar/4. Therefore

 eta(e_t+h_t)<= (5Kbar/4)/(6Kbar+1)<1/2.

C024 applies at every iterate and proves ||E_(t+1)||op<=||E_t||op. This is a consequence of its explicit small-step contraction lemma, not a consequence of Frobenius loss descent alone. The factor bounds used to apply it were established independently of any margin or operator-norm monotonicity.

## 3. First-step margin and a uniformly nonsingular output factor

Because B0=0, A1=A0 and B1=eta Delta A0^T. Let L=A0^T A0. The initial factor bound gives eta||L||op<=1. Then

 E1=Delta(eta L-I),
 U^T E1 E1^T U=V^T(I-2eta L+eta^2 L^2)V
                  <=I-eta V^T L V
                  <=(1-eta s^2 a^2)I.

Here eta^2 L^2<=eta L is a scalar spectral inequality for the PSD matrix L, and V^T L V=(A0 V)^T(A0 V)>=s^2 a^2 I. The scalar eta s^2 a^2 is in (0,1), since a<=b and eta s^2 b^2<1. As col(E1) is contained in col(U),

 ||E1||op<=sqrt(1-eta s^2 a^2)<=1-eta s^2 a^2/2.

Put delta0=eta s^2 a^2/2>0. Section2 makes this margin persist for all t>=1. By the known invariant output span, B_t=U R_t for a square r-by-r R_t. Hence E_t=U(R_t A_t-V^T), and Weyl gives sigma_min(R_t A_t)>=1-||E_t||op>=delta0. Also

 sigma_min(R_t A_t)<=sigma_min(R_t)||A_t||op,

by testing the transposed product on a left minimum-singular vector of R_t. The factor bound therefore yields sigma_min(R_t)>=delta0/sqrt(Kbar). This deduction does not assume A_t has full input rank, and remains valid for p>r.

## 4. Frobenius contraction with the same step forever

The A gradient is R_t^T(R_t A_t-V^T), so

 ||grad q_t||F^2>=delta0^2 ||E_t||F^2/Kbar.

Together with section2 this gives

 ||E_(t+1)||F^2 <=[1-eta delta0^2/Kbar]||E_t||F^2.

The multiplier is in (0,1) under the displayed bounds. Iteration from t=1, using ||E1||F<=sqrt(r), and sqrt(1-x)<=exp(-x/2), gives the rate in the statement because eta delta0^2/(2Kbar)=eta^3 s^4 a^4/(8Kbar). No step change or accuracy-dependent safe step is used.

## Nonempty spectral interval and general scale normalization

The same argument also covers normalized rank-r targets Delta=U Lambda V^T with sigma1=1 and mu=sigmar satisfying mu>1-delta0, with all constants above unchanged. The first-step Loewner estimate becomes

 U^T E1 E1^T U <=(1-eta s^2 a^2)Lambda^2<=(1-eta s^2 a^2)I,

and needs no commutation of Lambda with V^T L V. q0<=r/2 gives the same factor and operator-contraction bounds. Set beta=mu-1+delta0>0; then for all t>=1 the Frobenius residual is bounded by sqrt(r)exp[-eta beta^2(t-1)/(2Kbar)]. Thus at each s>0 there is a nonempty condition-number interval 1<=kappa<1/(1-delta0), although its width may be very small. This does not prove arbitrary condition number at every scale.

For a flat target with nonzero singular value alpha>0, let s'=s/sqrt(alpha), Kbar'=sqrt(r)((s')^2 b^2+1+4sqrt(r)), and choose original eta<=1/[alpha(6Kbar'+1)]. Normalizing both factors by sqrt(alpha) and Delta by alpha gives step eta'=alpha eta. Consequently

 ||B_t A_t-Delta||F<=alpha sqrt(r)exp[-alpha eta^3 s^4 a^4(t-1)/(8Kbar')].

The nonnormalized formula is a change of variables, not a new algorithm. The main unresolved population range is arbitrary condition number across all scales. Positive-noise proper-bottleneck empirical optimization and statistical stopping remain separate gaps. This application and its C024 dependency are unaudited; prior work may already imply some or all of the stated family.


Full deterministic C014 component:
# T419-C014 v1: empirical GD boundedness with an initialization-dependent step

Kind: bound. Target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This is an explicit anisotropic version of the published Gram-imbalance/descent method, not a solution of Target 2. It proves a trajectory component without assuming the iterates are bounded. The prior source is Du-Hu-Lee, arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 2.2 and Appendix B, Claim B.1; its full convergence theorems have different initialization/step hypotheses. C009 already identifies the exact covariance metric and C010 the positive-noise empirical landscape.

## Statement

Let C be any real positive definite p-by-p matrix, D any real m-by-p matrix, and r>=1. Put lambda=lambda_min(C)>0, c=||C||op, ell=||D||op, W=D C^(-1), and

 q(B,A)=(1/2)||(BA-W) C^(1/2)||F^2,

with B m-by-r and A r-by-p. This is the empirical regression objective up to a constant when C=XX^T/n and D=ZX^T/n. Initialize at any finite deterministic factors B0,A0, and define

 q0=q(B0,A0), J=||A0 A0^T-B0^T B0||F+1,
 R=||W||F+sqrt(2q0/lambda),
 K=sqrt(r)(J+2R), L=6Kc+ell.

For any fixed

 0<eta<=min{1/(1+2q0),1/L},

simultaneous ordinary factor GD satisfies, for every integer t>=0,

 q_t<=q0,
 ||B_t||F^2+||A_t||F^2<=K,
 ||(A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t)-(A0 A0^T-B0^T B0)||F<=2eta q0<1,
 sum_(t>=0) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/eta.

In particular the gradient tends to zero, every accumulation point is critical, and for every integer T>=1,

 min_(0<=t<T) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/(eta T).

All constants are finite and computable from C,D and the initialization. There is no Gaussian assumption and no low-rank assumption on W. No iterate-convergence, saddle-avoidance or statistical-risk assertion is included.

## Exact identities and product/factor bounds

Let G=BA C-D. The two factor gradients are G_B=G A^T and G_A=B^T G. With E_t=A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t the first-order cross terms cancel exactly, giving

 E_(t+1)-E_t=eta^2(G_A G_A^T-G_B^T G_B),
 ||E_(t+1)-E_t||F<=eta^2(||G_A||F^2+||G_B||F^2).

This cancellation only uses dependence on BA and does not require isotropic C. Also

 (||B||F^2+||A||F^2)^2
 <=r [||AA^T-B^TB||F^2+4||BA||F^2].

To verify it, write P=B^TB,Q=AA^T. Scalar trace Cauchy-Schwarz gives (tr(P+Q))^2<=r tr((P+Q)^2), and cyclicity of trace gives tr((P+Q)^2)=||P-Q||F^2+4 tr(PQ), tr(PQ)=||BA||F^2. No commutation is assumed.

When q<=q0, positivity of C gives ||BA-W||F<=sqrt(2q0/lambda), hence ||BA||F<=R. If additionally ||E-E0||F<=1, then ||E||F<=J, so the preceding trace bound implies

 ||B||F^2+||A||F^2<=sqrt(r) sqrt(J^2+4R^2)<=K.

The initialization meets these conditions and therefore has pair norm at most sqrt(K).

## Descent established before closing the boundedness induction

Suppose at the current iterate the pair norm is at most sqrt(K), and preceding steps have valid descent inequalities. Then

 ||grad q||F<=||BA C-D||op sqrt(||B||F^2+||A||F^2)
             <=(Kc/2+ell)sqrt(K).

Because eta<=1/(6Kc+ell), the proposed next point has pair norm at most 2sqrt(K). The connecting segment also lies in that ball. On that ball the Hessian quadratic form in a perturbation (dB,dA) is

 ||(dB A+B dA) C^(1/2)||F^2+2<BA C-D,dB dA>.

Its absolute value is at most

 [c(||A||op^2+||B||op^2)+||BA C-D||op]
 times (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2)
 <=[4Kc+(2Kc+ell)] (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2).

Here the first summand uses Cauchy-Schwarz on dB A+B dA; the cross term uses |<G,dB dA>|<=||G||op||dB||F||dA||F. Thus the Hessian operator norm on the segment is at most L. Taylor's theorem along that segment proves

 q_next<=q-eta||grad q||F^2+(L eta^2/2)||grad q||F^2
        <=q-(eta/2)||grad q||F^2.

In particular q_next<=q0. Telescoping the descent inequalities, including the proposed step, and using q>=0 yields

 sum_(j=0)^t eta^2||grad q_j||F^2<=2eta q0
 <=2q0/(1+2q0)<1.

Summing the imbalance increments now proves ||E_next-E0||F<=2eta q0<1. The product/factor bound therefore puts the endpoint back in the smaller ball of pair radius sqrt(K). This closes the induction without assuming a bound before proving descent on the required larger segment. The q0=0 case is included: both gradients vanish, the sequence is constant, and all inequalities still hold.

## Consequences and exact remaining gap

Telescoping for every finite horizon gives the infinite summability bound. A nonnegative summable sequence tends to zero, so the gradients vanish. Bounded finite-dimensional factor pairs have convergent subsequences; gradient continuity makes every subsequential limit critical. The running-minimum bound follows by averaging the finite sum. These statements do not require that the entire sequence converges to one point.

For B0=0 and a Gaussian A0, this provides an allowed positive step after observing the initialization, conditional on every full-row-rank design. It does not supply a single positive step independent of the unbounded Gaussian initializer. C013 shows that unconditional expected-limit risk with such an initialization-independent fixed step can diverge even at rank one.

Combining this bound with the already verified empirical strict-saddle landscape C010 is insufficient to conclude global optimization. One must additionally show that the specified zero/Gaussian initialization does not approach a nonglobal critical point, with all hypotheses of a saddle-avoidance theorem checked for its lower-dimensional initial support and step rule. Vanishing gradients do not establish that. Even convergence almost surely would not by itself justify passing to expected population risk; a failure-tail/integrability or finite-stopping argument is separately required. The usual full-ambient absolutely-continuous random-initialization theorem cannot simply be cited for the plane B0=0.

Independent reviewer audit and any novelty assessment remain pending. This is a deterministic bound recorded as a component, not an advertised new theorem or a completed target.


Full C024 contraction dependency:
# T419-C024 v2: small-step operator-norm residual contraction

Kind:moved. Target:1. Status:proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.

## Statement

Let E be any real m-by-p matrix, B any m-by-r matrix and A any r-by-p matrix. Set e=||E||op and h=||B||op^2+||A||op^2. For any eta>0 with eta(e+h)<=1/2, put

 Phi(E,B,A)=E-eta(BB^T E+E A^T A)+eta^2 E A^T B^T E.

Then ||Phi(E,B,A)||op<=||E||op. In particular, when E=BA-Delta, Phi is exactly the residual after one simultaneous GD step for ||BA-Delta||F^2/2. No rank assumption, Gaussian assumption, balance or commutation is required. The lemma gives a sufficient small-step condition, not an optimal one. It does not claim spectral monotonicity at an arbitrary loss-decreasing step.

The hardest point is that orthogonal dilation commutes with this particular nonlinear update after compression. The proof explicitly checks the quadratic term. The algebraic dilation is the classical Julia/Halmos construction; its primary provenance is P. L. Robinson, "Julia operators and Halmos dilations", arXiv:1803.09329, Theorem0 p.1 and Theorem1 p.2. The rectangular block here is the Julia operator with its column blocks switched; Theorem2 concerns the square-space special case. The construction and its properties are proved below from an SVD rather than assumed from a named theorem. The primary source gives the classical dilation, not this GD contraction. Literature overlap and independent correctness remain unaudited.

## 1. Orthogonal residuals

First suppose m=p=N and E=eQ for an orthogonal N-by-N matrix Q, with e>0. Multiplying Phi/e on the right by Q^T gives

 (Phi/e)Q^T=I-eta(DD^T+CC^T)+eta^2 e C D^T,

where D=B and C=Q A^T. Indeed E A^T B^T E/e=e Q A^T B^T Q, which becomes e C D^T after right multiplication by Q^T. This checks the order of the quadratic term.

Let W=[D C] be N-by-2r and set

 H = [[I_r,0],[-eta e I_r,I_r]].

The preceding matrix equals Z=I-eta W H W^T. Direct expansion gives

 I-Z^T Z = eta W[H+H^T-eta H^T W^T W H]W^T.

Now ||W||op^2<=||D||op^2+||C||op^2=h,

 H+H^T >=(2-eta e)I, and ||H||op<=1+eta e.

The first bound follows either from the 2-by-2 scalar block eigenvalues 2+eta e and 2-eta e, or the quadratic-form inequality 2|x^T y|<=||x||^2+||y||^2. The second follows by writing H=I+N, where the sole nonzero off-diagonal block of N has operator norm eta e. Consequently

 H+H^T-eta H^T W^T W H
 >=[2-eta e-eta h(1+eta e)^2]I
 >=[2-1/2-(1/2)(3/2)^2]I
 =(3/8)I>=0.

Only eta e<=1/2 and eta h<=1/2 are used in this estimate; they follow from the stated sufficient condition. It follows that Z^T Z<=I and ||Z||op<=1. Right multiplication by Q^T preserves the norm, so ||Phi||op<=e in this orthogonal case.

## 2. Explicit orthogonal dilation of an arbitrary rectangular contraction

Suppose e>0 and let F=E/e, so ||F||op<=1. The matrices I_m-FF^T and I_p-F^TF are positive semidefinite. Their positive semidefinite square roots define the (m+p)-by-(p+m) real matrix

 Q = [[F, (I_m-FF^T)^(1/2)],[(I_p-F^TF)^(1/2),-F^T]].

This is square because m+p=p+m. It is orthogonal. For a direct verification, take an SVD F=U Sigma V^T. It gives the exact intertwining identity

 F(I_p-F^TF)^(1/2)=(I_m-FF^T)^(1/2)F,

since each paired singular direction contributes the scalar sigma_i sqrt(1-sigma_i^2) on both sides, and the unmatched zero singular directions contribute zero. Multiplying Q Q^T therefore gives identity diagonal blocks and zero cross blocks. Thus Q Q^T=I, which for a finite square real matrix also implies Q^T Q=I. In particular the upper-left m-by-p compression of eQ is E. This proof also covers rectangular F with singular value1; no inverse of a defect square root is used.

## 3. Compression preserves the nonlinear update

Use the orthogonal residual Etilde=eQ, the padded factor Btilde=[B;0_(p-by-r)], and Atilde=[A,0_(r-by-m)]. These are compatible factors in the enlarged N=m+p dimensional problem, with ||Btilde||op=||B||op and ||Atilde||op=||A||op. The step condition is unchanged, so section1 gives ||Phi(Etilde,Btilde,Atilde)||op<=e.

Consider its first m rows and first p columns. The linear terms compress to BB^T E and E A^T A because Btilde Btilde^T and Atilde^T Atilde are zero off their leading diagonal blocks. For the quadratic term, the first m rows of Etilde Atilde^T equal E A^T, and the first p columns of Btilde^T Etilde equal B^T E. Hence the leading m-by-p block of

 Etilde Atilde^T Btilde^T Etilde

is exactly E A^T B^T E, not a block contaminated by the defect square roots. Therefore the full compressed residual is exactly Phi(E,B,A). Compression by orthogonal coordinate projections cannot increase operator norm, proving the lemma. If e=0, every term of Phi is zero, completing the missing degenerate case.

## Relation to GD and limitations

Multiplication of B_next=B-eta E A^T and A_next=A-eta B^T E gives the displayed Phi with its positive quadratic term. Thus the lemma applies to ordinary simultaneous GD without replacing it by alternating updates, a continuous flow, or a split contraction. At larger steps the proof does not give monotonicity. It provides no statistical-risk or convergence theorem without a separate factor bound and positive-margin argument. The application is saved separately as C025. body:
[Prop 38 of arXiv:2607.28578, 'On two differing geometric descriptions of the passage from microscopy to macroscopy in Ma'] Let $\Lop_q$ be uniformly elliptic on the connected closed manifold $M$, let $\alpha>0$, and let $\mathcal G_{\alpha,m}=\Ran(\alpha-\Lop_q)^{-m/2}$ with graph norm
	\[
		\|u\|_{\mathcal G_{\alpha,m}}=\|(\alpha-\Lop_q)^{m/2}u\|_{L^2(q)}.
	\]
	If $m>d/2+1$, then $\mathcal G_{\alpha,m}\hookrightarrow C^1(M)$ and is a scalar reproducing kernel Hilbert space; its gradient image, furnished with the quotient norm by constant potentials, is a Hilbert space of continuous vector fields with continuous point evaluation. If the $C^1$ vector-field embedding in \eqref{kernel-inclusion-eq} is required, it is sufficient to assume $m>d/2+2$. The lower threshold gives a distributional interpretation of the continuity operator.

body:
[Proposition 4.8 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] For every $\eps,\ka>0$,
the operator $H_{\ka,\eps}$ is self-adjoint on $L^2(D)$.
Its spectrum $\la_1(H_{\ka,\eps})\leq\la_2(H_{\ka,\eps})\leq\cdots$ is purely discrete, bounded below, and has no accumulation point.
Moreover, the corresponding eigenfunctions $\psi_1(H_{\ka,\eps}),\psi_2(H_{\ka,\eps}),\ldots$
form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(D)$. Finally, for any $f\in L^2(D)$,
\begin{align}

\mr e^{-t H_{\ka,\eps}}f=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\mr e^{-t\la_n(H_{\ka,\eps})}\big\langle\psi_n(H_{\ka,\eps}),f\big\rangle\psi_n(H_{\ka,\eps}).
\end{align}

body:
[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.00108, 'The double sphere solution in the liquid drop model'] There exists $V_0>0$ such that, for every
		\[
		0<V<V_0,
		\]
		the liquid drop energy functional admits a smooth embedded critical point
		$\Omega_V$ of volume $V$.
		
		As $V\to0$, the boundary $\partial\Omega_V$ consists of two nearly
		spherical lobes connected by a single catenoidal neck. More precisely,
		
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item
			each lobe is a normal graph over the boundary of a sphere of volume
			\[
			\frac V2+o(V),
			\]
			and away from the neck the convergence is smooth;
			
			\item
			after rescaling by the neck scale, the connecting region converges in
			$C^\infty_{\rm loc}$ to the standard catenoid;
			
			\item
			the neck is formed at the intermediate scale
			\[
			r\sim V^{4/3}.
			\]
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main Theorem

body:
[Lem 7 (Concatenation of absorbed one-step weak solutions) of arXiv:2607.28078, '2607.28078'] Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open and $\overline{D}$ compact, let $0=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_N=T$, and put $\varphi(t):=s_i$ for $t\in[s_i,s_{i+1})$.  Let $b$ and $\sigma$ be jointly Borel measurable. For a continuous path $\xi$ on $[0,T]$, write
\[
\tau_D(\xi):=\inf\{t\in[0,T]:\xi(t)\notin D\},
\]
where the infimum of the empty set is $\infty$. Suppose that, for every $i\in\{0,\cdots,N-1\}$, $y\in\overline D$, and every $\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ supported by $\overline D$, there is a weak solution $(Y^i,B^i)$ on $[s_i,s_{i+1}]$ of the absorbed frozen-law equation
\begin{equation}
Y^i(t)=y+\int_{s_i}^t\mathbf 1_{\{r<\tau^i_D(Y^i)\}}b\bigl(r,Y^i(r),\mu\bigr)dr+\int_{s_i}^t\mathbf 1_{\{r<\tau^i_D(Y^i)\}}\sigma\bigl(r,Y^i(r),\mu\bigr)\,dB^i(r),
\,\,t\in[s_i,s_{i+1}].
\end{equation}
The solution is absorbed after $\tau^i_D(Y^i):=\inf\{t\in[s_i,s_{i+1}]:Y^i(t)\notin D\}$ and has a finite second moment.
Then the joint laws of these stopped solutions admit a universally measurable selection in $(y,\mu)$.  Consequently, every initial law $\nu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ supported by $\overline D$ admits a concatenation $(X,B)$ on a stochastic basis $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_t\},\mathbb{P})$ such that $B$ is a Brownian motion, $\mathcal L_{X(0)}=\nu_0$, and, with $\tau_D:=\inf\{t\in[0,T]:X(t)\notin D\}$, the process $X$ is absorbed after $\tau_D$ and satisfies
\begin{equation}
X(t)=X(0)+\int_0^t\mathbf1_{\{r<\tau_D\}}b\bigl(r,X(r),\mathcal L_{X(\varphi(r))}\bigr)dr+\int_0^t\mathbf1_{\{r<\tau_D\}}\sigma\bigl(r,X(r),\mathcal L_{X(\varphi(r))}\bigr)dB(r).
\end{equation}

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.21729, 'Guidance for Prior Change via Density Ratio Estimation'] Define the prior ratio
$
r(\rvtheta_0)
=
\frac{q(\rvtheta_0)}
     {p(\rvtheta_0)}.
$
Further assume that the same forward diffusion process
$p(\rvtheta_t \mid \rvtheta_0)$
is applied under both priors.
Then, for any measurable and integrable function
$f(\rvtheta_t, \rvx, t)$,

\begin{equation}
\E_{q(\rvtheta_t,\rvx)}
[f(\rvtheta_t, \rvx, t)]
=
\E_{p(\rvtheta_t,\rvtheta_0,\rvx)}
\left[
r(\rvtheta_0)
f(\rvtheta_t, \rvx, t)
\right].

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition pr:hf_compactness of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Let $(W,d_W)$ be a compact metric space. Suppose that $\mathcal {K}^W$ is a collection of non-empty compact subsets $K \subseteq W$ each equipped with a continuous function $f\colon K \to Y$. Suppose that
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
  \item There exist $0_Y \in Y$ and $M \in (0,\infty)$ such that $\sup_{x \in K} d_Y(f(x),0_Y) \leq M$ for all $(K,f) \in \mathcal {K}^W$.
  \item For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ so that $d(x,y) < \delta$ implies $d_Y(f(x),f(y)) < \varepsilon$ for all $(K,f) \in \mathcal {K}^W$.
 \end{enumerate}
 Then $\mathcal {K}^W$ is relatively compact with respect to the metric $d_\infty$.

body: [Lemma 3.1 (Hoeffding-Type Bounds for Exchangeable Random Variables) of arXiv:2603.10190, 'Hoeffding-Type Concentration Bounds for Exchangeabl'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. Let $(X_{m})_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an infinitely exchangeable sequence of $[0,1]$ -valued random variables, and let $\rho$ be its de Finetti mixing measure. Define $\mu(q)\coloneqq\int_{[0,1]}xq(\mathrm{d}x),\qquad\tilde{\mu}_{+}\coloneqq\sup_{q\in\operatorname{supp}(\rho)}\mu(q),\qquad\tilde{\mu}_{-}\coloneqq\inf_{q\in\operatorname{supp}(\rho)}\mu(q).$ For $M\in\mathbb{N}$, set $\bar{X}_{M}\coloneqq\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}X_{m}$. Then, for every $M\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $t>0$, $\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left(\bar{X}_{M}-\tilde{\mu}_{+}\geq t\right)$ $\displaystyle\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}},\qquad\mathbb{P}\left(\tilde{\mu}_{-}-\bar{X}_{M}\geq t\right)\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}}.$ (3.1)

[Cor cor_SlepianPosCorr of arXiv:2608.17463, 'Persistence probabilities of fractional L\'evy fields indexed by hyperbolic space and othe'] Let $(E,d)$ be a metric space and let $(Y_t)_{t\in E}$ denote a real-valued, separable, centred Gaussian process such that $\mathbb{E}\left[Y_s Y_t\right] \geq 0$, $\forall s,t\in E$.
    Let $f: E\to \mathbb{R}$ be a measurable function that is continuous except for possibly countably many points. Let $E = A \cup B$. Then
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{P}\left(Y_t \leq f(t) ~ \forall t\in E\right) \quad \geq \quad \mathbb{P}\left(Y_t \leq f(t) ~ \forall t\in A\right) \cdot \mathbb{P}\left(Y_t \leq f(t) ~ \forall t\in B\right).
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor cor_SlepianPosCorr of arXiv:2608.17463

[Lemma lem:sparsify of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let $a_1,\dots,a_s$ lie in a Hilbert space, let $q$ be a probability vector
with full support $s$, and let
$V_q=\sum_iq_i\lVert a_i-\bar a_q\rVert^2$ where $\bar a_q=\sum_iq_ia_i$. For
every $1\le k\le s$ there is a probability vector $\lambda$ with
$|\operatorname{supp}\lambda|\le k$ and
\[
  \Bigl\lVert\,\sum_i\lambda_ia_i-\bar a_q\Bigr\rVert^2
  \ \le\ \frac{s-k}{k(s-1)}\,V_q .

body:
[Defn def:-1 of arXiv:2411.13403, 'Path weighting method for spot sensitivities and its variance reduction'] A function $f(x),\;x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is said to
have generalised derivatives in $L^{2}$, if for each $i$ there exists
a $C_{i}>0$ such that 
\[
\Big|\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}f(x)\partial_{i}g(x)dx\big]\vert\le C_{i}\Big(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}|\partial_{i}g(x)|^{2}dx\Big)^{1/2}
\]
for any $g\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ with compact support. By
the Riesz representation theorem, this is equivalent to the existence
of $\partial_{i}f\in L^{2}$ such that
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}f(x)\partial_{i}g(x)dx=-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\partial_{i}f(x)g(x)dx
\]
for any $g\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ with compact support.
title: Defn def:-1 of arXiv:2411.13403

[Lem ProjNormLinear of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $A:\mathbb{R}^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$
be a linear map, where $\mathbb{R}^2$ is equipped with the standard Euclidean norm. Let $\hat{A}:\left(\mathbb{R}^{2}\right)^{\otimes n}\rightarrow\left(\mathbb{R}^{2}\right)^{\otimes n}$
be the unique linear map such that 
\[
\hat{A}\left(v_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n}\right)=Av_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes Av_{n}.
\]
Then one has
\[
\Vert\hat{A}\left(w\right)\Vert\leqslant\Vert A\Vert_{\mathrm{op}}^{n}\Vert w\Vert
\]for all $w\in\left(\mathbb{R}^{2}\right)^{\otimes n}.$ Here $\|A\|_{\rm op}$ denotes the operator norm of $A$ and the tensor products are all equipped with the projective tensor norm.
title: Lem ProjNormLinear of arXiv:2506.18207

[Lemma lem-useful-fact of arXiv:2606.28631, '\Large \bf On the maximal displacement of subcritical branching random walks with stretche'] Let $\ell$ be a slowly varying function.
		
		\begin{itemize}
			\item[(i)] For any $0<z_1\leq z_2$, 
			$
			\lim_{x \to +\infty} \sup_{ y\in [z_1, z_2]} \big|  \ell(xy)/\ell(x) - 1\big| =0.
			$
			
			\item[(ii)] For any $A > 1$ and $\delta > 0$, there exists $K(A, \delta)$ such that
			\[
			\frac{\ell(y)}{\ell(x)} \leq A \max\left\{(y/x)^\delta, (y/x)^{-\delta}\right\} \quad \text{for all } x, y \geq K(A, \delta).
			\]
			Consequently, for any $\delta > 0$, we have
			\[
			x^{-\delta} \lesssim_\delta \ell(x) \lesssim_\delta x^{\delta}.
			\]
		\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem-useful-fact of arXiv:2606.28631

[Lemma lem:loop-F-bound of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j_0$ be a
sufficiently large integer.  
Let  
$\Psi_0$ be the initialising state with
$j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$ and $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$.  
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be  
the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following statement holds  for
every $t \geq  \tau_0+2$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-2}} = \textup{filling}$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} = \textup{refilling}$, and $j = j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.
Conditioned on $\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} $,
for all $k\in \Upsilon_{j+1,\geq j^2}$
and all 
$t'$ in the range 
$t-2 \leq t' < \mathrm{exit}(t-1)$, 
$F_k^{\psi_{t'}}(t'+1) \geq \min\{F_k^{\psi_{t-2}}(t-1),\mu_k^{\overline{\gamma}}\} - 2 \lambda(t'-t+2)$.

[Lemma l:killed of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $E$ be some Borel set of ${\mathbb R}$ and $\mathcal S=(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{(a,r)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}}$ be a collection of continuous processes. 
    For $(a,r)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}$, we let $\varphi(a,r):=\inf\{x \in E\cap (r,\infty)\,:\, \mathcal S_{r,x}(a) =0\}$. We suppose that 
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item for each fixed $(a,r)$, the process $(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)$ is the strong solution of (equation eq:BESQflow vary of the paper) up to time $\varphi(a,r)$. 
        \item Almost surely,
        \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
            \item for all $r\in {\mathbb R}$ and $a\ge 0$, $\mathcal S_{r,r}(a)=a$,
            \item for all $a\ge 0$ and  $r\le x<\varphi(a,r)$, the map $a' \mapsto \mathcal S_{r,x}(a')$ is c\`adl\`ag at $a$,
            \item for any  $a\ge 0$ and $r\le x \le y <\varphi(a,r)$, $y<\varphi(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),x)$ and $\mathcal S_{r,y}(a)=\mathcal S_{x,y}\circ \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)$,
            \item for all $r\ge 0$, $a\ge 0$ and $x\ge \varphi(a,r)$, $\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal S$ is a ${\rm BESQ}(\overline{\delta})$ flow killed on $E$ driven by $\mathcal W$.

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2608.30212, 'A Painlev\'e equation for the H\"ormander-Bernhardsson constant'] Let $k$ be even, $c\in J_{k,0}$, $c\ge 0$. Each function $\zeta =\pm  x_\ell$ satisfies the differential equation
\[
\dot{\zeta} = F(\zeta, c)
\]
with 
\[
F(\zeta,c) = \frac{\beta_k(c)}{c} \frac{\zeta (\zeta^2-1)}{\zeta^2 - \beta_k(c)}
\]
and
\[
\beta_k(c) = \frac{c\dot{h}_k(c)}{(2k+1) h_k(c)} = \frac{ cQ_{k,c}(0)^2}{2Q_{k,c}(1) Q_{k,c}(-1) + cQ_{k,c}(0)^2}
\]
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2608.30212, 'A Painlev\'e equation for the H\"ormander-Bernhardsson const'

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.00087, 'Translational tiles without spectra\\ in finite abelian $p$-groups'] Let $H$ be a finite abelian group.  Suppose $K\subset H$ has a spectrum
$E\subset\widehat H$ but does not tile $H$.  Suppose also that
\[
 E\oplus T_0=\widehat H,
 \qquad E\oplus T_1=\widehat H,
\]
and that for every $d\in(K-K)\setminus\{0\}$,
\begin{equation}
 \bigl|\widehat{\1_{T_0}}(d)\bigr|
 \ne
 \bigl|\widehat{\1_{T_1}}(d)\bigr|.
\end{equation}
Then
\[
 \Gamma=(T_0\times\{0\})\cup(T_1\times\{1\})
 \subset\widehat H\times\Z_2
\]
tiles $\widehat H\times\Z_2$ and is not spectral.

[Theorem thm-freeenergy of arXiv:2604.14318, '\large The free energy of the interacting Bose gas:\\\medskip a variational description \\'] Assume $\beta, \rho\in(0,\infty)$ to be fixed and suppose that $v$ satisfies Assumption (V). Fix a sequence of centred boxes $\Lambda_N\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\lim_{N\to\infty}|\Lambda_N|/N=1/\rho$. We partition (up to boundary elements) $\Lambda_N=\bigcup_{z\in Z_{N,R}}W_z $ into the subboxes $W_z=z+W=z+[-R,R]^d$ with  $Z_{N,R}\subset 2R\mathbb{Z}^d$. Then, in the limit as $N\to\infty$, followed by $R\to\infty$, the pair $\frac 1{|\Lambda_N|}(\mathfrak N_{\Lambda_N}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\ell, R}})}}},\mathfrak N_{\Lambda_N}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\ell, \neg R}})}}})$ satisfies under the transformed measure $\widehat{\tt Q }^{\ssup{\Lambda_N,{\rm bc}}}$ defined in (equation transformedmeasure of the paper) a large-deviations principle on the set $\{(\rho_1,\rho_2)\in[0,\infty)^2\colon \rho_1+\rho_2=\rho\}$ with continuous and convex rate function $(\rho_1,\rho_2)\mapsto \chi(\rho_1,\rho_2)-\overline \chi(\rho)$, where $\overline \chi(\rho)=\inf_{\rho_1+\rho_2=\rho}\chi(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ and
\begin{equation}
	\chi(\rho_1,\rho_2)\vcentcolon= \inf\Big\{{\rm h}^{\ssup{{\mathcal L },{\mathcal S }}}(P)+\langle F_U,P\rangle\colon 
	P\in {\mathcal M }_1^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\rm s}})}}}({\mathcal L }\times {\mathcal S }), \langle {\mathfrak N}_U^{\ssup {\ell,{\mathcal L }}},P\rangle=\rho_1 , \langle {\mathfrak N}_U^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\ell,{\mathcal S }}})}}},P\rangle=\rho_2\Big\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Explicit formula for constrained free energy

[Lemma concentration of arXiv:2411.04322, 'Bounding Hellinger Distance with Stein's Method'] If $S$ has a Lebesgue density, then, for all $u\in\mathbb{R}$,

|\sqrt{\mbb{P}(S > u)} - \sqrt{\Phi^c(u)}|
    \vee
|\sqrt{\mbb{P}(|S| > u)} - \sqrt{2\Phi^c(u)}|
&\leq
\sqrt{2}H(S,Z).
\end{talign} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \leq j \leq i \leq m}
  \sum_{r \leq a_i} \sum_{r' \leq a_j}
  \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]

For ANY nonempty set E of K inputs with 2K<sqrt(N), put h=g(1-2*1_E) and define the Boolean selector F(y,+1)=g(y), F(y,-1)=h(y). With base-2 entropy, I_t(F)=K/N. [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2603.26936, 'Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model'] Let $M$ be any compact manifold and $W=W_{\alpha,\rho}$ be the colored noise of Definition~\ref{def: G_alpha etc}. For any $\alpha>{(d-2)}/{2}$ and any finite measure $\mu$ on $M$, equation~\eqref{eq: SHE} admits a random field solution $\{u(t,x)\}_{t>0,x\in M}$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def: SHE mild}. The solution is $L^p(\Omega)$-continuous for all $p\geq2$ and
     there exist constants $C, \theta>0$, depending on $\alpha,\beta$ and $p$, such that
    \[
    \E[|u(t,x)|^p]^{\frac{1}{p}}
    \leq CJ_\mu(t,x)e^{\theta t}.
    \]
    Here $J_\mu(t,x):=\int_M P_t(x,y) \mu(dy)$ is the homogeneous solution to the heat equation starting from $\mu$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:continuum-value-selfsimilar of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] For every $T>0$ and every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
		\[
			\mathcal U(T,x)\stackrel d= T^{(4-d)/4}\mathcal U(1,0)\, .

		\[

			=
			T^{p(4-d)/4}\mathbb{E}\mathcal U(1,0)^p\, ,
			\qquad
			0<\mathbb{E}\mathcal U(1,0)^p<\infty \, .
		\]

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2511.01245, 'A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain'] For any even integer $m$, any $n \ge m$, and any two subsets $S, S' \subseteq \binom{[n]}{m}$ with $|S \cap S'| = \ell$, let $\overline{f_S} = \frac{f_S}{\langle f_S, f_S \rangle^{1/2}}$ and $\overline{f_{S'}} = \frac{f_S'}{\langle f_S', f_S' \rangle^{1/2}}$ be the $\ell^2(\pi)$-normalized vectors for $S$ and $S'$. Then
\[
    \langle \overline{f_S}, \overline{f_{S'}} \rangle = \frac{1}{\binom{2m+1-\ell}{m+1}}.
\]
Furthermore, for any even integer $m \le n$ and any $S \subseteq \binom{[n]}{m}$,
\[
    \langle f_S, f_S \rangle = \frac{1}{m+1} \binom{2m}{m}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $C\geq 1$, $\varepsilon > 0 $, there is $\delta > 0 $ such that the following holds. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra equipped with an inner product, $\vv_1, \ldots , \vv_n \in \mathfrak{g}$ an orthonormal basis, and assume 
    \[
          \Vert [\xx,\yy] \Vert \leq C \Vert \xx \Vert \Vert \yy \Vert   
    \]   
    for all $\xx ,\yy \in \mathfrak{g}$. Then for each $\ww \in \mathfrak{g}$ with $\Vert \ww \Vert < \delta $, there are $t_1, \ldots , t_k \in ( - \varepsilon , \varepsilon ) $ with 
    \[   \exp (\ww )  = \exp (t_1 \vv _1) \cdots \exp (t_k \vv _n )  \in G    \]
    for any Lie group $G$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. In fact, one can take $\delta  : = \min \{ \tfrac{\varepsilon}{4}, \tfrac{1}{64 n^2 C } \} $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.30990

$p/m\to c\in(0,\infty)$, and
\begin{equation}
  \min(d,n-d)=o(n).

Then $\operatorname{ESD}(S_n)$ converges almost surely to the ordinary MP law. Moreover,
(equation eq:unit-degree of the paper) is necessary and sufficient for the uniform

\[

\]

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try to prove the o(n) range bound via the excess-visits argument of Florescu-Levine-Peres in reverse. Result: FLP prove the range is at least of order n^{2/3} using the fact that a rotor walk that visits a site k times exits it in each direction about k/4 times, so the walk's displacement is controlled by the 'rotor field' which is a bounded perturbation of a divergence-free field; the upper bound o(n) would follow if the walk cannot be transient with positive density of new sites per step, i.e. if the visited set has a hole-filling property. A rigorous observation: if the walk visits each site of its range at least twice on average (i.e. range <= n/2), the argument via the odometer shows that the exit counts balance in each direction up to an error bounded by 1 per site, so the walk's position is the sum of a bounded-per-site error, giving |X_n| <= C sqrt(range) log ... I did not close this. Another route: the rotor walk with uniform rotors is a deterministic walk in a random medium; transience would require the walk to escape to infinity through a set of sites each visited a bounded number of times, and on Z^2 an escaping path visiting each site O(1) times forces the rotor field along the path to point outward consistently, an event of probability 0 for i.i.d. rotors only if the path is a.s. determined... circular. No result; the o(n) reduction stands as the sharpest known route. Obstruction: No upper bound on the range of rotor walk on Z^2 better than n.

For integers a,b not both zero, there exist integers x,y such that ax+by=gcd(a,b). More generally, the integers representable as ax+by are exactly the multiples of gcd(a,b).

Consequently, for integers a,b not both zero, gcd(a,b) is the least positive integer of the form ax+by with x,y integers.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Mixing of gap-jump exclusion on a discrete circle structural calculation Result: For m=1 the spectrum is exactly accessible. From occupied position x, any chosen different site y becomes the new position regardless of direction, and choosing x leaves it there. Thus every step produces the uniform law on K sites: P(x,y)=1/K. The nonconstant eigenvalues are0, tau2=1 and the discrete mixing time is one. This confirms K-independence in the simplest sector but contains no information about the m^3 growth. Check: The direction contributes no factor1/2 because there is only one particle and either direction encounters that same particle. Treating the rule as nearest-neighbor exclusion would incorrectly predict a K^2 relaxation time. Obstruction: With several particles the moved particle is chosen by the entire gap geometry. The obvious common-site common-direction coupling can retain a last disagreement for a long time, and no uniform sharp coalescence estimate has been obtained.

[Definition 15 of arXiv:2609.02169, '2609.02169'] Let $(B,\Theta)$ be an indecomposable principally polarized abelian
surface and let $C\subset B$ be a smooth symmetric theta divisor.  A
point $0\ne t\in B[3]$ is \emph{good} (with respect to $C$) if
$t\notin[2]_B(C)$.  Equivalently, there is no $x\in C$ with $2x=t$.
Because two symmetric theta divisors differ by a two-torsion translation,
the condition is independent of the chosen symmetric representative.
title: Definition 15 of arXiv:2609.02169

[Lemma 3 (Uniform height-dependent survival) of arXiv:2609.02257, 'Aperiodic random walks: uniform estimates, local limits and invariance principles'] There is a constant \(C>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\)
and all \(n,H\in\Z_{\ge0}\),
\begin{equation}
 \Pp(\tau_{N,H}>n)
 \le C\min\left\{1,\frac{H+1}{\sqrt{n+1}}\right\}.
 
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds for the dual array.

body:
[Prop 10 (Distinct maximal test curves with identical contact filtrations) of arXiv:2609.03296, 'Nonuniqueness of Model Potentials and Weak Geodesic Rays'] Let \(\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}\) be normalized as in
Setup~\ref{setup:sphere}, and let \(b_\rho\) be the cap model of
Proposition~\ref{prop:cap-models}. There exist
\[
 0<\delta<s_0^2<T^2<1,\qquad \epsilon>0,
\]
and distinct maximal test curves
\((\psi_\tau)_{\tau\in\RR}\) and
\((\theta_\tau)_{\tau\in\RR}\) on
\((\CP^1,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}})\) whose zero-contact sets agree literally for
every \(\tau\). More precisely,
\[
 \psi_\tau=\theta_\tau=0\quad(\tau\leq0),\qquad
 \psi_\tau=b_{\tau^2}\quad(0<\tau\leq T),
\]
\[
 \psi_\tau=\theta_\tau=-\infty\quad(\tau>T),
\]
and
\[
 \theta_\tau=b_{\tau^2}\quad(0<\tau\leq s_0).
\]
For \(s_0<\tau\leq T\), the function \(\theta_\tau\) is a normalized
positive-mass model potential satisfying
\[
 \{\theta_\tau=0\}=\{b_{\tau^2}=0\}=C_{\tau^2}.
\]
For every \(x\in\CP^1\), both parameter functions
\(\tau\mapsto\psi_\tau(x)\) and
\(\tau\mapsto\theta_\tau(x)\) are upper semicontinuous, concave, and
decreasing. The two curves are distinct for every
\(\tau\in(s_0,T]\).

body:
[Proposition 132 (Closed response relation, unbounded recovery, and genuine compression) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Regard
\[
 \mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}
 \subset\mathbb S_{\cP}^2\times\mathbb H_{\cP}^2
\]
as the closed linear relation obtained from the raw testing relation.  Its
multivalued part is
\[
 \operatorname{mul}\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}
 :=\{Z:(0,Z)\in\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}\}
 =\mathcal N_Q^{\rm vert}.
\]

\emph{Closability and single-valued closed recovery.}  The following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item $\mathcal N_Q^{\rm vert}=\{0\}$;
\item the closure of the raw covariance-differential relation is the graph of
a single-valued operator;
\item the raw covariance-differential relation is closable as an operator from
$\mathbb S_{\cP}^2$ to $\mathbb H_{\cP}^2$;
\item there is a unique closed linear operator
\[
 D_Q^{\rm cl}:\operatorname{Dom}(D_Q^{\rm cl})
 \subset\mathbb S_{\cP}^2\longrightarrow\mathbb H_{\cP}^2
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}=\operatorname{Graph}(D_Q^{\rm cl}),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Dom}(D_Q^{\rm cl})
 =\pi_Y(\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold, write $D_Q:=D_Q^{\rm cl}$.

\emph{Continuous compression in the inherited value topology.}  Under these
equivalent conditions, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item the inverse graph map
\[
 J_Q:\operatorname{Dom}(D_Q)\longrightarrow\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2},
 \qquad J_QY=(Y,D_QY),
\]
is continuous when the domain carries the topology inherited from
$\mathbb S_{\cP}^2$;
\item $D_Q:\operatorname{Dom}(D_Q)\to\mathbb H_{\cP}^2$ is continuous for that
value topology;
\item whenever $Y^n,Y\in\operatorname{Dom}(D_Q)$ and
$Y^n\to Y$ in $\mathbb S_{\cP}^2$, one has
$D_QY^n\to D_QY$ in $\mathbb H_{\cP}^2$;
\item the value domain $\operatorname{Dom}(D_Q)$ is closed in
$\mathbb S_{\cP}^2$.
\end{enumerate}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 &\text{value-process compression in the inherited }
       \mathbb S_{\cP}^2\text{ topology}\\
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal N_Q^{\rm vert}=\{0\}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \operatorname{Dom}(D_Q)\text{ is closed in }\mathbb S_{\cP}^2.
 \end{aligned}}
\end{equation}
Under these conditions $J_Q$ is a stable-causal homeomorphism from the
value domain onto the graph.  If $\mathcal N_Q^{\rm vert}=\{0\}$ but the value
domain is not closed, then $D_Q$ is a closed unbounded response operator for
the inherited value norm.  Its graph norm is
\begin{equation}
 \|Y\|_{\operatorname{gr}D_Q}
 :=\|Y\|_{\mathbb S_{\cP}^2}+\|D_QY\|_{\mathbb H_{\cP}^2}.
\end{equation}
Relabelling the graph by $Y$ equipped with this stronger norm retains the full
jet geometry and is not a genuine value-process compression.

If instead $0\ne Z_*\in\mathcal N_Q^{\rm vert}$, no value-only realization can
reproduce the full backward response program: along a testing-graph sequence
\[
 Y^n\to0\quad\text{in }\mathbb S_{\cP}^2,
 \qquad
 D_Q^{\rm pw}Y^n\to Z_*\quad\text{in }\mathbb H_{\cP}^2,
\]
one has
\[
 I(D_Q^{\rm pw}Y^n)\longrightarrow I(Z_*)\ne0.
\]

[Corollary 70 (Deviation and almost-sure convergence) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] In the symmetric same-field setting of
Theorem~\ref{thm:dominated-stability}, let $2\le r<\infty$ and suppose
$K_N\to K$ with
\[
 \norm{(\Prof_{m,r}(K_{N;i}-K_i))_i}_{E(I)}\le\varepsilon_N.
\]
For every $t\ge2$,
\begin{equation}

 \Prob\!\left(
  \norm{I_m(K_N-K)}_{\Sch_r}
  >eA_mC_{E,r}(t+r)^{m/2}\varepsilon_N
 \right)
 \le e^{-t}.
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}

 \sum_{N=1}^\infty
 \norm{(\Prof_{m,r}(K_{N+1;i}-K_{N;i}))_i}_{E(I)}<\infty,
\end{equation}
then $I_m(K_N)$ converges almost surely in $\Sch_r$ and the successive
differences are almost surely absolutely summable.
If instead
\begin{equation}

 \varepsilon_N\bigl(\log(N+1)+r\bigr)^{m/2}\longrightarrow0,
\end{equation}
then $I_m(K_N)\to I_m(K)$ almost surely in $\Sch_r$.

Let k_0 be a real number and let phi : [k_0, infinity) -> [0, infinity) be nonincreasing with phi(k_0) < infinity. Suppose there are constants C > 0, alpha > 0 and beta > 1 with phi(h) <= C (h - k)^(-alpha) phi(k)^beta for all h > k >= k_0. Then phi vanishes from a computable level on: phi(k) = 0 for every k >= k_0 + d, where d > 0 is defined by d^alpha = C phi(k_0)^(beta - 1) 2^(alpha*beta/(beta - 1)). WHERE IT FAILS: beta > 1 is not removable. For beta = 1 the conclusion is false: phi(k) = e^(-k) satisfies phi(h) <= C (h - k)^(-alpha) phi(k) for all h > k with C = sup_{t > 0} t^alpha e^(-t) < infinity, yet phi is never zero. The lemma also says nothing if phi(k_0) = infinity. Monotonicity of phi is used only to pass from the increasing sequence of levels to the level k_0 + d. In applications phi(k) is the Lebesgue measure of a super-level set {|u| > k} and the lemma is the closing step of the truncation method.
phi is nonnegative and nonincreasing on [k_0, infinity)
phi(k_0) is finite
phi(h) <= C (h - k)^(-alpha) phi(k)^beta for all h > k >= k_0
C > 0 and alpha > 0
beta > 1 strictly

The two-vertex blend of the transductive covariance penalty keeps the simplex's gain on EMIT and closes three quarters of its deficit to the pool's hand-tuned heuristic on OCO-2 (-0.27 there); the heuristic is itself label-free, so it was added as a third vertex with barycentric weights chosen by the same criterion. P26 (a) REFUTED: on OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads -0.09 vs the pool best and +0.18 vs the two-vertex blend; (b) HELD: on EMIT it reads +4.78 vs the pool best and +0.05 vs the two-vertex blend; (c) HELD: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool) are (0.09, 0.44, 0.47) on OCO-2 and (0.59, 0.24, 0.17) on EMIT; falsifier (three-vertex worse than two-vertex by more than 0.5 on either corpus) not triggered. [Definition 14 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] Let $N,s\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $s\geq 2$. Then the {\bf Krawtchouk polynomials}, $(K_m)_{m\leq N}$ are,
   \[K_{m,N,s}(x) = K_m(x) = \sum_{j=0}^m (-1)^j{x \choose j}{N-x\choose m-j}(s-1)^{m-j}\]
   Note that $x$ is not required to be integer valued which conflicts with the traditional definition of the binomial coefficient. Therefore we use a more general definition of the binomial coefficient that uses falling factorials; That is,
   \[{x \choose 0} = 1, \quad {x \choose j} = \frac{1}{j!}(x)(x-1)\cdots(x-j+1) \quad \text{for} \quad j\geq 1\]

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.00867, '2609.00867'] Let \(F:E\times E\to\mathbb R\) be measurable and assume that
\[
 \max\left\{
  \norm{F}_{L_x^\infty L_y^1(\mu)},
  \norm{F}_{L_y^\infty L_x^1(\mu)}
 \right\}<\infty.
\]
For an edge \(e=\{i,j\}\) with \(i<j\), write
\(F_e=F(x_i,x_j)\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Suppose that
\begin{equation}
 \int_E F(x,y)\,\mu(\dd y)\ge0
 \quad\text{for \(\mu\)-a.e. \(x\)},
 \qquad
 \int_E F(x,y)\,\mu(\dd x)\ge0
 \quad\text{for \(\mu\)-a.e. \(y\)}.
\end{equation}
If \(T\) is a tree on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), where \(n\ge2\), then
\[
 \left|\int_{E^n}\prod_{e\in E(T)}F_e\,
 \mu^{\otimes n}(\dd X^{1:n})\right|
 \le\left(\iint_{E^2}F(x,y)\,\mu(\dd x)\mu(\dd y)\right)
 \max\left\{
  \norm{F}_{L_x^\infty L_y^1(\mu)},
  \norm{F}_{L_y^\infty L_x^1(\mu)}
 \right\}^{n-2}.
\]

\item[(ii)] Suppose that \(F\in L^2(\mu^{\otimes2})\).  If
\(G\) is a connected graph on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with exactly one cycle,
then
\[
 \int_{E^n}\prod_{e\in E(G)}|F_e|\,
 \mu^{\otimes n}(\dd X^{1:n})
 \le \norm{F}_{L^2(\mu^{\otimes2})}^2
 \max\left\{
  \norm{F}_{L_x^\infty L_y^1(\mu)},
  \norm{F}_{L_y^\infty L_x^1(\mu)}
 \right\}^{n-2}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

 \right\}.

\begin{equation}
 \int_E|F_e|\,\mu(\dd x_i)\le M
 \qquad\text{for \(\mu\)-a.e. \(x_j\)}.
\end{equation}

\(i\) and \(j\).  Since \(x_i\) occurs only in \(F_e\), after taking absolute
values the integration in \(x_i\) is bounded by \(M\) times the integral over
the remaining variables.  Repeating \eqref{eq:one-vertex-integration} along a

body:
# Iid finite-support samples with fixed label noise and unit-norm ReLU teacher

T267 / Target 1 / C013 / proof draft (unaudited); novelty unestablished.
This removes stratification and vanishing label-noise amplitude from C010.
The remaining finite population support, paired initialization, tangent-
kernel limit and averaging over label noise are substantive restrictions.

## 1. Statement

Use C010's four unit inputs x_(s,t), uniform population distribution and
centered unit-norm ReLU teacher g_e=alpha_e(s+t+st). Fix nu in (0,1] and
label-noise amplitude sigma in (0,1], independently of feature scale e.
Take n(e)=ceil(sigma^2/alpha_e^2) independent population input samples,
and label each by g_e(x)+epsilon, with independent epsilon uniform +/-sigma.
Initialize an even-width two-layer ReLU net by independent Gaussian pairs
with equal hidden weights and opposite readouts +/-nu, as in C010.
Training inputs, label noises and initialization are mutually independent.
Train all parameters by simultaneous GD at step gamma=1/2 on empirical
squared loss divided by 2n(e). No post-initialization parameter tying.

Let Q_(m,e)(k) be clean population squared risk averaged over all training
label noises, conditional on input samples and network initialization.
Use C010's rates b_h and witness times k0,k1,k2,k3, and its central integer
interval I_e with B=log[b1/(b2+b12)]. Then in the iterated even-width-first,
feature-scale-second limit, with probability tending to one over iid
training inputs and initialization:

Q(k0)>Q(k1)<Q(k2)>Q(k3),
(Q(k0),Q(k1),Q(k2),Q(k3))/alpha_e^2 -> (4,7/2,4,3),

and every maximizer k_peak on I_e is interior and satisfies
b1 k_peak-B ->0. In particular

k_peak ~ (4pi/nu^2) e^(-1) log(1/e).

All convergence in probability uses the order lim_(e->0) limsup_(m->infinity)
of each failure probability. Sample size n(e) grows as 4sigma^2 e^(-4);
it is fixed during each width limit. The theorem does not assert high
probability over realized labels; risk itself averages over label noise.
No Gaussian-input or full Target1 solution is claimed.

## 2. Collapse repeated inputs exactly

Let N_i be the count of population point i, p_i=N_i/n, and
D=diag(4p_i). On the event all N_i>0 let bar y_i be the mean label in cell i.
The empirical loss equals

(1/2) sum_i p_i (f(x_i)-bar y_i)^2 + a parameter-independent constant.

Consequently every parameter update is exactly the update on these four
cell means with weights p_i. Conditional on counts, the cell-mean noise
has mean zero and diagonal covariance

V=diag(sigma^2/N_i)=(4sigma^2/n)D^(-1).

No Gaussian approximation or independence of Walsh coefficients is used.
The test law remains uniform on the population support, including when
the realized training counts are unequal.

## 3. Count concentration

Put delta=||D-I||. Each diagonal deviation has mean zero and variance 3/n,
because N_i is binomial(n,1/4). Chebyshev plus a union bound gives

P(delta>r)<=12/(n r^2).

Take r=e^(3/2). Since n is asymptotic to 4sigma^2 e^(-4), the failure
probability is O(e), for fixed sigma. For all small e, on the resulting
good event delta<=e^(3/2)<1/2, every cell is nonempty and
D lies between (1-delta)I and (1+delta)I. This is the only sample-count
event used. There is no fixed-count conditioning in the final theorem.

## 4. Weighted frozen-kernel stability without a slow-gap denominator

Let C be C009's deterministic full initial tangent matrix, with ||C||<=1,
and A=I-gamma C, gamma=1/2. Compare zero-start prediction iterations
using C and C D, both with the SAME cell-mean label vector bar y.
Write their residuals r_I(k),r_D(k) and prediction difference d(k).

The matrix I-gamma C D is similar, by D^(1/2), to the symmetric matrix
I-gamma D^(1/2) C D^(1/2). The latter has eigenvalues in [0,1] when
delta<=1/2, since gamma||D|| ||C||<=3/4. Thus

||r_D(k)|| <= kappa_delta ||bar y||,
kappa_delta=sqrt((1+delta)/(1-delta))<=sqrt(3)<2.

Subtracting the two iterations and using d(0)=0 gives

d(k)=-gamma sum_(j=0)^(k-1) A^(k-1-j) C(D-I)r_D(j).

For l>=0, spectral calculus yields
||gamma C A^l||<=1/(l+1): each eigenvalue is a(1-a)^l with a in [0,1/2],
whose maximum is bounded by 1/(l+1). Therefore

||d(k)||<=kappa_delta delta H_k ||bar y||,
H_k=sum_(j=1)^k 1/j <=1+log k, k>=1.

The crucial feature is logarithmic time growth rather than division by
the smallest eigenvalue of C. This argument does not assume that C and D
commute. For k=0 the difference is zero and H_0=0.

## 5. Uniform noise-averaged risk comparison

Let Q_D(k) denote the clean frozen risk using C D and the actual cell-
mean noise. Let Q_I,V(k) use C and the same noise covariance V. Since
||g||^2=12alpha^2 and tr V<=32alpha^2 on delta<=1/2 (n>=sigma^2/alpha^2),
E||bar y||^2<=44alpha^2<49alpha^2 and ||g||<4alpha.
The unweighted predictor has norm at most ||bar y||, and the weighted
predictor has norm at most (1+kappa_delta)||bar y||. Combining the risk
identity | ||a||^2-||b||^2 |<=||a-b||(||a||+||b||) with Section4 and
Cauchy--Schwarz, and dividing by four for the uniform population, gives

max_(k<=T)|Q_D(k)-Q_I,V(k)|/alpha^2 <=126 delta H_T.

For clarity this constant follows from kappa_delta<2,
(2+kappa_delta)E||bar y||^2+2||g||E||bar y|| <=252alpha^2;
the outside factor is kappa_delta delta H_T/4<delta H_T/2.

Now compare V with the balanced covariance V0=(4sigma^2/n)I.
The unweighted prediction noise map B_k=I-A^k has norm at most one.
Its risk covariance perturbation is at most

(1/4)||V-V0||_* <=4(sigma^2/n)delta/(1-delta)<=8alpha^2 delta.

Balanced covariance has Walsh variance sigma^2/n, while C010 uses alpha^2.
Let rho_round=sigma^2/(nalpha^2). Rounding n upward gives
0<=1-rho_round<=alpha^2/sigma^2. Each of four mode noise filters is at
most one, so the corresponding risk error is at most 4alpha^4/sigma^2.
Consequently, for C010's baseline zero-output curve Q_e^0,

max_(k<=T)|Q_D(k)-Q_e^0(k)|/alpha^2
 <=126 delta H_T+8delta+4alpha^2/sigma^2.

Choose T=ceil(e^(-5/2)). On the count-good event the right side is
O(e^(3/2)log(1/e))+O(e^4)=o(e). This is smaller than both C010's constant
normalized witness margins and its normalized central peak gap of order e.
All covariance arguments use exact second moments, not a central limit
approximation or a numerical experiment.

## 6. Actual nonlinear GD comparison under cell weights

We spell out the weighted extension of C010's finite-horizon argument.
On the count-good event ||D||<=3/2. For small e, each cell-mean label has
absolute value at most sigma+3alpha<2, hence ||bar y||<=4. The network
starts at zero. Use the deterministic neuronwise bounds of C009 with
R_0=4, S=14, L=2, n0=4, and replace its c_k by

gamma L (3/2)R_k/n0.

In its residual recurrence multiply the readout-kernel gradient term by
3/2 as well; the feature-motion term is already expressed through c_k.
This follows directly from replacing r by D r in both exact parameter
updates and bounding ||D r||<=3R/2. All resulting constants through a
fixed T are finite and uniform over D in [I/2,3I/2] and labels in [-2,2]^4.

Gaussian norm bounds, independent-pair strong laws, initial kernel
convergence and weighted initial gate-band mass are unchanged, since the
four possible input vectors are unchanged. Kernel drift and the exact
discrete-step gate remainder tend uniformly to zero. The frozen iteration
uses C D; its powers are bounded by sqrt(3) by Section4, so telescoping
still transfers predictions uniformly through T. Crucially the argument
is uniform over all bounded cell-mean label vectors; it does not take a
union over 2^n noise realizations or assume independent adaptive gates.
Uniform prediction control and the finite-horizon deterministic bounds
transfer noise-averaged risks as width tends to infinity for each fixed e.
Division by the fixed positive alpha^2 e is legitimate at this stage.

Thus max_(k<=T)|Q_actual(k)-Q_D(k)|/(alpha^2 e)->0 in probability over
initialization as width grows, on the count-good event, uniformly in its
counts. This claim does not give a uniform-in-e practical width threshold.

## 7. Witness and peak transfer, and remaining scope

The sample event fails with probability O(e). On it, Section5 gives
uniform surrogate-risk error o(alpha^2 e), and Section6 adds a vanishing
fixed-e width error. C010's positive risk witnesses and central peak
value gaps therefore transfer, first taking width to infinity and then
e to zero. Its entire integer peak interval and k3 lie below T for all
small e. The teacher identity and full tangent-kernel clocks are unchanged.
This proves the stated restricted theorem.

Fixed label noise, unit teacher norm and iid sampling are now explicit,
but n grows as e^(-4), the test population has only four atoms, readouts
are paired, risk averages over label noise and the proof is in a tangent-
kernel limit. It is not a generic Gaussian-design, macroscopic feature-
learning, realized-label high-probability, fixed-n, all-time, full-target
or novelty claim. C009/C010 and the uniform weighted nonlinear extension
await independent review. That extension is the least-trusted proof step.
No network training, dataset generation or large computation is needed.
All explicit definitions and width/scale limit order in proofs/IID_FIXED_NOISE.md
Uniform four-atom input law, unit-norm centered-ReLU single-index teacher; n(e)~4sigma^2 e^-4
Label noise independent symmetric +/-sigma, sigma fixed in (0,1]; clean risk averages over labels conditional on input sample and initialization
Paired Gaussian hidden initialization and opposite nonzero heads +/-nu, nu fixed in (0,1]; step 1/2, both layers trained
Finite-horizon comparison through T_e=ceil(e^-5/2); population support remains finite and initialization is not iid across individual neurons

body: [Proposition p:criterion-for-wt-chart of arXiv:2609.03731, 'Weightings and Lie groupoids'] Let $(M^n,N^p,\ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_\bullet)$ be a weighted manifold. Let $(U,\phi=(x^1,...,x^n))$ be a weighted coordinate chart, where $x^j$ has weight $w_j$. Let $(U,\psi=(y^1,...,y^n))$ be another coordinate chart. If $y^j\in \ensuremath{\mathcal{I}}_{w_j}$ for $j=1,...,n$ then there is an open neighborhood $V\subset U$ of $U\cap N$ such that $\psi|_V$ is a weighted coordinate chart.
title: Proposition p:criterion-for-wt-chart of arXiv:2609.03731

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] There are smooth embedded rotational tori
$X_j:M\to\R^{n+1}$ such that, for every $1\leq p<k/(k-1)$,
\[
 X_j\longrightarrow X
 \quad\text{in }C^1(M)\cap W^{2,p}(M).
\]
Let $S_{X_j}$ and $\nu_j$ denote the shape operator and outward unit normal
of $X_j$, respectively, and let $d\mu_{X_j}$ be its induced volume measure.
When the curvature and support-function measures are regarded as measures on
the fixed parameter manifold $M$,
\begin{align}
 \sigma_k(S_{X_j})\,d\mu_{X_j}
 &\longrightarrow\mathcal K_k[X],
 \\
 \langle X_j,\nu_j\rangle\,d\mu_{X_j}
 &\longrightarrow\langle X,\nu\rangle\,d\mu_X
 
\end{align}
in total variation.  In particular, the fixed-domain residual satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left\|
 \bigl(\sigma_k(S_{X_j})+\langle X_j,\nu_j\rangle\bigr)d\mu_{X_j}
 \right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Here $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}$ denotes the total variation norm.
After push-forward to $\R^{n+1}$, the two measures in
\eqref{eq:fixed-domain-curvature-TV}--\eqref{eq:fixed-domain-support-TV}
converge separately only weakly as Radon measures in general, whereas the
pushed-forward residual still converges to zero in total variation.

For bounded symmetric real S with variance V>0 and moment generating function having only imaginary zeros i*y_j (positive y_j with multiplicity), set X=S/sqrt(V), r=sqrt(V)*y_1 and B=3-E X^4. Hadamard factorization of F(sqrt(w)), of entire order at most 1/2, gives F(z)=product_j(1+z^2/y_j^2), V=2 sum_j y_j^-2 and kappa4(S)=-12 sum_j y_j^-4. Thus 12/r^4<=B<=6/r^2. The product yields E exp(tX)<=exp(t^2/2); hence uniform integrability of fourth powers. For a sequence obeying these hypotheses, Gaussian weak convergence to N(0,1) is equivalent to r tending to infinity. Bounded r along a subsequence forces every weak subsequential limit to be non-Gaussian. The Ising application requires zero field, ferromagnetic pair interactions, nonnegative block weights, spin-flip symmetry, and a justified Lee–Yang/Hurwitz passage to the actual Gibbs marginal.

of Theorem~\ref{thm:optimal-modulated-free-energy}.  Then
\begin{align}

 &\le\mathcal E_N(0)

  \E_{F^N(r)}\cU_{N,\rho_r}\!\left(

\end{align}
where
\(q_{\nabla\psi_r}(x,y):=(\nabla\psi_r(x)-\nabla\psi_r(y))
\cdot\nabla g(x-y)\).

[Lem 67 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have 
$\sM^{\siv}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\sv}(\alpha,q_0)$.

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} for this proof:
	\begin{center}
	\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
	\MSRheader\\
	\hline
	\GOODdefn\\
	\TMPTHRdefn
	\end{tabular}
	\end{center}
We see that the
$\siv$ and $\sv$ classes differ only in the condition on 
$\E[(w_t)^2]$: the $\siv$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:2.1} (i.e., $\E[(w_t)^2] \in [1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon]$), while the $\sv$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:2.2} (i.e., $\E[(w_t)^2] = 1$). 

Therefore, let us suppose we have controls $(q_* = q_0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the $(\alpha,q_0,L,\epsilon)$-{{$\siv$}} conditions. We then define
$(\tilde{q}_*,\tilde{b},\tilde{\sigma},\tilde{p},\tilde{\zeta},\tilde{\zeta}^\Ising)
=(q_* ,b,\sigma,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$, and
	\[\tilde w_t=\frac{w_t}{\bbE[(w_t)^2]^{1/2}}\,,\]
so that $\tilde{w}$ satisfies
condition~\ref{it:2.2}. We let $\tilde{X}=X$, and let
$\tilde{Y}$ be given by \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising} with $\tilde{w}$ in place of $w$, but with
the same initialization $\tilde{Y}(q_0)=Y(q_0)$ and the same Brownian motion $W$. 
 It is clear from these definitions that the modified controls continue to satisfy
conditions~\ref{it:1.2}, \ref{it:3.2}, \ref{it:6.2}, \ref{it:7.2}, and \ref{it:8.2}. 
For condition~\ref{it:4.1}, we note that for the two choices of $w$, the difference in the resulting values of 
$\budget(t;\alpha)$ is
	\[
    \frac{|\E[w_t]^2 - \E[\tilde w_t]^2|}{\alpha} = \frac{\E[w_t]^2}{\alpha} \bigg|1 - \frac{1}{\bbE[(w_t)^2]}
    \bigg|
    \le \frac{1+\epsilon}{\alpha} \cdot \frac{\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}\,.
\]
Since this tends to zero as $\epsilon \to 0$, we see that $\tilde{w}$ also satisfies
condition~\ref{it:4.1}, provided we adjust $\epsilon$. Finally, it follows from \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising} that
    \[
        \bbE\Big[ (Y(1)-\tilde Y(1))^2\Big]
        \leq
        \int_{q_0}^1
        \bbE[(\tilde w_t-w_t)^2]
        \,dt
        =
        \int_{q_0}^1
        \Big(
        \bbE [(w_t)^2]^{1/2} - 1
        \Big)^2
        \,dt
        \le 
        \Big(1 - (1-\epsilon)^{1/2}
        \Big)^2\,.
    \]
By the same estimate as in \eqref{eq:endpoint-condition-stability} in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:fair.in.tmp1}, $\tilde{Y}(1)$ also satisfies condition~\ref{it:5.1}, again provided we adjust $\epsilon$. 
Thus we have shown that for some $\tilde{\epsilon}$ tending to zero with $\epsilon$, we have
\[
    \cB_\epsilon(\cM^{\siv}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon,L_0))
    \subseteq \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}(\cM^{\sv}(\alpha,q_0;L,\tilde \epsilon,L_0)),
\]
Recalling the notations of Definition~\ref{d:measure.classes}, the claim follows.\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2607.22441, 'The martingale representation theorem for cylindrical martingale valued measures'] [$G$-valued martingale representation]

Let $M=(M(t, A): t \geq 0, A \in \calA)$ be a $G$-valued orthogonal M.V.M. with continuous paths and which possesses a unique quadratic variation.  
Assume that the operator-valued quadratic variation of $M$ is given by 
\begin{equation}
 \Gamma_{M}([0,t] \times A) = \int_0^t \int_A\; \Phi (r,u) Q\Phi^*(r,u)\; \lambda(du) dr, 
\end{equation}
where $Q$ is a bounded, non-negative, self-adjoint operator on $H$ with  representation  \eqref{representationCovariaQDefiCylinWhineNoiseMeasure}, $\lambda$ is a $\sigma$-finite measure on $U$, which is finite on the sets in $\mathcal{A}$, and $\Phi: \Omega \times[0,T] \times U \rightarrow \mathcal{L}(H,G)$ is such that $ (\omega,t,u) \mapsto \Phi(\omega,t,u)h$ 
is $\mathcal{P}_{T}\otimes \mathcal{B}(U)/\mathcal{B}(G)$-measurable for every $h \in H$.
Then $\Phi (\omega, t,u) \in \mathcal{HS}(H_{Q},G)$ and there exists a 
cylindrical $Q$-white noise measure $W=(W(t, A): t \geq 0, A \in \calA)$ on $H$ based on $\left(\mathbb{R}_{+} \times U, \mathcal{B}\left(\mathbb{R}_{+}\right) \otimes \mathcal{B}(U),Leb \otimes \lambda\right)$
in $H$ based on $\left(\mathbb{R}_{+} \times U, \mathcal{B}\left(\mathbb{R}_{+}\right) \otimes \mathcal{B}(U),Leb \otimes \lambda\right)$  defined with respect to an extended probability space $(\Omega \times \widetilde{\Omega}, \mathcal{F} \times \widetilde{\mathcal{F}}, \Prob \times \widetilde{\Prob})$ adapted to the filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_{t} \times \widetilde{\mathcal{F}}_{t}\}$, such that 
 $$
M(t,A)(\omega)= \int_0^t\int_A \Phi(\omega,r,u)W(dr,du)(\omega, \widetilde{\omega}),
$$ 
where the last equality must be interpreted as $G$-valued random variables.

[Lemma local of arXiv:2507.20324, 'Non-existence of several random fractals in Brownian motion and Brownian loop soup'] For $i=1,2,\ldots,5$, let $E_{i,j}$ be the event that $W_{i}$ returns to $\mathcal{D}_{jL}$ after hitting $\mathcal{C}_{(j+1)L}$. Then there exist $c,c'>0$, such that for any integer $j\leq [3L/4]$, and $i=1,2,\ldots,5$, we have
\[\mathbb{P}(E_{i,j}\cap E_{1})\leq ce^{-c'\sqrt{n}}\cdot2^{-2n}.\]
Let $E_{4}$ be the union of $(E_{i,j})_{1\le i\le 5,1\le j\le [3L/4]}$. Then by the union bound there exists $c''>0$ such that
\[\mathbb{P}(E_{4}\cap E_{1})\leq ce^{-c''\sqrt{n}}\cdot2^{-2n}.\]
title: Lemma local of arXiv:2507.20324

[Prop 2ptNestedCLE of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] For $v \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2 > 0$ small, we let $E^v_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}$ denote the event that for a GFF in a simply-connected domain $D$ with constant boundary value $v$ there exists a nested CLE$_4$ gasket of height $0$
that intersects both 
$\mathbb{D}(z_1,\varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2, \varepsilon_2)$.

We then have that 
\begin{itemize}
\item $$\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm nest}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2)) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{P}(E^{2\lambda n}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2})  
+O((\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/6}),$$
where $E^{\rm nest}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2)$ is the event that there is some gasket of nested CLE$_4$ that intersects both $\mathbb{D}(z_1,\varepsilon_1)$ and 
$\mathbb{D}(z_2,\varepsilon_2)$.

\item $$\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm odd}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2))
=\sum_{n \in 2\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{P}(E^{2\lambda n}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2})  
+O((\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}),$$
where $E^{\rm odd}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2)$ is the event that there is an odd gasket of nested CLE$_4$ that intersects both $\mathbb{D}(z_1,\varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2,\varepsilon_2)$.

\item $$\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm even}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2))
=\sum_{n \in 2\mathbb{Z}+1} \mathbb{P}(E^{2\lambda n}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2})  
+O((\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}),$$
where $E^{\rm even}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1, z_2)$ 
is the event that there is an even gasket of nested 
CLE$_4$ that intersects both 
$\mathbb{D}(z_1,\varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2,\varepsilon_2)$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 2ptNestedCLE of arXiv:2604.15146

[Proposition prop:local_well_posedness_homogenized_SPDE of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Let $\mu>0$ and $r\in (1,\infty)$. Let $Q$ be a parabolic cylinder with side length $\varrho\in (0,1/4]$ and center $(t_0,x_0)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}^d$.
Assume that 
\begin{equation}

F,G \in L^r_{\mathscr{P}}(\Omega;L^2(2Q;{\mathbb R}^{d\times d})).
\end{equation}
Let $(v^{N,\delta},\pi^{N,\delta},(\widetilde{\pi}_{k,\alpha}^{N,\delta})_{k,\alpha})$ be a local solution to the oscillating stochastic Stokes system (equation eq:turbulent_Stokes_scaling_quantitative of the paper) on $2Q$ for some $N\geq 1$ and $\delta\in (0,1]$ (see Definition (def:local_solutions_NSE of the paper)). 
Then there exists a unique solution $(\overline{v}^{N,\delta},\overline{\pi}^{N,\delta})$ to the homogenized Stokes system (equation eq:homogenized_PDE_linear of the paper) in the transposition sense (see Definition (def:solution_homogenized of the paper) below). Moreover 
\begin{align}
\nonumber
&\big({\mathbf E}\|\overline{v}^{N,\delta}\|_{L^\infty(I;L^2(B))}^r \big)^{1/r}
+
\big({\mathbf E}\|\nabla \overline{v}^{N,\delta}\|_{L^2(Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}+ \big({\mathbf E}\|\overline{\pi}^{N,\delta}\|_{H^{-1}(I;H^{-1}(B))}^r\big)^{1/r}\\
\nonumber
&\qquad\qquad \lesssim
\Big({\mathbf E}\Big\|v^{N,\delta}-\fint_{B} v^{N,\delta}\Big\|_{L^\infty(I;L^2(B))}^r\Big)^{1/r} +
\big({\mathbf E}\|\nabla v^{N,\delta}\|_{L^2(Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}\\ 
&\qquad\qquad
+\big({\mathbf E} \|(\nabla \widetilde{\pi}_{k,\alpha}^{N,\delta})_{k,\alpha}\|_{L^2(Q;\ell^2)}^r\big)^{1/r}+ \big({\mathbf E}\|F\|_{L^2(Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}+\big({\mathbf E}\|G\|_{L^2(Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}, 

\end{align}
where the implicit constant depends only on $\mu,r,\varrho$ and $d$. If, in addition to the above assumptions, it holds that $F,G \in L^r(\Omega;L^p(2I;L^2(2B)))$ for some $p\in (2,\infty)$, then 
\begin{align}
\nonumber
\big({\mathbf E}\|\overline{\pi}^{N,\delta}\|_{H^{-1,p}(I;H^{-1}(B))}^r\big)^{1/r}
 \lesssim
\Big({\mathbf E}\Big\|v^{N,\delta}-\fint_{B} v^{N,\delta}\Big\|_{L^\infty(I;L^2(B))}^r\Big)^{1/r} +
\big({\mathbf E}\|\nabla v^{N,\delta}\|_{L^2(Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}&\\ 
+\big({\mathbf E} \|(\nabla \widetilde{\pi}_{k,\alpha}^{N,\delta})_{k,\alpha}\|_{L^2(Q;\ell^2)}^r\big)^{1/r}+ \big({\mathbf E}\|F\|_{L^p(I;L^2(B))}^r\big)^{1/r}+\big({\mathbf E}\|G\|_{L^p(I;L^2(B))}^r\big)^{1/r}&, 

\end{align}
where the implicit constant depends only on $\mu,p,r,\varrho$ and $d$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Well-posedness of the homogenized Stokes system

[Proposition 122 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Let $\kappa,c > 0$ and suppose $\sqrt{2\theta \kappa} - \pi > c$ and $\min(\theta,\kappa) > c$. There exists $\eps_1,\eps_2>0$ small enough and $C>0$ large enough depending only on $c$ and satisfying the following conditions for all $\N$ large enough. Take any six parameters $-\infty < \mathfrak{a}_1<\mathfrak{b}_1< \mathfrak{a}_2< \mathfrak{b}_2 < +\infty$ and $\mathfrak{n}_1,\mathfrak{n}_2 \in \frac{1}{\N}\amsmathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, such that:
 \begin{enumerate}
  \item $\N \mathfrak{b}_1 -\N\mathfrak{a}_1 - \theta (\N\mathfrak{n}_1-1)\in \amsmathbb Z_{\geq 0}$ and $\,\N \mathfrak{b}_2 -\N\mathfrak{a}_2 - \theta (\N\mathfrak{n}_2-1)\in \amsmathbb Z_{\geq 0}$,
  \item $\N\mathfrak{a}_1\in\amsmathbb Z-\theta\frac{N-1}{2}$ and $\,\N\mathfrak{b}_2 \in\amsmathbb Z+\theta\frac{N-1}{2}$,
  \item $\mathfrak{a}_1 \in (-\alpha-2\eps_1,-\alpha-\eps_1)$,\, $\mathfrak{b}_1 \in (-\beta+\eps_1,-\beta +2\eps_1)$,\, $\mathfrak{a}_2 \in (\beta-2\eps_1,\beta-\eps_1)$,\, $\mathfrak{b}_2 \in (\alpha+\eps_1,\alpha+2\eps_1)$,
  \item $\big|\mathfrak{n}_1-\mu([\mathfrak{a}_1,\mathfrak{b}_1])\big|<\eps_2$ and $\big|\mathfrak{n}_2-\mu([\mathfrak{a}_2,\mathfrak{b}_2])\big|<\eps_2$,
  \item $\N\mathfrak{n}_1+ \frac{\N}{\theta}(\mathfrak{a}_2-\mathfrak{b}_1)-1+ \N\mathfrak{n}_2=N$.
 \end{enumerate}
Let us define the event $\mathcal{A}$ by the following two properties:
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item[A.] There are no particles outside the interval $[\N \mathfrak{a}_1,\N\mathfrak{b}_2]$.
 \item[B.] There are no holes in the interval $[\N\mathfrak{b}_1,\N\mathfrak{a}_2]$, \textit{i.e.} it is occupied by $\frac{\N}{\theta}(\mathfrak{a}_2-\mathfrak{b}_1)+1$ particles densely packed at distances $\theta$ from each other.
 \end{enumerate}
Then, $\mathcal{A}$ has probability at least $1 - C\exp(-\frac{\N}{C})$, and the discrete ensemble with Gaussian weight and conditioned on $\mathcal{A}$ and on the event that the $\N\mathfrak{n}_1$-th particle sits at position $\N \mathfrak{b}_1$ --- given $\mathcal A$, this implies as well that the $(\N \mathfrak{n}_1+ \frac{\N}{\theta} (\mathfrak{a}_2-\mathfrak{b}_1)\big)$-th particle sits at position $\N\mathfrak{a}_2$ --- and localized to $\mathfrak{A} := [\mathfrak{a}_1,\mathfrak{b}_1] \cup [\mathfrak{a}_2,\mathfrak{b}_2]$ yields an ensemble satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic}, \ref{Assumptions_offcrit}, \ref{Assumptions_analyticity} and the additional Assumption~\ref{Assumptions_extra}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 122 of arXiv:2601.16377

[Theorem thm:copula+iDCI of arXiv:2609.02832, 'Copula Transformations for Data-Consistent Inversion'] Suppose the assumptions of Section~2.2.3 hold so that the iDCI sequence converges to the limiting measure
$P^\infty$, and let $P^\infty_{\rm pred}:=P^\infty\circ\phi^{-1}$
denote its joint push-forward through the vector-valued QoI map.
Then, the associated density admits the representation
\[
\pi^\infty_{\rm pred}(y)
=
c_\infty(U_{\rm obs}(y))
\prod_{i=1}^{d}
\pi_{{\rm obs},i}(y_i),
\]
for a unique copula density
$c_\infty$.
Equivalently, $U_\infty(y)=U_{\rm obs}(y)$, where $U_\infty$
denotes the probability integral transform associated with
$\pi^\infty_{\rm pred}$.

body:
[Definition Bounded-Lipschitz distance of arXiv:2608.17648, 'Semicircular law with a few independent entries in a random matrix'] Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures on $(\mathbb{R}, \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}))$. The bounded-Lipshcitz distance between $\mu$ and $\nu$ is defined as 
    \[
        d_\mathrm{BL}(\mu, \nu) := \sup_{\substack {\|f\|_\infty \le 1, \\ \mathrm{Lip}(f) \le 1}} \left| \int_\mathbb{R} f\, d\mu - \int_\mathbb{R} f \, d\nu \right|,
    \]
    where
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{Lip}(f) &:= \sup_{x \ne y} \frac{|f(x) - f(y)|}{d(x, y)},\\
        \|f\|_{\infty} &:= \sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}} |f(x)|.
    \end{align*}
title: Bounded-Lipschitz distance

body:
[Theorem 6 (Canonical splittings and optional naturality) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] A source-independent pointwise lifting rule \(j:G\to\widetilde G\) is
multiplicative and transport-natural if and only if
\begin{equation}
 pj={\mathrm{Id}},\qquad
 j(g\star h)=j(g)\star j(h),\qquad
 \widetilde\alpha_{t,s}j=j\alpha_{t,s}.
 
\end{equation}
Writing \(j(g)=r(g)\star q(g)\), these conditions are equivalent to
\begin{align}
 r(g\star h)
 &=r(g)\star\rho(g)(r(h))\star f(g,h),
 \\
 r(\alpha_{t,s}g)
 &=\widetilde\alpha_{t,s}(r(g))\star d_{t,s}(g),
 
\end{align}
where \(r:G\to K\) and \(r({\mathbf 1})={\mathbf 1}\).  Every such splitting sends
causal characters to causal lifts.  If \(j\) is continuous and \(\bar A\)
is a càdlàg base anchor, then \(j(\bar A)\) is a càdlàg lifted anchor and
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde\Phi_{\sigma,\tau}=j(\bar\Phi_{\sigma,\tau})
 
\end{equation}
for all bounded stopping pairs.

More generally, if \(H\) is an adapted càdlàg lifted anchor and \(b\) is
an adapted càdlàg \(K\)-valued gauge with \(b_0={\mathbf 1}\), then
\(H^b_t=H_t\star b_t\) has stopped increments
\begin{equation}
 (L^b)_{\sigma,\tau}
 =\widetilde\alpha_{\tau,\sigma}(b_\sigma)^{-1}
  \star L_{\sigma,\tau}\star b_\tau.
 
\end{equation}
Thus optional completion preserves gauge arrows but selects no gauge.
Existence of a splitting does not imply uniqueness; within this
source-independent class, a canonical rule requires the admissibility
conditions to select a unique splitting.  For random characters the
unstopped rule requires \(j\) to be Borel, and the stopped assertion
requires continuity.
