[Lemma lem:veb-refilling-transition of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Consider the VEB setting, and let $\Psi = (g,\tau_g,j,\overline{z},\mathcal{S},\textup{refilling}) \in \ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$ be a high-level state.  Let $d$ and $\theta$ be real numbers with $d \ge 0$ and $0 \leq  \theta \leq 1/(64j^2)$, and suppose that $\overline{a}\in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$ is a $(d,j^{27},\theta,2)$-RS-good beginning. Conditioned on the events $\Psi(\tau_g) = \Psi$ and $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(\tau_g) = \overline{a}$, with probability at least $1-j^{-2j}$,  
the following events occur.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(\tau_g+j^{\phi+46})$ is a $(d+5j^{\phi+49}, j^{10}, \theta+3/j^4, 1)$-RS-good beginning.
\item For all $k\in [j]$ with $W_k \ge j^\chi$ and all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + j^{\phi+46}$, $p_kb_k^{E_g}(t) \le \lambda/80$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if these events occur and $V$ is well-behaved, then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(I)]
\item $\Psi(\tau_{g+1})$ is a refilling or stabilising state.
\item $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_{g+1}}(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(d+5j^{\phi+49},j^{10},\theta + 3/j^4, 1)$-RS-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ with $\tau_g \le t < \tau_{g+1}$, 
and all $k\in [j-1]$ with $W_k\geq j^{\chi}$, 
$\{k\} \in \mathcal{S}$  and $\mathcal{N}^{E_{g}}_{\{k\}}(t+1) \le \lambda /80$.
Moreover, there is at least one such $k\in [j-1]$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:veb-refilling-transition of arXiv:2602.21315

[Cor Cor_strong_alpha_convex of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] Let $I\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a nonempty open interval, $\alpha:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be an even function,
 and $L:I\to \mathbb{R}$ be a strongly $\alpha$-convex function.
Then
 \begin{align*}
   L\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^n t_ix_i\bigg)
   \leqslant \sum_{i=1}^n t_iL(x_i)
        -\sum_{i=1}^n t_i\alpha\bigg(x_i-\sum_{j=1}^n t_jx_j\bigg)
 \end{align*}
 for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in I$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in[0,1]$ satisfying $t_1+\cdots +t_n=1$.
title: Cor Cor_strong_alpha_convex of arXiv:2606.22183

[Lemma lem:comparison_effectiveresistance_percolation_domination of arXiv:2607.04002, 'Collisions of random walks in unimodular random graphs: applications to the random geometr'] Suppose that the following is true:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item On each good box $B_\mathbf z$ we can pick a vertex $v_{\mathbf z} \in V(G)$.
        \item There exists~$L > 0$ such that for any pair~$(\mathbf x, \mathbf y)$ satisfying~$X_{ \{\mathbf x, \mathbf y\} }=1$, the vertices~$v_{\mathbf x}$ and~$v_{\mathbf y}$ can be connected by a path $\gamma_{\mathbf x,\mathbf y}$ in $G$ totally contained within $B_{\mathbf x}\cup B_{\mathbf y}$ with length at most~$L$.
        \item The process~$\{X_e: e \in E(\mathbb{Z}^d)\}$ dominates a supercritical Bernoulli bond percolation process with parameter~$p$, which can be taken arbitrarily close to 1. 
    \end{enumerate}
    Then, there exists a probability space~$\widehat{\mathbb{P}}$ on which the domination holds, where the following statement is satisfied. There exists a constant~$C = C(d,L,p,M,R)>0$ such that
    $$ \widehat{\mathbb{P}} \left( \sup_{\mathbf z \in \partial_V\mathcal V_0} \mathcal R_\mathrm{eff}( \mathbf{z} \longleftrightarrow \infty ; \mathcal C_\infty ) \ge u \right) \leq \exp( -b u^\nu ), \quad \text{for } u \text{ large enough}. $$
title: Lemma lem:comparison_effectiveresistance_percolation_domination of arXiv:2607.04002

body: [Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.03951, 'Generalized Semi-Riemannian Submersions and Foliations'] The horizontal lift of vectors in $\mathcal{D}(q)$ at $p \in \pi^{-1}(q)$ is unique if and only if the vertical distribution $\mathcal{V}_p$ is non-degenerate. Moreover, if $\tilde{v}$ and $\hat{v}$ are two horizontal lifts of $v$, then there exists $v_0 \in \mathcal{R}_p$ such that $\tilde{v} = \hat{v} + v_0$. In particular, $g(\tilde{v}, \tilde{v}) = g(\hat{v}, \hat{v})$.

[Lemma lem:approx-slackness of arXiv:2606.14687, 'Lehner's operator norm formulas, semidefinite programming, and spiked matrix models'] Let $\bm A_0, \bm A_1, \dots, \bm A_n \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}_{\mathsf{herm}}$, let $(c, \bm Z)$ be feasible for the primal small SDP (equation eq:sc-sdp-small-primal of the paper).
    Recall that by Proposition~(prop:Z-pd of the paper) this implies $\bm Z \succ \bm 0$.
    Define $\Psi_{\bm Z}: \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}_{\mathsf{herm}} \to \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}_{\mathsf{herm}}$ by
    \[
        \Psi_{\bm Z}(\bm S) \colonequals \bm Z \Phi(\bm S)\bm Z.
    \]
    Suppose that $\bm S \succeq \bm 0$, $\Tr(\bm S) = 1$, and
    \[
        \Psi_{\bm Z}(\bm S) = \bm Z \Phi(\bm S)\bm Z = \rho \bm S
    \]
    for some $\rho > 0$ (that is, $\bm S$ is an eigenmatrix of the operator $\Psi_{\bm Z}$ with eigenvalue $\rho$).
    Then,
    \begin{equation}
        
        c - \langle c \bm I_d - \bm A_0 - \Phi(\bm Z) - \bm Z^{-1}, \bm S \rangle - (\sqrt{\rho} - 1)^2 \langle \bm Z^{-1}, \bm S\rangle \leq \Lambda_{\mathsf{sc}}(\bm A_0, \bm A_1, \dots, \bm A_n) \leq c.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition pcpp1 of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1\leq p<\infty$. \\
{\rm (1)} If $(X,Y)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$, then $(X,Y)$ has the $p$-$\mathrm{CPP}$.\\
{\rm (2)} If $(X, Y)$ has the $p$-$\mathrm{CPP}$, then it has the $q$-$\mathrm{CPP}$ for every $q > p$. \\
{\rm (3)} Suppose that $(X, Y)$ satisfies the $p$-$\mathrm{CPP}$. If $E$ is a $1$-complemented subspace of $X$ and $F$ is a closed subspace of $Y$, then $(E,F)$ has the $p$-$\mathrm{CPP}$.

[Lem 9 (Restricted Yamada--Watanabe theorem) of arXiv:2607.28078, '2607.28078'] Fix $\mu_0\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ and define $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal V}\subset\mathcal P(\mathcal C_T)$ by
\[
\mathfrak K_{\mathcal V}
:=\big\{\nu:\nu\circ e_0^{-1}=\mu_0,\,\,
\nu\circ e_t^{-1}\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\text{ for every }t\in[0,T],\,\,
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathcal V(t,\nu\circ e_t^{-1})<\infty\big\},
\]
where $e_t(w):=w(t)$ for $w\in\mathcal{C}_T$.
		
For any weak solution $(X,B)$ of \eqref{2.1} in the sense of Definition~$\rm\ref{de.2.1}$, defined on a filtered probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\{\mathcal F_t\},\mathbb P)$, set
\[
Y:=\bigl(X(0),B|_{[0,T]}\bigr),\,\,Y_t:=\bigl(X(0),B|_{[0,t]}\bigr),\,\,t\in[0,T].
\]
Such a weak solution $(X,B)$ is called compatible if $X$ is continuous and adapted and, for every $t\in[0,T]$ and every bounded Borel function
\[
h:C([0,t];\mathbb R^d)\rightarrow\mathbb R,
\]
one has
\[
\mathbb E\left[
h\bigl(X|_{[0,t]}\bigr)|\sigma(Y)\right]
=
\mathbb E\left[h\bigl(X|_{[0,t]}\bigr)|\sigma(Y_t)\right]\,\,\text{a.s.}
\]
A compatible weak solution $(X,B)$ is called $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal V}$-admissible if $\mathcal L_X\in\mathfrak K_{\mathcal V}$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[$\rm(1)$] There exists a compatible $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal V}$-admissible weak solution of \eqref{2.1}.
\item[$\rm(2)$] Pathwise uniqueness in the sense of Definition~$\rm\ref{de.2.1}$ holds within the class of $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal V}$-admissible strong solutions.
\end{enumerate}
		
Then there exists a Borel measurable non-anticipative map
\[
\Phi:\mathbb R^d\times C([0,T];\mathbb R^m)\rightarrow C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)
\]
such that, for every $t\in[0,T]$, there is a Borel map
\[
\Phi_t:\mathbb R^d\times C([0,t];\mathbb R^m)\rightarrow C([0,t];\mathbb R^d)
\]
satisfying
\[
\Phi(x,w)|_{[0,t]}=\Phi_t\bigl(x,w|_{[0,t]}\bigr).
\]
		
		Moreover, on every filtered probability space carrying an
		$\mathbb R^m$-valued Brownian motion $B$ and an
		$\mathcal F_0$-measurable random variable $X_0$ with
		$\mathcal L_{X_0}=\mu_0$, the process
		$X=\Phi(X_0,B)$ is the unique $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal V}$-admissible strong solution of \eqref{2.1} in the sense of
		Definition~$\rm\ref{de.2.1}$.

[Thm 4 (Main theorem for $n=2$) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $f,g\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}(X)$ be nonzero rational functions.
    Let $PFD(\frac{1}{f})=P_1+L_1+H_1$ and $PFD(\frac{1}{g})=P_2+L_2+H_2$ be partial fraction decompositions over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, see Theorem \ref{thm: PFD}, where $L_i=\sum_{j=1}^{d_i}\frac{c_{i,j}}{X-\alpha_{i,j}}$ for $i=1,2$.
    Let $D=f(x)\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+g(y)\frac{\partial}{\partial y}$ be a derivation.

    Then the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For almost all primes, the derivation $D$ modulo $p$ is $p$-closed.
        \item One of the following is true:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item We have $L_1=L_2=0$.
        \item We have $P_1=P_2=H_1=H_2=0$, and 
        
        there exists $\eta\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, $\eta\ne 0$, such that for all $i,j$ we have $\eta c_{i,j}\in {\mathbb{Q}}$.
    \end{enumerate}
        \item There exists a non-constant $F\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}(x,y)$ such that $D(F)=0$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Moreover, we can write explicit formulas for the killed element:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item (2a) We can take: $F\coloneqq \int \frac{dx}{f}-\int \frac{dy}{g}$.
        \item (2b) We can take: $G \coloneqq \op{exp}\left(N\eta \left(\int \frac{dx}{f}-\int \frac{dy}{g}\right)\right)$, where $N\ne 0$ is any integer such that $N\eta c_{i,j}\in \mathbb{Z}$.
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main theorem for $n=2$

[Definition Kk:(K1 K2) of arXiv:2605.16963, 'Stochastic Euler Equations with Pseudo-differential Noise: Continuous and Discontinuous Pe'] Let $d, m \ge 1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$. A subset $\mathscr O\subset {\mathrm{OP}}\mathfrak M^{s}$ is said to be bounded if
		$
		\big\{\mathscr{p}: {\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p})\in \mathscr O\big\}\subset \mathfrak M^{s}
		$
		is bounded with respect to the seminorms in (equation OPM seminorms of the paper). Let $\varsigma \ge 0$.
		We define
		\[
		\mathbb{M}^{\varsigma} \triangleq \left\{\mathcal K:\
		\text{there exist }\mathcal H={\mathrm{diag}}(\mathcal H_{1},\cdots ,\mathcal H_{m})\in\mathrm{OP}\mathfrak M^{\varsigma}
		\text{ and }\mathcal E\in\mathrm{OP}\mathfrak M^0\text{ such that }
		\mathcal K=\mathcal H+\mathcal E
		\text{ and  (Kk:(K1 K2) of the paper)  holds} \right\},
		\]
		where condition (Kk:(K1 K2) of the paper) is specified as follows:
		\begin{enumerate}[label={$(\mathbf{K}^{\varsigma})$},leftmargin=0.79cm]
			\item  
			$\mathcal H_{i} \in {\mathrm{OP}}\mathcal M^{\varsigma}$ and $\mathcal H_{i} + \mathcal H_{i}^{*} \in {\mathrm{OP}}\mathcal M^{0}$ for $1 \le i \le m$. 
			Moreover, the symbols of $\mathcal H$ and $\mathcal E$ are commuting matrices.
		\end{enumerate}
		A subset $\mathscr{N} \subset \mathbb{M}^{\varsigma}$ is called bounded if for every
		$\mathcal K\in\mathscr N$,  one can find a decomposition
		$\mathcal K=\mathcal H_{\mathcal K}+\mathcal E_{\mathcal K}$ such that
		$
		\{\mathcal H_{i,\mathcal K}:\mathcal K\in\mathscr N,1 \le i \le m\}$
		is bounded in $\mathrm{OP}\mathcal M^{\varsigma}$, 
		$	\{\mathcal H_{i,\mathcal K}+\mathcal H^*_{i,\mathcal K}:\mathcal K\in\mathscr N,1 \le i \le m\}$  is bounded in $\mathrm{OP}\mathcal M^0$,  and $\{\mathcal G_{\mathcal K}:\mathcal K\in\mathscr N\}$
		are bounded in $\mathrm{OP}\mathfrak M^0$.
title: Definition Kk:(K1 K2) of arXiv:2605.16963

[Defn 2 of arXiv:2608.16144, 'Central limit theorem in R\'enyi divergence for lattice random variables'] Let $P$ and $Q$ be two probability distributions on a countable set $\mathcal{X}$, with probability mass functions $\{p(x)\}_{x\in\mathcal{X}}$ and $\{q(x)\}_{x\in\mathcal{X}}$, respectively. For $\alpha>0$ and $\alpha\neq 1$, the R\'enyi divergence $D_{\alpha}(P\|Q)$ of order $\alpha$ of $P$ from $Q$ is defined by
$$
D_{\alpha}(P\|Q)=\frac{1}{\alpha-1}\log \sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}} \frac{p(x)^{\alpha}}{q(x)^{\alpha-1}}.
$$
By taking a limit, one can define the R\'enyi divergence for special orders $\alpha=0, 1, \infty$ by
\begin{align*}
D_{0}(P\|Q) &=-\log Q(\{x\in\mathcal{X}: p(x)>0\}),\\
D_1(P\|Q)&=\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}} p(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{q(x)},\\
D_\infty(P\|Q) &= \log\sup_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\frac{p(x)}{q(x)},
\end{align*}
where $D_1(P\|Q)$ is the classical Kullback--Leibler divergence (i.e., relative entropy) and the subindex 1 is usually omitted.
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.16144

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.25949, '2608.25949'] Let $(M,g,J)$ be a K\"ahler surface, dim M=4 and  let $\De,
dim\De=2$ be  a complex, conformal distribution  which means that
  $L_{\xi}g=\theta(\xi)g$ for $\xi\in\G(\De)$ on the distribution
$\E=\De^{\perp}$. Then for all $X,Y\in\G(\E)$ we have
$2\n_XY_{|\De}=-g(X,Y)\theta-\om(X,Y)J\theta$.

[Lemma lem:elem of arXiv:2510.00214, 'On the local well-posedness of randomly forced reaction-diffusion equations with $\bm{L^2}'] If $\delta,\alpha\in(0\,,1)$ and $\chi\in[0\,,1]$, then
	\[
		t^\alpha\mathrm{e}^{-\beta t}\int_0^t s^{-\alpha}|\log_+(1/s)|^\chi\, \mathrm{e}^{\beta s}\,\mathrm{d} s
		\lesssim \beta^{-(1-\delta)},
	\]
	uniformly for all $t\in(0\,,1]$ and $\beta>0$. When $\chi=0$, we can choose even $\delta=0$.

body:
[Lemma 49 of arXiv:2609.02819, 'Adelic Points and Unramified Brauer Approximation for Classifying Stacks'] A procyclic subgroup of $\Gal(\bar{k}/k)$ means a closed subgroup
topologically generated by one element.  Inflation induces an isomorphism
\[
 \operatorname{inf}:H^1(\Gamma,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(k,M).
\]
Under this isomorphism, the group in \eqref{eq:def-Sha-cyc} is identified with
\[
 \left\{\alpha\in H^1(k,M):
 \alpha|_P=0\text{ in }H^1(P,M)
 \text{ for every procyclic subgroup }
 P\subseteq\Gal(\bar{k}/k)\right\}.
\]
In particular, $\Sha^1_{\mathrm{cyc}}(k,M)$ is independent of the chosen
finite Galois extension $K/k$ through which the action factors.

[Propo conv_dist_vertex_subcritical of arXiv:2606.15339, 'Uniform integrability of the distance to the nearest leaf in random trees'] Let $\mathcal{T}_n$  have type II or III. Then
\[
\partial(\mathcal{T}_n,v_n)\xrightarrow{d}\partial(\mathcal{T}^{*}).
\]
Equivalently, for every $k\ge 1$,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbf{P}\bigl(\partial(\mathcal{T}_n,v_n)\ge k\bigr)
=\mathbf{P}\bigl(\partial(\mathcal{T}^{*})\ge k\bigr).
\]

body:
[Proposition H1sn of arXiv:2609.01990, 'Jacquet-Zagier treatment of the beyond endoscopy trace formula for \(\GL_2\)'] The term given by \(H_s^1(n)\) is equal to
    \[
    \frac{(4n)^{1-s} \pi^{s-\frac{1}{2}}}{4\Gamma(\frac{s+1}{2})} \sum_{f=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{f^{3-2s}} \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{l^{2-s}} \sum_{\xi \in \mathbb{Z}} \text{Kl}_{l,f}(\xi,n) I_{l,f}(\xi,n)
    \]
    where
    \begin{equation}
        I_{l,f}(\xi,n) = \int_{-1}^{1} (1-y^2)^{\frac{1}{2}-s} F_s(y) \Phi_1\left(\frac{\sqrt{\pi} lf^2}{2 \sqrt{n(1-y^2)}} \right) e\left(\frac{-\xi \sqrt{n} y}{2lf^2}\right) dy 
    \end{equation}
    with 
    \begin{equation}
        \Phi_1(x) = \Gamma \left(1-\frac{s}{2}, x^2\right) 
    \end{equation}
    and 
    \[
    \text{Kl}_{l,f}(\xi,n) = \sum_{\substack{a \mod 4lf^2\\a^2-4n \equiv 0 \mod f^2 \\ 
    \frac{a^2 -4n}{f^2} \equiv 0,1 \mod 4}} \left( \frac{a^2-4n/f^2}{l}\right) e^{\frac{2 \pi i \xi a}{4lf^2}}, \qquad \left( \frac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right): \text{ Legendre symbol}
    \]
title: Proposition H1sn of arXiv:2609.01990

body:
[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2605.20041, '\makeatletter \HRule \\[0.4cm] { \huge \bfseries Fourier Representations of Spectral Densi'] There exists a long-memory strictly stationary centered real-valued Gaussian process $(X_{t})_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ whose spectral measure is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure and whose spectral density is $\log$-summable and has an almost everywhere unboundedly divergent Fourier series.

As a result, this process is also purely nondeterministic and mixing (so it is weakly mixing and ergodic as well), and, denoting $f$ its spectral density, we have the following linear representations: $$X_{t}=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}a_{j}\varepsilon_{t-j}~\text{for all}~t \in \mathbb{Z},\,\text{and}~f(\lambda)=\frac{\sigma_{0}^{2}}{2\pi}\,{\left|\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}a_{j}\e^{ij\lambda}\right|}^{2}~\text{for all}~\lambda \in \mathbb{R},$$ where $(a_{j})_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a square-summable sequence with $a_{0}=1$, and $(\varepsilon_{t})_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ are i.i.d. Gaussian variables with mean zero and variance $\sigma_{0}^{2} > 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop: adding external field fluctuation of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Fix a good configuration $\tau\in\{0,1\}^n$.
    Let $\mathsf{a}_i=\frac{\mu^+_{\Lambda_N,{\epsilon} H^i}(\mathcal{E}_\tau)}{\mu^+_{\Lambda_N,{\epsilon} H^{i-1}}(\mathcal{E}_\tau)}-1$. For any $\kappa_1>0$, there exist absolute constants $c_2,c_3>0$, $c_4=c_4(\kappa_{1})>0$ and three sequences of random variables $\mathsf{b}_1,\cdots,\mathsf{b}_{n}$, $\mathsf{c}_1,\cdots,\mathsf{c}_{n}$ and $\mathsf{d}_1,\cdots,\mathsf{d}_{n}$ such that the following holds. We remark that $\mathsf{a}_i$, $\mathsf{b}_i$, $\mathsf{c}_i$, and $\mathsf{d}_i$ depend on the choice of $\tau$. When this dependency needs to be emphasized, we write them as $\mathsf{a}_i(\tau)$, $\mathsf{b}_i(\tau)$, $\mathsf{c}_i(\tau)$, and $\mathsf{d}_i(\tau)$.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item There exists a filtration $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for any $1\le i\le n$, $\mathsf{a}_i,\mathsf{b}_i,\mathsf{c}_i$ and $\mathsf{d}_i$ are measurable with respect to $\mathcal{F}_i$.
        \item For any $1\le i\le n$, conditioned on $\mathcal{F}_{i-1}$, $\mathsf{b}_i$ is a mean $0$ Gaussian variable with variance $\sigma_i^2$ where $ \sigma_i^2\le c_2{\epsilon}^2M^{\frac{7}{4}}$. In addition, if $\tau_i=1$, then we have $\sigma_i^2\ge c_3{\epsilon}^2M^{\frac{7}{4}}.$ 
        \item For any $1\le i\le n$, conditioned on $\mathcal{F}_{i-1}$, $\mathsf{c}_i$ has mean $0$. In addition, we have ${\mathbb{E}} \big(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathsf{c}_i\big)^2\\=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\big(\mathsf{c}_i\big)^2\le c_2{\epsilon}^4M^{\frac{7}{2}}\cdot n$.
        \item  ${\mathbb{E}} \sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathsf{d}_i^2\le c_4{\epsilon}^4M^{\frac{7}{2}}\cdot \iota^{-\frac{7}{4}-\kappa_{1}}$. In addition, we have ${\mathbb{P}}\Big(|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathsf{d}_i| \ge \sqrt{ \iota^{-2\kappa_{1}}\cdot \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sigma_i^2}\Big\}\Big) \\\le c_4\iota^{\kappa_{1}}.$
        \item For any $1\le i\le n$, we have ${\mathbb{P}}\Big(|\mathsf{a}_i-\mathsf{b}_i-\mathsf{c}_i-\mathsf{d}_i|\ge c_2({\epsilon} M^{\frac{7}{8}})^{2.7}\Big)\le c_2^{-1}\exp(-c_2\iota^{-\frac{7}{80}})$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; F0124_C21 version 1; status: independently checked proof. For the two-sided nearest-neighbor iid walk with independent iid fair sign scenery, let h_l(theta) be the unrestricted constant-word WHOLE no-cut coefficients in the positive interval expansion, theta=(1-p)/p. At theta=1/18 (p=18/19), the whole-block generating function H has a genuine positive-axis pole s in (9/11,1), so its coefficient root limsup exceeds one. The confined-path denominator G has G(9/11)=7/11>0 and G(1)<=-1/12<0; at a zero E=0 the auxiliary j is strictly negative, preventing cancellation in H=zq-z^2j^2/E. Monotonicity of coefficients in theta gives nonsummability for every 0<p<=18/19. Along a subsequence, whole-interval occupation conditioned on every competitor vacant tends to one, obstructing any summable length-only bound under every partial conditioning. This is a stronger raw-method barrier than confined-loop geometric estimates; it does not show any RWRS exterior is bad. Competition-normalized or restricted-history methods may still work. No novelty is asserted.

body:
Let a target width-D ReLU FNN have depth q>=1, weights A_i and biases a_i, i=1,...,q. Let the frozen width-D ReLU FNN have depth L>=q, weights W_l, and let every adapted bias be freely trainable. All weights are real D-by-D matrices; every layer, including the output layer, applies ReLU. Let X subset R^D be bounded, M=floor(L/q), and partition the frozen layers into consecutive blocks P_i={(i-1)M+1,...,iM} for i<q and P_q={(q-1)M+1,...,L}. Define B_i as the ordered product of W_l in P_i (later layers on the left), and E_i=A_i-B_i. For fixed integer 1<=R<=D, assume every W_l and every B_i+LR_j(E_i) for i=1,...,q and integers 0<=j<=R(M-1) are nonsingular, with fixed nested SVD truncations for each E_i. If R>=ceil(max_i rank(E_i)/M), then there exist rank-at-most-R additive weight updates at every frozen layer and choices of all biases such that the adapted FNN equals the target FNN at every x in X. This is an existence/expressivity statement; it provides no guarantee for gradient descent, fixed or zero biases, an unbounded input domain, or bounded-bit parameters.
Target depth q>=1 and frozen depth L>=q, equal square width D
Bounded input set and ReLU at every layer
All biases are trainable without size constraints
Assumption1: frozen weights and every stated partial low-rank correction are nonsingular
Rank threshold at least ceil(maximum block error rank /floor(L/q))
No claim about learnability or finite-sample excess risk

[Definition 11 (Block RQ decomposition) of arXiv:2608.28991, 'Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventio'] For client $k\in[K]$ with block ancestor structure $(\prec_k^\rblk,\cC_k)$, a block RQ decomposition of $\bH_k\in\bbR^{p_k\times n_k}$ is a factorization
\[
\bH_k=\bR_k\bQ_k,
\]
where $\bR_k\in\bbR^{p_k\times p_k}$ is block upper triangular with respect to $\cC_k$, namely
$[\bR_k]_{\rho_k(C_{k,i}),\rho_k(C_{k,j})}=0$  unless $C_{k,i}\preceq_k^\rblk C_{k,j}$,
and $\bQ_k\in\bbR^{p_k\times n_k}$ is row full-rank with unit-norm rows. Moreover, for every block $C\in\cC_k$ and every $i\in\rho_k(C)$, the row $[\bQ_k]_{i,:}$ is orthogonal to every row of $[\bQ_k]_{\bigcup_{C'\in anc_k^\rblk(C)}\rho_k(C'),:}$.
title: Block RQ decomposition

body: [Lem GH-finite-errors of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] Suppose that $(M_1,d_1)$ and $(M_2,d_2)$ are metric spaces so that $d_{{\mathrm{GH}}}((M_1,d_1), (M_2,d_2)) \leq \varepsilon$.  Then for all $x_1,\ldots,x_m \in M_1$ there is $y_1,\ldots,y_m \in M_2$ so that for all $i < j \leq m$ we have $$\left|d_1(x_i,x_j) - d_2(y_i,y_j)\right| \leq 4\varepsilon\,.$$

[Definition 2 (Strong solution) of arXiv:2608.21014, 'The stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equation in critical spaces'] Let $f\in L^1(a,\tau;X_0)$ a.s.\ and $g\in L^2(a,\tau;\gamma(\ell^2,X_{1/2}))$ a.s.\ be progressively measurable. A progressively measurable process $u\colon[a,\tau]\times\Omega\to X_0$ is called a \emph{strong solution} to~\eqref{eq:linear-stochastic-evolution} on $[a,\tau]$ if $u\in C([a,\tau];X_0)\cap L^2(a,\tau;X_1)$ a.s.\ and a.s.\ for all $t\in [a,\tau]$ 
    $$u(t)-u_a +\int_a^t Au(s)\, \dd s = \int_a^t f(s)\,\dd s+ \int_a^t g(s)\,\dd W(s).$$

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2608.27218, 'Mapping class groups have a unique Polish group structure'] Let \( S \) be a non-separating sphere in \( M_{1,2} \). 
		\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
			\item There are exactly three spheres disjoint from \( S \), one of which is separating.
			\item Let \( f \in \mcg(M_{1,2}) \) be a nontrivial mapping class such that \( f(S) = S \) and such that \( f \) stabilizes each component of \( \partial M_{1,2} \). 
				Then \( f \) transposes the non-separating spheres disjoint from \( S \) and \( f(S') \neq S' \) for every non-separating sphere \( S' \neq S \). 
				Moreover, if \( g \in \mcg(M_{1,2}) \) satisfies \( g(S) = S \), then either (i) \( g(S') = S' \) for every sphere \( S' \) or (ii) \( g(S') = f(S') \) for every sphere \( S' \). 
		\end{enumerate}

body: In graph theory, Kuratowski's theorem is a mathematical forbidden graph characterization of planar graphs, named after Kazimierz Kuratowski. It states that a finite graph is planar if and only if it does not contain a subgraph that is a subdivision of K_5 (the complete graph on five vertices) nor of K_{3,3} (the complete bipartite graph on six vertices with parts of size three, the utility graph).

body:
[Proposition p:PDirIntESA of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] Fix~$\pi\in\msP(\mbfT_\circ)$.
Then, the operator~$\tparen{\widehat\boldsymbol\mssL, \mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}}$ is essentially self-adjoint on~$L^2(\widehat\boldsymbol\nu_\pi)$.
Furthermore, its closure~$\big({\widehat\boldsymbol\mssL_\pi,\msD(\widehat\boldsymbol\mssL_\pi)}\big)$ is independent of~$\msR$.
\begin{proof}
We divide the proof into three steps.

\medskip\emph{Fiber-wise essential self-adjointness}.\quad
Fix~$\mbfs\in\mbfT_\circ$.
We claim that the operator~$\tparen{\mssI\otimes \boldsymbol\mssL^\mbfs, \mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}}$ is essentially self-adjoint on~$L^2(\delta_\mbfs\otimes \boldsymbol\nu)$ for every~$\mbfs\in\mbfT$.

We note that~$\Cyl{}{}$ embeds as~$L^2(\delta_\mbfs)\otimes \Cyl{}{}={\mathbb R}\otimes \Cyl{}{}\cong \Cyl{}{}$ into~$L^2(\delta_\mbfs\otimes\boldsymbol\nu)$, and we shall therefore, whenever necessary, regard~$\Cyl{}{}$ as a subspace of~$L^2(\delta_\mbfs\otimes\boldsymbol\nu)$ without further mention to the embedding.
Since~$(\boldsymbol\mssL^\mbfs,\Cyl{}{})$ is essentially self-adjoint on~$L^2(\boldsymbol\nu)$ for every~$\mbfs\in\mbfT$, the operator~$(\mssI\otimes\boldsymbol\mssL^\mbfs,\Cyl{}{})$ is essentially self-adjoint on~$L^2(\delta_\mbfs\otimes\boldsymbol\nu)$ for every~$\mbfs\in\mbfT$ by~[ReeSim80a].

Then, it suffices to show that~$\mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}$ contains~$\Cyl{}{}$.
To this end, we argue as follows. 
Since~$\msR_0$ is an algebra and separates points from open sets, and since~$\mbfs\in\mbfT_\circ$ (as opposed to~$\mbfT$), for each~$k$ there exists~$\varphi_k\in \msR_0$ with~$\varphi_k(s_k)=s_k^{-1}$ and~$\varphi_k\equiv 0$ on~$[0,s_{k+1}]\cup [s_{k-1},1]$ (where, conventionally,~$s_0\eqdef 1$).
Then, for each~$f\in\Cyl{}{}$, the function~$(\varphi_k\otimes f)^\star$ satisfies~$(\varphi_k\otimes f)^\star\in \mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}$.
Furthermore, in light of~(equation eq:FundFuncTrid of the paper), we have~$(\varphi_k\otimes f)^\star \big({\mathrm{em}(\mbfs,\mbfx)}\big)= f(x_k)$ for every~$k$.
Since~$f$ was arbitrary in~$\msA$, since every element of~$\Cyl{}{}$ has the form~$\Pi_{a\in A} f_a({\,\cdot\,}_a)$ for some finite~$A\subset{\mathbb N}$, and since~$\mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}$ is an algebra, this shows that~$\mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}\supset \Cyl{}{}$, which concludes the proof of the claim.

\medskip\emph{Essential self-adjointness of the direct integral}.\quad
In light of Remark~(r:DirInt of the paper), the operator~$\tparen{\widehat\boldsymbol\mssL, \mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}}$ is the direct integral of the measurable field of closable operators~$\mbfs\mapsto \tparen{\mssI\otimes \boldsymbol\mssL^\mbfs, \mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}}$.
The conclusion then follows from Lemma~(l:DirIntESA of the paper) and the first step.

\medskip\emph{Independence from~$\msR$}.\quad
It is clear from~(equation eq:ExtendedLonElementaryCyl of the paper) that, independently of the choice of~$\msR$, the domain~$\msD(\widehat\boldsymbol\mssL_\pi)$ contains the algebra~$\hCylP{}{0}$ defined with~$\msR=\mcB_b(\mbbI)$.
The conclusion then follows from the essential self-adjointness of $\tparen{\widehat\boldsymbol\mssL, \mathrm{em}^*\hCylP{}{0}}$, similarly to the proof of the independence from~$\mbbV_\pi$ in the proof of Theorem~(t:DirInt of the paper).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition FreeYMM of arXiv:2607.19037, 'Semiclassical analysis for Yang--Mills \\ random connections on compact surfaces'] Define the random connection $A^\mathsf{Free}_{\mathcal{S},\sigma}$ on $\mathcal{S}$ via its expectation for any functional $F$  by
\[
 \mathbb{E}  \Big[ F\big(A^\mathsf{Free}_{\mathcal{S},\sigma} \big)\Big]
=
\int_{G^{2g}} \prod_{a\in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f)} \mathrm{d} g_a\, 
 \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ F\Big( \iota_V\mathcal{L}_V^{-1}\left(\xi\sigma \right)+\sum_{a'\in\mathsf{Crit}_1(f)} \log g_{a'}[U_{a'}] \Big)  \Bigg].
\]
The law of $A^\mathsf{Free}_{\mathcal{S},\sigma}$ seen as a measure on $\mathcal{D}'^1(\mathcal{S},\mathfrak{g})$ is called the free boundary  Yang--Mills measure on $\mathcal{S}$.
title: Free boundary Yang--Mills measure

body:
[Lemma lem:packetless-exterior-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For every fixed $L<\infty$ there are $A_L<\infty$ and a numerical
$B<\infty$ with the following property.  Fix $c\ge1$, $m\le cN$, and a
complete doubled ribbon $\Gamma$ with total nonconstant slot count
$r\le L\log n$, and keep one packetless
aggregate-Ricci component $\mathcal C_\star$, including its selected
$\mathsf V$ incidence and reflected root, as an opaque part of the
once-normalized positive majorant $\mathfrak a_\star$.  Suppose no
unrecorded port-open singleton or packet assignment targets
$\mathcal C_\star$.  Let $\Omega_{\rm ext}$ be the complete temporal
records of all other Haar-separated components, let $R_{\rm ord}$ be
their ordinary selected roots, let $\mathfrak e_\rho$ be their factored
endpoint resources, and let $D_{\rm ext}\le1$ be the product of their
retained fractional debits.  If
$\mathfrak a_\omega$ is the resulting positive \emph{doubled} scalar
majorant for $\omega\in\Omega_{\rm ext}$, then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{\rm ext}}\mathfrak a_\omega
 \le A_L^r(r+1)^B\mathfrak a_\star D_{\rm ext}
       \prod_{\rho\in R_{\rm ord}}(m\mathfrak e_\rho).}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12r_8}$}
\]
The fixed special component supplies no endpoint coupon in this estimate.

[Prop 6 (Purple/Strong-Red overlap reduction) of arXiv:2608.26259, 'Cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for Potts Glauber Dynamics\\on lattice at High Temperature'] Set \(V_{\mathrm{P}}^{(1)}:=V_{\mathrm{P}}\), and, conditional on
\(\mathcal H_{G,Y}\vee\mathcal H_{\mathrm{SR}}\), let
\(V_{\mathrm{P}}^{(2)}\) be an independent copy of
\(V_{\mathrm{P}}^{(1)}\). Similarly, set
\(V_{\mathrm{SR}}^{(1)}:=V_{\mathrm{SR}}\), and, conditional on
\(\mathcal H_{G,Y}\vee\mathcal H_{\mathrm{P}}\), let
\(V_{\mathrm{SR}}^{(2)}\) be an independent copy of
\(V_{\mathrm{SR}}^{(1)}\). Then, for every \(x_0\in[q]^\Lambda\),

\[
\left\|
\Law(X_t^{x_0})-\pi
\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le
\left(
\mathbb E\left[
q^{|V_{\mathrm{P}}^{(1)}\cap V_{\mathrm{P}}^{(2)}|}-1
\right]
\right)^{1/2}
+
\left(
\mathbb E\left[
q^{|V_{\mathrm{SR}}^{(1)}\cap V_{\mathrm{SR}}^{(2)}|}-1
\right]
\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
d_\Lambda(t)
\le
\left(
\mathbb E\left[
q^{|V_{\mathrm{P}}^{(1)}\cap V_{\mathrm{P}}^{(2)}|}-1
\right]
\right)^{1/2}
+
\left(
\mathbb E\left[
q^{|V_{\mathrm{SR}}^{(1)}\cap V_{\mathrm{SR}}^{(2)}|}-1
\right]
\right)^{1/2}.
\]

body: Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables with E[X_i] = 0 and Var(X_i) < infinity for each i, and let S_k = X_1 + ... + X_k. Then for every lambda > 0, P(max_{1 <= k <= n} |S_k| >= lambda) <= Var(S_n) / lambda^2 = (sum_{i=1}^n Var(X_i)) / lambda^2. [Theorem 16 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Suppose Assumptions \ref{assump:X} and \ref{assump:dynamics} hold. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item There exist domains $\cS_\theta^+$ for $(C_\theta,R_\theta)$ and 
$\cS_g^+$ for $(C_g,R_g)$ for which the kernels and processes of
Definition \ref{def:DMFT} are well-defined and unique.
That is, (\ref{eq:dmft-theta}--\ref{eq:dmft-response}) have unique
$\cF_t$-adapted solutions for any $(C_g,R_g) \in \cS_g^+$,
the series (\ref{eq:dmft-Cg}--\ref{eq:dmft-Rg}) are absolutely convergent for
any $(C_\theta,R_\theta) \in \cS_\theta^+$, and there exists a
unique fixed point $(C_\theta,R_\theta,C_g,R_g) \in \cS_\theta^+
\times \cS_g^+$ satisfying (\ref{eq:dmft-Ctheta}--\ref{eq:dmft-Rg}).
\item Fix any $T>0$ not depending on $n$. Define
\[\g^t=\X\btheta^t-\int_0^t R_g(t,s)\btheta^s\d s.\]
Let $\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \delta_{\{(\theta_i^t,g_i^t,b_i^t)\}_{t \in
[0,T]}}$ be the empirical measure of sample paths
$(\theta_i^t,g_i^t,b_i^t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ and let
$\Law(\{(\theta^t,g^t,b^t)\}_{t \in [0,T]})$ be the joint law of these 
processes in Definition \ref{def:DMFT}, as probability measures on
$C([0,T],\R^3)$. Then almost surely
as $n \to \infty$,
\[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \delta_{\{(\theta_i^t,g_i^t,b_i^t)\}_{t \in [0,T]}}
\to \Law(\{(\theta^t,g^t,b^t)\}_{t \in [0,T]}) \text{ weakly and in
Wasserstein-2.}\]
\item Write $\langle \cdot \rangle$ for the expectation over $\{\b^t\}_{t \geq
0}$, conditional on $\X$ and $\btheta^0$. Then for any fixed $s,t \geq 0$
with $s \leq t$, almost surely as $n \to \infty$,
\[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \langle \theta_i^t\theta_i^s \rangle
\to C_\theta(t,s), \quad
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \langle g_i^t g_i^s \rangle
\to C_g(t,s), \quad
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \langle \theta_i^tb_i^s
\rangle \to \sqrt{2\gamma}\int_0^s R_\theta(t,\tau) \d \tau.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

STATUS: proof (unaudited), own-work draft. For the coupled scalar two-token joint-head factored-attention logistic gradient flow, every nonzero-imbalance leaf k^2-q^2=C has a unique reduced saddle and two escaping basins. In full R^3 almost every initialization escapes with kq,v of matching infinite sign, factors O(sqrt(log |v|)), head-normalized limit +/-e_v and margin Gamma_+ or Gamma_-. The finite saddle-stable set plus balanced planes is null. Balanced k=-q, v>0 and max root<kq<0 instead collapse to uniform attention and margin min a_i, showing an actual third fate on a null surface.

# Target 1: almost-everywhere full-space factored gradient-flow classification

Version 1, proof unaudited. Own work; novelty unestablished.
This concerns continuous gradient flow, not arbitrary-step GD.

## Statement

For n>=2, b_i,kappa_i>0, 0<a_i<b_i, set
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s) and
L(v,k,q)=mean_i log(1+exp(-v h_i(kq))).
Let p_bar be the unique zero of mean_i h_i. For every initial point with
C=k^2-q^2!=0, the Euclidean gradient flow exists globally forward and has
exactly one of these outcomes:

1. convergence to a finite point on the stationary curve v=0,kq=p_bar;
2. v,kq->+infinity, loss->0, normalized direction (v,k,q)/norm ->(1,0,0);
3. v,kq->-infinity, loss->0, normalized direction ->(-1,0,0).

The set in outcome 1, together with the excluded balanced surfaces C=0,
has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero. Hence almost every finite
initialization belongs to one of the two escaping basins. Both basins
are open in the FULL parameter space, are nonempty, and have respective
normalized minimum margins Gamma_+=min_i(a_i+b_i) and Gamma_-=min_i(b_i-a_i).
The second is strictly inferior, as in claim 010. The known imbalance
invariant is used for reduction, not claimed as a new result.

We do not classify trajectories on C=0 in this theorem. They really allow
another fate: on k=q=0, v solves v_dot=mean_i a_i/(1+exp(v a_i))>0,
so v->infinity and L->0 while attention stays uniform. In fact a relatively
open subset of the balanced plane has this fate: if k=-q!=0, v>0 and
R<kq<0, where R=max_i rho_i<0, then v increases, s increases toward zero,
and k,q tend to zero. To check this, all h_i(s)>=c>0, forcing v->infinity.

must not be omitted.

(k^2+q^2)^2=C^2+4s^2. Thus on a fixed nonzero-C leaf,

interval. The smooth full flow therefore has no finite-time blow-up,
in either time direction. Nonzero-C leaf coordinates are global charts on
each sheet: for C>0 fix sign k, solve
k=sign(k)sqrt((alpha_C(s)+C)/2), q=s/k;
for C<0 instead fix sign q and use the symmetric formula.

-A<=F_v<=0, F_0 strictly increases with unique zero p_bar, and G>0.

on each sheet. With u=s-p_bar, the two good quadrants v,u>0 and v,u<0
are forward invariant: s_dot has sign v; on the boundary v=0 the vector
field F_0(s) points into the respective quadrant. More explicitly, in
the positive quadrant v_dot>=-A v, so a strictly positive v cannot hit zero
in finite time, and u increases. Reflection treats the negative quadrant.

In a bad quadrant v>0,u<0, F(v,s)<=F_0(s)<0 and s_dot>0.
Both coordinates move monotonically toward their axes until one axis is
crossed or the orbit stays forever. Crossing an axis enters a good quadrant;
uniqueness excludes hitting the equilibrium in finite time. If the orbit
stays in the bad quadrant, it has a finite limit. Continuity and monotonicity
force F=alpha_C vG=0 at that limit, hence it is the saddle.
The other bad quadrant is handled by the reflected links -h_i(-s).
Nonstationary points on an axis enter a good quadrant immediately.

## Escape from good quadrants

Consider the positive quadrant. Then s increases from s_0>p_bar.
Suppose s tends to finite P. If v is bounded, compactness and
alpha_C G>0 imply integral_0^infinity v(t)dt<infinity.
Since |v_dot|<=H, the nonnegative function v is uniformly continuous;
the elementary disjoint-triangle argument gives v->0. But then
v_dot->F_0(P)>0, contradiction.

If v is unbounded, put R=max_i rho_i, h_i(rho_i)=0. If P<=R,
an example j with root R has h_j(s(t))<=0, hence g_j>=1/2;
on the compact s interval its derivative is >=d>0. Consequently
s_dot>=|C| d v/(2n). A finite P again implies integral v<infinity

 ds/dv=alpha_C(s) v (mean g_i h_i')/(mean g_i h_i)
       >=|C| d v/H,

contradicting finite P. Thus s->infinity. Eventually all h_i>=c>0;
v increases and cannot remain bounded, since bounded v keeps every g_i
bounded below. Therefore v->infinity. Reflection proves negative escape.

For the direction, let kappa_0=min_i kappa_i. On the positive tail,
alpha_C(s)<=|C|+2s and

 ds/dv<=(4M/c)(|C|+2s)v exp(-2kappa_0 s).

Thus d[exp(kappa_0 s)]/dv <=C_1 v, because

Integration gives s=O(log v). Since k^2+q^2=alpha_C(s), both
factors are O(sqrt(log v)) and are negligible relative to v.
The negative branch is identical after reflection. Endpoint margin and
zero-loss limits follow. By fixed C and |s|->infinity, both |k| and |q|
also tend to infinity (their squared difference is constant).

At the reduced equilibrium the linearization is

 [[-A_s,B_s],[alpha_C(p_bar) B_s,0]],
 A_s=mean h_i(p_bar)^2/4, B_s=mean h_i'(p_bar)/2>0.

Its determinant is negative; it is a hyperbolic saddle. The local stable
manifold is one-dimensional. The global stable set on a leaf is contained
in its countably many backward integer-time flow images, so is planar null;
the flow is a smooth local diffeomorphism (indeed globally defined here).

The full stationary curve E={v=0,kq=p_bar} is closed. The set
S={initial points whose distance to E tends to zero} is Borel: express
the limiting condition using countable thresholds and integer times.
For C!=0 our classification shows S is exactly the convergent set;
the leaf coordinate formulas also show convergence of k,q when s->p_bar.

the two planes k=q and k=-q, also null. This proves the asserted full-space

If for a time-slice $U_1(-T)$ (resp. $U_2(-T)$) of the spherical cap supersolution $U_1$ (resp. subsolution $U_2$) one has $u_0\leq U_1(-T)$  (resp. $\geq$), then $u(t) \leq U_1(t-T)$ (resp. $\geq$) for all $t>0$ for which the flows are defined.

body:
[Proposition 34 (Bulk confinement and one-outlier alternative) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(M_N\) denote either \(M_N^{(4)}\) or \(M_N^f\).  For every fixed
\(\delta>0\), all but possibly one eigenvalue of \(M_N\) lie in
\([-2-\delta,2+\delta]\) with probability \(1-o(1)\).  More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item if \(|\theta|\le1\), then
\(\spec(M_N)\subset[-2-\delta,2+\delta]\) with probability \(1-o(1)\);
\item if \(|\theta|>1\), then there is one eigenvalue on the side determined
by \(\theta\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{\rm out}(M_N)\longrightarrow
 \rho_\theta=\theta+\theta^{-1}.
\end{equation}
All remaining eigenvalues lie in \([-2-\delta,2+\delta]\).  In particular,
if \(0<\delta<|\rho_\theta|-2\), the outlier is the unique eigenvalue outside
that interval with probability \(1-o(1)\).
\end{enumerate}
title: Bulk confinement and one-outlier alternative

body: [Theorem 2 (Backward heat flow and the asymptotic distribution of zeros) of arXiv:2511.01456, 'Zero distribution of multiplicative Hermite and Laguerre polynomials'] Let $(P_n(x))_{n\in \N}$ be a sequence of polynomials  such that $\deg P_n = n$ for all $n\in \N$. Fix $t>0$.  Suppose that all zeros of each $P_n$ are real and belong to some  interval $[-C,C]$. Suppose also that, as $n\to\infty$,  $\llbracket  P_n \rrbracket_n$ converges  to some probability measure  $\rho$ weakly on $\R$. Then,  for every $t\geq 0$,  $\llbracket  \eee^{- \frac t{2n} \partial_x^2 } P_n\rrbracket_n$ converges  to $\rho \boxplus \mathsf{sc}_t$ weakly on $\R$. Here, $\boxplus$ denotes the free additive convolution of probability measures on $\R$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Backward heat flow and the asymptotic distribution of zeros

body:
[Theorem thrm:fatshatteringotimality of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho,\mathfrak{m})$ be a compact $d$-Ahlfors regular metric measure space of diameter $1$, where $d>0$, and let $B,L>0$. There are constants $\varepsilon_0,c,C>0$

, such that: 
for any
$
    \mathcal F
    \subseteq
    \operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho),\mathbb{R};L)
$
and any
$
    0<\varepsilon<\min\{B/2,L\varepsilon_0\},
$
if
\begin{equation}

    \sup_{f\in\operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho),[-B,B];L)}
    \inf_{\hat{f}\in\mathcal F}
    \|f-\hat{f}\|_\infty
\le
    \varepsilon,
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}

    c
    \left(
        \frac{L}{\varepsilon}
    \right)^d
\le
    \operatorname{fat}_{\varepsilon}(\mathcal F)
\le
    C
    \left(
        \frac{L}{\varepsilon}
    \right)^d.
\end{equation}
In particular, $
    \mathcal{F}_{M:L}
\subseteq
    \operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho),\mathbb{R};L)$ for any $M\in \mathbb{N}_+
$ and there is a constant $C_d'>0$
\footnote{Depending only on $(X,\rho,\mathfrak m)$.}
, such that~(equation eq:eps_approx__minimaxformulation of the paper) holds for $\mathcal F_{M:L}$ whenever
$
    M
    \ge
    C_d'
    (L/\varepsilon)^d.
$

body:
Fix -1<a<1 and sigma_a(t)=t for t>=0, sigma_a(t)=a*t for t<0, applied coordinatewise. A depth-L network has L affine layers, activation after the first L-1 layers, and an affine final output. Its squared parameter cost is sum_ell (||W_ell||_F^2+||b_ell||_2^2). For a function f and domain Omega, R_L is the infimum of this cost over all such finite-width networks equal to f on Omega; R_L=+infinity if the class is empty. Let Omega be a nonempty bounded open subset of R^d. Suppose f=g composed with h on Omega, where h:R^d->R^k and g:R^k->R^m are continuous finite piecewise-affine functions and k>=1. Translate h by a constant vector so h(Omega) lies in the strictly positive orthant, and compensate the input of g. There exist fixed finite depths L_h,L_g and finite constant B, independent of L, such that for every integer L>=L_h+L_g, R_L<=B+k*(L-L_h-L_g). Here B is the total squared parameter cost of fixed networks realizing the translated factors. Hence limsup_(L->infinity) R_L/L<=k. For k=0, the corresponding factorization means f is constant on Omega; using zero weights and the final output bias gives R_L<=||f||_2^2 for every L. A prescribed-width version requires widths sufficient for the fixed end subnetworks and width at least k in the middle; arbitrary narrow architectures are excluded.

body:
A homogeneous linear equation c_1 x_1 + c_2 x_2 + ... + c_k x_k = 0 with integer coefficients is partition regular over the positive integers if for every finite coloring of the positive integers N, there exists a solution (x_1, ..., x_k) in N^k where all x_i have the same color.
c_1, ..., c_k are non-zero integers
k >= 2
title: Partition Regular Linear Equation

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03821, 'Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via...'] In this article, we investigate the two-species zero-range process, a multi-species generalization of the classical zero-range process. First, we analyze its condensation regime, which directly parallels its single-species counterpart. As our main result, we establish the dynamical metastable behavior of the location of the single condensate, showing that its motion is governed by a simple Markov chain on the accelerated time scale $N^{1+\alpha}$, where $N$ denotes the total number of particles in the system and the parameter $\alpha>1$ governs the attractivity of the system. Another novelty of this work lies in the proof technique, which integrates the recently developed resolvent approach with the $H^{1}$-approximation method to rigorously characterize metastability.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.03821: Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via...

body: [Example 2.7 of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] Let (X_1, X_2, X_3) be dependent random variables with K_3 as their dependency graph, and let (X_i)_{4≤i≤9} be independent random variables that are also independent of (X_1, X_2, X_3). Then the vertex-disjoint union G of K_3 and 6 copies of K_1 is a dependency graph for (X_i)_{i∈[9]}. If every X_i takes values in a real interval of length c ≥ 0, then for every t > 0 Janson's inequality (Theorem 1.4 of the paper, with χ_f(G) = 3) gives P(Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i − E[Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t²/(27c²)), while Corollary 2.6 gives the better bound P(Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i − E[Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−8t²/(81c²)). The second bound uses the fractional forest vertex cover with weight 1/2 on each of F_1 = {1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7}, F_2 = {1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9} and F_3 = {2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9}: each G[F_k] is K_2 plus 4 copies of K_1, so (Σ_k w_k √(Σ_{{i,j}∈E(G[F_k])} (c_i + c_j)² + Σ_{T∈T(F_k)} c_{min,k,T}²))² = ((3c/2)·√(2² + 1 + 4))² = 81c²/4.

[Proposition prop:gen_dissip of arXiv:2609.03164, 'Energy Decay Induced by Localized Coercivity in the 3D Navier--Stokes Equations'] For every $\rho\in\mathcal P$, the operator $A(\rho)$ generates a
$\mathcal C_0$-semigroup $(e^{tA(\rho)})_{t\ge0}$ on $H$ and satisfies
\[
\|e^{tA(\rho)}\|_{\mathcal L(H)}\le1,\qquad \forall t\ge0.
\]
If there exists $\alpha_\omega>0$ such that
\begin{equation}

-\langle A(\rho)v,v\rangle_H \ge \alpha_\omega\|v\|_H^2,
\qquad \forall v\in D(A_0),
\end{equation}
uniformly for $\rho\in\mathcal P$, then
\[
\|e^{tA(\rho)}\|_{\mathcal L(H)}\le e^{-\alpha_\omega t},
\qquad \forall t\ge0,
\]
uniformly in $\rho$.

Combining this with (equation eq:Dk_positive of the paper) yields
\[
\langle A(\rho)v,v\rangle_H
=
\langle A_0v,v\rangle_H-\langle D_{K(\rho)}v,v\rangle_H
\le 0.
\]
Thus $A(\rho)$ is dissipative on $D(A_0)$.

Here fat_r(F) is the sequential fat-shattering dimension of F at scale r: the maximal depth of a tree that F shatters at scale r.

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Let $X$ be a random walk indexed by an infinite critical tree $\mathcal{T}$, $x_0,\dots,x_n \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, and $T \in \mathbb{T}_{m,n+1}$ a rooted planar tree with vertex set $\{x_0,\dots,x_n\}$.   \]

body: [Defn def:NW of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\Phi = (\varphi_t)$ be a (topological) flow on $M$. OPEN per arXiv:2609.02820v1 (Theorems 1.5–1.6, PDF pp.5–6); bounded later-work check found no settlement. In the critical iid particle–hole model on Z^4, particles take synchronous discrete-time simple random-walk steps and settle permanently into stationary holes. After immediate cancellation the iid integer-valued excess η is nonconstant, has mean zero and an exponential moment. Does P(the origin is strictly closer in ℓ1 distance to an unfilled hole than to an active particle at time t) tend to zero for every such law? The source proves yes for d≤3 and exhibits counterexamples for d≥5 with P(η=1)=P(η=−1)=p and P(η=0)=1−2p. It explicitly says simulations suggest this counterexample extends to d=4. This general particle–hole question is distinct from the original binary one-car-or-one-spot parking initial law. Novelty: KNOWN source gap; current openness not certified by zero indexed citations.

Every target-dependent slot depends on at most three consecutive entries of

body:
[Proposition 1 (Dynamical fluctuation expansion) of arXiv:2604.04100, '\LARGE Learning Equilibrium Fluctuation Expansions from Overdamped Langevin Dynamics'] Let  $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and assume that $X_\varepsilon$ is the solution of \eqref{SDE-0}  with initial data $\xi_{\varepsilon}$ satisfying Assumption \ref{A1}. Let $(\bar{X}_m)_{0\leq m\leq n}$ be the solution of \eqref{eq-barX0-intro}, \eqref{eq-barX1-intro}, \eqref{eq-barXm-intro}, respectively. We define the remainder terms as $$
w_{\varepsilon,m}(t)
:=\frac{X_\varepsilon(t)-\sum_{k=0}^{m}\varepsilon^{k/2}\bar X_k(t)}{\varepsilon^{m/2}},
\qquad 0\le m\le n,\,\,t>0.
$$ 
Then for each $p\ge1$ and $t>0$, there exists a constant $C(p,t,n)>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$, such that for all $m=0,1,\cdots,n$,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathbb{E}\bigl|w_{\varepsilon,m}(t)\bigr|^{2p}\leq C(p,t,n)\varepsilon^{p}.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Dynamical fluctuation expansion

[Definition 6 (Causally calibrated response program) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] A calibrated response program is \emph{causally calibrated} if every primitive
response target $\mathsf Y_\alpha$ carries uniformly continuous truncations
$\rho_t^\alpha$ satisfying
\[
 \rho_T^\alpha=I,
 \qquad
 \rho_s^\alpha\rho_t^\alpha=\rho_{s\wedge t}^\alpha,
\]
and the descended primitive responses are equivariant:
\begin{equation}
 R_\alpha^{\mathbb I}(\bar r_tu)
 =\rho_t^\alpha R_\alpha^{\mathbb I}(u).
\end{equation}
The product response target is equipped with the coordinatewise truncation.
A declared constructor is causally calibrated when it is uniformly continuous
for the chosen response uniformities and commutes with the corresponding
truncations.  In the metric response spaces used below the truncations are
nonexpansive.
title: Causally calibrated response program

[Corollary 27 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Under the same assumption in Proposition \ref{proposition672}, with $\mathbb{P}_h$-probability at least $1-O_{\beta,\Delta,p_0}(\frac{1}{|V|})$, the edge field denoising process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ satisfies $R$- approximate conservation of variance up to time $\theta_*$ with constant 
    $$
R\leq\exp\left(\frac{16\beta\Delta\ln|V|}{\alpha_*}\right).

[Theorem 109 (Primitive--PBW boundary beyond finite depth) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let finite-dimensional ancestry shells $G_m$ have cumulative rank
$M(x)=\sum_{m\le x}\dim G_m$, let $w_m\downarrow0$, and let
$T=\mathscr S(\bigoplus_m w_mI_{G_m})\mathscr S^*$ with
$\mathscr S^*\mathscr S=I+$compact.  If
\[
 M(x)\sim Ax^\delta(\log x)^\gamma,
 \qquad
 w_m\sim cm^{-\alpha}(\log m)^\eta,
\]
then, with $p=\delta/\alpha$ and $\theta=\gamma+p\eta$,
\[
 \mathcal N_T(R)
 \sim Ac^p\alpha^{-\theta}e^{pR}R^\theta.
\]
The corresponding real Mellin and Fredholm laws follow from
\Cref{cc:thm:regular-dictionary}.  For an exponentially attenuated free tower
on $q\ge2$ generators, the primitive zeta function has a logarithmic branch at
$p_0=(\log q)/\kappa_0$, whereas the PBW tower has a simple pole and its
$k$-fold tensor power has a pole of order $k$:
\[
 \zeta_{\rm prim}(p_0+\varepsilon)=\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1),
 \qquad
 \zeta_{\rm PBW}(z)=\frac1{1-qe^{-\kappa_0z}}.
\]
The lattice spectrum generally produces log-periodic counting oscillations.

[Corollaryen 7 (Exact anchored minibatch envelope) of arXiv:2608.18999, '2608.18999'] Let \(H\) be a nonzero real Hilbert space, let \(1<p\le2\), let \(n\ge1\), and let
\(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent copies of an \(H\)-valued random vector
with mean \(\mu\).  Fix a deterministic anchor \(a\in H\), \(\tau>0\),
and assume
\[
M_a=\E\norm{X_1-a}^p<\infty.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}
=a+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n C_\tau(X_i-a).
\]
Then, for every \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
\alpha\norm{\E\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}-\mu}
+\frac\beta\tau
\E\norm{\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}
         -\E\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}}^2
\le
K_p\!\left(\alpha,\frac\beta n\right)
\tau^{1-p}M_a.
\end{equation}
The constant is the smallest possible uniform constant over this class, and
its phase boundary is \(\alpha=p\beta/n\).

\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma smash-lQ of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group, and let ${\mathcal{F}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_2$ be families of closed subgroups. Then
    \begin{equation}
        {-}\smashp{-}\colon (\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}\times(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_2}\to(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2}.
    \end{equation}
    is a left Quillen bifunctor for the model structures as indiciated.
    \begin{proof}
        Write ${\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2$ for the family of closed subgroups $K\subset G\times G$ such that there exist $H_1\in{\mathcal{F}}_1,H_2\in{\mathcal{F}}_2$ with $K\subset H_1\times H_2$. Then $((eq:smash-equiv of the paper))$ factors as
        \[
            (\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}\times(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_2}
            \xrightarrow{\;{-}\smashp{-}\;}\big(\cat{$\bm{(G\times G)}$-Top}_*\big){}_{{\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2}
            \xrightarrow{\;\Delta^*\;}(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2},
        \]
        where the second functor is left Quillen by Lemma~(lemma:restr-equiv-lQ of the paper). We are therefore reduced to showing that the first functor is a left Quillen bifunctor.

        It suffices to verify the pushout product axiom for the generating (acyclic) cofibrations, which are of the form $(G_i/H_i\times f_i)_+$ for generating (acyclic) cofibrations $f$ of $\textbf{\textup{Top}}_*$ and $H_i\in{\mathcal{F}}_i$. The pushout product is then given by
        \[
            (G_1/H_1\times f_1)_+\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}}
            (G_2/H_2\times f_2)_+\cong
            \big((G_1\times G_2)/(H_1\times H_2) \times (f_1\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f_2)\big){}_+.
        \]
        As $\textbf{\textup{Top}}$ is a cartesian model category, $f_1\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f_2$ is a cofibration, acyclic if at least one of $f_1,f_2$ is so. As $(G_1\times G_2)/(H_1\times H_2)$ is $({\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-cofibrant by definition and since the $({\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-model structure is topological, the claim follows.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma smash-lQ of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] For fixed $k \ge 1$, as $n \to \infty$, 
the short-range correlations between the zeros of
 $\spec_{h_{n}}\cW(z)$ and
 $\spec_{h_{n+k}}\cW(z)$ are 
\begin{equation*}
g_{n,n+k}(z,z) = 
\begin{cases}
\disp 1-\frac{5}{4n^{2}}+O\left( \frac{1}{n^{3}}\right) <1 & \text{if $k=1$}, \\[4mm]
\disp \frac{4}{3}+
\frac{1}{12n^2}+O\left( \frac{1}{n^3}\right) 
>1 &
 \text{if $k=2$}, 
\\[4mm]
\disp 1 & \text{if $k\geq 3$}.  
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
Thus, the short-range correlations
between zeros of $\spec_{h_{n}}\cW(z)$ and zeros of 
$\spec_{h_{n+k}}\cW(z)$ display repulsion if $k=1$, 
attraction if $k=2$, and no short-range second-order correlation in the contact
 limit if $k\geq 3$. Moreover, $g_{n,n+1}(z,z)$ increases
 with $n$ and $g_{n,n+1}(z,z) \to 1$, and
$g_{n,n+2}(z,z)$ attains its maximum at $n=2$ and then
 decreases for $n\geq 2$, 
with $g_{n,n+2}(z,z) \to 4/3$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 5 (Algorithmic lower bound for comparison decoders) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] Let \(v:T\to\mathcal H\) be an embedding into a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and set
\(d(s,t)=\|v_s-v_t\|_{\mathcal H}\). Let
\[
Y=v_\Theta+\tau Z,
\qquad
\Theta\sim\pi,
\qquad
Z\sim N(0,I_{\mathcal H}),
\]
and let \(m\in\mathcal H\) be any reference center.  Set
\[
Q_{\tau,m}:=N(m,\tau^2I_{\mathcal H}),
\qquad
\mathcal I_{\pi,m}:=\frac{1}{2\tau^2}\int_T\|v_t-m\|^2\,\pi(dt).
\]
With \(\bar v_\pi:=\int_T v_t\,\pi(dt)\), the centered choice \(m=\bar v_\pi\) gives
\[
\mathcal I_{\pi,\bar v_\pi}=\frac{\mathsf V_\pi}{4\tau^2},
\qquad
\mathsf V_\pi:=\iint d(s,t)^2\pi(ds)\pi(dt).
\]

Let \(\widehat\Theta(Y)\) be an estimator with values in \(T\).
Assume that there is a penalty \(\Omega:T\to\mathbb R\) and nonnegative, integrable comparison errors
\(\varepsilon_{\rm opt}\) and \(\varepsilon_{\rm pen}\), measurable under the true joint law, such that
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
\|Y-v_{\widehat\Theta}\|^2+\Omega(\widehat\Theta)
\le
\|Y-v_\Theta\|^2+\Omega(\Theta)+\varepsilon_{\rm opt},\\
\Omega(\widehat\Theta)
\ge \Omega(\Theta)-\varepsilon_{\rm pen}.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Let the full comparison error be denoted by
\[
\varepsilon_{\rm cmp}:=\varepsilon_{\rm opt}+\varepsilon_{\rm pen}.
\]
If, for some \(c\in(0,1)\) and \(\Delta>0\),
\begin{equation}
\mathcal I_{\pi,m}+\log 2
\le
(1-c)\log\frac{1}{\rho_{\Delta,Q_{\tau,m}}(\widehat\Theta)},
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E_{\Theta,Y}d(\Theta,\widehat\Theta(Y))\ge c\Delta,
\end{equation}
and, for the Gaussian process \(X_t:=\langle Z,v_t\rangle\) built from the same Gaussian vector \(Z\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E_{\Theta,Z}\bigl[X_{\widehat\Theta}-X_\Theta\bigr]
\ge
\frac{c^2\Delta^2-\mathbb E_{\Theta,Z}\varepsilon_{\rm cmp}}{2\tau}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_{\rm cmp}\le c^2\Delta^2/2\), then the right-hand side is at least \(c^2\Delta^2/(4\tau)\).  Thus the exact ghost mass gives an algorithmic lower bound on the Gaussian range sampled by the comparison decoder, up to the explicit comparison error.

Ordinary nearest neighbor corresponds to \(\Omega\equiv0\) and \(\varepsilon_{\rm opt}=\varepsilon_{\rm pen}=0\).  The unrestricted norm-regularized nearest-neighbor rule
\[
\widehat\Theta_\lambda(Y)\in
\arg\min_{a\in T}\bigl\{\|Y-v_a\|^2+\lambda\|v_a\|^2\bigr\}
\]
is also covered with zero error whenever the realized outputs have norm at least the norm of the true parameter, as in the separating example in Theorem~\ref{thm:decision-aligned-separation}. This is a canonical minimum-complexity inductive bias consistent with modern perspectives, rather than an explicit restriction of the hypothesis class. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Algorithmic lower bound for comparison decoders

[Lemma 21 (Martingale bounds on infection paths) of arXiv:2604.00630, 'The contact process on a bipartite spatial network'] Assume that~$G$ is a bipartite graph, and consider the contact process on~$G$ in which the infection rates of types~$1$ and~$2$ are~$\lambda_1$ and~$\lambda_2$, respectively. Assume that~$\lambda_1,\lambda_2 < 1/4$.
	Let $\Gamma=(\Gamma_0,\ldots,\Gamma_\ell)$ be a vertex path in~$G$ with initial vertex~$\Gamma_0$ of type~$1$. Then, the probability that there exist~$t > 0$ and an infection path~$g:[0,t]\to V$ having $\Gamma$ as its ordered trace is at most $(2\lambda_1)^{\lceil|\Gamma|/2\rceil}(2\lambda_2)^{\lfloor|\Gamma|/2\rfloor}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Martingale bounds on infection paths

body: PROVED (separable case of the bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture, 2026-09-22). If Q(X)=sum_j lambda_j X_j^2 is diagonal in the independent coordinates X_j (densities <=1) and has at least three eigenvalues with |lambda_j|>=1, then Q(X) has a density bounded by pi, and pi is attained (X1^2+X2^2, uniforms). Proof: among three eigenvalues of modulus >=1, two share a sign (pigeonhole); each squared term lambda X^2 has density <= y^{-1/2}; two same-sign terms convolve to a density <= B(1/2,1/2)=pi (Beta integral); convolving the remaining independent terms cannot increase the sup (Young). Sharpness: one large eigenvalue gives density y^{-1/2} (unbounded); two opposite-sign give a logarithmic singularity (unbounded). The GENERAL non-separable case remains OPEN: it reduces to a uniform L1 bound on the characteristic function, but the per-direction oscillatory decay integral e^{isx^2}f dx = O(|s|^{-1/2}) is NOT uniform over densities <=1 (for each s there is an admissible f with |integral|>=1/2), so the coupled case needs the joint oscillatory-integral analysis (resolution of singularities). Paper: Downloads/Quadratic_Form_Bounded_Density_paper.pdf.

[Theorem 29 of arXiv:2609.01098, 'Gaussian upper bounds for averaged heat semigroups on graphs'] Let $r_0,C>0$. Assume that we have 
\[
\mathcal{P}_{r}(t,x,y)
\\
 \leq 
C
\frac{(1\vee S^{-2}(\sqrt{\rho(B_x(r),B_y(r))^2S^2+t^2}-t))^{\frac{n}{2}}}{\sqrt[\frac{2q(t)}{q(t)-1}]{m(B_x(\sqrt t))m(B_y(\sqrt t))}}
 \euler^{-tS^{-2}\zeta(\rho(B_x(r),B_y(r))S/t)}
\]
for all $t\geq r^2\geq r_0^2$ and $x,y\in X$, 
and the volume comparison estimate
\[
\frac{m(B_x(R))}{R^{n}}
\leq C 
\frac{m(B_x(r))}{r^{n}}, \quad r_1\leq r\leq R,
\]
for all $x\in X$.
Then, for all $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $r\geq 1\vee r_0$, and $U\subset B(r)$ satisfying $m(U)\geq \varepsilon m(B(r))$, we have 
\[
\lambda(U)
\geq 
\frac{C_n'}{r^{2+\varepsilon}}
\left(
\frac{m(B(r))}{m(U)}\right)^{\frac{2}{N}}\left[1\wedge \frac{1}{m(B(r))}\right] ^{\frac{1}{C_n'q(r^2)}}
\]
where $C_n'=C_n'(C,n)>0$ and 
\[
N\geq n\frac{q(r^2)}{q(r^2)-1}+ \frac{\ln \frac{1}{\varepsilon}}{\varepsilon}\frac{1}{\ln r}+\frac{1}{q(r^2)-1}\ln(1\vee m(B(r)))
\]

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). A probability measure mu on R is moment-determinate if it is the unique probability measure sharing its full sequence of moments (m_k)_{k>=0}. The Carleman condition gives a simple sufficient criterion: if sum_{k=1}^infinity m_{2k}^{-1/(2k)} = infinity, then mu is moment-determinate. In practice this is most often invoked via a stronger, easier-to-check sub-condition, such as subgaussian or lighter tails, for instance P(|X|>t) <= C exp(-ct^2), which implies the even moments grow at most at Gaussian rate and hence satisfy Carleman's sum divergence; a common proof strategy in random matrix theory and random measure convergence is to show convergence of all moments to those of a known moment-determinate limit, such as the compactly supported semicircle law, and then invoke Carleman's condition, or compact support directly, to upgrade moment convergence to convergence in distribution. It does not hold automatically for every measure with finite moments of all orders: the classical log-normal distribution is the standard counterexample, having finite moments of every order yet failing to be moment-determinate, so other measures share its entire moment sequence, meaning that verifying Carleman's sum diverges, or invoking compact support, is a genuinely necessary step, not a formality. Typical failure: Assuming that finiteness of all moments, or even termwise convergence of a sequence's moments to a limit's moments, is sufficient to conclude convergence in distribution, without checking that the limit measure is itself moment-determinate; the log-normal-type failure of moment determinacy is the standard cautionary example, and in random matrix or random measure contexts, using the method of moments toward a limit whose determinacy has not been separately established, as happens for some heavy-tailed spectral limits, can produce a plausible-looking but invalid convergence claim. Canonical reference: Carleman, 1926, Les Fonctions Quasi Analytiques, Gauthier-Villars; Akhiezer, The Classical Moment Problem, 1965, Hafner Publishing; Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, 2010, Cambridge University Press.

[Theorem 8 (Mod-$\phi$ convergence for multiset inversions) of arXiv:2608.14143, 'Mod-$\phi$ convergence for random variables with cyclotomic generating functions'] Assume that 
$$
M_N:=\max_{1\le i\le r(N)} m_i^{(N)} =  o(n_N),
$$
and set $s_N=n_N$. Suppose the limit
\[
\Sigma\ :=\ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{n_N}\sum_{i=1}^{r(N)}\frac{m_i^{(N)}\bigl(m_i^{(N)}+1\bigr)}{2}
\]
exists in $\R$. Then $X_N/n_N$ converges mod-$\phi$ with parameter $n_N$, normalization function
\[
\phi(z)\ :=\ \int_0^1 \log\Bigl(\frac{e^{tz}-1}{tz}\Bigr)\,dt,
\]
domain $\mathscr{D}=\{z\in\C:\ \frac{e^{tz}-1}{tz}\notin(-\infty,0]\ \text{for all }t\in[0,1]\}$, and limiting function
\[
\psi(z) = \exp\Bigl(\frac12\log\Bigl(\frac{e^{z}-1}{z}\Bigr)-\frac{z}{2}\,\Sigma\Bigr)
\ =\ \sqrt{\frac{e^{z}-1}{z}}\;e^{-\,\frac{z}{2}\Sigma}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mod-$\phi$ convergence for multiset inversions

$$
\mathcal{A}:=\{A_{uv}\mid (u,v)\in E\},\quad\text{where }A_{uv}:=\{\sigma:\sigma_u=\sigma_v=1\},\quad \forall (u,v)\in E.
$$ Let $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ be the event-field denoising process for $\mu$ with respect to this family $\mathcal{A}$. Then the resulting process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ is called the edge-field denoising process for $\mu$ on $G$.

body:
[Theorem thm:introduction-lattice-induction of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] The following assertions hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item
For every $d\geq 1$, each lattice-induced
probability-preserving Borel $\mathbb R^d$-space admits a
generating stealthy Delone cross-section.

\item
Let $\eta$ be an ergodic translation-invariant point process on
$\mathbb R$ with positive intensity and local second moments. If
\[
    \int_{0<|\xi|<1}
    \frac{1}{\xi^2}\,d\sigma_\eta(\xi)
    <
    \infty,
\]
then the translation action on its configuration space has a
nonzero eigenvalue and is lattice-induced.
\end{enumerate}

Consequently, an ergodic probability-preserving Borel
$\mathbb R$-space is lattice-induced if and only if it admits a
generating stealthy Delone cross-section. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stealthy cross-sections and lattice induction

Load-bearing hypothesis: the equivalence 'admissible shock ⇔ Lax inequalities f'(u_-) ≥ σ ≥ f'(u_+)' requires the flux to be convex (genuinely nonlinear) on the range of the data. For a nonconvex flux one must use Oleinik's full chord condition, which involves f at every intermediate state, not only the two endpoint derivatives. Counterexample: f(u) = u^4 - 5u^2 (so f'(u) = 4u^3 - 10u), left state u_- = 2, right state u_+ = -2. Since f(2) = f(-2) = -4, Rankine-Hugoniot gives the stationary shock σ = 0, and the Lax inequalities hold strictly: f'(2) = 12 > 0 > f'(-2) = -12. Yet the shock is NOT admissible: the chord joining (-2,-4) and (2,-4) is the constant -4, while f(0) = 0 lies ABOVE it, so Oleinik's condition fails; equivalently the Kruzhkov inequality with k = 0 requires σ(k - u_-) ≥ f(k) - f(u_-), i.e. 0 ≥ 4, which is false. The correct entropy solution of this Riemann problem is read off the least concave majorant of f on [-2,2] (the hull construction for a decreasing jump u_l > u_r): a shock from u_- = 2 down to u* = (√7 - 2)/3 ≈ 0.2153, the point at which the line through (2, f(2)) is tangent to the graph of f, then an attached rarefaction from u* down to -u*, then, by symmetry, a shock from -u* to u_+ = -2. The two shock speeds are -(16 + 14u*)/9 ≈ -2.113 and +(16 + 14u*)/9 ≈ +2.113, and the rarefaction sweeps the speeds between them. Auditor's check: whenever a proof calls a jump admissible using only characteristic speeds, verify convexity of the flux on the interval spanned by the two states; otherwise test the whole chord.
Counterexample flux f(u) = u^4 - 5u^2 with states u_- = 2, u_+ = -2, shock speed σ = 0
Lax inequalities compare σ only with f'(u_-) and f'(u_+)
Oleinik's condition requires the graph of f between the two states to lie on the correct side of the chord at EVERY intermediate value
For nonconvex flux the Riemann solution is generally a composite of shocks and rarefactions given by the convex (or concave) hull construction
title: Pitfall: Lax's Shock Inequalities Are Not Sufficient When the Flux Is Not Convex

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): Under affine spanning, projective simplicity, and coordinate-full homogenization, an affine fibre of density greater than 27/512 cannot have old geometric distance three. Structure: homogeneous compression yields an optimal residual plane; if it descends with any slack the old distance is ≤ 2; otherwise it has the saturated shared-h pattern, the balanced local relation reduces the old support to three or five coordinates, and long directions, flag estimates, planar spectra, the m = 8 exact normal forms, and the m ≤ 7 intrinsic enumeration cover every possible effective size. In each case either the density is ≤ 27/512 or an old rank-two residual certificate contradicts distance three. Notes: Quantifier: under the distance-three hypothesis EVERY optimal homogenized plane must be exceptional, so excluding any selected one suffices. Density threshold 27/512 ~ 0.0527. Finite components certified per p.27; this is a deterministic local theorem, not the determinant conjecture.

    $$
    \forall \varphi: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \text{ convex and such that } \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} \frac{|\varphi(x)|}{1 + |x|} < \infty, \; \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x) \mu(\mathrm{d}x) \leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(y) \nu(\mathrm{d}y).
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. 
	The space of random Lipschitz functions denoted by \(\mathrm{BL}_{\Omega}(\mathbb{R}^d) \) consists of all functions \( g : \mathbb{R}^d \times \Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \) satisfying the following properties.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item For every \( \omega \in \Omega \), the function \( x \mapsto g(x,\omega) \) is continuous.
		\item For every \( x \in \mathbb{R}^d \), the function \( \omega \mapsto g(x,\omega) \) is measurable.
		\item There exists a constant \( M > 0 \) such that on a set of full measure in \( \Omega \) 
		\begin{align*}
			\| g(\cdot, \omega) \|_{\mathrm{BL}} < M,
		\end{align*}
		where
		\[
		\| g(\cdot, \omega) \|_{\mathrm{BL}} := \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} |g(x,\omega)| + \sup_{\substack{x, y \in \mathbb{R}^d \\ x \neq y}} \frac{|g(x,\omega) - g(y,\omega)|}{|x - y|}.
		\]
	\end{itemize}
	Furthermore 
	\[
	\mathrm{Pr}_{\Omega}(\mathbb{R}^d) := \left\{ \nu \text{ is a probability measure on } \mathbb{R}^d \times \Omega \,\middle|\, \left( \Pi_{\Omega} \right)_{\ast} \nu = \mathbb{P} \right\},
	\]
	where $\Pi$ denotes the projection onto $\Omega$.

[DRAFT prior-art concept.] For nontrivial finitely generated groups G_1,G_2 with finite symmetric factor generating sets, independent bond percolation on Cay(G_1*G_2,S_1 union S_2) has critical parameter characterized by (chi_1(p)-1)(chi_2(p)-1)=1, where chi_i is expected root-cluster size on the corresponding factor Cayley graph. In the F_2 long-power family, G_1=G_2=Z, the b factor has chi_b=(1+p)/(1-p), and this specializes to p(2chi_N(p)-1)=1. The union-of-factor-generators assumption is essential; this formula is not asserted for arbitrary prescribed generating sets. Source: Kozakova arXiv:math/0611668v3, Theorem 1.

[Lemma LEM:var of arXiv:2412.09790, 'Critical threshold for weakly interacting log-correlated focusing Gibbs measures'] Given $N \in \mathbb{N}$, let $Y_N$ be as above.
Suppose that  $F:C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d) \to \mathbb{R}$
is measurable such that $\mathbb{E}\big[|F(Y_N)|^p\big] < \infty$
and $\mathbb{E}\big[|e^{F(Y_N)}|^q \big] < \infty$ for some $1 < p, q < \infty$ with $\frac 1p + \frac 1q = 1$.
Then, we have
\begin{align}
 \log \mathbb{E}\Big[e^{F(Y_N)}\Big]
= \sup_{\theta \in \mathbb H_a}
\mathbb{E}\bigg[ F( Y_N + \Theta_N) - \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 \| \theta(t) \|_{L^2_x}^2 dt \bigg], 

\end{align}
	
	
\noindent
where  
 the expectation $\mathbb{E} = \mathbb{E}_\mathbb{P}$
is taken  with respect to the underlying probability measure~$\mathbb{P}$.
Here, 
$\Theta_N = \pi_N \Theta$, 
where the process $\Theta$  is  defined by 
\begin{align}
\Theta (t)  =  \int_0^t \langle \nabla \rangle^{-\frac d2} \theta(t') dt'.

\end{align}

\noindent (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition PropSubMart of arXiv:2608.11178, 'A submartingale for the probability of avoiding the origin in one-point interaction ground'] Fix \(d\in\{2,3\}\), \(T,\gamma>0\), and
\(x\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). The process
\(\mathbf S^{T,\gamma}=\{\mathbf S_t^{T,\gamma}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\), defined by
\[
\mathbf S_t^{T,\gamma}
:=
S_{T-t}^{\gamma}(X_t),
\qquad
t\in[0,T].
\]
is a bounded, continuous
\(\mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma}\)-submartingale with respect to
\(\{\mathcal F_t^{T,x}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\). Moreover, if
\(\mathbf S^{T,\gamma}
=
\mathbf M^{T,\gamma}+\mathbf A^{T,\gamma}\)
denotes its Doob--Meyer decomposition, then the increasing component
\(\mathbf A^{T,\gamma}\) is constant during the excursions of \(X\) away
from the origin, while the martingale component satisfies
\(\mathbf M^{T,\gamma}\in L^2(\mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma})\) and is given by
\begin{align}
\mathbf M_t^{T,\gamma}
=
S_T^\gamma(x)
+
\int_0^t
\nabla S_{T-s}^\gamma(X_s)\cdot dW_s^{T,\gamma},
\qquad
t\in[0,T].

body: A series of real or complex terms sum a_n converges iff for every eps > 0 there is N such that |a_{n+1} + ... + a_m| < eps for all m > n >= N. In particular a convergent series has a_n -> 0, and absolute convergence implies convergence.

body:
For a connected finite plane honeycomb graph with f bounded faces and compatible prescribed boundary midpoint values, the homogeneous vertex-relation kernel has complex dimension f. Fewer than f additional complex linear conditions cannot determine interior midpoint values uniquely. Exactly f suffice: orient each internal edge, put J_e=(v-u)F(p_e)/2, and impose c_i^T J=0 on the real signed cycle vectors of the bounded faces. These constraints give a unique solution to the algebraic boundary problem; they are not claimed to hold for the actual SAW observable or to prove a scaling limit. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields

Let mu be a nonnegative Borel measure on R such that every polynomial is absolutely integrable and integral q(t)^2 dmu(t)>0 for every nonzero real polynomial q. Let p_k be its degree-k monic orthogonal polynomials, with p_0=1. Fix n>=1 and alpha in R, and write r_1<...<r_n for the n distinct real roots of p_n+alpha p_(n-1). There are strictly positive real numbers lambda_1,...,lambda_n such that integral f(t)dmu(t)=sum_(i=1)^n lambda_i f(r_i) for every real polynomial f of degree<=2n-2. These weights are unique. The parameter alpha is arbitrary real; no support-location restriction on the roots is added. The asserted exactness degree is2n-2, not2n-1 for arbitrary alpha. This is Lemma3.6 of Cohn-Kumar.

body:
[Proposition 2 (Probabilistic representation and error decomposition) of arXiv:2604.23133, 'High-Precision Framework for Expected Hitting Times Analysis in the Dice-Sum Process'] For every \(N \in \mathbb{N}\) and \(s \ge 0\), define
\[
F(s) := \mathbb{E}_s\big[\min(T,\omega_N)\big].
\]
Then, \(F\) satisfies the same recursion and boundary conditions as~\eqref{eq:ENdef}, and hence provides a solution of the truncated recursion.
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
E(s) - F(s)
\;=\;
\mathbb{E}_s\!\big[(T - \omega_N)\,\mathbf{1}_{\{\omega_N < T\}}\big].
\end{equation}
In words, \(\min(T,\omega_N)\) represents the truncated stopping time, and
\((T-\omega_N)\mathbf{1}_{\{\omega_N<T\}}\) is the additional waiting time incurred along paths that overshoot the cutoff \(N\) before hitting the target set~\(\mathcal{H}\).

	\end{equation}
	holds for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Let $(X_\epsilon)_{\epsilon\in (0,1)}$ be a family of $Y_\alpha$-valued random variables  that is uniformly tight in $ Y_0$ and has uniform tail estimates in $Y_1$, i.e.,

	\]
	as $N\to\infty$. Then $(X_\epsilon)_{\epsilon\in (0,1)}$ is also tight in $Y_\alpha$.

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.03428, 'A New Sufficient Condition for Oriented Graphs Determined by Their Generalized Skew Spectr'] Let $\Sigma\in \mathcal{F}_n$, and let $d_n$ be
the last invariant factor of $W(\Sigma)$. Suppose that $d_n$ is square-free and $
 \operatorname{rank}_2 W(\Sigma)=\left\lceil\frac n2\right\rceil.$
For every odd prime divisor $p$ of $d_n$, assume that the following conditions
hold:

\noindent\textup{(i)}
\[
\deg\operatorname{sfp}(\Phi_p(\Sigma;x))=\operatorname{nullity}_p W(\Sigma);
\]

\noindent\textup{(ii)} write
\[
\operatorname{sfp}(\Phi_p(\Sigma;x))
=
\varphi_1(x)\cdots\varphi_s(x)
\]
as a product of distinct monic irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_p$. Then $
\gcd\bigl(\varphi_i(x),\varphi_j(-x)\bigr)=1$,
whenever $i\neq j$.

Then $\Sigma$ is $\mathrm{DGSS}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 6 (Universality for random polynomials) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Let $K_1,\ldots,K_m$ be finite extensions of $\Q_p$, and let
$$
U\subseteq
\mc{O}_{K_1}^{\times,\new}
\times\cdots\times
\mc{O}_{K_m}^{\times,\new}
$$
be clopen. Suppose that
$$
P_n(x)=\xi_nx^n+\cdots+\xi_1x+\xi_0,
$$
where $\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_n$ are independent
$\epsilon$-balanced random variables in $\Z_p$. Then
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\E\left[
Z_U(P_n)
\right]
=
\int_U
\rho_{K_1,\ldots,K_m}^{(\infty),\poly}
(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\,dx_1\cdots dx_m.
$$
Here, the integral is taken with respect to the product Haar probability
measure on
$\mc{O}_{K_1}\times\cdots\times\mc{O}_{K_m}$, and
$\rho_{K_1,\ldots,K_m}^{(\infty),\poly}$ is the stabilized Haar polynomial
correlation function introduced above. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universality for random polynomials
