[Theorem 2.7 (van den Berg) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that $D$ is simply connected and that $\partial D$ is Minkowski nondegenerate with
Minkowski dimension $\msf d_M(\partial D)\in[1,2)$. That is,
\[0<\liminf_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}\leq
\limsup_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}<\infty,\]
where we define
\[\partial D_r=\left\{x\in\mbb R^2:\inf_{y\in\partial D}|x-y|<r\right\}.\]
There exists constants $c\in(1,\infty)$ and $\th>0$ such that
\begin{align}

c^{-1}t^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2}\leq\msf{A}(D)-\msf M_0(t)\leq ct^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2},\qquad t\in(0,\th).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Block-reversal involutions on $\llbracket n \rrbracket$ of arXiv:2509.02996, 'Group-averaged Markov chains: mixing improvement'] Let $n=2^k$ with $k\in\mathbb{N}$. For each $j\in \llbracket k \rrbracket$ define
	a permutation $\sigma^{(j)}$ of $\llbracket n \rrbracket$ by
	\[
		\sigma^{(j)}(i) := q\,2^{j} + \bigl(2^{j}-1-r\bigr) + 1, \quad \text{where } i-1 = q\,2^{j} + r \quad (q\in \mathbb{N}\cup \{0\},\ 0\le r < 2^j).
	\]
	Equivalently, partition $\llbracket n \rrbracket$ into consecutive blocks of length $2^{j}$:
	\[
	\llbracket 1,2^{j} \rrbracket,\ \llbracket 2^{j}+1,2\cdot 2^{j} \rrbracket,\ \dots,\ \llbracket (m-1)2^{j}+1,m2^{j}\rrbracket,\ \dots
	\]
	with $m \in \llbracket 2^{k-j} \rrbracket$ and within each block reverse the order, leaving different blocks disjoint.
title: Block-reversal involutions on $\llbracket n \rrbracket$

    be an \(\alpha\)-nice function (Assumption~(assmpt: sufficiently nice function of the paper)).
    Then, for any \(0\le \underline{t}<\overline{t}\le T\) the differential equation 
    \begin{equation}
        dx_t = \sigma(t,w_t, x_t) \, dg_t
        \quad\text{with initial condition}\quad x_{\underline{t}} = a \in \banachSpace[X] 
    \end{equation}
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\upshape]
        \item has a \underline{unique} solution
        \(x\) with \(x \in C^\alpha([\underline{t},\overline{t}], \banachSpace[X])\).
    \end{enumerate}
For any \(R>0\)
    there exist constants
    \[
        C_{\text{flow}}^R, C_{\text{flow,loc}}^R, C_{\text{init}}^R, C_{\text{driver}}^R, C_{\text{param}}^R

    \(\norm{w}_\alpha, \norm{\tilde w}_\alpha \le R\) and all \(0\le \underline{t}< \overline{t} \le T\) we have
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\upshape, resume]
        \item

        Let \(\psi\) be the flow starting at \(a\in \banachSpace[X]\) in time \(\underline{t}\) (the solution path), then we have
        \begin{align}
                        
            \norm{\psi(a; \underline{t}, \cdot)}_{\alpha} &\le C_{\text{flow}}^R

[Lemma 5 (Rank--one structure of $\E {[}M{) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] }$]
Let $A = \left[0, c\right]$, $B = \left(c, 1\right]$, and $u \left(t\right) = \left(2 t - c\right)^{-1 / 2}$. Define the function $\phi : \left[0, 1\right] \to \R$ by
\[
\phi \left(x\right)
\ := \
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{x \in A\right\}} + \sqrt{c} \, \mathbf{1}_{\left\{x \in B\right\}} u \left(x\right),
\]
where $\mathbf{1}_{x \in S}$ is the indicator function defined as
\[
\mathbf{1}_{x \in S}
\ = \
\begin{cases}
1, & x \in S, \\
0, & x \notin S,
\end{cases}
\]
for some set $S$. Then the limiting mean kernel $F$ from \eqref{eq:FWR} satisfies
\[
F \left(x, y\right)
\ = \
\phi \left(x\right) \phi \left(y\right).
\]

Consequently, if one forms the $n \times n$ matrix
\[
F^{\left(n\right)}_{k j}
\ := \
F \left(\frac{k}{n}, \frac{j}{n}\right),
\qquad
1 \le k, j \le n,
\]
then $F^{\left(n\right)}$ is rank one, since
\[
F^{\left(n\right)}
\ = \
v^{\left(n\right)} \left(v^{\left(n\right)}\right)^\top\!,
\qquad
v^{\left(n\right)}_k
\ := \
\phi \left(\frac{k}{n}\right).
\]
In particular, by Theorem \ref{thm:mean-kernel-limit}, the expectation matrix $\E[M]$ is asymptotically a rank--one matrix.

[Lemma lem:d_P_bound of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] \noindent{\nf(a)} Let $\bm\xi$ be a random vector in $L^q$, i.e. $\mathds{E}[|\bm\xi|^q]<\infty$, for some $q\in(0,1]$. Then, 
$$\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi},a\bm{\xi})\geqslant |1-a^q|\mathds{E}\big[|\bm\xi|^q\big] \quad \text{ for any constant }a \in(0,\infty).$$

\noindent{\nf(b)} Assume that the random vectors
$\bm\xi_1, \bm\xi_2, \bm\zeta_1, \bm\zeta_2$ are in $L^q$, for some $q\in(0,1]$, and that 
$(\bm{\xi}_1,\bm{\zeta}_1)$ and $(\bm{\xi}_2, \bm{\zeta}_2)$ are independent. Then the following inequality holds:
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi}_1+\bm{\xi}_2,\bm{\zeta}_1+\bm{\zeta}_2)
\leqslant \mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi}_1,\bm{\zeta}_1) + \mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi}_2,\bm{\zeta}_2).
\end{equation*}

body:
[Lemma 2605211341 of arXiv:2609.02626, 'Comparison principles and symmetry for subquadratic fractional $p$-Laplacian equations'] Let $N\ge 1$, $s\in (0, 1)$ and $p>1$. Suppose that $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded open set, and $u\in \widetilde{W}^{s,p}(\Omega)$ is a weak solution of
\[
(-\Delta)_p^s u= g\quad \mbox{in } \Omega,
\]
for some $g\in L^1_{loc}(\Omega)\cap W_0^{s, p}(\Omega)'$. Let $v\in L^1_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^N)$  satisfy
\[
{\rm dist}({\rm supp}(v), \Omega)>0, \quad \int_{\Omega^c}\frac{|v(x)|^{p-1}}{(1+|x|)^{N+sp}} {\rm d}x<\infty.
\]
Define
\[
h(x)=2\int_{{\rm supp} (v)}\frac{J_{u+v}(x, y)-J_u(x, y)}{|x-y|^{N+sp}} {\rm d}y, \quad \mbox{for a.e. }x\in \Omega.
\]
Then $u+v\in \widetilde{W}^{s,p}(\Omega)$ and it solves weakly $(-\Delta)_p^s (u+v)= g+h$ in $\Omega$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem thm:existence_bisections of arXiv:2609.00163, 'Decompositions and diagrams of symplectic surfaces in Weinstein domains'] Let $W$ be a Weinstein domain equipped with a specific handle structure, i.e., a choice of plurisubharmonic function $\rho: W \to \mathbb{R}$. For any bisection with divides $\mathcal{T}$ obtained from $\rho$, any ascending surface $F$ in $W$ can be symplectically isotoped into a bridge position with divides with respect to $\mathcal{T}$.

body:
PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. For deterministic x in R^d with d>=1 and s=||x||^2/d in (0,1], take independent standard Gaussian U(n by d), W(n by n), v(n), with n>=1. Define h=Ux/sqrt(d), a=tanh(h), H=Wa/sqrt(n), f=v^T tanh(H)/sqrt(n). With all raw U,W,v trainable and no biases, the diagonal NTK Theta_n=||grad_U f||_F^2+||grad_W f||_F^2+||grad_v f||^2 satisfies ||Theta_n-Theta_infty||_2<=37/sqrt(n). Here F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2, R(q)=E sech(sqrt(q)Z)^4 and Theta_infty=F(F(s))+(F(s)+s R(s))R(F(s)). This is also a W2 bound to the deterministic NTK point mass.
Two hidden layers of common width n; one fixed nonzero input, normalized squared norm <=1; independent Gaussian initialization; tanh; raw-parameter NTK scaling as stated; no trainable biases. Uses unaudited C021 and reviewed C002 v2 scalar kernel shape.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:2e54f669559ce1276dfe40f4e7ccfcb607ea68e74c8a28015756a0133b6fdbad","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/2e/2e54f669559ce1276dfe40f4e7ccfcb607ea68e74c8a28015756a0133b6fdbad.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f3aeefd89b9bd0bd89a56e7f3aa2fc2ce4fb878722b532ee4aa00190646ee9e0","bundle_entry_key":"t250_w712_c022","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c021-c022-transpose-tanh-ntk","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Tensor Programs and Gaussian shared-weight conditioning","draft":"w712/bundle_016.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:two-hidden-tanh-diagonal-ntk-rate","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C022 v1: n^(-1/2) rate for one initial two-hidden-layer tanh NTK program

Kind: narrowed. Target: 2, one transpose-using program.
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified. This is a one-input
diagonal NTK result, not the entire NTK matrix on multiple inputs or
a quantitative Master Theorem for arbitrary transpose programs.

## Model and statement

Let x in R^d be deterministic, with d>=1 and s=||x||^2/d in (0,1].
Let U in R^(n by d), W in R^(n by n) and v in R^n have independent
standard Gaussian entries, mutually independent, with n>=1. Define

    h=Ux/sqrt(d), a=tanh(h), H=Wa/sqrt(n),
    f(x)=v^T tanh(H)/sqrt(n).

All nonlinearities are coordinatewise. Train the raw parameters U,W,v
with the displayed scaling retained in the computational graph; there
are no bias parameters. The scalar diagonal empirical NTK is

    Theta_n(x,x)=||grad_U f||_F^2+||grad_W f||_F^2+||grad_v f||^2.

For Z standard Gaussian put

    F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2,
    R(q)=E sech(sqrt(q)Z)^4,
    q1=F(s), q2=F(q1), r1=R(s), r2=R(q1),
    Theta_infty=q2+(q1+s r1)r2.

Then, for all n>=1,

    ||Theta_n(x,x)-Theta_infty||_2 <=37/sqrt(n).     (1)

Equivalently, W2(Law(Theta_n(x,x)),delta_(Theta_infty)) is at most
37/sqrt(n), since coupling to a deterministic point has exactly that
L2 cost. The constant is universal on 0<s<=1 and deliberately loose.
The program genuinely uses W and W^T together; the quantitative shared-
weight step is C021, not an independent-backward-weight replacement.

## 1. Differentiate the exact finite-width program

Set qhat=||a||^2/n, D=diag(sech(h_i)^4), rhat=tr(D)/n,
g_j=sech(H_j)^2, b_j=v_j g_j and Rhat=||b||^2/n. Direct differentiation
with respect to the raw parameters in the stated parametrization gives

    ||grad_v f||^2 = Qhat2:=mean_j tanh(H_j)^2,
    ||grad_W f||_F^2 = qhat Rhat,
    ||grad_U f||_F^2 = s T,
    T=b^T W D W^T b/n^2.

For the last line grad_(U_ik) f=x_k sech(h_i)^2(W^Tb)_i/(n sqrt(d));
summing its square over i,k supplies exactly s, not an additional n.
Hence

    Theta_n=Qhat2+qhat Rhat+s T.                    (2)

Conditional on h, a,D are fixed with 0<=D<=I, and a!=0 almost surely
because s>0 and tanh vanishes only at zero. W,v are still fresh independent
Gaussians. C021 with g(t)=sech(t)^2 therefore gives, conditionally and
then unconditionally,

    ||T-rhat Rhat||_2<=9/sqrt(n).                   (3)

This is the only new transpose-conditioning input, and is unaudited.

## 2. Scalar forward and derivative moments

The h_i are iid N(0,s). Since tanh^2 and sech^4 lie in [0,1],

    ||qhat-q1||_2<=1/sqrt(n),
    ||rhat-r1||_2<=1/sqrt(n).                       (4)

Given h, the H_j are iid N(0,qhat). Thus

    ||Qhat2-F(qhat)||_2<=1/sqrt(n).

The independently reviewed C002 establishes that F is increasing and
concave, with F(0)=0 and F'(0+)=1. Consequently it is 1-Lipschitz on
[0,1]. Equations (4) give

    ||Qhat2-q2||_2<=2/sqrt(n).                      (5)

Given h, the pairs (H_j,v_j) are iid and E Rhat=R(qhat). Their individual
second moment is E[v_j^4 sech(H_j)^8]<=3. Conditional variance and total
expectation therefore give

    ||Rhat-R(qhat)||_2<=sqrt(3)/sqrt(n).             (6)

We also need a Lipschitz bound for R, proved here without an inverse
variance denominator. Let psi(t)=sech(t)^4. Its second derivative is

    psi''(t)=16 sech(t)^4 tanh(t)^2-4 sech(t)^6,

so |psi''|<=20 on R. If 0<=p<=q, take independent standard Gaussians
Z,Z'. The random variable sqrt(p)Z+sqrt(q-p)Z' has variance q. Taylor's
theorem, with a pointwise remainder at most 10(q-p)(Z')^2, and conditional
centering of the first-order term in Z', show

    |R(q)-R(p)|<=10(q-p).                          (7)

All expectations of the remainder are finite; psi' is bounded, so the
centered linear term is integrable. This includes p=0 and does not move
an uncontrolled derivative or limit through an integral.

## 3. Assemble the NTK rate without factoring dependent errors

Put Ahat=qhat+s rhat and A=q1+s r1. Both lie in [0,2]. From (2)--(3),

    ||Theta_n-[Qhat2+Ahat Rhat]||_2<=9/sqrt(n).      (8)

Expand the remaining product in the following exact order:

    Ahat Rhat-A r2
       =Ahat[Rhat-R(qhat)]
        +Ahat[R(qhat)-R(q1)]+(Ahat-A)r2.

Bounding Ahat pointwise by 2, r2 by 1, and using (4), (6), (7),

    ||Ahat Rhat-A r2||_2
       <=[2sqrt(3)+20+2]/sqrt(n).                  (9)

Neither Ahat nor qhat is assumed independent of Rhat. Triangle
inequalities with pointwise bounds suffice. Combine (5), (8), (9):

    ||Theta_n-Theta_infty||_2
       <=[33+2sqrt(3)]/sqrt(n)<37/sqrt(n),

using sqrt(3)<2. This proves (1).

## Scope, prior work, and remaining question

This is an explicit bounded-smooth-activation, diagonal, single-input
example of Target2. It does not control the NTK at two distinct inputs,
the full backward row distribution, growing depth, or reuse in a general
Tensor Program. The next mathematical extension is the off-diagonal
kernel: joint forward conditioning then has rank two and may become
ill-conditioned when the input features align.

Primary-source prior-work check: Hanin--Nica, arXiv:1909.05989v1,
Theorem1, PDF page4, treats ReLU diagonal NTK moments with zero-initialized
but trainable biases and two-sided second-moment comparability. That
comparability alone is insufficient to subtract the squared mean and
deduce a variance O(1/n); no such inference is used here. This is not a
claim that an n^(-1/2) tanh NTK rate is new in the literature. Independent
novelty assessment remains pending. The elementary Gaussian conditioning
mechanism itself is standard and is not claimed new.

Load-bearing checks: the precise raw-parameter normalization in section1;
the conditional independence required by C021; qhat>0 almost surely;
bounded derivatives for (6)--(7); and pointwise rather than independence
estimates in (9). At n=1 the conditioning still includes the rank-one
term, and (1) remains valid. There is no s=0 cancellation in the proof;
that case is outside the stated range. All checks are author checks only.
Formalization remains UNVERIFIED; no independently checked proof or

body: Let X be a Banach space and A: D(A) subset of X -> X a linear operator. There exists a strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t >= 0} of bounded linear operators on X with ||T(t)|| <= 1 for every t >= 0 (a contraction semigroup) whose infinitesimal generator is A if and only if: (i) A is closed and D(A) is dense in X; and (ii) every lambda > 0 lies in the resolvent set of A, with ||(lambda I - A)^{-1}|| <= 1/lambda for every lambda > 0. [standard, e.g. Pazy, Semigroups of Linear Operators and Applications to Partial Differential Equations]
title: Hille-Yosida Theorem (Contraction Semigroups)

[Theorem Thm:delocheightanealedgauss of arXiv:2604.24743, 'The impact of disorder and non-convex interactions on delocalisation of height functions'] Let $V : \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ be an annealed Gaussian potential. Then there exists an inverse temperature $\beta_V \in (0 , \infty)$ (depending on $V$) and a constant $c_0 > 0$ (universal) such that, for any $\beta \geq \beta_V$ and any $L \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}^*$,

     \mathrm{Var}_{L , \beta}^{\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}-V} \left[ \varphi(0) \right] \geq c_0 \ln L.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:explicit_current_1 of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be an ergodic diffusion with invariant measure $\mu$ whose
symmetric part $\mathcal{L}_S$ satisfies the Poincar\'e inequality~(equation eq:poincare of the paper)
with spectral gap $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}>0$ (Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper)). 
Let $\overline{J}_t(U)$ denote the empirical current according to Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper)
with ergodic mean $\E^\mu[\overline{J}_t(U)]=\E^\mu[v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U]= \E^\mu[W]$,
and let $\nu\ll\mu$ with $\mathrm{d}\nu/\mathrm{d}\mu\in L^2(\mu)$.
Then for all $t > 0$ and $a > 0$,
\begin{align}
  \mathbb{P}^\nu\left(\overline{J}_t(U) - \E^\mu[\overline{J}_t] \geq a\right)
  \leq
  \left\|\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu}{\mathrm{d}\mu}\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}
  \exp\left[-t\frac{\tilde\sigma_{J,1}^2}{c_{J,1}^2}h\left(\frac{c_{J,1} a}{\tilde\sigma_{J,1}^2}\right)\right],
  
\end{align}
where $h(u) \equiv 1 + u - \sqrt{1+2u}$ and we define
\begin{align}
  \tilde\sigma_{J,1}^2 \equiv
  \frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}} + 2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)},
  \qquad 
  c_{J,1} \equiv \frac{\|W-\E^\mu[W]\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}.
\end{align}

body:
[Theorem 1 (Risk Stability Under Conditional Generative Augmentation) of arXiv:2609.01410, 'On the Reliability of Generative Augmentation:\\ A Wasserstein-Based Theoretical and Empir'] Assume:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item The loss $\ell(f(x),y)$ is $L_\ell$-Lipschitz with respect to $x$.
    
    \item The hypothesis class $\mathcal F$ is measurable and induces a uniformly bounded loss.
    
    \item For each class $y\in\mathcal Y$,
    \[
    W_1(P_y,P_{G,y})
    \le
    \varepsilon_y .
    \]
\end{enumerate}

Then for any classifier $f$,
\begin{equation}
|R_{P_\alpha}(f) - R_P(f)|
\le
\alpha L_\ell \sum_{y \in \mathcal{Y}} \pi_y \varepsilon_y.
\end{equation}

If $\varepsilon_y \le \varepsilon$ uniformly, then
\begin{equation}
|R_{P_\alpha}(f) - R_P(f)|
\le
\alpha L_\ell \varepsilon.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Risk Stability Under Conditional Generative Augmentation

[Proposition 78 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(\Omega,\FF,\PP)$ be a probability space.
	If $X$ is a  random variable, then $F_X\in \mathcal{B}_\mathbb{R}/\mathcal{B}_{[0,1]}$, and $F_X(X)\sim_\PP\leb_{[0,1]}$ iff $F_X$ is continuous. 
	Conversely, let $U\sim_\PP \leb_{(0,1)}$. If $F:\mathbb{R}\to [0,1]$ is a distribution function (right-continuous, nondecreasing, $\lim_{-\infty}F=0$, $\lim_\infty F=1$),  putting $$F^\leftarrow(u):=\inf\{v\in \mathbb{R}:F(v)>u\},\quad u\in (0,1),$$ for its quantile function (a.k.a. right-continuous inverse), then $F^\leftarrow\in \mathcal{B}_{(0,1)}/\mathcal{B}_\mathbb{R}$ and $F^\leftarrow(U)\sim_\PP\dd F$.

[Lem uniform-exp-lower-bound of arXiv:2607.05097, 'Asymptotics of Lyapunov Exponents and Phase Transitions for Fluids with Degenerate Forcing'] For every $\tilde z_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\eta \in (0,\eta^*(\tilde z_0))$, and $\delta, c > 0$ there are $\rho, C > 0$ such that for all $z_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|z_0-\tilde z_0\| \leq \rho$, $\epsilon < \rho$, $v \in \mathbb{R}^n$, and $t \geq C$
    $$\|P_\eta(z_0)v\| \geq \delta \|v\| \implies \|P_{\eta}(z_0)e^{t A^\epsilon(z_0)}v\| \geq e^{(\lambda(A^\epsilon(z_0))-c)t}\|v\| \,,$$
    where $P_\eta(z_0)$ is as in (def:proj-eta of the paper).

[Cor DeepSets of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $d,K,F\in\mathbb N_+$, let
$
    \mathcal{K}
    \subseteq
    \mathcal P_{\operatorname{emp}}^{\le K}(\mathbb R^d)
$
be compact with respect to $d_\phi$, and let
$
    \phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^F
$
be a \texttt{ReLU}-MLP such that $T_\phi$ is injective on $\mathcal{K}$. 
\hfill\\
\noindent
For every $L>0$, every $L$-Lipschitz map
$
    f:(\mathcal{K},d_\phi)\to\mathbb R,
$
and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a \texttt{ReLU}-MLP
$
    \Psi:\mathbb R^F\to\mathbb R
$
such that
\begin{equation}

    \sup_{
        \nu=
        \frac{1}{\widetilde K}
        \sum_{k=1}^{\widetilde K}\delta_{z_k}
        \in\mathcal{K}
    }
    \left|
        f(\nu)
        -
        \Psi\left(
            \frac{1}{\widetilde K}
            \sum_{k=1}^{\widetilde K}\phi(z_k)
        \right)
    \right|
    <\varepsilon
\end{equation}
and the resulting Deep Set map $\big(
\mathcal P_{\operatorname{emp}}^{\le K}(\mathbb R^d),d_{\phi}\big)\ni 
    \nu
    \mapsto 
    \Psi\big(T_\phi(\nu)\big)
\in (\mathbb{R},|\cdot|)$
is $L$-Lipschitz. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universality of Lipschitz Deep Sets with Prescribed Regularity

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.01447, '2609.01447'] Let $X$ be a uniformly convex Banach space, let
$\rho:G\to O(X)$ be a group homomorphism, and let
$x\notin X^{\rho(G)}$.  Then there exists $a\in X^{\rho(G)}$ such that
\[
 \|x-a\|_X
 =\distop\bigl(x,X^{\rho(G)}\bigr)>0
\]
and the vector
\[
 v=\frac{x-a}{\distop\bigl(x,X^{\rho(G)}\bigr)}
\]
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|v\|_X=\distop\bigl(v,X^{\rho(G)}\bigr)=1,
 \qquad
 \sup_{g\in G}\|\rho(g)v-v\|_X\ge1.
\end{equation}

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): Choose an independent dominating set U in C_n of size d = ceil(n/3) whose cyclic gaps have (edge-)length two or three. Put L_u = A + B_u and R = span{L_u : u in U}; the L_u are independent. Orient the cycle: in a length-two gap u-v-u' take basis forms B_v, C_v; in a length-three gap u-v-w-u' take B_v, C_v, C_w. Together with A these are exactly n+1 full-dual forms, linearly independent by backward substitution through each gap. Modulo R: B_u = -A, C_u = B_v, B_w = C_w in the relevant gap cases, so every full-dual form has a signed basis representative with residual in R. Hence dcb(A_n) = dgeo(A_n) = ceil(n/3). Notes: Explicit optimal certificate, not just an existence bound. Form count checks: sum of gap lengths = n edges, so d gaps contribute n forms, plus A = n+1.

[Theorem intro-fredi of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] (Theorem (fredi of the paper))
  
  Let $n$ be a fixed integer. Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and assume
  that for every finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^{n \varepsilon} \left( \frac{1}{N} \log
    \mathbb{E}[H \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A),
    \ldots, \lambda_n (A))] - \sum_{j = 0}^{n - 1} \sum_{i = 0}^r
    \frac{1}{N^{j \varepsilon}} \Psi_j (x_i) \right) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi_n
    (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi_0, \ldots, \Psi_n$ are smooth functions in a complex neighborhood of
  $0$, the above convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$, and $0 <
  \varepsilon < n^{- 1}$. Then the $1 / N^{n \varepsilon}$ correction of the
  average empirical distribution of $N^{- 1} A$ is given by
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^{n \varepsilon} \left( \frac{1}{N^{k + 1}}
    \mathbb{E}[\ensuremath{\operatorname{Tr}} (A^k)] - \sum_{j = 0}^{n - 1} \frac{1}{N^{j
    \varepsilon}} \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}^{(j)}_k \right) =\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k^{(n)},
    
  \end{equation}
  where for every $j \in \{0, \ldots, n\}$
  \[ \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}^{(j)}_k := \sum_{b_1 + 2 b_2 + \cdots + j \text{} b_j
     = j} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - b_1 - \cdots - b_j} \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m
     - b_1 - \cdots - b_j) !b_1 ! \ldots b_j !} \text{{\hspace{8em}}} \]
  \begin{equation}
    \text{{\hspace{14em}}} \times \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'_0
    (x))^{k - m - b_1 - \cdots - b_j} (\Psi'_1 (x))^{b_1} \ldots (\Psi'_j
    (x))^{b_j}) \right|_{x = 0} . 
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn local_multiple_radial_SLE_kappa of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] The locally commuting $n$-radial $\mathrm{SLE}(\kappa)$ is a compatible family of measures 
\[
\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}
\]
on $n$-tuples of continuous, non-self-crossing curves $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}\right)$ for all simply connected domains $\Omega$ with marked points $\left(z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right)$ and target sets $\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)$. These measures satisfy the following conditions:

\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] \textbf{Conformal invariance}: If $\varphi: \Omega \to \Omega^\prime$ is a conformal map, then the pullback measure satisfies
    \[
    \varphi^* \mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega^\prime; \varphi(z_1), \varphi(z_2), \ldots, \varphi(z_n), \varphi(q)\right)}^{\left(\varphi(U_1), \varphi(U_2), \ldots, \varphi(U_n)\right)} 
    = \mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}.
    \]
    It suffices to describe the measure when $\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right) = \left(\mathbb{D}; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, 0\right)$. The definition for arbitrary $\Omega$ with a marked interior point $q$ can then be extended by pulling back via a conformal equivalence $\varphi: \Omega \to \mathbb{D}$ mapping $q$ to $0$.

    \item[(ii)] \textbf{Domain Markov property}: Let $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}\right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\mathbb{D}; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}$, and parametrize $\gamma^{(j)}$ by their own capacity in $\mathbb{D}$. For stopping times $\mathbf{t} = (t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n)$, define
    \[
    \tilde{U}_j = U_j \setminus \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}, \quad 
    \tilde{\gamma}^{(j)} = \gamma^{(j)} \setminus \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}, \quad 
    \tilde{\Omega} = \mathbb{D} \setminus \bigcup_{j=1}^n \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}.
    \]
    Then, conditionally on the initial segments $\bigcup_{j=1}^n \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}$, we have
    \[
    \left(\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)}, \tilde{\gamma}^{(2)}, \ldots, \tilde{\gamma}^{(n)}\right) 
    \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\tilde{\Omega}; \gamma^{(1)}_{t_1}, \gamma^{(2)}_{t_2}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}_{t_n}, q\right)}^{\left(\tilde{U}_1, \tilde{U}_2, \ldots, \tilde{U}_n\right)}.
    \]

    \item[(iii)] \textbf{Absolute Continuity with respect to independent SLE($\kappa$)}: Let $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}\right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\mathbb{D}; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, 0\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}$. Let $z_j(t) = e^{i \theta_j(t)}$, the capacity-parametrized Loewner driving function $t \mapsto \theta_j(t)$ for $\gamma^{(j)}$ satisfies
    \[ 
    \begin{aligned}
    \mathrm{d} \theta_j(t) &= \sqrt{\kappa} \, \mathrm{d} B_j(t) + b_j\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}(t)\right) \, \mathrm{d} t, \\
    \mathrm{d} \theta_k(t) &= \cot\left(\frac{\theta_k(t) - \theta_j(t)}{2}\right) \, \mathrm{d} t, \quad k \neq j,
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    where $B_j(t)$ are independent standard Brownian motions, and $b_j(\boldsymbol{\theta})$ are $C^2$ functions on the chamber 
    \[
    \mathfrak{X}^n = \left\{(\theta_1, \theta_2, \ldots, \theta_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n \mid \theta_1 < \theta_2 < \cdots < \theta_n < \theta_1 + 2\pi \right\}.
    \]
\end{itemize}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.12839, 'Spiking Neural Networks with Elephant Reinforcement'] Let \(N<\infty\). Consider the process
\[
Y_t=(V_t,S_t,K_t)
\in \mathbb N^N\times\mathbb Z^N\times\mathbb N^N.
\]
Assume that site \(i\) fires with rate
\[
\lambda_i(V,S,K)
=
\mathbf 1_{\{V_i>\alpha S_i^+\}},
\qquad
S_i^+=\max\{S_i,0\},
\]
and leaks with rate
\[
\gamma\mathbf 1_{\{V_i>0\}},
\qquad \gamma>0.
\]
When site \(i\) fires, \(V_i\) is reset to \(0\), its two neighbours receive
one unit of potential, and
\[
S_i\mapsto S_i+\xi_i,
\qquad
K_i\mapsto K_i+1.
\]
Then the process is non-explosive. More precisely, if \(N_t\) denotes the
number of events up to time \(t\), then
\[
\mathbb E[N_t]\leq (\gamma+1)Nt<\infty.
\]

body:
[Proposition eitherorProp of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] Let $({\mathcal M}, \tau)$  be   a semi-finite von Neumann algebra  
		and let \( E
		\) be a 
		symmetric   function space on $(0, \tau({\bf 1}))$ with an order continuous norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{E}$.  
		If \(X\) is a $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{E({\mathcal M}, \tau)}$-closed subspace of   \(E(\mathcal{M}, \tau)\), then one of the following holds:   
		\begin{enumerate}[\rm(a)]
			\item \(X\) is strongly embedded into \(E(\mathcal{M}, \tau)\); 
			\item  there exist a normalized basic 
			sequence \(\{y_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) in \(X\) and two mutually orthogonal  sequences  \(\{p_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}, \{q_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}
			\subseteq {\mathcal M}
			\)   
			of $\tau$-finite projections  such that
			\[
			\lim_{n \to \infty} \| y_n - p_n y_n q_n \|_{E({\mathcal M}, \tau)}= 0.
			\] 	
				In particular, \(\{y_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) has a subsequence 
                that is  equivalent to   a disjointly supported basic sequence in \(E(\mathcal{M},\tau)
	\). 
	Moreover, if \(X\) has a basis,  then the sequence \(\{y_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) can be chosen to be a block basis of the basis of \(X\).
		\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] For every $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $T>0$ and $u_0\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_0;H)$, equation~\eqref{Eq1} has a unique variational solution $u$ on $[0,T]$. The solutions obtained on different finite intervals are consistent and therefore define a global solution on $[0,\infty)$. Moreover, $t\mapsto\mathcal L u(t)$ belongs to $C([0,\infty);P)$ and
	\begin{align}
		&\mathbb E\sup_{0\leq r\leq T}\|u(r)\|^2
		+\mathbb E\int_0^T
		\big(\|u(r)\|_V^2+\|u(r)\|_p^p\big)dr
		\leq
		C_T\big(1+\mathbb E\|u_0\|^2\big),
	\end{align}
	where $C_T>0$ depends only on $T$ and the structural data and is independent of $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $u_0$. If $u_1,u_2$ are two solutions driven by the same Brownian motion with initial data $u_{0,1},u_{0,2}\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_0;H)$, then
	\begin{align}
		\mathbb E\|u_1(t)-u_2(t)\|^2
		\leq
		e^{(L_G-\bar\gamma)t}\mathbb E\|u_{0,1}-u_{0,2}\|^2,
		\qquad t\geq0.
	\end{align}
	Consequently, the law of the solution is determined by the initial law $\mathcal L u_0$.
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.02193

Let mu_omega be random probability Borel measures, I a bounded open interval, 1<p<infinity, and eta_n>0 a deterministic sequence tending to zero. Set F_n(omega,E)=integral eta_n/((t-E)^2+eta_n^2) dmu_omega(t), jointly measurable. If sup_n E integral_I F_n^p <= C<infinity, then almost surely mu_omega|I=rho_omega dE with rho_omega in Lp(I), and E integral_I rho_omega^p <= C/pi^p. For 0<p<=1, integral_I F_eta^p <= |I|^(1-p)pi^p holds for every probability measure, including atoms; those power bounds alone cannot imply ac. p>1 is sufficient, not necessary for ac, and the criterion may yield zero mass on I.

[Corollary 11 of arXiv:2608.18834, 'The Parabolic Anderson Model's Total Mass at Small Times: Geometry, Fluctuations, and Reno'] Suppose that Assumption \ref{Assumption} holds,
and let $\ka>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $H_0>1/2$ or $\partial D$ is sufficiently irregular, then the deterministic
heat diffusion mechanism dominates $u_\ka$'s total mass asymptotics. More specifically:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $H_0>1/2$ and \eqref{Equation: Regular Heat Content} holds, then
\[\lim_{t\to0} t^{-1/2}\big(|D|-\msf M_\ka(t)\big)=\frac{\sqrt{2}|\partial D|}{\sqrt{\pi}}\qquad\text{in probability}.\]
\item If \eqref{Equation: Fractal Heat Content} holds for any $\msf m\in(d-1,d)$, then
\[\lim_{t\to0}\frac{1}{\log t}\log\big||D|-\msf M_\ka(t)\big|=\frac{d-\msf m}{2}\qquad\text{in probability}.\]
\end{enumerate}
\item If $H_0=1/2$ and \eqref{Equation: Regular Heat Content} holds, then as $t\to0$, one has
\[\mbf E\big[|D|-\msf M_\ka(t)\big]\sim\frac{\sqrt{2}|\partial D|}{\sqrt{\pi}}t^{1/2}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sqrt{\mbf{Var}\big[|D|-\msf M_\ka(t)\big]}\sim\ka\mf c\,t^{1/2}.\]
In particular, the noise now has an impact on the first-order total mass asymptotic via $\ka$ and the constant $\mf c$ in \eqref{Equation: c Constant}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 11 of arXiv:2608.18834

body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Analyse M(1,1) on Z^2 through the range of the first-coordinate walk. Result: In M(1,1) the first coordinate moves only at first visits and the second at later visits; the set of visited vertices is the range, and the first-coordinate process is a simple random walk on Z run at the rate of new visits. Recurrence of M(1,1) would follow if the walk returns to the origin infinitely often; since the second coordinate performs a simple random walk on the column above the current first coordinate whenever the vertex was visited before, the walk behaves in each column like a 1D random walk (recurrent) until it hits an unvisited vertex, at which time the first coordinate steps. The number of new visits up to time n is the range R_n; the first coordinate after n steps is a simple random walk at time R_n, so |X^1_n| is of order sqrt(R_n), and the range of a planar walk-like process is at most n, giving |X^1_n| <= sqrt n; a return to the origin requires both coordinates to vanish. A heuristic: if R_n ≍ n/log n as for planar simple random walk then the first coordinate is diffusive at the slower clock, and the walk is 'more recurrent' than planar simple random walk, supporting the conjecture; but the range of M(1,1) is not that of simple random walk because the exploration is column-wise. A rigorous partial fact: M(1,1) is recurrent if and only if the first coordinate returns to 0 infinitely often at times when the second coordinate is 0; since within a column the second coordinate is a recurrent 1D walk that keeps returning to 0 until it finds a new vertex, and new vertices in a column are found at the ends of the visited interval, the question is whether the first-coordinate walk (which is a simple random walk in the clock of new visits) visits 0 infinitely often, which it does a.s. (1D recurrence), and whether at those visits the second coordinate is 0 - not automatic. So recurrence of M(1,1) reduces to: at the (infinitely many) times the first coordinate is 0, the second coordinate, which then performs a 1D walk in the column of 0 with the visited interval of that column, returns to height 0 before finding a new vertex - which has probability bounded below by a constant each time if the visited interval around height 0 in column 0 has length bounded... the visited interval in column 0 grows, and the probability of returning to 0 from the boundary of an interval of length L before exiting is of order 1/L... summing over the visits to column 0 gives a divergent series only if the interval lengths grow slowly enough. This is the crux and I did not settle it; the reduction is recorded. Key identity: M(1,1) recurrent iff, at the infinitely many returns of the first coordinate to 0, the second coordinate returns to 0 in column 0 before finding a new vertex; the return probability is of order 1/(visited interval length). Obstruction: Growth rate of the visited interval in column 0 not controlled.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Centered fourth-moment diameter inequality and reweighted Cauchy-profile critical points Result: Candidate sharp answer C=1. For any centered law Q of support diameter D, with a=E X^2 and b=E X^4, a<=D^2/4 and b+3a^2<=D^2*a. Reweighting mu by ((x-u)^2+R^2)^(-2) at a stationary Cauchy profile gives y=R^2<=3a when the second derivative is nonnegative, and 1/F=(b+2ay+y^2)/(a+y)<=D^2. Equality forces symmetric endpoint Bernoulli and a strict fourth-order maximum. Thus no local minimum has F<=1/D^2; each level 1/t for t>=D^2 has at most two roots. Biane parametrization and the source level-set lemma imply unimodality. Symmetric Bernoulli gives sharpness. Check: Second analytic route differentiates v_t directly at critical points. For symmetric Bernoulli on {-c,c}, v_t second derivative at 0 equals (4*c^2-t)/(t*sqrt(t-c^2)), so t<4*c^2=D^2 gives a positive density local minimum. The centered moment inequality follows independently from E[(X-Xprime)^4]<=D^2*E[(X-Xprime)^2]. These are same-author checks, not independent review. [Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] Let $\fg$ be a simple Lie algebra, not of symplectic type. 
Let $z \in Z \subset \BP \fg^*$ be a point on the adjoint variety $Z$ of $\fg$.  Then for the system of contact fundamental forms $S_z = \oplus_{k \geq 0} S_z^k$, $S_z^k \subset U_k(\fn_z)^*$,   we have 
    $$ S_z^{k+1}  =  \left\{ F \in U_{k+1}(\fn_z)^* \mid  \begin{array}{l}  \sX_v (F) \in S_z^k \mbox{ for all } v \in \fn_{z,1} \mbox{ and } \\  \sX_v (F) \in S_z^{k-1} \mbox{ for all } v\in \fn_{z,2} \end{array} \right\} $$ for all $k \geq 2$, where $\sX_v$ is the right-invariant vector field on the Heisenberg group of $\fn_z$ whose value at the origin is $v \in \fn_z$. Let A be a linear operator on a Banach space X, and let M ≥ 1, ω ∈ ℝ. The following are equivalent: (a) A generates a C_0-semigroup (T(t))_{t ≥ 0} with ‖T(t)‖ ≤ M e^{ωt} for all t ≥ 0; (b) A is closed, densely defined, every real λ > ω lies in ρ(A), and ‖(λ − A)^{-n}‖ ≤ M/(λ − ω)^n for all λ > ω and all n ≥ 1; (c) A is closed, densely defined, every λ with Re λ > ω lies in ρ(A), and ‖(λ − A)^{-n}‖ ≤ M/(Re λ − ω)^n for all such λ and all n ≥ 1. Contraction case (M = 1, ω = 0): A generates a contraction C_0-semigroup iff A is closed, densely defined, (0, ∞) ⊂ ρ(A) and ‖(λ − A)^{-1}‖ ≤ 1/λ for all λ > 0; here the single power n = 1 suffices. When M > 1 the estimates on all powers n cannot be dropped: the n = 1 bound alone is a strictly weaker (Kreiss-type) condition.
X is a Banach space
A is a linear operator, closed and densely defined in (b),(c)
the resolvent power estimates hold for every n ≥ 1 when M > 1

[Definition 14 (Square well model (SWM)) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to[-1,1]$,
    the \emph{square well model} (SWM) on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\alpha\in[-1,1]^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\SWM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\alpha) = \frac1{Z_{\SWM,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-\beta H_{\SWM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\alpha)} \diff\alpha,
    \]
    where $Z_{\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\alpha$ the Lebesgue measure, and
    \[
        H_{\SWM,\Lambda}^\zeta(\alpha) := \sum_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}} (\alpha_x-\alpha_y)^2 + \sum_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}} (\alpha_x-\zeta_y)^2.
    \]
    The label $\SWM$ is omitted when no confusion is likely to arise.
title: Square well model (SWM)

[Corollary lem:sumtointegral of arXiv:2609.01825, 'On everywhere locally soluble varieties \\ in families over toric bases'] Let $\vec W = (\log (B/X_1), \ldots, \log (B/X_k))$ and $1< \theta \leq 2$. Then, for $\gamma > \max_{1\leq l\leq k} \sum_{i=1}^s \frac{\varpi_{li}}{\alpha_i}$, we have
	\begin{multline*}
		\Upsilon(B; \vec X)
		= c_f \Bigl( \prod_{i=1}^s \alpha_i^{-\ell_i} \Bigr) \int_{\cal P(\vec W)}  \prod_{i=1}^s \mathrm e^{t_i} (t_i + 1)^{\ell_i} \,\mathrm d\vec t\\
		+ O\biggl(
		C_f (\log \theta)^{-A - s} \int_{\cal P(\vec W + (\gamma \log \theta,\ldots,\gamma\log\theta))} (\min\nolimits_i t_i + 1)^{-\delta} \prod_{i=1}^s \mathrm e^{t_i} (t_i + 1)^{\ell_i} \,\mathrm d\vec t
		\biggr)\\
		+ O\biggl(
		C_f \int_{\Xi} \prod_{i=1}^s \mathrm e^{t_i} (t_i + 1)^{\ell_i} \,\mathrm d\vec t

	\end{multline*}
	where
	\begin{equation*}
		\Xi = \cal P(\vec W + (\gamma \log \theta, \dots, \gamma \log \theta)) \setminus \cal P(\vec W - (\gamma \log \theta, \dots, \gamma \log \theta)).
	\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 5 of arXiv:2606.07194, 'Survival Probability of Markov Linear Reccurence Sequence in a Random Environment: Subcrit'] Let $\{Y_n\}$ be a strongly subcritical positive zero-absorbing MRSRE with $\rho\in (0,1)$. Assume that~(\ref{BnCond}) and ${\bf E}^{(h)}\kappa<\infty$ holds for some $h>h^*_+$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}
\item \begin{equation}

{\bf P}(Y_n>0|Y_0=i)\sim f^*_i \rho^n,\quad {\bf P}(Y_n=k|Y_n>0)\to p_k^*,\ n\to\infty,
\end{equation}
where $\{p_k^*\}$ is a distribution, and $\{f^*_i\}$ is a bounded sequence such that
$$
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty} p_{i,j} f^*_j=\rho f^*_i,\ i>0,\
\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} p_i^* p_{i,j}=\rho p^*_i,\ j>0,\
\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} p_i^* f^*_i=1;
$$
\item for any $h>h^*_+$ 
$$
{\bf P}(Y_n>0|Y_0=i)\le c i^h \rho^n,\ i>0,
$$
where $c=c(h)$ is some constant.
\item For any positive $h$ such that $R(h)<\rho$ and~(\ref{BnCond}) holds, the distribution $\{p_k^*\}$ has a finite $h$-th moment.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 5 of arXiv:2606.07194

[Corollary 12 (Tubular criterion) of arXiv:2607.20680, 'Exact Scale--Shape Factorization of the Typical Poisson--Voronoi Cell Volume in Arbitrary '] Define the zero-degeneracy locus by
  \[
    \mathcal D_{d,k}
    =
    \bigcap_{j=1}^{\infty}
    \overline{\{\theta\in\Theta_{d,k}:G(\theta)<1/j\}},
  \]
where closures are taken in \(\Sph^{dk-1}\). This set is closed, and every sequence \((\theta_n)\subset\Theta_{d,k}\) satisfying \(G(\theta_n)\to0\) has all its accumulation points in \(\mathcal D_{d,k}\). Suppose that, for some \(c,C,\beta,q,r_0>0\),
    \begin{equation}
    G(\theta)
    \geq
    c\,\operatorname{dist}(\theta,\mathcal D_{d,k})^\beta,
     
  \end{equation}    
    \begin{equation}
    \Haus^{dk-1}
    \bigl(
      \{\theta\in\Theta_{d,k}:
      \operatorname{dist}(\theta,\mathcal D_{d,k})\leq r\}
    \bigr)
    \leq Cr^q,
    \qquad 0<r\leq r_0.
    
  \end{equation}
If \(q>\beta k\), then
  \[
    \E[A_k^{-k}]<\infty.
  \]
In particular, \(q>\beta(d+1)\) is sufficient on the minimal-facet stratum. The existence of exponents satisfying these inequalities is not asserted here.

[Proposition 11 (Tail functions) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] For integers $n\ge 1$ and $h\ge 0$, we define
\[
q_n(h):=\Pp(H_n\le h),\qquad p_n(h):=1-q_n(h)=\Pp(H_n>h).
\]
Then:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $h\mapsto q_n(h)$ is non-decreasing and $h\mapsto p_n(h)$ is non-increasing.
    \item $n\mapsto q_n(h)$ is non-increasing and $n \mapsto p_n(h)$ is
        non-decreasing.
\end{itemize}

Assumptions (assu:space of the paper), (assu:noise of the paper), (assu:hat of the paper), and (assu:inv of the paper) hold.

and for any $u_0\in H_1$, and any $t\in [0,T]$, it holds that,
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{ess\,sup}\displaylimits_{0\leq s\leq t}\mathbb{E}\left(\|u(s)\|^2_1\right)+(2\alpha-\beta)\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\|u(s)\|_1^2\,ds \leq \|u_0\|^2_1 + \eta t,
\end{align*}
where $\beta\ge 0$ is as in Assumption (assu:inv of the paper).
In particular, for $u_0\in H_1$, $u\in L^\infty([0,T];L^2(\Omega;H_1))\cap L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;H_1)$.

body:
For unit vectors v,w in C^n, let P=vv* and Q=ww*. Their determinantal laws are single-site laws with probabilities |v_i|^2 and |w_i|^2. The optimal coupling cost for normalized Hamming distance on subsets of {1,...,n} equals (1/n)sum_i ||v_i|^2-|w_i|^2| and is at most trace|P-Q|/n. If both laws are invariant under a finite permutation group, averaging yields an invariant coupling of the same cost. This is a finite rank-one result, with no general equivariant approximation theorem asserted.

[Lemma lem:apriori of arXiv:2604.08462, 'Convergence of $k$-point functions in\\ high dimensional percolation'] For each $\epsilon > 0$, there is a $C_k=C_k(\epsilon)$ such that if $(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in G(\epsilon, n)$ then 
\[\tau_{k+1}(x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k) \leq C_k(\epsilon) \mathrm{dist}(x_0, \{x_1, \dots, x_k\})^{4-d} n^{(4-d) (k-1) - 2}. \]
Dependence of $C(\epsilon)$ on $\epsilon$ is polynomial:
\begin{equation}
C_k(\epsilon)\le c\epsilon^{-10dk},
\end{equation}
where $c$ does not depend on $\epsilon$.

body:
[Thm of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Fix \( j \in \{1, \ldots, n\} \), and suppose \( \mathcal{Z} \) is a positive solution to the system (1.2) such that
\[ \left|x_j - x_{j\pm 1}\right|^{-\Delta} \mathcal{Z}(x_1, \ldots, x_n) \to C \neq 0 \]
as \( x_j, x_{j\pm 1} \to \xi \), uniformly for fixed \( x_k \) with \( k \neq j, j\pm 1 \). Then the process \( Y_t = |X_t - X_t^{(j\pm 1)}| \) is absolutely continuous with respect to a time-changed Bessel process of dimension
\[ \delta = 1 + 2\Delta + \frac{4}{\kappa}. \]
Depending on the asymptotics, two cases arise:
\begin{itemize}
  \item If the limit (equation fusion1 of the paper) is non-zero, then \( \Delta = \frac{\kappa - 6}{\kappa} \) and \( \delta = 3 - \frac{8}{\kappa} < 2 \), so the curves can collide (\( Y_\tau = 0 \)) with positive probability.
  \item If the limit (equation fusion1 of the paper) vanishes but (equation fusion2 of the paper) is non-zero, then \( \Delta = \frac{2}{\kappa} \), so \( \delta = 1 + \frac{8}{\kappa} > 2 \), and \( Y_t > 0 \) almost surely for \( t \leq \tau \).
\end{itemize}

body:
[Lemma 170 (One-set flow and comparison perfection) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $\Phi$ be the field of
\Cref{lem:Euler-parameter-field-completion}.  There is a Borel full-capacity
set $G_{\rm fl}\subset G_{\rm reg}$, independent of all flow parameters,
such that
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{s,t}(x,y)
 =\Phi_{u,t}\bigl(x,\Phi_{s,u}(x,y)\bigr)
\end{equation}
for every $x\in G_{\rm fl}$,
$0\le s\le u\le t\le T$, and $y\in\mathbb R^m$.

More generally, let
$\widetilde\Phi:\Omega\times\Delta_T\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m$
be jointly Borel.  Suppose that outside one Borel polar set both parameter
fields are locally continuous and that, for every $P\in\cP$ and every fixed
$(s,y)$, the processes
$\Phi_{s,\cdot}(\cdot,y)$ and
$\widetilde\Phi_{s,\cdot}(\cdot,y)$ are indistinguishable under $P$.
Then there is one Borel $\cP$-polar set $N$, independent of
$P,s,t,y$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{s,t}(x,y)=\widetilde\Phi_{s,t}(x,y)
\end{equation}
for every $x\notin N$, $0\le s\le t\le T$, and
$y\in\mathbb R^m$.

[Theorem thm:Lie-formula of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] For every $f\in C_c^\infty(G)$, locally uniformly in $x$,
\begin{equation}
  A_hf(x)\longrightarrow\mathcal A_Gf(x),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal A_Gf(x)
  =\frac1{\widehat V}\left(
    \frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^kM_{ij}X_iX_jf(x)
    -\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^k
      M_{ij}\Tr(\ad_{X_j})X_if(x)
  \right).
\end{equation}
In particular, the drift vanishes when $G$ is unimodular.

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2607.11076, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation for Stochastic Differential Equations driven by Fractio'] Let $\{X^\varepsilon,\varepsilon>0\}$ be a family of random variables taking values in a Polish space $\mathscr{X}$. Let $\eta(\varepsilon)$ be a positive real-valued function going to $+\infty$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ and let $I$ be a rate function on $\mathscr{X}$. We say that $\{X^\varepsilon,\varepsilon>0\}$ satisfies the Laplace principle with speed $\eta^{-1}(\varepsilon)$ and rate function $I$ if for every bounded and continuous function $f:\mathscr{X}\to\mathbb{R}$
		\[
		\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0} -\eta^{-1}(\varepsilon)\ln\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left\{-\eta(\varepsilon)f(X^\varepsilon)\right\}\right] = \inf_{x\in\mathscr{X}}[I(x) + f(x)].
		\]

Let n>=2, 0<q<1 and lambda>=1. On the simple complete graph Kn, sample an edge subset A with probability proportional to q^k(A) lambda^|A|, where k(A) counts all connected components, including isolated vertices. Every pair of distinct edge indicators is negatively correlated. The q->0 limit at fixed lambda gives the same pairwise assertion for connected spanning subgraphs of Kn sampled with probability proportional to lambda^|A|, including the uniform case lambda=1. This does not assert negative association or the arbitrary-graph conjecture. Source: arXiv:2610.00549, Theorem 1.9 and Corollary 1.10, p. 6.

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] Assume
\begin{align} 
V\in C^2(\R) \quad \text{and} \quad 0<c_-\le V''\le c_+<\infty,
\end{align}
for some positive constants $c_+$ and $c_-$.
Let $\ell_0 \ge 1$, $p\ge 4$, and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function 
on $\mathcal{X}_N=\R^N$ for some $p'>p$
depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}=(\eta(x))_{x\in \La_{\ell_0}}$
such that $ \tilde{f}(u_0)  =0$ and 
$\tilde{f}' (u_0)=0$.  Then, there exists a constant $C=C(u_0,\ell_0)>0$, 
which is uniform in $N, \ell, \ga\in \R$, such that, for $T>0$, 
$\ell\geq \ell_0$ and a function $h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}  
& E_{\mu_{u_0}}\bigg[ \; \sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big| \int_0^t ds \; \sum_{x\in\T_N} 
   h(s,x)  r_s^{N,\ell;2}(x)  \Big|^p\; \bigg]\\
& \hskip 3mm \notag
    \le  C \Big( T^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2}\ell^{p/2} +T^{p-1} N^p \ell^{-3p/2}\Big)
        \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})} \int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}}|h(t,x)|^p dt,
\end{align}
where 
\begin{align}  
r_s^{N,\ell;2}(x)=f(\tau_x \eta^{N}_s)  - \frac{1}{2} \tilde{f}''(u_0)
\Big\{\Big(\big(\eta^{N}_s\big)^{(\ell)}(x)-u_0\Big)^2    
  -\frac{{\rm var}(u_0)}{2\ell+1} \Big\}.
\end{align}
and 
${\rm var}(u)=u'(\la(u)) = E^{\mu_u}[(\eta(0)-u)^2]$ is the variance of $\mu_u$;
see \eqref{eq:u-deri}.
Recall \eqref{eq:eta-ell-B} for $\eta^{(\ell)}(x)$ and we take $\eta_s^N$ 
for $\eta$.
On the other hand, when only $\tilde{f}(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
& E_{\mu_{u_0}}\bigg[\; \sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big| \int_0^t  ds \; \sum_{x\in{\T_N}} 
  \; h(s,x) r_s^{N,\ell;1}(x)\Big|^p\; \bigg]\\
&\hskip 3mm \notag
  \le  C \Big( T^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2}\ell^{p} +T^{p-1} N^p \ell^{-p}\Big)
        \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})} \int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}}|h(t,x)|^p dt,
\end{align}
where
\begin{align}  
r_s^{N,\ell;1}(x) = f(\tau_x \eta^{N}_s) 
  - \tilde{f}'(u_0)\Big\{\big(\eta^{N}_s\big)^{(\ell)}(x) - u_0\Big\}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 39 (Stegall's variational principle) of arXiv:2606.16636, 'Free energy of non-convex multi-species spin glasses with centered Ising spins'] Let $\mcl K$ be a convex and weakly compact set in a separable Hilbert space $\mcl H$, and let $g:\mcl K\to\R$ be an upper semi-continuous function bounded from above. Then, for every $\delta>0$, there exists $\iota\in \mcl H$ with $|\iota|_{\mcl H}\leq \delta$ such that $g+\la \iota,\cdot\ra_{\mcl H}$ attains its maximum on $\mcl K$.
title: Stegall's variational principle

[Definition d.fg of arXiv:2510.07682, 'From tug-of-war to Brownian Boost: \\ explicit ODE solutions for player-funded stochastic-'] For $\rho,\xi \in (0,\infty)$,
let $S_\rho(\xi,\bullet):\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} \to (0,\infty)$\hfff{srho} denote the unique solution to the differential equation
\[
 \frac{{\rm d}}{{\rm d}u} S_\rho(\xi,u) \,=\, - \frac{8\rho \, S_\rho(\xi,u)^{1+\rho}}{\big(1+S_\rho(\xi,u)^\rho\big)^2} \, ,
 \qquad S_\rho(\xi,0)=\xi \, .
\]
Associate to this solution the pair of functions $f_\rho(\xi,\bullet),g_\rho(\xi,\bullet): \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} \to (0,\infty)$\hfff{fgrho} by means of
\[
f_\rho(\xi,u) \,=\, \exp\!\left\{ 2 \int_0^{u} \Bigg(
 1 - \frac{2}{\big(1+S_\rho(\xi,r)^\rho\big)^2}\,\Big(1+(1-\rho)S_\rho(\xi,r)^\rho \Big)  \Bigg)\, {\rm d}r \right\}
\]
and
$$
g_\rho(\xi,u) \,=\, \xi \cdot  \exp\!\left\{ -2 \int_0^{u} \Bigg(
 1 - \frac{2}{\big(1+S_\rho(\xi,r)^\rho\big)^2}\, \Big((1-\rho)S_\rho(\xi,r)^\rho + S_\rho(\xi,r)^{2\rho}\Big) \Bigg)\, {\rm d}r \right\}
$$
for $u \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$.
When $u <0$, the integrals are specified in the usual way: $\int_a^b h = - \int_b^a h$ for $a > b$.
title: Definition d.fg of arXiv:2510.07682

[Corollary 14 (Gaussian rough paths) of arXiv:2605.30869, 'Approximate Transitivity of Young Translation on Rough Paths'] Fix  $\alpha \in (0,1]$ and $q \geq 1$ with $\frac{1}{q}+\alpha>1$. Let $X^n$ be a sequence of $C^{0;\alpha,q\text{-var}}$-valued Gaussian processes, and denote by  $\cH_{X^n}$ their Cameron-Martin spaces. Assume that $\mathbf{X}$ is a $\mathcal{C}^{0;\alpha}_{\mathbf{1}}$-valued random variable, such that
 \[
 \lim_{n \to \infty} S_{\lfloor \alpha^{-1} \rfloor}\left( X_n \right) = \mathbf{X} \mbox{ in probability, in }\mathcal{C}^{0,\alpha}_{\mathbf{1}}.
 \]
Further assume that
\[
\cH = \left\{ h = \lim_{n \to \infty} h_n \mbox{ in }C^{\alpha,q\text{-var}}, \;\; h_n \in \mathcal{H}_{X^n}, \sup_{n\geq 0} \|h_n\|_{\cH_{X^n}} < \infty \right\}
\]
is dense in $C^{0;\alpha,q\text{-var}}_0$. Then the law of $\mathbf{X}$ has full support in $\mathcal{C}^{0;\alpha}_{\mathbf{1}}$.

[Theorem thm:observable-suboptimality-CS of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Suppose Assumptions~(assump:strong-convexity of the paper)--(assump:stepsize-bound of the paper) hold. Let $t_0 \ge 4$ and $\eta_t = 2/(\mu(t+1))$ for every $t \ge t_0$, and let $R_0$ be an $\mathcal{F}_{t_0-1}$-measurable quantity satisfying $R_0 \ge Z_{t_0}$ almost surely. Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$, the process $\{\widehat U_t^{\mathrm{sub}}(\alpha)\}_{t \ge t_0}$ is fully observable and satisfies
\[
    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t\ge t_0:\
        f(\bar x_t) - f(x^\star)
        \le
        \widehat U_t^{\mathrm{sub}}(\alpha)
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Observable confidence sequence for $f(\bar x_t) - f(x^\star)$

geodesic cone condition with fixed parameters $(r_0,\theta)$. Assume
\[
K\subset\Omega,

\]

[Definition 12 (Decorated $p$-adic harmonizable fractional stable motion) of arXiv:2606.24056, 'Decorated stable $p$-adic self-similar processes with stationary increments'] Let \(0<\alpha\le2\), \(H>0\), and 
\(\phi_s:\T\to\R\), \(s\in\Z/L\Z\) be bounded measurable functions.   For
\(n\in\Nzero\), define
\begin{equation}
  f_n(k,r,u,s)
  =
  p^{-kH}
  \left(
    \phi_{s+k}\left(r+\frac{un}{p^k}\right)-\phi_{s+k}(r)
  \right),
\end{equation}
where \(s+k\) is modulo \(L\), and \(u n/p^k\) denotes the class in
\(\T\) obtained from any integer representative of
\(u\in(\Z/p^k\Z)^\times\).  Let
\(M_\alpha\) be a real symmetric \(S\alpha S\) random measure on \(E\) with
control measure \(\mu\). Then, the decorated $p$-adic harmonizable fractional stable motion is defined as 
\[
  X_n=\int_E f_n\,dM_\alpha,\qquad n\in\Nzero.
\]
title: Decorated $p$-adic harmonizable fractional stable motion

[Prop P:properties-elpp of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, and let $\mathcal{Q}^\rho$ be a subsequential limit in law of $\mathcal{Q}_n^{\rho_n}$ along a sequence $\rho_n \to \rho$. Then $\mathcal{Q}^\rho$ satisfies the following properties. In what follows, $c> 0$ are universal constants, and we define
		$\mathcal{G}^\rho(x, s; y, t) = \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s; y, t) + \frac{(x-y)^2}{(t-s)}$ for any $(x,s;y,t)\in \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item \textup{(Independent increments)} For any disjoint collection of time intervals $(s_i, t_i), i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$, the increments
		$\mathcal{Q}^\rho(\cdot, s_i; \cdot, t_i)$
		are independent.
		\item \textup{(Metric composition)} For any fixed $r < s < t$ and $x, y \ge 0$, we have
		$$
		\mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s; y, t) = \max_{z \ge 0} \mathcal{Q}^\rho(x, s; z, r) + \mathcal{Q}^\rho(z, r; y, t).
		$$
		\item \textup{(KPZ scaling)} Fix $q > 0$, and consider the rescaled field
		$$
		\mathcal{Q}^{\rho, q}(x, s; y, t) := q^{-1} \mathcal{Q}^\rho(q^2x, q^3 s; q^2 y, q^3 t).
		$$
		Then $\mathcal{Q}^{\rho, q}$ is a subsequential limit of the sequence $\mathcal{Q}^{q \rho_n}_n$.
		\item \textup{(One-point tail bounds)} For $u = (x, s; y, s + t) \in \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$, and all $a > 0$,
		\begin{align*}
			\mathbb{P}( \mathcal{G}^\rho(u)< - a t^{1/3}) &\le 2\exp(-c a^3), \\
			\mathbb{P}( \mathcal{G}^\rho(u) > a t^{1/3} + t (\rho\vee 0)^2) &\le 2\exp\left(-c a^{3/2} \left(1 \wedge \frac{\sqrt{a}}{(\rho \vee 0) t^{1/3}}\right)\right).
		\end{align*}
		Furthermore, for $u = (0, s; 0, s + t)$ on the diagonal, we have the following Gaussian lower bound: for all $0 < a < t (\rho\vee 0)^2$,
		\begin{align*}
			\mathbb{P}( \mathcal{G}^\rho(u) < -a + t (\rho\vee 0)^2) &\le 2\exp\left(- \frac{ca^2}{(\rho\vee 0)t}\right).
		\end{align*}
		\item \textup{(Two-point spatial tail bound)} 
        There is a universal constant $C_0>0$, such that for any $u = (x, s; y, s+t), u' = (x, s; y + z, s+t)  \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, and 
        $a>C_0\max(z^{3/2}/t, \sqrt{z}|x-y|/t, \sqrt{z} (\rho\vee 0))$,
        we have:
		\begin{equation}
			
\mathbb{P}(|\mathcal{G}^\rho(u) - \mathcal{G}^\rho(u')| \ge a\sqrt{z}) \le 2 \exp(- c a^2).
		\end{equation}
		\item \textup{(Two-point temporal tail bound)} There is a universal constant $C_0>0$, such that for any $u = (x, s; y, s + t), u' = (x, s; y', s+t + r)  \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, where $0<r<t$ and $(x, s), (y, s+t), (y', s + t + r)$ are all collinear, and $a > C_0\max(r^{2/3}(x-y)^2/t^2, r^{2/3}(\rho\vee 0)^2)$, we have:
		\begin{equation*}
			\mathbb{P}(|\mathcal{G}^\rho(u) - \mathcal{G}^\rho(u')| \ge a r^{1/3}) \le 2 \exp(- c a^{3/2}).
		\end{equation*}
		\item \textup{(Basic parabolic shape estimate)} For any $(x, s; y, s + t) \in \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$ and $a, \delta > 0$ we have:
		\begin{equation*}
            \begin{split}
                \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{G}^\rho(x, s; y + z, s+ t) &\le t(\rho\vee 0)^2  + a t^{1/3} + \delta z^2 \text{ for all } z \in [-y, \infty)) \\

body:
[Corollary cor:sharp of arXiv:2608.25279, 'Provable Non-Acceleration of Standard Strang\\ Splittings of Kinetic Langevin Dynamics'] \begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(i)] For the tuning
\begin{equation*}
 h=\frac1{4\sqrt\kappa},
 \qquad
 \gamma=4\sqrt\kappa,
 \qquad
 Q=Q_{1/(4\sqrt\kappa),\,4\sqrt\kappa}^{U},
\end{equation*}
there is a universal
constant $C_1<\infty$ such that, for every $\kappa>1$, $d\ge1$,
$U\in\mathcal U_\kappa^d$, every initial state $z$, and every
$\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation*}
 t_{\mathrm{mix}}(z,\varepsilon;Q,\pi)
 \le C_1\kappa\log\!\left(\frac{C_1\kappa(1+W_2(\delta_z,\pi))}{\varepsilon}\right),
\end{equation*}
where $\pi$ is the unique invariant law of $Q$.
\item[\rm(ii)] Let $\mathfrak t$
be any numerically
stable fixed-parameter OBABO tuning rule, let $C,c>0$ and $a,b\ge0$
be constants, let $\tau:(1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfy
$\tau(\kappa)=o(\kappa)$ as $\kappa\to\infty$, and let
$\kappa_0>1$. Then there exist $\kappa\ge\kappa_0$ and
$U\in\mathcal U_\kappa^2$ such that $Q_{h_\kappa,\gamma_\kappa}^U$ has a
unique invariant law $\pi$, and there are $z\in\mathbb R^4$ and
$n\in\mathbb N$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\delta_z(Q_{h_\kappa,\gamma_\kappa}^U)^n-\pi}_{\mathrm{TV}}
 >C\kappa^a\bigl(1+W_2(\delta_z,\pi)\bigr)^b
   \exp\!\left(-\frac{cn}{\tau(\kappa)}\right).
\end{equation}
In particular, no such bound holds with $\tau(\kappa)=\kappa^\alpha$
for any $\alpha<1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sharpness of the diffusive scale

[Definition def:scaleFunction of arXiv:2412.05030, 'Characterization of Subordinate Symmetric Markov Processes'] For constants $0 < \alpha_1 \le \alpha_2$, 
  we say a continuous function $\psi : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ satisfies $LU(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$
  if $\psi$ is strictly increasing, $\psi(0) = 0$, $\psi(1) = 1$  and 
  there exists constants $C \ge 1$ such that
  \begin{align}
    C^{-1} \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{\alpha_1} \le \frac{\psi(R)}{\psi(r)} \le C \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{\alpha_2}, \qquad 0 < r \le R.
  \end{align}
  We call such function $\psi$ a scale function.
title: Scale function

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Any bounded operator $T\in B(H)$ can be decomposed as
$$T=U|T|$$
with $U$ being a partial isometry, and with $|T|=\sqrt{T^*T}$.

body:
[Theorem 22 (Two-parameter rough integral on rectangular domains) of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] Let 
\[
Z \in \mathcal{D}^{p, q}_{\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y}}\big([a, b] \times [c,d], \mathrm{Hom}(V \boxtimes W, F)\big).
\] 
Then the limit
\[
\int_{[a,b] \times [c,d]} Z_{s, u} \, d(\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y})  
   :=  \lim_{\left|\mathcal{P} \times \mathcal{D}\right| \to 0} 
   \sum_{\mathcal{P}\times \mathcal{D}} \Omega^Z
\]
exists and satisfies the estimate
\begin{align*}
\Bigg|
\int_{[a,b]\times[c,d]} Z_{s,u}\, d(\mathbf{X}_s,\mathbf{Y}_u)
- \Omega^Z\begin{pmatrix} a, b \\ c, d \end{pmatrix}
\Bigg|
&\le C_{p,q,T}\Big[
      A(\theta,T,\mathbf{R})\,
      \omega_{\mathbf{X}}(a,b)^{\theta}\,
      \omega_{\mathbf{Y}}(c,d)^{\theta} \\
&\qquad
      + B_X(c,d)\,\omega_{\mathbf{X}}(a,b)^{\theta}
      + B_Y(a,b)\,\omega_{\mathbf{Y}}(c,d)^{\theta}
\Big].
\end{align*}

where $\theta = \min(\frac{\floor{p} + 1}{p}, \frac{\floor{q} + 1}{q})$ and 
\begin{align*}
&A(p, q, \mathbf{R}) 
= \left( \sup_{j \in [0:\kappa)} \| \mathbf{X}^{(j+1)} \|_{p_j} \right)
  \left( \sup_{k \in  [0:\lambda)} \| \tilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(k+1)} \|_{\tilde{p}_k} \right)
  \left( \sup_{(j,k)\in [0:\kappa) \times [0:\lambda)} \| \mathbf{R}^{(j,k)} \|_{(q_j,\tilde{q}_k)} \right),\\
&B_{X}(c,d)
= 
\sup_{(j,k)\in [0:\kappa) \times [0:\lambda)}\left[ 
  \|\mathbf{X}^{(j+1)}\|_{\frac{p}{j+1}}\,
  \|\mathbf{Y}^{(k+1)}\|_{\frac{q}{k+1}}\,
  \big\| R^{1, (j,k)}
       \big\|_{\frac{p}{\kappa - j}}\,
  \omega_{\mathbf{Y}}(c,d)^{\frac{k+1}{q}}
\right],\\
&B_{Y}(a,b)
= \sup_{(j,k)\in [0:\kappa) \times [0:\lambda)}
\left[
   \|\mathbf{X}^{(j+1)}\|_{\frac{p}{j+1}}\,
  \|\mathbf{Y}^{(k+1)}\|_{\frac{q}{k+1}}\,
  \big\| R^{2,(j,k)}\!
       \big\|_{\frac{q}{\lambda - k}}\,
  \omega_{\mathbf{X}}(a,b)^{\frac{j+1}{p}}
\right].
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Two-parameter rough integral on rectangular domains

[Theorem Jac-thm of arXiv:2609.00592, 'Bounded cohomology property on Jacobian elliptic surfaces with simplicial Mori cones'] Let $X$ be a Jacobian elliptic surface with finite Mordell-Weil group and  exactly one reducible fiber. 
\begin{enumerate}
	\item If $\chi(\mathcal O_X)\ge\rho(X)$, then $\overline{\operatorname{NE}}(X)$ is simplicial. 	
	\item If  $\chi(\mathcal O_X)\ge\rho(X)$ and $q(X)=0$, then $X$ satisfies the BCP.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Jac-thm of arXiv:2609.00592

[Proposition 27 of arXiv:2510.27589, 'Geodesic switches and exceptional times in dynamical Brownian last passage percolation'] Fix $\beta\in (0,1/2)$, $\mu\in(0,1)$ and $\varepsilon>0$. For any $p\in \{0\}_{\RR}$ and $q\in \{n\}_{\RR}$ with $\slope(p,q)\in (\mu,\mu^{-1})$, and for all $n$ large enough and all $[s,t]\subseteq \RR$, we have
  \begin{equation}
    
    \EE[\switch_{p}^{q,[s,t]}([\![\beta n, (1-\beta)n]\!]_\RR)]\leq n^{5/3+\varepsilon}(t-s).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 27 of arXiv:2510.27589

body:
[Theorem 44 of arXiv:2609.00245, 'Higher-order Gaussian bounds for maximally subelliptic boundary value problems'] The following statements hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item \(\MetricW\) and \(\MetricV\) are metrics on each connected component of \(\ManifoldNOne\),
            and the topology generated by either of them agrees with the topology on \(\ManifoldNOne\) as a manifold.
        \item \(\MetricV[\xi][\eta]\wedge 1\approx \MetricW[\xi][\eta]\wedge 1\), \(\forall \xi,\eta\in \CompactOne\).
    \end{enumerate}
    Fix \(\Omega\Subset \ManifoldNOne\) open and relatively compact with \(\CompactOne\Subset \Omega\).
    There exists \(\delta_1\in (0,1]\)
     such that the following hold:
     \begin{enumerate}[resume*]
        \item \(\forall \xi\in \CompactOne\), \(\delta\in (0,\delta_1]\), \(\Vol[\BV{\xi}{\delta}]\approx \Vol[\BW{\xi}{\delta}]\).
        \item \(\forall \xi\in \CompactOne\), \(\forall \delta\in (0,\delta_1]\), \(\Vol[\BV{\xi}{2\delta}]\lesssim \Vol[\BV{\xi}{\delta}]\).
        \item \(\forall \xi\in \CompactOne\), \(\forall \delta\in [\delta_1,\infty)\), \(\Vol[\BV{\xi}{\delta}]\wedge 1\approx 1 \approx \Vol[\BV{\xi}{\delta_1}]\).
        \item For each fixed \(\delta_0\in (0,\delta_1]\), 
        \begin{equation*}
            \Vol[\BV{\xi}{\delta_0}]\approx_{\delta_0} 1,\quad \forall \xi\in \CompactOne,
        \end{equation*}
        where the implicit constants depend on \(\delta_0\) but not on \(\xi\).
        
        \item \(\overline{\bigcup_{\xi\in \CompactOne,\delta\in (0,\delta_1]} \BV{\xi}{\delta}}\Subset \Omega\).
     \end{enumerate}
     There exist two sets, \(\SSetOne,\SSetTwo\subseteq \CompactOne\times (0,\delta_1]\),
     such that \(\SSetOne\cup\SSetTwo = \CompactOne\times (0,\delta_1]\);
     for \((\xi,\delta)\in \SSetTwo\) 
     there exists \(\Psi_{\xi,\delta}:\Cubengeq{1}\rightarrow \BV{\xi}{\delta/2}\);
     and for \((\xi,\delta)\in \SSetOne\) there exists 
     \(\Phi_{\xi,\delta}:\Cuben{1}\rightarrow \BV{\xi}{\delta/2}\)
     such that the following hold:
     \begin{enumerate}[resume*]
        \item \(\left\{ (\xi, \delta) : \xi\in \CompactOne\cap \BoundaryN, \delta\in (0,\delta_1] \right\}\subseteq \SSetTwo\).
        \item \(\forall (\xi,\delta)\in \SSetOne\), \(\Phi_{\xi,\delta}(0)=\xi\).
            \(\forall (\xi,\delta)\in \SSetTwo\), \(\exists u_n\in [0,1/8)\) with \(\Psi_{\xi,\delta}(0,u_n)=\xi\);
            when \(\xi\in \BoundaryN\), \(u_n=0\).
            
        \item \(\forall (\xi,\delta)\in \SSetOne\), \(\Phi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cuben{1} \right)\subseteq \Omega\)
            is open and \(\Phi_{\xi,\delta}:\Cuben{1}\xrightarrow{\sim} \Phi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cuben{1} \right)\)
            is a \(\CinftySpace\)-diffeomorphism.
            \(\forall(\xi,\delta)\in \SSetTwo\), \(\Psi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cubengeq{1} \right)\subseteq \Omega\)
            is open and \(\Psi_{\xi,\delta}:\Cubengeq{1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cubengeq{1} \right)\)
            is a \(\CinftySpace\)-diffeomorphism.
        \item \(\exists \gamma_0\in (0,1]\) such that the following hold:
            \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph{enumi}.\roman*)]
                \item \(\forall (\xi,\delta)\in \SSetOne\),
                    \begin{equation*}
                        \BV{\xi}{\gamma_0 \delta} 
                        \subseteq \Phi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cuben{1/4} \right)
                        \subseteq \Phi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cuben{1} \right)
                        \subseteq \BV{\xi}{\delta/2}.
                    \end{equation*}
                \item \(\forall (\xi,\delta)\in \SSetTwo\),
                    \begin{equation*}
                        \BV{\xi}{\gamma_0 \delta} 
                        \subseteq \Psi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cubengeq{1/4} \right)
                        \subseteq \Psi_{\xi,\delta}\left( \Cubengeq{1} \right)
                        \subseteq \BV{\xi}{\delta/2}.
                    \end{equation*}
            \end{enumerate}
     \end{enumerate}
     For \((\xi,\delta)\in \SSetOne\), set \(V_j^{\xi,\delta,1}:=\Phi_{\xi,\delta}^{*} \delta V_j\) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 44 of arXiv:2609.00245

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.03386, 'Twisted Gradient Flow Approach to Vegetation-Rainfall-Bushfire Interactions Model'] (\cite[Lemma 2.10]{ito-2019}) For each $v \in W^{1,2}(0,T\,;L^2(\Omega))$ and $\bar{z} \in W^{1,1}(0,T\,;L^2(\Omega))$ the function 
$t \mapsto \|v(t)\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}(t)$}}}^2$ is absolutely continuous from $[0,T]$ into $\mathbb{R}$, and we have the following energy inequality for the 
state-dependent norm associated with the quasi-variational inner products for a.e. $t \in (0,T)$:

\begin{equation*}
\left| \frac{d}{dt} \|v(t)\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}(t)$}}}^2-2(v'(t),v(t))_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}(t)$}}}\right| \le \delta^3 C_3
\|\bar{z}'(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \|v(t)\|_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\bar{z}(t)$}}}^2,
\end{equation*}

where the constant $C_3>0$ is the same one as in (2) of Lemma \ref{Lemma-2-2}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.03386

[Proposition prop:SDPI of arXiv:2605.16904, 'Positive-rate PCA and IPS with stationary Bernoulli measures are rapidly forgetful \footno'] Let $\Sigma$ be finite set.
	Let $\theta\colon\Sigma\times\Sigma\to(0,1)$ be a strictly positive stochastic matrix with stationary distribution~$q\colon\Sigma\to(0,1)$.  Let $\kappa>0$ be such that $\theta(a,b)\geq\kappa q(b)$ for each $a,b\in\Sigma$.
	Then, $D(p\theta \relto q)\leq (1-\kappa) D(p \relto q)$ for every probability distribution $p\colon\Sigma\to[0,1]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix $\alpha$ and suppose that $\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)$ holds.
	Then 
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\alpha(x)
	\ge
	a(1-\delta)L_\alpha-bL_\alpha,
	\]
	and for every $\beta\neq\alpha$,
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\beta(x)
	\le
	a\bigl(|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|+\rho\bigr)-bL_\beta.
	\]
	
	Consequently,
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\alpha(x)
	-
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\beta(x)
	\ge
	a\bigl(
	(1-\delta)L_\alpha
	-
	|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|
	-
	\rho	
	\bigr)
	-
	b(L_\alpha-L_\beta).
	\]
	
	In particular, if
	\[
	|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|
	<
	(1-\delta)L_\alpha-\rho-\frac{b}{a}(L_\alpha-L_\beta),
	\]
	then
	\[
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\alpha(x)
	>
	\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{pen}}_\beta(x).

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.20613, 'Random walks on wreath products \\and spectral gaps for coloured interchange processes'] Let $\Lambda=(\lambda^\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$ be a $G$-multipartition of $n$.  Then
\[
\dim V_\Lambda^{\Sn_n}
=
\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma}
\dim \Schur_{\lambda^\gamma}(\C^{d_\gamma}).
\]
Moreover, $V_\Lambda$ occurs in $\mathcal P_n(G)$ if and only if $\len(\lambda^\gamma)\leqslant d_\gamma$ for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 16 of arXiv:2609.03726, 'Inverse Scattering for Single Photons in Quantum Optics'] Let $k_\rho$ be the threshold from Lemma \ref{lem_LAP} with $l=[n/2]+1$ and $\delta=3/4$. Let $k>k_\rho$ and let $\alpha,\theta\in\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ satisfy $\theta\neq\alpha$.
If $\mathcal{I}_{\rho_1}$ and $\mathcal{I}_{\rho_2}$ are equivalent in the sense of \eqref{eq:equivalence_relation}, then
\begin{equation}
    A_k^{\rho_1}(\theta,\alpha) = A_k^{\rho_2}(\theta,\alpha),
\end{equation}
where $A_k^{\rho_j}(\theta,\alpha)$ denotes the scattering amplitude associated with $\rho_j$, $j=1,2$.

In particular, the equivalence class $[\mathcal I_\rho]_\infty$ determines
$A_k(\theta,\alpha)$ for every $k>k_\rho$ and every non-forward pair
$\theta\ne\alpha$.
title: Corollary 16 of arXiv:2609.03726

[Theorem THM24 of arXiv:2412.08886, 'On domination for (non-symmetric) Dirichlet forms'] Let $({\mathscr E},{\mathscr F})$ and $({\mathscr E}',{\mathscr F}')$ be two Dirichlet forms on $L^2(E,m)$ such that ${\mathscr E}'\preceq {\mathscr E}$.  Denote $\tilde{{\mathscr F}}$ as the closure of ${\mathscr F}'$ in ${\mathscr F}$ with respect to the ${\mathscr E}_1$-norm, and define
\[
	\tilde{{\mathscr E}}(f,g):={\mathscr E}(f,g),\quad f,g\in \tilde{{\mathscr F}}.
\]
Then, ${\mathscr E}'$ is strongly subordinate to $\tilde{{\mathscr E}}$, and ${\mathscr E}$ is a Silverstein extension of $\tilde{{\mathscr E}}$.  Furthermore, if $(\tilde{\mathscr E}^1, \tilde{\mathscr F}^1)$ is another Dirichlet form on $L^2(E, m)$ that satisfies these two conditions, then $(\tilde{\mathscr E}^1,\tilde{\mathscr F}^1)=(\tilde{{\mathscr E}},\tilde{{\mathscr F}})$.

    $$
    for some $\delta>0$.
    Let $\tilde{\beta}$ be the map from Theorem~\ref{thm:ClusterFrequency}. Then
    $$\mathbb E \big[ \tilde{\beta}(o,\omega^{(\lambda)}_p) \big]  \ge \delta.$$    
    In particular, $\tilde{\beta}(o,\omega^{(\lambda)}_p)>0$ with positive probability.

[Theorem RoughInt of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] \emph{([GH19])}
For any $T>0$, let $\mathbf X=(X,X^2)\in \mathscr{C}^\gamma([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$ for some $\gamma\in(1/3,1/2]$ and let
$(Y,Y^{\prime})\in\mathscr{D}_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma}([0,T];\mathcal{H}_\alpha^d)$.
Then one has that the rough integral
$$\int_{s}^{t}S_{t-u}Y_{u}d \mathbf X_u:=\lim_{|\mathcal{P}|\to 0}\sum_{[u,v]\in\mathcal{P}}S_{t-u}(Y_u \delta X_{v,u}+Y_{u}^{\prime} X^2_{v,u})$$
exists in $\hat{C}^\gamma([0,T];\mathcal{H}_\alpha)$,
where the limit is taken along any partitions $\mathcal P$ of $[s,t]$ such that mesh $|\mathcal P| \rightarrow 0$.
Furthermore, for any $0\leq\beta<3\gamma$ one has the bound
\begin{align} 
& \Big \|\int_{s}^{t}S_{t-u}Y_{u}d \mathbf X_{u}-S_{t-s}Y_{s} \delta X_{t,s}-S_{t-s}Y_{s}^{\prime} X^2_{t,s} \Big\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\alpha+\beta}} \nonumber\\
 \lesssim &   \big(|R^{Y}|_{2\gamma,\alpha}|X|_{\gamma}+\|Y'\|_{\gamma,\alpha}|X^2|_{2\gamma}\big)|t-s|^{3\gamma-\beta},
\end{align}
and the map
$$(Y,Y')\rightarrow (U,U'):=\Big(\int_0^\cdot S_{\cdot-u}Y_u d \mathbf X_u,Y \Big)$$
is continuous from $\mathscr D_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma} ([0,T]; \mathcal{H}_\alpha^d )$ to $\mathscr D_{S,\mathbf X}^{2\gamma} ([0,T]; \mathcal{H}_\alpha )$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem RoughInt of arXiv:2411.06089

[Definition def:wall of arXiv:2609.00970, 'The unique predual problem for Lipschitz spaces, revisited'] A non-empty closed subset $W\subset M$ is a \emph{geodesic wall} in $M$ if there exist two sets $A,B\subset M$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label={\upshape{(\alph*)}}]
\item $M$ equals the disjoint union $A\cup W\cup B$,
\item $W\subset\overline{A}\cap\overline{B}$,
\item $A,B$ are open and connected, and
\item for any $a\in A$, $b\in B$ there exists $w\in W$ such that $d(a,w)+d(w,b)=d(a,b)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:wall of arXiv:2609.00970

body:
[Thm 4 of arXiv:2608.13208, 'Universality in dimension $1$ of kinetically constrained lattice gases'] KCLGs in one dimension divide in three universality
classes:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $c(-1,0,\bone_{(-\infty,-1]})\neq0$ and $c(-1,0,\bone_{[0,\infty]})\neq0$,
then $q_{c}=0$. In this case the model is \emph{noncooperative} (see
\cite{Shapira2024Noncooperative} and Section \ref{subsec:noncooperative}
below).
\item If $c(-1,0,\bone_{(-\infty,-1]})=0$ and $c(-1,0,\bone_{[0,\infty)})=0$,
then $q_{c}=1$. We say in this case that the model is \emph{blocked}.
\item If $c(-1,0,\bone_{(-\infty,-1]})\neq0$ and $c(-1,0,\bone_{[0,\infty)})=0$
or vice versa, then $q_{c}\in(0,1)$. We call such models \emph{one-sided}.
\end{enumerate}
By $\bone_{(-\infty,-1]}$ (respectively $\bone_{[0,\infty)}$) we
mean the configuration filled in $(-\infty,-1]$ (respectively $[0,\infty)$)
and empty elsewhere. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2608.13208

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] There exist couplings of an ORA walk \(Q_T^{\mathrm O}\) and an
	S-ORA walk \(Q_T^{\mathrm S}\), both of length \(T\), such that,
	possibly under different couplings,
	\[
	Q_T^{\mathrm S}
	=
	G_T^{\mathrm L}Q_T^{\mathrm O},
	\qquad 
	Q_T^{\mathrm S}
	=
	Q_T^{\mathrm O}G_T^{\mathrm R},
	\]
	where \(G_T^{\mathrm L}\), \(G_T^{\mathrm R} \in \mathcal H_d\) are signed
	permutation matrices. Consequently, for every $I\subseteq [d]$ and every $X\subseteq \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we have
	\[
	\norm{Q_T^{\mathrm S}}_\infty
	\stackrel{\mathrm d}=
	\norm{Q_T^{\mathrm O}}_\infty,
	\qquad
	\kappa_I(Q_T^{\mathrm S})
	\stackrel{\mathrm d}=
	\kappa_I(Q_T^{\mathrm O}),
	\qquad
	\Theta_{Q_T^{\mathrm S}}(X)
	\stackrel{\mathrm d}=
	\Theta_{Q_T^{\mathrm O}}(X).
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 24 of arXiv:2608.18557

    \]
  \end{enumerate}

For 1 <= p < q <= infinity there is no constant C such that ||x||_p <= C ||x||_q for every finitely supported complex sequence x: the sequence of N ones followed by zeros has ||x||_p / ||x||_q = N^(1/p - 1/q), unbounded in N. So the factor n^(1/p - 1/q) in the finite-dimensional comparison cannot be replaced by a constant.

[Definition def: graph model 2 of arXiv:2411.02898, '\vspace{-1.5cm}The connectivity and phase transition in inhomogeneous random graphs of fin'] For each $i = 1, \dots, r$, let $m_i$ be a positive integer, $\bm{a}_i$ a length $m_i$ vector with positive entries, and $\bm{c}$ a $m_i \times m_i$ symmetric matrix with non-negative entries. Write $M_i = \sum_{j=1}^{i} m_i$. Let $\bm{d}$ be a $M_r \times M_r$ symmetric matrix with non-negative entries. \\
Define \[\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}} (n, r, (m_i), (\bm{a}_i), (\bm{c}_i), \bm{d}, p(n), p'(n))\]
as the random graph formed by taking the disjoint union of 
\[G_i := \ensuremath{\mathbb{G}} (n, m_i, \bm{a}_i, \bm{c}_i, p(n)),\  i = 1, \dots, r \]
and adding edges $x \in G_i, y \in G_j$ for $i \neq j$ with probability \[q_{(i,k)(j,l)} = d_{(M_{i-1}+k)(M_{j-1}+l)} p'(n),\] independently, where $k, l$ are the vertex types of $x, y$, respectively.
title: Definition def: graph model 2 of arXiv:2411.02898

body: [Definition of arXiv:2609.00636, 'Forcing monochromatic subdivisions'] A family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs is said to be \textit{degree-Ramsey bounded}, or \textit{$R_\Delta$-bounded}, if for every $s\in \mathbb{Z}^+$ and for every $G \in \mathcal{G}$ the degree-Ramsey number $R_\Delta(G;s)$ is bounded by a function depending only on $\Delta(G)$ and $s$.

body: [Definition 23 (Compressible vectors) of arXiv:2607.08696, 'Spectrum of Directed Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] Fix $m < n$ and $\delta>0$. A vector $v \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is said to be $(m,\delta)$-compressible if there exists $u \in {\rm Sparse}(m)$ such that $\|v-u\|\le \delta$. The set of such vectors is denoted by ${\rm Comp}(m,\delta)$. Its complement in $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$, the set of $(m,\delta)$-incompressible vectors is denoted by ${\rm Incomp}(m,\delta)$.
title: Compressible vectors

[Lem 11 (Poisson equation) of arXiv:2506.21087, 'Quasi-Stationary Distributions of Interacting Dynamical Systems and their approximation'] Assume \ref{condpzero}, \ref{condpun} and \ref{condpdeux}. For any $\mu\in{\cal P}({\MM})$, for any measurable function  $f:{\MM}\rightarrow\ER$, the Poisson equation \eqref{Poissonequa} admits a unique solution denoted $Q_\mu f$ and
defined by
\begin{equation}

 Q_\mu f(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \left(\kmu^n f(x) -\Pi_\mu (f)\right).
\end{equation}
Furthermore, there exists a constant $C$ such that,
\begin{itemize}

\item[(a)]  For every $\mu,\alpha \in {\cal P}(\MM)$,  
$$| \alpha Q_\mu f | \leq C \Vert f \Vert_\infty \Vert \alpha - \Pi_\mu \Vert_{VT}.$$
\item[(b)] For every $\mu \in{\cal P}(\MM)$, 
$$\Vert Q_\mu f - Q_\nu f \Vert_\infty \leq C \Vert f \Vert_\infty  \Vert \mu- \nu \Vert_{TV}.$$

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Poisson equation

[Thm eq:RootDecomp of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\Delta$ be the set of
all nonzero roots with respect to a given Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}.$
Then $\mathfrak{g}$ can be written as the direct sum 
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}+\sum_{\alpha\in\Delta}\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha}.
\end{equation}
In this decomposition, one has $\dim\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha}=1$ for
each $\alpha\in\Delta$. Moreover, if $\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta\in\Delta$
then $[\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha},\mathfrak{g}^{\beta}]=\mathfrak{g}^{\alpha+\beta}.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Root Space Decomposition
