body:
[Corollary $n/\log n$ threshold of arXiv:2512.05896, 'T\'oth's buses and the ``detachment process'''] Asymptotic regimes ($n\to\infty$) in terms of \(k(n)\):

 1. super-linear growth (\(k(n)\gg n\), i.e. \(\lambda_n\to 0\))
$R_{n,k}\sim \frac{2}{k}\ \longrightarrow\ 0.$

 2. Linear growth (\(k(n)\sim c\,n\) for some \(c>0\))
\[
R_{n,k}= \frac{e^{1/c}-1+1/c-1/c^2}{n}+\mathcal{O}\!\Big(\frac{1}{n}\Big)
 \longrightarrow\ 0.
\]

 3. Sublinear, but still above threshold (\(\tfrac{n}{\log n}\ll k(n)\ll n\))
Here \(\lambda_n=o(\log n)\) (possibly large but \(o(\log n)\)). Then
$
R_{n,k}\sim \dfrac{1}{k}\ \longrightarrow\ 0.
$

 4. Critical regime (\(k(n)\sim \tfrac{n}{\alpha\log n}\) with fixed \(\alpha>0\))
\[
R_{n,k}\sim n^{\alpha-1},
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\begin{cases}
\alpha<1:& R_{n,k}\to 0,\\[4pt]
\alpha=1:& R_{n,k}\to 1,\\[4pt]
\alpha>1:& R_{n,k}\to\infty.
\end{cases}
\]

 5. Subcritical regime (\(k(n)\ll \tfrac{n}{\log n}\), i.e. \(\lambda_n\gg \log n\)). Then
$
R_{n,k}\sim \dfrac{e^{n/k}}{n}\ \longrightarrow\ \infty.
$

---

In summary,
\[
R_{n,k}\asymp \max\!\left\{\frac{e^{n/k}}{n},\,\frac{1}{k}\right\},
\]
with the phase transition occurring at \(k(n)\sim n/\log n\),
where \(R_{n,k}\) crosses from vanishing  to diverging.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \underline{super-linearly many buses:}  $k(n)\gg n$ (so $\lambda_n\to 0$). Then $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\sim n\to\infty$;
  $\displaystyle \frac{\mathrm{Var}^{(n)}(L^n_k)}{E^{(n)}[L^n_k]^2}\sim \frac{\lambda_n}{n}=\frac{1}{k(n)}\to 0$.

\item \underline{Linearly many buses:} $k(n)\sim c\,n$ with $c\in(0,\infty)$. Then $\lambda_n\to 1/c$, so
  $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\sim n e^{-1/c}\to\infty$ and the ratio $\sim \frac{e^{1/c}-1}{n}\to 0$.
  
\item \underline{Slightly above the threshold:}  $k(n)=\dfrac{n}{(1-\varepsilon)\log n}$ with $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$.
Then $\lambda_n=(1-\varepsilon)\log n$, so $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\asymp n^{\varepsilon}\to\infty$ and the ratio $\to 0$.

\item \underline{Slightly below the threshold:}  $k(n)=\dfrac{n}{(\log n + c)}$ with  $c\in\mathbb R$.
Then $\lambda_n=\log n + c$, so $E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\to e^{-c}\in(0,\infty)$ while
$\displaystyle \frac{\mathrm{Var}^{(n)}(L^n_k)}{E^{(n)}[L^n_k]^2}\to e^{c}\ (\neq 0)$; the criterion in Theorem (thm: conc of the paper) fails.
  
\item \underline{Too few buses:}  $k(n)\ll \dfrac{n}{\log n}$ (so $\lambda_n\gg \log n$). Then 
$E^{(n)}[L^n_k]\to 0$ and $\displaystyle \frac{\mathrm{Var}^{(n)}(L^n_k)}{E^{(n)}[L^n_k]^2}\to\infty$; the criterion in Theorem (thm: conc of the paper) fails.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $n/\log n$ threshold

[Lemma lem:product of arXiv:2609.02820, 'Sharpness and critical scaling of parking'] Fix $0\leq\lambda\leq\lambda_1$ and finitely many sites carrying the tilted
	law, and condition on the remaining randomness. Let $F$ and $Z$ be functions
	of the counts, walks, and uniform variables at these sites, each
	invariant under relabeling the particles at a site. Suppose $F$ takes values in $[0,1]$ and
	does not decrease when a particle is added. Suppose $Z$ is nonnegative and
	integrable, does not increase when a particle is added, and changes by at
	most one when a single particle is added or deleted. Then
	\begin{equation}
		|\Cov_\lambda(F,Z)|\leq3\,\partial_\lambda\mathbb{E}_\lambda F\,.
	\end{equation}

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. Let d>=2 and let an equal-weight identity-covariance three-Gaussian teacher have planar means (a,0),(-a/2,3sqrt(3)a/2),(-a/2,-3sqrt(3)a/2), a>0. For an equal-weight identity-covariance mixture-score student with planar means (s,0),(t,v),(t,-v), three reduced population DDPM excess-risk stationary equations imply full unrestricted criticality. For risk F=E||score_student-score_teacher||^2, define planar responsibilities w, posterior mean r, discrepancy h=r-r_teacher and J=[w_j(u_j-r)] over the two-dimensional teacher mixture. The full mean Hessian splits into a planar six-by-six block and d-2 identical perpendicular blocks K=2E[ww^T+J^T J-w h^T J-J^T h w^T]. Reflection decomposes the planar block into even/odd three-by-three blocks and K into a two-by-two block and a scalar. Thus for d>=3 positivity of blocks of sizes 3,3,2,1 is equivalent to positive definiteness of the full Hessian; for d=2 only the planar blocks occur. This is an exact finite-noise certificate reduction for arbitrary finite a,s,t,v, not a root enclosure, stability verdict, bifurcation location, new general symmetry theorem or resolution of Target 2.
d>=2; teacher and student means planar as explicitly specified
equal weights and identity component covariance for teacher and student

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:db304008efaf035d6a786c20db55eb6f0952fedbef4efe02440c187e6c5c25fb","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/db/db304008efaf035d6a786c20db55eb6f0952fedbef4efe02440c187e6c5c25fb.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:dcaefeed7c723b4b285a26af04710d4c81b4dad4c4a6d10d8f5fc62ca1f5597e","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c21","bundle_id":"population.t309-finite-noise-stability-reduction-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_014.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:gaussian-mixture-ddpm-finite-noise-reflection-perpendicular-hessian","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C21 v1; proof (unaudited); Target 2 route 12 auxiliary certificate reduction.

# Exact finite-noise stability blocks for reflection-symmetric planar DDPM students

This supplies an exact reduction for the finite-noise stability step left by C20. It does not certify stability at any new amplitude or locate a bifurcation. No novelty finding or general-target move is asserted. The proof uses differentiated finite-mixture formulas and Gaussian integration, not a high-noise asymptotic expansion.

## 1. Setup and statement

Let d>=2 and fix a plane identified with R^2. The teacher is the equal-weight spherical mixture whose planar means are

    (a,0), (-a/2,3 sqrt(3)a/2), (-a/2,-3 sqrt(3)a/2), a>0,

and whose component covariance is I_d. Embed the student means in that plane, with

    u_0=(s,0), u_+=(t,v), u_-=(t,-v).

The student also has equal weights and covariance I_d. For general planar student means u_j, define

    w_j(y)=exp(y.u_j-||u_j||^2/2)/sum_l exp(y.u_l-||u_l||^2/2),
    r(y)=sum_j w_j u_j, h(y)=r(y)-r_*(y),
    J(y)=[w_0(u_0-r), w_+(u_+-r), w_-(u_--r)].       (1)

Here r_* is the teacher posterior mean and expectation E_y below is under its two-dimensional noisy mixture q_2. The population excess DDPM risk is F=E||score_student-score_teacher||^2, with no factor 1/2. At planar means it equals E_y||h(y)||^2 exactly.

The three equations partial_s F=partial_t F=partial_v F=0 imply full unrestricted mean criticality, including every ambient direction. At such a point the full mean Hessian is the direct sum of a six-dimensional planar block and d-2 identical perpendicular blocks

    K=2 E_y[ww^T+J^T J-w h^T J-J^T h w^T].          (2)

The planar block further splits into two explicit three-dimensional reflection blocks. The perpendicular block splits into a two-dimensional label-symmetric block and a one-dimensional label-antisymmetric block. Thus, for d>=3, positive definiteness of four matrices of sizes 3,3,2,1 is sufficient and necessary for positive definiteness of the full Hessian. For d=2 only the two planar blocks occur. This certifies a nondegenerate strict local minimum when the reduced gradient is zero; it does not characterize degenerate minima.

All expressions are exact two-dimensional expectations for arbitrary finite a,s,t,v. No noncollinearity is needed for the identities. Noncollinearity can be imposed separately when continuing the C06 branch.

## 2. Exact planar derivatives

For any planar direction p=(p_0,p_+,p_-), set

    L_j=(y-u_j).p_j, Lbar=sum_j w_j L_j,
    A_p=sum_j w_j p_j+sum_j w_j(u_j-r)L_j,
    B_p=2 Cov_w(p,L)+Cov_w(u,(L-Lbar)^2-||p||^2).

Cov_w(f,g)=sum_j w_j(f_j-E_w f)(g_j-E_w g), interpreted as a vector when f is vector valued. Direct differentiation of the softmax weights, including the second derivative -||p_j||^2 of each logit, gives

    D_p r=A_p, D_p^2 r=B_p,
    D_p^2 F=2 E_y[||A_p||^2+h.B_p].                 (3)

Polarization supplies the six-by-six planar Hessian. Equivalently the planar gradient for component j is

    grad_{u_j} F=2 E_y w_j[h+(y-u_j)((u_j-r).h)].    (4)

This form computes all reduced derivatives without differentiating a high-dimensional integral. At any fixed finite means, the score difference is bounded by the student and teacher mean norms. Parameter derivatives introduce polynomial factors in y with bounded softmax weights. Local Gaussian-mixture domination therefore justifies differentiation and polarization under the expectation to the finite orders used here.

## 3. The perpendicular Hessian and the essential logit bias

Perturb one perpendicular coordinate by mean components tau z_j, with z=(z_0,z_+,z_-). Let X denote the standard normal observation in that coordinate; it is independent of y under the teacher. At tau=0 define

    mu=w^T z, B=Jz, V=E_w z^2-mu^2.

The logit increments are tau X z_j-tau^2 z_j^2/2. Hence

    w'_j=w_j X(z_j-mu),
    w''_j=w_j[X^2((z_j-mu)^2-V)-(z_j^2-E_w z^2)]. (5)

The planar posterior derivative is X B and the perpendicular posterior derivative is mu. Averaging the planar second derivative over X, using E X^2=1, gives

    E_X r_planar''=-2 mu B.                       (6)

Indeed the average coefficient in (5) is -2 mu w_j(z_j-mu). The teacher has zero perpendicular posterior mean, so no perpendicular second derivative contributes to its inner product with the base score difference. Differentiating the squared error therefore yields

    D_z^2 F=2 E_y[mu^2+||B||^2-2 mu h.B]=z^T K z,

which proves (2).

The negative quadratic norm term in each logit is essential. Dropping it leaves a spurious Cov_w(u,z^2) contribution in (6), and generally changes the Hessian. As a simple consistency check, z=(1,1,1) gives mu=1 and B=0, so z^T K z=2: translating every mean equally in a normal direction changes the risk by exactly tau^2.

For multiple perpendicular coordinates, each first planar derivative contains its own independent standard Gaussian X_i. Cross products average to zero for distinct i, and the mean-norm logit has no mixed second derivative between distinct orthogonal axes. The normal posterior derivatives also occupy orthogonal coordinates. Consequently the perpendicular Hessian is I_{d-2} tensor K. Mixed planar/perpendicular Hessian blocks vanish by oddness in X_i. All perpendicular first derivatives vanish for the same reason.

## 4. Reflection blocks and full criticality

Order planar coordinates as (x_0,y_0,x_+,y_+,x_-,y_-). Reflection of the physical second coordinate together with exchanging labels + and - acts by

    T(x_0,y_0,x_+,y_+,x_-,y_-)
      =(x_0,-y_0,x_-,-y_-,x_+,-y_+).

The teacher and risk are invariant under this orthogonal involution. The proposed student lies in its fixed space. Thus its gradient has no T-odd component. The map (s,t,v) spans the fixed space with full rank, so the three reduced stationary equations force its entire planar gradient to vanish. Section 3 supplies the remaining ambient criticality.

Let e_i be the six standard basis vectors. Orthogonal bases for the T-even and T-odd spaces are

    Q_even=[e_1,(e_3+e_5)/sqrt(2),(e_4-e_6)/sqrt(2)],
    Q_odd =[e_2,(e_3-e_5)/sqrt(2),(e_4+e_6)/sqrt(2)].

At a reflection-fixed point, the planar Hessian H commutes with T, by differentiating the invariance twice. Therefore Q_even^T H Q_odd=0. Its two blocks are H_even=Q_even^T H Q_even and H_odd=Q_odd^T H Q_odd, both of size three. This splitting holds even before imposing stationarity.

On each perpendicular coordinate the same physical reflection leaves the perpendicular axis unchanged and swaps student labels +,-. Consequently K commutes with S(z_0,z_+,z_-)=(z_0,z_-,z_+). With three-dimensional standard basis f_j, set

    P_even=[f_1,(f_2+f_3)/sqrt(2)],
    P_odd=(f_2-f_3)/sqrt(2).

Then K_even=P_even^T K P_even has size two, K_odd=P_odd^T K P_odd is scalar, and the off-block term vanishes. Together with Section 3 this proves the stated fixed-size Hessian test in every ambient dimension.

For underlying locations nu with noisy means M=a nu, gradients and Hessians at fixed a acquire factors a and a^2 respectively. Therefore stationary points and Hessian signs are unchanged by that fixed-a parameter conversion. A changing-noise algorithm still needs C20's explicit learning-rate conversion.

## Scope and next unpaid certificate

This is an exact certificate reduction, not a finite-noise stability verdict. To establish continuation beyond the small-amplitude regime one must connect enclosed zeros of the three reduced equations to the C06 bad branch, for example by overlapping uniqueness boxes, and prove positivity of all applicable blocks over the relevant parameter/noise boxes. A positive excess-risk bound must separately certify nonglobality; enclosing some stationary point could instead locate the teacher's global minimum. Alternatively one may exhibit and certify a loss of positivity on the continued branch. Any computer-assisted implementation must use outward-rounded integration or exact bounds, with Gaussian tails controlled. Floating-point roots or sampled Hessian eigenvalues would be numerical evidence only.

The finite rational script checks (5)--(6), the common-normal-translation value, a wrong-logit-bias control and the reflection eigenspaces. It does not independently certify analytic differentiation, root existence or block positivity. 		|\nabla r|^2+m\langle \phi\nabla^Nr, \mathbf{H}\rangle.

body:
[Corollary cor:geometry of arXiv:2608.28330, 'Realising atomless laws as distance distributions on metric measure spaces'] Let $\Theta$ be an atomless Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R_+$ such
	that $0\in\operatorname{supp}\Theta$.  For every $L>1$, there is a realisation
	$(S,d,\mu)$ of $\Theta$ such that $\operatorname{supp}\mu=S$ and $d$ is
	$L$-bi-Lipschitz equivalent to an ultrametric $u$ on $S$.  In fact,
	\[
	u(x,y)\leq d(x,y)\leq Lu(x,y),
	\qquad x,y\in S.
	\]
	If $\Theta$ has bounded support, then $S$ may be chosen compact and
	homeomorphic to the Cantor space.  In this case,
	\[
	\{d(x,y):x,y\in S\}=\operatorname{supp}\Theta,
	\qquad
	\operatorname{diam} S=\max\operatorname{supp}\Theta.
	\]
	If $\Theta$ has unbounded support, then $S$ may be chosen proper and
	homeomorphic to a countable disjoint union of Cantor spaces.

[Theorem 15 of arXiv:2512.00570, 'Makeenko--Migdal equations for lattice Yang--Mills--Higgs'] Let $G\in \{SO(N),U(N), SU(N)\}$. Fix an edge $e$ and let $s$ be a collection of strings.  The following identity holds 
	\begin{equs}[e15]
		{}&\Big(-2 \,r(s)\,c_\mfg+2\nu \big(r(s)-t(e)^2\big)\Big) \phi(s)
		\\	=
		&\mp\beta \sum_{s' \in \mD^\pm_e(s) } \phi(s')
		\mp\kappa \sum_{s' \in \mB^\pm_e(s) } \phi(s')\mp 2\mu \sum_{s' \in \mT^\pm_e(s) } \phi(s')
		\mp 2\lambda\sum_{s' \in \mS^\pm_e(s) } \phi(s')
		\\

		\mp 2\mu \sum_{s' \in \mM^\pm_{e,\backslash U}(s) } \phi(s')\mp 2\lambda \sum_{s' \in \mX^\pm_{e,U}(s) } \phi(s')
		\mp 2\mu \sum_{s' \in \mX^\pm_{e,\backslash U}(s) } \phi(s') \\

body:
[Definition 12 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $S$ be a set.
    A family $\mathcal{B}\subset \mathcal{P}(S)$ of subsets of $S$ is called a \emph{bornology} on $S$ if it satisfies the following three conditions. 
    \begin{enumerate} 
        \item $\mathcal{B}$ is a cover of $S$ (i.e.~ $\bigcup_{B\in \mathcal{B}}B=S$).
        \item $B_1 ,B_2\in \mathcal{B}$ implies $B_1\cup B_2\in \mathcal{B}$. 
        \item $B\in \mathcal{B}$ and $B'\subset B$ imply $B'\in \mathcal{B}$. 
    \end{enumerate}
    The pair $(S,\mathcal{B})$ is called a \emph{bornological space}.
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2608.25785

[Lem def:yosida of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Consider the notation and assumptions from (general-mild-existence of the paper). For each $n \geq 1$ define
    $$
    R_n \coloneqq n(n - A)^{-1} = \int_0^\infty ne^{-nt}S(t)dt 
    $$
    
    and $F_n \coloneqq R_nF$,  $G_n \coloneqq R_nG$. 
    Then, there is a unique strong solution $x_n(t)$ (called Yosida approximations of (equation eq:gefx of the paper))
    of the problem
    \begin{equation}
    dx_n(t) = [Ax_n(t) + F_n(x_n(t))]dt + G_n(x_n(t))dW_t \,, \quad x_n(0) = R_n x_0 \,.
    \end{equation}
    Furthermore, $(x_n)_{n \geq 1}$ converge as $n \to \infty$ to the mild solution $x$
    of (equation eq:gefx of the paper) in $L^p(\Omega; C([0,T];B))$ for all $p,T > 0$.

body:
[Lemm 10 of arXiv:2608.30357, 'Mean convergence for Banach space-valued random elements indexed in measure spaces'] Let $X, Y$ be $\cX$-valued random elements.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item If $X$ and $Y$ are independent, then they are diagonally negatively dependent.

\item $X, Y$ are diagonally negatively dependent if and only if $Y, X$ are. Moreover, \eqref{def:PDND} holds for a set $A \in \cB(\cX)$ if and only if it holds for $A^c$.

\item Let $(\cY, \|\cdot\|_\cY)$ be a separable Banach space and let $f \colon \cX \to \cY$ be $\cB(\cX)/\cB(\cY)$-measurable. If $X, Y$ are diagonally negatively dependent, then so are $f(X), f(Y)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemm 10 of arXiv:2608.30357

body:
[Theorem 16 (Riemannian stopping criterion) of arXiv:2609.00571, '\textbf{Shape Optimization and Bernoulli Free Boundary Problems\\ for the Riemannian $p$-L'] Assume the compactness, state-stability and boundary-flux stability
hypotheses, together with (RC), (SC), and (RA). Suppose that the
successive construction produces
\[
c_0>c_1>c_2>\cdots>c
\]
and
\[
c_j\downarrow\ell.
\]
Let $(R_N)$ satisfy
\[
q(R_N)>c,
\qquad
q(R_N)\longrightarrow c.
\]
Assume, in addition, that for every sufficiently large $N$ the
first-crossing index
\[
k_N=\min\{j\geq0:c_j\leq q(R_N)\}
\]
exists. Then
\[
q(R_N)-c_{k_N}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
c_{k_N}\longrightarrow c,
\]
and consequently
\[
\boxed{\ell=c.}
\]
The limiting pair $(\Omega^\ast,u_{\Omega^\ast})$ therefore satisfies
\[
\begin{cases}
-\Delta_{p,g}u_{\Omega^\ast}=0
&\text{in }\Omega^\ast\setminus K,\\
u_{\Omega^\ast}=1

Let d>=3 be an integer and rho in (0,1/2). Define h(x)=-x log x for x>0 and h(0)=0, using natural logarithms. For beta in [0,rho] put Gamma(beta)=sqrt((1/2-rho)^2+(rho-beta)^2)-(1/2-rho) and define F(beta,gamma)=(d/2)[2h(beta)+2h(gamma)+4h(rho-beta-gamma)+h(1-4rho+2beta+2gamma)]-(d-1)[h(beta)+2h(rho-beta)+h(1-2rho+beta)], then f(beta)=F(beta,Gamma(beta)). These entropy arguments are nonnegative at Gamma, with the continuous h(0) convention at endpoints. Suppose f(beta)<=f(rho^2) for every beta in [0,rho]. For uniform simple labelled d-regular graphs G_{n,d}, dn even and n tending to infinity, alpha(G_{n,d})/n is at least rho-o(1) with probability 1-o(1), and the limiting independence ratio alpha_d is at least rho (Gerencser-Harangi arXiv:2510.12600v3, Theorem 1.1 p.2, equations (18)-(21) p.12). Under the same condition the Markovian independent-set process of density rho on the infinite d-regular tree is typical (Theorem 4.3 p.13). This process has vertex P(1)=rho, transitions P(1|1)=0 and P(1|0)=rho/(1-rho), and subtrees are independent conditional on a vertex label. Typical means that for every fixed radius R and every epsilon>0, for all sufficiently large valid n, with probability at least 1-epsilon the graph admits a {0,1} labeling whose empirical radius-R rooted-neighborhood law differs from that process law by less than epsilon in total variation (Definition 3.2 p.9); the approximating labeling need not be exactly independent before removing bad edges. A global maximum at beta=rho^2 is required, not just a negative second derivative there. The paper already computes fprime(rho^2)=0 and fsecond(rho^2)=((d-2)rho^2+2rho-1)/(rho^2(1-rho)^2(1-2rho+2rho^2)) in Claim 8.1 p.21. Therefore the unaugmented criterion necessarily has rho<=1/(1+sqrt(d-1)); for d=3 this cap is sqrt(2)-1, below .4361. This necessary local-stability condition is not sufficient for the global maximum condition, and it is not an upper bound on the graph independence ratio. The paper's later augmentation is a distinct step and is not ruled out by this cap. Every printed numerical lower bound still needs a rigorous evaluation of the full global inequality before being reused as an exact worker bound.
d integer at least 3; rho strictly between 0 and 1/2
Full global overlap inequality f(beta)<=f(rho^2) for all beta in [0,rho]
Uniform simple labelled random d-regular graph, dn even, n tends to infinity
Typical-process conclusion concerns fixed-radius empirical local statistics

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2512.08745, 'Variance strikes back: sub-game--perfect Nash equilibria in time‑inconsistent $N$‑player g'] Let {\rm\Cref{assumpDPP_NplayerGame}} and {\rm\Cref{assumption:regularityForNecessity}} hold, and let $\hat\balpha^N \in \mathcal{N}\!\mathcal{A}_{s,N}$ be a sub-game--perfect Nash equilibrium. Then, one can construct a tuple 
\[
(\Y^N,\Z^N,\M^{\star,N},\N^{\star,N},\Z^{m,\star,N},\Z^{n,\star,N}) \coloneqq (Y^{i,N}, \Z^{i,N}, M^{i,\star,N}, N^{i,\star,N}, \Z^{i,m,\star,N},\Z^{i,n,\star,N})_{i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}},
\]
that satisfies the system \eqref{BSDE_NplayerGame} and, for some $p \geq 1$, the integrability condition
\begin{align*}
&\sup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}}} \Bigg[ \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \big|Y^{i,N}_t\big|^p + \bigg(\int_0^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \big\|{Z}_t^{i,\ell,N}\big\|^2 \d t\bigg)^\frac{p}{2} \Bigg] \\
&+\esssup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \Bigg\{\sup_{t \in [0,T]} \Big\{ \big| M^{i,\star,N}_t\big| + \big| N^{i,\star,N}_t \big| \Big\} + \sup_{\tau \in \cT_{0,T}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{N}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{\tau}}_{\smalltext{\cdot}}} \Bigg[ \int_\tau^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \Big( \big\|Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 + \big\|Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 \Big) \d t \Bigg] \Bigg\} < +\infty.
\end{align*}
It holds that $V^{i,N}_t = Y^{i,N}_t$, $\P\text{\rm--a.s.}$, for every $t \in [0,T]$. Moreover,
\begin{align}
\hat\balpha^N_t \in \cO_{N}\big(t, \X^N_{\cdot \land t}, \Z^N_t, \M^{\star,N}_t, \N^{\star,N}_t, \Z^{m,\star,N}_t, \Z^{n,\star,N}_t\big), \; \text{\rm for}\; \d t \otimes \d \P\text{\rm--a.e.} \; (t,\omega) \in [0,T] \times \Omega.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor stabilization-exists of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let ${\mathcal R}\subset\smash{\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T,*}}$ small. Then $\smash{\CAT_T^{S\textup{-cc},\textup{${\mathcal R}$-ex}}}\hookrightarrow\CAT_T^\textup{$S$-cc}$ admits a left adjoint restricting to $\textup{Pr}^S_T\to\textup{Pr}^{S,\textup{${\mathcal R}$-ex}}_T$, and both of these adjunctions are smashing localizations. In particular, there exists for any pointed $S$-presentable ${\mathcal{C}}$ an \emph{$\bm{\mathcal R}$-stabilization}, i.e.\ an $S$-cocontinuous $\Sigma^\infty\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to\ul\Sp^{\mathcal R}_{S\triangleright T}({\mathcal{C}})$ to an $S$-presentable ${\mathcal R}$-stable $T$-$\infty$-category, such that for any $S$-cocomplete ${\mathcal R}$-stable ${\mathcal{D}}$
    \[
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}(\Sigma^\infty,{\mathcal{D}})\colon\ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}(\ul\Sp^{\mathcal R}_{S\triangleright T}({\mathcal{C}}),{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}).
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        Note that if $X,Y\in{\mathcal R}(A)$ act invertibly, then so does $X\otimes Y$. We may therefore assume that ${\mathcal R}$ is a symmetric monoidal subcategory, and the first claim follows by applying Theorem~(thm:sym-mon-localization-for-modes of the paper) to $\core{\mathcal R}\hookrightarrow\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T,*}$. The second claim is then an instance of Lemma~(lemma:smash-module-internal-hom of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let U ⊂ C be open and let f_n be holomorphic on U with f_n → f uniformly on every compact subset of U. Then f is holomorphic on U, and for every k ≥ 1 the derivatives f_n^(k) converge to f^(k) uniformly on every compact subset of U. Quantitatively, if the closed disk of radius 2r about a lies in U and g is holomorphic on U, then sup over |z - a| ≤ r of |g^(k)(z)| ≤ k! r^{-k} sup over |z - a| ≤ 2r of |g(z)|. The same holds for series: a series of holomorphic functions converging locally uniformly may be differentiated term by term any number of times. The convergence of derivatives is locally uniform, not uniform on all of U.

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] For every $z$ with $\Re z>0$, the form $\mathfrak h_z$ is
densely defined, closed, and sectorial on the common domain $\mathcal D$.
Its associated operator, denoted by $H_z$, is the weak realization of
\[
       -\frac12\Delta+zQ.
\]
More precisely,
\[
 \mathcal D(H_z)
 =\left\{f\in\mathcal D:
 -\frac12\Delta f+zQf\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)
 \text{ in the sense of distributions}\right\}.
\]
Furthermore,  $H_z $ has compact resolvent and $H_z^*=H_{\overline z}$.

[Lemma lem:1* of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $q\in (0,1/5)$ and $\Phi\in (0,1/10)$. 
   Then for all $b \in (0,1)$ sufficiently small (depending only on $q,\Phi$), the following is true. For all $z\in \mathbb{C},r>0$, there exist deterministic (depending only on $z,r,q,\Phi,b$) points $u_+,u_-,v_+,v_-$ satisfying $u_+,u_-\in B_{\Phi r}(z-r)$ and $v_+,v_-\in B_{\Phi  r}(z+r)$ such that the balls of Euclidean radius $2br$ around $u_+,u_-,v_+,v_-,u,v$ are all pairwise disjoint and the intersection of the following events, which we call $G_r(z)$, occurs with probability at least $q$.
   \begin{enumerate}
   \item  $\mathscr{X}_{u_-,v_-}^{u_+,v_+}$
   \item  $\Gamma_{u_+,u}\cup \Gamma_{u_-,u}\subseteq B_{\Phi r}(z-r)$ and $\Gamma_{v,v_+}\cup \Gamma_{v,v_-}\subseteq B_{\Phi r}(z+r)$.
   \item  $\mathrm{dist}(\Gamma_{u,v_+}\cup \Gamma_{u,v_-}, \{u_+,u_-\})\geq 2br$ and $\mathrm{dist}(\Gamma_{u_+,v}\cup \Gamma_{u_-,v}, \{v_+,v_-\})\geq 2br$

   \item $\mathrm{dist}(\Gamma_{u_-,u}\cup \Gamma_{u_+,u}, \Gamma_{v,v_-}\cup \Gamma_{v,v_+})\geq 2br$
   \end{enumerate}
   Further, the points $u_+,u_-,v_+,v_-$ can be chosen such that the family of events $\{G_r(z)\}_{z\in \mathbb{C}, r>0}$ is translation and scale invariant.

body:
Let (S,g) be a compact, oriented, boundaryless smooth Riemannian 2-manifold (surface) with Gaussian curvature K. Then the integral of K over S with respect to the Riemannian area element dA equals 2*pi times the Euler characteristic of S: integral_S K dA = 2 pi chi(S). More generally, if S has piecewise smooth boundary, integral_S K dA + integral_{boundary S} k_g ds + sum of exterior angles at corners = 2 pi chi(S), where k_g is the geodesic curvature of the boundary.
S is compact, oriented, and without boundary
g is a smooth Riemannian metric on S

The local Gauss-Bonnet formula for a single geodesic triangle T with interior angles alpha, beta, gamma states integral_T K dA = alpha+beta+gamma-pi (this local identity is itself proved via the structure equations of an orthonormal frame, essentially an application of Stokes' theorem to the curvature 2-form and the connection 1-form). Summing this identity over all F triangles: the left side sums to integral_S K dA, since the triangles partition S; on the right side, summing all interior angles of all triangles gives 2 pi V (the angles surrounding each of the V vertices sum to 2 pi), and summing the F copies of -pi gives -pi F. Hence integral_S K dA = 2 pi V - pi F. Using the triangulation identity 3F=2E, direct algebra confirms 2 pi V - pi F = 2 pi (V-E+F): the difference 2pi(V-E+F) - (2piV-piF) equals -2piE+3piF = pi(3F-2E) = 0. Therefore integral_S K dA = 2 pi (V-E+F) = 2 pi chi(S).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:c1fd189475f9669f6e1d375b115cb02df9ccf19cb173abf439ef25d92982d191","revision_digest":"sha256:69d98e8d3f6054f1867f5fab74d6eacb6d1226b8aae7d5dd37f5c562805f10ef","source_id":"wikipedia:Gauss-Bonnet theorem","source_revision":"as-read-2026-08-02","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition 11 (Compatibility conditions) of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Fix $k\geq1$. Assume $ u_0\in H^{k+1}(\Omega)$, $v_0\in H^k(\Omega)$, 
and
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^\ell u_-
\in
C_{\mathrm b}\bigl((-\infty,0];
H^{k+1-\ell}(\Omega)\bigr),
\qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k.
\end{equation}
Assume also that
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^\ell f
\in
C\bigl([0,T];H^{k-\ell}(\Omega)\bigr),
\qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\partial_t^k f\in C([0,T];L^2(\Omega))$. 

We say that $(u_0,v_0,u_-,f)$ satisfies the compatibility conditions of
order $k$ if the following two conditions hold.

(i) The forward jets agree with the corresponding prehistory jets:
\begin{equation}
\partial_t^j u_-(0-,\cdot)=U_j
\quad\text{in }H^{k+1-j}(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\end{equation}

(ii) The forward jets satisfy the Dirichlet boundary condition:
\begin{equation}
U_j\in H^{k+1-j}(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\end{equation}
 
For $0\leq j\leq k$, define the concrete differentiated initial history
by
\begin{equation}
\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}(s,\cdot)
:=
U_j-\partial_t^j u_-(-s,\cdot),
\qquad s\geq0.
\end{equation}
Then \eqref{eq:corner-compatibility} is equivalently
\[
\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}(0,\cdot)=0
\quad\text{in }H^{k+1-j}(\Omega),
\qquad 0\leq j\leq k.
\]
Here $\widehat\eta_j^{\,0}$ denotes the concrete history function. If
$\eta_j^0\in\mathcal M$ denotes the corresponding abstract history
element, no pointwise value $\eta_j^0(0)$ is being asserted.
title: Compatibility conditions

body: [Defn def-ring of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] For $p \geq 1$ and $q\geq 0$, a \textbf{ring} with inner perimeter $p$ and outer perimeter $q$ is a planar map $R$ with two distinguished faces: an outer face of perimeter $2p$ and and an inner face of perimeter $2q$, with the following properties. The two distinguished faces do not share any vertices, and every face of $R$ other than the two distinguished faces is a quadrilateral which shares a vertex with each of the inner face and the outer face.

[Theorem 19 (Linearity \citep{malinovskii2025higgs}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] To leading order in the per-layer quantization perturbations (the first-order
term vanishing at the trained optimum), the increase in the
model's perplexity decomposes as a sum of per-layer
contributions, each a layer-specific constant times that layer's relative
squared weight error $\|\Delta W_l\|_F^2/\|W_l\|_F^2$. Minimizing each per-layer
error is therefore aligned, in the small-perturbation regime, with minimizing
end-to-end degradation.

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2608.20252, '2608.20252'] A set $A$ belonging to $C([0,T], \Omega)$ or $\mathcal{D}([0,T],\Omega)$ is compact exactly when
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] $\{\pi_t: \pi\in A\}$ is relatively compact in $\Omega$ for each $t\in[0,T]$.
\item[(b)] $\lim_{\gamma\downarrow 0} \sup_{\pi\in A} \bar{w}_\pi(\gamma)  =  0$
where $\bar{w}_\pi = w_\pi$ on $C([0,T], \Omega)$ and $\bar{w}_\pi = w'_\pi$ on $\mathcal{D}([0,T], \Omega)$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 8 of arXiv:2608.20252

[Proposition 34 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Suppose $\cX$ is a Banach space, $\cU \subseteq \cX$ is an open set, and $-\infty < a < T < \infty$.
If $f \colon [a,\infty) \times \cU \to \cX$ is locally Lipschitz in space, locally uniformly in time; $c_1,c_2 \in C([a,T];\cX)$; and $y_1,y_2 \in C([a,T];\cU)$ satisfy
\[
y_i(t) = c_i(t) + \int_a^t f(s,y_i(s))\,\d s \qquad (a \leq t \leq T, \; i=1,2),
\]
then
\[
\norm{y_1(t) - y_2(t)}_{\cX} \leq  e^{C(t-a)}\sup_{a \leq s \leq t}\norm{c_1(s) - c_2(s)}_{\cX} \qquad (a \leq t \leq T),
\]
where $C = c_{J,K}$ is as in \eqref{eq.locLip} with $J \coloneqq [a,T]$ and $K \coloneqq y_1([a,T]) \cup y_2([a,T])$.
In particular, if $c_1 \equiv c_2$, then $y_1 \equiv y_2$.
title: Proposition 34 of arXiv:2604.03213

body:
Let S be a smooth surface in R^3 with its induced Riemannian metric (first fundamental form), and let K denote its Gaussian curvature (the product of the two principal curvatures). Then K at each point is an intrinsic invariant: it can be computed entirely from the first fundamental form and its derivatives, without reference to how S is embedded in R^3. Consequently, if f: S -> S' is a local isometry between two surfaces in R^3 (a diffeomorphism preserving the induced metric), then K_S(p) = K_{S'}(f(p)) for every p in S.
S is a smooth surface immersed in Euclidean R^3
f is a diffeomorphism between surfaces preserving the induced first fundamental form

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $\Phi$ be an ID valuation with the L\'evy measure $\Lambda$, and
  let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ and $b_1,\dots,b_m$ be real numbers and
  $K_1,\dots,K_n$ and $L_1,\dots,L_m$ be compact convex sets. Then the
  finite sums $\sum a_i\Phi(K_i)$ and $\sum b_j\Phi(L_j)$ are
  independent if and only if the $\Lambda$-outer measure vanishes on the
  complement of the set of valuations $\psi$ such that $\sum a_i\psi(K_i)=0$ or
  $\sum b_j\psi(L_j)=0$.

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] There exists a sequence of random $\mathfrak{g}$-valued $1$-forms $(A_N)_{N\geqslant 0}$ on $\mathcal{S}$ such that the following properties hold, where $(\Lambda_N)_{N\geqslant 0}$ is the sequence of Morse lattices from Section~(s:Morselattice of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each $N$, let $(g_e)_{e \in \mathbb{E}_N}$ be a discrete connection on $\Lambda_N$ with law $\mathrm{DS}(\rho,\Lambda_N)$. 
Then the family of loop holonomies of $A_N$ has the same law as the family of loop holonomies of $(g_e)_{e \in \mathbb{E}_N}$, in the sense that
\[
\big(\mathrm{Hol}(A_N,c)\big)_{c \in \mathrm{Loop}_o(\Lambda_N)}
\;\stackrel{\mathrm{law}}{=}\;
\big(\mathrm{Hol}\big((g_e)_{e\in\mathbb{E}_N},c\big)\big)_{c \in \mathrm{Loop}_o(\Lambda_N)}.
\]
\item There exists a random distributional $1$-form $A$ on $\mathcal{S}$ such that
\[
A_N \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{\;\mathrm{law}\;} A
\]
in $\mathcal{D}^{'^2}(\mathcal{S},\mathfrak{g})$, where the test $1$-forms are taken to vanish to all orders on the boundary of $\mathcal{S}$. 
Moreover, the limit $A$ coincides with the random $1$-form constructed in the first part of the article.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary Cor:distance1 of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] Let $1\leq d\leq n/2$ and $1\leq k<n$. Denote $p=d/n$ and assume 
$p(1-p)(n-k)\geq 1$.  Let $V \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a (fixed) subspace 
of dimension $k$ and  $u\in \mathbb{C}^n$ be a (fixed) vector. 

Let $\delta$ be a random vector drawn uniformly from the set of all vectors in $\{0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ ones  and denote the distance from $\delta + u$ to $V$ by $r$. 
Let $E(p)=E(d/n)$ 

be the parameter from Theorem~~(thm:distance of the paper) 
(note that to define it we need to deal with a Bernoulli random vector). 
Then for any $t>0$ we have
\[
 \mathbb{P}_{\delta}\left(\left|r- E(p) \right|\geq t\right) \leq

C\sqrt{d}\, e^{-ct^2},
\]
where $C, c$ are positive absolute constants.

TECHNIQUE CARD. For a non-negative variable, couple it with a variable having the size-biased law; when the two are close, Stein's method gives normal and Poisson approximations and concentration bounds. Ross, Definition 3.7: for X ≥ 0 with E[X] = μ < ∞, X^s has the size-bias distribution with respect to X if E[Xf(X)] = μE[f(X^s)] for all f with E|Xf(X)| < ∞; by Proposition 3.11, dF^s(x) = (x/μ) dF(x). Theorem 3.13: if moreover Var(X) = σ², X^s is defined on the same space as X, W = (X − μ)/σ and Z ~ N(0,1), then d_W(W, Z) ≤ (μ/σ²) √(2/π) √(Var(E[X^s − X | X])) + (μ/σ³) E[(X^s − X)²]. Theorem 4.10: if W ≥ 0 is integer valued with E[W] = λ > 0, W^s is a size-bias coupling of W and Z ~ Po(λ), then d_TV(W, Z) ≤ min{1, λ} E|W + 1 − W^s|. Theorem 7.6: if X ≥ 0 with E[X] = μ and 0 < Var(X) = σ² < ∞, and X^s is a size-biased coupling of X with |X − X^s| ≤ C < ∞, then (1) if X^s ≥ X, P((X − μ)/σ ≤ −t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2Cμ/σ²)); (2) if E[e^{θX}] < ∞ for θ = 2/C, then P((X − μ)/σ ≥ t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2(Cμ/σ² + Ct/(2σ)))).

[Proposition 5 (Universality of GMC) of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Fix a compact interval $\cI$ and $f\in\mathbf{M}$ satisfying \eqref{eq:TwistCondition}.
     In both the critical and subcritical phases, in the space $\mathcal{M}(\cI)$ of Radon measures on $\cI$ equipped with the topology of weak convergence,  the sequence of measures $\mu_{N,\ep}^{\text{GMC}}$ converges in probability as $\min(N,1/\varepsilon)\to\infty$ to a non-trivial, non-atomic measure $\mu_{\infty}^{\text{GMC}}$.
    In the subcritical phase $\theta\in(0,1)$, $\mu_{N,\varepsilon}^{\text{GMC}}(\cI)$ converges in $L^r$ as $\min(N,1/\varepsilon)\to\infty$ to $\mu_{\infty}^{\text{GMC}}(\cI)$ for all $r\in[1,\frac1\theta)$.
title: Universality of GMC

[Pro LebesgueCharacteristic of arXiv:2411.13465, 'Height-offset variables and pinning at infinity for gradient Gibbs measures on trees'] Let $\nu$ either denote the free measure or a GGM of height-period $2$ associated with any fuzzy chain $\bar{\mu}$ and let  $\varphi_\infty^\nu$ denote the respective characteristic function of $H^{\rho,0}$. Then the following is true:
\begin{enumerate}[a)]
    \item There is a constant $0< c<\infty$ such that 
\[ \vert \varphi^\nu_\infty(t) \vert \leq \exp\left(-c \vert t \vert \right) \text{ for all } t \in \mathbb{R}. \]
\item By reverse Fourier-transform, $H^{\rho,0}$ thus has a Lebesgue density $f_{H^{\rho,0}}$ which is infinitely often differentiable.
\end{enumerate}
title: Exponential bound on limiting characteristic function

[Cor 6 of arXiv:2606.13459, 'Symmetric Cooperative Motion in Higher Dimensions'] When $A(u) = u^{m+1}$, the associated operator $\scheme=\scheme[A]$ satisfies
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item The scheme $\mathcal{S}[A]$ is monotone on $\mathcal{B}^{+}_{\sfrac{1}{2}}(\Z^{d})$.
		\item For all $q \in L^1(\Z^{d}) \cap \mathcal{B}^{+}_{\sfrac{1}{2}}(\Z^{d})$, $\sum_\x \scheme q(\x) = \sum_\x q(\x)$,

[Prop sparsestack-double-overlap of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $\zeta_k\ge2$ be an integer sequence such that $k$ is
an integer multiple of $\zeta_k$, set
$b(k):=k/\zeta_k$, and let $n_k$ satisfy $n_k/k\to\infty$.
Further, assume that $\zeta_k^4/k\to 0$, and
let $a_k$ be any sequence such that
\[
\varepsilon_k:=a_k\frac{\zeta_k^4}{k}\to0;\quad a_k\to\infty.
\]
Let $S^{(k)}\in\mathbb R^{n_k\times k}$ be a SparseStack matrix with row
sparsity $\zeta_k$ and block size $b(k)$, and define
$M^{(k)}:=(S^{(k)})^\top\in\mathbb R^{k\times n_k}$.
Then the matrix $M^{(k)}$ has
column sparsity $\zeta_k$ and, with probability $1-o(1)$, satisfies
the \hyperref[ass:local-sparse-double-overlap]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{local sparse double-overlap condition}}}{} with parameter $\varepsilon_k$.

body: [Corollary 35 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Assume that $\b(v)=\frac12P|R^*(v)|$ for all $v\in V$. Then $\b_{\max}\alpha\leq\frac1{\ell}R_{\max}^{(a)}$, and therefore $$M=\max\{F_{\max},R_{\max}^{(a)},R_{\max}^{(b)},(R_{\max}^{(c)})^2,1\}.$$ Assume that $\alpha\to\infty$, with $\ell$ fixed and $M=O(\alpha^{\sfrac12}/(\log\alpha)^2)$. For any FMIS $S$ of $G$, we have $$\mathscr{P}(S)=\overline{\mathscr{P}}:=\exp\left(P|F|+\tfrac12P^2\sum_{v\in V}|R^*(v)|\right)\prod_{t=1}^{\alpha}\frac{t}{n_t},$$ such that $\mathbb{P}(\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}=S\,|\,|\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}|=\alpha)$ is asymptotically uniform. Hence, the total number of FMISs of $G$ is $(1+O(\mathscr{E}(\alpha,M)))\overline{\mathscr{P}}^{-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2609.03195, 'Lecture hall polytopes and\\Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths'] The image under $\phi$ of the set of standard monomials of $\mcA(b)$ is a basis of $A(b)$ as a vector space. For each non-standard monomial $x_{\pi_1}\cdots x_{\pi_k}$ of $\mcA(b)$ there exists a relation, called \emph{straightening relation}, of the form
    \[
    x_{\pi_1}\cdots x_{\pi_k} - x_{\eta_1}\cdots x_{\eta_k}\,\,\in\,\,\mcI
    \]
    where $\eta_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus \eta_k$ is the canonical decomposition of the L-S path $\pi_1 + \cdots + \pi_k$; in particular $x_{\eta_1}\cdots x_{\eta_k}$ is a standard monomial. Moreover the quadratic straightening relations generate the ideal $\mcI$.

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let $V \subset [0,\infty)^n$ be closed. $\partial_{SW} V$ satisfies the following. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\forall x \in V, \ \exists x' \in \partial_{SW}V$ such that $x' \leq' x$. 
\item $\partial_{SW}V \subset \partial V$ 
\item $\partial_{SW}V$ is Borel measurable
\end{enumerate}

Let n>=1 data (x_i,y_i) in R^d times {-1,+1} satisfy ||x_i||_2<=1. Assume a unit vector w_star and a fixed gamma>0 satisfy y_i <x_i,w_star> >= gamma for every i. Define ell(q)=log(1+exp(-q)), L(w)=(1/n)sum_i ell(y_i<x_i,w>), and full-batch GD w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k) with constant eta>0. For all w, the Hessian of log L(w) is bounded above by the identity matrix. In fact its eigenvalues lie in [-1,1]. Along the GD step, log L(w_{k+1})<=log L(w_k)-eta(1/L(w_k)-eta/2)||grad L(w_k)||_2^2. Consequently, if an iterate s satisfies L(w_s)<=2/eta, then L(w_k) is non-increasing for every k>=s and remains <=2/eta. Zero initialization is not needed for this lemma. The local log-risk calculation only uses the bounded-feature part of the source data hypotheses.
Finite nonempty binary-labeled data with Euclidean feature norms <=1
Unit separating vector w_star and margin gamma>0
Averaged logistic risk and full-batch constant-step gradient descent
Some nonnegative integer s satisfies L(w_s)<=2/eta

[Lemma L:51 of arXiv:2606.23865, 'Uniform-in-time Gaussian fluctuations for multiscale nonlinear stochastic systems via Mall'] Let the process  $Z$ be defined in equation (equation E:Z-process of the paper) above. Then, for any $t \ge r_1 \vee r_2,$ and the process $Q \in L^{2p}(\Omega)$, there exists a time-independent positive constant $K$ such that 
$$\frac{1}{\eta^p} \mathbb{E} \left[ \left| \int_{r_1 \vee r_2}^t Z_{t,s} Q_s \thinspace dW_s^2 \right|^{2p} \right] \le \frac{K}{\eta}  \int_{r_1 \vee r_2}^t e^{- \frac{2p \lambda}{\eta}(t-s)} \mathbb{E} (|Q_s|^{2p}) \thinspace ds. $$

[Lem compare Derivative-general of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $K,L\subseteq\mathbb{C}$
    be disjoint compact subsets. Then there exists a constant
    $C>0$ (depending only on $K$ and $L$) such that for any differentiable
    map $F:K\to K$ and 
    \[
    G=\phi_{w'}\circ F\circ\phi_{w}^{-1}:\phi_{w}(K)\to\phi_{w'}(K)
    \]
    where $\phi_{w}(z)=\frac{1}{z-w}$ with $w,w'\in L$, we have 
    \[
    \frac{1}{C}\norm{F'}_K<\norm{G'}_{\phi_w(K)}<C\norm{F'}_K.
    \]

body:
[Proposition prop:rep of MAP of arXiv:2512.21159, '\textsc{From multitype branching Brownian motions\\ to branching Markov additive processes'] Let $(\chi(t), \Theta(t))_{t\ge0}$ be a MAP. Let $0=T_0<T_1<\dots$ be successive jump times of $\Theta$. For each $i,j\in \mathcal{I}$, there exist an i.i.d.\ sequence of random variables $(U_{ij}^{n}, n\ge 1)$, and an i.i.d.\ sequence of L\'{e}vy processes $(\chi_i^{n},n\ge 1)$, such that  these $\Theta,\chi_i^n, U_{ij}^n$ are independent, and that for $n\ge 0$, $t\in [T_n,T_{n+1}),$
    \[\chi(t) = \mathbbm{1}_{\left\{ n>0 \right\} } \left(\chi(T_n-)+U_{ij}^{n}+\chi_j^{n}(t-T_n)\right),
    \]
    where $i=\Theta(T_n-)$ and $j = \Theta(T_n)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.06392, '2608.06392'] Let the assumptions of {\hyperref[AISRLem-critical1]{Lemma~\ref{AISRLem-critical1}}} hold,
    and let ${\mathcal{S}_\mu}$ denote the Stone constant. Then the renewal correction term
\[
    \Delta_R(t):=(Q_F\ast{U})(t)-\frac{1}{\,\mu\,}\int_{[0,t]}Q_F(u)\,du
\]
    is asymptotically equivalent to the equilibrium tail $Q_F$, and
\begin{equation}
    \Delta_R(t)\sim \frac{2{\mathcal{S}_\mu}}{\mu}\,\frac{L(t)}{t}  \qquad \text{as} \quad t\to\infty.
\end{equation}

Lemma~\ref{lem:anti-dissipative-generator-jacobian}, write
\[
\widetilde\tau_D:=\inf\left\{t\ge0:\widetilde Z_t\in D\right\},
\qquad
\widetilde\E_z[\cdot]:=\E\left[\,\cdot\mid\widetilde Z_0=z\right].
\]
With
\[
\widetilde\zeta_\eps^m=\widetilde\tau_{\partial W_m}\wedge\widetilde\tau_{A_\eps},
\qquad
\widetilde\zeta_\eps^s=\widetilde\tau_{\partial W_s}\wedge\widetilde\tau_{S_\eps},
\]
for $z\in W_m$,
\[
1-h_\eps(z)\le
e^{(H(z)-U(\sigma))/\eps}
\widetilde\E_{\Theta_*z}\left[e^{\gamma d\,\widetilde\zeta_\eps^m}\right],
\]
and for $z\in W_s$,
\[
h_\eps(z)\le
e^{(H(z)-U(\sigma))/\eps}
\widetilde\E_{\Theta_*z}\left[e^{\gamma d\,\widetilde\zeta_\eps^s}\right].
\]

body: In mathematics, an action of a group $G$ on a set $S$ is, loosely speaking, an operation that takes an element of $G$ and an element of $S$ and produces another element of $S.$ More formally, it is a group homomorphism from $G$ to the automorphism group of $S$ (the set of all bijections on $S$ along with group operation being function composition). One says that $G$ acts on $S.$

[Lemma large_deviation_Bern of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $\xi_1, ..., \xi_n$ be a sequence of i.i.d. $\Bern(p)$ random variable with $p \in (0, 1)$. Let $S_n := \sum_{i = 1}^n \xi_i$, then we have
\begin{align}
    &\text{ for } \forall \delta > 0, \hspace{2mm} \mathbf{P}\left(\frac{S_n}{n} \ge p(1 + \delta)\right) \le \exp\left(- \frac{np\delta \log(1+\delta)}{4}\right), \\
    &\text{ for } \forall \delta \in (0, 1), \hspace{2mm} \mathbf{P}\left(\frac{S_n}{n} \le p(1 - \delta)\right) \le \exp\left(- \frac{np\delta^2}{4}\right),  \\
    &\text{ for } \forall \delta > 0 \text{ and } k \in \mathbb N, \hspace{2mm} \mathbf{P}\left(\sup_{n \ge k} \frac{S_n}{n} \ge p(1 + \delta)\right) \le \frac{\exp\left(- \frac{kp\delta \log(1 + \delta)}{4}\right)}{1 - \exp\left(- \frac{p\delta \log(1 + \delta)}{4}\right)}  \\
    &\text{ for } \forall \delta \in (0, 1) \text{ and } k \in \mathbb N, \hspace{2mm} \mathbf{P}\left(\inf_{n \ge k} \frac{S_n}{n} \le p(1 - \delta)\right) \le 8 \delta^{-2} \exp\left(- \frac{kp\delta^2}{4}\right) 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ be a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold and let $\delta$ be a simple closed geodesic in $M$. Then $\delta$ lifts to a set of hyperbolic lines $\{\delta_i\}$ in $\mathbb H^3$. For each $i \ne j$, define the \textit{orthocurve} $s_{ij}$ to be the shortest hyperbolic line segment in $\mathbb H^3$ between $\delta_i$ and $\delta_j$. Define the \textit{midplane} $D_{ij}$ to be the hyperbolic plane in $\mathbb H^3$ which meets $s_{ij}$ orthogonally at its midpoint.

By considering the completion $\overline{\mathbb H^3}$ and corresponding boundary $\partial \mathbb H^3$ ($\cong S^2$), we have a curve $\lambda_{ij} = \partial D_{ij}$ which separates the pair of points $\partial \delta_i$ from the pair of points $\partial \delta_j$.
The set of simple closed curves $\{ \lambda_{ij} \mid i \ne j\}$ in $\partial \mathbb H^3$ is known as the \textit{Dirichlet insulator family} associated to the geodesic $\delta$.

We say that a Dirichlet insulator family $\{\lambda_{ij} \mid i \ne j\}$ is \textit{non-coalescable} if there does not exist $i, j_1,j_2,j_3$ such that $\lambda_{ij_1} \cup \lambda_{ij_2} \cup \lambda_{ij_3}$ separates the two points $\partial \delta_i$. See (fig:DIT of the paper) for an example where this condition fails.

[Lem 12 of arXiv:2607.24170, '\large\bf ON NON-MONOTONICITY OF LOGARITHMIC ENERGY\\ FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] There are constants $C_0,\delta_0>0$, depending only on the finite
collection of configurations in Lemma~\ref{LemSelectedZeros}, with
the following property.  Let $\mathbf{A}$ be one of those
configurations after division by $\sqrt3$, and let $\mathbf{E}$ be a
complex $3\times3$ matrix satisfying
$\|\mathbf{E}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\delta_0$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em]
\item for the all-common configuration, two eigenvalues $\lambda$ of
$\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{E}$ satisfy
$|\lambda|\leq C_0\|\mathbf{E}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, and the remaining
eigenvalue satisfies
$|\lambda-\mathfrak{c}\sqrt3|
\leq C_0\|\mathbf{E}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$;
\item for every selected simple-zero configuration,
$\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{E}$ has an eigenvalue $\lambda$ satisfying
$|\lambda|\leq C_0\|\mathbf{E}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$.
\end{enumerate}
All eigenvalues are counted with algebraic multiplicity.

[Proposition 15 (Tensor-product rule) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] For $S\subset[m]$ and $T\subset[n]$, the flattening
$\Flat_{S\sqcup(m+T)}(K\boxtimes L)$ is unitarily equivalent to
$\Flat_S(K)\otimes\Flat_T(L)$.  Hence, for $1\le r\le\infty$,
\begin{equation}

 \Prof_{m+n,r}(K\boxtimes L)
 =\Prof_{m,r}(K)\Prof_{n,r}(L).
\end{equation}

body:
[Defn def:distribution of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] A linear functional $\nu$ on $C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ is called a \emph{compactly 
supported distribution} if there exist $C,K\geq 0$ and $m\in \mathbb{Z}_+$ so 
that
$$
	|\nu(f)| \leq 
	C\max_{0\leq k \leq m} \sobnorm{f^{(k)}}{0}{[-K, K]}
	\quad\text{for all }f\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}).
$$
The \emph{support} $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nu$ of a compactly
supported distribution $\nu$ is the smallest closed set 
$A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ so that $\nu(f)=0$ for all $f\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$
that vanish in a neighborhood of $A$.
title: Defn def:distribution of arXiv:2412.00593

For the neutral boundary state both signs of B_1 occur, so its private defect is zero -- and this can dominate a SPANNING, FULL-CLOSED fibre, not merely an isolated nonspanning boundary state. Attach k further stable-set vertices z_1,...,z_k each adjacent to both boundary vertices 0,2 and to nothing else: in the positive half the neutral endpoint pattern has 2^{k+1} extensions (B_1 and all z_j free), each other endpoint pattern has one. So no inequality dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= C * L_{Q|W} can hold with an absolute C. [Theorem theorem1 of arXiv:2411.13875, 'Large deviations at the origin of random walk in random environment'] Consider a random walk in a uniformly elliptic i.i.d.\ environment. 
Then, the following assertions hold true:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] There exists $\vec{p}_\ast=(p_\ast(e))_{e \in \mathbb V} \in \mathcal K_{\mathbb P}$
  such that  
\begin{equation}

I_q(0)=I_a(0)=-\log\Big(\sum_{e\in \mathbb V}\sqrt{p_\ast(e)p_\ast(-e)}\Big)=:I(0).
\end{equation}
Furthermore, if the walk is either non-nestling or marginally nestling, then $p_*\in\partial 
\mathcal K_{\mathbb P}$.

\item[(ii)] Suppose that the random walk is either non-nestling or marginally nestling. Then, for each $\varepsilon>0$ there exists some period $(\mathbf n_\varepsilon,\mathbf p_\varepsilon)$ such that
\[
|I(0)-I_{(\mathbf n_\varepsilon,\mathbf p_\varepsilon)}(0)|\le \varepsilon.
\]
\item[(iii)] Suppose that the random walk is either non-nestling or marginally nestling. Then, for each $\varepsilon>0$ there exists some period $(\mathbf n_\varepsilon,\mathbf p_\varepsilon)$ and a $\delta_0>0$ such that for every $\delta\in(0,\delta_0)$,
\begin{equation}

\mathbb P\big( \liminf_{N \to \infty} G^{\varepsilon, \delta}_{N,\bf n_\varepsilon,\bf p_\varepsilon}\big) =1 
\end{equation}
and, for $\mathbb P$-almost every $\omega \in \Omega$,
\[
-I(0)-\varepsilon \leq 
\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\log P_{0,\omega}(A^\varepsilon_{N,\mathbf n_\varepsilon,\mathbf p_\varepsilon})\leq \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{N}\log P_{0,\omega}(X_N=0) \leq -I(0).
\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Dfn 1 of arXiv:2606.05964, 'Strong Solutions to SDEs with Supercritical Drift arising in Navigation Models'] Let $\tau=\inf\{t\ge 0:R_t=0\}$. We say that an
$(\mathcal F_t)$-adapted process $(R_t,\Theta_t)_{t\in[0,\tau]}$ is a
\emph{strong solution to \eqref{state} up to $\tau$} if:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every $t<\tau$ one has $R_t>0$, and $(R_s,\Theta_s)_{s\in[0,t]}$ is a
strong solution to \eqref{state} on $[0,t]$ in the usual sense of
\cite[Def.~2.1, Chap.~5]{ks}; in particular it is continuous and the integrability
condition
\begin{equation}
\int_0^t\bigl(|\mu_1(R_s,\Theta_s)|+|\mu_2(R_s,\Theta_s)|\bigr)\,ds<\infty
\end{equation}
holds for every $t<\tau$, and
\[
R_t=r+\int_0^t\mu_1(R_s,\Theta_s)\,ds,\qquad
\Theta_t=\theta+\int_0^t\mu_2(R_s,\Theta_s)\,ds+\sigma B_t;
\]
\item the limit $(R_\tau,\Theta_\tau):=\lim_{t\nearrow\tau}(R_t,\Theta_t)$ exists
almost surely.
\end{enumerate}

T250-w712-C005 v1. Target 1. Status: proof (unaudited).

Let Q_0=q_0 in [0,1] be deterministic, and let
Q_(l+1)=n^(-1) sum_(i=1)^n tanh(sqrt(Q_l) Z_(l+1,i))^2,
with fresh independent standard normal samples at each step, conditional on the entire past. For every b>0, integer n>=432b, and integer L>=0,

    E exp[b sum_(l=0)^(L-1) Q_l^2 +12b Q_L] <= exp(12b q_0).       (1)

In particular, the occupation moment without the terminal term has the same upper bound, uniformly in depth.

Proof. C002 proves F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2<=q-q^2/6 for q in [0,1]. The single-neuron random variable Y lies in [0,1] and satisfies Var(Y)<=E Y^2<=3q^2. For |x|<=1 and 0<=s<=1, the exponential series and e<3 give e^(sx)<=1+sx+s^2 x^2. Indeed the absolute remainder beyond the linear term is at most s^2 x^2 sum_(k>=2) 1/k!<s^2 x^2. For centered X=Y-EY, this implies

    E exp(sX)<=exp(s^2 Var(Y)).

Fix a>0. If a/n<=1, conditional independence of the n neuron samples gives

    E[exp(a Q_(l+1)) | past]
       <= exp[a F(Q_l)+3a^2 Q_l^2/n].

This multiplication uses iid samples within the new layer after conditioning on the past; it does not multiply marginal bounds across layers. If n>=36a, then 3a^2/n<=a/12. Consequently

    E[exp(a Q_(l+1)+(a/12)Q_l^2) | past] <= exp(a Q_l).

    E exp[b sum_j sum_(l<L) Q_(j,l)^2] <= exp[12b sum_j q_(j,0)].

Apply the scalar inequality at parameter bp to each marginal chain, then take the product of the p-th roots.

Correlation stability products. For a pair j,k, put
P_L=product_(l<L)[1+8(Q_(j,l)^2+Q_(k,l)^2)].

uniformly over all L. This follows from 1+x<=exp(x) and the p=2 occupation bound at b=8r. In particular ||P_L||_4<=exp[96(q_(j,0)+q_(k,0))] for n>=27648.

Load-bearing hypotheses: (i) B is symmetric; (ii) D(A) ⊂ D(B); (iii) ‖Bx‖ ≤ a‖Ax‖ + b‖x‖ on D(A) with a strictly less than 1. What fails. Dropping symmetry: take A self-adjoint unbounded and B = icA with 0 < c < 1. Then D(A) = D(B) and ‖Bx‖ = c‖Ax‖, so the relative bound is c < 1, yet A + B = (1 + ic)A has spectrum (1 + ic)σ(A), which is not contained in ℝ, so A + B is not self-adjoint; it is not even symmetric. Losing the strict inequality: take B = −A (symmetric, relative bound exactly a = 1, b = 0). Then A + B = 0 on D(A), which is symmetric and essentially self-adjoint but not self-adjoint on D(A), since D(A) ≠ H when A is unbounded; the conclusion 'self-adjoint on D(A)' is false at a = 1, and only Wüst's weaker conclusion (essential self-adjointness) survives. Dropping relative boundedness entirely: A = −d²/dx² on H²(ℝ) and B = multiplication by −x⁴ (maximal domain) are both self-adjoint and C_c^∞(ℝ) is a common dense invariant-looking core, but −d²/dx² − x⁴ is not essentially self-adjoint on C_c^∞(ℝ) (it is in the limit circle case at both ±∞, with deficiency indices (2,2)); the sum of two self-adjoint operators is in general neither self-adjoint nor essentially self-adjoint on the intersection of their domains, and that intersection can even be {0}. Also note that the relative bound of the perturbation must be measured against A itself, not against A + B, and that the infimum defining the relative bound need not be attained, so 'a ≤ 1' in a cited inequality is not the same as 'relative bound a < 1'. Audit rule: check symmetry of B, the domain inclusion, and the strict inequality with the constants actually produced by the estimate.

[Lem 27 of arXiv:2608.13727, 'Hitting-time mixing for the star transposition shuffle'] Let \(s_n\), \(s\), \(\gamma_{n,s}^\star\), and \(c_n^\star(s)\) be
    defined as in equations \eqref{eq:def-of-sn} and
    \eqref{eq:def-of-gamma-n-s-star}. Let \(1\le M_n\le n\) and let
    \(T_n \subseteq [n]_\star\) satisfy
    \([M_n]_\star\subseteq T_n\) and \(|T_n|=n^{o(1)}\). Suppose that
    \(|c_n^\star(s)| \leq (\log \log n)/2 - 4 \log \log \log n\). Then
    the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \(\bbP[\cG(T_n)] = (1 + O(n^{-1+o(1)})) \, \bbP[\cG(M_n)] \, (\gamma_{n, s}^{\star})^{|T_n| - M_n + 1} \, n^{M_n - 1 - |T_n|}\),
        \item \(\bbP[\cF(M_n)] = (1 + O(n^{-1+o(1)})) \bbP[\cG(M_n)] \exp(-\gamma_{n, s}^\star)\),
        \item for every \(L_n=n^{o(1)}\),
        \(\sum_{S \supseteq [M_n]_\star,\, |S| \leq L_n} \bbP[\cG(S)] \leq n^{o(1)} \bbP[\cF(M_n)]\).
    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem 20 (\cite{BD19}) of arXiv:2508.04938, 'Perfect t-embeddings of doubly periodic Aztec diamonds'] Let~$K$ be a Kasteleyn matrix, defined by~\eqref{eq:K_def}, of the Aztec diamond of size~$k\ell N$ with~$k\times \ell$ doubly periodic weights satisfying the assumption~$\beta_i^v < 1 < \alpha_i^v/\gamma_i^v$ for all~$i=1,\dots,\ell$.

Then,
\begin{multline*}
  K^{-1}( w_{\ell x'+i',ky'+j'},  b_{\ell x+i,ky+j}) 
  =\\
  -\left(\frac{\mathbf{1} \{\ell x+i \geq \ell x'+i'+1\}}{2\pi\i}\int_\Gamma \prod_{m=2\ell x'+2i'+2}^{2\ell x+2i} \phi_m(z)z^{y'-y}\frac{\d z}{z}\right)_{j'+1,j+1}\\
  +\Bigg(\frac{1}{(2\pi\i)^2}\int_{\Gamma_s}\int_{\Gamma_l}\left(\prod_{m=1}^{2i'+1}\phi_m(z_1)\right)^{-1}\Phi(z_1)^{-x'}\widetilde \phi_-(z_1)\widetilde \phi_+(z_2)\Phi(z_2)^{x-kN} \\
  \times
  \prod_{m=1}^{2i}\phi_m(z_2)\frac{z_1^{y'}}{z_2^y}\frac{\d z_2\d z_1}{z_2(z_2-z_1)}\Bigg)_{j'+1,j+1} .
\end{multline*}
The contours are positively oriented and given by~$\Gamma_s = \{|z| = r_s\}$,~$\Gamma_l = \{|z| = r_l\}$ for~$r_s < 1 < r_l$, and~$\Gamma = \{|z| = 1\}$, and~$\phi(z)=\widetilde\phi_{-}(z)\widetilde\phi_{+}(z)$ is the Wiener-Hopf factorisation. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 11 (Transfer-operator representation for Markov families) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $S$ be finite and, for each $i = 1,\dots,W$, let $P^{(i)}$ be the law of a Markov chain on $S$ with initial distribution $\mu_i$ and transition matrix $K_i$.
Define $\mu_\alpha(x) := \prod_i \mu_i(x)^{\alpha_i}$, and $T_\alpha(x,y) := \prod_i K_i(x,y)^{\alpha_i}$.
Then
\[
  Z_t(\alpha)
  = \sum_{x_0,\dots,x_t}
     \mu_\alpha(x_0)\prod_{s=0}^{t-1} T_\alpha(x_s,x_{s+1})
  = \langle \mu_\alpha, T_\alpha^t \mathbf{1}\rangle.
\]
If $T_\alpha$ is irreducible and aperiodic (e.g., Perron--Frobenius applies) and $\mu_\alpha \not\equiv 0$ (the weighted initial supports overlap, i.e.\ $Z_0(\alpha) > 0$), then $\lim_{t \to \infty}\frac{1}{t}\log Z_t(\alpha) = \log r(T_\alpha)$,
where $r(T_\alpha)$ is the Perron--Frobenius spectral radius. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Transfer-operator representation for Markov families

[Definition def:SaS-rv of arXiv:2606.02003, 'Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion:\\ Definition and Fundamental Properties'] A real random variable $\xi$ is \emph{symmetric $\alpha$-stable
(S$\alpha$S) with scale $\sigma \geq 0$} if
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{i\theta\xi}\bigr]
= e^{-\sigma^\alpha|\theta|^\alpha},
\quad \theta \in \mathbb{R},
\end{equation}
for some $\alpha \in (0,2]$. We write $\xi \sim \mathrm{S}\alpha\mathrm{S}(\sigma)$
and define $\|\xi\|_\alpha := \sigma$.
title: S$\alpha$S random variable

body:
[Lemma lem:countwk of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Take any $X, H \in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$, and $M\ge 0$. There exist $C,c>0$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] $\sum_{G\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}, |G-H|\ge M}|\mathscr F(X;H,G)|\le C2^X\exp(-cM^2/X)$.
    \item[(ii)] $|\mathscr F(X;H,G)|\le CX^{-1/2}2^X\exp(-cM^2/X)$, for any $G \in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$, such that $|G-H|\ge M$.
    \item[(iii)] $\sum_{G\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}, G\ge M}|\mathscr F(X;0,G)|\le CX^{-1/2}2^X\exp(-cM^2/X)$.
    \item[(iv)]  $|\mathscr F(X;H,0)|\le CX^{-1}2^X\exp(-cM^2/X)$, whenever $H\ge M$.
    \item[(v)] $|\mathscr F(X;0,0)|\le CX^{-3/2}2^X$.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2607.27786, 'Gaussian free field in annulus: \\BPZ equations and crossing probabilities for level lines'] Fix $r>0$ and an even number $n=2N$. 
For $\bs{\alpha}, \bs{\beta}\in\LX_n$, we write $\bs{x}=\ee^{\ii\bs{\alpha}}$ and $\bs{y}=\ee^{\ii\bs{\beta}-r}$. 
Suppose $\Gamma$ is Dirichlet GFF in annulus $\A_r$. For $j\in \{1, \ldots, n\}$, let $\gamma^j$ be the level line of $\Gamma+\varphiann{n}$ starting from $x_j$, where $\varphiann{n}$ is the bounded harmonic function in annulus $\A_r$ with alternating boundary data~\eqref{eqn::boundarydata}. 
\begin{itemize}
\item The level lines $\bs{\gamma}=(\gamma^1, \ldots, \gamma^n)$ are continuous curves and they are deterministic functions of the field $\Gamma$ almost surely. 
\item We parameterize $\bs{\gamma}=(\gamma^1, \ldots, \gamma^n)$ by the $n$-time parameter. Let $(\gamma, \nu)$ be a regular Legendre curve in $H^2(-1)$ with geodesic curvature $\kappa_g(t)$ and parallel curve $P_d(t) = \cosh d \gamma(t) + \sinh d \nu(t)$. Then $P_d'(t) = (\cosh d + \kappa_g(t) \sinh d) \ell(t) \mu(t)$. Consequently, $P_d$ is singular at $t$ if and only if $\tanh d = -1/\kappa_g(t)$, which occurs precisely when $P_d(t)$ intersects the hyperbolic evolute $E(t)$.
(\gamma, \nu) is a regular Legendre curve

[Theorem 20 of arXiv:2607.22441, 'The martingale representation theorem for cylindrical martingale valued measures'] Let $X$ be a separable, reflexive Banach space and let $(m_t: t \geq 0)$ be an $X$-valued square integrable martingale, with operator quadratic covariation satisfying
$$\langle x^*_1(m), x^*_2(m)\rangle_t=\int_0^t \Bigl(\Phi (r)Q \Phi(r)^* x^*_1, x^*_2\Bigr)_H\,dr, \quad \forall x^*_1, x^*_2 \in X^*,$$ 
for $Q\in \mathcal{K}^+(H)$ and $\Phi: \Omega \times[0,T]  \rightarrow \mathcal{L}(H,X)$ is $ (\omega,t) \mapsto \Phi(\omega,t)h$ 
is $\mathcal{P}_{T}/\mathcal{B}(X)$-measurable for every $h \in H$. Then there exists an $H$-valued $Q$-Wiener process $B=(B_t: t \geq 0)$, defined on an extended probability space $(\Omega \times \widetilde{\Omega}, \mathcal{F} \times \widetilde{\mathcal{F}}, \Prob \times \widetilde{\Prob})$ adapted to the filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_{t} \times \widetilde{\mathcal{F}}_{t}\}$ such that
\begin{equation}

m_t(\omega)=\int_0^t \Phi(\omega, r)\, dB_r (\omega, \widetilde{\omega}).
\end{equation}
This equality must be taken as $X$-valued random variables.

A two-sided sequence (X_j)_{j in Z} is m-dependent, for a fixed nonnegative integer m, if sigma(X_j:j<=k) and sigma(X_j:j>=k+m+1) are independent for every integer k. One-dependence is m=1. This is independence of entire separated sigma-fields, not just pairwise independence of coordinates. Stationarity is a separate assumption: all finite-dimensional laws are invariant under integer shifts. For an m-dependent stationary sequence, every event-ratio mixing coefficient psi(n) is zero for n>m, hence the sequence is psi-mixing.
Two-sided sequence; fixed nonnegative integer m
title: Bradley one-dependent and m-dependent stationary sequences

body:
[Proposition 39 (Coherent response completion and global decoding) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] The coherent response space
$\mathsf R_{\mathfrak Q_2}^{\rm coh}$ is causal Polish, closed in the ambient
profile carrier $\widetilde{\mathsf R}_{\mathfrak Q_2}^{\eta}$, and invariant
under deterministic stopping.  The core map
\eqref{eq:coherent-core-response-profile} extends uniquely by completion to a
stable-causal isometric homeomorphism
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal O_{\mathfrak Q_2}:
 \mathsf Z_{\eta;\mathcal S_2,1}(H)
 \longrightarrow\mathsf R_{\mathfrak Q_2}^{\rm coh},
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{\mathfrak Q_2}(x,A,q)
 =\bigl(x,(\jmath_AA_{s,t})_{s,t},(\jmath_Qq_{s,t})_{s,t}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Its inverse is the globally defined stable-causal decoder
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D_{\mathfrak Q_2}(x,\alpha,\chi)
 =\operatorname{ch}_{\tau_0}^{-1}(x,A,q),
 \qquad
 A_{s,t}=\jmath_A^{-1}\alpha_{s,t},\qquad
 q_t=\jmath_Q^{-1}\chi_{0,t},
\end{equation}
where $q_{s,t}=q_t-q_s$ and
$\tau_0=(\eta;\mathcal S_2,\mathcal S_1)$.  Thus
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D_{\mathfrak Q_2}\mathcal O_{\mathfrak Q_2}=I,
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{\mathfrak Q_2}\mathcal D_{\mathfrak Q_2}=I
 \quad\text{on }\mathsf R_{\mathfrak Q_2}^{\rm coh}.
\end{equation}
Thus $\mathcal D_{\mathfrak Q_2}$ is defined on the full declared response
target $\mathsf R_{\mathfrak Q_2}^{\rm coh}$.

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Extreme least singular values of Gaussian row submatrices and a phase retrieval stability problem (arXiv:2607.06249, July 2026) proves that if A_m in F^{N_m x m}, F = R or C and d_F = dim_R F, has independent standard Gaussian entries and N_m/m -> gamma > 1, then the minimum over row subsets T of size m of sigma_min(A_{m,T}) is (gamma^gamma / (gamma - 1)^(gamma - 1))^(-m/d_F + o_P(m)), and that when N_m = gamma m + O(1) the convergence of m^{-1} log of that minimum has probability error O(1/m). body:
[Theorem thm:positive-zero-results of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Let $\beta>0$. Every nonzero zero of $\phi_\beta$ lies in the open left
    half-plane. There are only finitely many nonreal zeros, counted with
    multiplicity, and they occur in conjugate pairs.
    
If $\beta=n_\beta$ is a positive integer, then $1/\phi_{n_\beta}$ is rational,
$\mathcal Z_{n_\beta}$ consists of exactly $n_\beta$ simple zeros, and
\[
\begin{cases}
\text{all these zeros are nonreal}, & \text{if $n_\beta$ is even},\\
-3n_\beta-4\text{ is the unique real zero}, & \text{if $n_\beta$ is odd}.
\end{cases}
\]

If $\beta$ is noninteger, let
\[
        \beta=n_\beta+\theta_\beta,
        \qquad 
        \text{with }
        n_\beta=\lfloor\beta\rfloor \text{ and }
\theta_\beta\in(0,1).
\]
If $n_\beta$ is even, then $\phi_\beta$ has exactly $n_\beta$ nonreal
zeros, counted with multiplicity. If $n_\beta$ is odd, then
$\phi_\beta$ has at most $n_\beta+1$ nonreal zeros, counted with
multiplicity. If this upper bound is attained, then all real zeros are
simple.
    
    Moreover, for every $\sigma>0$ such that
    $\phi_\beta$ has no zero on $\textnormal{Re} z=-\sigma$, 
    \begin{equation}
        \text{the set }    \mathcal Z_{\beta,\sigma}
            :=
            \{\rho\in\mathcal Z_\beta:-\sigma<\textnormal{Re}\rho<0\}
            \text{ is finite.}
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Zero structure for $\beta>0$

[Proposition 4 (\textsf{Stationary Stein identity}) of arXiv:2609.02064, 'Coalescence and fluctuations of O'Connell--Yor polymers\\ via the free-energy correlation '] Fix $n\geq1$, $\be>0$, and $m\geq0$.  Let
  $\mathbf y=(y_0,\ldots,y_m)\in\R^{m+1}$ and set
  \[
    \mathbf F_{\mathbf y}^{\be}
    =
    \bigl(
      F_{y_0}^{\rstat,\be},\ldots,
      F_{y_m}^{\rstat,\be}
    \bigr).
  \]
  Suppose that $\varphi\in C^1(\R^{m+1})$ and
  $\|\nabla\varphi\|_\infty<\infty$.  Then the map
  $
    x\mapsto
    \EE\bigl[
      \varphi(\mathbf F_{\mathbf y}^{\be})
      F_x^{\rstat,\be}
    \bigr]
  $
  is continuously differentiable on every connected component of
  $\R\setminus\{y_0,\ldots,y_m\}$.  Moreover, for every
  $x\notin\{y_0,\ldots,y_m\}$,
  \begin{align}
    &\frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \EE\bigl[
      \varphi(\mathbf F_{\mathbf y}^{\be})
      F_x^{\rstat,\be}
    \bigr]
  =
    \sum_{j=0}^{m}
    \EE\left[
      \partial_j\varphi(\mathbf F_{\mathbf y}^{\be})
      \left(
        Q_x^{\rstat,\be}\{\ga_n>-x\}
        -\ind_{\{x>y_j\}}
      \right)
    \right].
  \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsf{Stationary Stein identity}

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). The regime question of the two-regimes lemma was put to the pools: the elasticity of the out-of-fold least-squares residual norm to the target norm on the calibration rows, the members' own elasticities, and the additive-floor share, per output group. P21 (a) REFUTED: the out-of-fold residual elasticity to the target norm is 0.38, 0.42, -0.06, 0.41 on Y1..Y4 against the pre-registered 0.7 - the member errors are closer to additive than multiplicative; (b) REFUTED: the lowest elasticity is on Y3 and the largest floor share on Y4, not Y2; (c) HELD: OCO-2 target norms vary by a factor 1.4, 1.4, 1.3 between the 10th and 90th percentiles and n_eff/n is 0.95, 0.94, 0.96; falsifier (every EMIT group below 0.4) not triggered (0.38, 0.42, -0.06, 0.41). Consequence: the relative weights 1/||y||^2 are far from Aitken's on EMIT, Kish's n_eff of the relative fit (146 of 932 rows on Y2) is a genuinely unbalanced fit, and Y2 is singled out by the six-fold wider spread of its targets (p90/p10 6.4 against about 2), not by an error floor.

body:
[Theorem thm: percolation_reference of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $d\ge2$. For $m\ge1$ and $p\in(0,1)$, consider Bernoulli site percolation with parameter $p$ on $\mathbb{T}_m^d$, and let $\mathrm{GC}=\mathrm{GC}(m,p)$ denote its largest open cluster, with ties broken arbitrarily. 
    \begin{itemize} 
    \item[(i)] For every $p > p^{\mathrm{site}}_c(d)$, there exist constants $C=C(d,p)>0$ and $c=c(p)>0$ such that the following holds for all large $m$. Set
    \[
    n(m):=\left\lceil C(\log m)^{1/(d-1)}\right\rceil .
    \]
    Then, with probability at least $1-m^{-1}$, every box of side length $n(m)$ contains at least $c \, n(m)^d$ vertices of $\mathrm{GC}$. Moreover, we can choose $c(p)$ such that $c(p) \rightarrow 1$ as $p \rightarrow 1$.
    \item[(ii)] There exists $p_o(d) \in (0,1)$ such that, for every $p\in(p_o(d),1)$, there exists $\beta=\beta(d)>0$ such that, for every $m\ge1$ and every $U\subseteq\mathbb{T}_m^d$ 
    \[
    \mathbb P_p\bigl(U\cap\mathrm{GC}=\varnothing\bigr)
    \le
    \exp\left(-\beta |U|^{(d-1)/d}\right) + e^{-\beta m} \, .
    \]
    \item[(iii)] For every $p>p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(d)$ and every $\gamma>1$, there exists $C'=C'(d,p)>0$ such that, upon setting
    \[
    r(m):=\left\lceil(\log m)^\gamma\right\rceil ,
    \]
    we have
    \[
    \mathbb P_p\left(
    \mathrm{diam}(\mathrm{GC}\cap B)
    \le C'r(m)
    \ \text{for every box $B$ of side length $r(m)$}
    \right)
    \longrightarrow 1
    \]
    as $m\to\infty$. Here $\mathrm{diam}$ is measured in the intrinsic graph metric of $\mathrm{GC}$ on the full torus $\mathbb{T}_m^d$; thus, connecting paths may leave $B$.
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm: percolation_reference of arXiv:2608.00399

[Proposition 24 (Nesterov risk recursion) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] Under the covariance relation in Proposition~\ref{prop:noise-geometry}, the expected excess risk satisfies the two-sided
recursion
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{E}\mathcal E_k
    \eqsim
    \cS_{\nesterov}(k)
    +
    \frac{\eta^2\sigma^2}{B}\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\mathcal K_{\nesterov}(\tau)
    +
    \frac{\eta^2}{B}\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\mathcal K_{\nesterov}(\tau)
    \mathbb{E}\mathcal L_{k-1-\tau}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:nes_lookahead_loss_control} gives the required control of the look-ahead risk by the
next-step risk.  In particular, under the stable small-step condition,
\[
    c\,\mathbb{E}\mathcal E_{m+1}-C\frac{\eta^2\sigma^2}{B}
    \le
    \mathbb{E}\mathcal L_m
    \le
    C\,\mathbb{E}\mathcal E_{m+1}.
\]

[Definition E_rho of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] For a graph $H$, let 
${\mathcal A}(H)$ be the set of all 
pairs $(e,A)$ 
such that $A$ is a graph and $e$ is an edge in $\langle A\rangle_H\setminus A$. 
We define the {\it critical $H$-activation density}  as 
\begin{equation}
\rho(H)=\inf_{(e,\,A)\in{\mathcal A}(H)}\, 
\max_{e\subset F\subseteq A\cup e}\, 
\frac{e(F)-1}{v(F)-2}.
\end{equation}
title: Definition E_rho of arXiv:2605.15066

[Lem toy_problem of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $\sigma^1$ and $\sigma^2$ be
  two independent Markov jump processes with the transition rates of
  figure~(fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2016 of the paper)
  (resp. (fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2017 of the paper)) and let
  $N_1^L$ and $N_2^L$ be two independent Poisson processes with rate
  $\gamma_L$ independent of the $\sigma^i$. \green{Denote $0 = \Theta^{L, i}_0 < \Theta^{L, i}_1 < \cdots$ the jump times of $N_i^L$. If one sets
$$
S^L(t) := \sum_{i = 1, 2} \sum_{k = 1}^{+\infty} 1_{\{ \Theta^{L,i}_k \le t \}}  (-1)^i \sigma^i(\Theta^{L,i}_k) \text{ and } \ I(t) := \int_0^t (\sigma^2(s) - \sigma^1(s))ds
$$}
then one has
$$
\mathbb P \left( \sup_{t \le T} \left| \frac{1}{\gamma_L} S^L(t) - I(t)\right| \ge \epsilon \right) \le \frac{2}{\epsilon} \sqrt{\frac{T}{\gamma_L}}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem toy_problem of arXiv:2411.13964

$$p_v:=1-\sum_k\alpha_kv_k.$$

body:
[Definition 15 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] $[-\infty,\infty]:=\mathbb{R}\cup \{-\infty,\infty\}:=$ the extended real line. 

The orderings $\leq$ and $<$ are extended to $[-\infty,\infty]$ from $\mathbb{R}$ in the natural way: $-\infty \leq a\leq \infty$ for all $a\in [-\infty,\infty]$; $-\infty<a$ iff $a\in (-\infty,\infty]=\mathbb{R}\cup \{\infty\}$ and $a<\infty$ iff $a\in [-\infty,\infty)=\{-\infty\}\cup \mathbb{R}$. 

We introduce the intervals $[-\infty,a]:=\{-\infty\}\cup (-\infty,a]$ for $a\in [-\infty,\infty)$ (with $(-\infty,-\infty]:=\emptyset$) etc. in the obvious way.

	We specify $0\cdot (\pm\infty):=0=:(\pm\infty)\cdot 0$ and $\infty+(-\infty):=0=:(-\infty)+\infty$.  The remainder of the ``arithmetic'' in $[-\infty,\infty]$ is (then) defined in the ``natural'' way, e.g. $a\cdot \infty=\sgn(a)\infty$ for $a\in [-\infty,\infty]\backslash\{0\}$, $a+\infty=\infty$ for $a\in (-\infty,\infty]$, $\infty-\infty:=\infty+(-\infty)=0$, $\vert \pm\infty\vert=\infty$ etc. 
	
	We endow $[-\infty,\infty]$ with the standard topology corresponding e.g. to the metric $d$ given by $d(x,y):=\vert \arctan(x)-\arctan(y)\vert$ for $\{x,y\}\subset [-\infty,\infty]$ ($\arctan(\infty):=\pi/2$ and $\arctan(-\infty):=-\pi/2$).
	
	 A map with values in $[-\infty,\infty]$ will be said to be numerical\footnote{For our purposes here. In general one would also consider complex-valued functions to be numerical, but we shall not be concerned with those, except for mentioning them in passing here and there.}.
title: Definition 15 of arXiv:2604.01685

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2606.02036, 'Self-intersection local times for Volterra Gaussian processes in stochastic flows with int'] Let $\mu^{(1)}$ and $\mu^{(2)}$ be deterministic probability measures in $\cM_m$ and $x_1$ and $x_2$ be the corresponding solutions to \eqref{eq:Eq_interaction} with the initial measures $\mu^{(1)}$ and $\mu^{(2)}$, respectively.  
Let
$\rho^{(k)}_i(v,t)=\frac{1}{\mid \det \D x_i(v,t)\mid^{k-1}},$ for $ i=1,2.$   Then, 
$$

$$
for all $T>0$, $k\geqslant 2$,  and $c$ is some a constant.

body:
[Lemma lem:fg of arXiv:2603.05467, 'Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph'] For every $d\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$, there exist $t=t(d,k), a_0=a_0(d,k), r_0=r_0(d,k), C=C(d,k) > 0$ such 
that the following holds.
Suppose that $0 < a < a_0, 0 < r < r_0$, the finite set $V \subseteq \ensuremath{ \mathbb R}^d$
and the function $f :S^{d-1} \to (-t,t)$ are such that  
$f$ is odd and $a$-Lipschitz and moreover

$$ \left|B\left( (1+f(u))\cdot u, r \right) \cap V\right| \leq k, $$

\noindent
for all $u \in S^{d-1}$.
Then there also exists a function $g : S^{d-1} \to \ensuremath{ \mathbb R}$ that is odd, $(Ca)$-Lipschitz and satisfies 

$$ |f(u)-g(u)| < Car \quad \text{ and } \quad 
B\left( (1+g(u)) \cdot u, a^{C}\cdot r  \right) \cap V = \emptyset, $$

\noindent 
for all $u \in S^{d-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:fg of arXiv:2603.05467

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2604.01336, 'Euler scheme for stochastic functional differential equations driven by fractional Brownia'] Let $h$ be a function defined on $[\![ 0, T]\!]^{2}$ and $\mu>1$. Then the following inequalities hold true:
		
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item Whenever $h(t_i, t_{i+1})=0$ for all $0\le i <n-1$, we have
			$$
			\left\|h\right\|_{\mu}\leq C_{\mu}\left\|\delta h\right\|_{\mu},
			$$
			with
			$$	\left\|h\right\|_{\mu}=\sup_{(u,v)\in\mathcal{S}_2([\![0, T ]\!])}\frac{|h(u,v)|}{|v-u|^\mu}
			\quad\text{and}\quad
			\left\|\delta h\right\|_{\mu}=\sup_{(s,u,v)\in\mathcal{S}_3([\![0, T ]\!])}
			\frac{|\delta h(s,u,v)|}{|v-s|^\mu}.$$
			\item In the general case where the quantities $h(t_i, t_{i+1})$ do not all vanish, we obtain:
			\begin{equation*}
				\left\|h\right\|_{\mu}\leq C_{\mu}\left\|\delta h\right\|_{\mu}
				+ \mathcal{M}_{\mu}(h),
				\quad\text{where}\quad
				\mathcal{M}(h) \equiv \sup\left\{ \frac{|h(t_i, t_{i+1})|}{|t_{i+1}-t_{i}|^{\mu}} ; \,  0\le i <n-1 \right\} .
			\end{equation*}
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
