This family satisfies the named target's sample-size condition whenever n is chosen large enough to satisfy that condition as well.

## Deterministic convergence, retaining the covariance metric

Subtract the constant empirical residual at W. The resulting loss is

 q(B,A)=||(BA-W) C^(1/2)||F^2/2,

with product gradient G=BA C-D. Let E=BA-W and F_t=A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t. C014 proves, for the first two step bounds above,

 q_(t+1)<=q_t-(eta/2)||grad q_t||F^2,
 ||F_t-F_0||F<=2eta q0,
 ||B_t A_t||F<=R.

Its proof establishes these inequalities without assuming factor boundedness in advance, and works with this anisotropic covariance, not a substituted isotropic GD. The third step bound makes

 2eta q0<=h0 q0/[2(1+q0)]<h0/2.

Hence F_t>=h0 I/2 and A_t A_t^T>=h0 I/2 for all t. The square input factor is essential. Since grad_B q=E C A_t^T,

 ||grad q||F^2 >=(h0/2)||E C||F^2
               >=h0 lambda q.

Combine this with descent to get q_(t+1)<=(1-eta h0 lambda/2)q_t. The multiplier is nonnegative: K bounds the initial factor-pair squared norm, so K>=h0, and eta<=1/(6Kc+||D||op) implies eta h0 lambda<=1/6. Iterate and use q>=lambda||E||F^2/2. If q0=0, the gradients vanish and the same conclusion is immediate.

No high-probability complement is discarded here. C and A0 meet these deterministic assumptions almost surely; the step is selected from their realized values. Defining an arbitrary measurable positive step on the null singular event has no effect on any expectation claim.

## An integrable product bound independent of the initializer

The fact that eta is allowed to depend on A0 does not itself establish expectation convergence. For every t on the almost-sure event,

 ||B_t A_t-Delta||F^2<=2R^2+2||Delta||F^2.

Here R depends only on the training data, because B0=0 makes q0 independent of A0. We now prove its expectation is finite.

Conditional on X, write W=Delta+N C^(-1/2), where N has iid N(0,sigma^2/n) entries and its conditional law is independent of X. Thus

 E[||W||F^2 | X]=||Delta||F^2+(m sigma^2/n)tr(C^(-1)),
 E[2q0 | X]=||Delta C^(1/2)||F^2+mp sigma^2/n.

Since R^2<=2||W||F^2+4q0/lambda, its conditional expectation is at most

 2||Delta||F^2+(2m sigma^2/n)tr(C^(-1))
 +2||Delta||F^2 ||C||op||C^(-1)||op
 +(2mp sigma^2/n)||C^(-1)||op.

It remains to check the covariance moments used in this expression. A fully elementary bound suffices; no asymptotic random-matrix approximation is needed.

## Exact finite inverse-covariance moment check

Let G=X^T be the n-by-p standard Gaussian design. For each column j let d_j be its distance from the span of the other p-1 columns. Almost surely these spans have dimension p-1. The j-th row of the left pseudoinverse G^+ has squared norm d_j^(-2): it is the normalized residual vector of column j after orthogonal projection onto the other columns. Consequently

 sigma_min(G)^(-2)<=||G^+||F^2=sum_j d_j^(-2),
 sigma_min(G)^(-4)<=p sum_j d_j^(-4).

Conditional on the other columns, d_j^2 is chi-squared with k=n-p+1 degrees of freedom, by Gaussian orthogonal projection. Its density is t^(k/2-1)e^(-t/2)/(2^(k/2) Gamma(k/2)). Direct integration gives, for k>4,

 E[d_j^(-4)]=1/[(k-2)(k-4)].

No independence between different d_j is assumed. Therefore

 E||C^(-1)||op^2
 <= n^2 p^2/[(n-p-1)(n-p-3)]<infinity.

Also ||C||op<=tr C and the sum of np independent squared standard Gaussians gives

 E||C||op^2<=E[(tr C)^2]=p^2+2p/n.

Cauchy-Schwarz now proves E[||C||op||C^(-1)||op]<infinity. The first inverse moments are finite by the second-moment bound, and tr(C^(-1))<=p||C^(-1)||op. This proves that the data-only dominating variable 2R^2+2||Delta||F^2 is integrable, including in the zero-noise case.

## Passing to expected risk and identifying the known comparator

Pointwise product convergence and the integrable bound allow the dominated convergence theorem on the joint probability space of training data and initialization. Hence the limiting expectation equals E||W-Delta||F^2. For standard Gaussian designs the known inverse-Wishart mean is E[(XX^T)^(-1)]=I_p/(n-p-1), n>p+1; conditioning on X gives

 E||W-Delta||F^2=m sigma^2 E tr((XX^T)^(-1))
                          =sigma^2 m p/(n-p-1).

This is the standard overdetermined OLS risk, also given by Zindari-Mulayoff-Stich, arXiv:2605.19018, Theorem 1 and Proposition 3 (printed p.4; inverse-Wishart computation in Appendix IV.1). The mean formula is used only to identify the finite risk explicitly; the elementary moment argument above already proves the expectation passage.

The rank-p constraint imposes no restriction on an m-by-p regression product, so reduced-rank regression with r=p is exactly OLS. This explains the factor-one comparison and the essential limitation: there is no proper input-side rank bottleneck. C013 does not contradict this theorem because its positive step must be chosen independently of the Gaussian initializer; the present safe step uses its smallest singular value and norm. All claims remain unaudited, and novelty is not asserted.


Deterministic C014 component supplied in full:
# T419-C014 v1: empirical GD boundedness with an initialization-dependent step

Kind: bound. Target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This is an explicit anisotropic version of the published Gram-imbalance/descent method, not a solution of Target 2. It proves a trajectory component without assuming the iterates are bounded. The prior source is Du-Hu-Lee, arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 2.2 and Appendix B, Claim B.1; its full convergence theorems have different initialization/step hypotheses. C009 already identifies the exact covariance metric and C010 the positive-noise empirical landscape.

## Statement

Let C be any real positive definite p-by-p matrix, D any real m-by-p matrix, and r>=1. Put lambda=lambda_min(C)>0, c=||C||op, ell=||D||op, W=D C^(-1), and

 q(B,A)=(1/2)||(BA-W) C^(1/2)||F^2,

with B m-by-r and A r-by-p. This is the empirical regression objective up to a constant when C=XX^T/n and D=ZX^T/n. Initialize at any finite deterministic factors B0,A0, and define

 q0=q(B0,A0), J=||A0 A0^T-B0^T B0||F+1,
 R=||W||F+sqrt(2q0/lambda),
 K=sqrt(r)(J+2R), L=6Kc+ell.

For any fixed

 0<eta<=min{1/(1+2q0),1/L},

simultaneous ordinary factor GD satisfies, for every integer t>=0,

 q_t<=q0,
 ||B_t||F^2+||A_t||F^2<=K,
 ||(A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t)-(A0 A0^T-B0^T B0)||F<=2eta q0<1,
 sum_(t>=0) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/eta.

In particular the gradient tends to zero, every accumulation point is critical, and for every integer T>=1,

 min_(0<=t<T) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/(eta T).

All constants are finite and computable from C,D and the initialization. There is no Gaussian assumption and no low-rank assumption on W. No iterate-convergence, saddle-avoidance or statistical-risk assertion is included.

## Exact identities and product/factor bounds

Let G=BA C-D. The two factor gradients are G_B=G A^T and G_A=B^T G. With E_t=A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t the first-order cross terms cancel exactly, giving

 E_(t+1)-E_t=eta^2(G_A G_A^T-G_B^T G_B),
 ||E_(t+1)-E_t||F<=eta^2(||G_A||F^2+||G_B||F^2).

This cancellation only uses dependence on BA and does not require isotropic C. Also

 (||B||F^2+||A||F^2)^2
 <=r [||AA^T-B^TB||F^2+4||BA||F^2].

To verify it, write P=B^TB,Q=AA^T. Scalar trace Cauchy-Schwarz gives (tr(P+Q))^2<=r tr((P+Q)^2), and cyclicity of trace gives tr((P+Q)^2)=||P-Q||F^2+4 tr(PQ), tr(PQ)=||BA||F^2. No commutation is assumed.

When q<=q0, positivity of C gives ||BA-W||F<=sqrt(2q0/lambda), hence ||BA||F<=R. If additionally ||E-E0||F<=1, then ||E||F<=J, so the preceding trace bound implies

 ||B||F^2+||A||F^2<=sqrt(r) sqrt(J^2+4R^2)<=K.

The initialization meets these conditions and therefore has pair norm at most sqrt(K).

## Descent established before closing the boundedness induction

Suppose at the current iterate the pair norm is at most sqrt(K), and preceding steps have valid descent inequalities. Then

 ||grad q||F<=||BA C-D||op sqrt(||B||F^2+||A||F^2)
             <=(Kc/2+ell)sqrt(K).

Because eta<=1/(6Kc+ell), the proposed next point has pair norm at most 2sqrt(K). The connecting segment also lies in that ball. On that ball the Hessian quadratic form in a perturbation (dB,dA) is

 ||(dB A+B dA) C^(1/2)||F^2+2<BA C-D,dB dA>.

Its absolute value is at most

 [c(||A||op^2+||B||op^2)+||BA C-D||op]
 times (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2)
 <=[4Kc+(2Kc+ell)] (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2).

Here the first summand uses Cauchy-Schwarz on dB A+B dA; the cross term uses |<G,dB dA>|<=||G||op||dB||F||dA||F. Thus the Hessian operator norm on the segment is at most L. Taylor's theorem along that segment proves

 q_next<=q-eta||grad q||F^2+(L eta^2/2)||grad q||F^2
        <=q-(eta/2)||grad q||F^2.

In particular q_next<=q0. Telescoping the descent inequalities, including the proposed step, and using q>=0 yields

 sum_(j=0)^t eta^2||grad q_j||F^2<=2eta q0
 <=2q0/(1+2q0)<1.

Summing the imbalance increments now proves ||E_next-E0||F<=2eta q0<1. The product/factor bound therefore puts the endpoint back in the smaller ball of pair radius sqrt(K). This closes the induction without assuming a bound before proving descent on the required larger segment. The q0=0 case is included: both gradients vanish, the sequence is constant, and all inequalities still hold.

## Consequences and exact remaining gap

Telescoping for every finite horizon gives the infinite summability bound. A nonnegative summable sequence tends to zero, so the gradients vanish. Bounded finite-dimensional factor pairs have convergent subsequences; gradient continuity makes every subsequential limit critical. The running-minimum bound follows by averaging the finite sum. These statements do not require that the entire sequence converges to one point.

For B0=0 and a Gaussian A0, this provides an allowed positive step after observing the initialization, conditional on every full-row-rank design. It does not supply a single positive step independent of the unbounded Gaussian initializer. C013 shows that unconditional expected-limit risk with such an initialization-independent fixed step can diverge even at rank one.

Combining this bound with the already verified empirical strict-saddle landscape C010 is insufficient to conclude global optimization. One must additionally show that the specified zero/Gaussian initialization does not approach a nonglobal critical point, with all hypotheses of a saddle-avoidance theorem checked for its lower-dimensional initial support and step rule. Vanishing gradients do not establish that. Even convergence almost surely would not by itself justify passing to expected population risk; a failure-tail/integrability or finite-stopping argument is separately required. The usual full-ambient absolutely-continuous random-initialization theorem cannot simply be cited for the plane B0=0.

Independent reviewer audit and any novelty assessment remain pending. Moreover D_p=0 precisely when mu=nu, because the positive weights force equality of all dyadic cell masses, and these partitions generate the Borel sigma field of Q.

Own-work draft, claim T323-OFFAXIS-001 v2, status proof (unaudited). For three tokens x_i in S^2 under self-inclusive normalized attention dot x_i=(I-x_i x_i^T) sum_j exp(beta x_i^T A x_j)V x_j / sum_j exp(beta x_i^T A x_j), take A=V=diag(1,1/2,-2), beta=2. There is a locally asymptotically stable equilibrium x1=(-q,0,-sqrt(1-q^2)), x2=(-1,0,0), x3=(-q,0,sqrt(1-q^2)), where q is the unique root in (19/1000,191/10000) of exp(2q)+3q exp(-4+6q^2)-q exp(4-2q^2)=0. Its three directions are distinct and noncollinear, and its basin is open with positive product volume. The hyperbolic sink persists in some open neighborhood of (A,V,beta)=(V0,V0,2), with V real symmetric of signature (2,1); A may be unaligned and is realizable as Q^T K. Thus an almost-everywhere two-antipodal-cluster conclusion is false on an open family. This does not classify all initial states. Full tangent-Hessian negativity is certified by exact outward-rounded dyadic intervals; the proof and implementation still require independent audit. Clustering attractors were reported numerically by Altafini 2025; no claim that the phenomenon itself is new.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:31393958d812b62d481d9e2f1cf6fce9ce058d23d13a5315abc5d60b709c81ee","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/31/31393958d812b62d481d9e2f1cf6fce9ce058d23d13a5315abc5d60b709c81ee.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:c6e994366a6cb7c08d5aa377cbcc5effa5dafd4c0bce3534f8762c5143cd94cb","bundle_entry_key":"three-direction-sink","bundle_id":"population.t323-certified-three-direction-sink-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"spherical self-attention dynamics","draft":"w696/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:analysis.dynamical_systems:t323-certified-three-direction-attention-sink-open-parameter-family","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T323-OFFAXIS-001 v2: a three-direction attracting equilibrium

Status: proof (unaudited), computer-assisted. Kind: moved; target 2.
The hardest finite step is negativity of the full six-dimensional tangent
Hessian, including directions out of the symmetry plane. It is checked
with outward-rounded exact dyadic intervals, not floating-point spectra.
Independent audit and literature priority checking remain separate.

## Statement

For three self-inclusive tokens on S^2, let

    V0 = diag(1, 1/2, -2), beta0=2, Q^T K=V0.

The normalized attention flow has a locally asymptotically stable
equilibrium with three distinct, noncollinear token directions

    x1=(-q,0,-s), x2=(-1,0,0), x3=(-q,0,s),
    19/1000 < q < 191/10000, s=sqrt(1-q^2).

It has an open basin of positive product volume. Consequently the claim
that almost every start has an antipodal two-cluster limit is false for
this signature-(2,1) model. The result is robust: such a three-direction
hyperbolic sink persists for all (A,V,beta) in some open neighborhood of
(V0,V0,2), where A=Q^T K is the score matrix and V is restricted to real
symmetric matrices. Thus the counterexample holds on an open parameter
family, including unaligned A. No explicit neighborhood radius or
classification of every other basin is asserted.

## Scalar reduction and exact existence

Write

    S=exp(-4+6q^2), O=exp(4-2q^2), M=exp(2q), L=exp(2).

These are the pair self-score, the opposite-pair score, the score
between a pair token and the middle token, and the middle self-score.
The symmetric unnormalized attention matrix is

    W = [[S,M,O],[M,L,M],[O,M,S]].

Let h_i=sum_j W_ij V0 x_j and alpha_i=x_i dot h_i. The middle
token is stationary by reflection symmetry. Both pair tokens are
stationary if and only if

    f(q)=M+3qS-qO=0.                                      (1)

Indeed h_1=(-q(S+O)-M,0,-2s(O-S)) and h_3 is its z-reflection.
Equation (1) gives h_i=2(O-S)x_i for i=1,3. Also
h_2=(L+2qM)x_2. Normalizing by the positive row sums does not change
stationarity. These identities give exactly

    alpha_1=alpha_3=2(O-S), alpha_2=L+2qM.                 (2)

The certificate proves f(19/1000)>0, f(191/10000)<0, and

    f'(q)=2M+3S+36q^2 S+(4q^2-1)O < 0

throughout the closed interval. Continuity and the intermediate value
theorem give a unique root in its interior. Its s is strictly positive;
q is neither zero nor one. The three stated unit vectors are distinct
and not collinear, and the two pair directions are not antipodal.

## Full tangent Hessian and attraction

Use the aligned interaction energy

    E(X)=(1/(2 beta)) sum_ij exp(beta x_i^T V x_j).

Its product-metric gradient has components P_i h_i; normalized attention
is the same gradient ascent under the positive metric
g_X(U,U)=sum_i Z_i |u_i|^2, Z_i=sum_j W_ij. This identity is the
known aligned variational structure from Geshkovski, Letrouit,
Polyanskiy and Rigollet, arXiv:2312.10794 Section 3.4.

At a critical point, geodesic differentiation for tangent U gives

    Hess E[U,U] = sum_ij W_ij u_i^T V u_j
                 -sum_i alpha_i |u_i|^2
                 +(beta/2)sum_ij W_ij
                  (u_i^T V x_j + x_i^T V u_j)^2.         (3)

Both ordered pairs and self-indices are included. The last term follows
by differentiating each exponential twice; the first two follow from
the mixed score derivative and the spherical geodesic acceleration
x_i''=-|u_i|^2 x_i. The factor 1/(2 beta) cancels the two symmetric
mixed-score contributions to give the first term in (3).

Use the following orthonormal tangent basis, each vector supported on
only the indicated token, in this order:

    (s,0,-q) at token 1; (0,0,1) at token 2;
    (s,0,q) at token 3; e2 at token 1; e2 at token 2; e2 at token 3.

The program evaluates the symmetric bilinear matrix of (3), using (2)
only at the unique root. Interval evaluation encloses that matrix for
the root without substituting an approximate root. It then computes
an interval LDL^T factorization of minus the Hessian. Every diagonal
pivot interval is strictly positive; the six lower endpoints exceed,
respectively, the integers

    106, 5, 78, 109, 3, 102.

The exact endpoints and all 36 entry intervals are in
logs/offaxis_certificate.json. The script additionally verifies a simpler
certificate: for D=diag(1,2,1,1,1,1), B=D(-H)D has positive diagonal
and strictly positive lower bounds for every diagonal-dominance margin
B_ii-sum_{j!=i}|B_ij|. Indeed, using 2|z_i z_j|<=z_i^2+z_j^2 gives
z^T B z >= sum_i (B_ii-sum_{j!=i}|B_ij|)z_i^2>0 for z!=0.
Thus negative definiteness can also be checked without the LDL routine.
Interval LDL^T encloses the exact
algebraic factorization entry by entry; each division is by an interval
bounded away from zero. Positive exact pivots imply that minus the
Hessian is positive definite. Thus the Hessian is negative definite
in all six tangent directions, not merely in the scalar ansatz.

At a critical point the normalized-flow linearization is G^{-1}H,
where G is the positive metric matrix and H the energy Hessian.
It is similar to the symmetric negative-definite matrix
G^{-1/2}H G^{-1/2}. All eigenvalues are strictly negative. The smooth
ODE linearization theorem gives a hyperbolic attracting equilibrium
and an open basin. Every nonempty open subset of (S^2)^3 has positive
product Riemannian volume.

## Persistence: an open family, including non-gradient models

In a fixed product of local sphere charts near the equilibrium, the
row-normalized vector field depends analytically on the entries of
A=Q^T K, on symmetric V, and on beta>0. Its state Jacobian at the
certified point is invertible. The implicit function theorem continues
the equilibrium to a neighborhood of (V0,V0,2). Eigenvalues of the
state Jacobian depend continuously as an unordered set, so their real
parts remain negative after shrinking the neighborhood. Distinctness
and noncollinearity of the three token directions are open conditions,
as is signature (2,1) of V. Shrink the neighborhood again to preserve
all three properties. This gives a positive-volume basin for each
parameter in an open family, without invoking a Lyapunov function
for the perturbed, possibly unaligned system. Any real A is realizable
as Q^T K by taking Q=I and K=A.

## Reproducible arithmetic and truncation bounds

Run from the worker folder:

    python -X utf8 T323/scripts/certify_offaxis.py

The script uses only Python's standard library, with integer and
Fraction arithmetic. Each interval endpoint is an integer multiple of
2^-96. Addition is exact on that grid; multiplication and division use
integer floor and ceiling on all relevant endpoint combinations.
Squaring handles zero-crossing intervals. Square root uses integer
isqrt at the scaled endpoints with an explicit ceiling correction.

To enclose exp(x), the script first evaluates each rational endpoint
after exact repeated halving until |t|<=1/4. It uses the Taylor
polynomial of degree N=24 and the rigorous error

    R <= |t|^(N+1) / ((N+1)! (1-|t|)).

This is the Lagrange remainder with exp(|t|)<=1/(1-|t|), the latter
following termwise from the exponential and geometric series. All
polynomial and remainder calculations use exact Fractions. The two
rational bounds are rounded outward to the dyadic grid, then squared
with outward rounding once per halving. Monotonicity of exp combines
the two endpoint enclosures. No floating-point comparison enters a
certificate assertion. The script also performs 55 arithmetic checks
against exact rational operations and elementary exact containments.
Its SHA256 is included in the certificate log. The LDL routine also
accepts a known positive-definite 2 by 2 matrix and rejects an indefinite
one as explicit controls, included in the 55 checks.

## Scope and provenance

The earlier floating-point trajectory locates the candidate only;
it is not used as a proof of a bound. The exact certificate and analytic
reduction establish the claimed equilibrium independently of that run.
Kuehn-Yoon arXiv:2604.26085 Theorem 5.2 concerns pure-mode equilibria
x_i=s_i e_p and does not directly describe this three-direction state.
The identity synchronization theorems do not apply to this indefinite
V. The known gradient metric and elementary persistence theorems are
not claimed as new. Altafini, arXiv:2511.11553, Section 5 Remark 6,
PDF p22, reports clustering attractors in simulations and explicitly
leaves their analytical stability unverified. This result is an exact
stability certificate for a specific open parameter family; multistability
and clustering attractors were already observed in that paper.
Altafini's newer arXiv:2610.13518 Theorem 2, PDF p8, treats a discrete-time
model and gives stability criteria for consensus and bipartite equilibria.
Its Proposition 1 characterizes existence of the clustering class
implicitly; it does not supply this continuous-time three-direction
certificate. Priority remains bounded by the recorded searches and
subject to specialist review. No assertion of an almost-everywhere
classification of all initial configurations is made.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:63d418c01a16816e641210447ff5648026d7371deb90ea60869cee1c14527401","revision_digest":"sha256:6e62f610bdea54cccad7eca1890ecf26cc98ef0664d9acca4a7d07411a41bcdd","source_id":"owner:w696:T323-OFFAXIS-001-v2","source_revision":"v2; proof (unaudited); scripts/certify_offaxis.py and logs/offaxis_certificate.json","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 3 (Lower-tail bound for weighted Bernoulli sums) of arXiv:2608.18392, 'On Samuels' Conjecture'] Let $T := \sum_{i=1}^nw_iB_i$, where $B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_i)$ independently, $0\leq p_i \leq1$ and $0\leq w_i\leq1$. Let $0<a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_n$ satisfy $w_ip_i\leq a_i$. Assume
\begin{equation}
d := 1-\mathbb{E}T = 1-\sum_{i=1}^nw_ip_i >0.
\end{equation}
For $1\leq i\leq n$, write $C_i := \sum_{j=i}^na_j$.
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}(T<1)
\geq
\min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{a_j}{d+C_i} \right).

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lower-tail bound for weighted Bernoulli sums

[Thm main-SPDE-thm-2 of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Suppose (sass-A of the paper)-(SPDE-lyap of the paper) hold when $x_t$ is written as $(u_t,z_t)$ where $u_t = (x_t)_i$ for all $i = 1,\dots,d$. Consider the processes 
    $(r_i(t),v_i(t),x_{-i}(t),\theta) = (\|(x_t)_i\|_{L^1}, (x_t)_i/\|(x_t)_i\|_{L^1}, x_{-i}(t),\theta)$ (where $x_{-i}$ is the vector with $i$th coordinate omitted) on
    
    $$
    \mathcal{M}^{(i)} = [0,\infty) \times \{x \in C(\overline D)_+ \mid \|x_1\|_{L^1} = 1\} \times \Theta
    $$
    with invariant set $\mathcal{M}_0^{(i)} = \mathcal{M}_0^{(i)} \cap \{r_i = 0\}$. 
    Define  $\phi_i: \mathcal{M}^{(i)} \to C(\overline D)_+ \times \Theta$ with $\phi_i(r_i,v_i,x_{-i},\theta) = (x,\theta)$, where $x$ is obtained from  $x_{-i}$ by inserting $r_iv_i$ to $i$th coordinate. Furthermore, we set
    $$\mathcal{M}^* \coloneqq C(\overline D)_+ \times \Theta \,, \quad \mathcal{M}_0^* \coloneqq \{x \in C(\overline D)_+ \mid x_i = 0 \text{ for some } i=1,\dots,d\} \times \Theta \,.$$
    For each choice of $i=1,\dots,d$ and $\mu \in P_{inv}(\mathcal{M}_0^*)$ with $\mu(\{x_i = 0\}) = 1$ define
    \begin{equation}
        r_i(\mu) \coloneqq \inf_{\nu \in P_{inv}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(i)}), \phi_i^*\nu = \mu} \mu (\ip{v}{\tilde e_i} + \ip{\tilde F_i(r,v,z)}{1_i} - \frac{1}{2}\|\tilde G_i(r,v,z)^*1_i\|_U^2)
    \end{equation}
    (here $\phi_i^*\nu$ is the pushforward of the measure $\nu$, i.e. $\phi_i^*\nu(A) = \nu(\phi_i^{-1}(A))$). For arbitrary $\mu \in P_{inv}(\mathcal{M}_0^*)$, we write $\mu = p\mu_1 + (1-p)\mu_2$ for some $p \in [0,1]$ and $\mu_1,\mu_2 \in P_{inv}(\mathcal{M}_0^*)$ satisfying $\mu_1(\{x_i = 0\}) = 1$ and $\mu_2(\{x_i = 0\}) = 0$, and then define $r_i(\mu) \coloneqq pr_i(\mu_1)$ (this is possible because $\{x_i = 0\}$ is an invariant set).

    
    If $\max_{i = 1,\dots,m} r_i(\mu) > 0$ for all $\mu \in P_{inv}(\mathcal{M}_0^*)$ then $x_t$ is stochastically persistent in the sense of (main of the paper) (with $\mathcal{M}_+ = \mathcal{M}^* \setminus \mathcal{M}_0^*$ and $X_t = (x_t,\theta)$).

[Definition def:cert of arXiv:2607.05226, 'The Exact Worst-Case Tail Probability under Bounded Kurtosis'] Let $S=[t,\infty)$ (one-sided) or $S=\{|x|\ge t\}$ (two-sided). A \emph{certificate}
for the bound $\mathbb{P}(X\in S)\le B$ over $\mathcal{C}(\kappa)$ is a polynomial in the moment monomials of
$\mathcal{C}(\kappa)$,
\[
q(x)\;=\;\lambda_0 + \lambda_1 x + \lambda_2 x^2 + \lambda_4 x^4,
\qquad \lambda_4\ge 0,
\]
together with sum-of-squares data witnessing the two pointwise inequalities
\begin{align}
q(x) &\;\ge\; 0 \quad\text{for all } x\in\mathbb{R}, \\
q(x) &\;\ge\; 1 \quad\text{for all } x\in S, 
\end{align}
such that $B=\lambda_0+\lambda_2+\lambda_4\kappa$. We call the certificate
\emph{degree-$4$} when $\lambda_4>0$ and \emph{degree-$2$} when $\lambda_4=0$; these are
the only two kinds. Only \emph{constrained} moments carry
multipliers: the coefficient of $x^3$ is zero because $\mathbb{E} X^3$ is not constrained in $\mathcal{C}(\kappa)$,
and $\lambda_4\geq 0$ because (A3) is an inequality in the direction $\le\kappa$.
For (equation eq:cert-event of the paper) on $[t,\infty)$ we use the exact Markov--Luk\'acs form
$q-1=\sigma_0+(x-t)\,\sigma_1$ with $\sigma_0,\sigma_1$ sums of squares; (equation eq:cert-glob of the paper)
is an explicit sum of squares. Such data make the two inequalities checkable by expanding
polynomial identities and verifying positive semidefiniteness of small Gram matrices;
no analysis is required.

body:
[Defn d:ssm-pp of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] The Gibbs spin model~(equation eqn:gibbs of the paper) satisfies {\em averaged weak spatial mixing} on the graph $\Psi = \Psi(\cdot)$ with respect to the input process $\mathcal{P}$ if
the following conditions hold: 
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]

\item  for any finite subset ${\cal X } \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, there exists a spatial mixing function 
$\mathcal{A}_{\Psi({\cal X })}: 2^{\cal X } \times 2^{\cal X } \to [0, \infty)$ 
such that   
\begin{equation} 
d_{\textnormal{TV}} \big( \mathcal{L}(V_{{\cal X }''} \mid V_{\partial {\cal X }'} = \v_{\partial {\cal X }'}),  
\mathcal{L}(V_{{\cal X }''} \mid V_{\partial {\cal X }'} = {z}_{\partial {\cal X }'}) \big)  
\leq \mathcal{A}_{\Psi({\cal X })}({\cal X }'', \partial {\cal X }'),
\end{equation}  
for all subsets ${\cal X }'' \subset {\cal X }' \subset {\cal X }$ and boundary conditions $\v_{\partial {\cal X }'}, {z}_{\partial {\cal X }'}\in \mathbb{K}^{\partial {\cal X }'}$, and 
\vskip.2cm
\item   
for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$ the functions 

\begin{equation} 
\mathfrak{a}_p(k):=\sup_{B \in {\cal B}_b} \sup_{x_1,\ldots, x_p\in B}  
\mathbb {E} _{\bk x1p} \big[\mathcal{A}_{\Psi(\mathcal{P} \cap B)} (\bk x1p, \partial \mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p))\big],  \ \  k \in \mathbb{N},
\end{equation}  

are fast decreasing as \( k \to \infty \).  
Here, \(\mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p) = \bigcup_{i=1}^p \mathfrak{B}_k(x_i)\) and the boundary $\partial$ of \(\mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p)\) is again with respect to~\(\Psi(\mathcal{P} \cap B)\);
${\cal B}_b$ are the bounded Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$. 
We  assume that the mapping $((\mathbb{R}^d)^p,\hat\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d}})\owns(\bk x1p,\tilde\mu)=(\bk x1p,\Psi(\mu)) \mapsto \mathcal{A}_{\Psi}(\bk x1p,\partial^\Psi\mathfrak{B}_k(\bk x1p))\in\mathbb{R}$ is measurable for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Without loss of generality, we assume that $\mathfrak{a}_p$ are increasing in $p$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Averaged weak spatial mixing of the Gibbs spin model on a random spatial  graph

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2512.05340, 'The rate of convergence of the critical mean-field $O(N)$ magnetization via multivariate n'] Suppose $V$ satisfies Assumption \ref{assumption: assumptions on V}, and let $\mu$ have Lebesgue density proportional to
  $e^{-V}$.
  Let $W,W'$ be identically distributed $\RR^d$-valued random variables, defined on the same probability space, such that if $\delta:=W'-W$ then
  $W$ and $\delta\delta^\transpose$ are both integrable. 
  Let $\sF\supseteq\sigma(W)$ be a $\sigma$-algebra, let $\lambda>0$, and define $R_1$ and $R_2$ so that
    \begin{equation}
      \mathbb{E}[\delta|\mathcal{F}] = \lambda(-\grad V(W) + R_{1}),
      
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{equation}
      \mathbb{E}\left[\delta\,\delta^{\transpose}\big|\mathcal{F}\right] = 2\lambda(\id + R_{2}).
      
    \end{equation}
    Then there exists a constant $C\in(0,\infty)$ such that
    \begin{equation}
      d(\sL(W),\mu)
      \leq C\left\lbrace \frac{1}{\lambda}\mathbb{E} [|\delta|^{3}(|\log|\delta|| \vee 1)] + \mathbb{E}|R_{1}|
      + \sqrt{d}\,\mathbb{E}\,\|R_{2}\| \right\rbrace. 
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2512.05340

body: [Proposition 14 of arXiv:2512.10761, 'Special times for the point set process of the Brownian Net'] If $z=(x,t)$ is a $C_n$ point and $\pi\in\mathcal{N}$ is an incoming path at $z$. [Lemma lem:root_declumping of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Set $\pi_n=\P(G_{k_n}(\mathcal T)=1)$ and
$\widehat{\pi}_n=\P(\widehat{G}_{k_n}(\mathcal T)=1)$.
Set
$$
b_B=\P\bigl(k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)\in B,\
k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)\ge1\bigr)>0.
$$
Then $\widehat\pi_n\ge b_B\pi_n$ for every $n \geq 1$. In addition:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]  If $(n\pi_n)$ is bounded, then $
n\widehat{\pi}_n-c_B n\pi_n\to0$.
\item[(ii)] If $n\pi_n\to\infty$, then $n\widehat{\pi}_n\to\infty$.
\item[(iii)] Finally, if $(G_k)$ satisfies Assumption (hyp:S of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with
respect to $(M_n)$, then $(\widehat G_k)$ satisfies Assumption (hyp:M of the paper)
along $(k_n)$ with respect to the same cutoff.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2607.26254, 'A Simple Model of Sea Spray'] Suppose, $\mathcal{F}(dr)=\mathcal{F}(r) dr$ and $ \mathcal{F}(r)$ is strictly positive on a finite interval $[r_{min},r_{max}]$ and equal to zero otherwise. Suppose $r\to\zeta(r)$ is continuous on $[r_{min},r_{max}]$ and $(t,r)\to (r_t,z_t(r))$ is continuous on,  

$$
A=\{\,(t,r)\mid0\leq t\leq \zeta(r),\,\,  r_{min}\leq r\leq r_{max},\,\}.
$$

\mpar
Finally, suppose $m$ is a continuous function of $z.$ Then,
$$
z_{100}=\max_{(r,t)\in A} z_t(r).
$$
\begin{proof}
Let $z^{**}=\max_{(t,r)\in A} z_t(r).$ Note that  $z_{100}\leq z^{**}$ since no droplet ever exceeds this height. Suppose, on the other hand, that $w< z^{**}.$ Since $z$ is a continuous function and $A$ is a closed set, $z$ attains its maximum value, hence  $z_t(r)>w$  for all $(t,r)$ in an open subset of $A.$ In particular, there is an interval $[a,b]\subset [r_{min}, r_{max}]$ such that,
$$
\int_0^\infty r_t^31_{(0,w]}(z_t(r))dt  < \int_0^\infty r^3_t1_{(0,z_{100}]}(z_t(r))dt
$$
for all $r\in [a,b]$. Thus,
\begin{align*}
m(w) & = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi\rho   \int_0^\infty \negthickspace \int_0^\infty r^3_s\, 1_{(0,w]}(z_s(r))\mathcal{F}(dr) ds\\
& <\tfrac{4}{3}\pi\rho   \int_0^\infty \negthickspace \int_0^\infty r^3_s\, 1_{(0,z_{100}]}(z_s(r))\mathcal{F}(dr) ds\\
& = m(z_{100}),
\end{align*}
since $\mathcal{F}(r)$ is strictly positive on $[a,b].$ By continuity this implies,
$$
m(z^{**})=\lim_{z\to z^{**}}m(z)\leq m(z_{100}),
$$
and because $m$ is non-decreasing, we have $z^{**}\leq z_{100}$ which proves the result.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

UNREVIEWED ELEMENTARY OBSTRUCTION. On a finite graph with marked a!=b and x>0, the law proportional to x^length conditioned on length n is uniform over n-edge a-to-b paths, but its marginal is a mixture over n. On the hexagon C6 with adjacent a,b, its short-path probability is 1/(1+x^4), whereas the uniform length-1 law assigns probability 1. Thus the ensembles differ at finite scale. This proves neither inequivalence nor equivalence of their scaling limits; an explicit transfer estimate remains needed. The rooted P0003 law also leaves its endpoint free.

Ma, Wang, Chi and Chen, Implicit Regularization in Nonconvex Statistical Estimation, arXiv:1711.10467v3, Lemmas 1-2, PDF p24. Let a_j be independent N(0,I_n), fix a deterministic unit signal x_*, put y_j=(a_j^T x_*)^2 and f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_j ((a_j^T x)^2-y_j)^2. Fix a sufficiently small absolute constant C1>0 and sufficiently large absolute constants C2,c0. If m>=c0 n log n, then on a simultaneous event of probability at least 1-O(m n^(-10)), every point x with ||x-x_*||<=2C1 and max_j |a_j^T(x-x_*)|<=C2 sqrt(log n) satisfies ||x-eta grad f(x)-x_*||<=(1-eta/2)||x-x_*|| whenever 0<eta<=1/[5C2(10+C2)log n]. The event is uniform in x, so the point may depend on the samples. This is an absolute projection bound for unit signal, not the relative-error bound C2 sqrt(log n)||x-x_*||. The cited statement does not replace n log n samples by alpha n or by itself preserve the region along a trajectory.

body: [Lemma lem:lf-covariance of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] For $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, set $\Delta_\alpha:=\frac{\alpha}{2}(Q-\frac{\alpha}{2})$. Let $(\alpha_i,z_i)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{H}$ and $(\beta_j,s_j)\in\mathbb{R}\times\partial\mathbb{H}$ for $i=1,...,m$ and $j = 1,...,n$. Suppose $f:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{H}$ is a conformal map, such that $f(s_j)\neq\infty$ for all $j$. Then $$\mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb{H}}^{(\alpha_i,f(z_i))_i,(\beta_j,f(s_j))_j} = \prod_{i=1}^m\prod_{j=1}^n|f'(z_i)|^{-2\Delta_{\alpha_i}}|f'(s_j)|^{-\Delta_{\beta_j}}f_*\mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb{H}}^{(\alpha_i,z_i)_i,(\beta_j,s_j)_j}. $$

[Lemma 26 (Fixed-$\delta$ elliptic auxiliary identities) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Fix $\delta>0$.  Let $h_\delta$ and $h_\delta^*$ be the hitting committors in
\eqref{eq:committors}.  There exists a finite positive Borel measure
$\eta_{\eps,\delta}$ supported on $\partial A$ such that, for every
$\varphi\in C^2(\partial A)$ and every admissible extension $\Phi$,
\begin{equation}
    \int_{\partial A}\varphi d\eta_{\eps,\delta}
    =
    \int_{\calD}h_\delta^*(z)
    \left(-\calL_{\eps,\delta}\Phi\right)(z) \pi^\eps(dz).
\end{equation}
If $\psi\in C^2(\overline\calD)$ satisfies
\[
    \psi=1\quad\text{near }\overline A,
    \qquad
    \psi=0\quad\text{near }\overline B\cup\partial\calD,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    \Cap_{\eps,\delta}(A,B;\calD):=\eta_{\eps,\delta}(\partial A)
    =
    \int_{\calD}h_\delta^*
    \left(-\calL_{\eps,\delta}\psi\right) d\pi^\eps.
\end{equation}
For every $M<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
    \int_{\partial A}g_{\delta,M} d\eta_{\eps,\delta}
    =
    \int_{\calD}h_\delta^*F_{\delta,M} d\pi^\eps.

[Ppn 138 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If $\psi:\bbR^{d_1}\to\bbR^{d_2}$ is Lipschitz, then $\psi$ preserves $\bbW_2$ convergence.
If $d_1=2,d_2=1$ and $\psi(X,Y)=XY$, then $\psi$ preserves $\bbW_2$ convergence for sequences on which $X$ is uniformly bounded.

\begin{proof}
The first statement follows because $L$-Lipschitz maps increase $\bbW_2$ distances by at most a factor of $L$.
For the second statement, suppose 
$X_N\to X$ and $Y_N\to Y$ in $L^2$, with $|X_N|\leq C$ almost surely for all $N$. 
We will argue that this implies $X_NY_N\to XY$ in $L^2$, and the assertion then follows. First,
the uniform bound on $X_N$ gives
  \[
  \E\Big[(X_NY_N-X_NY)^2\Big]
  \le C^2 \E\Big[(Y_N-Y)^2\Big]
  = o_N(1)\,,
  \]
so $X_NY_N$ and $X_NY$ are close in $L^2$. For $T$ growing sufficiently slowly with $N$, we then bound
  \[
  \E\Big[ (X_NY-XY)^2\Big]
  \le T^2\E\Big[ (X_N-X)^2\Big]
  + 4C^2\E\Big[Y^2; |Y| \ge T\Big]
  \le T^2 o_N(1) + o_T(1)\,,
  \]
where the last term is because $Y^2\in L^1$. Therefore $X_NY$ converges to $XY$ in $L^2$, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Ppn 138 of arXiv:2608.29416

Let G be a finite connected undirected graph on n>=2 vertices with holding transitions permitted, and let C be the set of symmetric entrywise nonnegative stochastic matrices supported on its allowed edges and diagonal. Write J=11^T/n and mu(P)=||P-J||_op, the second-largest eigenvalue modulus. There exists an optimal minimizer of mu on C invariant under all graph automorphisms. In fact, if P_star is any minimizer, averaging Q P_star Q^T over permutation matrices Q representing Aut(G) gives an invariant minimizer. Its off-diagonal transition probabilities are constant on each edge orbit. This optimizes real transition weights on a fixed support; averaging integral matchings need not produce an integral matching. [Theorem 29 (Spectral approximation) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:local-wp}, fix a compact
$K\Subset\R^3$ and the fixed localization pair
$(\chi_K^\circ,\rho_K^\circ)$ from
\eqref{eq:reference-localization-and-lifetime}.  Denote the corresponding solution of the localized auxiliary system and its
fixed-point variables by
$(u^\circ,v^\circ,\mathcal N^\circ,Z^\circ)$, and denote their
finite-cutoff counterparts by
$(u_\Lambda^\circ,v_\Lambda^\circ,
  \mathcal N_\Lambda^\circ,Z_\Lambda^\circ)$.
Their restrictions to the backward cone $\mathcal Q_{K,T}$ represent the
local fields and source.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.45em]
\item \emph{Fixed-profile dyadic cutoffs.}
For every fixed-profile dyadic cutoff there is an event $\Omega_K^\circ$ of
probability one, which may depend on the chosen profile, such that, for every $\omega\in\Omega_K^\circ$ and every
$T<\tau_K(\omega)$, the finite-cutoff fixed point exists for all sufficiently
large dyadic $\Lambda$ and
\begin{align}
  Z_\Lambda^\circ&\longrightarrow Z^\circ
  &&\text{in }\mathcal Z_T,
  \\
  \bigl(\chi_K(u_\Lambda^\circ-u^\circ),
  \chi_K(v_\Lambda^\circ-v^\circ)\bigr)
  &\longrightarrow0
  &&\text{in }C([0,T];\mathcal D'(\R^3))^2
  
\end{align}
for every $\chi_K\in C_c^\infty(\R^3)$ equal to one near $K$.  The three source terms converge in the topology
\eqref{eq:nonlinear-source-topology}.  If
$\eta_K\in C_c^\infty(\R^3)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \eta_K\equiv1\ \text{near }K,
 \qquad \eta_K\chi_K^\circ=\eta_K,
\end{equation}
then
\[
 \eta_Ku_\Lambda^\circ v_\Lambda^\circ
 \longrightarrow \eta_K\mathcal N^\circ
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'((0,T)\times\R^3).
\]

\item \emph{Arbitrary admissible cofinal cutoffs.}
Let $(\pi_{\Lambda_n})_{n\ge1}$ be an admissible cofinal cutoff sequence and
let $T\in(0,1]$ be deterministic.  There are Borel events
$\mathcal A_{n,T}^K$ and strongly measurable $\mathcal Z_T$-valued random
variables $Z_{n,T}^\circ$ whose restriction to $\mathcal A_{n,T}^K$ is the
finite-cutoff fixed point.  If $Z_T^\circ$ denotes the strongly measurable
restriction of $Z^\circ$ to $[0,T]$ on $\{T<\tau_K\}$, then
$(\mathcal A_{n,T}^K,Z_{n,T}^\circ)$ converges to $Z_T^\circ$ in probability
on $\{T<\tau_K\}$ in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:partial-probability-convergence}.  The same conclusion
holds for every continuous seminorm on
$C([0,T];\mathcal D'(\R^3))^2$ and for the source norms in
\eqref{eq:nonlinear-source-topology}.
\end{enumerate}

For any other fixed localization pair $(\chi,\rho)$ adapted to $(K,1)$,
the same conclusions hold on its existence interval, and the limiting fields
and source agree with those obtained from the fixed pair
$(\chi_K^\circ,\rho_K^\circ)$ on every common interval. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Spectral approximation

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $\mathcal{R}:=\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}^d}$ be the set of all real-valued sequences on $\mathbb{N}^d$.
Equipped with pointwise addition $+$ and the convolution product $*$ in \eqref{eq:conv}, $(\mathcal{R},+,*)$ is a commutative ring
with unity. The identity element (unit) is the sequence $\ez$ defined by

\[
\ez(k)=
\begin{cases}
1, & k=0_d,\\
0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

If there exists $b:\mathbb{N}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $a*b=b*a=\ez$, then $a$ is \emph{convolutionally invertible} and $b$ is called
its \emph{convolutional inverse}, denoted by $a^{(-1)}$.

Moreover, the map $\Phi:\mathcal{R}\to \mathbb{R}[[x_1,\ldots,x_d]]$ defined by $\Phi(a)=P_a$ is a ring isomorphism. In particular,
for all $a,b\in\mathcal{R}$,
\[
P_{a+b}(x_{1:d})=P_a(x_{1:d})+P_b(x_{1:d}),\ \
P_{a*b}(x_{1:d})=P_a(x_{1:d})\,P_b(x_{1:d}),\ \
P_{\ez}(x_{1:d})=1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 9.1 of arXiv:2503.23159, 'Hall's marriage theorem'] A sufficient condition for a family A of hypergraphs to have an SDR is that, for every subfamily B of A, there is a matching M in S B which cannot be pinned by fewer than |B| disjoint edges from S B. If each edge in each hypergraph is a singleton, the hypothesis reduces to that of Hall’s theorem (each hypergraph can be represented as a set, the union of its singleton edges), and the conclusion is the same as Hall’s.
title: Theorem 9.1 of arXiv:2503.23159: Hall's marriage theorem

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.30166, 'Square Functions and Rectifiability\\ under Monotone Transformations of the Density'] Let $\mu$ be an $n$-AD-regular measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with constant $c_0$ and
$\mu(\mathbb{R}^d)=\infty$. Let $F\colon(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Borel function and
bi-Lipschitz on $J_0$ with constant $\lambda$. Then $\mu$ is uniformly $n$-rectifiable if and only if
there exists a constant $c$ such that, for any ball $B(x_0,R)$ centered at $\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$,
\begin{equation}
\int_0^R\!\!\int_{x\in B(x_0,R)} |\Delta^F_\mu(x,r)|^2\, d\mu(x)\,\frac{dr}{r}
\;\le\; c\,R^n.
\end{equation}
Quantitatively: if (equation eq:carleson of the paper) holds with constant $c'$ then
(equation eq:carlesonF of the paper) holds with constant $\lambda^2 c'$, and if (equation eq:carlesonF of the paper)
holds with constant $c$ then (equation eq:carleson of the paper) holds with constant $\lambda^2 c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.30166

[Proposition balancing_l1 of arXiv:2506.20932, 'Thinning to improve two-sample discrepancy'] Consider any vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_m \in \mathbb{R}^{N}$. There is an online algorithm 
to choose \(\varepsilon_1, \ldots, \varepsilon_m = \pm 1\) so that the running sums satisfy
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E \sup_k \left\| \sum_{i = 1}^{k} \varepsilon_i v_i \right\|_{\infty} 
\leq 2 \sup_i \|v_i\|_1 \left[ 
3 + \log_2 \left(
1 + \frac{\sum_i \|v_i\|_1}{2 \sup_i \|v_i\|_1}
\right)
\right]
= O\bigl(\sup_i \|v_i\|_1 \log m\bigr).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma l:DirIntESA of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] Let~$\zeta\mapsto \big({A_\zeta,D_\zeta}\big)$ be a measurable field of closable operators.
Then, $(A,D)$~is essentially self-adjoint on~$H$ if and only if~$(A_\zeta, D_\zeta)$ is essentially self-adjoint on~$H_\zeta$ for $\nu$-a.e.~$\zeta\in Z$.
\begin{proof}
Assume~$(A_\zeta, D_\zeta)$ is essentially self-adjoint for $\nu$-a.e.~$\zeta\in Z$.
Then, respectively by~[Lan75] for the closure, by the assumption, and again by~[Lan75] for the adjunction
\[
\overline{A}=\dint{Z} \overline{A_\zeta} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\nu(\zeta) = \dint{Z} A_\zeta^* \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\nu(\zeta) = A^* \,\mathrm{.}
\]
The converse implication follows in a similar way.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l:DirIntESA of arXiv:2411.14936
See \cite{Dhar1991,Majumdar1992,Jarai2014minimal}.

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered.
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows

[Definition def:iota-adj of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Choose one side of $T_i$ in $M$. Choose a small collar neighbourhood on that side and identify it with $T_i \times [0, 1]$ (such that $T_i = T_i \times \{ 0 \}$). We get a map (independent of the choice of collar neighbourhood and identification)
\[
\iota_i \colon \pi_1 \Diff^+(T_i) \rightarrow \pi_0 \Diff^+_{T_i \times \{ 0, 1 \} }(T_i \times [0, 1]) \rightarrow \pi_0 \overline{\Diff}^+(M,(B_h),(T_i),(M_j))
\]
by taking the adjunction and extending a diffeomorphism of $T_i \times [0, 1]$ by the identity on $M \setminus T_i \times [0, 1]$.
title: Definition def:iota-adj of arXiv:2609.00233

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: H^s(R^n) embeds into L^∞(R^n) ∩ C^0 only for s > n/2, strictly; the borderline s = n/2 is excluded. Concrete counterexample, n = 2 (s = 1): u(x) = log log(1/|x|) for 0 < |x| < e^{−1}, extended by 0. Then ∫|∇u|² = 2π ∫_0^{e^{−1}} dr / ( r log²(1/r) ) = 2π < ∞ and ∫ u² < ∞, so u ∈ H¹(R²), yet u is unbounded at the origin. General n: choose f with f̂(ξ) = (1+|ξ|)^{−n} (log(2+|ξ|))^{−1} ≥ 0; then ∫ (1+|ξ|²)^{n/2}|f̂|² dξ < ∞ (radially, ∫ dρ/(ρ log²ρ) converges) so f ∈ H^{n/2}(R^n), while ∫ f̂ dξ = ∞ (∫ dρ/(ρ log ρ) diverges); since f̂ ≥ 0, an L^∞ bound on f would force ∫ f̂ < ∞ (test against a Gaussian approximate identity with positive Fourier transform and use monotone convergence), so f ∉ L^∞. Consequences: an energy-critical argument may not conclude a pointwise bound from the energy norm; ‖u‖_{L^q_t L^∞_x} estimates at the critical regularity generally require Besov spaces, since Ḃ^{n/2}_{2,1} embeds into L^∞ while H^{n/2} does not. This is the same phenomenon that makes the Lebesgue-space wave Strichartz estimates carry the restriction r < ∞ (the Littlewood–Paley summation of the dyadic blocks needs r < ∞, and at r = ∞ one lands in Besov spaces). The failure of the endpoints (q,r) = (2,∞) — Schrödinger in n = 2, wave in n = 3 — is a separate matter, proved by explicit counterexamples of Montgomery-Smith and of Klainerman–Machedon, not a corollary of this embedding failure.
title: Pitfall: H^{n/2} Does Not Embed in L^∞ (the Critical Sobolev Endpoint Fails)

[Lemma ex:finite-perturbation of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, and connected graph, and fix $o\in V$. For $m>0$ consider the configuration $\sigma(v)=1+m\,\mathbf{1}_{\{v=o\}}$.
		Then for every $x\in V$ and $n\geq 0$, we have $u_n(x)=m g_n(x,o)$, and hence $u_\infty(x)=m\,g(x,o)\in[0,\infty]$. In particular, $\sigma$ stabilizes if and only if the random walk on $G$ is transient. If the walk is recurrent, then $\sigma$ explodes.

body:
[Theorem 8 (Random regular graphs: pointwise version) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(d\ge 3\), \(u\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta\in\mathbb N\) with \(\theta>1\). Let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, with law \(p_{d,n}\). Assume
\[
d>2c_{\theta,u}
=
2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
\]
Then for every \(\delta>0\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(c>0\) such that for every
\[
t\ge T_{\theta,u}(d)+\delta,
\]
one has
\[
p_{d,n}\!\left(
\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Random regular graphs: pointwise version

body:
[Defn 5 of arXiv:2606.04636, 'A Thomson-type variational principle for diffusion coefficients'] $V_{0}$ is the space of admissible flows with vanishing
divergence, that we write formally as
\begin{equation}
V_{0}=\left\{ \phi\in\cH_{2}:\left\langle \div\phi,\div\phi\right\rangle =0\right\} .
\end{equation}
For $\phi\in\cH_{2}$, $\left\langle \div\phi,\div\phi\right\rangle =0$
should be understood by the completion under $\left\langle \cdot,\cdot\right\rangle $.
That is, there exists a sequence $(\phi_{n})_{n\in\N}$ of flows with
well defined divergence that converge in $\cH_{2}$ to $\phi$, such
that $\left\langle \div\phi_{n},\div\phi_{n}\right\rangle \xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0$.
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2606.04636

body:
[Prop 33 (Change of uniformizer) of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\pi$ and $\pi'$ be two uniformizers of $\sO_K$, and let $m\geq0$
satisfy $e\leq p^m$. Then there is a canonical natural equivalence
\[
T_{\pi,\pi'}^{(m)}\colon
R\Gamma_{\rm crys}
\bigl(
 \sX_{\OK^\pi}^{(m)} 
/\sO_K^\pi\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma_{\rm crys}
\bigl(
 \sX_{\OK^{\pi'}}^{(m)} 
/\sO_K^{\pi'}\bigr)
\]
such that
\[
\rho_{\pi',m}^{\rm int}
\simeq
T_{\pi,\pi'}^{(m)}\circ\rho_{\pi,m}^{\rm int}.
\]
These equivalences satisfy
\[
T_{\pi,\pi}^{(m)}=\id,
\qquad
T_{\pi',\pi''}^{(m)}\circ T_{\pi,\pi'}^{(m)}
\simeq
T_{\pi,\pi''}^{(m)}.
\]

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED.

[Cor GHProps of arXiv:2411.18563, 'Lower tails for triangles inside the critical window'] Under Condition~(ConditionThm1 of the paper), the following events hold wvhp with respect to $G \sim \mu_{\lambda,\zeta}$. Setting $\overline \Delta:=\mathbb{E}_{\lambda,\zeta} \Delta(G)$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item  $\delta(G) = (1+o(1))\Delta(G) =(1+o(1))\overline\Delta$,
\item $\alpha_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta}=(1+o(1))\alpha(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ for all $v\in V(G)$,
\item $\rho_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta}=(1+o(1))\rho(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ for all $v\in V(G)$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\mathbb{E}_{\lambda,\zeta}(\alpha_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta})=(1+o(1))\alpha(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\lambda,\zeta}(\rho_{G_v,\lambda,\zeta})=(1+o(1))\rho(\overline\Delta,\lambda,\zeta)$ for all $v\in V(G)$.
title: Cor GHProps of arXiv:2411.18563

[Lemma lem:break_loops of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] {amy-cle-resampling}}]

Suppose that $\Gamma$ is a nested ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa}${} in a simply connected domain $D$. For each $a\in(0,1)$, $b>0$ there exists $p > 0$ such that the following holds. 

Let $z\in D$ and $j_0\in\mathbf{Z}$ be such that $B(z,2^{-j_0})\subseteq D$. There exists a resampling $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ of $\Gamma$ within $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$ for each $j>j_0$ with the following property. Let $G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ be the event that
\begin{itemize}
 \item no loop in $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ crosses the annulus $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$,
 \item denoting $\mathcal {C}$ the loops in $\Gamma$ that cross $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$, the collection of loops of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ remain the same in each connected component of $\mathbf{C} \setminus \bigcup\mathcal {C}$ that is not surrounded by a loop in $\mathcal {C}$ and intersects $B(z,2^{-j})$, and the gasket of $\Gamma$ in these components is contained in the gasket of $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$, let $\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k}$ be the event that the number of $j=j_0+1,\ldots,j_0+k$ so that
\[ \mathbf{P}[ G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j} \,|\, \Gamma ] \geq p\]
is at least $(1-a)k$.  Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[(\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k})^c] = O(e^{-b k}) \]
where the implicit constant does not depend on $z,j_0,k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:regularityarea of arXiv:2607.19037, 'Semiclassical analysis for Yang--Mills \\ random connections on compact surfaces'] Let \(\gamma: [0,1]\to \Sigma\) be an oriented \(C^1\) curve such that, for all \(t\in [0,1]\), the scalar product
\[
\left\langle \gamma'(t), V^\perp(\gamma(t)) \right\rangle_{T_{\gamma(t)}\Sigma}
\]
has a constant sign. Denote by \(t_0\) the first time at which \(\gamma\) meets an unstable curve \(W^{u}(a)\), with \(a\in \mathrm{Crit}(f)_1\), and define
\[
\tau(t) = \ell\big(\gamma_{[t, t_0]}\big).
\]
Then \(\tau\) is strictly monotone and \(C^1\) for all \(t\) sufficiently close to \(t_0\), with \(t \le t_0\). For \(\delta>0\) small enough, the map
\[
[0,\delta]\ni \tau \mapsto \sigma\big(\angle(\gamma_{[t(\tau), t_0]})\big)
\]
belongs to \(C^{1-}\), where \(t(\tau)\) denotes the inverse function of \(t\mapsto \tau(t)\).

More precisely, as \(t\to t_0\), one has the asymptotic estimate
\begin{equation}
\sigma\big(\angle(\gamma_{[t, t_0]})\big) = \mathcal{O}\big(\tau(t)\log \tau(t)\big).
\end{equation}
In particular, the derivative \(\partial_t \sigma\big(\angle(\gamma_{[t, t_0]})\big)\) exhibits a logarithmic singularity in \(\tau\), namely
\[
\partial_t \sigma\big(\angle(\gamma_{[t, t_0]})\big) = \mathcal{O}\big(\log \tau(t)\big),
\]
and satisfies \(\partial_t \sigma\big(\angle(\gamma_{[t, t_0]})\big) \in L^p([0,t_0])\) for all \(1 \le p < \infty\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:regularityarea of arXiv:2607.19037

[Corollary 20 (Finite volume OZ for a single cluster boundary) of arXiv:2604.21669, 'Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts:\\ II. order-order interface convergence'] Let \(0<J<U\) satisfy \(\sinh 2J=e^{-2U}\). There exist \(c_0,c>0\) such that, for any sequence \(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{c_0}\geq k_n\geq c_0\ln(n)\), there exists\(n_0\geq 1\) such that for any \(n\geq n_0\), \(m_n \geq c_0n\), there exists a probability measure \(\tilde{\bndMeas}_n\) on \(\SetRootMarkBackCont \times \SetRootMarkForwCont\) satisfying
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \(\tilde{\bndMeas}_n\) is supported on pairs of simple paths \((\eta_L,\eta_R)\) with \(\norm{\displace(\eta_L)}_{\infty},\norm{\displace(\eta_R)}_{\infty} \leq k_n^2\),
		\item defining \(v(\eta_L,\eta_R) = v_R-v_L-\displace(\eta_L)-\displace(\eta_R)\), for any \(f\) function of \(\Gamma_+\),
		\begin{multline*}
			\Big|\sum_{m\geq 0}\sum_{\eta_L,\eta_R} \tilde{\bndMeas}_n(\eta_L,\eta_R) \tilde{\OZ}_{v(\eta_L,\eta_R)}^+\big[f(v_L + \eta_L\concatenate\bar{\eta}_1^M \concatenate \eta_R)\big]
			\\
			-\Phi_{n}\big[f(\Gamma_+)\bgiven v_R\in \calC\big]\Big|
			\leq
			\norm{f}_{\infty}e^{-ck_n},
		\end{multline*}where \(\eta_1^M \sim \tilde{\OZ}_{v(\eta_L,\eta_R)}^+\).
	\end{itemize}
	The same result holds for \(\calC',\Gamma_-, v_L',v_R'\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite volume OZ for a single cluster boundary

[Thm 27 of arXiv:2604.25725, 'What is The Probability That A Random Graph With A Given Degree Sequence is Connected?'] Let $H$ be a graph on $[n]$  such that $H$ is a possible subgraph on a graph with degree sequence $\cD$, and   $uv\not\in  E(H)$. Then,
\begin{multline*}
    \Cprob{ij \in E(G)}{H \subseteq G}\\
    \ge \left(1-\frac{2D^*+6d(n)}{2m-2|E(H)|}\right)\frac{(d(i)-d_H(i))(d(j)-d_H(j))}{2m-2|E(H)|+(d(i)-d_H(i))(d(j)-d_H(j))}.
\end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 27 of arXiv:2604.25725

[Prop 14 of arXiv:2604.03206, 'The extreme statistics of some noncolliding Brownian processes'] Let $a \in \R$ and $0 < s,t \leq T$ and $m \geq 1$. Set $M_b = \max_{y \in [0,T]} |b(y)|$.
    There is a constant $C = C_{a, T, M_b, m, \mu_i}$ such that for all $x \in \R$ and $y \geq a$,
    $$ |S_{m,-s} \cdot S^{hypo(b)}_{m,t}(u,v) | \leq e^{C(|x|+1)} (|y|^m + 1)e^{-\frac{y^2}{4T}}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 14 of arXiv:2604.03206

body:
[Prop brw+killing of arXiv:2608.13084, '\bf Branching random walk in random environment'] If $A$ is finite and connected subset in ${\mathbb Z}^d$ with $\#A\ge 2$, then for the branching random walk absorbed outside $A$, we have
\[
{\mathbb P}^{(A)}_x(Z_n \ge 1, \forall n\ge 0)>0, \forall x\in A,
\]
if and only if 
\begin{equation}
\left(\sum_k kp_k \right) \times \rho_A >1.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop brw+killing of arXiv:2608.13084

body:
[Prop consistency of arXiv:2412.04918, 'On one dimensional weighted Poincar\'e inequalities for Global Sensitivity Analysis'] Given $i \in \{ 1,\ldots, d \}$ and a finite interval $[a_i,b_i]$, we assume that $\mu_i \in \mathcal{P}(a_i,b_i)$ and that the main effect $f_i \in \mathscr{C}^{1,2}_{*}(a_i,b_i)$ satisfies $f'_i(a)\neq 0$ and  $f'_i(b)\neq 0$. Moreover we assume that $\frac{\partial f }{\partial x_i}(X)\in L^2 $. \\
Let $(X_1,\ldots, X^{(n)})$ be an i.i.d. sample generated from $X$ and consider an estimator $\widehat{f_i}$ constructed with respect to this sample. We assume the following (almost sure) hypothesis:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $\widehat{f_i}$ is centered with respect to $\mu_i$. 
\item[(ii)] $\widehat{f_i} \in \mathscr{C}^{1,2}_{*}(a_i,b_i)$ satisfies $\widehat{f_i} '(a)\neq 0$ and  $\widehat{f_i} '(b)\neq 0$. 
\item[(iii)] $\widehat{f_i}$ converges uniformly to $f_i $ on $[a_i,b_i]$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$.
\item[(iv)] $\widehat{f_i}'$ converges uniformly to $f_i '$ on $[a_i,b_i]$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$.
\end{itemize}
Then almost surely, the data-driven weight $\widehat{w_{i}}=w_{\widehat{f_i}}$ converges uniformly to $w_{f_i}$ on $[a_i,b_i]$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$. Moreover, the Monte-Carlo estimator 
\[
\widehat{\nu_{i}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n \widehat{w_{i}}(X_i^{(k)})\abs{\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(X^{(k)})}^2\]
converges almost surely to $\nu_{i,w_{f_i}}$ as $n\rightarrow \infty$.
title: Prop consistency of arXiv:2412.04918

[Conj 13 of arXiv:2603.00353, 'Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups'] Let $\Gamma=([n],w)$ be an arbitrary hypergraph with non-negative weights. Then $\lambda_{\min}^*(\Gamma,\kmp_2)$ is the smallest non-trivial eigenvalue in the $\U(n)$-spectrum of $\Gamma$. Namely,
    \[
        \lambda_{\min}^*(\Gamma,\kmp_2) = \inf_{\triv\ne\rho\in\irr(\U(n))}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho) = \min_{\triv\ne\rho\in\irr(\U(n))}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho).
    \] (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture 13 of arXiv:2603.00353

[Definition of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Fix positive integers $0<D_1<D_2<\cdots<D_{\dim \mathcal{D}_R}$. We say that a profile 
$$B=(B_1,\cdots,B_N)\in (\mathcal{D}_R)^N,\quad  \sum_i\|B_i\|_{HS}^2\in[\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2}],$$
lies in regularity class $d$, denoted $B\in\mathfrak{Reg}(d)$, if we can find a $d$-dimensional subspace $W\subset \mathcal{D}_R=\Sigma_R^\perp$, such that $W=\operatorname{span}(B_1,\cdots,B_N)$  and the covariance operator 
$$
\Gamma_B:=\sum_{j=1}^N B_j\otimes B_j^*
$$has smallest singular value at least $N^{-D_d}$ on $W$.

[Lemma 66 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Assume the same notation as in Definition \ref{Def.LETop}. Then, $L^N_1, L^N_2$ are a.s. increasing paths on $\llbracket 0, M \rrbracket$. Fix $b \in \llbracket 1, M \rrbracket$, $A, B \in \mathbb{Z}$, and an increasing path $g$ on $\llbracket 0, b \rrbracket$, such that $\mathbb{P}_N(E(A,B,g)) > 0$, where
$$E(A,B,g) = \{ L_1^N(0) = A, \hspace{2mm} L_1^N(b) = B, \hspace{2mm} L^N_2 = g \}.$$
Then, for any $E \subseteq \Omega(0,b,A,B)$, we have 
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}_N(L^N_1 \in E \vert E(A,B,g)) = \frac{\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{Geom}}^{0,b, A, B}(\{Q \in E\} \cap \{Q \succeq g\} )}{\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{Geom}}^{0,b, A, B}(Q \succeq g)},
\end{equation}
where $Q$ has law $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{Geom}}^{0,b, A, B}$.

[Lem 16 of arXiv:2608.13727, 'Hitting-time mixing for the star transposition shuffle'] Let \(s\) be an integer satisfying
    \[
        \left|\frac{s-\lfloor n\log n\rfloor}{n}\right|
        \leq \frac{\log\log n}{2}-2\log\log\log n+\frac{5}{n}.
    \]
    Let \(\beta_{\lambda^{(i)}}\) be the eigenvalues of \(Q\), the transition kernel associated to the star transposition walk. Then
    \[\sum_{\lambda\in\cS}d_\lambda\sum_{i\in J(\lambda)}d_{\lambda^{(i)}}\beta_{\lambda^{(i)}}^{2s} \leq n^{-\omega(1)}. \]
title: Lem 16 of arXiv:2608.13727

Conditional reduction, independent review pending: let W be a continuous adapted real chordal Loewner driver, W_0=0, with dg_t(z)=2/(g_t(z)-W_t)dt in one usual filtration. For three real marks 0<a<b<c put X=g_t(a)-W_t and Y_i=g_t(b_i)-W_t, b_1=b,b_2=c. On each stopped compact localization with 0<X<Y_1<Y_2 and positive separations, assume BOTH C(X/Y_i) are local martingales, where C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) integral_0^u [v(1-v)]^(-2/3)dv. Smooth inversion of the first makes W a semimartingale; the two Ito signed-measure equations force zero finite variation part and local martingale bracket 6dt. If the assumption holds for a countable mark/localization family covering every finite time, W/sqrt(6) is Brownian motion. The square-lattice martingale approximation needed to apply this reduction is unproved in this draft.

[Definition 5 (Bessel Space) of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] For $p\in [1, \infty]$ and $\alpha> 0$ the Bessel space $\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d)$ is defined by
\[
\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d):=\{\, g_{\alpha}\star f\colon\, f\in L^p(\Rr^d) \,\},
\]
where $g_0:= \delta_0$, so that $g_{0}\star f =f$.  The space $\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d)$ is endowed with the norm
\[
\|F\|_{\mathcal{L}^p_{\alpha}(\Rr^d)} :=\|f\|_{L^p(\Rr^d)}
\]
where $f\in L^p(\Rr^d)$ such that $F=g_{\alpha}\star f$.
title: Bessel Space

body:
[Lemma lem:ht.graph-laws of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] Let $\hat G^{(\ell)}[\hat X]$ be the inhomogeneous random graph on $[N_{L-\ell}]$ with edge densities
\[
b_\ell^{\neq}(I,J) = B\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\hat X_J^{(\ell)}, \qquad I\neq J,
\]
and self-loop densities
\[
\tfrac12 [b_\ell^{\neq}(I,I)+b_\ell^{=}(I)]
= \tfrac12\big[B\big(\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\big)^2+C\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\big].
\]
Let $\hat G_{\ell,\gamma,\delta,\eta}[\hat Y]$ be the inhomogeneous stable-law random graph on $[N_{L-\ell}]$ with edge densities
\[
c_\ell^{\neq}(I,J) = \delta \hat Y_I\hat Y_J, \qquad I\neq J,
\]
and self-loop densities
\[
\tfrac12\big[c_\ell^{\neq}(I,I)+c_\ell^{=}(I)\big] = \tfrac12\big[\delta(\hat Y_I)^2+\eta\hat Y_I\big].
\]
Then, for every measurable set $\mathcal A$ of graphs on $[N_{L-\ell}]$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_U\big[P\big(\hat G^{(\ell)}[\hat X]\in\mathcal A\mid U\big)\big]
&= P\big(\hat G^{(\ell)}[\hat X]\in\mathcal A\big),\\
\mathbb{E}_U\big[P\big(\hat G_{\ell,\gamma,\delta,\eta}[\hat Y]\in\mathcal A\mid U\big)\big]
&= P\big(G_{\ell,\gamma,\delta,\eta}[Y]\in\mathcal A\big).
\end{aligned}
\]
In the first line, the law on the right-hand side is the annealed graph law obtained by first sampling an i.i.d.\ family of block variables with the same law as $\hat X_I^{(\ell)}$ and then sampling edges and self-loops conditionally independently. In the second line, the law on the right-hand side is the annealed stable-law graph law.

Suppose the spatial domain E is homogeneous and the connection kernels are translation-invariant K_{alpha beta}(x, x') = w_{alpha beta}(|x - x'|). If the neural field Jacobian matrix satisfies the Hurwitz condition at the homogeneous resting state u^*, then u^* is exponentially asymptotically stable in L^2(E).
Kernels are translation-invariant
Jacobian is Hurwitz across all spatial wavenumbers

body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Design the algorithm and check whether the exploration frontier remains Markov. Result: For bond percolation the peeling frontier is a two-colour boundary (free/blocked edges) and the algorithm peels the edge at the colour change, keeping the unexplored region a Boltzmann map with a boundary of the same type. For site percolation the colour lives on vertices and after peeling a face the newly exposed boundary vertices are uncoloured; the natural algorithm peels the edge whose left endpoint is black and right endpoint is uncoloured, colouring the new vertices as they appear. The unexplored region is then a Boltzmann map with a boundary condition that is a word in {black, white, uncoloured}, and the difficulty is that the length of the black segment is no longer a Markov chain by itself: the future depends on the positions of uncoloured vertices along the boundary. The frontier becomes Markov if one records the boundary word, which is an infinite-dimensional state. On triangulations the problem was solved (Angel-Curien) because degree-3 faces expose at most one new vertex per step, keeping the state finite; for general Boltzmann maps with large faces a peeled face exposes many uncoloured vertices at once. So a Markov site-percolation peeling exists exactly when faces expose boundedly many vertices, i.e. for bounded face degrees, and the general Boltzmann case requires a state space of boundary words; whether the threshold can still be computed from a word-valued Markov chain is the open part. Obstruction: Unbounded face degrees expose many uncoloured boundary vertices at once; the frontier state is a word, not an integer.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0058-a-peeling-algorithm-exploring-site-percolation-on-boltzmann-maps
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved
title: Attempt on A peeling algorithm exploring site percolation on Boltzmann maps

Let mu be a probability measure on a metric space (M, d). The measure mu satisfies the transportation inequality T_1(c) if and only if for every 1-Lipschitz function f: M -> R and all lambda in R, int_M exp(lambda * (f - int f dmu)) dmu <= exp(c * lambda^2 / 2).

c > 0

[Definition 28 of arXiv:2606.12670, 'The censored stochastic six-vertex model and parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials'] Configurations $\eta\colon\{x\in\mathbb Z:x\leq k\}\to\{0,1\}$ with exactly $k$ particles can be identified with partitions with at most $k$ rows, by extending them with value $1$ to the right of $k$ and applying the identification of particle configurations and partitions above.
    On these configurations define the measure
    \[
    \pi^k(\lambda)=v_{(\infty^k)}(\lambda)=q^{|\lambda|}\prod_{i=1}^k(1-q^i)\,,
    \]
    where $v_{(\infty^k)}$ is the limit $n\to\infty$ of $v_{(n,\dots,n)}$, i.e., the parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig R-measure indexed by the partition with $k$ rows of length $n$.

\(S(\alpha_i,\beta_i)\), \(1\le i\le m\), partition \(\Z\), and that
the moduli \(\alpha_i>1\) are pairwise distinct.  Then
\[
 \{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m\}
 =\left\{\frac{2^m-1}{2^j}:0\le j<m\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Fraenkel's conjecture

body: [Theorem 14 of arXiv:2604.24821, '\textbf{Asymptotics of Parking Search in Hyperfractal Networks}'] In the jumpless model, we have $\mathbb{E}[\km-\bT(\lambda)]=\frac{\log_2\lambda}{d_F}+O(1)$ and $\km-\bT(\lambda)=\frac{\log_2\lambda}{d_F}+O(1)$. The $O(1)$ terms are periodic random functions of $\log\lambda$. The convergence is in moment and in distribution.

body:
[Lem 6 of arXiv:2605.07369, '2605.07369'] Let $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a stochastic process taking values in $\rr$ and satisfying the stochastic approximation algorithm  (\ref{sa-0}).
Assume that  the conditions (\ref{sa-2}) and (\ref{g}) hold.
Then, for any $\varepsilon>0$ and $F>0$, there exists a positive constant $\delta\in(0,1)$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, we have
\begin{align*}
\pp\left(\left|X_{n+1}-x^*\right|\ge \varepsilon\right)&\le \pp\Big(\left|X_{[\delta n]}-x^*\right|>F\Big)+
\pp\left(b \left|\sum_{i=[\delta n]}^n \frac{U_{i+1}}{i+1}\right|\ge 2\varepsilon\right)\\
&\ \ \   +\sum_{k=[\delta n]}^n\pp\left(b \left|\sum_{i=k+1}^n \frac{U_{i+1}}{i+1}\right|\ge \frac{\varepsilon}{4}\right).
\end{align*}
Here, $[\delta n]$ denotes the integer part of $\delta n$. The constant $\delta$ can be chosen to satisfy
$$
0<\delta<\exp\left(-\frac{2(F+\varepsilon)}{b K_1 \varepsilon}\right),
$$
where $K_1$ is defined in (\ref{g}).

body:
[Theorem thrm:RM of arXiv:2607.07309, 'Quantitative limit theorems for generalized P\'olya urns with applications to random tree '] Let $(X_n)$ and $(\Delta M_n)$ be sequences of random variables, adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_n)$, taking values in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $(\gamma_n)$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers, $F: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be a measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $P$ be a symmetric, positive-semi-definite $n \times n$ matrix. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
    \item [(i)] For all $n \ge 0$ we have $ X_{n+1}= X_n + \gamma_{n}(F(X_n)+\Delta M_{n+1})$
    \item [(ii)] $\mathbb{E}[\Delta M_{n+1}\mid \mathcal{F}_n]=0$
    \item[(iii)]  For all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $\langle F(X_n),X_n -z\rangle_P \le-A\left\lVertX_n -z\right\rVert_P^2$ for some  $z \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $A > 0$.
    \item[(iv)] For all $n \ge 0$ we have $\mathbb{E}[\norm{F(X_n)+\Delta M_{n+1}}_P^2 \mid \mathcal{F}_n] \le K$ for some $K>0$
    \item[(v)] $\sum_{n=0}^\infty \gamma_n = \infty$ and $\sum_{n=0}^\infty \gamma_n^2 < \infty$.
 \item [(vi)] $\mathbb{E}[\left\lVertX_0 - z\right\rVert_P^2] < L$ for some $L>0$
\end{itemize}
Then $X_n$ converges to $z$, with respect to the semi-norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_P$, almost surely and in $L^2$. In other words
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVertX_n-z\right\rVert^2_P\right] \to 0 \mbox{ and } \left\lVertX_n-z\right\rVert_P \to 0 \mbox{ almost surely.}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thrm:RM of arXiv:2607.07309

[Definition Markov semigroup of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $(X_t)_{t \ge 0}$ denote a continuous-time Markov process on \emph{state space} $\Omega$. 
    Let $(P_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be the associated \emph{Markov semigroup} operator; $P_t$ acts on functions $f: \Omega \to \R$ via $P_tf(x) = \E[f(X_t) | X_0 = x]$. 
    Throughout, we assume that the semigroup is \emph{reversible} with respect to stationary distribution $\pi$. 
    Furthermore, let $\Lap$ denote the \emph{infinitesimal generator} of $P_t$, i.e.,  $P_t = e^{-t\Lap}$. 
    For functions $f, g: \Omega \to \R$, we define the \emph{Dirichlet form} as $\calE(f, g) = \E_{\pi}[f\Lap g]$.
title: Markov semigroup

[Definition 17 of arXiv:2606.19115, 'Finite free perpetuities'] Let $n\in \N$, $a\in \C$ and $b\in \C\setminus \{1,1-\frac1n,1-\frac2n,\dots,\frac1n\}$.
We define $p_{n,(a,b)}\in \pols_n(\C)$ by
\[
\coef{k}{n}\!\left(p_{n,(a,b)}\right)
= (-1)^k\,\frac{(-an)_k}{((b-1)n)_k},
\qquad k=0,1,\dots,n,
\]
where $(x)_0:=1$ and
\[
(x)_k = x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1), \qquad k\ge 1,
\]
denotes the rising factorial.

[Lemma Source relaxation of arXiv:2603.28520, 'The Supercritical Loop O(1) and Random Current Models: Uniqueness and Mixing'] Let $q\in \mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$, $d\geq 2$ and $p>p_{slab},$ and suppose that $\phi$ is a weak limit of the form
$$
\phi[\;\cdot\;]=\lim_{G_n\nearrow \mathbb{Z}^d}\phi^0_{G_n,p,q}[\;\cdot\mid \mathcal{F}_{A_n} ]
$$
for $A_n\in (\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})^{\partial_vG_n}$ with $\sum_{v\in \partial_vG_n} A_{n,v}=0.$ Then, there exist $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq  \{0,1\}^{E(\mathbb{Z}^d)}$ (possibly random), such that
$$
\phi=\lim_{n\to\infty} \phi^{\xi_n}_{\Lambda_{n},p,q}.
$$

[Conjecture conj:main of arXiv:2608.10184, 'The sharp SAT/UNSAT phase transition in random ellipsoid fitting'] Let $p(n,d) := \mathbb{P}\{\exists S \succeq 0 :\ x_i^{\top} S x_i = d \ \ \forall i \in [n]\}$, where $x_1,\dots,x_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0,I_d)$. For every $\varepsilon > 0$, as $d \to \infty$,
\[
\limsup_{d\to\infty} \frac{n}{d^2} \le \frac{1-\varepsilon}{4}
\;\Longrightarrow\; p(n,d) \to 1,
\qquad\qquad
\liminf_{d\to\infty} \frac{n}{d^2} \ge \frac{1+\varepsilon}{4}
\;\Longrightarrow\; p(n,d) \to 0 .
\] (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: The ellipsoid fitting conjecture

[Lemma lem:gaussian-spatial-truncation of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying that
\begin{align}
  \sup_{u\in\SS^{d-1 }}\PP_{x\sim\mu}\bigl(\,|\langle u,x \rangle |>t\,\bigr)
  \;\le\;A\,\exp\!\big(-({t} /{b})^{c}\bigl ), 
\end{align}
for some $b>0$, $c>0$ and $A>0$ and all $t>0$. 
Let $f$ be a bounded function on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|f\|_{L^\infty(\RR^d)}\le M$. 
Then for every $\varepsilon>0 $, if we set $R >2(\sigma + b) \cdot \big(\log (2A  / \varepsilon^2) +d \log 5 \big)^{1/c'}$, where $c'=\min\{c,2\}$,  it holds that  that $\norm{T_\sigma f - T_\sigma (f\cdot \ind_{B_R})}_{\mu}\le M \varepsilon$.
title: Lemma lem:gaussian-spatial-truncation of arXiv:2512.04371

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Assume $X,Y,Z$ are $G$-valued random variables with finite entropies. Then

    \dR(X,Z) \leq \dstar(X,Z) \leq \dR(X,Y)+\dR(Y,Z).
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
