[Theorem 40 of arXiv:2608.30570, '2608.30570'] There is a compatible complex structure $J_1$ in ${\mathbb C}^2$, such that the K\"ahler angle $\alpha$ of the surface $\Sigma$ defined by (\ref{e-Sigma}) lies between $-\frac{\pi}{2}+\bar\phi$ and $\frac{\pi}{2}-\bar\phi$. In particular, by choosing $\bar\phi$ close to $\frac{\pi}{2}$, we know that for any $\varepsilon >0$, there is a symplectic translating soliton $\Sigma$ with respect to $J_1$, such that $\cos\alpha\geq 1-\varepsilon$.

Furthermore, the translating soliton $\Sigma$ constructed above has bounded second fundamental, genus 0, first Betti number 0, extrinsic quadratic area growth, and
\begin{equation*}
      \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{\Sigma\cap\{r<|{\bf x}|<2r\}}|{\bf H}|^2d\mu>0.
\end{equation*}
In particular,
 $$
  \int_{\Sigma}|{\bf H}|^2d\mu=\infty.
 $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 40 of arXiv:2608.30570

body: [Definition of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] \emph{An RKHS isomorphism} from $\mathcal{H}_1$ to $\mathcal{H}_2$ is a bijective bounded linear map $T : \mathcal{H}_1 \to \mathcal{H}_2$ defined by $T(k_x^1)=\overline{\lambda(x)}k_{\varphi(x)}^2$ for all $x\in X_1$, where $\lambda: X_1\to\mathbb{C}$ is a non-vanishing function and $\varphi: X_1\to X_2$ is a bijection.

[Lemma lem:pruning-intervals-laminar-and-order of arXiv:2605.16086, 'Loop pruning and downward deviations for maximum local time of discrete-time simple random'] Assume $i<j$ in $I$. Then $\zeta(i)$ and $\zeta(j)$ are laminar: either they are disjoint up to endpoints, or one is contained in the other.
Moreover, if both steps are pruned and the intervals are in the containment case, then exactly one of the following alternatives holds:
\[
\textup{(C1)}\ \zeta(j)\subsetneq \zeta(i),\ i\le \zeta^-(j);
\qquad
\textup{(C2)}\ \zeta(i)\subsetneq \zeta(j),\ \zeta^+(i)\le j-1;
\qquad
\textup{(C3)}\ \zeta(i)=\zeta(j).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:pruning-intervals-laminar-and-order of arXiv:2605.16086

[Theorem of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] If $m = \arg \min_{i=1,...,k} \lambda_i$, then the CDFs have asymptotics
        
        \[\begin{cases}
            1-F_k(T)  \sim   C_{m,k}\exp(-\lambda_m T), & T \uparrow \infty \text{ and k fixed,}\\
            F_k(T)  \sim \frac{\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i}{k!} T^{k}, &  T = o((s_{k}/k)^{-1}),\\
        \end{cases}\]
        \noindent where $T = o((s_k/k)^{-1})$ denotes any sequence of pairs $(T_n, k_n)$ so that $\lim_{n \to \infty} s_{k_n}T_n/k_n = 0$. More generally, in the same $T = o((s_k/k)^{-1})$ regime and for any finite $m \geqslant 0$
        \[\frac{F_k(T) - \sum_{r=0}^{m} a_{r,k}}{a_{m, k}} \to 0, \qquad a_{r,k} := (-1)^r \frac{h_{r}(\lambda_1,..., \lambda_k)\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i }{(k+r)!} T^{k+r}.\]
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coa'

[Cor 12 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] Let ${\sf d}$ be a distance function consistent with the given topology on 
 $E$.
Suppose that the jumping measure $J$ satisfies $\frac{D_1}{{\sf d}(x,y)^{p_1}}{\m}({\d} x){\m}({\d} y)\leq 
J({\d} x{\d} y)\leq \frac{D_2}{{\sf d}(x,y)^{p_2}}{\m}({\d} x){\m}({\d} y)$ for some $D_1,D_2>0$ and $0<p_1\leq p_2<\infty$.
Assume $1\land\frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}}\in L^1(E;{\m})$ for a fixed $o\in E$. 
Then the following hold. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(1)]
$u\in D(\mathscr{E})^{\diamond}_{\loc}$ implies 
$\left(1\land \frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}} \right)|u|\in L^1(E;{\m})$.
\item[\rm(2)] Further suppose that 
$1\land\frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}}\in L^1(E;{\m})$ holds for any $o\in E$. 
If $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}$ and  
$\left(1\land \frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}} \right)|u|\in L^1(E;{\m})$ holds for any $o\in E$, then $u\in D(\mathscr{E})^{\diamond}_{\loc}$.
\end{enumerate}
Assume $1\land\frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}}\in L^2(E;{\m})$ 
for a fixed $o\in E$. 
Then the following hold. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(3)]
$u\in D(\mathscr{E})^{\dag}_{\loc}$ implies 
$\left(1\land \frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}} \right)|u|^2\in L^1(E;{\m})$.
\item[\rm(4)] For $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}$, 
$\left(1\land \frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}} \right)|u|^2\in L^1(E;{\m})$ implies $u\in D(\mathscr{E})^{\dag}_{\loc}$.
\end{enumerate}

Let N>=0 be an integer, and let nu be a real signed Borel measure on R for which every polynomial is absolutely integrable with respect to the total variation measure |nu|. The measure nu is positive definite up to degree N if integral f(t)^2 dnu(t)>0 for every nonzero real polynomial f of degree<=N. Equivalently integral f(t)^2 dnu(t)>=0 for all such polynomials, with equality only for the zero polynomial. This is Cohn-Kumar Definition3.4. It is positivity of a finite-degree quadratic form, not a claim that nu is a nonnegative measure or that squared norms in higher degrees are positive.

body: A set A of positive integers is sum-distinct if its 2^|A| subset sums are pairwise different. Exhaustive enumeration shows there are exactly two sum-distinct 5-element subsets of {1,...,13}, namely {3,6,11,12,13} and {6,9,11,12,13}, and none of the C(12,5) = 792 five-element subsets of {1,...,12} is sum-distinct, so the least such N is exactly 13. The 32 subset sums of {3,6,11,12,13} are 0, 3, 6, 9, 11 to 34, 36, 39, 42, 45. In Lean 4 (the formal-conjectures statement Erdos1.erdos_1.variants.least_N_5) the kernel decides the witness half, and the 792-set lower bound compiles in 425 s once maxRecDepth is raised. The corresponding statement for n = 9 (least N = 161) does not reduce to a finite witness check of the same size.

body:
[Lemma l:W.is.subgaussian of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] Let
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal{H}} =  \{\|I_n+W\|_{\operatorname{op}}\le 4 \}.
    
\end{equation}
If $d \ge (1+\epsilon) n$ for some arbitrarily small constant $\epsilon>0$, then there exists a constant $c>0$ only depending on $\epsilon$ such that 
$\mathbb{P}_0(W \in {\mathcal{H}}^c) \leq \mathop{\rm exp}(-cn)$ 
and,
for any zero-diagonal symmetric matrix $U$,
\[
\mathbb{E}_{X\sim \mathbb{P}_{0}}[\mathop{\rm exp}( \langle U,W\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal H}\rangle)]\le \mathop{\rm exp}\left(\frac{2 \|U\|^2}{d}\right)+1\le 2\mathop{\rm exp}\left(\frac{2\|U\|^2}{d}\right).
\]

\begin{proof}

Recall that $W=XX^\top -I_n$, so 

${\mathcal{H}}$ is implied by the event
$\{\|X\|_{\rm op} \le 2\}$.
Let $Z$ be an $n\times d$ matrix with i.i.d.\ standard gaussian entries, and let $D$ be the $n\times n$ diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $\|z_1\|,\ldots,\|z_n\|$. Then $X$ is equidistributed as $D^{-1}Z$, so we can bound
    \[\|X\|_{\rm op} \le 
    \frac{\|Z\|_{\rm op}}
        {\min_i \|z_i\|}\,.\]
By the standard concentration inequality for Gaussian matrices~[vershynin2010introduction], we have
\[\|Z\|_{\rm op}
\le\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{n}
+t\]
with probability at least $1-2\mathop{\rm exp}(-t^2/2)$. By the standard concentration bound for chi-squared random variables (Lemma~(l:chi.square.lower.tail of the paper)), we have
    \[
    \min\Big\{ \|z_i\|
    : 1\le i\le n\Big\}
    \ge d-(2d)^{1/2} t
    \]
with probability at least $1-n\mathop{\rm exp}(-t^2/2)$.  Taking $t=cn^{1/2}$, we conclude that with probability at least $1-3n\mathop{\rm exp}(-c^2 n/2)$, we have
\[\|X\|_{\rm op} \le \frac{1+(1+c)/\sqrt{1+\epsilon}}{[1-\sqrt{2}c/\sqrt{1+\epsilon}]^{1/2}} \le 2\,,\]
where the last inequality holds by choosing $c$ to be a sufficiently small constant  depending on $\epsilon$. 

Next, let $W_m$ denote the principal submatrix of $W$ formed by the first $m$ rows and columns. We will truncate on the event
$\mathcal H_m= \{\| I_m+W_m\|_{\operatorname{op}}\le 4 \}$.
Note that ${\mathcal{H}}_{m+1} \subset {\mathcal{H}}_{m}$ for all $1 \le m \le n-1$ and $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_n$. Abbreviating $u_n$ for the last column of $U$, we can bound
\begin{align*}
     &\ \mathbb{E}_{X\sim \mathbb{P}_{0}}\Big[\mathop{\rm exp}( \langle U,W\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal H}\rangle)\Big]\\
   \le &\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_n}
   \bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg( \sum_{i<j}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)
   \mathbf{1}\{W_n \in \mathcal H_n\}\bigg]+1\\
   \le&\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(
   \sum_{i<j<n}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)\mathbf{1}\{ W_{n-1} \in \mathcal H_{n-1}\} \mathbb{E}_{x_n}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(
   \bigg\langle \sum_{i<n} u_{in}x_i,x_n
   \bigg\rangle
   \bigg)\bigg]\bigg]+1\\
    \le&\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\sum_{i<j<n}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)\mathbf{1}\{W_{n-1}\in \mathcal H_{n-1}\}\cdot \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{ (u_n)^\top (I_{n-1}+ W_{n-1}) u_n}{2d}\bigg)\bigg]+1\\
    \le&\ \mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}}\bigg[\mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\sum_{i<j<n}u_{ij}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\bigg)\mathbf{1}\{W_{n-1} \in \mathcal H_{n-1}\}\bigg]\cdot \mathop{\rm exp}\left(\frac{2 \|u_n\|^2
    }{d}\right)+1\,,
\end{align*}
where the second-to-last inequality is by Lemma~(lem:beta.mgf of the paper), and the
 last inequality holds because we have $\|I_{n-1}+W_{n-1}\|_{\operatorname{op} }
\le 4$ on the event ${\mathcal{H}}_{n-1}$.
Iterating the above gives the claimed bound.
\end{proof}
title: Lemma l:W.is.subgaussian of arXiv:2607.02013

[Thm weak_convergence of arXiv:2605.29073, 'Volterra clocks and their pure-jump limits: \\hitting times of curved boundaries'] Let $\left(W^n\,, X^n\right)_{n \geq 0}$ be a sequence of weak solutions to (equation eq:Volterra_clock of the paper) on $[0\,,T]\,$, for the sequence of inputs $(G_0^n\,, K^n\,, f^n\,, \lambda^n\,, \nu^n)_{n \geq 0}\,$, where $\lambda^n\,, \nu^n \geq 0\,$, $f^n$ satisfies Assumption (assumption:f of the paper), $K^n \in L^1_{loc}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+\,, \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+)$ and $G_0^n : \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+ \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$ is non-decreasing with $G_0^n(0) = 0\,$, for each $n \geq 0\,$. Suppose that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $K^n(t)\,dt \Rightarrow \delta_0(dt)$ weakly on $[0\,,T]\,$.
        \item $G_0^n \to G_0$ pointwise on $[0\,,T]\,$, where $G_0$ is continuous.
        \item $f^n \to_{l.u.} f$ on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$, with $\sup_{n \geq 0} \sup_{x \geq 0} f^n(x) / (1 + x^2) < + \infty\,$.
        \item $\lambda^n \to \lambda$ and $\nu^n \to \nu\,$.
    \end{itemize}
    Then, we have the weak convergence of processes 
    $$
    \left(W^n\,, X^n \right) \overset{n \to \infty}{\implies} \left(W^*\,, X^*\right)
    $$
    on $D^{\circ}[0\,,T]\,$, where $W^*$ is a standard Brownian motion and 
    $$
    X^*_t = \inf\{s \geq 0\,:\, (1+ \lambda)s - \nu\,W^*_{f(s)} > G_0(t)\}\,, \quad t \leq T\,.
    $$

[Proposition 37 (Combined high-tail comparison and constant) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Fix $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$, and put $Q=1-\alpha$ and $S=1-\beta$.  Let $\nu_n^{\alpha,\beta}$ be the stationary law of the combined count chain \eqref{eq:combined-transition}, and let $w_{n,k}^{\alpha,\beta}$ be defined by \eqref{eq:combined-lucky-scale}.  There are constants $0<c<C<\infty$ and an integer $M<\infty$, depending only on $\alpha,\beta$, such that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and all $M\le k\le n$,
\[
        c w_{n,k}^{\alpha,\beta}
        \le \nu_n^{\alpha,\beta}(k)
        \le C w_{n,k}^{\alpha,\beta}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
        \nu_n^{\alpha,\beta}(n)
        \sim
        \frac{1}{(S;S)_\infty}
        \frac{n!}{n^n}Q^nS^{n(n+1)/2}.
\]

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.01742, 'Large deviation principles for SPDEs with locally Lipschitz coefficients'] (\cite[Lemma A.1]{BMS} and \cite[Lemma A.4]{LWYZ17})
Let $K$ be a compact set in $\mathbb R$ and let $\{V^\varepsilon(t,x):(t,x)\in[0,T]\times K\}$ be a family of real-valued functions. Assume that
\begin{itemize}
  \item[(A1).] for any $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times K$,
     $$\lim_{\varepsilon\rightarrow 0}|V^{\varepsilon}(t,x)|=0;$$
  \item[(A2).] there exist $\beta_1,\beta_2>0$ satisfied that for any $(t,x),(t',x')\in[0,T]\times K$,
$$
|V^\varepsilon(t,x)-V^\varepsilon(t',x')|\le C_{6,4}(|t-t'|^{\beta_1}+|x-x'|^{\beta_2}),
$$
where $C_{6,4}$ is a constant independent of $\varepsilon$.
\end{itemize}
Then for any $\theta\in(0,1)$, we have
$$\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\|V^\varepsilon\|_{\theta\beta_1,\theta\beta_2}=0. $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.01742

body: Mordell-Weil theorem: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K. Then A(K), the group of K-rational points of A, is a finitely generated abelian group, called the Mordell-Weil group; equivalently A(K) is isomorphic to Z^r x T, where r >= 0 is the rank and T is the finite torsion subgroup. The special case in which A = E is an elliptic curve and K = Q is Mordell's theorem, which answers a question apparently posed by Henri Poincare around 1901 and was proved by Louis Mordell in 1922; the general case is due to Andre Weil (1928). It is a foundational theorem of Diophantine geometry and of the arithmetic of abelian varieties.
title: Mordell–Weil theorem

body:
[Df reachability of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] For two vertices $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$ in the associated directed graph $G_w$, we say that $\Delta'$ is \emph{reachable} from $\Delta$ in $G_w$, and write $\Delta\rightsquigarrow_w\Delta'$, if there exists a directed path from $\Delta$ to $\Delta'$; that is, a finite sequence $(\Delta_0,\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_I)$ of vertices in $G_w$ such that $\Delta_0=\Delta$, $\Delta_I=\Delta'$, and $(\Delta_{i-1},\Delta_i)\in E_w$ for all $i=1,2,\ldots,I$.
  Furthermore, we say $\Delta$ \emph{reaches infinity} in $G_w$, and write $\Delta\rightsquigarrow_w\infty$, if there exists an infinite self-avoiding directed path from $\Delta$; that is, a sequence $(\Delta_0,\Delta_1,\ldots)$ of distinct vertices such that $\Delta_0=\Delta$ and $(\Delta_{i-1},\Delta_i)\in E_w$ for all $i\in\mathbb{N}$.
title: Reachability

[Thm stargrp_NS-NStability of arXiv:2606.29829, ''] Let $\lambda\vdash n$, and $\mathscr{B}_{\lambda}$ be the orthonormal basis of $V^{\lambda}$ containing the normalized GT-vectors. Also, for every $n\geq 1$, let $\mathfrak{f}_n:S_n\longrightarrow\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function. Then,
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The sequence of $\{\mathfrak{f}_n\}_n$ is noise sensitive with respect to the interchange process on $\ST$ if and only if for all positive integer $k>0$
		\[	\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\;\sum_{\lambda\vdash n} \frac{f^{\lambda}}{n!^2}\sum_{\substack{T\in\std(\lambda)\\n-1-k<c(b_T(n))\leq n-2}}\sum_{S\in\std(\lambda)}\left|\text{The }(S,T)\text{th entry of the matrix }\Big[\widehat{\mathfrak{f}_n}(\lambda)\Big]_{\mathscr{B}_{\lambda}}\right|^2=0.\]
		\item The sequence of $\{\mathfrak{f}_n\}_n$ is noise stable with respect to the interchange process on $\ST$ if and only if for all $\delta>0$ there exists a positive integer $k$ such that
		\[\sup_n\;\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\frac{f^{\lambda}}{n!^2}\sum_{\substack{T\in\std(\lambda)\\c(b_T(n))\leq n-1-k}} \sum_{S\in\std(\lambda)}\left|\text{The }(S,T)\text{th entry of the matrix }\Big[\widehat{\mathfrak{f}_n}(\lambda)\Big]_{\mathcal{B}_{\lambda}}\right|^2<\delta.\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] Fix a positive integer~$h$.

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). A Nash inequality on a graph with Dirichlet form E and reference measure mu has the form ||f||_2^{2+4/d} <= C E(f,f) ||f||_1^{4/d} for all f in the domain of the form, where d is an effective dimension parameter. Such an inequality is classically equivalent, by results of Nash and later Carlen-Kusuoka-Stroock, to an on-diagonal heat-kernel upper bound p_t(x,x) <= C' t^{-d/2} for the associated Markov semigroup, and combining it with matching volume-growth and effective-resistance-growth estimates, within the general framework relating resistance growth to heat-kernel decay used for fractal-like and random graphs, yields two-sided sub-Gaussian or Gaussian heat-kernel bounds. On graphs where effective resistance to the complement of a ball of radius n grows like n^zeta and volume grows like n^alpha, this gives sub-Gaussian heat-kernel estimates with off-diagonal decay governed by the exponent alpha+zeta, a technique central to analysis on fractals and on random graphs such as critical percolation clusters or random walk among random conductances. The technique does not give the resistance or volume exponents themselves, which are separate geometric inputs, and a full two-sided heat-kernel estimate typically requires both the Nash-type inequality, giving the upper bound, and a separate lower-bound argument, often via a chaining construction or an elliptic Harnack inequality. Typical failure: Assuming ordinary Euclidean Gaussian heat-kernel scaling, of the t^{-d/2} exp(-|x-y|^2/4t) form, transfers automatically to a random or fractal-like graph without re-deriving the resistance exponent zeta; on structures such as the incipient infinite cluster of critical percolation, or random conductance models with heavy-tailed conductances, the correct scaling is sub-Gaussian with zeta != 1, and using the Euclidean exponent silently mis-states both the walk dimension and the tail behavior of the heat kernel. Canonical reference: Nash, 1958, American Journal of Mathematics; Carlen, Kusuoka and Stroock, 1987, Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare; Barlow, 2004, Annals of Probability; Kumagai, Random Walks on Disordered Media and their Scaling Limits, 2014, Springer.
a well-defined Dirichlet form and reversible Markov chain with a reference measure mu
a valid Nash-type functional inequality with a specified effective dimension d
for two-sided estimates: matching volume-growth and effective-resistance-growth bounds on balls
typically also an elliptic Harnack inequality, or comparable regularity, to establish the matching lower heat-kernel bound
title: Technique: Nash Inequality and Heat-Kernel Bounds via Resistance

[Lemma lem:Geo_RW_LD of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] For $q \in (0,1)$, let $S$ be an i.i.d. random walk with $\mathbb E[e^{tS(1)}] < \infty$ for all $t$ in a neighborhood of the origin. Let $\mu = \mathbb E[S(1)]$. Then, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exist constants $0 < \alpha < \beta$  so that, for all integers $1 \le k \le n$, 
    \[
    \mathbb P\Bigl(\Bigl|S(k) - \mu k\Bigr| \ge \varepsilon n\Bigr) \le e^{\alpha k - \beta n}.
    \]
title: Lemma lem:Geo_RW_LD of arXiv:2605.22787

body: Standard Brownian motion (the Wiener process) is a stochastic process W with W_0 = 0, independent increments, W_t - W_s distributed N(0, t - s) for s < t, and continuous paths. body:
[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $(\mu_{T,x})_{T\geq1,x\in\mathbb R^d}$ be probability measures on $\mathbb R$, with
characteristic functions $\chi_{T,x}$.  Suppose that, for every compact
$K\subset\mathbb R^d$, the following hold for some $\sigma^2>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item Locally uniformly in $(x,v)$, 
       \[
       \chi_{T,x}(v/\sqrt T)\longrightarrow \mathrm e^{-\sigma^2v^2/2}.
       \]
 \item There are $\varepsilon,c,C,\gamma>0$ such that for $T$ large enough
       \[
       \sup_{x\in K}|\chi_{T,x}(u)|
       \leq C\bigl(\mathrm e^{-cTu^2}+ \mathrm e^{-\gamma T}\bigr),
       \qquad |u|\leq\varepsilon.
       \]
 \item For every $0<\delta<R<\infty$, there are $C_{K,\delta,R},\eta>0$
       such that for $T$ large enough
       \[
       \sup_{\substack{x\in K\\\delta\leq|u|\leq R}}
       |\chi_{T,x}(u)|
       \leq C_{K,\delta,R}\mathrm e^{-\eta T}.
       \]
\end{enumerate}
Then, for every directly Riemann-integrable $h$ and every $M<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{x\in K\\|a|\leq M}}
 \left|
  \sqrt T\int_\R \mu_{T,x}(\de y) \, h(y-a)
  -\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}
   \int_\R \de y \, h(y)
 \right|
 \longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
title: Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.19744

body:
[Defn 1 of arXiv:2608.30380, 'Morita Induction and Geometric Ideals in $\ell^p$ Roe-Type Algebras'] Let $A$ and $B$ be Banach algebras.  A \emph{Morita equivalence} between $A$ and $B$ consists of Banach bimodules
\[
 {}_B E_A^{<},\qquad {}_A E_B^{>},
\]
and continuous bilinear pairings
\[
 \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_B:E^{<}\times E^{>}\longrightarrow B,
 \qquad
 {}_A\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:E^{>}\times E^{<}\longrightarrow A,
\]
with norm at most one, satisfying the usual module covariance and balancing identities
\begin{align}
\langle be^{<},e^{>} \rangle_B = b\langle e^{<},e^{>} \rangle _B, &\quad \langle e^{<},e^{>}b \rangle_B = \langle e^{<},e^{>} \rangle_Bb, \notag\\
{}_A\langle ae^{>},e^{<} \rangle = a{}_A\langle e^{>},e^{<} \rangle, &\quad {}_A\langle e^{>},e^{<}a \rangle = {}_A\langle e^{>},e^{<} \rangle a, \notag\\
 \langle e^{<}a,e^{>}\rangle_B&=\langle e^{<},ae^{>}\rangle_B,
 \tag{2.1}\\
 {}_A\langle e^{>}b,e^{<}\rangle&={}_A\langle e^{>},be^{<}\rangle,
 \tag{2.2}
\end{align}
for $e^{<}\in E^{<}$, $e^{>}\in E^{>}$, $a\in A$ and $b\in B$, together with
\begin{align*}
 \langle e^{<},e^{>}\rangle_B f^{<}
 &=e^{<}\,{}_A\langle e^{>},f^{<}\rangle,\\
 e^{>}\langle f^{<},f^{>}\rangle_B
 &={}_A\langle e^{>},f^{<}\rangle f^{>},
\end{align*}
for $e^{<},f^{<}\in E^{<}$ and $e^{>},f^{>}\in E^{>}$.  We also require both pairings to be full,
\[
 \clspan{\langle E^{<},E^{>}\rangle_B}=B,
 \qquad
 \clspan{{}_A\langle E^{>},E^{<}\rangle}=A,
\]
and all four module actions to be nondegenerate.  Here nondegeneracy means that the linear span of the corresponding module products is dense; for example, $\overline{AE^{>}}=E^{>}$ and $\overline{E^{>}B}=E^{>}$.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.30380

[Introcor 6 (Convergence of ergodic averages) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] In each of Theorems \ref{thm:crit}, \ref{thm:posdens}, \ref{thm:mhintro}, \ref{thm:eventual} and \ref{thm:gibbsintro}, let
$(X_{k})_{k \in \Nz}$ be the Markov chain with kernel $T$ started in an arbitrary
initial distribution $\mu$, and let $\Prb_{\mu}$ denote its law on the space of
trajectories. Then for every measurable map $f : \XX \to \R$ with
$\int_{\XX} |f| \dd\pi < \infty$,
\[
  \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(X_{k}) \longrightarrow \int_{\XX} f \dd\pi
  \qquad (n \to \infty), \quad \Prb_{\mu}\text{-almost surely.}
\]
If $f$ is bounded, the convergence holds in addition in $L^{r}(\Prb_{\mu})$ for every
number $r \in [1,\infty)$. If $\mu \le M\pi$ for some number $M \in [1,\infty)$ ---
for instance if $\mu = \pi$ --- then, for every number $r \in [1,\infty)$, the
convergence holds in $L^{r}(\Prb_{\mu})$ for every $f$ with
$\int_{\XX} |f|^{r} \dd\pi < \infty$.

In Theorems \ref{thm:posdens}--\ref{thm:gibbsintro}, where $\pi$ is presented by a
density $p$ with respect to a reference measure $\lambda$, the integrals against $\pi$
read $\int_{\XX} f(x)\,p(x)\dd\lambda(x)$ and the condition $\mu \le M\pi$ says that
$\mu$ has a $\lambda$-density bounded by $Mp$. Theorem \ref{thm:crit} names no
reference measure, and the statement is the one displayed above. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence of ergodic averages

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] The latent processes $\mathbf{X}_n = \{(X_n, c_n)\}$ evolve according to 
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbf{X}_n = \Psi(\mathbf{X}_{n-1}, \tau_n) = (\Psi_x(x, c, t), \Psi_c(x, c, t)).
		
	\end{equation}
	where
	\begin{align}
		\Psi_x(x, c, t) &= x \left(1 + \frac{t}{c}\right)^{-p} + \xi,  \\
		\Psi_c(x, c, t) &= \frac{\Psi_x(x, c, t)}{\,\frac{x}{c} \left(1 + \tfrac{t}{c}\right)^{-p-1} + \tfrac{\xi}{\gamma}}, 
	\end{align}
	with parameters $\mu> 0, \gamma> 0, \xi > 0$ and $p>1$.
	Equivalently, the update equations can be written as
	\begin{align*}
		&X_n = X_{n-1} \left(1  + \frac{\tau_n}{c_{n-1}} \right)^{-p} + \xi \\
		&\frac{X_n}{c_n} =  \frac{X_{n-1}}{c_{n-1}} \left(1  + \frac{\tau_n}{c_{n-1}} \right)^{-p-1} + \frac{\xi}{\gamma}.
	\end{align*}
	Define $\Phi(t, x, c)$ as
	\begin{align}
		\Phi(t, x, c) & = \int_0^t  \lambda_{n-1}(s; x, c) \D s= \int_0^t \left( \mu + \frac{x c^p}{(c+s)^p} \right)\, \D s \\
		& = \mu t + \dfrac{x c}{p-1}\left( 1 - \bigg(1+\dfrac{t}{c}\bigg)^{-p+1}  \right). 
	\end{align}
	The inter-arrival time $\tau_n$ is generated via the inverse transform
	\[
	\tau_n = \Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon_n,  X_{n-1}, c_{n-1}),
	\]
	where the inverse is taken with respect to $t$ for fixed $x$ and $c$,
	and $\{\varepsilon_n\}$ is an i.i.d. sequence drawn from $F_\varepsilon$
	satisfying $F_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ (so that $\varepsilon_n \ge 0$ a.s.), $\mu_{\varepsilon} = \mathbb{E}[\varepsilon] < \infty$,
	and $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon^2] < \infty$.
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2607.20838

Let n ≥ 2 and let (q,r), (q̃,r̃) be wave-admissible pairs (2 ≤ q, 2 ≤ r, 1/q + (n−1)/(2r) ≤ (n−1)/4, (q,r,n) ≠ (2,∞,3)) with r < ∞ and r̃ < ∞. Let s ∈ R satisfy the scaling relations 1/q + n/r = n/2 − s = 1/q̃' + n/r̃' − 2. If u solves ∂_t²u − Δu = F on I × R^n with 0 ∈ I, u(0) = u0 ∈ Ḣ^s(R^n), ∂_t u(0) = u1 ∈ Ḣ^{s−1}(R^n), then ‖u‖_{L^q_t L^r_x(I×R^n)} + ‖u‖_{C(I;Ḣ^s)} + ‖∂_t u‖_{C(I;Ḣ^{s−1})} ≤ C ( ‖u0‖_{Ḣ^s} + ‖u1‖_{Ḣ^{s−1}} + ‖F‖_{L^{q̃'}_t L^{r̃'}_x(I×R^n)} ), with C = C(n,q,r,q̃,r̃) independent of I. Examples (n = 3): ‖u‖_{L^4_{t,x}} ≲ ‖u0‖_{Ḣ^{1/2}} + ‖u1‖_{Ḣ^{−1/2}} + ‖F‖_{L^{4/3}_{t,x}}; and ‖u‖_{L^5_t L^{10}_x} ≲ ‖u0‖_{Ḣ¹} + ‖u1‖_{L²} + ‖F‖_{L^1_t L^2_x}.

[Definition stoch_domination of arXiv:2504.00512, 'Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model at the edge'] {\rm{(i)}} Let
	\[\xi=\left(\xi^{(N)}(u):N\in\mathbb N, u\in U^{(N)}\right),\hskip 10pt \zeta=\left(\zeta^{(N)}(u):N\in\mathbb N, u\in U^{(N)}\right),\]
	be two families of non-negative random variables, where $U^{(N)}$ is a possibly $N$-dependent parameter set. We say $\xi$ is stochastically dominated by $\zeta$, uniformly in $u$, if for any fixed (small) $\tau>0$ and (large) $D>0$, 
	\[\mathbb P\bigg(\bigcup_{u\in U^{(N)}}\left\{\xi^{(N)}(u)>N^\tau\zeta^{(N)}(u)\right\}\bigg)\le N^{-D}\]
	for large enough $N\ge N_0(\tau, D)$, and we will use the notation $\xi\prec\zeta$. 
	
	If for some complex family $\xi$ we have $|\xi|\prec\zeta$, then we will also write $\xi \prec \zeta$ or $\xi=\mathrm{O}_\prec(\zeta)$. 
	
	\vspace{5pt}
	\noindent {\rm{(ii)}} As a convention, for two deterministic quantities $\xi$ and $\zeta$, we will write $\xi\prec\zeta$ if and only if $|\xi|\le N^\tau |\zeta|$ for any constant $\tau>0$. 

 \vspace{5pt}
	\noindent {\rm{(iii)}} Let $A$ be a family of random matrices and $\zeta$ be a family of non-negative random variables. Then, we use $A=\mathrm{O}_\prec(\zeta)$ to mean that $\|A\|\prec \zeta$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the operator norm. 
	
	\vspace{5pt}
	\noindent {\rm{(iv)}} We say an event $\Xi$ holds with high probability (w.h.p.) if for any constant $D>0$, $\mathbb P(\Xi)\ge 1- N^{-D}$ for large enough $N$. More generally, we say an event $\Omega$ holds $w.h.p.$ in $\Xi$ if for any constant $D>0$,
	$\mathbb{P}( \Xi\setminus \Omega)\le N^{-D}$ for large enough $N$.
title: Stochastic domination and high probability event

body:
[Corollary cor:MMi-c of arXiv:2606.24881, 'Queues with Correlated Service Times --- the $M/M_D/c$ Model'] Consider the $M/M_i/c$ queueing model. Let
\[
M:=\sum_{i=1}^c \mu_i.
\]
Then the queue is stable if and only if
\[
\lambda < M.
\]

Moreover, the stationary distribution satisfies the following properties.

\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For \(n\ge c+1\), the full-busy states satisfy the recursion
\begin{equation}
(\lambda+M)\pi_n
=
\lambda \pi_{n-1}
+
M\pi_{n+1}.
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] The geometric tail is given by
\begin{equation}
\pi_n=\pi_c r^{\,n-c}, \qquad n\ge c,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
r=\frac{\lambda}{M}.
\end{equation}

\item[(iii)] For a subset state \(s\subseteq \{1,\ldots,c\}\) with
\(|s|=m\le c-2\), the balance equation is
\begin{equation}
\Bigl(\lambda+\sum_{i\in s}\mu_i\Bigr)\pi_s
=
\sum_{u:\,a(u)=s}\lambda \pi_u
+
\sum_{j\notin s}\mu_j\,\pi_{s\cup\{j\}}.
\end{equation}

\item[(iv)] For a subset state \(s\subseteq \{1,\ldots,c\}\) with
\(|s|=c-1\), let \(j(s)\) be the unique idle server, i.e.
\[
\{j(s)\}=\{1,\ldots,c\}\setminus s.
\]
Then the balance equation is
\begin{equation}
\Bigl(\lambda+\sum_{i\in s}\mu_i\Bigr)\pi_s
=
\sum_{u:\,a(u)=s}\lambda \pi_u
+
\mu_{j(s)}\,\pi_c.
\end{equation}

\item[(v)] The linking equation at level \(c\) is
\begin{equation}
(\lambda+M)\pi_c
=
\lambda \sum_{|s|=c-1}\pi_s
+
M\pi_{c+1}.
\end{equation}
Using (equation eq:MMi-geo of the paper), this may be written equivalently as
\begin{equation}
M\pi_c
=
\lambda \sum_{|s|=c-1}\pi_s,
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\pi_c
=
r\sum_{|s|=c-1}\pi_s.
\end{equation}

\item[(vi)] The normalization condition is
\begin{equation}
\sum_{\substack{s\subseteq \{1,\ldots,c\}\\ |s|\le c-1}} \pi_s
+
\frac{\pi_c}{1-r}
=
1.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}

Hence the stationary distribution of the \(M/M_i/c\) queue is determined
by the geometric tail (equation eq:MMi-geo of the paper) together with the finite boundary
system (equation eq:MMi-boundary-subset of the paper)--(equation eq:MMi-link2 of the paper) and the
normalization condition (equation eq:MMi-normalization of the paper).

body: In mathematics, the term homology, originally introduced in algebraic topology, has three primary, closely related usages. First, there is the homology of a chain complex, a sequence of abelian groups, called homology groups, which are regarded as fundamental invariants of the chain complex. Secondly, when one can associate a chain complex to a different mathematical object, one can also associate its homology to that object. Distinct procedures of associating chain complexes to a given object are grouped into homology theories. Finally, homology is important in the study of topological spaces. Under nice conditions in which distinct homology theories for a single topological space produce the same homology groups, one can define a single homology of a topological space. This last notion of homology is closely related to topological ideas frequently discussed in popular mathematics such as the holes of a surface or the cycles of a graph. There is also a related notion of the cohomology of a cochain complex, giving rise to various cohomology theories, in addition to the notion of the cohomology of a topological space.
title: Homology (mathematics)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Suppose $(M^0, g)$ closes smoothly at $s = 0$ and that $H, F_1, \dots, F_r$ extend continuously to $s = 0$. Let $J := \{\, j : F_j(0) = 0 \,\}$. Then necessarily $H(0) = 0$, and exactly one of the following holds:
	
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $J = \varnothing$ (\emph{bolt of codimension two}): only the circle fibers collapse, and the sub-manifold $Q$ at $\{s=0\}$ is diffeomorphic to $N$.
		\item $J = \{ j_0 \}$ (\emph{nut-type collapse}): $(N_{j_0}, g_{j_0})$ is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{CP}^{n_{j_0}}$ with the Fubini--Study metric, $|q_{j_0}| = 1$, and $Q \cong \prod_{k \neq j_0} N_k$ is a bolt of codimension $2 n_{j_0} + 2$. When $r = 1$ this means $P \cong S^{2n+1}$ and the entire leaf collapses to a \emph{nut} $Q = \{ \mathrm{pt} \}$; for $r \geq 2$ the collapse is a nut \emph{fiberwise over} the bolt $Q$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03332

[Definition def:circuit-primitives of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For an ordered finite set $S$ of oriented carrier labels, write
$\mathscr H_S=\bigotimes_{u\in S}H_u$, with every factor equipped with
the Euclidean Hilbert norm.  A \emph{normalized Brauer primitive} is a
signed carrier permutation, a wedge reversal, full transpose, a share
turn, a through string, the orthogonal antisymmetrizer, or a cup/cap
normalized so that its operator norm is one.  A share turn is the fixed
signed boundary permutation, possibly followed by full transpose,
induced when a principal pivot reverses one of the two ordered boundary
intervals.  The two coefficient primitives are
\[
 \widehat C_{uv}=\iota_{uv}C\pi_{uv}:H_u\otimes H_v\to H_u\otimes H_v,
\]
where $\pi_{uv}$ is the normalized orthogonal projection and
identification onto $\Lambda^2H$, and $\iota_{uv}=\pi_{uv}^*$; hence
$\widehat C_{uv}$ is zero on $\operatorname{Sym}^2H$ and has norm $K$.
The other coefficient primitive is the restriction/re-expression of
(eq:2.1.3 of the paper) as the Bianchi transfer
\[
 (\Phi_CY)_{ik}=\sum_{m,n}C_{in,mk}Y_{mn},
 \qquad Y\in\Lambda^2H.
\]
The first Bianchi identity identifies the latter with the physical action
of $C$.  A \emph{safe gate} is a typed composite of these primitives,
including the $AA$ words and correctly oriented $AB$ words used below.
Its degree is the number of coefficient primitives.  Thus a degree-$d$
safe gate $G:\mathscr H_S\to\mathscr H_T$ satisfies
$\|G\|_{\rm op}\le K^d$; untouched factors are ancillary identities.

A coefficient box has four darts
$L_{i,0},L_{i,1},R_{i,0},R_{i,1}$.  For a column pairing $q$, a
\emph{packet} is a connected component of the box-incidence graph whose
edges are the $q$-pairs joining different boxes.  A $q$-pair joining the
two darts of one wedge is forbidden and gives zero.  An allowed
\emph{smoothing} chooses at each box either
\[
 h_i^{\parallel}=\{L_{i,0}R_{i,0},L_{i,1}R_{i,1}\},\qquad
 h_i^{\times}=\{L_{i,0}R_{i,1},L_{i,1}R_{i,0}\}.
\]
The alternating circuits of $q\vee h$ are the \emph{smoothing
carriers}; adjoining one carrier means adjoining one identity factor
$I_H$.  The smoothing support $\operatorname{supp}_h(i)$ of a box is the
one- or two-element set of $q\vee h$ carriers containing its two
$h$-passages.  A \emph{ported pair comb} on two chosen carriers consists of all
boxes whose smoothing support is that pair, together with every singleton-support box
assigned to it exactly once; removing all other support groups leaves
their boundary darts as linearly ordered typed ports.  These definitions
fix the domains and codomains of every safe word, fold, comb, and
attachment below.

An \emph{ambient rooted ribbon record} $\Gamma$ consists of a common
finite dart set, its coefficient boxes and local wedge signs, a row
pairing $p$, a column pairing $q$, a rooted trace pairing $r$, and the
declared boundary/root data.  Thus $p\vee r$ is the disjoint union of the
original trace circuits in that record; its components, not temporary
proof cuts, receive the normalization bases below.  The more detailed
Weingarten data carried by $\Gamma$ are specified in
(def:ribbon-record of the paper).
title: Typed circuit primitives

[Definition 3 (Riemannian complex) of arXiv:2609.00183, '2609.00183'] A {\bf Riemannian complex} is a cell complex $Y$ equipped with a collection of metrics $G=\{G^S\}$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item each cell $S$ of $Y$ is endowed with a smooth metric $G^S.$ 
    \item the metric $G^S$ is smooth in the interior of $S$ and extends smoothly to $\partial S.$
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $F$ is a face of $S$, then
\[
G^S|_{F}=G^{F}.
\]

[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $d \in \N$, $p \in [1,\infty]$, $m \in \N_0$ and $\alpha \in (0,1]$ and set $r := m + \alpha$.
  We say that $f : [0,1]^d \to \R$ belongs to $C^{m,\alpha}([0,1]^d)$
  if $f$ is $m$ times continuously differentiable with
  \[
    \| f \|_{C^{m,\alpha}}
    := \max
       \Bigl\{ 
         \| f \|_{L^\infty},
         \quad
         \max_{\beta \in \N_0^d, |\beta| = m} \,\,
           \sup_{x,y \in [0,1]^d, x \neq y} \,\,
             \frac{|\partial^\beta f (x) - \partial^\beta f(y)|}{\norm{x-y}^\alpha}
       \Bigr\}
    < \infty
    .
  \]
  Then, as a subset of $\XX = L^p ([0,1]^d)$, the set
  \[
    \SC
    := \bigl\{ f \in C^{m,\alpha}([0,1]^d) \,\,:\,\, \| f \|_{C^{m,\alpha}} \leq 1 \bigr\}
  \]
  satisfies $\md(\SC) = \frac{d}{r}$,
  there exists a Borel probability measure on $\XX = L^p ([0,1]^d)$
  that is critical for $\SC$,
  and the family of neural networks
  \(
    (\CalA_n)_{n \in \N} = \bigl(\CalNN_n (3,\R^d)\bigr)_{n \in \N}
  \)
  defined in \Cref{prop:NNApproximationOfControlledComplexity} (with $g = 3$)
  is optimal for $\SC$ in the class of families of controlled complexity in $L^p([0,1]^d)$.
  In particular, a phase transition as in
  \Cref{thm:PhaseTransitionForFamiliesWithControlledComplexity} occurs.
title: Proposition 15 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Definition \cite{gel2013spaces,kashpirovsky1978equality,van1987functional} of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] For $\alpha,\beta > 0$, we define the one-sided Gelfand--Shilov spaces as
\[ \mathcal S_{\alpha} = \{ \phi \in \mathcal{S} : \exists a > 0, D > 0 : |\phi(x)| \le D \exp(-\alpha a |x|^{1/\alpha}) \} \]
and
\[ \mathcal S^{\beta} = \{ \phi \in \mathcal{S} : \exists b > 0, D > 0 : |\hat \phi(x)| \le D \exp(-\beta b |x|^{1/\beta}) \} \]

[Corollary 41 (The Metropolis--Hastings algorithm converges; Theorem \ref{thm:mhintro}) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $(\XX,\XXA)$ be a measurable space, $\lambda$ a $\sigma$-finite measure on it,
and let the target be $\pi(A) = \int_{A} p \dd\lambda$ for a measurable map
$p : \XX \to (0,\infty)$ with $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$. Let the proposal be the
Markov kernel $Q(A \mid x) = \int_{A} q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)$, given by an
$\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable map $q : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ with
$\int_{\XX} q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$ for every $x \in \XX$, define the
acceptance probability
\[
  a : \XX\times\XX \to [0,1], \qquad
  a(y \mid x) := \min\Bigl\{ 1,\ \frac{p(y)\,q(x \mid y)}{p(x)\,q(y \mid x)} \Bigr\}
  \quad\bigl(:= 1 \text{ when } q(y \mid x) = 0\bigr),
\]
and let $T$ be the Metropolis--Hastings kernel
\[
  T(A \mid x) := \int_{A} a(y \mid x)\,q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) + r(x)\,\ind_{A}(x),
  \qquad
  r(x) := 1 - \int_{\XX} a(y \mid x)\,q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) .
\]
Assume
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item $q(y \mid x) > 0$ for $(\lambda\otimes\lambda)$-almost every $(x,y) \in \XX\times\XX$;
  \item for every $x \in \XX$ the set $\{ y \in \XX : q(y \mid x) > 0 \text{ and } q(x \mid y) > 0 \} \in \XXA$ has positive $\lambda$-measure.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and
$\tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - \pi} \to 0$ for every initial distribution $\mu \in \Prob$.

Both hypotheses hold in either of the following two cases, which are the ones met in
practice and which give Theorem \ref{thm:mhintro}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item $q(y \mid x) > 0$ for every $(x,y) \in \XX\times\XX$;
  \item $q$ is symmetric, $q(y \mid x) = q(x \mid y)$ for all $(x,y)$, and
        $q(y \mid x) > 0$ for $(\lambda\otimes\lambda)$-almost every $(x,y)$.
\end{enumerate}

DRAFT; independent referee pending. For a unit-rate Poisson process N, M^n_t=1-t+nN_{t/n}, 0<=t<=1, is a nonnegative true martingale in its own natural filtration. Its paths eventually equal 1-t on the entire interval almost surely, because the first Poisson jump time is positive. Thus it converges uniformly almost surely to a continuous deterministic non-martingale. Uniform integrability is absent: E[M^n_t]=1 but E[1-t]=1-t. Joint path convergence alone cannot pass a renormalized observable's conditional martingale identity to the limit.

body:
[Definition 2 (Admissible deterministic diagonal resolution) of arXiv:2606.16662, '2606.16662'] A deterministic diagonal resolution for a finite family \(\cM\) assigns to
each label \(\tau\in\cM\) deterministic diagonal Volterra operators
\(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda\) and \(\Ctr^\tau_\Lambda\) such that
\begin{equation}
        D^\tau_\Lambda=\Ret^\tau_\Lambda+\Ctr^\tau_\Lambda .
\end{equation}
The first term is retained and the second is subtracted from the raw mixed
block.  The resolution is dyadically admissible if, for each label with
\(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda\ne0\), there exists \(\delta_\tau>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
        \|\Ret^\tau_{\Lambda,N,Q}P_Qw\|_{C_TL^2}
        \le C_{\mathfrak P}N^{-\delta_\tau}
        \bigl(\|P_Qw\|_{L_T^\infty L^2}
        +\|P_Q\partial_tw\|_{L_T^\infty L^2}\bigr)
\end{equation}
for \(0<T\le T_0\) and \(Q\le c_{\rm ap}N\), uniformly in \(\Lambda\).
For every fixed \((N,Q)\), the corresponding two-time scalar kernels are
also required to converge in
\(C_{t,s}\cL(\ell_q^2,\ell_q^2)\).

The retained term may be any prescribed finite linear combination of scalar
diagonal branches, provided the combined kernel satisfies
\eqref{eq:retained-block-bound} and fixed-block convergence.  The raw
resolution is \(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda=D^\tau_\Lambda\), while the fully
Wick-subtracted resolution is \(\Ret^\tau_\Lambda=0\).
title: Admissible deterministic diagonal resolution

Fix n>=2 and a finite interval [a,b]. Let probability laws F_j supported on [a,b] converge weakly to F. Suppose each F_j is n-completely mixable: there is a coupling of n variables with marginal F_j and sum equal almost surely to n mu_j, where mu_j=integral x dF_j(x). Then F is supported on [a,b], mu_j tends to mu=integral x dF(x), and F is n-completely mixable with constant sum n mu. In particular, fixing one center c throughout preserves center c under the weak limit. The order n stays fixed; feasibility with n changing along the approximations does not imply this conclusion for any fixed order.
Fixed integer order n>=2
All marginal laws supported on one common compact real interval
Weak convergence and constant-sum couplings as stated

[Thm t:def-YM of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] There exist a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ satisfying
$$
\mathcal{S}(\Sigma\setminus\{a_{2g+2}\},T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g})\subset \mathcal{H}\subset\mathcal{S}^\prime(\Sigma\setminus\{a_{2g+2}\},T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g}),
$$
with continuous embeddings and a measure $\mu_{\operatorname{YM}}$ of total mass $Z_{\operatorname{YM}}$ on $\mathcal{H}$ endowed with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra such that the following holds
\begin{enumerate}
 \item for $\mu_{\operatorname{YM}}$ almost every $A$, $\iota_V(A)=0$;
 \item for every $p\geqslant 1$, for every $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_p$ in $\Omega^1_c(\Sigma\setminus\{a_{2g+2}\},\mathfrak{g})$ and for every Borel set of $ \mathbb{R} ^p$, one has
 $$
 \mu_{\operatorname{YM}}\left(\left\{(\langle A,\psi_1\rangle,\ldots,\langle A,\psi_p\rangle)\in B\right\}\right)=\mathbb{M}_{\operatorname{YM}}\left(\left\{(\langle A(\xi,\mathrm{b}),\psi_1\rangle,\ldots,\langle A(\xi,\mathrm{b}),\psi_p\rangle)\in B\right\}\right);
 $$
 \item for every $\kappa>0$ and for $\mu_{\operatorname{YM}}$ almost every $A$, $A\in H_{\operatorname{loc}}^{-1-\kappa}\left(\Sigma\setminus\{a_{2g+2}\},T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g}\right).$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Existence of the Yang--Mills measure

body:
Let S={4^k:k>=1}, sigma_n=min(sqrt(n)/4,1+dist(n,S)/4) for n>=0, and let epsilon be one fair random sign. On the ray with edges j-1 to j assign tau_j=1+(sigma_j-sigma_(j-1)) epsilon. These weights lie in [3/4,5/4], and their unique minimizing path to n has T_n=n+sigma_n epsilon. Its mean is n, variance is sigma_n^2, and E exp(alpha |T_n-E T_n|/sqrt(Var T_n))=exp(alpha) for every alpha>0. Define a as the upper uniform concentration threshold: inf q for which some alpha>0 makes sup_(n>=1) E exp(alpha |T_n-E T_n|/n^q) finite. Define b as the lower uniform variance threshold: sup q for which some N has inf_(n>N) Var T_n/n^(2q)>0. Then a=1/2 and b=0. The weights share epsilon and are nonstationary; this is not an iid undirected Z^2 law.
A ray graph
Dependent nonstationary edge weights driven by a common fair sign
The stated sigma_n sequence

body: [Prop 3 of arXiv:2608.27022, 'On LCK Geometry of Gauduchon Connections'] If $\omega$ is an lcK metric on a compact complex manifold $(M, J)$ of $\mathrm{dim}_{\mathbb{C}}\geq 3$ such that $\Ric^{t,1}=f\omega$ for some smooth function $f$ on $M$, then either $f\equiv 0$ or $\omega$ is globally conformally K\"ahler and $f$ has a sign.

[Lemma l:localized_energy_inequality of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] In the setting of Proposition (prop:local_energy of the paper), for all $\phi\in C^{\infty}_{{\rm c}}(B)$ with $\int_B \phi^2=1$ and $\psi\in C^{\infty}_{{\rm c}}((t_0-\varrho^2,t_0])$, it holds that
\begin{align}
\nonumber
\psi^2(t)\int_{B}  \phi^2 |\widetilde{v}_\phi(t)|^2 
&\leq
  \int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\partial_t (\psi^2)\int_{B} \phi^2 |\widetilde{v}_\phi|^2 \\
  \nonumber
&+ 2\int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t \psi^2\int_B \pi \nabla\cdot (\phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)-\nu \nabla \widetilde{v}_\phi : \nabla (\phi^2  \widetilde{v}_\phi) - F: \nabla (\phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)\\
\nonumber
& + \sum_{n}\int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\psi^2\int_B\nabla \widetilde{\pi}_n \cdot (\zeta_n\cdot \nabla) (\phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)\\ 
\nonumber
&+\sum_{n}\int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\psi^2 \int_B\phi^2 |-\nabla \widetilde{\pi}_n + (\zeta_n\cdot \nabla) \widetilde{v}_\phi + G_n|^2\\
&+2 \sum_n \int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^t\psi^2 \Big(\int_B [-\nabla\widetilde{\pi}_n + (\zeta_n \cdot \nabla) \widetilde{v}_\phi+G_n ]\cdot( \phi^2 \widetilde{v}_\phi)\Big)\,\mathrm{d} W^n,

\end{align} 
 a.s.\ for all $t\in I=(t_0-\varrho^2,t_0)$.
title: Lemma l:localized_energy_inequality of arXiv:2607.15140

[Lem decomposing F into a composition of mobius transformations of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $(T,v)$ be a rooted tree of maximum degree at most $\Delta\in \mathbb{N}$. 
    Let $n\in \mathbb{N}$ and let $u\in S^*_T(v,n)$.
    The function $F_{T,n;u}$ as defined above can be written as $f_{\lambda_n}\circ  \cdots f_{\lambda_1}$,
    where $\lambda_{i}$ is equal to the ratio $R_{T_{n,i},w_{i}}$ of the rooted tree $({T}_{n,i},w_i)$ for $i=1,\ldots, n$ and is contained in $[\ell_\Delta(\lambda),\lambda]$.
title: Lem decomposing F into a composition of mobius transformations of arXiv:2603.17858

body: [Theorem \cite{martin2020stationary}, Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Running the queue-length process $Q_i$ in its stationary distribution~(equation initial2 of the paper), and recording the corresponding outputs $d\left(i\right)$, produces the stationary distribution $\nu_{\lambda,\mu-\lambda}^{\left(2\right)}$ of the two-type ASEP on $\mathbb{Z}$. In this distribution, the density of first-class particles is $\lambda$, while the density of second-class particles is $\mu-\lambda$. body:
[Cor 13 (Quasistationary coupling) of arXiv:2604.12853, 'Coupling Markov Chains \\with a Common Image Chain'] Let $\Xoriginal$, $\Yoriginal$ and $\Zoriginal$ be quasistationary Markov chains, with state spaces $A$, $B$, and $C$, and absorbing states $\rho_A$, $\rho_B$, and $\rho_C$ respectively. Suppose for maps $f:A \to C$ and $g: B \to C$ satisfying $f^{-1}(\rho_C) = \{\rho_A\}$ and $g^{-1}(\rho_C) = \{\rho_B\}$ that 
    \[
    (f(\Xoriginal_t))_{t \ge 0} \eqdist \Zoriginal \eqdist (g(\Yoriginal_t))_{t \ge 0}.
    \]
    Then  $\Xoriginal, \Yoriginal$ and $\Zoriginal$ have equal absorption probabilities, say $\lambda$, and there is a quasistationary Markov chain $(X_t,Y_t)_{t \ge 0}$ with 
    absorbing state $(\rho_A, \rho_B)$ and absorption probability $\lambda$ such that $(X_t)_{t \ge 0} \eqdist \Xoriginal$, $(Y_t)_{t \ge 0} \eqdist \Yoriginal$, and $f(X_t) = g(Y_t)$ for all $t \ge 0$. In particular, 
    the absorption times of the coordinates coincide. The marginal chains $X$ and $Y$ may be taken to be conditionally independent given $(f(X_t))_{t \ge 0}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Quasistationary coupling

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2604.15874, 'On Continuous Data Assimilation for a class of 2D and 3D stochastic non-Newtonian fluids o'] Assume that condition \eqref{third-grade-paremeters-res} and Hypothesis \ref{hyp-noise} are satisfied. Also, let $\f \in \Vbb^*$ and $\Urm_0 \in \Hbb$. 
	Then, the system \eqref{STGF-CDA} admits a unique strong solution $\Urm$ with $\Pbb$-a.s. paths in

body:
[Lemma lem:measurable-operator-field-calculus of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] From the preceding definitions we obtain the following three properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.1em,itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt]
 \item If $S$ and $T$ are measurable, then
 \[
  S^*,\ ST\quad\text{are measurable operator fields}.
 \]
 Consequently, measurable bounded operator fields are closed under adjoints,
 products, and polynomials.

 \item Let $(T^{(\ell)})_{\ell\ge1}$ be measurable bounded operator fields.  If
 \begin{equation*}
  T_\mu^{(\ell)}\xrightarrow[\ell\to\infty]{\rm s}T_\mu
  \qquad\text{for every }\mu,
 \end{equation*}
 then $T=(T_\mu)_\mu$ is measurable.

 \item Suppose $T$ is measurable and every $T_\mu$ is positive,
 self-adjoint, and compact.  Then, for every $F\in C_b([0,\infty))$, every
 open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$, and every $n\ge1$,
 \begin{equation}
  \begin{gathered}
   F(T),\ \mathbf 1_I(T)\quad\text{are measurable operator fields},\\
   \mu\longmapsto\lambda_n(T_\mu)
   \quad\text{is measurable}.
  \end{gathered}
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:measurable-operator-field-calculus of arXiv:2608.02459

body:
[Theorem thm:terminal-lift of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Assume Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) and
(ass:drift-multiplier of the paper).  For every
regular weight $w$, every interval $I=(r_0,r_1)$, and
$
 F\in H_{x,w}^1(I),\, \eta\in H^1(\mu_{r_1}),
$
one has
\begin{equation}
 D_x\mathcal U_I(F,\eta)
 =\mathcal P_{1,I}^{-1}(D_xF,D_x\eta)
 \in H_{x,w}^1(I;\mathbb R^d).
 
\end{equation}
In particular, for $\psi\in H^1(\mu_T)$, recall
$v^\psi=\mathcal U(0,\psi)$ and set
\begin{equation*}
p^\psi:=\mathcal P_1^{-1}(0,D_x\psi).
\end{equation*}
The terminal identities are
\begin{equation}
 p^\psi=D_xv^\psi,\qquad D_xp^\psi=D_x^2v^\psi,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}_T^Xp^\psi=D_x\psi(X_T).
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every $\alpha\geq0$, $v^\psi$ is the unique
order-$\alpha$ occupation Sobolev solution with data $(0,\psi)$, and
there exists a constant $C=C(T,\lambda,\Lambda,M_1(a),\Lambda_b)>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert v^\psi\right\rVert_0^2+\left\lVert D_xv^\psi\right\rVert_0^2
 +\left\lVert D_x^2v^\psi\right\rVert_0^2
 \leq C\norm\psi_{H^1(\mu_T)}^2.
 
\end{equation}
title: Theorem thm:terminal-lift of arXiv:2608.16119

body:
[Theorem 12 (Deterministic resolvent comparison) of arXiv:2609.01770, 'Support of Dyson Brownian Motion'] Let \(Y_n\) be a deterministic Hermitian \(n\times n\) matrix, and there exists a constant $K>0$, such that 
$\supp(\mu_{Y_n})\subset [-K,K]$. Let \(\mu\) be a
compactly supported probability measure. Assume that there exist a constant
\(\fc>0\), scales \(\varepsilon=\varepsilon_n\geq n^{-1}\) and
\(\eta=\eta_n>0\), and an error parameter \(\delta_n>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
\eta\leq n^{-\fc}\varepsilon,
\qquad
\delta_n\to 0.
\end{equation}
Let \(u=u_n\in\bR\) satisfy \(\dist(u,\supp\mu)\geq\varepsilon\), and assume
\begin{equation}
\sup_{z\in B(u+\ri\eta,\eta/2)}
\bigl|m_{Y_n}(z)-m_{\mu}(z)\bigr|
\leq \frac{\delta_n}{n\eta}.
\end{equation}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\lambda_i^{(n)}\notin[u-\eta,u+\eta],
\qquad 1\leq i\leq n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Deterministic resolvent comparison

body:
[Lem 191 (annealed first moment bounds for 
$E^{\sigma,\tau}$ and $E^{\frozen,\sigma,\tau}$
with $\sigma,\tau\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let
$Q^{\sigma,\tau}=E^{\sigma,\tau}+\tilde{Q}^{\sigma,\tau}$ as in Definitions~\ref{d:Q} and \ref{d:tQ}. Then, for $N$ large enough, we have
	\[\bbE
	\Big|\Delta E^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d)\Big| 
	\le L^{O(1)}\bigg\{\eta\delta^{1/2} + \frac{\BUCKETS\delta}{N}
	\bigg\}
	\]
for all $\sigma,\tau\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$. The same bound holds with $E^\frozen$ in place of $E$.
\begin{proof}
This is similar
to the proof of Corollary~\ref{c:Q.first.quenched}. Recall 
that Lemma~\ref{l:qv.simplification} implies
	\[
	\Big|\Delta E^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d)\Big| 
	\le O\bigg(
	\eta^2
	+\sum_{\rho\in\{\sigma,\tau\}}\bigg[
	\eta\Big(\Delta\tilde{Q}^\rho(q_d)\Big)^{1/2}
	+\Big( \Delta \bar{D}^\rho(q_d)\Big)^2
	\bigg]\bigg)\,.
	\]
By Lemmas~\ref{l:barD.II.second}--\ref{l:barD.Ising.second}, for all $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$ we have
	\[\E\Big[\Delta\bar{D}^\sigma(q_d)^2\Big]
	\le\frac{ L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS\delta}{N}
	\,.\]
By Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched} and the bound $\E[(\MAX_N)^2]\le L^{O(1)}$ from Proposition~\ref{p:Y.kolmogorov}, for all $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$ we have
	\[
	\E\bigg[\Big(\Delta\tilde{Q}^\sigma(q_d)\Big)^{1/2}\bigg]
	\le L^{O(1)} \delta^{1/2}\,.
	\]
Combining the bounds gives the claim, recalling that $\eta\ll\delta$ from Assumption~\ref{a:params}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:U_process* of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Suppose $z=0$ and $\widehat{\delta}>0$. For any $r> 0$, $\frac{V(-r)+r}{r}$ has distribution $\mathcal{B}(\frac{\widehat{\delta}}{2},\frac{\delta}{2})$.
\item The family $(P^z_*,z\ge 0)$ defines a time-homogeneous Feller process. For any $z\ge 0$, the process  $\left(V(-r)+r,\, r\ge 0\right)$ is a homogeneous $(\mathscr{W}^*_r)_{r\ge 0}$-adapted Feller process starting from $z$. 
\item Suppose $z>0$ and write $\mathrm{x}:=\inf\{r\ge 0\,:\, V(-r)<z\}$.  We have $\frac{z}{\mathrm{x}+z}\sim\mathcal{B}(\frac{\delta}{2},1)$ and conditionally on  $\{{\rm{x}}= x \}$, $\frac{ V(-x)+x}{x+z}\sim \mathcal{B}(\frac{\delta+\widehat{\delta}}{2},1)$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. Scarce calibration, the ratio-metric criterion (P41, 240 calibration rows, split B, three-vertex form, registered and R_1 choices side by side): P41 (a) HELD: at n_cal = 240 the R_1 blend reads +1.17 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered three-vertex blend reads -1.83); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R_1 blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells (at least 25); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.38 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. [Lemma Lemme Propriétés des particules of arXiv:2504.03627, 'Richardson’s model and the contact process with stirring: long time behavior.'] \begin{enumerate}
        \item At each time $t>0$, the positions $(P_t^a)_{a\in \mathbb Z^2}$ of the particles at time t form a partition of $\mathbb Z^2$.
        \item The process $(\Tilde{\xi}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ verifies the strong Markov property. 
        \item Once a particle $a\in \mathbb Z^2$ is infected, it is infected forever:
        $$\text{if }\Tilde{\xi}_t(a)=(1,P_t^a),\text{ then: }\forall s\ge t,~\Tilde{\xi}_s(a)=(1,P_s^a).$$ 
        \item The origin is healthy at time $t$ if and only if a healthy particle is on the origin at time $t$:
        $$0\notin \xi_t \iff\exists a\in \mathbb Z^d,~\Tilde{\xi}_t(a)=(0,0).$$ 
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma Lemme Propriétés des particules of arXiv:2504.03627

[Proposition proposition1124 of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Fix some $d\in\mathbb{N}_+$ and some $\sigma\in(0,\sigma_0)$, and consider the following set of subspaces 
$$
\mathcal{W}(d,\sigma):=\{E\in\operatorname{Gr}(d,\mathcal{D}_R):Y(E)=Y_\sigma(E)\}
.$$ Let $m_Z\in\mathbb{N}$ be such that $$\dim\mathcal{D}_R\leq m_Z^2.$$
Then we can find a constant $C_{(proposition1124 of the paper)}>1$ depending only on the module $Z$ and the coefficients $R_1,\cdots,R_n$ such that for any $\delta>0$,
   \begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
&\mathbb{P}^{\Omega_{\text{good}}}(\inf_{B\in\mathfrak{Reg}(d), \operatorname{Span}\{B_i\}\in\mathcal{W}(d,\sigma)}\|\mathfrak{D}_aB\|\leq\delta)\\&\leq \delta^{2(N-1-m_Z^6)}(C_{(proposition1124 of the paper)}N)^{(D_d+2)2m_Z^2N}\sigma^{-4(N-1)m_Z^2}.\end{aligned}
   \end{equation}In particular, taking $
   \delta=\sigma^{4m_Z^2}(C_{(proposition1124 of the paper)}N)^{-8m_Z^2D_d-1}$, we get, whenever $N$ is sufficiently large, 
   $$
 \mathbb{P}^{\Omega_{\text{good}}}(\inf_{B\in\mathfrak{Reg}(d), \operatorname{Span}\{B_i\}\in\mathcal{W}(d,\sigma)}\|\mathfrak{D}_aB\|\leq\ \sigma^{4m_Z^2}(C_{(proposition1124 of the paper)}N)^{-8m_Z^2D_d-1})\leq\exp(-N\log N).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition proposition1124 of arXiv:2606.01664

[Theorem smoothsequence1 of arXiv:2412.04013, 'Rate estimates for total variation distance with applications\thanks{The author gratefully'] Let $F,F_{n}\in (\mathbb{D}^{\infty,\infty})^{d}$, $n\in \mathbb{N}$ be a family of functionals
with corresponding Malliavin matrices $\sigma,\sigma_{n}$.
Assume that, for all $r>0$, $q\geq 1$,
$$
E[|\mathrm{det}(\sigma)|^{-r}]+\sup_{n\in \mathbb{N}}E[|\mathrm{det}(\sigma_{n})|^{-r}]<\infty,
$$
and also 
$$
\Vert F\Vert_{q,r}+\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\Vert F_{n}\Vert_{q,r}<\infty.
$$	
Then for all $\epsilon>0$ there is a constant $C_{\epsilon}$ such that
$$
d_{TV}(F_{n},F)\leq C_{\epsilon}d_{FM}^{1-\epsilon}(F_{n},F).
$$
Furthermore, for the respective densities $f,f_{n}$,
$$
\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}|f_{n}(x)-f(x)|\leq C_{\epsilon}d_{FM}^{1-\epsilon}(F_{n},F).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 47 (Exact form of the mixture tail) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] In the setting of Proposition~\ref{prop:mixture}, fix $x > 0$ and an adapted posterior $(\rho_t)$ with $\rho_t \ll \mu$, and set
\[
  \cA_x := \Bigl\{\exists\,t : \int_\Lambda \log E_t(\lambda)\,\rho_t(\dd\lambda)
          - \KL(\rho_t\|\mu) \geq x\Bigr\},
  \qquad
  \cV_x := \{\exists\,t : \overline E_t \geq e^x\},
\]
so that $\cA_x$ is the event of~\eqref{eq:mixturePAC} in the exponential case $E_t(\lambda) = \exp(\lambda Y_t - \overline\Psi_t(\lambda))$.
Then $\cA_x \subseteq \cV_x$ and
\[
  \PP(\cA_x) = \PP(\cV_x) - \PP\bigl(\cV_x \setminus \cA_x\bigr),
  \qquad
  \cV_x\setminus \cA_x
  = \cV_x \cap \bigl\{\forall\,t:\ \KL(\rho_t\|\rho^*_t) > \log\overline E_t - x\bigr\},
\]
the second event being read at those $t$ with $\overline E_t>0$, the only ones at which either event can occur.
It vanishes when $\rho_t \equiv \rho^*_t$, at which $\cA_x = \cV_x$.
If $\overline E$ is a martingale with $\overline E_0 = 1$ and $\overline E_t \to 0$ a.s., then Theorem~\ref{thm:firstpassage-exact} at level $e^x$ evaluates $\PP(\cV_x)$ and
\begin{equation}
  \PP(\cA_x)
  = e^{-x}\Bigl(1 - \E\bigl[J\,\ind\{\sigma < \infty\}\bigr]\Bigr)
    - \PP\bigl(\cV_x\setminus \cA_x\bigr),
\end{equation}
with $\sigma := \inf\{t : \overline E_t \geq e^x\}$ and $J := \overline E_\sigma - e^x \geq 0$ the overshoot.
Under those hypotheses equality holds in~\eqref{eq:mixturePAC} exactly when $\PP(\cV_x\setminus \cA_x) = 0$ and $J = 0$ a.s.\ on $\{\sigma<\infty\}$.
For a mixture that is a strict supermartingale the first-passage term includes, beyond the overshoot, the predictable loss shed before the crossing and the mass that never crosses. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact form of the mixture tail

body:
Let L be an exactly quadratic loss with symmetric positive semidefinite Hessian H. At theta let G=grad L(theta) satisfy A=G^T H G>0. Let g_B be the mean of B>=1 iid finite-second-moment gradients with mean G and per-example covariance Sigma. Write C=tr(H Sigma)>=0 and B_noise=C/A. For the update theta_next=theta-eta*g_B, E[L(theta_next)]=L(theta)-eta*||G||^2+(eta^2/2)*(A+C/B), exactly. The unique real minimizing step is eta_opt(B)=||G||^2/(A+C/B)=eta_max/(1+B_noise/B), where eta_max=||G||^2/A. The optimal expected loss decrease is Delta_opt(B)=Delta_max/(1+B_noise/B), where Delta_max=||G||^4/(2*A). If B_noise>0, batch B=B_noise in the continuous interpolation achieves half Delta_max. For a general smooth loss, the source obtains these expressions from a quadratic Taylor model; without a controlled remainder they are not exact guarantees, iteration-complexity bounds, or global convergence rates.

\[
   \mathbb{E}\left\lvert X+Y\right\rvert^{r}\ge \mathbb{E}\left\lvert X-Y\right\rvert^{r}
\]
holds for every random vector \((X,Y)\) satisfying either the discrete model (equation eq:discrete-model of the paper)-(equation eq:discrete-positive of the paper) or the density model (equation eq:density-positive of the paper)-(equation eq:density-model of the paper), with \(\mathbb{E}\left\lvert X\right\rvert^{r}<\infty\), if and only if \(0<r\le2\).

body:
[Thm 12 of arXiv:2608.30173, '2608.30173'] There exist $\va_1\in(0,1)$ and $C>0$, depending only on the fixed
data, such that the following assertions hold for every
$\va\in(0,\va_1)$ and every normalized function
$
u\in\mathcal D\cap\V(u_\infty,\ell,\delta;\va)
$
satisfying
$
\|\mathcal R_u-r_\infty\|_{C^0(\Omega)}<\va
$
and
$
\int_\Omega u^{\frac{2n}{n-2}}\,\ud x=1.
$
Let
\[
u=\sigma+w
\]
be the decomposition determined by \eqref{eq:vp} and \eqref{eq:decomposition-1}. Recall from \eqref{eq:Gu} that
\[
 \mathfrak G(u)
 =
 \left(
 \int_\Omega
 |\mathcal R_u-r_\infty|^{\frac{2n}{n+2}}
 u^{\frac{2n}{n-2}}\,\ud x
 \right)^{\frac{n+2}{2n}}.
\]
Then we have
\begin{itemize}

\item[(i)] \textbf{Estimate of the amplitude parameters.}

If $u_\infty\equiv0$, then
\be
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}|\alpha_k-1|
={}&
O\left(\mathfrak G(u)\right)+
O\left(\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{2-n}\right)
+
O\left(\sum_{i\neq j}\Lambda_{i,j}\right).
\end{aligned}
\ee

If $u_\infty>0$, then
\be
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}|\alpha_k-1|
={}&
O\left(\mathfrak G(u)\right)+
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}
\lambda_k^{-\frac{n-2}{2}}
\right)
+
O\left(
\sum_{i\neq j}\Lambda_{i,j}
\right).
\end{aligned}
\ee

Under the additional assumption that
$
Y_\Omega(u)\geq r_\infty,
$
we have
\be
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}|\alpha_k-1|
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
O\left( \mathfrak G(u)\right)
+
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}
\lambda_k^{
2-n}
\right),
& u_\infty\equiv0,\\[4mm]
\displaystyle
O\left( \mathfrak G(u)\right),
& u_\infty>0.
\end{cases}
\ee

\item[(ii)] \textbf{Estimate of the orthogonal remainder.}

If $u_\infty\equiv0$, then
\be
\begin{aligned}
\|w\|
={}&
O\left( \mathfrak G(u)\right)\\
&+
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{-\frac{n+2}{2}}
\right)+O\left(
\sum_{i\neq j}
\Lambda_{i,j}^{\frac{n+2}{2(n-2)}}
\left(
\ln\Lambda_{i,j}^{-1}
\right)^{\frac{n+2}{2n}}
\right),
& n>6,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}
\lambda_k^{-4}(\ln\lambda_k)^{\frac23}
\right)+O\left(
\sum_{i\neq j}
\Lambda_{i,j}
\left(
\ln\Lambda_{i,j}^{-1}
\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}
\right),
& n=6,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{2-n}
\right)+O\left(
\sum_{i\neq j}\Lambda_{i,j}
\right),
& n=3,4,5,
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\ee

If $u_\infty>0$, then
\be
\begin{aligned}
\|w\|
={}&
O
\left( \mathfrak G(u)
\right)\\
&+
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
O\left(\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}
\lambda_k^{-\frac{n+2}{4}}
(\ln\lambda_k)^{\frac{n+2}{2n}}\right)+O\left(\sum_{i\neq j}
\Lambda_{i,j}^{\frac{n+2}{2(n-2)}}
\left(
\ln\Lambda_{i,j}^{-1}
\right)^{\frac{n+2}{2n}}\right),
&n\geq6,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle
O\left(\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{\frac{2-n}{2}}\right)+O\left(\sum_{i\neq j}\Lambda_{i,j}\right),
&n=3,4,5,
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\ee

If $u_\infty\equiv0$ and $Y_\Omega(u)\geq r_\infty$, then, 
\be
\begin{aligned}
\|w\|
={}&
O\left(\mathfrak G(u)\right)+
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{-\frac{n+2}{2}}(\ln\lambda_k)^\frac{n+2}{2n}
\right),
& n\geq6,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{2-n}
\right),
& n=3,4,5.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\ee

If $u_\infty>0$ and $Y_\Omega(u)\geq r_\infty$, then
\be
\|w\|
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
O\left(\mathfrak G(u)\right)+
O\left(
\mathfrak G(u)^{\frac{(n+2)}{2(n-2)}(1+\gamma)}
\left(-\ln\mathfrak G(u)\right)^{\frac{n+2}{2n}}\right),\quad
&n\geq6,\\[5mm]
\displaystyle
O\left(\mathfrak G(u)\right), \quad
&n=3,4,5.
\end{cases}
\ee

\item[(iii)] \textbf{Estimate of the regular-part parameters.}

Suppose that $u_\infty>0$. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\bm z'|^2
={}&
o(|\bm z''|^2)+
O\left(\mathfrak G(u)^{1+\gamma}\right)+
O\left(
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}
\lambda_k^{-\frac{n-2}{2}(1+\gamma)}
\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Under the additional assumption that
$
Y_\Omega(u)\geq r_\infty,
$
we have
\[
|\bm z'|^2
=
o(|\bm z''|^2)
+
O\left(\mathfrak G(u)^{1+\gamma}\right).
\]

\end{itemize}

[Lemma 12 (Contraction) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] For every $h \in \Sign$ with $h(\XX) = 0$ and every number $n \in \Nz$,
\[
  \tv{T^{n} \circ h} \;\le\; \tv{h} .
\]
In particular $\tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - T^{n}\circ\nu} \le \tv{\mu-\nu}$ for all
$\mu,\nu \in \Prob$, and the map

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. For every finite positive integer N,P,M, let X_R=U_R V_R^T/sqrt(N) have independent Rademacher factor entries and X_G=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N) have independent standard Gaussian factor entries. With d=NP, D=d M^2[12(N+P)+8]/N^4 and T=893026 d^5 M^10/N^5, for 0<s<=D/(322560 T), I(X_R;sqrt(s)X_R+G)-I(X_G;sqrt(s)X_G+G)>=D s^4/80 and mmse(X_R)-mmse(X_G)>=D s^3/12. Here each MMSE uses its own Gaussian observation at SNR s and Frobenius loss. The SNR interval shrinks with dimension, so this is not a counterexample to limiting Gaussian-factor extremality at fixed SNR.
N,P,M positive finite integers
All factor entries independent within each model
Independent Gaussian observation noise
Dimension-dependent SNR interval as stated

Target 2, finite-size special case. Proof draft, unaudited.
This does not settle extremality at a fixed SNR after the extensive-rank limit.

Let N,P,M>=1 be integers. Compare the product signals

 X_R=U_R V_R^T/sqrt(N),   X_G=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N),

where the entries in U_R,V_R are independent uniform signs and the
entries in U_G,V_G are independent standard Gaussians; all factor
arrays are independent in their respective models. Let G be an
independent standard Gaussian observation matrix. Set d=NP, b=M/N.
Define

 D = d M^2/N^4 [12(N+P)+8] > 0,
 T = d^5 M^10/N^5 (893026),
 s_0 = D/(322560 T) > 0.

Then for 0<s<=s_0 the proposed conclusions are

 I(X_R;sqrt(s)X_R+G)-I(X_G;sqrt(s)X_G+G) >= D s^4/80,

 mmse(X_R|sqrt(s)X_R+G)-mmse(X_G|sqrt(s)X_G+G)
      >= D s^3/12.                                      (1)

Here mmse denotes E||X-E[X|Y]||_F^2, the MMSE of the scaled product.
For the unscaled product UV^T the MSE is N times larger; normalization
by NP preserves the strict comparison.

## Proof

Both vectorized products have mean zero, covariance b I_d, globally
symmetric distributions, and finite moments of every order. Their
third cumulants vanish. The fourth-cumulant formula in the expansion
proof gives

 ||K4_G||^2-||K4_R||^2
  = (M/N^2)^2 d [ (36-4)+12(P-1)+12(N-1)]
  = D.                                                   (2)

The rectangle terms cancel. The fourth moments of the factor laws are
3 and 1, respectively. In particular, the Gaussian FACTOR product has
the larger fourth-cumulant norm; it is not a Gaussian vector signal.

The tenth moments of a scalar standard Gaussian and a scalar sign
are 945 and 1. The explicit factor-moment bound (11) of
finite_moment_expansion.md gives

 E||X_G||^10+E||X_R||^10
    <= d^5 M^10/N^5 (945^2+1)=T.                         (3)

Subtracting their mutual-information expansions gives D s^4/48,
with absolute remainder at most 2688 T s^5. For s<=s_0 this is at
most D s^4/120, proving the first inequality of (1), since
1/48-1/120=1/80.

For the MMSE use equation (7) and the expansion of F from
finite_moment_expansion.md. For bounded symmetric signals,

 mmse(X|sqrt(s)X+G)
   = db-db^2 s+db^3 s^2-(db^4+||K4||^2/6)s^3+Q(s),

 |Q(s)| <= 26880 E||X||^10 s^4,                         (4)

because the fourth derivative of F is bounded by
2^4 8! E||X||^10 and the third-order Taylor remainder divides by
4!=24. This bound passes to finite tenth moments under the centered
and covariance-normalized truncation in Section C of that proof.

The needed MMSE convergence follows directly: posterior overlap is
an integral of

 ||E[X phi(y-sqrt(s)X)]||^2 / E[phi(y-sqrt(s)X)],

which converges pointwise on compact y-sets under L^2 convergence of
the signal and is bounded by E[||X||^2 phi(y-sqrt(s)X)] by conditional
Cauchy-Schwarz. Its integral outside ||y||<=L is at most
E[||X||^2 1_{||sqrt(s)X+G||>L}], which vanishes uniformly for the
truncation sequence by its uniformly bounded fourth moments and
Gaussian tails. Thus posterior overlaps and MMSE converge. The same
argument works at s=0 directly.

Subtracting (4) gives a leading difference D s^3/6 and error at most
26880 T s^4. At s<=s_0 this is at most D s^3/12, proving the second
inequality of (1).

Every denominator is positive, including N, T and 322560. The endpoint
s=0 gives equality, so strict comparison is asserted only for s>0.
The constants are deliberately conservative.

## What the statement does and does not decide

For every fixed finite triple of dimensions, Gaussian factors fail
to maximize both product MMSE and mutual information over iid
unit-variance factor priors. Rademacher factors have strictly larger
values on the displayed interval. This is compatible with the scalar
Gaussian-SIGNAL extremality theorem, which optimizes over Gaussian
input X itself rather than Gaussian U and V.

The explicit interval depends on dimension and shrinks to zero under
proportional growth. No comparison of the limiting functions at fixed
positive SNR follows. In particular this is not a disproof of the
limiting Gaussian-factor conjecture in Target 2.

Checks: N=P=M=1 gives D=32, T=893026 and leading MI difference
2s^4/3, leading MMSE difference 16s^3/3. The sign of each comparison,
the factor 6 in (4), and the fact that this SNR interval is not uniform
are the critical checks. Novelty is unestablished; independent review

body: Method (campaign status: audited-pass): Transfer from real signed projective classes to a binary quotient. Given a real residual R of dim d, replace R by R_0 = span of (every f in D_n in the zero class) and (every f - sigma*g in R, sigma in {+-1}, witnessing a class equality). R_0 is rational, contained in R, of dim d_0 <= d, and induces exactly the same classes. Put Lambda = R_0 cap Z^{n+1}; it is saturated, hence a direct summand of Z^{n+1}, so its mod-2 reduction has dimension d_0. Signs die in characteristic two, so the real signed partition (zero class included) REFINES the coset partition mod Lambda-bar. All D_n vectors have odd weight; translating by A=e_0 lands in the even-weight space E with basis u_i=e_0+e_i, sending A->0, B_i->u_i, C_i->u_i+u_{i+1}. Set W = Lambda-bar cap E, dim W <= d_0 <= d. Notes: No reduction-of-rank assumption is hidden: passing to the SATURATED lattice is precisely what stops a denominator divisible by 2 from invalidating the mod-2 argument (S10 lines 269-272, p.162). The zero class costs no lost +1 (S11 lines 104-106). Field-critical: the argument is R -> F_2 and uses sigma=+-1 |-> 1.

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. [Lemma 31 (One-sided Fourier uniqueness) of arXiv:2609.01826, 'An extension theory for fully fractional Schr\"odinger equations with memory'] Let $g\in L^2(\mathbb R)$ be supported in $[0,\infty)$, and let
$\mathscr G=\mathscr Fg$ be its Fourier transform. If $\mathscr G$ vanishes on a
measurable subset of $\mathbb R$ of positive measure, then $g=0$ almost everywhere.
In particular, if $\mathscr G(\omega)=0$ for almost every $\omega>0$, then $g=0$.
