[Thm main of arXiv:2607.10105, 'The four-dimensional Anderson model: a case study for critical SPDEs'] Fix $\lambda$ small enough. Then there exists a suitable choice of renormalization constants $\mathcal C_\varepsilon$ (depending on $\varepsilon$ and $\rho$), such that the sequence of random fields converges in law \[\lambda_\varepsilon^{-1}\cdot (G_\varepsilon(x,y)-G(x,y))\xrightarrow{\mathrm{law}}\mathcal H(x,y)\qquad \textrm{as }\varepsilon\to 0,\] and the limit $\mathcal H(x,y)$ is a centered Gaussian random field with covariance function independent of the cutoff function $\rho$, which is
\begin{equation}\mathbb E(\mathcal H(x_1,y_1)\mathcal H(x_2,y_2))=\frac{2\pi^2}{2\pi^2-\lambda^2}\int_{\mathbb T^4}G(x_1-z)G(y_1-z)G(x_2-z)G(y_2-z)\,\mathrm{d}z.\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem l:weakM1transf of arXiv:2605.08983, 'A functional limit theorem for self-normalized linear processes with random coefficients a'] Let $(A_{n}, B_{n})$, $n=0,1,2,\ldots$, be stochastic processes in $D^{2}$ such that, as $n \to \infty$,
\begin{equation}
(A_{n}, B_{n}) \xrightarrow{d} (A_{0}, B_{0})
\end{equation}
in $D^{2}$ with the weak $M_{1}$ topology. Suppose $x_{n}$ and $y_{n}$, $n=0,1,2,\ldots$, are elements of $D^{1}$ with $x_{0}$ and $y_{0}$ being continuous, such that, as $n \to \infty$,
$$x_{n}(t) \to x_{0}(t) \qquad \textrm{and} \qquad y_{n}(t) \to y_{0}(t) $$
uniformly in $t$. Then
$$ (A_{n} +x_{n}, B_{n} + y_{n}) \xrightarrow{d} (A_{0} + x_{0}, B_{0} + y_{0})$$
in $D^{2}$ with the weak $M_{1}$ topology. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem l:weakM1transf of arXiv:2605.08983

[Proposition layering of arXiv:2606.09488, 'The temporal stochastic block model'] Let $m \in {\mathbb N}$ be a fixed integer and let $(G_i)_{i\in [m]}$ be a sequence of ${\mathbb S}{\mathbb B}{\mathbb M}\left(n,k,\boldsymbol{a},\frac{1}{m}P\right)$. Then, we can couple $(G,\pi)$ with $(G_i)_{i\in[m]}$ in such a way that 
$$E(G) = \bigsqcup_{i=1}^{m} E(G_i), \quad \textrm{ and } \quad \forall i\in [m-1],\quad \max_{e \in E(G_i)} \pi(e) < \min_{e\in E(G_{i+1}) }\pi(e).$$

body: [Theorem 1.2 of arXiv:2604.02746, 'Zero-Freeness of the Hard-Core Model with Bounded Connective Constant'] Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a family of finite graphs with lower connective constant $\mu_{\inf}(\mathcal{H})$. Then, for any $0<\lambda<\lambda_{c}(\mu_{\inf}(\mathcal{H}))$, there exists a $\delta$ depending on $\lambda$ and $\mathcal{H}$ such that for any $H\in\mathcal{H}$, the partition function $Z_{H}$ is zero-free on $\mathcal{L}_{\delta}([0,\lambda])$.

[Proposition prop:tropp_moment of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let independent random matrices $\mathbf{X}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_n \in \mathbb{H}(d)$ satisfy for all $k = 1, \dots, n$, all $p = 2, 3, \dots$, with some $K > 0$ and positive-definite matrices $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k$
    \[
    \E \mathbf{X}_k = 0,
    \quad
    \E \mathbf{X}^p_k \preccurlyeq \frac{p!}{2} K^{p-2} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k.
    \]
    Let $\sigma^2 \coloneqq \norm*{\sum^n_{k = 1} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k}. $ Then for all $t \ge 0$
    \[
    \mathbb{P} \lr{\lambda_{\max}\left(\sum^n_{k=1} \mathbf{X}_k\right) \ge t} \le d \elr{- \frac{t^2}{2 (\sigma^2 + K t)}}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:AHM-modular of arXiv:2607.13990, 'Effective Resistance in Fixed-Rank External-Field Measures\\ and Constant-Stretch Correlat'] Suppose that every nonterminal conditional covariance $C\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}$ of the sampler satisfies, for fixed constants $\rho,\beta>0$,
\begin{align}
    CD^{-1}C
&\succeq
    \rho C,
\\
    \Phi_C\left(C^\dagger(\mathbf e_a-\mathbf e_b)\right)
&\le
    \beta
\qquad
    \text{for every distinct }a,b\in[q].

\end{align}
Then the sampler has relative-interior stretch at most
\begin{equation}
    \frac{2\beta}{\rho}.

\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem t:geo of arXiv:2505.11389, '\bf The Poisson Multiplication Formula'] Fix $m\geq 1$ and consider integers $k_1,\dots,k_m\geq 1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_m \in L^2(\mathbb{P})$ be such that
$$
F_i \in \bigoplus_{q = 0}^{k_i} C_q, \quad i=1,\dots,m,
$$
and set $K := k_1+\cdots +k_m$ and $\Phi := \prod_{i=1}^m F_i$. For $p\in [1,2]$, consider the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[\bf (i-$p$)] $\Phi\in L^p(\mathbb{P})$;
    \item[{\bf (ii-$p$)}] for all $q=1,\dots,K$, one has that
    $$
    \sum_{|W| = q } Q(D_{z_1,\dots,z_q}^{[W]}(F_1,\dots,F_m))\in L^1(\mathbb{P}), \quad \mbox{for $\mu^q$-a.e. $z_1,\dots,z_q$},
    $$
    and the mapping
    $$
(z_1,\dots,z_q)\mapsto \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{|W| = q } Q(D_{z_1,\dots,z_q}^{[W]}(F_1,\dots,F_m))\right]
    $$
    is in $L^p(\mu^q)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, one has that {\bf (ii-$p$)} implies {\bf (i-$p$)} for all $p\in [1,2)$, and also that {\bf (i-$2$)} and {\bf (ii-$2$)} are equivalent. Moreover, if either condition {\bf (i-$2$)} or {\bf (ii-$2$)} is satisfied, then the chaotic decomposition (equation chaosdec of the paper) of $\Phi$ is such that $h_q = 0$ for all $q>K$, and
\begin{equation}
h_q(z_1,\dots,z_q) = \frac{1}{q!} \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{|W| = q } Q(D_{z_1,\dots,z_q}^{[W]}(F_1,\dots,F_m)) \right], \quad q=1,\dots,K.
\end{equation}

[Thm some.precise.degrees.biased of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let $b\geq 1$, then the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For every cycle $C_t$, we have $s_{MB}^b(C_t) = s_{BM}^b(C_t) = b+2 .$
\item[(b)] For the wheel $W_t$ with an even number $t$ of spokes, we have $s_{MB}^b(W_t) = s_{BM}^b(W_t) = 2b+3 .$
\item[(c)] For every tree $T$, we have $s_{MB}^b(T) = s_{BM}^b(T) = 1 .$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\Omega_j\to\Omega^\ast,
\qquad
c_j\downarrow\ell,
\]

\begin{equation}
\begin{cases}

&\text{in }\Omega^\ast\setminus K,\\
u^\ast=1

u^\ast=0
&\text{on }\partial\Omega^\ast,\\
-\partial_{\nu_g}u^\ast=\ell
&\text{on }\partial\Omega^\ast.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem:convex-linear-bound of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N$ be i.i.d.\ mean-zero variables with finite
		variance. Let $F$ be convex in each
		coordinate and suppose that, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely, for every $1\leq i\leq N$,
		\[
			0\leq\partial_i^+F\leq b_i\, ,
		\]
		where the $b_i$ are deterministic. Then there is a universal
		$C<\infty$ such that, for every $L>0$,
		\[
			\mathbb{E}\left[\left(
			F-\mathbb{E} F-\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbb{E}[\partial_i^+F]\xi_i
			\right)^2\right]
			\leq CL^2\sum_{i=1}^N\Var(\partial_i^+F)
			+C\eta(L)\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i^2\, ,
		\]
		where, for an independent copy $\xi_1'$ of $\xi_1$,
		\[
			\eta(L)\coloneqq
			\mathbb{E}\left[(\xi_1-\xi_1')^2
			\mathbf{1}_{\{|\xi_1-\xi_1'|>L\}}\right]\, .
		\]

Let f:R^d->R be C1,P a fixed symmetric positive-definite matrix,eta>0,and beta in[0,1). Run m_(t+1)=beta*m_t+(1-beta)*grad f(x_t),x_(t+1)=x_t-eta*P^(-1)*m_(t+1),from arbitrary x_0,m_0. For ftilde(y)=f(P^(-1/2)y),unpreconditioned EMA heavy ball initialized at y_0=P^(1/2)x_0,p_0=P^(-1/2)m_0 satisfies y_t=P^(1/2)x_t,p_t=P^(-1/2)m_t for all t. For a positive-definite quadratic Hessian H,the equilibrium is linearly asymptotically stable exactly when lambda_max(P^(-1/2)H P^(-1/2))<2*(1+beta)/(eta*(1-beta)). At beta=.9 the threshold is 38/eta. Above threshold an unstable mode exists;initialization at the equilibrium still stays fixed. This is fixed-preconditioner conjugacy and its quadratic consequence,not adaptive Adam tracking. Draft,independent review pending.

[Theorem 12 (The symmetric-function action) of arXiv:2609.03881, 'Eulerian insertion operators and an Eulerian form of the Pieri rule'] Let \(g\in\Lambda_m\) and \(f\in\mathrm{QSym}_N\).  Since every symmetric function is quasisymmetric, we have
$\Lambda_m\subseteq\mathrm{QSym}_m$.
Thus \(gf\in\mathrm{QSym}_{N+m}\).
Then we have
\[
 \Phi_{N+m}(gf)=\rho(g)\Phi_N(f).
\]
In particular, for every partition \(\lambda\),
$\Phi_{N+|\lambda|}(s_\lambda f)
 =\G_\lambda\Phi_N(f)$.
Moreover, for all partitions \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\), we have
\[
 \G_\lambda\G_\mu
 =\sum_{\nu\vdash|\lambda|+|\mu|}
   c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\G_\nu.
\]

[Prop prop-harmonic-conv of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Assume that we are in the setting of Proposition~(prop-min-harmonic of the paper). 
Let $\{\mathcal G_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ be an increasing family of finite, connected subgraphs of $\mathcal G$ whose union is all of $\mathcal G$ such that $\mathcal A\subset \mathcal V\mathcal G_n$ for every $n\geq 1$. 
For $n\geq 1$, let $h_n^\phi : \mathcal V\mathcal G_n\to\mathbbm R$ be the unique function which agrees with $\phi$ on $\mathcal A$ and is $\mathcal G_n$-discrete harmonic\footnote{If $x\in\mathcal G_n$ has at least one neighboring vertex in $\mathcal G$ which is not in $\mathcal G_n$, then the condition that $h_n^\phi$ is $\mathcal G_n$-discrete harmonic at $x$ is different from the condition that $h_n^\phi$ is $\mathcal G$-discrete harmonic at $x$.}
on $\mathcal V\mathcal G_n\setminus\mathcal A$. 
Let $h^\phi : \mathcal V\mathcal G \to \mathbbm R$ be the energy-minimizing function with $h^\phi|_{\mathcal A} \equiv \phi$, as in Proposition~(prop-min-harmonic of the paper). 
Then $\lim_{n\to\infty} h_n^\phi(x) = h^\phi(x)$ for each $x\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$.

[Definition 8 (Endpoint local exponent) of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] For a nonnegative random variable \(W\) with \(\mathbb E W=1\), define
\[
    A_{\mathrm{loc}}(W)
    =
    \sup_{q>1}
    \max\left\{
        0,\,
        \frac{q-1-\log_2\mathbb E[W^q]}{q}
    \right\},
\]
where the \(q\)-term is interpreted as \(0\) whenever
\(\mathbb E[W^q]=\infty\).

body: Let D(n) be the set of |a - b| over all factorizations n = ab. For k = 2 the integers {48, 240} satisfy D(48) intersect D(240) = {8, 22} (Erdos-Rosenfeld 1997), and for k = 3 the integers {6925500, 37901500, 108448956} have the four differences {420, 3780, 14940, 76860} common to all three (Jimenez-Urroz 1999), so both cases of the problem (k positive integers whose factor-difference sets share at least k values) hold. Since d lies in D(N) exactly when d^2 + 4N is a perfect square, the integers N sharing a fixed set of differences are read off the divisors of fixed numbers; a complete enumeration of this kind shows that the only integers carrying all four differences 420, 3780, 14940 and 76860 are the three above, so no fourth integer extends this triple and a k = 4 example needs a different set of differences (Bremner 2019 gives one). The intersection is finite because every element of D(n) is at most n.

[Lemma lem:modulus of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a compact interval of length $l$ and let $\phi \colon I\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and increasing.  Then there exists a continuous, strictly increasing, concave function $\omega \colon [0,l]\to[0,\infty)$ with $\omega(0)=0$ such that
\begin{equation}
    0\le \phi(b)-\phi(a)\le\omega(b-a)
    \qquad\text{whenever }a,b\in I
    \quad \text{with } a\le b.
\end{equation}
Consequently, $\omega^{-1}$ is convex and strictly increasing on $[0,\omega(l)]$.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Locate the obstruction between the known polynomial regimes and a finite threshold. Result: Delocalisation is known in d = 3 for W >= N^{c} with explicit c (Yang-Yau-Yin quantum-diffusion results for W >> N^{1-eps} and later improvements), and the mean-field reduction of the source suggests W >> N^{1-eps}; a finite W_c requires an argument uniform in N at fixed W, i.e. a renormalisation-group or supersymmetric proof of diffusion for the Green function, which exists only for the density of states (Disertori-Pinson-Spencer in d = 3) and not for eigenvector delocalisation. The gap between 'W a power of N' and 'W fixed' is the same as between the T-expansion of Yang-Yau and a genuinely non-perturbative statement. A rigorous partial fact: the Thouless criterion (conductance ~ W^2 (N/W)^{2-d} ... ) predicts W_c = O(1) in d = 3 because the conductance grows with N at fixed W, and the source's heuristic is consistent; but no rigorous statement. No result. Obstruction: All rigorous delocalisation results need W to grow with N; a fixed-W argument is non-perturbative.

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] We keep the assumptions and notation of Theorem \ref{VHCcvstable}. Let $\mathscr G\! \subset \! \ccF$ be $\sigma$-field. Let $E$ and $E'$ be Polish spaces equipped with their respective Borel $\sigma$-field. The product spaces below 
are equipped with product topology. For all $n\ino \bbN^*$, let $r_n \ino \bbN$, let  $U_n$ be a $E$-valued r.v.~and let $Z_n \! : \bD (\bbR_+, \bbR) \! \times \! E \! \to E'$ be a measurable function. We assume for all $n\ino \bbN^*$ 
that $\tau_{\geq n} $ and $\tau_n$ are independent from $(\mathscr G,U_n)$, that  
$r_n/n \! \to \! r\ino (0, 1)$ and that conditionally given $\ccG$, the joint convergence 
\begin{equation}
 M_{\geq n}:= \Big(  \big( \tfrac{1}{b_n}V_{ (ns) \wedge r_n} (\tau_{\geq n})\big)_{\! s\in \bbR_+}\,  ,\,  Z_n \big(V_{ \cdot \wedge r_n} (\tau_{\geq n}), U_n \big) \Big) \underset{n\to \infty}{-\!\!\!-\!\!\!\longrightarrow}  \big( X^{_{(r)}}_{^{\!}}, Z \big)
\end{equation}
holds weakly on $\bD (\bbR_+, \bbR)\! \times \! E'$. Here we furthermore assume that 
$X^{_{(r)}}_{^{\!}}$ has the same law as $X_{\cdot \wedge r}$ under $\bN (\, \cdot \, \big| \, \zeta \geko 1)$ and that 
$( X^{_{(r)}}_{^{\!}}, Z)$ is independent from $\mathscr G$. Then, conditionally given $\mathscr G$, the joint convergence 
\begin{equation}

M_{n}:= \Big( \big( \tfrac{1}{b_n}V_{ (ns) \wedge r_n} (\tau_{ n})\big)_{\! s\in \bbR_+}\,  ,\,Z_n \big(V_{ \cdot \wedge r_n} (\tau_{n}), U_n \big) \Big) \underset{n\to \infty}{-\!\!\!-\!\!\!\longrightarrow}  \big( Y^{_{(r)}}_{^{\!}}, Z' )
\end{equation}
holds weakly on $\bD (\bbR_+, \bbR)\! \times \! E'$ where the r.v.~$( Y^{_{(r)}}_{^{\!}} \!\!  , Z' )$ is independent from $\mathscr G$ 
and such that  
$\bE [ F(  Y^{_{(r)}}_{^{\!}}\!\!  , Z')] \eqo \bE [ F( X^{_{(r)}}_{^{\!}}\!\! , Z ) D_r(X^{_{(r)}}_{^{r}}) ]$ for all bounded measurable functions $F$ on 
$\bD (\bbR_+, \bbR)\! \times \! E'$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2511.20519, '\textbf{High-dimensional limits arising from \\ hyperbolic Poisson $k$-plane processes}'] Let $\varepsilon>0$. Let $(d_n,k_n)_{n\geq 1}$  be an  admissible sequence such that $d_n\to\infty$ and  $k_n/d_n\to 1/2$.
Write $r_n := 2k_n-d_n-1$.
Then the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
     \item[\emph{(a)}]  If $\limsup\limits_{n\to\infty}d_n^{-1} r_n^{d_n/k_n} < e\pi$, then \(J(d_n,k_n,\varepsilon) \to 0\) as $n\to\infty$.
     \item[\emph{(b)}]  If $\liminf\limits_{n\to\infty}d_n^{-1} r_n^{d_n/k_n} > e\pi$, then \(\JJ(d_n,k_n,\varepsilon) \to 1\) as $n\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 10 of arXiv:2511.20519

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: Let a stationary occupation measure record active, idle-on, setting-up and off servers. Average power is a linear functional of that measure, while mean waiting equals E[Q]/Lambda by Little law when finite. Minimizing E[Q]/Lambda+eta*E[power] for eta>=0 produces supported frontier points. If policies share a common regenerative empty/reset state and have finite cycle moments, randomizing between them at those epochs produces convex mixtures of cycle reward rates. The mixing weight is cycle-length biased; averaging policy labels without that correction gives the wrong frontier. Check: If a cycle uses policy A with probability p, its reward rate is [p*E[R_A]+(1-p)*E[R_B]]/[p*E[L_A]+(1-p)*E[L_B]], directly from renewal reward. The coefficient of A rate is p*E[L_A] divided by the same denominator. [Defn dm of arXiv:2601.09537, 'Gene genealogies in haploid populations evolving according to sweepstakes reproduction'] We partition the pre-limiting  transition matrix $\Pi_N$ into
\be
\Pi_N = A_N + c_N B_N + R_N
\ee
where the non-zero  entries of $A_N$ are the probability of  the identity
transition, or of a dispersion. An entry of $A_N$ of order $\ensuremath{{O}\left( 1 \right)}$ is of the
form,  for   $\xi \in \mathcal{S}_{n,{\ensuremath{\mathds h} }} \setminus \mathcal{E}_{n,{\ensuremath{\mathds h} }}$, 
\bd
    A_N(\xi, \textrm{\tt disp}(\xi)) = C(\xi,  \textrm{\tt disp}(\xi)  )
    \frac{(N)_j}{ (2N)_j } \ensuremath{\mathds{E}\left[ \nu_1 \cdots \nu_j  \right]}
\ed
where $\textrm{\tt disp}$ is a generic  dispersion map,  which disperses at
least one marked chromosome, and  $C(\xi,  \textrm{\tt disp}(\xi))$  is a
combinatorial probability  of order $\ensuremath{{O}\left( 1 \right)}$ for dispersing marked 
chromosomes, given that at most one marked parent is assigned to any parent
pair.   Otherwise we set, for $\xi \in \mathcal{S}_{n,{\ensuremath{\mathds h} }} \setminus
\mathcal{E}_{n,{\ensuremath{\mathds h} }}$,  
\bd
   A_N(\xi, \xi) = 1 - \sum_{\eta = \textrm{\tt disp}(\xi) }  A_N(\xi, \eta),
\ed
and  $ A_N( \xi, \xi) = 1$ for all $\xi \in \mathcal{E}_{n, {\ensuremath{\mathds h} }}$.   
The non-zero entries of $B_N$ are probabilities of  mergers, of the form
\be
   B_N(\xi,  \textrm{\tt merge}(\xi) ) =   C(\xi,  \textrm{\tt merge}(\xi) ) \frac{(N)_j}{ (2N)_{k_1 + \cdots + k_j}
     } \EE{ (\nu_1)_{k_1}  \cdots (\nu_j)_{k_j} },
\ee
where $k_1 \ge 2$, and $k_2 \ldots, k_j = 1$ are the number of single-marked diploid individuals
assigned to a given parent pair,    $\textrm{{\tt merge}}:

body:
For a real number t write ||t|| for its distance to the nearest integer. Fix an irrational alpha and suppose alpha is DIOPHANTINE of type (C, tau): there are constants C > 0 and tau >= 1 with

  ||q alpha||  >=  C * q^{-tau}    for every integer q >= 1.

Then:

(i) (the small divisors are only polynomially small) for every nonzero integer q,
      | e^{2 pi i q alpha} - 1 |  =  2 | sin(pi q alpha) |  >=  4 ||q alpha||  >=  4 C |q|^{-tau}.
    The upper bound | e^{2 pi i q alpha} - 1 | <= 2 pi ||q alpha|| always holds, so the two sides are comparable to ||q alpha||.

(ii) (solving the cohomological equation) Let R_alpha(x) = x + alpha on the circle T = R/Z and let f be a C^infinity function on T with mean zero. Then the equation u(x + alpha) - u(x) = f(x) has a C^infinity solution u, unique up to an additive constant, given on Fourier coefficients by u-hat(q) = f-hat(q) / (e^{2 pi i q alpha} - 1) for q nonzero. Quantitatively |u-hat(q)| <= |q|^{tau} |f-hat(q)| / (4C), so one loses tau derivatives: in Sobolev scale ||u||_{H^{s - tau}} <= (4C)^{-1} ||f||_{H^s}, and the analogous statement holds in Holder scale with an epsilon loss.

(iii) (how common the hypothesis is) For every tau > 1, Lebesgue-almost every alpha is Diophantine of type (C, tau) for some C = C(alpha) > 0; for tau = 1 the alpha satisfying the condition are exactly the badly approximable ones (bounded partial quotients), a set of Lebesgue measure zero and full Hausdorff dimension; for tau < 1 no alpha satisfies it at all, by Dirichlet's theorem.

WHERE IT FAILS. If alpha is LIOUVILLE (no such C, tau exist), the conclusion of (ii) fails badly: choose q_1 < q_2 < ... with ||q_k alpha|| < q_k^{-k} and define f by f-hat(q_k) = f-hat(-q_k)-bar = ||q_k alpha||^{1/2} and all other coefficients zero. These coefficients decay faster than any power of q_k, so f is C^infinity with mean zero, yet |u-hat(q_k)| >= ||q_k alpha||^{1/2} / (2 pi ||q_k alpha||) = 1 / (2 pi ||q_k alpha||^{1/2}), which blows up faster than any polynomial in q_k. Hence no solution u exists in L^2, and not even a distributional solution exists. So the Diophantine condition is not a technical convenience: it is what separates solvability from non-solvability. Note also that (ii) gives no information at all about the SPEED of ergodic averages by itself, and that the estimates degrade as C -> 0, so any application that needs uniformity must track C and tau explicitly.
alpha is irrational and satisfies ||q alpha|| >= C q^{-tau} for all integers q >= 1, with C > 0 and tau >= 1
||t|| denotes the distance from t to the nearest integer
in part (ii), f is C^infinity on the circle R/Z with mean zero, and the rotation is x -> x + alpha
solutions are sought up to an additive constant; L^2 and distributional solutions are compared by Fourier coefficients
title: Small divisor estimates for a Diophantine circle rotation

[Definition of arXiv:2608.26904, 'Hyperarithmetic directions can all be exceptional for Marstrand's projection theorem'] For any $D \in 2^\omega$, $p \in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $\delta > 0$, the {\em $D$-computable Kolmogorov complexity of $p$ with precision $\delta$} is
\[
	K_\delta^D(p) = \min\{ K^D(i) : |p - q_i| < \delta\}.
\]
The {\em $D$-computable dimension of $p$} is
\[
	\={cdim}^D(p) = \liminf_{\delta \to 0} \frac{K_\delta^D(p)}{-\log_2 \delta}.
\]

  $S$ and $T$ with $S<T$, there exists a positive constant $C = C_{S,T}$, such
  that the following statements hold with $\widetilde{\rho}_1$
  and $\widetilde{\rho}_2$ defined as in~(equation E:trho1-trho2 of the paper).

  \begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]

    \item If either $\beta \in (0,2)$ or $\beta = 2$ and $\gamma \ge 1$, then
          for all $(t, x, y)\in [S,T]\times \mathbb{R}^{2d}$, it holds that
          \begin{align} 
            \mathbb{E}\left[\left(u(t, x) - u(t, y)\right)^2\right]
            \le C
            \begin{dcases}
              |x-y|^{2 (\widetilde{\rho}_1 \wedge 1)},        & \widetilde{\rho}_1 \neq 1, \\
              |x-y|^2 \big(1 + \big| \log(|x-y|) \big| \big), & \widetilde{\rho}_1 = 1.
            \end{dcases}
          \end{align}

          
          

          
          
          
          
          
          
          
          

    \item If $\beta = 2$ and $\gamma \in [0, 1)$, then for all $(t, x, y)\in [S,T]\times
            \mathbb{R}^{2d}$, it holds that
          \begin{align}
            \mathbb{E}\left[\left(u(t, x) - u(t, y)\right)^2\right]
            \le C
            \begin{dcases}
              |x-y|^{2 (\widetilde{\rho}_2 \wedge 1)},        & \widetilde{\rho}_2 \neq 1, \\
              |x-y|^2 \big(1 + \big| \log(|x-y|) \big| \big), & \widetilde{\rho}_2 = 1.
            \end{dcases}.
          \end{align}

  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Let $s\in(0,2)$ and $p\in(1,\infty)$. Then for all $f, g\in\mathscr S(\R^n)$, define the remainder term
   \[
   R_s(f,g) := \flap(fg)-f\,\flap g-g\,\flap f.
   \]
   Then
   \[
       \norm{R_s(f,g)}_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim \begin{cases}
           \norm{\flap f}_{L^p(\R^n)}\norm {g}_{L^\infty(\R^n)}, &\text{if }s\in (0,1),\\
          \norm{(-\triangle)^{\frac{s-1}{2}}f}_{L^p(\R^n)}(\norm {Dg}_{L^\infty(\R^n)}+\norm {(-\triangle)^{1/2}g}_{L^\infty(\R^n)}), &\text{if }s\in [1,2).
       \end{cases}
   \]

body:
Theorem 6: d >= 2, E[tau_e^2] < infinity, F(0) < p_c, xhat a direction of curvature for the limit shape
Wehr-Aizenman bound chi_x >= (1 - (d-1) xi_x)/2: the hypotheses of Newman-Piza Theorem 2
Theorem 7: F(0) < p_c, E[exp(beta tau_e)] < infinity for some beta > 0, xhat a direction of curvature
chi_x >= 1/8 holds only when d = 2; xi_x <= 3/4 is stated for d >= 2
the exponents are Newman-Piza's own definitions, not Chatterjee's and not each other's

THE CURVATURE HYPOTHESIS IS NON-CONSTRUCTIVE. Directions of curvature are known to exist - at least four, by symmetry, via a non-constructive argument the survey reproduces - but no explicit direction, not even a coordinate axis, is provably one. Every consequence of Theorem 6 or Theorem 7 inherits that. The log-variance lower bound of Theorem 2 does NOT: it is direction-uniform and curvature-free.
WITHOUT curvature the best bounds on the wandering exponent are still 0 <= xi <= 1, the upper bound following directly from the shape theorem.
WHERE THE 3/4 COMES FROM: Theorem 6 combined with chi' <= 1/2, which the survey attributes to Kesten and to Alexander. The survey also gives an alternative modern route to xi_x <= 3/4 through Damron-Hanson-Sosoe's exponential concentration at chi = 1/2 + delta.
RELATION TO THE SCALING RELATION: the survey records that Theorem 6 is 'a version of the inequality chi >= 2 xi - 1', and that Newman-Piza describe their own argument as essentially a rigorous version of the Krug-Spohn heuristic for the relation.
SOURCE: Newman-Piza (1995), Ann. Probab. 23, 977-1005. Read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), theorems 'thm:NPScaling' and 'thm:exponent_bounds' and equation 'eq:WehrAiz', tex lines 2698-2723.
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim. Lane P4 did not read Newman-Piza (1995).
title: Newman-Piza (1995), Theorems 6 and 7: in d >= 2 with E[tau_e^2] < infinity and F(0) < p_c, if xhat is a DIRECTION OF CURVATURE of the limit shape then xi_x <= (1 + chi')/2; under the Theorem-2 hypotheses they also get the Wehr-Aizenman bound chi_x >= (1 - (d-1) xi_x)/2; and if in addition E[exp(beta tau_e)] < infinity for some beta > 0 then xi_x <= 3/4 and, in d = 2 only, chi_x >= 1/8. Every one of these carries the NON-CONSTRUCTIVE curvature hypothesis.

body: Let X be a Banach space, Y a normed vector space, and F a family of bounded linear operators from X to Y. Suppose F is pointwise bounded: for every fixed x in X, the set {||Tx|| : T in F} is bounded in [0, infinity). Then F is uniformly bounded in operator norm, i.e. sup over T in F of ||T|| is finite, so ||Tx|| <= C ||x|| holds for all T in F and x in X with one constant C. The proof uses the Baire category theorem, and completeness of X is essential.
title: Uniform boundedness principle (Banach-Steinhaus theorem)

[Lemma 28 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] Let \(\mathsf a_n>0\), and suppose that
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathsf a_n^{1/n}=\lambda>0.
\]
Fix \(h\ge1\), and put
\(\mathcal R_n=\mathsf a_{n+h}/\mathsf a_n\).  If there are
\(b>0\), \(K<\infty\), and \(n_0\) such that
\[
  \mathcal R_n\ge b,\qquad
  \mathcal R_{n+h}-\mathcal R_n\ge-\frac{K}{n},
  \qquad n\ge n_0,
\]
then
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathcal R_n=\lambda^h.
\]

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2604.09248, '\bfseries Limit laws for longest edges in empty region graphs'] Assume the same set-up as in Theorem \ref{thm:PoisConvAbstract} and denote by $L_{t,W}$ the length of the longest edge with midpoint in $W$, i.e., 
$$
L_{t,W} := \max\Big\{\|x-y\|:(x,y)\in\eta_{t,\neq}^2,(\eta_t-\delta_x-\delta_y)(S(x,y))=0,{x+y\over 2}\in W\Big\}. 
$$
Then, for any $t\geq 2$,
$$
\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{Kol}}\big(\gamma tL_{t,W}^d-\log(t)-\log(\kappa_d/(2\gamma)),G_W\big) \leq \begin{cases}
        c\log^{-(d-2)}(t), & d \ge 3,\\
        c\log^{-1/2}(t), & d=2,
    \end{cases}
$$
where $c$ is a constant only depending on $d$, $\vol(W)$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$, and $G_W$ is a Gumbel distributed random variable with distribution function $\PP(G_W\leq s)=\exp(-\vol(W)e^{-s})$ for $s\in\RR$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2604.09248

[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2606.18047, 'Analysis of the asymmetric shelf shuffle'] For fixed $i\geq 1$, we have 
\[
\sum_{n\ge 0}u^n\E_{\nu^{(p)}_{n,m}}[N_i]=\frac{1}{1-u}\sum_{r\ge 1}\frac{B^{(m,p)}_{i,r}}{i}u^{ir}.
\]
In particular, 
\begin{equation*}
\E_{\nu^{(p)}_{n,m}}[N_i]
=
\frac{1}{i}
\sum_{r=1}^{\lfloor n/i\rfloor}
B^{(m,p)}_{i,r}.

\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 5 of arXiv:2606.18047

[Lemma lem:bm3 of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take any $D>1$ and $0<\epsilon<1$.
			Let $X, Y, Z$ be three independent Brownian motions, each with drift in $[-D, D]$.
			Then we have
			\[
			\mathbb{P}\left[ X(x)+Y(x) < \epsilon, \; Z(x)-Y(x) < \epsilon, \forall x\in[0,1]  \right] < C_0\epsilon^3 D^3.
			\]
            where $C_0>0$ is a universal constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:bm3 of arXiv:2604.10020

body:
[Theorem 2 (Parabolic subsolution identities for Hermite energies) of arXiv:2607.07712, 'Parameter-Space Heat Flow, Gaussian Density Ratios, and Sharp Hermite Truncation Rates'] Let \(F_\tau\) solve
\[
\partial_\tau F_\tau
=
\frac12\Delta_uF_\tau
\]
in the sense above.  Then each Hermite block energy satisfies
\begin{equation}
\left(
\partial_\tau-\frac12\Delta_u
\right)
E_m(\tau,u)
=
-
\|\nabla_u\Pi_mF_\tau(u;\cdot)\|_{L^2(\gamma_d;\mathbb R^d)}^2
\le0.

\end{equation}
Similarly, each Hermite truncation-tail energy satisfies
\begin{equation}
\left(
\partial_\tau-\frac12\Delta_u
\right)
T_M(\tau,u)
=
-
\|\nabla_u(I-\Pi_{\le M})F_\tau(u;\cdot)\|_{L^2(\gamma_d;\mathbb R^d)}^2
\le0.

\end{equation}
If, in addition,
\[
F_\tau=e^{(\tau/2)\Delta_u}F_0
\]
and the heat-kernel representation is justified, then
\[
E_m(\tau,u)
\le
e^{(\tau/2)\Delta_u}E_m(0,u),
\qquad
T_M(\tau,u)
\le
e^{(\tau/2)\Delta_u}T_M(0,u).
\]

body:
[Lemma l:decomposition-curve of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma,\tilde{\gamma}$ be two curves as in Theorem~(t:local-holonomies of the paper) such that $\gamma([0,1])=\tilde{\gamma}([0,1])$ and such that $\gamma(0)=\tilde{\gamma}(0)$. Then, one has almost surely
 $$
 \mathrm{g}_{\gamma}(1)=\mathrm{g}_{\tilde{\gamma}}(1).
 $$
 Moreover, if one decomposes $\gamma=\gamma_1\star\left(\gamma_2\star\left(\ldots\star\gamma_J\right)\right)$ into elementary pieces (including the blowup case of \S(ss:blowup-Wiener-max of the paper)), then
 $$
  \mathrm{g}_{\gamma}(1)=\mathrm{g}_{\gamma_J}(1)\ldots\mathrm{g}_{\gamma_2}(1)\mathrm{g}_{\gamma_1}(1),
 $$
 and $(\mathrm{g}_{\gamma_J}(1),\ldots,\mathrm{g}_{\gamma_2}(1),\mathrm{g}_{\gamma_1}(1))$ are independent random variables. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l:decomposition-curve of arXiv:2607.24640

body: [Theorem 44 (Carath\'eodory) of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $\AA$ be an algebra on $X$ and $\mu:\AA\to [0,\infty]$ satisfy $\mu(\emptyset)=0$ and [countable additivity] $\mu(\cup_{n\in \mathbb{N}}A_n)=\sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}}\mu(A_n)$ for every sequence $(A_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in $\AA$ consisting of pairwise disjoint sets for which $\cup_{n\in \mathbb{N}}A_n\in \AA$. Then $\sigma_X(\AA)\subset \MM(\mu^*_X)$ and $\mu^*_X\vert_{\sigma_X(\AA)}$ is an extension of $\mu$ to a measure on $\sigma_X(\AA)$. If furthermore [$\sigma$-finiteness] there exists a sequence $(A_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ in $\AA$ with $\cup_{n\in \mathbb{N}}A_n=X$ and with  $\mu(A_n)<\infty$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$, then the extension of $\mu$ to a measure on $\sigma_X(\AA)$ is unique and $\mu^*_X\vert_{\MM(\mu^*_X)}=\overline{\mu^*_X\vert_{\sigma_X(\AA)}}$.
title: Carath\'eodory

body: In computability theory, the Church–Turing thesis is a thesis about the nature of computable functions. It states that a function on the natural numbers can be calculated by an effective method if and only if it is computable by a Turing machine. The thesis is named after American mathematician Alonzo Church and the British mathematician Alan Turing. Before the precise definition of computable function, mathematicians often used the informal term effectively calculable to describe functions that are computable by paper-and-pencil methods. In the 1930s, several independent attempts were made to formalize the notion of computability:In 1933, Kurt Gödel, with Jacques Herbrand, formalized the definition of the class of general recursive functions: the smallest class of functions that is closed under composition, recursion, and minimization, and includes zero, successor, and all projections. In 1932–33, Alonzo Church created a method for defining functions called the λ-calculus. Within λ-calculus, he defined an encoding of the natural numbers called the Church numerals.
title: Church–Turing thesis

[Lem 59 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The set $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha)$ from \eqref{e:sM.Lip} can be expressed as

    \]
for $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0)$
as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip.q0}.
\begin{proof}
    For any $q_0 \in [0,1]$, the inclusion $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha)$ is trivial, so it suffices to prove
    \beq
        \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha) \subseteq \bigcup_{q_0 \in [0,1]} \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0)\,.
    \eeq
Consider any sequence $\epsilon_n\downarrow0$. Then, for $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)$ defined in \eqref{e:cM.Lip}, we have
    \[ \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha)

    \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon_n)
    \,.

Consider any measure $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha)$. For any $n\ge 1$, there exists $L_n$ (depending on $\mu,\epsilon_n$) and a sequence of $L_n$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA^n_{N_j})_{j\ge 1}$ with

    \eeq
Abbreviate $\bsig_{n,j} 
\equiv \cA^n_{N_j}(\bG,\bg^\aux)$.

    Let $q_0 \in [0,1]$ be any subsequential limit of the $q_0(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.
    We will show that $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0)$, from which the result follows.

[Lemma0 of arXiv:2411.08846, 'On the Number of Crossings and Bouncings\\ of a Diffusion at a Sticky Threshold'] Let $X$ be the sticky Brownian motion of stickiness parameter $\rho>0 $, defined on the probability space $(\Omega, \bF, (\bF_t)_{t\ge 0}, \Prob_x) $ such that $X_0 = x $, $\Prob_x$-a.s..
Let $ (f_n,k_n,g_n,h_n;\,n\in\IN) $ be the functions defined for all $n \in \IN$ and $x\in \IR $ by 
$f_n(x) := \Prob_{x} \left(  X_{1/n} = 0 \right) $, 
$k_n(x) := \mathbbm{1}_{\{x\not = 0\}} f_n(x/\sqrt n) $, 
$g_n(x) := \Prob_{x} \left( x X_{1/n} < 0 \right) $, 
$h_n(x) := \sqrt n g_n(x/\sqrt n) $.
It holds that 
\begin{enumerate}
	[label={\upshape (\roman*)}]
	\item  $\lim_{n \rightarrow  \infty} f_n(0) = 1 $ and 
	$\lim_{n \rightarrow  \infty} \sqrt n (1- f_n(0)) = 
	{2 \sqrt{2}}/{\rho \sqrt \pi} $,
	\item  the sequence $(k_n)_n $ satisfies~(equation eq_connd_gn_aggreg of the paper) and $\lim_{n \rightarrow  \infty} m_{\sqrt n \rho}( k_n )  =  2 \sqrt{{2}/{\pi}} $,
	\item  the sequence $(h_n)_n $ satisfies~(equation eq_connd_gn_aggreg of the paper) and $\lim_{n \rightarrow  \infty} m_{\sqrt n \rho}( h_n )  = 1/{\rho} $.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm.PR of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] Let $\sigma:\mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ 
		and $b:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ 
		be continuous in $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
        
	
	
	
	
    Assume 
    that the following 
		two conditions hold:
		\begin{itemize}
			\item \textit{Local weak monotonicity}: for all 
			 $R\in[0,\infty)$, $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ 
			with $\|x\|,\|y\|\le R$:
			\begin{equation}
			    2\langle x-y,\,b(x)-b(y)\rangle
			+\|\sigma(x)-\sigma(y)\|^2
			\le K_R\|x-y\|^2,
			\end{equation}
			where $K_{R}$ is a positive constant depending on $R$. 
			\item\textit{Weak coercivity}: for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$:
			\begin{equation}
			    2\langle x,\,b(x)\rangle+\|\sigma(x)\|^2
    			\le K_1(1+\|x\|^2).
			\end{equation}
		\end{itemize}
		Then for any $\mathcal{F}_0$-measurable map 
		$X_0:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^d$, 
		there exists a (up to $\mathbb{P}$-indistinguishability) unique strong 
		solution $(X_t)_{t\ge 0}$ to the SDE (equation eq:sde_appendix of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 (Trajectory Lemma) of arXiv:2606.02856, 'Geometric Routing in Geometric Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] Let \(w_0 \geq w_1(\eps_1) \), \(D_0 \geq D_1(\eps_1)\), and denote \(M := \min\{w_0, D_0\}\).
Let \(f_0(n) = \om{1}\) be any growing function such that \(f_0(n) = \oh{\log\log n}\).
Let \(s\) be the starting vertex, suppose \(D_s \geq D_0\), denote by \(P\) the geometric path induced by all vertices in \(V_{\geq D_0}\). And suppose that there exists a first vertex \(u_1 \in P \cap \overline{V}(w_0, D_0)\)
Then, with probability
\[
1 - \Oh*{ M^{-\Om{1}}},
\]
there exists a subpath \(P' = (u_1, \ldots, u_\ell) \subseteq P \) starting at \(u_1\) such that:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item \(P' \subseteq \overline{V}(w_0, D_0) \).
\item Either \(P' \subseteq V_1 \), or \(P' \subseteq V_2\), or there exists a vertex \(u_\ell'\) such that \(\{u_1, \ldots, 	u_\ell'\} \subseteq V_1 \) and \(\{u_{\ell'+1}, \ldots, u_\ell\} \subseteq V_2\).
\item Let \(\{u_i, u_{i+1}, u_{i+2}\}\) be consecutive vertices on \(P' \cap V_1 \). Then \(w_{u_{i+2}} \geq w_{u_i}^{\gamma(\zeta_1 \eps_1)}\).
\item Let \(\{u_i, u_{i+1}, u_{i+2}\}\) be consecutive vertices on \(P' \cap V_2 \), and suppose \(u_i\) is not the vertex with smallest index in \(P' \cap V_2 \). Then 	\(D_{u_{i+2}} \leq D_{u_i}^{1/\gamma(\eps_1)}\).
\item The length \(\ell\) of the path \(P'\) satisfies 
\[\ell \leq \frac{2 + \oh{1}}{|\log(\tau - 2)|} \log \log n.\]
More precisely, the length of \(P'\) is upper bounded by
\[
\frac{1 + \oh{1}}{|\log(\tau - 2)|} \left( \log \log_{w_0} (D_{u_1}^d) + \log \log_{D_0} (D_{u_1}) \right) + \Oh{f_0(n)}.
\]
\item The following holds:
\[
\mathbb{E}_{<D_0}\left[ \abs{ \N(u_\ell) \cap V^+(u_\ell, \eps_1) \cap V_{<D_0} } \right] = \Om{M^{\Om{1}}},
\]
where \(\mathbb{E}_{<D_0}\) denotes the expectation w.r.t. uncovering the vertices whose distance to target is at most \(D_0\), conditioned on the position and weight of \(u_\ell\).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Trajectory Lemma

[Maintheorem 1 of arXiv:2609.02449, 'Finite Directional Coefficient Modules over Euler Fibers of $A$-Hypergeometric Systems'] Let $A\in\Mat_{d\times n}(\Z)$ have rank $d$, let $\bm{\beta}\in\C^{d}$, put $L=\Ker_{\Z}(A)$, and fix an $L$-generic direction $\bm{w}\in\R^{n}$.
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
\item For every exponent lattice $\Lambda\in\mathfrak{L}_{\bm{\beta}}$, the classwise directed formal logarithmic solution space is represented by the finite directional coefficient module through the isomorphisms in \cref{thm:directed-coefficient-module-presentation}.
\item An exponent lattice contributes a nonzero directed formal logarithmic solution space if and only if it possesses a bounded inclusion-minimal negative-support stratum; every such stratum minimum is realized as a lowest exponent by \cref{thm:minimal-support-solutions-nonvanishing}.
\item Only finitely many exponent lattices contribute, by \cref{thm:finiteness-admissible-exponent-lattice-family}.
\item Every contributing classwise directional coefficient module and the all-lattice directional coefficient module have finite length, by \cref{thm:finite-length-classwise-all-lattice-modules}.
\item The dimension of the all-lattice directed formal logarithmic solution space is given by \eqref{eq:introduction-global-length-dimension}, and every normalized coefficient family is explicitly realized as a formal logarithmic series by \cref{thm:formal-logarithmic-realization}.
\item All realizable lowest exponents are determined by the finite criteria in \cref{thm:finite-criterion-all-classwise-realizable-exponents,thm:polynomial-colon-ideal-criterion-classwise-realizability}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Maintheorem 1 of arXiv:2609.02449

[Lem 2 (Fixed-particle Eynard--Mehta lemma) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $T$ be a nonnegative integer and $P$ a positive integer. For each $t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}$, let $(E_t,\mu_t)$ be a sigma-finite measure space. Let
\[
 \phi_i\colon E_0\to\C,\qquad
 \psi_j\colon E_T\to\C,\qquad 1\leq i,j\leq P,
\]
and let $W_t\colon E_t\times E_{t+1}\to\C$ for $0\leq t<T$. For $s<t$, define $W_{s,t}$ by convolution of $W_s,\ldots,W_{t-1}$. Define
\[
 F_i^{(t)}=\phi_i*W_{0,t},
 \qquad
 G_j^{(t)}=W_{t,T}*\psi_j,
\]
with $F_i^{(0)}=\phi_i$ and $G_j^{(T)}=\psi_j$.

Suppose that all integrals below converge absolutely and that
\[
 \det[\phi_i(x_j^{(0)})]
 \prod_{t=0}^{T-1}\det[W_t(x_i^{(t)},x_j^{(t+1)})]
 \det[\psi_i(x_j^{(T)})]
\]
is nonnegative almost everywhere and has positive finite integral $Z$ with respect to
\[
 \prod_{t=0}^T\prod_{a=1}^P\mu_t(\dd x_a^{(t)}).
\]
Define
\[
 M_{ij}
 =
 \int_{E_t}F_i^{(t)}(x)G_j^{(t)}(x)\,\mu_t(\dd x).
\]
This value is independent of $t$. Then $M$ is invertible,
\[
 Z=(P!)^{T+1}\det M,
\]
and the point process on the disjoint union of $E_0,\ldots,E_T$ formed by the $P$ coordinates at every time is determinantal relative to the direct-sum measure, with correlation kernel
\[
 K(s,x;t,y)
 =
 -\ind_{\{s<t\}}W_{s,t}(x,y)
 +
 \sum_{i,j=1}^P
 G_j^{(s)}(x)(M^{-1})_{ji}F_i^{(t)}(y).
\]

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] \leavevmode
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
    \item For every $\Box$-p frame $\mathfrak{F}$, $\beta \mathfrak{F}$ is $\Box$-condensed and $\Box$-brilliant.
    \item For every $\Diamond$-p frame $\mathfrak{F}$, $\delta \mathfrak{F}$ is $\Diamond$-condensed and $\Diamond$-brilliant.
  \end{enumerate}
  \begin{proof}
    (1)
    ($\Box$-condensed)
    Take any $x \leq x' \sqsubset_\beta y''$, then there is $y'$ such that $(x \leq) x' \sqsubset y' \leq y''$.
    By $\Box$-p of $\mathfrak{F}$, there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y \leq y' (\leq y'')$,
    then $x \sqsubset y \leq y''$, so $x \sqsubset_\beta y''$.
    ($\Box$-brilliant)
    Take any $x \sqsubset_\beta y' \leq y''$, then there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y \leq y' (\leq y'')$.
    then $x \sqsubset y \leq y''$, so $x \sqsubset_\beta y''$.

    (2)
    ($\Diamond$-condensed)
    Take any $x'' \geq x \sqsubset_\delta y$, then there is $y'$ such that $x \sqsubset y' \geq y$.
    By $\Diamond$-p of $\mathfrak{F}$, there is $y''$ such that $x'' \sqsubset y''$ and $y'' \geq y' (\geq y)$,
    then $x'' \sqsubset y'' \geq y$, so $x'' \sqsubset_\delta y$.
    ($\Diamond$-brilliant)
    Take any $x' \sqsubset_\delta y' \geq y$, then there is $y''$ such that $x' \sqsubset y'' \geq y' (\geq y)$,
    then $x' \sqsubset y'' \geq y$, so $x' \sqsubset_\delta y$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 31 (Compatible prefix time) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space with
$\dim V\geq2$, and let
$\gamma\colon[0,T]\to V$ be a continuous bounded-variation path. Set
\[
l=\log S(\gamma),
\qquad
v=\gamma_T-\gamma_0,
\]
and assume that
\[
R(l)=\infty,
\qquad
v\neq0.
\]
Fix $\ell\in V^*$ such that $\ell(v)=1$, put $W=\ker\ell$, and write
\[
\gamma_t-\gamma_0=x_t v+X_t,
\qquad
x_t=\ell(\gamma_t-\gamma_0),
\qquad
X_t\in W.
\]

Give $W$ an auxiliary Euclidean norm and let $W_{\C}$ be its
complexification. For every finite symmetric set
$\Lambda\subset2\pi\Q$, define the real Hilbert space
\[
E_\Lambda
=
\set{(z_\omega)_{\omega\in\Lambda}
\in\prod_{\omega\in\Lambda}W_{\C}:
 z_{-\omega}=\overline{z_\omega}}
\]
with the norm inherited from the Hilbert direct sum, the decorated
transverse path
\[
B_t^\Lambda(\gamma)
=
\left(
\int_0^t \e^{i\omega x_s}\dd X_s
\right)_{\omega\in\Lambda},
\qquad 0\leq t\leq T,
\]
and the orthogonal map
\[
T_\Lambda\colon E_\Lambda\to E_\Lambda,
\qquad
(T_\Lambda z)_\omega=\e^{i\omega}z_\omega.
\]
Denote by the same symbol the induced graded automorphism of tensor
series, and set
\[
r_t^\Lambda
=S\bigl(B^\Lambda(\gamma)|_{[0,t]}\bigr),
\qquad
h_\Lambda=r_T^\Lambda.
\]

Then there exists $t_*\in[0,T]$ such that, for every finite symmetric
$\Lambda\subset2\pi\Q$,
\begin{equation}
h_\Lambda
=a_\Lambda T_\Lambda(a_\Lambda)^{-1},
\qquad
a_\Lambda=r_{t_*}^\Lambda.
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\[
r_{t_*}^\Lambda
=h_\Lambda T_\Lambda\bigl(r_{t_*}^\Lambda\bigr)
\]
for every such $\Lambda$.
title: Compatible prefix time

[Corollary 22 (Optimal contracted-link exponent) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Let $1<r<\infty$.
Let $\alpha_{\mathrm{link}}(r)$ be the infimum of the numbers
$\alpha\ge0$ for which
\[
 \operatorname{Link}:
 \Sch_{r,\infty}\times\Sch_{r,\infty}
 \longrightarrow
 \Sch_{r,\infty}(\log\Sch)^{-\alpha}
\]
is uniformly bounded over all Hilbert spaces and all finite-rank inputs.
Then
\begin{equation}

 \alpha_{\mathrm{link}}(r)=\frac1r.
\end{equation}
The endpoint is attained.  The same minimum is obtained when the bound is
required for all inputs in the full weak ideals.

[Lemma trappingball of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Let $G$ be a graph satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for some $\mathfrak{c}_0 > 0$ and $\upalpha\in(0,1)$. Then, for every integer $\mathtt{r}_n \geq \mathfrak{c}_0$ and every $v \in V$, there exists $r\in[\mathtt{r}_n, 2\mathtt{r}_n]$ such that
\[
\frac{|\partial^+ B_v(r)|}{|B_v(r)|} \leq \frac{8}{r^\upalpha}\,,
\]
where $B_v(r)$ is the ball of radius $r$ in $G$ centered at the vertex $v$, and $\partial^+ B_v(r) = B_v(r+1)\setminus B_v(r)$.
In particular, its conductance has $\Phi(B_v(r)) \leq 8\Delta r^{-\upalpha} $, where $\Delta \leq \mathfrak{c}_0 e$ is the maximum degree in $G$.

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let $(M^n,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, locally conformally flat
Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq7$ with nonnegative scalar curvature.
Suppose $(M^n,g)$ is not finitely covered by a torus,
\(H_1(M^n;\mathbb Z)=0\), and $\Gamma:=\pi_1(M)$ is infinite. Then $\Gamma$
is non-elementary. Furthermore, if \(\Gamma\) is torsion-free, then
\[
1<\dim_{\mathcal H}\Lambda(\Gamma)\leq\frac{n-2}{2}.
\]

body: In number theory and complex analysis, a modular form is a type of function of a complex number variable that possesses a high degree of symmetry, of a certain kind. Similarly to a periodic function of a real variable, a modular form repeats or transforms in a certain way when its argument is subjected to a particular transformation. Unlike an ordinary periodic function, its symmetries include transformations such as replacing a complex number z by −1/z, and the transformation law is not an exact symmetry of the function, but more like the transformation law of a quasiperiodic function: the function picks up an additional factor, depending on the transformation. Modular forms serve as an important bridge between complex analysis, number theory, and geometry. Modular forms also appear in other areas, such as algebraic topology, sphere packing, and string theory.
title: Modular form

body: [Definition 2.1 of arXiv:2605.25323, 'Slow Convergence of Ising and Spin Glass Models with Well-Separated Frustrated Vertices'] For ε > 0, the mixing time is defined as τ(ϵ) = min{t : max x∈S X y∈S ||P t′(x, y), π(y)|| ≤ϵ, for all t′ ≥t}. A Markov chain is rapidly (or polynomially) mixing if the mixing time is bounded above by a polynomial in log S, the length of a description of a state in S. A chain is slowly mixing if the mixing time is bounded below by an exponential function.
title: Definition 2.1 of arXiv:2605.25323: Slow Convergence of Ising and Spin Glass Models with Well-Separated Frustrated Vertices

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let  $\lambda_1(\beta)>\lambda(\beta) $ denote the next eigenvalue of
 $H_\beta $.  Then, for every compact  $K\subset\mathbb R^d $,
\begin{equation}
 Z_T(\beta,x)
 =\mathrm e^{-\lambda(\beta)T}\phi_\beta(x)\|\phi_\beta\|_1
 \left(1+O_K\!\left(\mathrm e^{-[\lambda_1(\beta)-\lambda(\beta)]T}\right)\right)
 
\end{equation}
uniformly for  $x\in K $.  In particular, the same assertion holds with
an  $O_x(\cdot) $ error for every fixed  $x $.

[Lem OSSS of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^N\to\{0,1\}$ be an increasing Boolean function.
  For any algorithm $\mathcal{A}$,
  \[
  \Var_p(f)\le p(1-p)\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_p(i,f;\mathcal{A})\Inf_p(i,f).
  \]
  Here,
  \[
  \Inf_p(i,f):=\mathbb{E}_p[|f-(f\circ\mathrm{Flip}_i)|]
  \]
  denotes the influence of the $i$th bit on $f$, where $\mathrm{Flip}_i\colon\{0,1\}^N\to\{0,1\}^N$ is the map that flips the $i$th value. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 2.3 (Von Neumann’s Minimax Theorem (see [Sim95]) of arXiv:2203.06168, 'Cheeger Inequalities for Vertex Expansion and Reweighted Eigenvalues'] Let X, Y be compact convex sets. If f is a real-valued continuous function on X × Y with f(x, ·) concave on Y for all x ∈X and f(·, y) convex on X for all y ∈Y , then min x∈X max y∈Y f(x, y) = max y∈Y min x∈X f(x, y). Several eigenvalue optimization problems can be formulated as semidefinite programs.

body: The Arzelà–Ascoli theorem is a fundamental result of mathematical analysis giving necessary and sufficient conditions to decide whether every sequence of a given family of real-valued continuous functions defined on a closed and bounded interval has a uniformly convergent subsequence. The main condition is the equicontinuity of the family of functions. The theorem is the basis of many proofs in mathematics, including that of the Peano existence theorem in the theory of ordinary differential equations, Montel's theorem in complex analysis, and the Peter–Weyl theorem in harmonic analysis and various results concerning compactness of integral operators.
title: Arzelà–Ascoli theorem

[Lemma 15 (Interior saturation) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] Given $s\in(0,1)$, there is $R=R(f,s)>0$ with the following property.  If
$D\subset\R^d$ is a domain, $u$ is a bounded positive solution of
$-\Delta u=f(u)$ in $D$ with $0<u\leq1$, and $B_R(x)\subset D$, then
\begin{equation}
 u(x)\geq s.
\end{equation}
The radius $R$ is independent of $D$ and of any boundary condition imposed on
$\partial D$.

[Proposition 8 (First moment) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] For \(t<t_*\),
\begin{equation}

        m'
        =
        \frac12m^2+m-\frac12\sum_{k\geq1}q_k^2.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}

        m'\geq\frac12m(m+1),
\end{equation}
\[
        1\leq t_*\leq2\log2,
        \qquad
        \int_0^t(m(s)+1)\,ds\leq2\log m(t),\quad t<t_*,
\]
and \(m(t)\uparrow\infty\) as \(t\uparrow t_*\).

For finite simple graphs G (n vertices, Laplacian L_G, eigenvalues 0 = lambda_1 <= ... <= lambda_n) and H (m vertices, L_H, 0 = mu_1 <= ... <= mu_m), the Cartesian product G box H has vertex set V(G) x V(H), with (g, h) adjacent to (g', h) when g ~ g' in G and to (g, h') when h ~ h' in H. The largest Laplacian eigenvalue of G box H is lambda_n + mu_m. If G and H are connected with at least two vertices each, the second smallest eigenvalue (algebraic connectivity) of G box H is min(lambda_2, mu_2).

[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with
$
\mathrm{diam}(G)\le c\log n
$, $\delta\in (0,1), \varepsilon\ge \varepsilon_1>0$,
and suppose that $G$ contains $\lceil n^{1-\delta'}\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint hierarchical-stars
\[
HS(v^{(\ell)}):=\mathrm{HStar}\bigl(v^{(\ell)},\{u_i^{(\ell)}\}_{i\le \lceil n^\varepsilon\rceil },\{w_{i,j}^{(\ell)}\}_{i\le \lceil n^\varepsilon\rceil ,\ j\le  \lceil n^{\varepsilon_1}\rceil}\bigr),
\qquad
\ell=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta'}\rceil.
\]
Fix any non-empty set
$
\mathcal I\subseteq \{1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta'}\rceil \}
$.
Assume that at time $0$, for every $\ell\in\mathcal I$, the center $v^{(\ell)}$ is $(\frac14 n^{\varepsilon_3},n^{\varepsilon_2})$-HS-lit with respect to $HS(v^{(\ell)})$, where
\(
\varepsilon_2=\frac{1}{200}\min\{\lambda,\rho,1\}\min\{\varepsilon,\varepsilon_1\},
\varepsilon_3=\frac14\varepsilon_2,
\varepsilon_4=\tfrac{1}{16\cdot 200}\min\{\rho, \lambda, 1\}\cdot24\varepsilon_2.
\)
Then there exists an event $A$ such that $A$ implies that, for every
$
\ell=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta'}\rceil,
$
the center $v^{(\ell)}$ is $(\frac14 n^{\varepsilon_3},n^{\varepsilon_2})$-HS-lit with respect to $HS(v^{(\ell)})$ at time $\exp(n^{\varepsilon_3/2})$, and, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
\mathbb P(A)\ge
1-\exp(-n^{\varepsilon_4/20}).
\]

[Lemma 33 of arXiv:2608.18688, 'Regularity Preservation for Jump-Type Stochastic Transport Equations with Singular Drift'] For all $n$ and for every $p\geq 1$, we have 
\be
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\int E[|u_n(t,x)|^p]dx\leq C_p
\ee
and 
\be
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\int E[|\nabla u_n(t,x)|^p]dx\leq C_p
\ee 
where $C_p$ is a constant dependent only on $p$.

[Theorem nier_Hardyego of arXiv:2411.08220, 'Nonlocal operators with Neumann conditions'] [Hardy inequality]
    For $u\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)\cup(1,2)$,
    \begin{align}
    \mathcal{E}[u] \geq (\mathcal{C}_\alpha + \mathcal{D}_\alpha) \int_D u^2(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\,\mathrm{d}x + \mathcal{C}_\alpha \int_{D^c} u^2(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\,\mathrm{d}x,
    \end{align}
    where
    \[
        \mathcal{C}_{\alpha} = \mathcal{A}_{1,\alpha} \Big[\alpha^{-1} - \frac{\big(\Gamma(\tfrac{\alpha+1}{2})\big)^2}{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}\Big]> 0 \qquad and \qquad
        \mathcal{D}_{\alpha} = \mathcal{A}_{1,\alpha} \int_0^1 \frac{(1-t^{(\alpha-1)/2})^2}{(1-t)^{\alpha+1}}\,{\rm d}t > 0.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Aldous and Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Open Problem 7.27 (Chapter 7, p. 259) asks whether, over arc-transitive graphs excluding the n-cycles, tau* = O(n log n), tau2 = O(n) and tau*/(2 tau0) = 1 + o(1). Our result (id P0208, 2026-09-08): all three claims are FALSE. The counterexample is the lexicographic product C_m[Kbar_2] for odd m >= 5 - the m-cycle with every vertex split into two non-adjacent twins - which is connected, 4-regular, arc-transitive and not a cycle, on n = 2m vertices. With g(j) = j(m-j) + m the mean hitting time at cycle-distance j and 2m the twin hitting time: tau* = 2*floor(m^2/4) + 2m ~ n^2/8 (quadratic, not O(n log n)); tau2 = 1/(1 - cos(2 pi/m)) ~ n^2/(8 pi^2), because A(C_m[Kbar_2]) = A(C_m) tensor J_2 so the relaxation time is the m-cycle's own; and tau*/(2 tau0) tends to 3/2, not 1 + o(1). Verification, as the source words it: exact hitting times by linear algebra at m = 5, 7, 9, 11, 15, 21 (all five formulas exact at every size); arc-transitivity checked mechanically at m = 5, 7, 9 (the group generated by the rotation, one reflection and one fibre swap has order 2^m * 2m and its orbit of one arc is all 8m arcs); and a Lean file P0208.lean with nine theorems, no sorry, axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only. Not formalised: uniqueness of the solution of (I-P)h = 1 and the tensor eigenvalue computation, both standard and checked numerically. Prior art not cleared. odd m >= 5 simple random walk on the lexicographic product C_m[Kbar_2] (n = 2m vertices, 4-regular, arc-transitive, not a cycle)

[Thm Inverse4 of arXiv:2609.01350, 'New classes of trace-form permutation polynomials and their compositional inverses'] Let $q=2^m$ with $m$ odd, and let
$f_2(x)=x+\gamma{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}\big(c_1x+c_2x^2+x^{2q-1}\big)$ with
$c_1,c_2\in\mathbb F_{q^2}$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb F_{q^2}\setminus\mathbb F_q$
satisfying
\[
  \gamma^{3(q-1)}=1,\qquad
  1+{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_1\gamma)=\gamma^{2q-1},\qquad
  {\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_2\gamma^q)=0,
\]
so that $f_2$ is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb F_{q^2}$ by
Theorem~(Result2 of the paper)(3). Then
\begin{equation}
  f_2^{-1}(x)=
  \begin{cases}
    0
      & \text{if } x=0,\\[0.8em]
    x+\gamma^{q-1}\Big(h_2(x)+\dfrac{{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(x^3)}{x^{q+1}}\Big)
      & \text{if } x\neq0,\ r=0,\\[0.8em]
    x+\gamma^{q-1}\Big(h_2(x)+\dfrac{{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(x^3)}{x^{q+1}}
      +r^{1/3}+\dfrac{P}{r^{1/3}}\Big)
      & \text{if } x\neq0,\ r\neq0,
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}
where
\[
  P=h_2(x)^2+h_2(x)\,{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}\big(\gamma^{q-1}x^q\big)
    +\frac{{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(\gamma x)^3\,{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(x)^3}{\gamma^3\,x^{2q+2}},
  \qquad
  r=P\Big(h_2(x)+\frac{{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(x)^3}{x^{q+1}}\Big).
\]

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.29536, 'Multi-hop visibility through the vacant set of Poissonian obstacles'] Let $\mathcal C$ be the occupied set of a Poisson-Boolean model in dimension $d\geq 2$, the Poisson cylinders in dimension $d\geq 3$ or the Brownian interlacements in dimension $d\geq 3$ (see Section~\ref{sec:notation+models} for the precise definitions). Let $\delta_r$ be as above and let $h_r=\sqrt{r\log r}$ for the Brownian interlacements in dimension $d=3$ and, otherwise, $h_r=\sqrt r$.
For any $N\geq 0$, there exist $c = c(d,N,\mathrm{law}(\mathcal C))$ and $C = C(d,N,\mathrm{law}(\mathcal C))$ such that 
\begin{equation}
c\,\Big(\frac{r}{\delta_r}\Big)^{d-1}\Big(\frac{h_r}{\delta_r}\Big)^{dN} f(r) 
\leq P_{\mathrm{vis}}^N(r)\leq 
C\,\Big(\frac{r}{\delta_r}\Big)^{d-1}\Big(\frac{h_r}{\delta_r}\Big)^{dN} f(r).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2609.01020, '2609.01020'] Assume that $f=(f_1,\ldots , f_d)\colon X\longrightarrow \CC_s^d$ 
satisfies the Thom condition in a direction $a\in \CC^d \setminus \mathrm{C}_{\{0\}}(\Delta_f)$. 
Then there exists a neighborhood $U\subset \CC^d \setminus \mathrm{C}_{\{0\}}(\Delta_f)$ 
of $a$ and $0<\e_0 \ll 1$ such that for any 
$0<\eta \ll \e \leq \e_0$ the restriction 
\begin{equation}
B(0;\e) \cap f^{-1}(D_{\eta}^\ast \cap \CC^\ast U) \longrightarrow D_{\eta}^\ast \cap \CC^\ast U 
\end{equation}
of $f$ is a locally trivial fibration, where we set 
\begin{equation}
D_{\eta}^\ast \coloneq \{s=(s_1, \ldots , s_d) \in \CC^d \mid 0< 
\sqrt{\abs{s_1}^2+ \cdots +\abs{s_d}^2} <\eta \}.

[Lemma 1 (Conditional Tweedie identity) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Suppose that \(\E\|X_0\|^2<\infty\) and that differentiation may be
interchanged with the noising integrals in
\eqref{eq:noised-distribution} and \eqref{eq:noised-posterior-law}.  For
\(t>0\), define
\[
m_t(x)=\E[X_0\mid X_t=x],
\qquad
m_t^r(x)=\E[X_0\mid X_t=x,R=r].
\]
Then, for every \(r\) with \(0<p_R(r)<\infty\),
\begin{equation}

\nabla_x\log p_t(x\mid r)=\frac{a_tm_t^r(x)-x}{\Delta_t},
\end{equation}
and the smoothed likelihood force is
\begin{equation}

g_t(x,r):=\nabla_x\log p(r\mid X_t=x)
=
\frac{a_t}{\Delta_t}\{m_t^r(x)-m_t(x)\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conditional Tweedie identity

body: A differentiable function f on R^n is L-smooth if its gradient is L-Lipschitz: ||grad f(x) - grad f(y)|| <= L ||x - y|| for all x, y. L-smoothness implies the descent inequality f(y) <= f(x) + <grad f(x), y - x> + (L/2) ||y - x||^2.

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2605.21424, 'A dice game, a multinomial walk, and the inverted Dirichlet distribution'] Let \(\alpha>0\) and let \((G_n)_{n\in \N_{\ge 1}}\) be a sequence of random variables, where \(G_n\) has a \(\operatorname{Gamma}(\alpha n,1)\) distribution, for every \(n\in\N_{\ge 1}\). Then 
\[
\lim_{n\to \infty}\P\Big(\sqrt{\alpha n}\Big(\frac{G_n}{\alpha n}-1\Big)\le b\Big)=\Phi(b),
\]
where \(\Phi(b)=\int_{-\infty}^b\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{z}{2}}dz\) denotes the standard normal CDF.

body:
[Corollary 12 (State-selection alternatives under a fixed calibration) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Assume the response program is causally calibrated.  Let $C^\circ$ be a
candidate coordinate on the descended operational core, with values in a
complete Hausdorff causal uniform space and commuting there with the declared
truncations, and let
$\mathsf Z_{\mathfrak R}$ be the completion generated by the declared
calibrated response profile.  Then the following alternatives are exhaustive.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item If $C^\circ$ is not constant on response-equivalence classes, the
declared program identifies core inputs carrying different $C^\circ$-values.
The coordinate does not descend and is invisible to the declared program.
\item Suppose $C^\circ$ descends to the response quotient but is not uniformly
continuous for the response-generated uniformity.  Then the present
calibration does not control that coordinate.  Retaining it requires adjoining
its uniform structure and recompleting with the refined calibration.  In a
metrizable presentation,
failure is witnessed by pairs $u_n,v_n$ with response distance tending to zero
but with the $C^\circ$-distance bounded away from zero.
\item Suppose $C^\circ$ is uniformly continuous.  It then extends uniquely to
a uniformly continuous stable-causal coordinate
$C:\mathsf Z_{\mathfrak R}\to\mathsf C$.  Relative to a proposed
stable-causal compression $\pi:\mathsf Z_{\mathfrak R}\to\mathsf Y$, the
coordinate is propagated exactly when there is a stable-causal
$\widetilde C:\mathsf Y\to\mathsf C$ such that
$C=\widetilde C\circ\pi$.
\item If the extension in \textup{(iii)} exists but no such factorization
through $\pi$ exists, then $\pi$ is not lossless for any response package
containing $C$.  In particular, a coordinate of the least state may be removed
through $\pi$ only when the whole least state admits stable-causal
recovery from $\pi(\mathsf Z_{\mathfrak R})$.
\end{enumerate}
The same alternatives apply to a tangent or derivative coordinate after its
scale and response calibration have been declared.

 \delta_\ell(R\e)\leq C_\ell d^{(\lceil\ell/2\rceil-2)_+},\quad\ell=2,\dots,2N+2,\\
d^2/\la\leq C_0, \qquad R\e \leq \min(1/3, 2/(4C_2+C_3), \rho_0),\end{align}
where $\rho_0$ is as in Assumption~\ref{assume:D} and the $\delta_\ell$ are as in \eqref{deldef}, with $H=I_d+\nabla^2\psi(0)$. Then
\bs
\mathbb P\left(\mathcal N\left(0_{d+1}, \,I_{d+1}\right)\in  D_\la\right) = \frac{e^{-\la/2}\la^{-1/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi\det H}}\left(1+\sum_{m=1}^{N-1}a_m\left(\frac{d^2}{\la}\right)^{m} + \Rem_N\right),\es where 
\bs
\max_{m=1,\dots,N-1}|a_m|&\leq C(C_2,\dots,C_{2N+2}, N),\\
|\Rem_N|&\leq C(C_0, C_2,\dots,C_{2N+2}, N)\bigg(\frac{d^2}{\la}\bigg)^{N}.\es Here, $a_m$ is as in~\eqref{amdef}, with the $\g_k$ as in~\eqref{gkdef1}, where $\g(x)\equiv1$ and $\z(x,0)=\|x\|^2/2 +(\psi(x)+1)^2/2$. In particular, 
\bs
d^2a_1 = & - 1  -\frac12\mathrm{Tr}(\nabla^2\psi_H(0_d)) +\frac{1}{12}\|\nabla^3\psi_H(0_d)\|^2_{F} + \frac18\|\langle\nabla^3\psi_H(0_d),I_d\rangle\|^2 \\

body: [Theorem teoexlp of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1 \leq q, r < \infty$ and $1 < p < \infty$ be given. Then, the pair $(\ell_p, \ell_q)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_r$ if and only if $q< p$ or $r \geq p^*$.

body:
[Defn 3 of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] [Distinguishability With Respect to Fixed Sequences] 
Fix two sequences of distributions $\mu_{n}, \nu_{n}$ that take on values in the set $\mathcal{S}_{n}$, and let $f_{n}$ be a sequence of functions from $\mathcal{S}_{n}$ to $\mathbb{R}$.

We say the sequence $f_{n}$ \textit{weakly} distinguishes $\mu_{n}$ and $\nu_{n}$ if
\be 
\sqrt{\max(\Var_{\mu_{n}}(f_{n}),\Var_{\nu_{n}}(f_{n}))} = O(|\mathbb{E}_{\mu_{n}}[f_{n}] - \mathbb{E}_{\nu_{n}}[f_{n}] |),
\ee 
and \textit{strongly} distinguishes if the LHS is 
$o(|\mathbb{E}_{\mu_{n}}[f_{n}] - \mathbb{E}_{\nu_{n}}[f_{n}] |)$.
title: Definition 3 of arXiv:2608.17374

body:
[Theorem 1 (Exact marked renewal at the stopping times) of arXiv:2608.06299, '2608.06299'] Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$ be independent Haar-random elements of
$\pinf$.  Then the vectors
\[
        \rho_0^{(r)},\rho_1^{(r)},\ldots
\]
are iid and uniformly distributed on $\F_q^r$.  Moreover,
\[
        J_n^{(r)}
        =
        \one_{\{L_r(n+1)>L_r(n)\}}
        =
        \one_{\{\rho_n^{(r)}\ne0\}},
        \qquad n\ge0.
\]
Consequently, the variables $J_0^{(r)},J_1^{(r)},\ldots$ are iid
Bernoulli variables with
\[
        \Prob(J_n^{(r)}=1)=1-q^{-r}.
\]
Conditionally on $J_n^{(r)}=1$, the projective mark
$[\rho_n^{(r)}]\in\mathbb P^{r-1}(\F_q)$ is uniform. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact marked renewal at the stopping times

body: Ergodic theory is a branch of mathematics that studies statistical properties of deterministic dynamical systems; it is the study of ergodicity. In this context, "statistical properties" refers to properties which are expressed through the behavior of time averages of various functions along trajectories of dynamical systems. The notion of deterministic dynamical systems assumes that the equations determining the dynamics do not contain any random perturbations, noise, etc. Thus, the statistics with which we are concerned are properties of the dynamics.
title: Ergodic theory

[Lemma lemma 2 of arXiv:2411.12474, 'Multi-type branching processes with immigration generated by point processes'] Under the assumptions of 
Theorem (thm: DPP2 of the paper) and (equation eq:strong of the paper),
\begin{enumerate}
    \item if $\delta>\rho$, then
for some $A_i \in \mathbb{R}_+$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\mleft [ Z_i(t)\mright ]\stackrel{\infty}{\sim} A_ie^{\delta t},
\quad
\text{and}
\quad
\operatorname{Var}(Z_{i}(t)) = 
	\begin{cases}
	\bo{e^{\max\{2\rho, \delta\} t}} & \text{if $\rho > 0$ and $\delta\neq2 \rho$},\\
		\bo{t e^{\delta t}} & \text{if $2\rho=\delta > 0$}.
	\end{cases}
\]
\item if $\delta=\rho>0$, then for some $A_i'\in \mathbb{R}_+$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\mleft [ Z_i(t)\mright ]\stackrel{\infty}{\sim} A'_ite^{\delta t},
\quad
\text{and}
\quad
\operatorname{Var}(Z_{i}(t)) = 
		\bo{e^{2\delta t}}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. The identities above need independent coordinates. Let X_1 = X_2 = B with B uniform on {0, 1}. For f = B: H_0 = 0, H_1 = H_2 = 1/4, so the inversion formula returns W_1 = 1/2 and W_2 = -1/4; R_0 = R_1 = 0 and R_2 = 1/4, so D_2 = -1/4; and redrawing one coordinate from its correct marginal while keeping the other gives mean squared change 1/4 averaged over the two choices, while 2 R_1 = 0. For f = B - 1/2: A_0 f = 0 and A_1 f = A_2 f = f, so the formal P_1 f = 2f and P_2 f = -f, P_1 is not idempotent, and ||P_1 f||^2 + ||P_2 f||^2 = 5/4 while Var(f) = 1/4.

[Corollary 17 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] Let $P$ be the transition matrix of the RWBD chain. Then, $\Phi$ is an eigenfunction of $P$ with eigenvalue $\alpha$ if
         \[\alpha= 1 - \frac{n}{d(n-1)}\quad \text{and}\quad \Phi(x) = 1 \frac{nx}{d(n-1)}\]
         \begin{proof}
           Clearly $\alpha = \lambda_1$. Hence, consider $K_1(x)$
            \begin{align*}
            K_1(x) &= \sum_{j=0}^1 (-1)^j{x \choose j}{d-x \choose 1-j}(n-1)^{1-j}\\
            &= (-1)^0{x\choose 0}{d-x \choose 1}(n-1)^{1} + (-1)^1{x \choose 1}{d-x\choose 0}(n-1)^{0}\\
            &= (d-x)(n-1) -x\\
            &= d(n-1) -nx\\
            &\propto 1 -\frac{nx}{d(n-1)} = \Phi(x)
            \end{align*}
            Thus, $\Phi(x)$ is an eigenfunction with eigenvalue $\alpha$.
         \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 17 of arXiv:2604.07478

body: [Theorem 4.6 of arXiv:2110.09034, 'On the construction of cospectral nonisomorphic bipartite graphs'] Let GL and GH be bipartite graphs. Let GL be a biregular bipartite graph with distinct degrees and let GH be balanced. [Definition Definition_DBM of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] For a real $\beta>0$, the Dyson Brownian Motion (DBM) is the (unique,
strong) solution\footnote{For $0<\beta<1$ a special care is needed, because particles start to collide, see [cepa1997diffusing].} of the system of $N$ stochastic differential equations
\begin{equation}
 
\mathrm{d}Y_i(\tau )=\frac{\beta}{2}\,\sum_{j\neq i} \frac{1}{Y_i(\tau )-Y_j(\tau )}\,\mathrm{d}\tau +
\mathrm{d}W_i(\tau ), \quad i=1,2,\ldots,N,
\end{equation}
where $W_1,W_2,\ldots,W_N$ are independent standard Brownian motions.
title: Definition Definition_DBM of arXiv:2411.10829

[Theorem 8 (Theorem~4.1 of \cite{FK06}) of arXiv:2607.12666, 'Sample-path Large deviations for \\Scheduled Arrival Processes with Unpunctuality'] Let $\{X^{(n)}\}$ be a sequence of processes in $D([0,T])$. Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a dense set $T_0\subset[0,T]$ such that, for every $t\in T_0$, the sequence $\{X^{(n)}(t)\}$ is exponentially tight in $\R$;
\item for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n
\log\Pbb\bigl(w'(X^{(n)},\delta,T)>\varepsilon\bigr)
=-\infty.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then $\{X^{(n)}\}$ is exponentially tight in $D([0,T])$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem~4.1 of \cite{FK06}

[Lemma lem:propagation_xi of arXiv:2607.08914, 'Linear spreading speed in non-monotone population models'] Let $\xi^{\pm}_{k}$ be \emph{comparison density profiles}. For

  $\zeta \in E^\mathbb{Z}$ define the event
  \begin{equation*}
    A_k(x,\zeta) \coloneq
    \Big\{ \delta_R(y,\zeta) \in \big[\xi_k^{-}(y), \xi_k^{+}(y)\big]
      \quad \text{for all } y \in B_R(x) \Big\}.

  Then

    \mathbb{P}\Big( \xi_{k+1}^{-}(x) \le \delta_R(x, F(\zeta,U)) \le \xi_{k+1}^{+}(x)
      \Bigm| A_k(x,\zeta) \Big)
    \ge 1-C \exp(- c V_R),
  \end{equation*}
  where $c,C>0$ are constants dependent on $ \varepsilon, \delta$ and $\mu$
  but not $R$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let Y be finite with a distinguished always-true empty fact bot, and let p be a random probability vector with law nu. For each p put F(p)=supp(p) union {bot}, H(p)=Y\F(p). Fix O subset Y with O subset F(p) nu-almost surely, and require U=Y\O nonempty. Fix a generator g on Y and a partition Pi into nonempty cells, both fixed relative to p~nu. Define q=p^Pi by q(y)=p(B)/|B| on B in Pi and TV(q,g)=(1/2)*sum_y |q(y)-g(y)|. Then E_nu[(p(U)-TV(q,g)-g(H(p)))_+] <= max_(y in U) Pr_nu(y in F(p)) + |O|*max_(y in U) E_nu[p(y)]. In the language-model application nu is the posterior after observing training data; O, g and Pi are fixed conditional on those data. No conclusion that every uncalibrated generator hallucinates is asserted.
Finite Y, distinguished bot, F=supp(p) union {bot}, and observed O true almost surely.
Nonempty unobserved U; g and Pi fixed under the posterior draw.

\bigwedge_{s = 1}^{m} \; \bigwedge_{t = 1}^{2^s}
\neg \textsc{Stop}\!\left(\mathcal{O}_{s,t}, \varepsilon, w\right)
\Biggr),
\]
where $\{\mathcal{O}_{s,t}\}$ are the dyadic sub-orbits of $\mathcal{O}$
(Definition~(def:dyadic-suborbit of the paper)), and where $\Phi(\mathcal{O})$ holds if and only if
\[
\textsc{Stop}(\mathcal{O}, \varepsilon, w)
\;\vee\;
\textsc{SubStop}(\mathcal{O}_+^{\mathrm{ext}}, \varepsilon, w)
\;\vee\;
\textsc{SubStop}(\mathcal{O}_-^{\mathrm{ext}}, \varepsilon, w)
\;\vee\;
|\mathcal{O}| = 2^M.
\]
The forward and backward extensions are defined by
\[
\mathcal{O}_+^{\mathrm{ext}} = (\sigma \circ \rho^i)_{i = b+1}^{b+2^m},
\qquad
\mathcal{O}_-^{\mathrm{ext}} = (\sigma \circ \rho^i)_{i = a - 2^m}^{a - 1}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let f : R^d -> C be Lebesgue measurable and finite almost everywhere, let E be a measurable set of FINITE measure, and let eps > 0. Then there is a CLOSED set F contained in E with |E \ F| < eps such that the RESTRICTION of f to F is continuous. Moreover one may take g in C_c(R^d) with g = f on F and sup |g| <= sup |f|. The theorem does not assert that f is continuous AT the points of F as a function on R^d: the indicator of the rationals is nowhere continuous on R, yet it agrees with the zero function off a set of measure zero, and Lusin's F can be taken to be any closed set of irrationals of nearly full measure. Finiteness of |E| may be relaxed to sigma-finiteness by exhausting E, at the price of stating the conclusion with |E \ F| < eps for each piece. [standard; e.g. Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Theorem 2.24]
f measurable and a.e. finite
|E| < infinity (or E sigma-finite, applied piecewise)
the measure is Borel regular, so that inner regularity by closed sets is available

[Theorem thm:mSDE-path-subgaussian of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Suppose that $\Omega^{(A)}_{\gamma}$ from \pref{eq:event-opnorm} and $\Omega^{(\mathrm{free})}$ from \pref{eq:event-free} both hold.

Let $0 < T < \infty$.
Let $\mathcal W:=C^0([0,T],\mathbb R^n)$, equipped with the uniform norm
$\|x\|_\infty:=\sup_{0\leqslant t\leqslant T}\lpnorm{x_t}$, and let
$P:=\dist(\widehat{m}_\cdot)$ be the law of the full path of the ASL-TAP SDE~\pref{eq:asl-tap-m} on $\mathcal W$.
For some constant $C_K$, define
\[
c_{T_2}:=\frac{3T}{\gamma^2}\exp\left(\frac{3T(T+4)C_K^2}{\gamma^{12}}\right).
\]
Then:

\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}]
For every probability
measure $\mu$ on $\big(\mathcal W,\mathcal B(\mathcal W)\big)$, where $\mathcal B$ is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathcal W$,
\[
d_{W,2}(P,\mu)^2\ \leqslant\ 2c_{T_2}\,H(\mu\mid P).
\]

\item[\textup{(ii)}]
For every $P$-integrable $K_F$-Lipschitz functional $F:(\mathcal W,\|\cdot\|_\infty)\to\mathbb R$,
    \[ \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}_{P}\left[\exp\left(\lambda\left(F - \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}_{P}[F]\right)\right)\right] \leqslant \exp\left(\frac{\lambda^2c_{T_2}K_F^2}{2}\right),\qquad \forall \lambda \in \mathbb R. \]
    In sub-Gaussian tail bound form,
\[
\mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}_P\Big(\big|F-\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}_P[F]\big|>r\Big)
\ \leqslant\
2\exp\!\left(-\frac{r^2}{2c_{T_2}K_F^2}\right),
\qquad r>0.
\]
\end{enumerate}
