[Proposition3prime 14 of arXiv:2608.28528, 'Strong solutions of SDEs with critical discontinuities in diffusion coefficients'] Assume that $\theta>0$ in the definition of $\rho$ is fixed sufficiently
small. There exist positive constants $C_0$ and $K$, independent of the
smoothness and boundedness of $b$ and $f_i$, such that, for every $n\geq 1$,
every $0\leq T_0<T_1\leq T$, and every $1\leq \alpha_i\leq d$,
\begin{equation}
 \left\|
 \mathbf E\int_{\Delta_n(T_0,T_1)}
       \prod_{i=1}^n
       \nabla_{\alpha_i}f_i(t_i,X_{t_i}^{\,\cdot})
       \,dt_1\cdots dt_n
 \right\|_{L^2_\rho(\mathbb R^d)}^2
 \leq
 C_0K^n(T_1-T_0)^{\frac{\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, $K$ can be made arbitrarily small by requiring the form-bounds
$\delta$ and $\nu$ in \eqref{b_fbb} and \eqref{fbb_fi} to be sufficiently
small.

=

[Proposition 29 (Response characterization of the split topology) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $a\in\operatorname{Fin}(H)_{\rm sk}$ and
$q\in\operatorname{Fin}(H)_{\rm sa}$.  The gauges induced by the two
coefficient classes satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{K\in\mathbb K_A}|\operatorname{Tr}(K^*a)|=\|a\|_2,
 \qquad
 \sup_{S\in\mathbb K_Q}|\operatorname{Tr}(Sq)|=\|q\|_1.
\end{equation}
Consequently the Hausdorff completion of the common finite-rank central
skeleton in the topology determined by the principal response syntax is
canonically
\begin{equation}
 H\times\mathcal S_2(H)_{\rm sk}\times\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}.
\end{equation}
The stochastic identification of the two central coordinates is given by
\Cref{prop:semimartingale-verifies-principal-response}.

[Lemma lem:eta-barycenter-identification of arXiv:2606.29557, 'Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states'] Let \(\mathbf q_T^Y\) denote the \(\mathsf Y_T\)-marginal of
\(\mathbf q_T\). Then \(\mathbf q_T^Y\) is equivalent to
\(\mathbb W_T^m\), and the version in
(equation eq:eta-bar-gamma-barycenter of the paper) may be chosen so that
\begin{equation}
  \overline\gamma_t(Y)
  =
  \Pi_t(Y)
  =
  \mathbb E_{\mathbf q_T}
  \left[
    X_t\mid\sigma(Y_s:0\le s\le t)
  \right].
  
\end{equation}
Moreover, under Wiener measure, and hence under every equivalent measure,
\(\Pi\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  \mathrm d\Pi_t
  =
  \mathfrak l_t(\Pi_t)\,\mathrm d t+
  \sqrt{\eta}
  \sum_{k=1}^m
  \mathcal E_{L^{(k)}}(\Pi_t)
  \left(
    \mathrm d Y_t^k
    -
    \sqrt{\eta}\,b^{(k)}(\Pi_t)\,\mathrm d t
  \right).
\end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Combine the known factorial-type lower bound heuristics with Graham's Borel-type bounds. Result: The source cites Graham's Borel-type bounds on the remainder; if the coefficients a_i satisfy |a_i| >= c K^i i! for infinitely many i then the radius is zero, and the computed a_i (Clisby-Liang-Slade) grow consistently with factorial growth. A rigorous proof of divergence would follow from a lower bound on the number of lace diagrams contributing with the same sign at order i, i.e. a non-cancellation statement; the lace expansion for SAW has alternating-sign contributions (pi^{(N)} with sign (-1)^N) so cancellation cannot be excluded without an explicit asymptotic analysis of the diagram sums. A standard trick for proving zero radius is to exhibit a singularity of the generating function at every point of a circle, which is unavailable here since the 'function' is only asymptotic. I tested the computed coefficients' ratio a_{i+1}/a_i (from the source's cited values, not recomputed here): the ratios increase roughly linearly in i, consistent with factorial growth, but 11 terms cannot certify it. No proof; the conjecture is recorded with the concrete criterion (non-cancellation of leading lace diagrams) that would prove it. Obstruction: Alternating-sign lace contributions may cancel; no asymptotic diagram count with sign control.

[Proposition 27 (A polygonal path avoiding double degeneracies) of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] Let $d, n$ be positive integers, let $\mathcal B \subset \operatorname{GL}_n(\R)$
be finite, and let $X, Y \in \R^{d\times n}$ be regular. Then there exists a
piecewise linear path $\gamma\colon [-1,1] \to \R^{d\times n}$ consisting of at
most two line segments such that $\gamma(-1) = X$, $\gamma(1) = Y$, the path
meets $\bigcup_{B \in \mathcal B} \bigcup_{|I|=d} D_{B,I}$ at finitely many
times $t_1 < \dots < t_L$ only, and for every $\ell \in \{1,\dots,L\}$ and
every $B \in \mathcal B$ the point $\gamma(t_\ell)$ lies on at most one wall
$D_{B,I}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: A polygonal path avoiding double degeneracies

[Definition def: plus minus interface of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Let $$\mathtt{Dob}^+:=\partial\Lambda_N\cap \{z=(z^{(1)},z^{(2)})\in\mathbb Z^d, z^{(2)}\geq 0\},\quad \mathtt{Dob}^-:=\partial\Lambda_N\cap \{z=(z^{(1)},z^{(2)})\in\mathbb Z^d, z^{(2)}<0\}$$
    denote the upper and bottom half parts of the boundary of the box $\Lambda_N.$ Then the Dobrushin boundary condition (denoted $\pm$) is the boundary condition that being plus on $\mathtt{Dob}^+$ and minus on $\mathtt{Dob}^-.$ Now given any configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{\Lambda_N}$ satisfying Dobrushin boundary condition, we define the upmost plus--minus boundary interface $\gamma=\gamma(\sigma)$ as follows.

Let
$
\mathtt{Plus}(\sigma)=\{z\in\Lambda_N:\sigma_z=1\}
$
denote the set of plus spins. By definition, we have
$
\mathtt{Dob}^+\subset \mathtt{Plus}(\sigma).
$
Since $\mathtt{Dob}^+$ is connected in $\mathbb Z^2$, there exists a unique connected component of $\mathtt{Plus}(\sigma)$ containing $\mathtt{Dob}^+$, which we denote by $\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)$.

Define
\[
\Lambda^+(\sigma)
=
\big\{
z\in\Lambda_N:
\text{every path from }z
\text{ to }\partial\Lambda_{N+1}
\text{ intersects }
\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)
\big\},
\]
and let
$
\Lambda^-(\sigma)=\Lambda_N\setminus\Lambda^+(\sigma).
$
Intuitively, $\Lambda^+(\sigma)$ is obtained by filling in all holes of $\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)$.

We then define
\[
\gamma^+(\sigma)
=
\{x\in\Lambda^+(\sigma):
\exists y\in\Lambda^-(\sigma)
\text{ with }
x\sim_* y
\}
\setminus \mathtt{Dob}^+,
\]
and
$\gamma^-(\sigma)=\partial_{\mathrm{ext}}\Lambda^+(\sigma)\setminus \mathtt{Dob}^-.$
Here $x\sim_* y$ means that $x$ and $y$ are $*$-neighbors. By planar duality, $\gamma^+$ forms a connected set of plus spins, while $\gamma^-$ forms a $*$-connected set of minus spins. Hence
$
\gamma=(\gamma^+,\gamma^-)
$
defines a plus--minus interface. Moreover, $\gamma$ is the upmost interface, since every $*$-connected minus path from $\mathtt{Dob}^-$ to $\mathtt{Dob}^-$ must intersect $\gamma^+$.

Finally, let $\Sigma_\gamma$ denote the collection of configurations satisfying $\gamma(\sigma)=\gamma$.
It is easy to see that 
$\Sigma_\gamma=\{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{\Lambda_N}: \sigma_{\mid \mathtt{Dob}^+\cup\gamma^+}=1, \sigma_{\mid \mathtt{Dob}^-\cup\gamma^-}=-1\}.$
For convenience, write
$
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,\epsilon h}(\gamma)
=
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,\epsilon h}(\Sigma_\gamma),
$
and similarly
$
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,0}(\gamma)
=
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,0}(\Sigma_\gamma),
$
where the superscript $\pm$ indicates Dobrushin boundary conditions.
title: Definition def: plus minus interface of arXiv:2606.13147

\end{equation} 
Then \(u(x,y)\) is the solution to the Poisson equation \eqref{Poisson_eq}.
Moreover, \(u(x,y)\in C^2\). For all \((x,y)\in \mathbb{R}^n\times \mathbb{R}^m\), \(D_xu(x,y)\) and \(D^2_{xx}u(x,y)\) is linear growth, that is for all \((x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^m\times \mathbb{R}^n\), there exists a constant $L_u>0$ such that 
$$|D_xu(x,y)|\vee|D^2_{xx}u(x,y)|\le L_u(1+|x|+|y|).$$
And \(D_yu(x,y), D^2_{xy}u(x,y), D^2_{yy}u(x,y)\) is globally bounded, that is there exists a constant $L_u>0$ such that 
$$|D_yu(x,y)|\vee|D^2_{xy}u(x,y)|\vee|D^2_{yy}u(x,y)|\le L_u.$$
Moreover, when \(Y\) is independent of \(x\), \(\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}^m}|u(x,y)|\le C(1+|y|)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:optimal-four-mark of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For every $h\geq2$, put
\[
 D_h^{\max}=\binom{h+2}{2}+\mathbf 1_{\{2\nmid h\}}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\qquad \eta_0(h)=D_h^{\max}.\qquad}
\end{equation}
Writing
\[
 Q_h=1+\binom{h+1}{2},
\]
the minimum is attained by
\begin{equation}
 A_h^\star=\{0,1,Q_h,D_h^{\max}\}.
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\[
 R_h^{-1}(4)=\binom{h+2}{2}+1+\mathbf 1_{\{2\nmid h\}}
\]
in the positive-label interval convention.

[Definition {\cite[Definition 4.10 of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] {Gabai1983_FoliationsAndTheTopologyOf3Manifolds_PUB},[AgolZhang2022_GutsInSuturedDecompositionsAndTheThurstonNorm_ARXv1]}]
Let \((N,\gamma)\) be a taut sutured manifold and let \(S\) be the maximal set of pairwise disjoint non-parallel product annuli and product disks in \(N\).
We define the \emph{sutured guts} \(\mathrm{Guts}(N)\) of \((N,\gamma)\) as the sutured manifold obtained from \((N,\gamma)\) by decomposing along \(S\) and discarding \emph{windows}, namely, product sutured manifold components.

The sutured guts is well-defined up to isotopy class of inclusion map by classical JSJ decomposition theory \autocite{Johannson1979_HomotopyEquivalencesOf3ManifoldsWithBoundaries_PUB} \autocite{JacoShalen1979_SeifertFiberedSpacesIn3Manifolds}.

[Theorem 11 (Finite-network well-posedness) of arXiv:2608.16701, 'Order-Sensitive Fast-Synapse Limits in Sparse Excitatory--Inhibitory Threshold--Reset Netw'] For every finite graph, every $\varepsilon>0$, and every regularization
label $o$, the event protocol has a unique global trajectory.  Moreover, for
every $T<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 M_i^{N,\varepsilon,o}(T)
 \le 1+\left\lfloor\frac{T}{\rho_i}\right\rfloor
 \le 1+\left\lfloor\frac{T}{\rho_*}\right\rfloor.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, bounded intervals contain only finitely many firing events.

body:
[Thm 25 of arXiv:2511.22156, ''] There is a Feller process $((X_t)_{t>0},(P^x)_{x\in \tilde{F}})$ on $\tilde{F}$ such that there exists a transition density $p_t(x,y)$ satisfying the two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimate 
	\begin{equation}
	\begin{split} 
		C_1\frac{1}{\mu(B(x,t^{1/\beta}))}\exp(-C_2(\frac{|x-y|^{\beta}}{t})^{\frac{1}{\beta-1}})&\leq p_t(x,y)\\&\leq C_3\frac{1}{\mu(B(x,t^{1/\beta}))}\exp(-C_4(\frac{|x-y|^{\beta}}{t})^{\frac{1}{\beta-1}})
	\end{split} 
	\end{equation}
	for $x,y\in\tilde{F}$ and $t>0$. Here, $C_1$--$C_4$ are the same constants in \eqref{e:6.6}. 
	\begin{proof}
		The proof is essentially the same as the construction of Barlow and Bass \cite{barlow1989construction,BB19993d}. We briefly review the key steps here.
		
		First, by \eqref{e:6.4} and the same proof of \cite[Proposition 5.5(c)]{BB19993d},  
		\[
		P_n^x(\sup_{0<s<t}|X^{(n)}_t-x|\geq r)\leq C_7\exp(-C_8(\frac{r^{\beta}}{t})^{\frac{1}{\beta-1}})\quad\hbox{ for } x\in\tilde{F}_n\hbox{ and }r\geq3^{-n},
		\]
for some constants $C_7,C_8>0$, and hence the law of $P_n^{x_n},n\geq1$ is tight for a bounded sequence $x_n\in\tilde{F}_n$ by the Aldous criterion for tightness  (see \cite[Theorem 16.10 and 16.11]{Kallenberg} for example). 
		
		Next, by the elliptic Harnack inequality (Theorem \ref{theorem4.1}), the mean exit time estimate \eqref{e:6.7} and the same proof of \cite[Section 3.1]{BBKT}, we have 
		$U_\lambda^{(n)}f\hbox{ is equicontinuous for }f\in C_c(\tilde{F}_n)$,
		where $U_\lambda^{(n)}$ is the resolvent operator associated with $X^{(n)}$, i.e. 
		\[
		U_\lambda^{(n)}f(x)=E_n^x[\int_0^{\infty}e^{-\lambda t}f(X_t^{(n)})dt].
		\]
		Hence, by a diagonal argument, there is a subsequence $n_k$ so that $U_\lambda^{(n_k)}f$ converges uniformly on $\tilde{F}$ for every $f\in C_c(\tilde{F}_0)$. 
		
		Finally, by the same argument of \cite[Section 6]{barlow1989construction}, there is a $\mu$-symmetric Feller process $X$ on $\tilde{F}$ such that $P^{x_k}_{n_k}((X^{(n_k)}_t)_{t\geq 0}\in \bullet)$ weakly converges to $P^x((X_t)_{t\geq 0}\in \bullet)$ for every $x_k\in \tilde{F}_{n_k}$ and $x\in\tilde{F}$ such that $x_k\to x$. The transition density estimate \eqref{e:6.22}  follows from \eqref{e:6.11} by taking the limit. \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 24 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] Let $D$ be an open set. 
Suppose that $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\diamond}$ satisfies \eqref{eq:2.3}.  
If $u$ is $\mathscr{E}$-subharmonic in $D$, then $u$ is subharmonic in $D$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{df:stochasticsubharmonicity}.  
Moreover, under {\bf (AC)}, if $u$ is finely continuous and {\rm(}nearly{\rm)} Borel measurable, then $u$ is subharmonic in $D$ without exceptional set.

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2505.20799, 'A note on the improved sparse Hanson-Wright inequalities'] Assume that $\{\delta_{i}, 1\le i\le n \}$ and $\{\zeta_{i}, 1\le i\le n \}$ are two independent sequences of random variables, where $\delta_{i}\sim\textnormal{Bernoulli}(p_{i})$ are independent and $\zeta_{i}$ are independent centered $\alpha$-sub-exponential random variables.
	Consider a random vector $\xi=(\xi_{1}, \cdots, \xi_{n})$  with $\xi_{i}=\delta_{i}\cdot\zeta_{i}$. Let $A=(a_{ij})_{n\times n}$ be a symmetric fixed matrix. Then for $0<\alpha\le 2$ and $t\ge 0$
	\begin{align}
		&\mathbb{P}\{\vert \xi^\top A\xi-\mathbb{E}\xi^\top A\xi\vert\ge L(\alpha)^{2}t  \}\nonumber\\
		\le& 2\exp\left(-c(\alpha)\min\left\{ \frac{t^{2}}{\sum_{k}a_{kk}^{2}p_{k}+\sum_{i\neq j}a_{ij}^{2}p_{i}p_{j}}, \left(\frac{t}{\Vert A\Vert_{l_{2}\to l_{2}}}\right)^{\alpha/2}  \right\}      \right),\nonumber
	\end{align}
where $L(\alpha)=\max_{i}\Vert \zeta_{i}\Vert_{\Psi_{\alpha}}$ and $c(\alpha)$ is a positive constant depending only on $\alpha$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2505.20799

[Lem 86 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] \begin{enumerate}
\item For a real number $r > 0$, $\psi^*A_S - r F$ is nef if and only if 
\[
r \le \frac{1}{a+2}.
\]
In particular, $D$ is a nef but not ample.
\item For a real number $r > 0$, $\psi^*A_S - r F$ is pseudoeffective if and only if 
\[
r \le \frac{2(a+1)}{a(a+2)}.
\]
\item Either $G|_F = \msq_1 + \msq_2$ for some distinct smooth points $\msq_1, \msq_2 \in F$ of $T$ or $G|_F = 2 \msq_3$ for some smooth point $\msq_3 \in F$ of $T$.
\end{enumerate}

Let (x_s,y_s), 1<=s<=m, be a binary-labelled dataset with m>=1, y_s in {-1,1}, and empirical label mean b=(1/m) sum_s y_s satisfying |b|<1. For a prediction g(x), the mixed-input curriculum paper uses L_cov(g,y,x)=max{0,1-y*b-g(x)*(y-b)}. Definition2 states this for a binary-valued estimator; Theorem3 applies the same formula to a real neural-network score. Since y^2=1, L_cov=(1-y*b) max{0,1-y*g(x)}. Thus b=0 recovers the hinge loss, and the under-represented label class receives the larger multiplicative weight.
Binary labels; finite nonempty dataset; empirical label mean strictly between -1 and1.
The algebraic weighted-hinge identity holds for every real score.

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Let $A$ be a Borel subset of $\mathbb{R}^N$. The \textit{$\alpha$-dimensional capacity of $A$ with respect to the metric $m$} is the reciprocal of the minimal energy:\[
\mathrm{Cap}_\alpha(A) := \left[\inf_{\mu \in \mathcal{P}(A)} \mathcal{E}_\alpha(\mu)\right]^{-1},
\]where $\mathcal{P}(A)$ denotes the set of probability measures that are compactly supported within $A$.
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2512.07202

[Prop prop_boundary_continuity_no_flats of arXiv:2606.23648, '\textsc{Optimal Stopping for a Diffusion with Unobserved Bernoulli Drift}'] Let \(J\subset\mathcal I\) be an interval on which the boundary regime is fixed. Suppose that, for every \(x\in J\), the relevant side branches of \(y\mapsto\Phi(x,y)\) in the fixed-\(x\) construction are strictly monotone: the right branch, containing \(b(x)\), is strictly increasing, and, whenever \(a(x)>-x\), the left branch, containing \(a(x)\), is strictly increasing. 
    
    Then the boundary functions are continuous on \(J\). More explicitly, if \(a(x)>-x\) on \(J\), then both \(a(\cdot)\) and \(b(\cdot)\) are continuous on \(J\). If \(a(x)=-x\) on \(J\), then \(b(\cdot)\) is continuous on \(J\), while \(a(x)=-x\) is continuous automatically.

[Prop propconvquad of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] Let $(\gamma_i)$ be a sequence of smooth functions such that, for all $i\in \mathbb{N}$, $\operatorname{supp}(\gamma_i)\subset (0,\mathfrak{T}_i)$ and $\gamma_i \in \ker (J_i)$. Let $Q_i=\langle \Delta_L^i\cdot ,\cdot \rangle_i$, where $\langle \cdot ,\cdot \rangle_i$ denotes the $L^2$ scalar product for the metric $g_i$. We assume that for all $p\in \mathbb{N}$, $\gamma_i^{(p)}$ converges uniformly to some $\gamma_\infty^{(p)}\in C^\infty([0,\pi],\mathbb{R})$ such that $\operatorname{supp}(\gamma_\infty)\subset (0,\pi)$. We also assume that there exists a closed interval $K\subset (0,\pi)$ such that $$\bigcup_{i\in \mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}}\operatorname{supp}(\gamma_i)\subset K.$$
Then $$Q_i(T_i(\gamma_i))\underset{i\to +\infty}{\longrightarrow} Q_c(T(\gamma_\infty)).$$
title: Prop propconvquad of arXiv:2608.25865

[Theorem 10 (I-MMSE formula, Guo, Shamai and Verdú\cite{GuoShamaiVerdu2005}) of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] Let $U$ be an $m$-dimensional random vector with $\E\|U\|^2<\infty$, let $G\sim \cN(0,I_m)$ be independent of $U$, and for $\gamma\ge 0$ set
\[
Y^{\gamma}=\sqrt\gamma\,U+G.
\]
Then the mutual information (measured in nats) satisfies
\[
\frac{d}{d\gamma} I(U;Y^{\gamma})=\frac12\,\E\bigl[\|U-\E[U\mid Y^{\gamma}]\|^2\bigr].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: I-MMSE formula, Guo, Shamai and Verdú\cite{GuoShamaiVerdu2005}

For every $n\ge1$, $v\in {\mathbb{Z}}^2_{\geq0}$ and $1\le s\le\frac{1}{18}|v|_1^{1/3}$ such that $|v|_1\le n$ and $|v_2-v_1|\le s|v|_1^{2/3}$, we have with $w=n\mathbf{e}_+-v$ and $k=\lfloor 2s|v|_1^{2/3}\rfloor+1$ that

$$
{\mathbb{P}}\Big(\hat{\omega}_{(j-1)\mathbf{e}_2+\mathbf{e}_1}^V(\hat{\lambda}^-)\leq \Delta'_j \leq \hat{\omega}_{(j-1)\mathbf{e}_2+\mathbf{e}_1}^V(\hat{\lambda}^+)\text{ for all }-k\le j\le k\Big)\ge1-C\exp(-cs^3).

[Prop mr of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $Z_{s,t}$ be a family of $\mathcal M(\Bbb R^2)$-valued random variables indexed by $-\infty <s\le t<\infty$ with $s,t\in\Bbb Q,$ all defined on some complete probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\Bbb P)$. Suppose that the following are true: 
    \begin{enumerate}
    

    \item $Z_{s_j,t_j}$ are independent under $\Bbb P$ whenever $(s_j,t_j)$ are disjoint intervals.

        \item For all $f\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R^2)$ and all $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ with $\int_\Bbb R\psi=1$, we have that $$\int_{\Bbb R^4 } \delta^{-1}\psi(\delta^{-1}(y-w))\cdot f(x,z) Z_{t,u}(dy,dz) Z_{s,t}(dx,dw)  \to \int_{\Bbb R^2} f(x,z) Z_{s,u}(dx,dz)$$ in probability as $\delta\to 0$, whenever $s<t<u$.

        \item For $n\in \Bbb N$ and $\phi,\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ we have that \begin{align*}\Bbb E\bigg[ \bigg( \int_{\Bbb R^2}& \phi(x) \psi(y)Z_{s,t}(dx,dy) \bigg)^n \bigg] \\&= \int_{\Bbb R^{n}} \prod_{k=1}^n \phi(x_k) \mathbf E_{\mathrm{BM}^{\otimes n}}^{(x_1,...,x_n)} \bigg[\prod_{k=1}^n \psi(B^k_{t-s}) e^{\sum_{1\le i<j\le n} L_0^{B^i-B^j}(t-s)} \bigg] dx_1 \cdots dx_n.
        \end{align*}
        The expectation on the right side is with respect to a $n$-dimensional Brownian motion $(B^1,...,B^n)$ started from $(x_1,...,x_n)$, and $L_0^X$ denotes the local time at 0 of the semimartingale $X$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then 
    there exists a $C(\Bbb R^4_\uparrow)$-valued random variable $\tilde Z$ defined on the same probability space, such that $(Z_{s,t},f) = \int_{\Bbb R^2} f(x,z) \tilde Z_{s,t}(x,z)dxdz$ almost surely, for all $(s,t)\in\Bbb Q^2$ (with $s<t$) and $f\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R^2)$. 
    
    Furthermore, there exists a space-time white noise $\xi$ on $\Bbb R^2$, defined on the same probability space, with the property that $\tilde Z_{s,t}$ are the \textbf{propagators} of (equation she of the paper) driven by $\xi$: for all $s,x\in \Bbb R$ the function $(t,y)\mapsto \tilde Z_{s,t}(x,y)$ is a.s. the It\^o-Walsh solution of the equation (equation she of the paper) started from time $s$ with initial condition $\delta_x(y)$. In particular, the finite-dimensional marginal laws $(Z_{s_1,t_1},...,Z_{s_m,t_m})$ are $\mathrm{uniquely\; determined}$ by Conditions (1) - (3), for any finite collection of indices $s_j\le t_j$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $M$ be a compact metrizable group acting freely on the compact space $\wt B$. 
Let $\rho: M \to {\rm GL}_d(\bb C)$ be a continuous linear representation for some integer $d \geq 1$. 
Then, for every $b \in B = \wt B / M$, there exists a unique complex vector space structure
on the fiber $\pi^{-1}(b)$ such that, for any $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\wt b M = b$,
the map 
\begin{align*}
\psi_{\wt b}:  \bb C^d  &    \longrightarrow  \pi^{-1}(b)  \notag\\
v & \longmapsto  (\wt b, v) M
\end{align*}
is a linear isomorphism.

[Lemma 61 of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] Assume \(A_{\mathrm{loc}}(W)>0\), and let
\(
    0<\sigma<A_{\mathrm{loc}}(W).
\)
Then there exist constants
\(C_{\gamma,\sigma}<\infty\),
\(c_{\gamma,\sigma}>0\),
\(\eta_{\gamma,\sigma}>0\)
such that, for every \(n\ge1\),
\[
    \mathbb P
    \left(
        \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal A_n}
        |\widehat{\mu_\gamma}(\xi)|
        >
        C_{\gamma,\sigma}2^{-\sigma n/2}
    \right)
    \le
    C_{\gamma,\sigma}\exp(-c_{\gamma,\sigma}2^{\eta_{\gamma,\sigma}n})
    +
    C_{\gamma,\sigma}2^{-c_{\gamma,\sigma}n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
    |\widehat{\mu_\gamma}(\xi)|
    =
    O(|\xi|^{-\sigma/2})
    \qquad(|\xi|\to\infty)
\]
almost surely.

[Lemma 3 (Location of conformal factor extremum) of arXiv:2608.26619, 'Uniqueness of Positively Curved Ancient Ricci Flows on Surfaces with Boundary'] Let $g(\psi,\theta,t) = u(\psi,t)g_{0}$, $0\leq t< T$ be a radially symmetric {Ricci flow with boundary} (i.e. not dependent on $\theta$) with the initial data $u(\psi,0) = u_0(\psi)$ satisfying $\partial_\psi u_0 \geq 0$. Then for $0\leq t<T$ and all $\psi\in[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]$ we have
    $$\partial_\psi u(\psi,t)\geq0.$$
    Consequently, the conformal factor $u(\psi,t)$ always achieves its maximum value on the boundary $\{\psi = \pi/2\}$ and its minimum value at the pole $\{\psi=0\}$, whenever the initial data exhibits the same behavior. Furthermore, if the inequality is strict away from the pole, it remains so throughout the evolution.

body:
Let a finite nonempty binary-labeled data set (x_i,y_i), y_i in {-1,+1}, and a real-valued predictor Phi(theta;x) with theta in R^d be given. For each fixed x, theta -> Phi(theta;x) is locally Lipschitz and admits the chain rule: for every locally absolutely continuous arc z, (Phi(z(t);x))'=<h,z'(t)> for every h in its Clarke subdifferential at z(t), for almost every t. Assume common positive homogeneity degree L>0: Phi(a theta;x)=a^L Phi(theta;x) for every a>0. Put q_i(theta)=y_i Phi(theta;x_i), q_min(theta)=min_i q_i(theta), and E(theta)=sum_i exp(-q_i(theta)), without averaging by sample size. Let theta:[0,infinity)->R^d be a locally absolutely continuous Clarke gradient-flow trajectory satisfying theta'(t) in -partial^C E(theta(t)) almost everywhere. Assume there is a finite t0 with E(theta(t0))<1. Every accumulation point u of theta(t)/||theta(t)||_2 as t->infinity has q_min(u)>0, and theta_star=u/q_min(u)^(1/L) satisfies the Clarke KKT conditions for minimizing (1/2)||theta||_2^2 subject to q_i(theta)>=1 for every i. Explicitly there are lambda_i>=0 and h_i in partial^C q_i(theta_star) with theta_star=sum_i lambda_i h_i and lambda_i(q_i(theta_star)-1)=0 for every i, in addition to feasibility. This gives stationarity of every limiting direction. It does not assert that the entire direction trajectory converges, nor that its KKT points are local or global margin optima. The exponential-loss gradient-flow part of Theorem 4.4 is stated here; the source's separate smooth gradient-descent learning-rate hypotheses are not being imported.

Summed exponential loss and a globally defined locally absolutely continuous Clarke gradient-flow trajectory

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2608.26516, '2608.26516'] Let $A$ be a proper PAC learner for a class $\mathcal{H}$ with a sample complexity $n_A(\epsilon,\delta)$. Then there exists a proper PAC learner $\widetilde A$ for $\mathcal{H}$ and a sequence $\gamma_m\to0$ such that for every realizable sample $S$ of size $m$,
\[
\emp_S(\widetilde A_m(S))\le\gamma_m.
\]
Moreover, one may take $n_{\widetilde A}(\epsilon,\delta) \le R(\epsilon,\delta)\, n_A\!\left(R(\epsilon,\delta)^{-2},R(\epsilon,\delta)^{-1}\right)$,
where $R(\epsilon,\delta) = \left\lceil\max\set{2,\epsilon^{-1/2},2/\delta}\right\rceil$.

[Lemma 24 (Uniform curvature-response profiles) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] For every $\varrho\in[0,1]$, problem
\eqref{eq:intro-curvature-response} has a unique solution
$\chi_\varrho\in H^1(\R_+)$.  In addition,
\begin{equation}
 \chi_\varrho\leq0,\qquad
 [0,1]\ni\varrho\longmapsto\chi_\varrho
 \text{ is continuous into }H^1(\R_+)\cap C_b^1(\R_+),
\end{equation}
and there are constants $C,c>0$, independent of $\varrho$, such that
\begin{equation}
 |\phi_\varrho'(y)|+
 \sum_{j=0}^2|\chi_\varrho^{(j)}(y)|
 \leq Ce^{-cy}\qquad(y\geq0).
\end{equation}
At the Neumann endpoint this gives $\chi_1=0$.
title: Uniform curvature-response profiles

Let T be a first-order theory in a language L, and let lambda = max(|L|, aleph_0). If T has an infinite model, then T has a model of every cardinality kappa >= lambda; moreover, every infinite L-structure M has, for each cardinal kappa with lambda <= kappa <= |M|, an elementary substructure of cardinality kappa, and elementary extensions of every cardinality >= max(|M|, lambda). In particular a first-order theory in a countable language with an infinite model has models of every infinite cardinality; first-order logic cannot pin down an infinite cardinality (Skolem's paradox: countable models of set theory exist if any do).

Let G_n=(V_n,E_n) be finite simple undirected graphs, with |V_n| even and tending to infinity, maximum degree at most a fixed integer Delta, and every connected component having at least three vertices. Let E_n' be a uniformly random perfect matching of V_n and let G_n^*=(V_n,E_n union E_n'), using the graph-union model of the source. The discrete-time simple random walk on G_n^* exhibits total-variation cutoff with probability tending to one. For each fixed epsilon in (0,1/2), there is C(Delta,epsilon)>0 such that, with probability tending to one, t_mix(epsilon)-t_mix(1-epsilon)<=C(Delta,epsilon) sqrt(log |V_n|). Its t_mix(1/4) is of order log |V_n| with probability tending to one. This does not identify the optimal deterministic matching, does not require connected base graphs, and does not cover unbounded base degree without further conditions.

[Definition Langevin diffusion on $\R^N$ of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $\pi$ be a distribution on $\R^N$ with density at $x$ proportional to $e^{-V(x)}$ for some function $V$. The \emph{Langevin diffusion} process with stationary distribution $\pi$ is the solution to the stochastic differential equation
    \[ \dif Z_t = - \grad V(Z_t) \dif t + \sqrt{2} \dif B_t, \]
    where $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ is a standard Brownian motion.
title: Langevin diffusion on $\R^N$

\min(f(\mathbf{p}), 1 - f(\mathbf{p})) \ge c \prod_{i=1}^{s+1} p_i^k
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 31 of arXiv:2609.03248, 'Connections between colored restricted $b$-ary and ordinary partitions'] Let $b\geq 2$ and $\rho\geq 1$ be integers. Then the sequence
$\left(\overline{C}_b^\rho(n)\right)_{n\geq 0}$ of $\rho$-color $b$-ary 
partitions of $n$ in which the multiplicity of each part with color $i$ is a 
muliple of $i$, satisfies the identities
\begin{align}
&\sum_{j=0}^{\frac{\rho(\rho+1)}{2}}T(\rho,j)\overline{C}_b^\rho(bn-j)
=\overline{C}_b^\rho(n),\\
&\sum_{j=0}^{\frac{\rho(\rho+1)}{2}}T(\rho,j)\overline{C}_b^\rho(bn+r-j)
= 0 \qquad (1\leq r\leq b-1),
\end{align}
where we assume that $\overline{C}_b^\rho(m)=0$ for $m<0$.

[Proposition 94 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(\Omega,\AA,\PP)$ be a probability space, $\BB$ be a sub-$\sigma$-field of $\AA$ and $f\in \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP[ f^+]\land \PP [f^-]<\infty$. The conditional expectation enjoys the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
			\item (Stability.) If $f\in \BB/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$, then $\PP[ f\vert \BB]=f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\item (Law of total expectation/tower property.) $\PP[\PP[f\vert \BB]]=\PP[ f]$.
			\item Let $\CC$ be another sub-$\sigma$-field of $\AA$.
			
			\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
				\item  (Repeated conditioning/tower property (bis).) If $\BB$ and $\CC$ are comparable with respect to inclusion, then $ \PP_\BB\PP_\CC f=\PP_{\BB\cap\CC}f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
				\item  (Irrelevance of trivial events.) If $\BB\lor \PP^{-1}(\{0,1\})=\CC\lor \PP^{-1}(\{0,1\})$, then $\PP_\BB f=\PP_\CC f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\end{enumerate}
			\item  (Irrelevance of negligible events.)  If  also $g\in  \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$  with $f=g$ a.s.-$\PP$, then $\PP g^-\land \PP g^+<\infty$ and $\PP_\BB f=\PP_\BB g$ a.s.-$\PP$. 
			\item (Conditioning w.r.t. a trivial $\sigma$-field.) If $\BB\subset \PP^{-1}(\{0,1\})$, then  $\PP$-a.s. $\PP_\BB f=\PP f$. In particular $\PP_{\{\emptyset,\Omega\}} f=\PP f$.
			\item (Additivity.) If also $g\in  \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ and $\PP f^-\lor \PP g^-<\infty$, then $\PP_\BB(f+g)=\PP_\BB f+\PP_\BB g$ a.s.-$\PP$. 
			\item (Sufficient condition for defining property.) Assume $\PP\vert f\vert<\infty$. Let also $g\in \mathcal{B}/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$, $\PP\vert g\vert< \infty$. In order that $\PP_\BB f=g$ a.s.-$\PP$ it is sufficient that $\PP[f;B]=\PP[g;B]$ for all $B\in \Pi\cup \{\Omega\}$, where $\Pi\subset 2^\Omega$ is some $\pi$-system  with $\sigma_\Omega(\Pi)=\BB$.
			\item (Defining property extended.) For $h\in \BB/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP(hf)^+\land \PP(hf)^-<\infty$ one has $\PP(h\PP_\BB f)^+\land \PP(h\PP_\BB f)^-<\infty$ and $\PP[hf]=\PP[h\PP_\BB f]$. 
			\item (Conditional determinism/``taking out what is known''. Homogeneity.) If $g\in \BB/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP (fg)^+\land \PP (fg)^-<\infty$, then $\PP_\BB(gf)=g\PP_\BB f$ a.s.-$\PP$. In particular if $c\in \mathbb{R}$, then $\PP_\BB(cf)=c\PP_\BB f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\item  (Monotonicity.) If also $g\in \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP g^-\land \PP g^+<\infty$ and if $f\leq g$ a.s.-$\PP$ (remember: the latter is equivalent to $\PP[f;B]\leq \PP[g;B]$ for every $B\in \AA$), then $\PP_\BB f\leq \PP_\BB g$ a.s.-$\PP$.
			\item (Triangle inequality.) $\vert \PP_\BB f\vert\leq \PP_\BB\vert f\vert$ a.s.-$\PP$. 
			
			\item In this item only we drop the a priori assumption that $\PP f^-\land \PP f^+<\infty$.  Let $(f_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $\AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ and $g$ an element of $\AA/\mathcal{B}_{[0,\infty]}$, such that $\PP g<\infty$ and $f_n^-\leq g$ a.s.-$\PP$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$. 
			
			\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
				\item  (Monotone convergence.) If $f_n\uparrow f$ as $n\to \infty$ a.s.-$\PP$, then $\PP f^-<\infty$ and $\PP_\BB f_n\uparrow \PP_\BB f$ a.s.-$\PP$.
				\item  (Fatou's lemma.) $\PP(\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n)^-<\infty$ and $\PP_\BB\liminf_{n\to\infty} f_n\leq \liminf_{n\to\infty}\PP_\BB f_n$ a.s.-$\PP$.
				\item  (Dominated convergence.) If $\vert f_n\vert\leq g$ a.s.-$\PP$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$ and $f_n\to f$ as $n\to\infty$ a.s.-$\PP$, then $\PP \vert f\vert<\infty$ and $\PP_\BB f=\lim_{n\to\infty}\PP_\BB f_n$ a.s.-$\PP$ and also in $\LL^1(\PP)$.
			\end{enumerate}
			\item
			\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
				\item (Independent conditioning.) If $\BB'$, another sub-$\sigma$-field of $\AA$, and $f'\in \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ with $\PP (f')^+\land \PP (f')^-<\infty$, are such that $\BB\lor \sigma(f)$ is independent of $\BB'\lor \sigma(f')$ under $\PP$, and if furthermore $\PP(ff')^+\land \PP(ff')^-<\infty$, then $\PP_{\BB\lor \BB'}(ff')=(\PP_{\BB}f)(\PP_{\BB'}f')$ a.s.-$\PP$.

[Theorem thm:le-cam-inequality of arXiv:2608.06159, 'Majority Dynamics on Resampled Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi Graphs:\\[0.5ex] Gaussian Winner '] Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\) be independent Bernoulli random variables with
\(\P(\xi_i=1)=p_i\). We denote
\[
W\coloneqq\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i,
\qquad
\lambda\coloneqq\sum_{i=1}^np_i,
\]
and let \(P\sim\Pois(\lambda)\). Then
\begin{align}
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\left|
\P(W=k)-e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^k}{k!}
\right|
\le
2\sum_{i=1}^np_i^2.

\end{align}
Equivalently, under the previous total-variation convention, we have
\begin{align}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\bigl(\mathcal L(W),\mathcal L(P)\bigr)
\le
\sum_{i=1}^np_i^2,

\end{align}
where \(\mathcal L(W)\) and \(\mathcal L(P)\) denote the laws of \(W\) and \(P\), respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 3 (Explicit Main Theorem for $n=2$ over Rational Numbers) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $f,g\in \mathbb{Q}(X)$ be nonzero rational functions.
    Let $D=f(x)\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+g(y)\frac{\partial}{\partial y}$ be a derivation on the field $\mathbb{Q}(x,y)$.

    Then the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exists a non-constant $F\in \mathbb{Q}(x,y)$ such that $D(F)=0$.
        \item One of the following is true:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item All complex residues of $\frac{1}{f}$ and $\frac{1}{g}$ are zero.
        \item There exists irreducible polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in \mathbb{Q}[x],g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{Q}[y]$ and rational numbers $c_1,\ldots,c_n, d_1,\ldots,d_m \in\mathbb{Q}$ such that
        \[
        \frac{1}{f}=\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{c_i f_i'}{f_i}, \hspace{1cm} \frac{1}{g}=\sum_{i=1}^m \frac{d_i g_i'}{g_i}.
        \]
        \item There exists a quadratic extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$, irreducible polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{Q}[y]$ that split over $L$ into conjugate factors $f_i=f_{i1}f_{i2}$ and $g_j=g_{j1}g_{j2}$, and $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in L\setminus \mathbb{Q}$, $d_1,\ldots,d_m\in L\setminus \mathbb{Q}$ satisfying $c_i+\overline{c_i}=0,d_j+\overline{d_j}=0$ such that
        \[
        \frac{1}{f}=\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{c_i (f_{i1}'f_{i2}-f_{i2}'f_{i1})}{f_i}, 
        \hspace{1cm} 
        \frac{1}{g}=\sum_{i=1}^m \frac{d_i (g_{i1}'g_{i2}-g_{i2}'g_{i1})}{g_i}.
        \]
    \end{enumerate}  
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Explicit Main Theorem for $n=2$ over Rational Numbers

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a twice differentiable function $f:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R$, in order for $x\in\mathbb R^N$ to be a local extremum, we must have $f'(x)=0$, and:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f''(x)\geq0$ is needed for $x$ to be a local minimum.

\item $f''(x)>0$ guarantees that $x$ is a local minimum.

\item $f''(x)\leq0$ is needed for $x$ to be a local maximum.

\item $f''(x)<0$ guarantees that $x$ is a local maximum.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 9 (Intrinsic jet formulation of the change-of-variable formula) of arXiv:2608.12225, 'Higher-order variation and\\ pathwise It\^o calculus on manifolds'] Let $p\geq2$, let $X\in V_p(M,\pi)$, and let $\nabla$ be an
affine connection on $M$. For $f\in C^p(M,\mathbb R)$, set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal D_{\pi,X}^{(p),\nabla}(f)
:={}&
\int_0^T
\left\langle
T_\nabla^{p-1}f(X_t),
d_\pi^{p-1}X_t
\right\rangle
+
\frac1{p!}
\int_0^T
\left\langle
\nabla^{(p)}f(X_t),
d[X]_{\pi,t}^{(p)}
\right\rangle .
\end{aligned}
\]
Then $\mathcal D_{\pi,X}^{(p),\nabla}(f)$ depends only on the
reduced $p$-jet
\[
t\longmapsto
[j_{X_t}^p f]
\in
X^*\bigl(J^p(M,\mathbb R)/\mathbb R\bigr),
\]
and is independent of the choice of affine connection $\nabla$.
Moreover,
\[
\mathcal D_{\pi,X}^{(p),\nabla}(f)
=
f(X_T)-f(X_0).
\]
The connection-dependent decomposition into the 
lower-order term and the $p$-th variation term represents an
intrinsic linear functional of the reduced $p$-jet of $f$ along $X$.

body:
For iid Galton-Watson offspring p_k with p0=0, finite mean m>1 and an exponential moment sum b^k p_k<infinity for some b>1, the deterministic speed v(lambda) of the discrete-time walk with parent weight lambda and child weight 1 is differentiable for every lambda in (0,m). In particular, differentiability at lambda=1 follows from this theorem, while the Einstein relation of Ben Arous-Hu-Olla-Zeitouni concerns lambda=m. Source: Bowditch and Tokushige, arXiv:1906.07913, Theorem 1.1, ALEA 17 (2020), 609-642. This states differentiability, not a sign for v'(lambda) or continuity of that derivative at lambda=m.

[Proposition 8 (Tensor form) of arXiv:2609.03958, '2609.03958'] Let $n\geq 2$ and $K\geq 0$. Suppose that $\lambda\in \Gamma_2$ satisfies $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\geq -K$ and $\sigma_2(\lambda)=f$ with $f_0\leq f\leq f_1$ for two constants $f_1\geq f_0>0$ and that $$\ell_i:=\sigma_1(\lambda)-\lambda_i,\ \ \ i=1,\ldots,n.$$
Let $\mathcal T=(\mathcal T_{ijk})$ be a completely symmetric three-tensor and define
\[ s_k:=\sum_i\mathcal T_{iik},
 \qquad q_k:=\sum_i\ell_i\mathcal T_{iik},
\]
then there exist  some constants $C>0$ and $J_0>0$ depending only on $n$, $K$, $f_0$ and $f_1$ such that  
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i,j,k}\mathcal T_{ijk}^2-\sum_k s_k^2
 \geq\frac{7}{6}\frac{1}{\sigma_1(\lambda)+J_0}\sum_k \ell_k s_k^2
      -C\sum_kq_k^2.
\end{equation}
title: Tensor form

[Lemma lem:parabolic-realization-brownian-probes of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Suppose Assumption~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) holds.  Fix $\alpha\geq0$,
let $w=t^\alpha e^\phi$ be a regular weight of order $\alpha$, and let $q$ be
a smooth terminal-gap field whose derivatives have uniform polynomial growth.
Put $F_0^{\rm tan}:=-(\partial_s+\Delta_y/2)q$.  For every sufficiently small
$r>0$ there is $F_r\in L_w^2$ with a terminal gap and
$u_r=SF_r$ whose source and Hessian energies satisfy
\begin{align*}
 r^{1-\alpha}\left\lVert F_r\right\rVert_w^2
 \longrightarrow
 e^{\phi(0)}\norm{F_0^{\rm tan}}_{L^2(s^\alpha\,\mathrm d s\,\mathrm d\gamma_s)}^2,\quad
 r^{1-\alpha}\norm{\operatorname{Hess}_gu_r}_{w,g}^2
 \longrightarrow
 e^{\phi(0)}\left\lVert D_y^2q\right\rVert_{L^2(s^\alpha\,\mathrm d s\,\mathrm d\gamma_s)}^2
 \qquad(r\downarrow0).
\end{align*}
title: Parabolic tangent transfer

\(C<\infty\), depending only on \(K\) and \(\lambda\), with the following

whose local \(\TT^2\)-orbits have diameter at most \(d\leq\beta_0\).  If \(U\)
is a smooth symmetric two-tensor with zero average over the local
\(\TT^2\)-orbits, then
\begin{equation}
        \|U\|_{C^0(M,h)}
        \leq C d\,\|U\|_{C^1(M,h)}.
\end{equation}

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2609.00974 (conj environment labelled conj: alg int conj).] Let $K/\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ be an algebraic extension of fields. Let $\F$ be a foliation on $K$, which admits a model over the ring of integers $\cO_L$, where $L$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}$.

 The following are equivalent:
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item The foliation $\F$ is algebraically integrable, i.e., it is of the form $\F=\op{Der}_{W}(K)$ for a subfield $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\subset W\subset K$.
 \item For almost all primes $p$ and all maximal ideals $q$ over $p$ in $\cO_L$ the reduction modulo $q$ of $\F$ is $p$-closed, i.e., it defines a $1$-foliation.
 \end{enumerate} (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)

[Theorem th marche of arXiv:2411.05541, 'Gaskets of $O(2)$ loop-decorated random planar maps'] Let $\nu$ be a probability distribution on $\mathbb{Z}$ such that $h^\downarrow$ is $\nu$-harmonic on $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$ and such that $\nu$ is not the Dirac mass at zero $\delta_0$. Assume that
	\begin{equation}
		\forall k\ge 1, \qquad \qquad \nu(k-1) \ge \nu(-k-1).
	\end{equation}
	Then,
	\begin{itemize}
		\item Either $\sum_{k\ge 1} k(\nu(k-1)-\nu(-k-1))\in [0,1)$ and there exists $c>0$ such that
		$$
		\nu(-k)\mathop{\sim}\limits_{k \to \infty} \frac{c \log k}{k^2};
		$$
		\item Or $\sum_{k\ge 1} k(\nu(k-1)-\nu(-k-1))=1$ and there exists a slowly varying function $L$ such that $L(k)= o(\log k)$, $1= O(L(k))$ and
		$$
		\nu(-k)\mathop{\sim}\limits_{k \to \infty} \frac{L(k)}{k^2}.
		$$
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th marche of arXiv:2411.05541

[Theorem 6 (Uniform CNN approximation of the autoregressive statistic) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Let \(T\geq2\). For any \(M>0\) and \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\), let \(\bm C_\epsilon\) be the collection of channel sizes used in the ReLU multiplication approximant and take \(\bm L=(L_\epsilon)\), \(\bm k=\{k_{1,1}=2,k_{1,l}=1:l=2,\ldots,L_\epsilon\}\), \(\bm{\mathcal P}=\{(\operatorname{Pool}_{1,l},w_{1,l},s_{1,l})=(\operatorname{Id},1,1):l=1,\ldots,L_\epsilon\}\) and \(\bm m=(1)\), where \(L_\epsilon=O\{\log(2+(T-1)M^2/\epsilon)\}\). Then there exists \(f_{\epsilon,M}^{AR}\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{CNN}}(T,1,\bm L,\bm k,\bm{\mathcal P},\bm C_\epsilon,\bm m)\) such that \(\sup_{\bm X\in\mathcal X_M}\lvert f_{\epsilon,M}^{AR}(\bm X)-S_{AR}(\bm X)\rvert\leq\epsilon\). For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
$
\mathbb I\{f_{\epsilon,M}^{AR}(\bm X)>\lambda\}
=\mathbb I\{S_{AR}(\bm X)>\lambda\},
\bm X\in\mathcal X_M,
\lvert S_{AR}(\bm X)-\lambda\rvert>\epsilon.
$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop Product Expectation is Gaussian pdf of arXiv:2607.17393, 'Optimal Covariance Estimates for Schr\"odinger Semigroups with White Noise in $d=1,2$'] Fix $d\in\{1,2\}$, $x_i,y_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$ for $i=1,2$ and $s,t>0$. Then,
\[\mathbb{E}[\alpha_{t,s}(B_t^{x_1,x_1},\overline{B}_s^{y_1,y_1})\alpha_{t,s}(B_t^{x_2,x_2},\overline{B}_s^{y_2,y_2})]=\int_{[0,t]^2}\int_{[0,s]^2}g^d_{K(s,t,u,v)}(x_1-y_1,x_2-y_2)dudv
\]
where $g^d_{K(s,t,u,v)}$ is a centered multivariate Gaussian density on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d$ with covariance matrix $K(s,t,u,v)=K_0(s,t,u,v)\otimes I_d$
for the matrix function $K_0$
in (equation eqn. Bridge difference covariance of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Defn 31 (\cite{RT}) of arXiv:2608.26068, 'All once-extended 3D TQFTs are Reshetikhin--Turaev theories'] Let $M$ be a closed connected 3-manifold and $\Gamma$ a labelled embedded ribbon graph in $M$ with ribbon-colouring $K$ and vertex labels $\set{f_v}$. The invariant $\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) \in k$ is defined as follows: 

    Let $L$ be a framed link in $S^3$ (viewed as an embedded $S^1\times I$) with $\# L$ components, and $(\Gamma,K,\set{f_v})$ a labelled embedded ribbon graph in $S^3$ such that performing surgery on $L$ yields the pair $(M,|\Gamma|)$. Then, we have an embedding of $|\Gamma\cup L|$ in $S^3$; call this a \emph{surgery presentation} of the pair $(M,|\Gamma|)$. $\Gamma\cup L$ is now a labelled ribbon graph with some uncoloured loops. Additionally, let $X_L$ be the trace of the framed link $L$ (the 4-manifold with boundary $M$ given by attaching 2-handles to $D^4$ along the framed link $L$). Define $\sigma(X_L)$ to be the signature of $X_L$.

    The invariant on the labelled embedded ribbon graph $\Gamma$ is a scalar multiple of the operator invariant of $\Gamma\cup L$: $$\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) := p_-^{\sigma(X_L)}\sqrt{D}^{-\sigma(X_L)-\# L-1} F(\Gamma \cup L,K,\set{f_v}).$$

    In general, if $M$ is not connected, say $(M,\Gamma) = \bigsqcup (M_i,\Gamma_i)$ where each $M_i$ is connected, then we define $$\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) := \prod\tau(M_i,\Gamma_i,K|_{\Gamma_i},\set{f_v})$$ to be the product of $\tau$ over all the components.

body:
[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For every field $\kk$, the class $\RV$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item It is invariant under permutations of variables and nonnegative
rational linear substitutions, including coordinate restriction.
\item It is closed under products.
\item If $f\in\RV$, then every ordinary coordinate derivative
$\partial_x^\gamma f$ lies in $\RV$.
\item It is closed under coordinatewise lower and upper truncations in the
divided-power basis.
\item It is invariant under common divided-power translations:
\[
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha]}\in\RV
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha+\gamma]}\in\RV.
\]
\item If $f\in\RV$, then its factorial normalization $\Nrm(f)$ lies in
$\RV$.
\item If $F_1,F_2$ have realizable factorial normalizations, then
$\Nrm(F_1F_2)$ lies in $\RV$.
\item Full polarization preserves $\RV$.
\item Membership is invariant under arbitrary field extension; for
polynomials with rational coefficients, it depends only on
$\operatorname{char}(\kk)$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lem 13 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Suppose assumptions (A2) and (A4) hold for some $R_0>0$.
Let $D$ be an  open subset of $\sX$.
Then for each $z_0\in \partial D$ and $R\in (0, R_0/16),$    there exists $C=C(z_0, R)>1$   such that

\E_x\tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R)}\leq C \, \E_x\tau_{D\cap B(z_0, R/2)}, \quad x\in D\cap B(z_0, R/4).
\end{equation}
 If  assumptions (A2') and (A5) hold, then the multiplicative constant $C$ in \eqref{e:2.12} depends only on $R.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:tangent-ball-convergence-general of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] Let $K\Subset O$. For $x\in K$ and small $h$, the sets $B_{x,h}$ lie in a
common compact subset of $\mathbb R^n$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{x\in K}|B_{x,h}\mathbin\triangle\widehat B_x|
  \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Consequently, locally uniformly in $x\in O$,
\begin{align}
  \int_{B_{x,h}}\xi_i\xi_jJ_x(\delta_h\xi)\,\,d\xi
  &\longrightarrow M_{ij}(x),
  &&1\leq i,j\leq k,
  \\
  \int_{B_{x,h}}J_x(\delta_h\xi)\,\,d\xi
  &\longrightarrow\widehat V_x.
  
\end{align}
More generally, if $\Psi(x,\xi)$ is continuous on a neighborhood of a common
compact set containing the tangent and rescaled balls, then, for
$\theta\in\{0,1\}$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{B_{x,h}}\Psi(x,\xi)J_x(\delta_h\xi)^\theta\,\,d\xi
 \longrightarrow
 J_x(0)^\theta\int_{\widehat B_x}\Psi(x,\xi)\,\,d\xi .
\end{equation}
The convergence is locally uniform in $x$.

body:
[Definition 17 (Fiber-equivalent torus fibrations) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let
\[
        \pi_i:M\to S^1_i,\qquad i=0,1,
\]
be torus fibrations.  The target circles are not part of the fixed data and may
be different.  Choose a basepoint \(x\in M\) and, for each \(i=0,1\), an identification
\(\pi_1(S_i^1,\pi_i(x))\cong\ZZ\), and let
\[
        \alpha_{\pi_i,x}:\pi_1(M,x)\longrightarrow\ZZ,
\]
be the surjective homomorphism induced by \(\pi_i\).  Changing the
identification changes \(\alpha_{\pi_i,x}\) by a sign.  Equivalently, \(\pi_i\)
determines a cohomology class \([\pi_i]\in H^1(M;\ZZ)\), well-defined up to
sign.  We say that \(\pi_0\) and \(\pi_1\) are \emph{fiber-equivalent}
if
\[
        [\pi_0]=\pm[\pi_1]\in H^1(M;\ZZ).
\]
Equivalently, after choosing a common basepoint,
\[
        \ker\alpha_{\pi_0,x}=\ker\alpha_{\pi_1,x}\subset\pi_1(M,x).
\]
For a different basepoint, the two kernels are changed by the same conjugacy
convention.  Thus, in fiber-subgroup language, the definition says that the
images of the two fiber fundamental groups agree, up to this usual conjugacy
ambiguity.
title: Fiber-equivalent torus fibrations

[Definition def:allHspaces of arXiv:2609.03980, 'Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant H'] Let $\Gamma$ be a relatively open subset of the boundary $\partial \Omega$ of some bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We define the following subspaces of $L^2(\Omega)$.
    \begin{align*}
    H^1_0(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^1_\Gamma(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^{\operatorname{div}}_0(\Omega)& \coloneq   \{f\in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}_N(f) = 0\},\\
        H^{\operatorname{div}}_\Gamma(\Omega)& \coloneq   \{f\in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}_N(f) = 0\},\\
        H^\Delta(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\},\\
         H^\Delta_0(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1_0(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\},\\
          H^\Delta_\Gamma(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1_\Gamma(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\}.
    \end{align*}
    The first two spaces are equipped with the usual $H^1$-norm, the third and fourth with the usual $H^{\operatorname{div}}$-norm,
    and the latter three spaces with the norm $$
        \|f\|_{H^\Delta(\Omega)}^2  \coloneq  \|f\|^2_{H^1(\Omega)}+ \|\Delta f\|^2_{L^2(\Omega)}
    $$
title: Definition def:allHspaces of arXiv:2609.03980

[Lemma 14 (Localized complexity of bounded isotonic calibration) of arXiv:2608.24858, 'Bellman Calibration for Marginalized Importance Weighting in Offline Reinforcement Learnin'] Let \(0<\tau\le M\), and let
\[
  \overline{\mathcal W}_N
  =
  \{u=\theta\circ\widehat w_\pi:
    \theta\text{ nondecreasing},\
    \tau\le u\le M\}.
\]
Define
\[
  \mathcal H_N=\{\log u:u\in\overline{\mathcal W}_N\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal H_N^\circ
  =
  \{h-\mathbb E_{\nu}h:h\in\mathcal H_N\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal H_{N,\Delta}
  =
  \{h_1-h_2:h_1,h_2\in\mathcal H_N^\circ\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal W_N^{\rm norm}
  =
  \left\{
    \frac{u}{\mathbb E_{\nu}u}:u\in\overline{\mathcal W}_N
  \right\}.
\]
For \(Q_{\nu,\Delta}\) and \(Q_{\nu,\pi}\) as in
\eqref{eq:calibration-critical-radius}, define
\[
  \mathcal G_{N,\times}
  =
  \{(x,x^+)\mapsto \omega(x)b(x^+):
    \omega\in\mathcal W_N^{\rm norm},\ b\in\mathcal H_{N,\Delta}\}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\tau,M}<\infty\) such that, for every \(r>0\),
\begin{equation}

\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal R_N(\mathcal H_{N,\Delta},r;P)
  &\le
  C_{\tau,M}
  \left\{\sqrt{\frac{r}{N}}+\frac{1}{Nr}\right\},
  \qquad P\in\{\nu,\mu_{0,\pi}\},\\
  \mathcal R_N(\mathcal G_{N,\times},r;Q)
  &\le
  C_{\tau,M}
  \left\{\sqrt{\frac{r}{N}}+\frac{1}{Nr}\right\},
  \qquad Q\in\{Q_{\nu,\Delta},Q_{\nu,\pi}\}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Consequently, the corresponding critical radius satisfies
\[
  \mathfrak r_{N,\rm fit}
  \le
  C_{\tau,M}N^{-1/3}.
\]
Moreover, one may take
\[
  C_{\tau,M}
  \le
  C\{1+M/\tau\}^{4}
\]
for a universal finite \(C\).

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: A Feller topology for limits of reversible Markov chains structural attempt Result: The suggested unweighted heat-kernel metric can be infinite in a basic admissible example. For Brownian motion on the two-torus, the squared row-distance integrated against exp(-t)dt equals sum_(k in Z^2) |1-exp(2pi*i*k.h)|^2/[1+8pi^2*|k|^2]. At h=(1/2,0), every odd k1 has numerator4. Each dyadic annulus contains order N^2 such terms of order N^-2, so the series diverges. A repair is to use w(t)=exp(-t)/(1+G(2t)), where G is the integrated diagonal heat trace: Fubini gives finite weighted row norm for almost every state. Check: Parseval computes the row norm exactly; integrating the nonnegative Fourier series is justified by Tonelli. For the repaired weight, the average row squared norm is integral w(t)*G(2t)dt<=1. This produces an almost-everywhere finite Hilbert-space pseudometric after identifying indistinguishable rows. Obstruction: Brownian motion already has a good usual topology, so the divergence refutes only the illustrative formula, not the existence conjecture. Completing a heat-kernel embedding can add states; proving valid transition kernels and the Feller property on that completion is still missing.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0235-a-feller-topology-for-limits-of-reversible-markov-chains
No independent review

body: Let X_1, X_2, ... be independent random variables and fix a constant c > 0. For each i define the truncation Y_i = X_i 1(|X_i| <= c). Then the series sum_{i=1}^infinity X_i converges almost surely if and only if all three of the following series converge: sum_i P(|X_i| > c), sum_i E[Y_i], and sum_i Var(Y_i). If one of the three series diverges, the partial sums of sum X_i do not converge almost surely. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]
title: Kolmogorov's Three-Series Theorem

body:
Let T be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space (X, B, mu) and let P and Q be countable measurable partitions with H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity. Write P_n for the join of T^{-i}P over 0 <= i <= n-1 and h_mu(T,P) = lim_n (1/n) H_mu(P_n) (the limit exists by subadditivity and equals the infimum over n). Then h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P) + H_mu(Q | P). Two standard consequences: if P refines Q then H_mu(Q | P) = 0 and hence h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P), so the partition entropy is monotone under refinement; and |h_mu(T,P) - h_mu(T,Q)| <= H_mu(P | Q) + H_mu(Q | P), i.e. the map P -> h_mu(T,P) is 1-Lipschitz for the Rokhlin metric. WHERE IT FAILS: finiteness of H_mu(P) and H_mu(Q) is used - with infinite-entropy partitions both sides can be infinite and the inequality carries no information. The inequality is one-sided: nothing bounds h_mu(T,P) from below in terms of h_mu(T,Q) unless the conditional entropy in the other direction is also controlled. It is an inequality between the entropies of PROCESSES, not of the partitions: H_mu(Q) <= H_mu(P) + H_mu(Q|P) is the (easier) static statement and must not be quoted in its place.
(X,B,mu) is a probability space and T preserves mu (invertibility is not needed)
P and Q are countable measurable partitions
H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity
entropies are taken with a fixed logarithm base throughout

[Thm 6 of arXiv:2606.29132, '\bf Local Well-posedness of General Mean Field Game Master Equations'] Let Assumption \ref{assum-MFGVC} hold and denote $R_0:= L_g + 1$, $R_1 := 2R_0 L_0$, $R_2:= R_0\vee R_1+2$. There exists a constant $\e_0>0$, depending only on $d$,  $L_g$, $L_{\sigma^0}$, $L_0$, and $L(R_2)$, such that the following hold whenever $0<T\leq\e_0$:

\no(i) The FBSDEs \reff{MFGVC-FBSDE1}-\reff{MFGVC-FBSDE2} are well-posed and the MFGVC admits an  MFE $(\a^*, \bm^*)$ at $(0,\mu)$. Moreover, $\bm^*$ is unique.

\no(ii) The master equation \eqref{MFGVC-master}  has a unique classical solution $V\in\cC^{k,2}_b$, and it holds that:
\bea

\left.\ba{c}
\bm^*_t = \cL_{X^\xi_t|\cF^0_t},\q \a^*_t(x) = \phi\big(t, x, \pa_x V(t,x,\bm^*_t), \pa_{xx} V(t,x,\bm^*_t), \bm^*_t\big);\\
Y^{i,\xi}_t = \pa^{(i)}_x V(t, X^\xi_t, \bm^*_t),\q Z^{i, \xi}_t = \cI^{\pa_x^{(i)} V}_t(\Xi^{'\xi}_t),  \\
Y^{i,x}_t = \pa^{(i)}_x V(t, X^x_t, \bm^*_t),\q Z^{i, x}_t = \cI^{\pa_x^{(i)} V}_t(\Xi^{'x}_t), \\
\mbox{where}\q \cI^{\f,1}_t(\zeta') := \pa_x \f(t, x, \bm^*_t)\big(2\pa_{\g} H(\zeta')\big)^{1\over 2} ,\\
\dis \cI^{\f,0}_t(\zeta') :=  \pa_x \f(t, x, \bm^*_t) \si^0(x, \bm^*_t)+  \int_{\dbR^d} \pa_\mu \f(t, x, \bm^*_t, \tilde x)\si^0(\tilde x, \bm^*_t)\bm^*_t(d\tilde x).
 \ea\right.
\eea
Here $\pa^{(i)}_x V$ denotes the $i$-th derivative of $V$ with respect to $x$, $i=0,1,2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:B-inverse of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] The matrix $B$ is invertible. Its inverse $B^{-1}$ is lower triangular with
\begin{equation*}
  (B^{-1})(k,\ell)
  =
  \begin{cases}
    \displaystyle
    (-1)^{\,k-\ell}\,\frac{1}{(k-1)!}\binom{k-1}{\ell-1},
      & 1\le \ell\le k\le n,\\[6pt]
    0,& \ell>k.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lemma-6.14 of arXiv:2412.08964, 'Phase transition and critical behavior in hierarchical\\integer-valued Gaussian and Coulom'] Let~$\beta>\beta_\text{\rm c}$. For each~$A>0$ there exists~$\delta_0>0$ and $\epsilon_0>0$ such that,  for~$\Sigma_0$ defined by~$A$ and any $\delta,\delta'\in(0,\delta_0]$, 
\begin{equation}

\bigl|\partial_\ell F_q(\boldsymbol\lambda)\bigr|
\le\begin{cases}
b(b-1)\theta^{q^2}\lambda(1)+O(\epsilon^2)
,\qquad&\text{if }|q-\ell|=1,
\\
b\theta^{q^2}+O(\epsilon^2),\qquad&\text{if }q=\ell\ge2,
\\
(b\theta^{q^2}+O(\epsilon^2))(bA\epsilon)^{|q-\ell|},\qquad& \text{if } |q-\ell| \ge 1,
\\
1- \frac12 b(b-1)\lambda(1)^2,\qquad&\text{if }q=\ell=1,
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
holds for all $\boldsymbol\lambda\in\Sigma_0$ and all $q,\ell\ge1$ provided that $\epsilon:=\sqrt{b\theta-1}\in(0,\epsilon_0)$. Here the implicit constants in~$O(\epsilon^2)$ terms do not depend on~$q$ and~$\ell$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2607.27082, '2607.27082'] Let \(X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}\) be either
\begin{itemize}
    \item a Brownian motion on \(\mathbb{R}\) with variance parameter \(\sigma^2>0\), or
    \item a symmetric strictly \(\alpha\)-stable Lévy process on \(\mathbb{R}\), with
    \(1<\alpha<2\), whose Lévy measure is given by \eqref{Levygene}.
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(t_1\in(0,1)\) and \(C>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
  \PP(\tau_1^+(X)\le t)\le Ct
  \qquad\text{for all }t\in(0,t_1].
\end{equation}
Moreover, the distribution function
\[
  F(t):=\PP(\tau_1^+(X)\le t),\qquad t>0,
\]
is continuous on \((0,\infty)\).

body: [Definition Goods of arXiv:2505.11721, 'Variational principles for Hausdorff and packing dimensions of fractal percolation on self'] According to [ref5], say that the attractor $K$ of the IFS $\{f_i\}_{i\in\mathcal I}$ is a \textit{good} sponge if, for each $p\in P_{\mathcal{I}}$ and $x\in\mathbb R_+$,  setting $D=D(p,x)=\{1\le k\le d: \chi_k(p)\le x\}$, for all $i,j\in \mathcal I$, either $f_i$ and $f_j$ overlap exactly on $\mathbb R^D$, that is $\pi^D\circ {f_i}_{|[0,1]^d}= \pi^D \circ  {f_j}_{|[0,1]^d}$, or $\pi^D\circ {f_i}((0,1)^d)\cap \pi^D\circ  {f_j}((0,1)^d)=\emptyset$.

There is a constant $C_n<\infty$ such that for every $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)\cap H^1(\mathbb R^n)$, $\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^n)}^{1+\frac2n}\le C_n\,\|f\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^n)}^{\frac2n}\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^n)}.$ Both hypotheses are needed: the inequality interpolates the $L^2$ norm between the $L^1$ mass and the Dirichlet energy. It is the standard route from the energy identity to on-diagonal heat kernel bounds: if $u$ solves $\partial_tu=\mathrm{div}(A\nabla u)$ with $A$ measurable and uniformly parabolic and $u(0)=g\in L^1\cap L^2$, then $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C(n,\lambda)t^{-n/2}\|g\|_{L^1}$, i.e. the kernel obeys $\Gamma(x,t;y,s)\le C(t-s)^{-n/2}$.

body:
[Defn 1 of arXiv:2609.03512, ''] Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$, and let $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ be a vector of positive integers. The \emph{blow-up} $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by replacing each vertex $v_i$ with an independent set
\[
V_i = \{v_i^1,\ldots,v_i^{m_i}\}
\]
of $m_i$ vertices, and joining $v_i^s$ to $v_j^t$ if and only if $v_iv_j\in E(G)$. We call $V_i$ the \emph{part of $G\bigodot m$ corresponding to $v_i$}, and say that $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplication of vertices} (Golumbic \cite{Graph-multiplication-Golumbic}, p.~53).

If $m_j=1$ for all $j\ne i$, we say $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplying the single vertex $v_i$}; if moreover $m_i=2$, this is called \emph{duplicating} $v_i$ (Henning and Southey \cite{Henning-Michael}). If $G$ has a vertex of degree $2$, \emph{degree-$2$ vertex duplication} denotes the operation of duplicating any such vertex.

For graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_k$, we write $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$ for the family of all graphs obtainable from some $G_\ell$ by multiplication of vertices. Since $G\bigodot(1,\ldots,1)=G$, each $G_\ell$ itself belongs to $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$.

\[     \theta_\mu(T) \le (m^+  (d-\alpha^-)_+ + \delta) \log T\, \text{\textup{Cap}}_f(B(T + T^\delta ) )  , \]
where $(x)_+ = \max\{0,x\}$. Moreover if $\mu$ is regular in the sense of (equation e:rss of the paper), then for every $\delta > 0$ there exists an $\varepsilon > 0$ such that, as $T \to \infty$, eventually

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2506.13571, '2506.13571'] Let $K$ be a real separable Hilbert space. We say $X$ is a Gaussian random variable on $K$ if 
$\langle X, k \rangle_K$ is Gaussian for any $k\in K$.
We say $X$ is centered,
 if $\langle X, k \rangle_K$ is centered for any $k\in K$.
We say $X$ is non-degenerate, 
if $\langle X, k \rangle_K$ is not a constant for any  nonzero $k\in K$.\footnote{In other words, a constant is viewed 
as a degenerate Gaussian random variable (with zero variance).  
When the dimension of $K$ is finite, the non-degeneracy is equivalent to that the finite-dimensional
Gaussian vector has a non-singular covariance matrix.}

a short Weierstrass model
\[
 W_1: \ Y^2=X^3+A(\u)X+B(\u),
\]
where
\begin{align*}
A={}&-27(\u^2-\u+1)
(\u^6+229\u^5+270\u^4-1695\u^3
 +1430\u^2-235\u+1),\\
B={}&54(\u^{12}-522\u^{11}-8955\u^{10}

&\qquad-253239\u^6+316290\u^5
-218058\u^4+80090\u^3-14631\u^2+510\u+1),

and also to the model
\begin{multline}
W_2: \ 
 y^2-(\u^2-\u-1)xy

=x^3-\u^2(\u-1)x^2-5\u(\u-1)(\u^2-\u+1)(\u^3+2\u^2-5\u+1)x

Its discriminant is

\end{equation}

[Prop 213201 of arXiv:2606.29143, 'Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables'] Let $A = (a_1, ..., a_m)^{'}$ and $Q = (q_1, ..., q_m)^{'}$ be two numerical vectors with $\min(a_1, ..., a_m) \geq 0, \max(a_1, ..., a_m) > 0$ and $0 = q_0 < q_1 < q_2 < ... < q_m = 1$. Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with inverse distribution function $F_X^{-1}(t)$ and $w_k$ be the weights defined by ((529108 of the paper)). Then for any positive integer $r$ it holds that  
$$E[(X_{A, Q})^r] = \sum^m_{k = 1}w_kE[X^r \,|\, F^{-1}_X(q_{k - 1}) \leq X \leq F^{-1}_X(q_k)].$$
title: Prop 213201 of arXiv:2606.29143

DRAFT: proof (unaudited), w726-T332-C4 v1. Assumptions: n>=1, 0<=c<=n, d>=1; G(n,c/n) with iid standard-Borel marks independent of edges; common measurable permutation-invariant local rule F_(t,degree)(own mark; own state and neighbor states), independent of graph size and remote structure; initial state depends only on own mark; all iterates on full graphs and induced subgraphs lie in the same fixed Borel K subset R^d of diameter D<infinity; maximum-input Lipschitz constant <=rho in (0,1), uniformly over degree, marks and layers; nu_L is the root-output law of a similarly iid-marked PGW(c) tree with the same update rules; depth can depend arbitrarily on n. Let mu_(n,L) be the empirical output measure and nu_L the PGW(c) root-output law for a local GNN with a bounded invariant state set K subset R^d of diameter D and degree-uniform maximum-input contraction rho in (0,1). For every depth L, radius r and fixed partition of K into M Borel cells of diameter at most epsilon, E W1(mu_(n,L),nu_L) <=2D rho^r+2epsilon+(3D/2)sqrt(M(1+c)^(2r+2)/n). One may take M<=(1+D sqrt(d)/epsilon)^d. With b=log(1/rho), C_d=2+(3/2)(1+sqrt(d))^(d/2) and kappa=b/[2log(1+c)+(d+2)b], sup_L E W1 <=D[2/rho+C_d(1+c)^(2/(d+2))] n^(-kappa). D=0 gives exact equality. The bound also controls expected bounded-Lipschitz distance. Independent review pending; no literature-priority claim.

body: [Lemma 28 of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] Let $K \subset \overline\BD$ be a connected compact set. Let $x \in \BD_{\BQ}$. Let $\tau$ be the first time $t$ that $\SCB_t(\SCL(x); D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ intersects $K$. Then, a.s., there exists exactly one loop $\SCL$ with $\overline{\mathop{\mathrm{int}}(\SCL)} \cap K \neq \emptyset$ such that $D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD}(\SCL(x), \SCL)= \tau$. The same holds for a ball from a non-trivial arc $\alpha \subset \partial \BD$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition prop:vanishingG11 of arXiv:2606.01937, 'Stationary fluctuations for an exclusion process with mass and energy conservation'] Assume that $(\alpha_p,\alpha_e)=(0,1)$ and $\kappa >2$. Then, we have $\mathbf{G}_{22}^2(\kappa ,\rho ,\mathcal{E} )> 0$ for any $\rho \in (0,1)$ and $\mathcal{E} \in (\rho,\kappa\rho)$. Moreover, if $0<\rho <1-\frac{2}{\kappa}$, there exists an energy value~$\mathcal{E}^\star = \mathcal{E}^\star (\kappa ,\rho )\in (\rho ,\kappa\rho )$ for which $\mathbf{G}_{11}^1(\kappa ,\rho ,\mathcal{E}^\star )=0$.

[Lem 6 of arXiv:2608.01860, 'A Variational Characterization of a Gibbs Measure related to the Aviles-Giga Functional'] The following processes are martingales with respect to the natural filtration of $X$ and the Wiener measure $\mathbb{P}$: 
   \begin{align*}
    [\![\nabla Y_T^4]\!]\coloneq&(\nabla Y_T)^4- 6\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_1Y\rangle_T(\partial_1Y_T)^2-6\langle\partial_2Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T(\partial_2Y_T)^2-2\langle\partial_2Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T(\partial_1Y_T)^2\\
    &-2\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_1Y\rangle_T(\partial_2Y_T)^2-4\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T^2+3\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_1Y\rangle_T^2+3\langle\partial_2Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T^2\\
    &+2\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_1Y\rangle_T\langle\partial_2Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T\\
    &-8 \int_0^T\int_0^s \partial_1 Y_u\ d(\partial_2 Y_u) \ d\langle\partial_1 Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_s -8 \int_0^T\int_0^s \partial_2 Y_u\ d(\partial_1 Y_u) \ d\langle\partial_1 Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_s\\
    &-8 \int_0^T\int_0^s \partial_1 Y_u\ d\langle\partial_2 Y,\partial_2 Y\rangle_u\ d(\partial_1Y_s)-8 \int_0^T\int_0^s \langle\partial_2 Y,\partial_2 Y\rangle_u\ d(\partial_1 Y_u)\ d(\partial_1Y_s)\\
    &-8 \int_0^T\int_0^s \partial_2 Y_u\ d\langle\partial_1 Y,\partial_1 Y\rangle_u\ d(\partial_2Y_s)-8 \int_0^T\int_0^s \langle\partial_1 Y,\partial_1 Y\rangle_u\ d(\partial_2 Y_u)\ d(\partial_2Y_s),
    \\
    [\![\nabla Y_T^3]\!]\coloneq&(\nabla Y_T)^3-\begin{pmatrix}
        3\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_1Y\rangle_T\partial_1Y_T+2\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T\partial_2Y_T+\langle\partial_2Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T\partial_1Y_T\\ 
        3\langle\partial_2Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T\partial_2Y_T+2\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_2Y\rangle_T\partial_1Y_T+\langle\partial_1Y,\partial_1Y\rangle_T\partial_2Y_T

[Definition 30 (Decision tree, stopping time {\cite[Definition~2.4) of arXiv:2605.30030, 'Critical exponents for planar random-cluster model with cluster-weight~$q=4$'] {duminil2022planar}}]
    A \emph{decision tree} is a pair~$\mathbf{T} = (e_1, (\psi_t)_{2\leq t\leq n})$ where~$e_1\in E$ and for each~$2\leq t\leq n$, the input of~$\psi_t$ is~$(e_{[t-1]},U_{[t-1]})$ and it returns~$e_t\in E\setminus\{e_1,\dots,e_{t-1}\}$. A \emph{stopping time} for~$\mathbf{T}$ is a random variable~$\tau$ taking values in~$\{1,\dots,n,\infty\}$, for which each~$\{\tau\leq t\}$ is measurable in terms of~$(e_{[t]}, U_{[t]})$.

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For a graph $X$, with adjacency matrix $d\in M_N(0,1)$, we have:
$$(d^k)_{ij}=\#\Big\{i=i_0-i_1-\ldots-i_{k-1}-i_k=j\Big\}$$
That is, the $k$-th power of $d$ describes the length $k$ paths on $X$.
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[Proposition prop:catcher-cluster of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For every \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\), every sequence \(\delta_n\downarrow0\)
has a subsequence along which the cell trace of the random-walk loop-catcher
converges in distribution for the Hausdorff metric to a random continuum
\(K_\lambda^{D;a,b}\subset\overline{D}\) with
\(K_\lambda^{D;a,b}\cap\partial D=\{a,b\}\), whose law satisfies (equation eq:intro-main-id of the paper) for every compact obstacle away
from \(a,b\).  Consequently the existence part of
Theorem~(thm:main of the paper) holds.

[Definition def:vee of arXiv:2412.04589, 'Inverting the Markovian projection for pure jump processes'] Let $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ and $(\mathcal{F}^i)_{i \in I}$ be $\sigma$-algebras on some space. Let $\mathbb{F} = (\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \geq 0}$, $\mathbb{G} = (\mathcal{G}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\mathbb{F}^i = (\mathcal{F}^i_t)_{t \geq 0})_{i \in I}$ be filtrations on the same space. We denote
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), nosep]
		\item $\mathcal{F} \vee \mathcal{G} \coloneqq \sigma(\mathcal{F} \cup \mathcal{G})$ and $\bigvee_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}^i \coloneqq \sigma(\bigcup_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}^i)$,
		
		\item $\mathbb{F} \lor \mathbb{G} \coloneqq (\mathcal{F}_t \lor \mathcal{G}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $\bigvee_{i \in I} \mathbb{F}^i \coloneqq (\bigvee_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}^i_t)_{t \geq 0}$,
		
		\item $\mathbb{F} \vee \mathcal{G} \coloneqq (\mathcal{F}_t \lor \mathcal{G})_{t \geq 0}$. 
	\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:vee of arXiv:2412.04589

[Lemma 37 of arXiv:2608.18688, 'Regularity Preservation for Jump-Type Stochastic Transport Equations with Singular Drift'] Assume that $H(\omega,\cdot)\in L_{loc}^p(\mR^d)$ for $P$-a.e. $\omega$ and there exists a sequence $\{H_n\}_{n\in\mN}$ of random fields such that 
	
	(1) $H_n(\omega,\cdot)\to H(\omega,\cdot)$ in distributions in probability, namely
	\ce 
	P-\lim_{n\to\infty}\int H_n(\omega,x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int H(\omega,x)\varphi(x)\,dx.
	\de 
	
	(2) $\{H_n\}_{n\in\mN}\in W_{loc}^{1,p}$  for $P$-a.e. $\omega$ and for every $R>0$ there exists a constant $C_R>0$ such that 
	\ce 
	E\left[\int_{B_R}|\nabla H_n(x)|^p\,dx\right]\leq C_R
	\de 
	uniformly in $n$.
	
	Then $\{H\}_{n\in\mN}\in W_{loc}^{1,p}$  for $P$-a.e,
	\ce 
		E\left[\int_{B_R}\partial_{x_i} H_n(x)\varphi(x)Z\,dx\right]=E\left[\int_{B_R}\partial_{x_i} H(x)\varphi(x)Z\,dx\right]
	\de 
	for all $\varphi\in C_0^{\infty}(\mR^d)$ and bounded r.v. $Z$,
		\ce 
P-\lim_{n\to\infty}\int\partial_{x_i} H_n(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=-\int H(x)\partial_{x_i}\varphi(x)\,dx
	\de 
		for all $\varphi\in C_0^{\infty}(\mR^d)$ and for every $R>0$
	\ce 
	E\left[\int_{B_R}|\nabla H(x)|^p\,dx\right]\leq \limsup_{n\to\infty}	E\left[\int_{B_R}|\nabla H_n(x)|^p\,dx\right].
	\de (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 37 of arXiv:2608.18688

body: [Corollary 6 (Law of Robustness for Discontinuous Functions) of arXiv:2603.02806, 'The Price of Robustness: Stable Classifiers Need Overparame'] Let n iid observations come from a law on a bounded path-connected input space X in dimension d, with c-isoperimetric input marginal. Let F be a finite class of classifiers X -> {-1,1}, with every positive-class preimage closed, and log|F|>=n. For epsilon,delta in (0,1), let R_*=min_{f in F} R_0-1(f). There is a universal K>0 such that if R_*>=epsilon, K/sqrt(n)<epsilon/3, and sqrt(2log(2/delta)/n)<epsilon/2, then with probability at least 1-delta, simultaneously for every f in F, empirical R_0-1(f)<=R_*-epsilon implies S(f)<max{(3K/epsilon)sqrt(c log|F|/(nd)), sqrt((8c/d)log(6K/epsilon))}.

     \widehat  \nu_h (u) = e^{h\varphi (u)}, \ee

   \be | \partial ^{\alpha }\varphi_2 (u) |
    \leq A_{\alpha } (|u|^2 +1).
  \ee

    Let $M = P_f(M', M'')$ be a parallel connection.
    If $M'$ and $M''$ have G-quadratic (reduced) 
    Orlik--Solomon algebras then so does $M$.
    In particular, if $M$ and $N$ are supersolvable matroids, then for any $f\in M$, $g\in N$, both $\rOS(P_{f,g}(M, N))$ and $\OS(P_{f,g}(M, N))$ are G-quadratic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Further,

body:
[Thm FirstPresentation of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ \mathcal{Q} $ be an acyclic quiver with $ N $ vertices such that the vertices $ 1, \ldots, n $ are mutable 
	and $ n+1, \ldots, N $ are frozen.  
	Let $ K $ be a field
	and let $ \boldsymbol{x} = (x_1, \ldots, x_N ) $ be an $ N $-tuple of elements that are algebraically independent over $ K $.
	The cluster algebra $ \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{Q}) \subset K(\boldsymbol{x}) =  K(x_1, \ldots, x_n, \ldots, x_N) $ (defined over $ K $) corresponding to $ \mathcal{Q} $ is isomorphic to
	
	\begin{equation}
		 
		K[x_{n+1}^{\pm 1}, \ldots, x_{N}^{\pm 1}][x_1, \ldots, x_n, x_1', \ldots, x_n']
		/ \langle x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \} \rangle 
	\end{equation}
	where $ (x_1', \ldots, x_n') $ is another tuple of algebraically independent elements over $ K $, 
	the products range over those vertices $ i $ of $ \mathcal{Q} $ for which there is an arrow $ i \rightarrow k $ (resp.~$ i \leftarrow k $),
	and
	$ b_{ik} \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} $ is the number of arrows $ i \rightarrow k $ which is negative if there are arrows $ i \leftarrow k $. 
	\\
	Moreover, 
	$ (x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \}) $ 
	is a Gr\"obner basis for the ideal which it generates with respect to any term order
	giving preference to $ x_1', \ldots, x_n' $ over $ \boldsymbol{x} $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:CGO-PhS_int-by-parts of arXiv:2609.00257, 'Stability estimates for the initial-to-final-state inverse problem'] [zbMATH07801151]\sl 
Consider $F \in L^2(\Sigma)$ such that 
there exists $c > 0$ so that $e^{c|\mathrm{x}|} F \in L^2(\Sigma)$.
Let $u \in C([0,T]; L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ satisfy the conditions

\[
\left\{

		\begin{aligned}
		& (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u = F & & \textnormal{in} \enspace \Sigma, \\
		& u(0, \centerdot) = u(T, \centerdot) = 0 &  & \textnormal{in} \enspace \mathbb{R}^n.
		\end{aligned}

	\right.
\]

For every $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$,
consider a measurable function 
$v^\nu : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ such that

\[ \sup_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} \big[ 2^{-|\alpha|/2} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} \big] + \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} 2^{|\alpha| \theta} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} < \infty, \]
for some $\theta \in (0, 1/2)$. Then,

\[\int_\Sigma (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u \overline{v^\nu} = \int_\Sigma u \overline{(i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta)v^\nu} \, \]
for all $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:CGO-PhS_int-by-parts of arXiv:2609.00257

body:
[Theorem thm:cheeger-M of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] Let $A\subset S$ with $\pi(A)\le 1/2$ be a set achieving the Cheeger
constant~$h_P$, and assume $h_P \le 1 - \pi(A)$ (at equality the bound
below has zero numerator; see Remark~(rmk:cheeger-balanced of the paper)).
Then there exists $x^*\in A$ with $P(x^*,A)\ge 1-h_P$, and
\[
  M
  \;\ge\;
  r(x^*)
  \;\ge\;
  \frac{(1-h_P)\log\dfrac{1-h_P}{\pi(A)}
  +h_P\log\dfrac{h_P}{1-\pi(A)}}{\log\!\bigl(1/\pi(x^*)\bigr)}.
\]
The term involving $h_P$ is interpreted by continuity as $0$ when $h_P=0$.
In particular, for small $h_P$,
$M \gtrsim \log(1/\pi(A))/\log(1/\pi_{\min})$.

[Prop prop-min-harmonic of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Let $\mathcal G$ be as in Section~(sec-overview of the paper). 
Let $\mathcal A\subset \mathcal V\mathcal G$ be a non-empty finite set of vertices. 
For each $\phi : \mathcal A \to \mathbbm R$, there exists a unique function $h^\phi : \mathcal V\mathcal G\to \mathbbm R$ such that $h^\phi |_{\mathcal A} = \phi$ and $\operatorname{Energy}(h^\phi)$ is minimal among all functions $f : \mathcal V\mathcal G\to\mathbbm R$ with $f|_{\mathcal A} = \phi$. This function $h^\phi$ is discrete harmonic on $\mathcal V\mathcal G\setminus \mathcal A$ and has finite Dirichlet energy. 
Furthermore, the mapping $\phi \mapsto h^\phi$ is linear. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm_lip of arXiv:2510.00214, 'On the local well-posedness of randomly forced reaction-diffusion equations with $\bm{L^2}'] If $A>1$ satisfies
	\begin{equation}
		L_bK_b^{-1}\log(8AK_b)<1,
	\end{equation} 
	then there exists a predictable random field
	$u=\{u(t\,,x)\}_{(t,x)\in \mathscr{D}(\infty)}$ that is a mild solution to (equation SHE of the paper)
	and satisfies the following sub-Gaussian moment bound:
	\[
		\E\left( |u(t\,,x)|^k\right)
		\le (2A/t)^{k/4}\left( \|u_0\|_{L^2[0,1]} +  
		\sqrt{k} \right)^k \mathrm{e}^{4AK_b k t},
	\]

[Corollary cor:accelerated-rigidity-restated of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] Under the Chebyshev-accelerated iteration with degree-$m$ polynomial $Q_m^\ast$ (as in (thm:variational of the paper)), the rigidity time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\text{cheb}}(\delta) \;\le\; \frac{1}{m} \cdot \frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2 \log(1 / |Q_m^\ast(\lambda_3)|)},
\]
where $|Q_m^\ast(\lambda_3)| \sim (1 - \sqrt{1-\lambda_2^2}/\lambda_2)^m$ for large $m$. Optimizing over $m$ yields the $\sqrt{\kappa}$ speedup over the basic power iteration.

[Thm 14 of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] \cite{nsz}.
    Let  $\phi _i : G_i \to G$ be a sequence of good approximations with regular neighborhoods $A_i \subset G_i$ and $A \subset G$. If $G$ is a Lie group, then there is a sequence of subgroups $H_i  \leq G_i $ such that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item The sequence $H_i$ is small.
        \item $H_i \trianglelefteq \langle A_i \rangle $ for $i$ large enough.
        \item For any sequence $H_i ' \leq G_i$ of small subgroups, one has $H_i ' \leq H_i$ for $i$ large enough. 
        \item $G_i ' : = \langle A_i \rangle / H_i$ is a Lie group for $i$ large enough.
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
