Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on
$\mathcal{X}_N$ for some $p'>p$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$ 
such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.  Then, there exists 
a constant $C = C(u_0,\ell_0)$ such that, for $\ell \geq  \ell_0$,  and 
a function $h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x)\\
& \hskip 20mm \times\Big\{
E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm  \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2}\ell^{p/2} \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times \Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^p \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1N \sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}

[Proposition 31 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Let $\{\mu_n, \mu\} \subset {\cal D}$ and let $\{A^n, A\}$ be the corresponding PCAFs.
Assume that $d_{\cal D}(\mu_n, \mu) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then the following assertions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm (1)] For any compact set $K \subset E$, there exists a subsequence $\{n_k\}$ such that the PCAFs $A^{n_k}$ converge to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to $K$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$. That is,
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} \left| \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA^{n_k}_u - \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA_u \right| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E.
$$

\item[\rm (2)] Suppose there exists a compact nest $\{F_\ell\}$ satisfying the following tail estimate:
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\ell \to \infty} \sup_{\nu \in {\cal S}_{c,00}^1} \left\{ \left( \sup_n \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu_n \right) \vee \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu \right\} = 0.
\end{equation}
Then, there exists a further subsequence $\{n'_k\}$ such that $A^{n'_k}$ converges to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$:
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} |A^{n'_k}_s - A_s| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E,
$$
where ${\cal S}_{c,00}^1 := \{ \nu \in {\cal S}_0 : \mathrm{supp}[\nu] \text{ is compact}, \nu(E) \le 1 \text{ and } \|U_1\nu\|_\infty \le 1 \}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop 4 (Exact interlacing transition densities) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $(z_{ij})_{i,j\geq1}$ be independent centered circular complex Gaussian variables with $\E\abs{z_{ij}}^2=1$. Let $((m_t,n_t))_{t=0}^H$ be an elementary up-right path of positive integer pairs. Put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 X_t&=(z_{ij})_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m_t\\1\leq j\leq n_t}},
 &p_t&=\min(m_t,n_t),\\
 q_t&=\max(m_t,n_t),
 &r_t&=q_t-p_t.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Almost surely, $X_t$ has $p_t$ distinct positive squared singular values
\[
 \lambda_1^{(t)}>\cdots>\lambda_{p_t}^{(t)}>0.
\]
For $x_1>\cdots>x_k>0$, put
\[
 \Delta_k(x)=\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq k}(x_i-x_j).
\]

For $x_1>\cdots>x_p>0$ and $y_1>\cdots>y_p>0$, define
\[
 s_p(x,y)
 =
 \ee^{-\sum_{j=1}^py_j+\sum_{i=1}^px_i}
 \frac{\Delta_p(y)}{\Delta_p(x)}
 \ind_{\{y_1>x_1>y_2>x_2>\cdots>y_p>x_p\}}.
\]
For $r\geq1$, $x_1>\cdots>x_p>0$, and $y_1>\cdots>y_{p+1}>0$, define
\[
 \begin{split}
 b_{p,r}(x,y)
 &=
 \frac1{(r-1)!}
 \ee^{-\sum_{j=1}^{p+1}y_j+\sum_{i=1}^px_i}
 \frac{\Delta_{p+1}(y)}{\Delta_p(x)}\\
 &\quad\times
 \frac{\prod_{j=1}^{p+1}y_j^{r-1}}
      {\prod_{i=1}^px_i^r}
 \ind_{\{y_1>x_1>\cdots>y_p>x_p>y_{p+1}>0\}}.
 \end{split}
\]
Conditionally on $\lambda^{(t)}=x$, the density of $\lambda^{(t+1)}$ is $s_{p_t}(x,y)$ when $p_{t+1}=p_t$, and it is $b_{p_t,r_t}(x,y)$ when $p_{t+1}=p_t+1$. In the second case $r_t\geq1$. Both functions integrate to one over their decreasing chambers. Consequently, conditionally on $\lambda^{(0)}$, the multi-time density of
\[
 (\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(H)})
\]
is the product of these transition densities.

If $(M_N)$ is nondecreasing and
\[
 \sup_N(M_{N+1}-M_N)\leq K,
\]
the path $(M_N,N)$ has the same exact product representation after refining each transition into one column addition followed by $M_{N+1}-M_N$ row additions. At most $K+1$ elementary kernels are used per sample-size transition.

[Corollary 65 (Quantitative scheme-independent convergence to the common primitive) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $Y^n$ be any sequence of total Borel raw-causal finite-variation
regularizations as in \Cref{thm:defect-energy-transfer}, and fix $q\ge2$.
For the Borel continuous-path totalization
$(\widehat J^{\mathrm c},Q^{\mathrm c})$ from
\Cref{cor:common-representative}, put
\[
 \Delta_n
 :=\|J^{Y^n}-\widehat J^{\mathrm c}\|_{\infty;\mathcal S_2}
   +\|Q^{Y^n}-Q^{\mathrm c}\|_{\infty;\mathcal S_2}.
\]
Then, for every $\delta>0$,
\begin{equation}
 c_{\Smax}(\Delta_n>\delta)
 \le
 \left[
 \frac{C(\sqrt{q\Lambda}+B\sqrt T)
       \mathfrak d_q(Y^n)}{\delta}
 \right]^q.
\end{equation}
Consequently $\mathfrak d_q(Y^n)\to0$ implies that the full sequence
$(J^{Y^n},Q^{Y^n})$ converges in upper capacity to $(\widehat J,Q)$ in the
product uniform $C([0,T];\mathcal S_2)^2$ topology.  Convergence in
$\tau_{\eta;\mathcal S_2,\mathcal S_1}$ is obtained under the separate
spatial-tail and modulus hypotheses.

body:
[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2609.03248, 'Connections between colored restricted $b$-ary and ordinary partitions'] Let $\rho\geq 1$ and $b\geq 2$ be integers. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] the numbers $\overline{C}_b^\rho(n)$ of $\rho$-color $b$-ary 
partitions of $n$ in which the multiplicity of each part with color $i$ is a
multiple of $i$ and
\item[(b)] the numbers $\overline{Y}_n$ of ordinary partitions of $n$ with
parts not exceeding $\rho$
\end{enumerate}
are connected by the recurrence relation
\begin{equation}
\overline{C}_b^\rho(bn+j)
=\sum_{k=0}^n\overline{Y}_{bk+j}\overline{C}_b^\rho(n-k) \qquad 
(j=0, 1,\ldots b-1).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 25 of arXiv:2609.03248

[Definition Linear-tilt localization scheme of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $\mu = \mu_0$ be a probability measure,  $(\mu_t)_{t \in \Z_{\ge 0}}$ be a localization process.
    A linear-tilt localization scheme is one where $\mu_t$ is  defined by
    \[ \mu_{t+1}(x) = \mu_t(x) \left( 1 + \langle x-\mean(\mu_t) , Z_t\rangle \right) \]
    where $Z_t$ is a random variable with $\E[Z_t | \mu_t] = 0$ and $\mean(\mu_t)$ denotes the mean of $\mu_t$.

[Theorem 8 (Functional central limit theorem for the empirical survival function) of arXiv:2609.00292, 'Extinction, Survival and Fluctuations for the Spatial Maki--Thompson Model on Infinite Gra'] For every $T>0$,
    define
    \[
        \mathbb{S}_{n}(t) := |B_{n}|^{1/2}\bigl(s_{n}(t)-s(t)\bigr), \qquad 0
        \le t\le T.
    \]
    Then
    \[
        \mathbb{S}_{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d}\mathbb{S}\qquad\text{in }D(
        [0,T]),
    \]
    where $D([0,T])$ is endowed with the Skorokhod $J_{1}$-topology and $\mathbb{S}=(\mathbb{S}(t))_{0\le t\le T}$ is a
    centered Gaussian process with continuous sample paths. The covariance kernel of the limiting process is
    \[
        K_S(s,t)
        :=
        \lim_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{1}{|B_n|}
        \operatorname{Cov}\bigl(S_n(s),S_n(t)\bigr),
        \qquad s,t\ge0,
    \]
    where the existence of the limit follows from the proof below. Moreover, \[\sigma_S^2(t):=K_S(t,t)>0 \text{for all} t\ge0.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Functional central limit theorem for the empirical survival function

[Lemma 11 (Kernel expansion and stretch inputs) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] With high probability, for every fixed $r$,
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{a\in V(\Kernel)}d_{\Kernel}(a)^r=O_r(N),
\end{equation}
and consequently $\sum_{z\in V(\Core)}d_{\Core}(z)^r=O_r(N_c)$ for every fixed
$r$. Let $P_{\Kernel}$ be the discrete-time simple-random-walk kernel on
$\Kernel$. The smallest nonzero eigenvalue of $I-P_{\Kernel}$, acting on
$L^2$ of the degree-stationary law, is bounded below by an absolute constant.
In particular, if $\Delta_{\Kernel}$ is the unnormalized graph Laplacian, then
\[
        f^{\mathsf T}\Delta_{\Kernel}f
        =\sum_{ab\in E(\Kernel)}(f(a)-f(b))^2
        \ge c\sum_{a\in V(\Kernel)}f(a)^2
\]
whenever $\sum_a f(a)=0$. Thus every pair of kernel vertices has
effective resistance $O(1)$.

If $L_e$ denotes the stretch of a kernel edge, then for every fixed $r$,
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{e\in E(\Kernel)}L_e^r=O_r(N\eps^{-r}).
\end{equation}
In addition, for every fixed $r$ and every kernel-measurable choice of edge
weights $q_e$, fixed after conditioning on the kernel and independent of the
stretch lengths, with $0\le q_e\le1$ and $\sum_e q_e=O(N)$,
\[
        \sum_e L_e^r q_e=O_r(N\eps^{-r})
\]
with high probability over the stretches; the same remains true after
multiplying $q_e$ by any fixed-degree polynomial in the endpoint degrees.

[Thm Ineq-Log-Sobolev-Constant of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the Ising Model'] For the Ising model given by
$$\mathbb{P}(\sigma)\varpropto\exp\left(\dfrac{\beta}{2}\langle\sigma,A\sigma\rangle\right),$$
the log-Sobolev constant $\gamma_\beta$ satisfies the inequality
$$\gamma_\beta^{-1}\le\dfrac{1}{2}+\beta\cdot\lVert A\rVert\cdot\exp\left(2\lVert A\rVert\int_0^\beta\chi_s\text{d}s\right),$$
where $\lVert A\rVert$ is the spectral radius of $A$, $\chi_s:=\sup\limits_{x\in V(G)}\sum\limits_{y\in V(G)}\mathbb{E}_s(\sigma_x\sigma_y)$ and $\mathbb{E}_s$ denotes the expected value with inverse temperature equal to $s$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 85 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We have $\cN(0,1) \in \sM^{\sideal}(\alpha,0)$.

\begin{proof}
We repeat the part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} specifying the $\sideal$ class:
	\begin{center}
	\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
	\MSRheader\\
	\hline
	\SUPERPERFECTdefn
	\end{tabular}
	\end{center}
We will exhibit controls $(q_*,b,\sigma,q,p,\zeta,\zeta^{\Ising}) \in \Adm^{\sideal}(\alpha,0)$ such that $\mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta) = \cN(0,1)$. To this end, we let
    \[
        (q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta) = (0,0,1,1,\delta_0),
    \]
    so that the process $X(t)$ defined by \eqref{e:formal.sde.main} is simply
    \[
        X(t) = \int_0^t \,dB(u) = B(t)\,,
    \]
and clearly we have 
	\[
	\mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)
	=
	\Law(X(1)) = \cN(0,1)\,.\]
    We then set $\zeta^{\Ising} = \delta_0$, and $w$ to be any progressively measurable control with $\bbE[(w_t)^2] = 1$ for all $t\in [0,1]$ such that $Y(t)$ defined in \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising} satisfies $|Y(t)| = 1$ almost surely.
    The fact that such a $w$ exists follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:Yt-process-always-is-completable} (where we set $q_0 = \gamma(1) = 0$, which makes $\tilde Y, \tilde W, \tilde w, \tilde \cF_Y$ therein degenerate). 

    The above controls clearly satisfy conditions \ref{it:1.2}, \ref{it:2.2}, \ref{it:3.5}, \ref{it:5.2}, \ref{it:6.2}, \ref{it:7.2}, and \ref{it:8.2}.
    Moreover, for the above choices of $b,\sigma$, we have $\Cost(t) = 0$, so condition~\ref{it:4.3} is satisfied.
    Thus these controls belong to $\Adm^{\sideal}(\alpha,0)$, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 37 (Timelike slice estimate) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] For any interval $[t_2,t_3]$ contained in $\Interval=[t_0,t_1]$, consider the function on~$\Sbb^1$ defined by
\be
\mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]}(x) \coloneqq \int_{[t_2,t_3]\times\{x\}\times\Tbb^2} (2T_\chi^{11} + \Ebf_0(\Pbb) + \Ebf_0(\Qbb)) \Omega \, \dVundeux , \qquad x\in\Sbb^1 ,
\ee
where $\dVundeux=|t|\,\Omega \,dt\,dy\,dz$ is the volume form induced by~$g$.
There exists a constant $C>0$ depending only on $t_0,t_1$ (but not $t_2,t_3$), the initial energy~$\mathcal E(t_0)$, volume~$\mathcal V(t_0)$, initial bounded-variation norms of $\ell,\log\Omega,\Kpar$, and minimal conformal length~$\mathcal L_{\min}$ such that
\be
\|\mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]}\|_{\BV(\Sbb^1)}
= \Var(\mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]};\Sbb^1) + \| \mathcal F_{[t_2,t_3]} \|_{L^\infty(\Sbb^1)} \leq C .
\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Timelike slice estimate

[Prop obj_0-1and1-2 of arXiv:2601.00119, 'The largest common subtree of two random trees'] Let $c>0$, $\alpha\in (0,1)\cup (1,2)$, and let $X_1,X_2,\dots$ be i.i.d.~random variables such that $\mathbf{P}(|X_1|>x)\leq c x^{-\alpha}$ for all $x>1$. \[\mathbf{P}(S_m\ge t m^{1/\alpha})\le C \exp(-t/s) .\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

        and $\del{\mathcal{G}_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$-adapted processes $Z = \deln{Z_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$, $\tilde{Z} = \deln{\tilde{Z}_t}_{t \in \sbr{0,1}}$ such that 
        \begin{itemize}
            \item $\deln{Z,B}$ and  $\deln{\tilde{Z},\tilde{B}}$ satisfy  (equation eqn:firstsde of the paper) and (equation eqn:2ndsde of the paper) respectively, and
            \item $\pi$ is the joint law of  $(Z,\tilde{Z})$: $\pi = \deln{Z,\tilde{Z}}_{\#}\mathbb{P}$.
        \end{itemize}
        In particular, the joint law of $(B,\tilde{B})$ under $\mathbb{P}$ is a bicausal Wiener coupling. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma L-Lip of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] \noindent  For each $n\geq 1$, the map $L_{n}:[0,1]^{2}
\rightarrow \lbrack 0,1]$ is uniformly Lipschitz on $[0,1]^{2}$.
Consequently, since under the standing density assumption $L_{0}\in
C([0,1]^{2})$, the full family $(L_{n})_{n\geq 0}$ is relatively compact in $
C([0,1]^{2})$ with the uniform topology.

In particular, every sequence $\{L_{n_{k}}\}_{k=0}^{\infty }$ with $
n_{k}\rightarrow \infty $ admits a subsequence, again denoted by $
\{L_{n_{k}}\}$, and a limit $L^{\ast }:[0,1]^{2}\rightarrow \lbrack 0,1]$
such that 
\begin{equation}
\sup_{(x_{1},x_{2})\in \lbrack 0,1]^{2}}\left\vert
L_{n_{k}}(x_{1},x_{2})-L^{\ast }(x_{1},x_{2})\right\vert \rightarrow 0\quad 
\text{as }k\rightarrow \infty .  
\end{equation}
Moreover, each such $L^{\ast }$ is a continuous distribution function on $
[0,1]^{2}$, and its marginals 
\begin{equation}
L_{1}^{\ast }(x)=L^{\ast }(x,1),\qquad L_{2}^{\ast }(x)=L^{\ast }(1,x)

\end{equation}
are continuous strictly increasing distribution functions on $[0,1]$.
title: Lemma L-Lip of arXiv:2507.01406

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The number of $t$ vectors in the string representation of multifurcating ranked tree shapes with $K$ internal nodes and $N$ leaves with $K_{0}(t)=k_{0}$ and $K_{1}(t)=k_{1}$ is the number $A_K(k_{0},k_{1})$ that satisfy the following recursion:
\begin{align} 
    A_K(k_{0}, k_{1}) &= A_{K-1}(k_{0}-1, k_{1}) \times (K-k_{0}-k_{1}) + \\
    &\qquad A_{K-1}(k_{0}-1, k_{1}+1)\times (k_{1}+1) + \nonumber \\
    &\qquad A_{K-1}(k_{0}, k_{1}-1)\times k_{0}.  \nonumber
    \nonumber
\end{align}
with initial values: $A_K(1,K-1)=1$, $A_K(K-1,0)=1$. If $(k_0, k_1) \notin \mathcal{K}_K$, then $A_K(k_0, k_1)=0$.
title: Proposition 7 of arXiv:2506.10856

[Theorem thm:terminal-transfer of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] Let $B_N\in\mathbb R$ and $C_N>0$.  Suppose that for every fixed $x$,
\begin{equation}
        M_N(B_N+C_Nx)\to \Lambda(x),
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda(x)\in[0,\infty)$, and
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{j=1}^N q_{N,j}(B_N+C_Nx)^2\to0.
\end{equation}
Then the Poissonized completion time $X_N$ satisfies
\[
        \mathbb P\left({\frac{X_N-B_N}{C_N}}\le x\right)\to e^{-\Lambda(x)}.
\]
If additionally
\[
        B_N\to\infty,\qquad {\frac{B_N}{C_N}}\to\infty,\qquad \sqrt{B_N}=o(C_N),
\]
then the same limit holds for the discrete completion time $T_N$.

[Cor 13 of arXiv:2609.00254, 'On the geometry and cohomology of almost abelian solvmanifolds'] Let $G_A$ be a $2n$-dimensional almost abelian Lie group with Lie algebra
    $\mathfrak{g}_A= \mathbb{R}e_0 \ltimes_A \mathfrak{h}$, where $A$ is diagonal. Then $G_A$
    admits a left-invariant generalized Calabi--Yau structure of type $k$ if and only if the diagonal
    entries of $A$, listed with multiplicity, can be reordered in one of the following forms:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item $\mathrm{spec}(A) = \{\underbrace{\lambda_1, \lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_{k}, \lambda_{k}}_{k \text{ identical pairs}}, \mu, \underbrace{\zeta_1, -\zeta_1, \dots, \zeta_{n-k-1}, -\zeta_{n-k-1}}_{n-k-1 \text{ opposite pairs}} \}$, with $k \le n-1$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k \lambda_i=0$;
        \item $\mathrm{spec}(A) = \{\underbrace{\lambda_1, \lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_{k-1}, \lambda_{k-1}}_{k-1 \text{ identical pairs}}, \mu, \underbrace{\zeta_1, -\zeta_1, \dots, \zeta_{n-k}, -\zeta_{n-k}}_{n-k \text{ opposite pairs}} \}$, with $k \ge 1$ and $\mu + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \lambda_i=0$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Primary preprint theorem, Jan Nagel, arXiv:2610.08181v1, Theorem1.4(PDFpage4). Fix an integer d>=1 and alpha in(0,1). Independently at each vertex, mark it with probability alpha and attach countably infinitely many children; an unmarked vertex has exactly d children. At an unmarked nonroot vertex give the parent weight1 and each child weight beta>0, hence parent probability1/(1+d beta) and each-child probability beta/(1+d beta); an unmarked root chooses a child uniformly. At a marked vertex the walk selects its first unvisited child. Its deterministic distance speed v_infinity(beta) exists. If alpha>1-1/(72 e d), where e is the exponential base, then v_infinity is strictly increasing on(0,infinity). With reciprocal parent bias lambda=1/beta, the corresponding speed is strictly decreasing on(0,infinity). This statement is for the specified infinite-degree fresh-child process; it supplies no monotonicity theorem at a fixed finite replacement degree N.

alpha in(0,1),alpha>1-1/(72 e d)

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2609.04069, 'Positive and Negative Square Energies of $2$-Connected Graphs'] For $n\geq3$, we have, 
$$
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
  \text{ }n & \spen(C_n) & \sneg(C_n)\\ \hline
  n\text{ even}
   & n & n\\[2mm]
  n\equiv3\pmod4
   & n-1+\sec(\pi/n) & n+1-\sec(\pi/n)\\[2mm]
  n\equiv1\pmod4
   & n+1-\sec(\pi/n) & n-1+\sec(\pi/n)
 \end{array}
$$
In particular,
$$
 \spen(C_n)\geq n
 \text{ if and only if }
 n\not\equiv1\pmod4,
 \qquad
 \sneg(C_n)\geq n
 \text{ if and only if }
 n\not\equiv3\pmod4.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:joint of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $m\ge2$, $\beta>0$, $m\beta>1$, set $\delta=m\beta/2$ and $d=m-1$, and write $\xi=\xi^{\beta,\delta}$. For $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)\in\mathbb R^d$ define
\[
H_b(t):=\mathbb E\prod_{j=1}^d|\xi(tb_j)|^\beta,
\qquad
A(b):=\sum_{j=1}^d b_j,
\qquad
B(b):=\sum_{j=1}^d b_j^2.
\]
Then, uniformly for $b$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R^d$,
\begin{equation}
H_b(t)=1-\beta tA(b)\mathbb E S_1
+\frac{t^2}{2}\left[\beta^2A(b)^2\mathbb E S_1^2-\beta B(b)\mathbb E S_2\right]+o(t^2).
\end{equation}
For real $\delta$ the zero process is reflection symmetric, hence $\mathbb E S_1=0$.

body: Let J be a small category (the index or diagram shape) and D: J -> C a functor (a diagram of shape J) into a category C. A cone over D is an object X of C together with morphisms mu_j: X -> D(j), one for each object j of J, such that for every morphism alpha: j -> j' in J, D(alpha) o mu_j = mu_{j'} (composing with D(alpha) recovers the other leg of the cone). A limit of D is a cone (L, (pi_j)) that is universal among cones over D: for every other cone (X, (mu_j)) there is a unique morphism u: X -> L in C such that pi_j o u = mu_j for every j. Dually, a cocone under D is an object Y with morphisms nu_j: D(j) -> Y such that nu_{j'} o D(alpha) = nu_j for every alpha: j -> j' in J, and a colimit is a universal such cocone (Co, (iota_j)): for every cocone (Y,(nu_j)) there is a unique morphism v: Co -> Y with v o iota_j = nu_j for every j. Products, equalizers, and pullbacks are examples of limits; coproducts, coequalizers, and pushouts are examples of colimits.

body:
[Theorem 2 (The Blocking Probability) of arXiv:2609.01559, 'Erlang Loss Model with Energy Constrained Servers'] Let
\[
\rho_Q = \frac{\lambda}{\mu}, \qquad 
\rho_C = \frac{\lambda p}{\gamma}, \qquad 
\rho = \rho_Q + \rho_C,
\]
and define
\[
Z_k = \sum_{n=0}^k \frac{\rho^n}{n!}.
\]
Then, the blocking probability is given by
\[
\mathbb{P}(Q+C = k) = \frac{\rho^k/k!}{Z_k}.
\]
\begin{proof}
We begin by computing the marginal distribution of $N = Q + C$:
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}(N=n) 
&= \sum_{q=0}^n \mathbb{P}(Q=q, C=n-q) \\
&= \frac{1}{Z_k} \sum_{q=0}^n \frac{\rho_Q^q}{q!} \frac{\rho_C^{n-q}}{(n-q)!}.
\end{align}

Using the binomial identity
\[
\sum_{q=0}^n \frac{\rho_Q^q}{q!} \frac{\rho_C^{n-q}}{(n-q)!}
= \frac{(\rho_Q + \rho_C)^n}{n!}
= \frac{\rho^n}{n!},
\]
we obtain
\[
\mathbb{P}(N=n) = \frac{\rho^n/n!}{Z_k}, \quad n=0,\dots,k.
\]
Thus, $N$ is a Poisson$(\rho)$ random variable conditioned on $N \le k$.  Finally, we set the total queue length and number of charging servers equal to $k$ and therefore we obtain 
\[
\mathbb{P}(Q+C = k)
= \mathbb{P}(N=k)
= \frac{\rho^k/k!}{Z_k}.
\]
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Blocking Probability

body:
[Lemma lem:Bernoulli-basic of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Let $(B_s)_{s\ge 0}$ be the Bernoulli numbers, defined by
\[
  \frac{z}{e^z - 1}
  = \sum_{s=0}^\infty B_s \frac{z^s}{s!},\qquad |z|<2\pi.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $B_0=1$, $B_1=-\frac12$, and $B_{2m+1}=0$ for all $m\ge 1$.
  \item For all integers $m\ge 1$,
  \[
    |B_{2m}|
    \le \frac{2(2m)!}{(2\pi)^{2m}}.
  \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Basic properties of Bernoulli numbers

[Defn 21 of arXiv:2608.13208, 'Universality in dimension $1$ of kinetically constrained lattice gases'] For an admissible flow $\phi$ we define (when
the sums converge): 
\begin{eqnarray}
\left\langle \phi,\phi\right\rangle  & = & \frac{1}{2}\mu\left[\left(\sum_{x\in\Z}\tau_{x}\phi(\eta,\eta^{-1,0})\right)^{2}\right],\\
\left\langle \phi^{1},\phi\right\rangle  & = & \frac{1}{2}\sum_{x\in\Z}\mu\left[\phi(\eta,\eta^{x-1,x})(\eta(x-1)-\eta(x))\right],
\end{eqnarray}
where $\tau_{x}$ is the translation by $x$.
title: Definition 21 of arXiv:2608.13208

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2506.18558, '2506.18558'] Suppose that Assumptions {\rm\ref{A1}} and {\rm\ref{A2}} hold.  Let $F:\RR_{+}\times \RR^n\times\RR^m\rightarrow \RR$ satisfy that for any $t\ge0$, $x_1,x_2\in \RR^n$ and $y_1,y_2\in \RR^m$,
$$
|F(t,x_1,y_1)-F(t,x_2,y_2)|\le  C(|x_1-x_2|+|y_1-y_2|).
$$
Then, for any $T>0$, there is a constant $C_T>0$ such that for any $0\le  t_0<t\le  T$ and $Z_{t_0}\in\mathscr{F}_{t_0}$ with $\EE|Z_{t_0}|^2<\infty$,
\begin{align*}
\left|\EE\left[\int^t_{t_0}\left(F(s/\varepsilon,X^{\varepsilon}_s, Y^{\varepsilon}_s) -F(s/\varepsilon,X^{\varepsilon}_s, \hat Y^{\varepsilon}_s)\right) Z_{t_0}ds\right]\right|
\le  C_{T}(1+|x|+|y|) \left(\EE|Z_{t_0}|^2\right)^{1/2}\delta^{1/2}.
\end{align*}
title: Lemma 9 of arXiv:2506.18558

body:
[Lemma lem:advancing-escape-final of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Consider the VEB setting, and let $\Psi = (g,\tau_g,j,\overline{z},\mathcal{S},\textup{advancing}) \in \ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$ be a high-level state. 
Let $S$ be the (sole) set in $\mathcal{S}$ (Definition~(def:advancing-state of the paper)).
Suppose that $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$  is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning. Conditioned on the events $\Psi(\tau_g) = \Psi$ and $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(\tau_g) = \overline{a}$, with probability at least $1-\exp(-400j/\lambda^2)$, 
the following events occur. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $(6j^{25},j^{27},2/(\xi j^3),2)$-RS-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g + j^{22} \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\mathcal{N}_S^{E_g}(t+1) \le \lambda|S|/80$.
\end{enumerate} 
Moreover, if these events do occur and $V$ is well-behaved, then the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(I)]
\item $\Psi(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(j+1)$-advancing or $(j+1)$-filling state.
\item $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_{g+1}}(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(j+1)^7$-AF-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ with $\tau_g \le t < \tau_{g+1}$,   $\mathcal{N}^E_S(t+1) \le \lambda |S|/80$. Moreover, $S$ is non-empty.
\end{enumerate}

# Absolute remainder obstruction in the Li-Nica displayed rescaling

Status: route-failure/source diagnostic, proof draft (unaudited). This is not a disproof of the intended correlation limit. It identifies what cannot follow solely from the printed absolute remainder estimate.

Source: Li-Nica arXiv:2310.12079v2, Section4.1, Eqs.(4.13), (4.15), (4.16), (4.18)-(4.20). The source defines its random big-O using bounds on all absolute moments, with constants independent of n and layer l. Its correlation recursion contains an O(n^(-3/2)) absolute remainder. The proof then sets q_l=l^2(1-rho_l).

An error R_(n,l) in rho_(l+1) contributes exactly -(l+1)^2 R_(n,l) to q_(l+1). Equivalently the normalized left side l^2 q_(l+1)/(l+1)^2 in Eq.(4.18) receives -l^2 R_(n,l). From the printed absolute bound alone, the resulting estimate is O(l^2 n^(-3/2)), not O(l^(-2) n^(-3/2)). For l proportional to n, the former is O(n^(1/2)), which is insufficient for an n-step diffusion approximation. Additional correlation-dependent remainder structure could repair this; the absolute estimate alone cannot.

This failure of implication has an exact deterministic counterexample. Take n=m^2, l=n and R_(n,l)=m^-3=n^-3/2. It satisfies every required pth absolute-moment bound with constant1. The transformed error l^2 R=m, whereas the printed l^-2 n^-3/2 scale is m^-7. Their ratio m^8 diverges. Thus no fixed big-O constant can deduce the latter from the former.

There is also a separate sign inconsistency in the displayed proof. The 1/n part of Eq.(4.16) begins with -2(1-rho_l)/n. Subtracting it in the update for 1-rho therefore produces +2q_l/n after multiplication by l^2, as Eq.(4.18) itself shows before simplification. Eq.(4.19) instead prints -2q_l/n. This observation is separate from C012's Ito comparison; both need source review by the named Claude reviewer.

The PDF first10pages independently confirm the theorem/log-SDE mismatch in Eqs.(4.7)-(4.8); the rescaling equations above were read from primary HTML. Nothing here asserts that the paper's exact, unprinted remainder lacks a stronger small-defect bound. It is the missing stronger bound, together with entrance control, that must be supplied to use this proof route rigorously. [Prop martingaledeouf of arXiv:2603.21634, 'Individual-based stochastic model with unbounded growth, birth and death rates: a tightnes'] Under the \hyperlink{gen}{general setting}, let $F \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}([0,R_{\max}] \times \mathbb{R})$ and $\varphi \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^{+} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+})$. 
\begin{itemize}
\item[$\mathrm{(i)}$] Assume that for all $t \geq 0$,
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}b(x)\bigg| F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}+\delta_{x_{0}}+\delta_{x-x_{0}}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg| \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty,$$
and
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}d(x)\bigg| F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg| \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty.$$
Then $(\mathfrak{M}_{F,\varphi,t})_{t \geq 0}$ is a $(\mathcal{F}_{t})_{t \geq 0}$-martingale.
\item[$\mathrm{(ii)}$] Suppose in addition that for all $t \geq 0$,
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}b(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}+\delta_{x_{0}}+\delta_{x-x_{0}}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty,$$
and
$$\mathbb{E}\left( \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}d(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s \right) < + \infty.$$
Then $(\mathfrak{M}_{F,\varphi,t})_{t \geq 0}$ is a square-integrable martingale, with predictable quadratic variation given for all $t \geq 0$ by
\begin{align*}
\left\langle \mathfrak{M}_{F,\varphi}  \right\rangle_{t}  := & \hspace{0.1 cm} \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}b(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}+\delta_{x_{0}}+\delta_{x-x_{0}}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s  \\
& + \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+}}}d(x)\bigg[ F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}-\delta_{x}) - F_{\varphi_{s}}(R_{s},\mu_{s}) \bigg]^{2} \mu_{s}(\mathrm{d}x) \mathrm{d}s
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
title: Prop martingaledeouf of arXiv:2603.21634

[Lemma lem:global-feasible-second of arXiv:2605.11108, 'Empirical Convergence of Even-Order Gromov--Wasserstein Functionals'] Fix $\theta\in \Theta$. Let $\mu',\nu'$ be probability measures supported on compact sets
\[
\mathcal{X}'\subset B_x,
\qquad
\mathcal{Y}'\subset B_y,
\]
and let $(\phi,\psi)$ be an optimal pair for $\operatorname{OT}_{c_\theta}(\mu',\nu')$, normalized as in
Lemma~(lem:dual-pair-bounds of the paper). Let $\overline\phi$ be the extension from
Lemma~(lem:first-potential-extension of the paper). Define
\[
\mathsf C_\theta f(y):=\inf_{x\in B_x}\bigl(c_\theta(x,y)-f(x)\bigr),
\qquad
y\in B_y,
\]
and set
\[
\widetilde\psi:=\mathsf C_\theta\overline\phi.
\]
Then:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=2em]
\item[a.] $\widetilde\psi(y)=\psi(y)$ for all $y\in \mathcal{Y}'$;
\item[b.] $(\overline\phi,\widetilde\psi)$ is dual feasible on $B_x\times B_y$, i.e.
\[
\overline\phi(x)+\widetilde\psi(y)\le c_\theta(x,y)
\qquad
\text{for all }(x,y)\in B_x\times B_y;
\] and 
\[
\operatorname{OT}_{c_\theta}(\mu',\nu')
=
\int \overline\phi\,d\mu' + \int \widetilde\psi\,d\nu'.
\]
\end{itemize}

[Lemma lem:small-power-numerical-radius of arXiv:2605.21744, 'Return Probability for the Switch--Walk--Switch Lamplighter Walk on a Regular Tree'] Let \(0<\gamma<\pi^2/2\). Then there exist constants
\[
    \varepsilon=\varepsilon(\gamma)>0,
    \qquad
    m_0=m_0(\gamma)<\infty,
\]
such that the following holds. If \(S\) is a contraction on a Hilbert space
and \(m\ge m_0\), then
\[
    \|S^m\|\le \varepsilon
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    w(S)\le 1-\frac{\gamma}{m^2},
\]
where
\[
    w(S)=\sup_{\|u\|=1}|\langle Su,u\rangle|
\]
is the numerical radius of \(S\).

body:
[Prop 24 (One-time complex Gaussian log-window tails) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let \(\gamma>0\), and let \((M_N)_{N\geq1}\) be positive integers such that
\[
\frac{M_N}{N}\longrightarrow\gamma.
\]
For each \(N\), let \(X^{(N)}\) be an \(M_N\times N\) matrix with independent centered circular complex Gaussian entries of second absolute moment one. Define
\[
Q_N=N^{-1}X^{(N)}(X^{(N)})^*,
\qquad
\lambda_1^{(N)}=\lambda_{\max}(Q_N),
\]
\[
\mu_{+,N}
=
\frac{(\sqrt{M_N}+\sqrt N)^2}{N},
\qquad
\sigma_{+,N}
=
\frac{\sqrt{M_N}+\sqrt N}{N}
(M_N^{-1/2}+N^{-1/2})^{1/3},
\]
and
\[
\chi_N^+
=
\frac{\lambda_1^{(N)}-\mu_{+,N}}{\sigma_{+,N}}.
\]
Then, for every fixed \(u>0\) and \(v>0\),
\[
\Prob\left(
\chi_N^+\geq u(\log N)^{2/3}
\right)
=
\exp\left(
-\frac43u^{3/2}\log N+o(\log N)
\right),
\]
and
\[
\Prob\left(
\chi_N^+\leq-v(\log N)^{1/3}
\right)
=
\exp\left(
-\frac1{12}v^3\log N+o(\log N)
\right)
\]
as \(N\to\infty\).

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a connected, compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $X,Y$ be independent random variables on $G$ with finite entropies. 
     There exists a continuous function (independent of $G$, $X$ and $Y$),
     $$
     f:(-\infty,0] \to [0,+\infty), \text{ such that } f(x) = 0 \text{ if and only if } x=0
     $$
     and 
        $$
        \delta_{\mathrm{EPI}} = h(X+Y)-\frac12h(X)-\frac12h(Y) \geq \max{\{f(h(X)),f(h(Y))\}}.
        $$
       

        In fact, we may take 
         \begin{align}
f(x) =
\begin{cases} 
\frac{-x^5-4x^6}{16+8x^4} & \text{if } -\frac{1}{8}\leq x\leq 0\\ 
f(-\frac{1}{8}) & \text{if } x < -\frac{1}{8}.
\end{cases}
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

d >= 2
i.i.d. edge weights tau_e >= 0
P(tau_e = 0) < p_c
E[tau_e^2 (log tau_e)_+] < infinity (the '2 + log moments' condition)
||x||_1 > 1

GENERALITY, IN THE AUTHORS' OWN WORDS: 'The proof applies equally to absolutely continuous, discrete and singular continuous distributions and mixtures thereof, and requires only 2+log moments. The main result extends work of Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm and Benaim-Rossignol.' So the field already HAS distributional generality with no transfer argument, under a moment condition strictly weaker than bounded support.
METHOD: follows Benaim-Rossignol but represents each edge weight as a push-forward of an infinite Bernoulli sequence and bounds the entropy with the Gross two-point inequality, which needs a careful analysis of the discrete derivatives plus greedy lattice animals.
TWO PAPERS, DO NOT MERGE THEM: this is Damron-Hanson-Sosoe, 'Sublinear variance in first-passage percolation for general distributions', arXiv:1306.1197, Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 163 (2015). Their OTHER paper, 'Subdiffusive concentration in first-passage percolation' (arXiv:1401.0917), is the concentration inequality, not this variance bound.
SOURCE AND WHAT WAS CHECKED WHERE: the arXiv:1306.1197v2 abstract gives d >= 2, the C||x||/log||x|| form, and the 2+log moment condition in the authors' own words. It does NOT state P(tau_e = 0) < p_c; that hypothesis was read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), theorem 'thm:DHS222', tex lines 1176-1179.
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim for the complete hypothesis set (because the percolation hypothesis came from the survey, not the abstract), with the generality and the moment condition independently confirmed against the authors' abstract.
title: Damron-Hanson-Sosoe (2015): for d >= 2, if P(tau_e = 0) < p_c and E[tau_e^2 (log tau_e)_+] < infinity, then there is C > 0 with Var T(0,x) <= C ||x||_1 / log ||x||_1 for every x with ||x||_1 > 1. This '2 + log moments' result is the best UNCONDITIONAL variance upper bound known for lattice first-passage percolation, and as of August 2026 nothing has beaten its log factor on Z^d.

[Proposition prop:int-ik-coincides of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a $\Diamond$-p model, then
  $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \iff x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ and $x \in W$.
  \begin{proof}
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall only prove the modal cases.
    We note that $\Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent by the proof of Proposition (prop:hybrid-persistency of the paper).

    ($\Box\Leftrightarrow$)
    Easily proven by the induction hypothesis.

    ($\Diamond\Rightarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then $\forall x'\, (x \leq x' \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \exists y'\, (x' \sqsubset y' \mathrel{\text{\&}} y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi))$.
    This and $x \leq x$ imply that there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$, then $y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Leftarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
    Now take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x'$,
    then by the $\Diamond$-p condition, $x' \geq x \sqsubset y$ implies that there is $y'$ such that $x' \sqsubset y' \geq y$.
    Here, $y \leq y' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by persistency,
    so $y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:int-ik-coincides of arXiv:2608.29708

[Theorem_internal theo:katz_convergence of arXiv:2507.12601, 'Multi-type logistic branching processes with selection: frequency process and genealogy fo'] {Kat91}}]
Let $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of processes of the form (equation eq:X_n-Katz of the paper) satisfying the asymptotic continuity (equation eq:katzenberger_asymptotic_cont of the paper) as well as $X_n(0) \Rightarrow X_n(0)\in\Gamma$.
Under Assumptions 1--3, the following holds true for every $V\subset\!\subset U$:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The sequence $\left(X_n^{\tau_n(V)}, Z_n^{\tau_n(V)}, \tau_n(V)\right)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is relatively compact in the natural product space ${\mathbb D([0,+\infty); \mathbb R^d)\times \mathbb{D}([0,+\infty);\mathbb R^m)\times [0,+\infty]}$.
    \item For any limit point $(X, Z,\tau)$ of the above sequence, we have that 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $(X,Z)$ is a continuous semimartingale,
        \item $X(t) \in\Gamma$ for every $t\geq 0$ a.s.,
        \item $\tau \geq \inf\{t \geq 0\;:\; X(t) \not\in \mathring{V}\}$ {a.s.},
        \item one has
        \[
        \begin{split}
            X(t) &= X(0) + \int_0^{t\wedge\tau} \partial\Phi \cdot \sigma\big( X(s)\big)\;\mathrm{d} Z(s) + \dfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j=1}^d\sum_{k,\ell=1}^m \int_0^{t\wedge\tau} \partial_{ij}\Phi \sigma^{ik}\sigma^{j\ell} \big(X(s)\big) \;\mathrm{d}[Z^k, Z^\ell](s).
        \end{split}
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 8 (Cauchy Property of the Penalized Sequence) of arXiv:2604.14893, 'Well-Posedness of Generalized Mean-Reflected McKean--Vlasov Backward Stochastic Differenti'] Under Assumptions (A1)--(A5), for a given $k\ge{}1$, there exists a constant $C_k>0$ independent of $m$ and $n$ such that for any $m,n\ge{}1$, the solution sequence $(Y^{n,k},Z^{n,k})_{n={}1}^\infty$ of the penalized equation satisfies the following estimate:
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{0\le{} t\le{} T}|Y_t^{m,k} - Y_t^{n,k}|^2\right] + \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T |Z_s^{m,k} - Z_s^{n,k}|^2\dif s\right] \le{} C_k\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right).
\]
Therefore, this sequence forms a Cauchy sequence in $S^2\times H^2$.
title: Cauchy Property of the Penalized Sequence

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2605.09706, 'A dyadic construction of a three-dimensional attractive point interaction Markov family'] Fix $T,\beta,\varepsilon>0$, $m \ge 1$, and $x\in\overline E_\varepsilon$. Let  $X^{(m)}=\{X_t^{(m)}\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be the step-function process defined in~\eqref{EqDefDyadicStepInterpolation}. The following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For every $\omega\in\Omega_\varepsilon^{\mathbb D_T}$, the path
$t\mapsto X_t^{(m)}(\omega)$ is piecewise constant on the intervals $\big[k2^{-m}T,(k+1)2^{-m}T\big)$ for $k=0,1,\dots,2^m-1$
and is c\`adl\`ag on $[0,T]$ with values in $\overline E_\varepsilon$.

\item The function $X^{(m)}_{\cdot}:\Omega_\varepsilon^{\mathbb D_T}\to D([0,T];\overline E_\varepsilon)$, defined by $X^{(m)}_{\cdot}(\omega):=\big(t\mapsto X_t^{(m)}(\omega)\big)$ for $\omega\in\Omega_\varepsilon^{\mathbb D_T}$, is $\mathcal F^{\mathbb D_T}_\varepsilon/\mathcal B(D([0,T];\overline E_\varepsilon))$-measurable.

\item For every $t\in\mathcal D_m$, we have $X_t^{(m)} = X_t$. In particular, the finite-dimensional distributions of $X^{(m)}$ at times belonging to $\mathcal D_m$ agree with those of the dyadic skeleton $\{X_t\}_{t\in\mathbb D_T}$ under $\mathbb P_x^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Defi 9 (Classical symbols) of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $m \in \mathbb{R}$. A function $p : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is a classical symbol of order $m$, and we write $p \in S_{\rm cl}^m$, if $p\in S^m$ and if for all~\(j\in \Nn\) there exists $p_{m-j}\in S^{m-j}$, homogeneous of degree $m-j$ in $\xi$, smooth for $\xi \neq 0$ such that 
\[
    p - \sum_{j=0}^N\omega(\xi)p_{m-j} \in S^{m-N-1}\quad \text{for all } N\geq 0,
\] 
where $\omega \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ vanishes in a neighborhood of $0$ and equals $1$ for $|\xi| \geq 1$. 
We write $\sigma_m(p)=p_m$ and we say that $p_m$ is the principal symbol of $p$.
title: Classical symbols

body:
[Definition graph_operations of arXiv:2608.13716, 'Graph Causal Optimal Transport \\ and Wasserstein Distances'] Let $G = (V, E)$ be a directed graph, and $A \subseteq V$. We write $G_A$ for the subgraph of $G$ given by $(A, E \cap (A\times A))$.
    
    Moreover, the graph $G^+$ is defined as the directed graph with vertex set $V \cup \left\{*\right\}$, where $*$ is some vertex label that is not already in $V$, and edge set
    $$E \cup \setdef{(i, *)}{i \in V}.$$

    When $V = \left\{1, \ldots, n\right\}$, we canonically pick the label $*$ to be $n+1$.

    Let $G_1 = (V_1, E_1)$, $G_2 = (V_2, E_2)$ be directed graphs. Through a relabelling, we may assume without loss of generality that $V_1$ and $V_2 $ are disjoint. We define their \emph{disjoint union graph} $G_1 \oplus G_2$ as the directed graph with vertex set $V_1 \cup V_2$ and edge set
    $E_1 \cup E_2$.
title: Definition graph_operations of arXiv:2608.13716

body:
[Lemma Affine invariance of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:affine_invariance}
Let $X \in_R \mathbb{R}^d$ be discrete, 
let $f_Y \in \Sym(X)$, 
let $A$ be a linear bijection on $\mathbb{R}^d$
and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^d$. 
Then $f_{AY - b} \in \Sym(AX + b)$. 

Moreover, for any fixed $c>0$, $H(AY-b) \ge cH(AX + b)$ iff $H(Y) \ge cH(X)$, 
and for $d=1$ and nonzero $a \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Var(aY-b) \ge c\Var(aX+b)$ iff $\Var(Y) \ge c\Var(X)$. 

\begin{proof}
For the first claim it is sufficient to check the symmetry equations, 
and indeed
\[ 
f_{AX+b + AY-b}(z)

= f_{X+Y}(A^{-1} z)
= f_{X+Y}(-A^{-1} z)

= f_{AX+b + AY-b}(-z). 
\]

Also, $H(AY-b) = H(Y)$ and $H(AX+b) = H(X)$. 
Finally, $\Var(aY-b)= a^2\Var(Y)$ and $\Var(aX+b) = a^2\Var(X)$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Affine invariance

[Corollary C:units of arXiv:2609.03939, 'Arithmetic probability measures'] Suppose K is regular and there exists an algebraic unit $\beta$ such that 
each element of $\mathcal O(\beta)$ either lies in $K$ or
in a bounded component of $\mathbb{C} \setminus K$ not containing 0.
Then $\mu_t:= \mu_t (0, K)$
is an arithmetic probability measure if and only if
\[
\int \log |z|\,d\mu_t(z)\geq 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\int \log |P_{\beta}(z)| \,d\mu_t(z)\geq 0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary C:units of arXiv:2609.03939

[Cor lambda'_survival of arXiv:2505.12127, 'Generalised principal eigenvalues and global survival of branching Markov processes'] The following holds.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item  We have
      \[
        \lambda'_c \le \inf_{x\in E}\liminf_{t\to\infty} \frac 1 t \log {\mathbb E}_x[N_t] \le \sup_{x\in E}\limsup_{t\to\infty} \frac 1 t \log {\mathbb E}_x[N_t] = \lambda_c''.
      \]
    \item If ${\mathbb P}_x(\ensuremath{\mathrm{glSurv}}) > 0$ for all $x\in E$, then $\lambda'_c(m) \ge 0$.
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    

    \item 
      Suppose the branching is purely local. Then,
      \[
    \text{$\lambda'_c > 1$ implies for all $x\in E: {\mathbb P}_x(\ensuremath{\mathrm{glSurv}})>0$ and }\forall \lambda<\lambda'_c:{\mathbb P}_x\left(\liminf_{t\to\infty} \frac 1 t \log N_t \ge \lambda\right) > 0.
  \]
  Moreover, we have $\lambda'_c = \frac 1 t \log \rho'_{c,x}(P_t)$ for every $t>0$ and every $x\in E$.
    \item We have for every $x\in E$,
      \[
        {\mathbb P}_x\left(\limsup_{t\to\infty} \frac 1 t \log N_t \le \lambda''_c\right) = 1.
      \]
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let r and s be probability mass functions on a finite set with total variation distance c = (1/2) sum_x |r_x - s_x|, let alpha, beta >= 0, M = max(alpha, beta), m = min(alpha, beta) and delta = M - m. Then D = (1/2) sum_x |alpha r_x - beta s_x| satisfies max(delta/2, M c - delta/2) <= D <= delta/2 + m c. Both bounds are attained for every alpha, beta >= 0 and c in [0, 1]. Writing alpha = M, beta = m: the upper bound by r = (1 - c, c, 0), s = (1 - c, 0, c); when m > 0, the lower bound by r = (1 - c, c), s = (1, 0) if M c <= delta, and by r = (1 - c, c, 0), s = (k, 0, 1 - k) with k = M(1 - c)/m if M c >= delta. If m = 0 then D = M/2 for all r, s.

body:
[Lemma lem:ricci-internal-hard of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a complete squared-shell child through its monomer--dimer,
coefficient-pairing, ribbon, status, incidence, and Haar-residual data,
except that the complete reflection/status orbit and the complete
weak-order, equality, and finite-gap sum are retained inside the residual
component $\mathcal C_R$ containing the selected aggregate-Ricci root
$R$.  Suppose $\mathcal P_R=\varnothing$ and, after equal-time fusion,
$\mathcal C_R$ contains at least one independently token-bearing hard
resource: either a nonsingleton packet child for which the one-token
presentation has already proved a numerical factor
$\delta_P\le N^{-1}$, or a time-indexed linear Jacobi child
$-2N^{-1}W_i$.  An unsplit mixed/full-centered hard block with only unit
or $n^{-1/2}$ relative cost is not included.  A resolved fixed-column
child whose complete closed coefficient scalar has a proved factor
$\delta_P\le N^{-1}$ relative to the bare Euler carrier is included.
Nor is a resource in a different Haar-separated component.

Let $f_R\in\{1,2\}$ be the number of fundamental $p\vee r$ circuits hit
by the four Ricci legs, let
\[
 \mathfrak e_R=\frac Cn\|B\|_F\|B'\|_F,
\]
and let $\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}$ be the remaining positive,
once-normalized circuit-anchored terminal majorant.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{\text{weak orders, equality blocks, finite gaps,}\\
                  \text{and typed states inside }\mathcal C_R}}
 |\operatorname{Contr}_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}|
 \le A_L^{r_R}(r_R+1)^B
      \mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}\mathfrak e_RN^{-1}.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12m}$}
\]
Consequently the complete packetless subfiber in which the Ricci
component has such a resource satisfies the shell bound on the right of
(eq:3.3.1w-12k of the paper).

[Lemma S-cocompleteness-repr of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] A $T$-$\infty$-category $\mathcal C$ is $S$-cocomplete if and only if the following three conditions are satisfied: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item The $T$-$\infty$-category $\mathcal C$ is fiberwise cocomplete. 
\item For every morphism $s\colon A\to B\in S$, the restriction $s^*\colon\mathcal C(B)\to \mathcal C(A)$ admits a left adjoint $s_{!}$. 
\item For any pullback
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            X\arrow[d,"s'"']\arrow[dr,pullback]\arrow[r,"f'"] & A\arrow[d,"s"]\\
            C\arrow[r,"f"'] & B
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    in $\PSh(T)$ with $s$ in $S$ and $C\in T$, the restriction along $s'$ admits a left adjoint $s'_!$, and the Beck-Chevalley map $s'_!f'^*\to f^*s_!$ is an equivalence. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:first-order-score of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(A>0\) and assume (ass:standing of the paper) with \(r\geqslant r_0\) (the value of \(r_0\) is
  specified below for each expansion). Then there exists \(\sigma_0 > 0\) such that, for every
  \((y,\sigma)\in\mathcal Y_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\), \(x=\pi(y)\), \(a = a(y,\sigma)\), it
  holds that
  \begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{s}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-1}\big(\mathsf S_0(a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma\mathscr R_{0,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=2 \\
    \mathbf{H}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big( \mathsf H_0(a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma\mathscr R_{0, \mathbf{H}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=3 \\
    \dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big(\dot{\mathsf S}_0 (a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma \mathscr R_{0,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=3.
  \end{align*}
  Here, the coefficients \(\mathsf S_0\), \(\mathsf H_0\) and \(\dot{\mathsf S}_0\) are explicitly
  given by the formulas below and have all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-r_0+1\) in the
  variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\), uniformly bounded for \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\|
  \leqslant A\), and \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\):
  \begin{align*}
    \mathsf S_0 (a,x,\sigma) &= \mathbf J_\nu^\top (a,x,\sigma)\nabla_a \mathsf L_0(a,x), \\
    \mathsf H_0 (a,x,\sigma) &= \mathbf J_\nu^\top(a,x,\sigma)
    \mathrm{D}_a^2 \mathsf L_0(a,x) \,\mathbf J_\nu(a,x,\sigma), \\
    \dot{\mathsf S}_0(a,x,\sigma) &= -\mathsf S_0 (a,x, \sigma)
    - (\mathrm{D}_a\mathsf S_0(a,x,\sigma))[a].
  \end{align*}
  The functions \(\mathscr R_{0,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}\), \(\mathscr R_{0,\mathbf{H}_\sigma}\) and \(\mathscr R_{0,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}\) have
  all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-r_0\) in the variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\),
  uniformly bounded for \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\| \leqslant A\), and
  \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\). Derivatives in \(x\) are computed in the stratum coordinate
  \(\theta\), after writing \(x=\Phi(\theta,0)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): After Theorem 1 each row is h_a(x) = q_a(x_C) + lambda_a*x_j for at most one j outside C (tag 19). Call j conditionally free if for SOME realized core value X_C = c both signs of X_j occur among points of S having that same core value. If a row uses a conditionally free j, evaluating on two such points gives q_a(c)+lambda_a and q_a(c)-lambda_a both in {+-1}; since lambda_a is nonzero these are the two distinct signs, so q_a(c) = 0 and lambda_a = +-1 (tag 20). body:
[Lemm l:cond-var-comparison of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $X$ be a random variable such that $\mathbb{P}(|X|>m) \leqslant Ce^{-cm^{3/2}}$ for some $C,c>0$ and all $m\geqslant0$.
    Let $Y,Z$ be random $d$-dimensional vectors on the same probability space as $X$, for some $d\geqslant 1$.
    We have
    \begin{align*}
        \Bigl|
            \mathbb{E}[\Var(X|Y)] - \mathbb{E}[\Var(X|Z)]
        \Bigr|
        \leqslant C'\,\mathbb{P}(Y\ne Z)^{0.9}
    \end{align*} 
    for some $C'>0$ depending only on $C,c$.
    (The exponent $0.9$ can be replaced with any $\kappa<1$.) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary cor:accelerated-rigidity of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] Under the Chebyshev-accelerated scheme $Q_m^\ast$, the rigidity time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\mathrm{cheb}}(\delta) \le \frac{1}{m} \cdot \frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2 \log(1/\epsilon_m)} + 1, \qquad
\epsilon_m := \frac{1}{|T_m(1/\lambda_2)|}.
\]
For large $m$, $\epsilon_m \sim (1 - \sqrt{1-\lambda_2^2}/\lambda_2)^m$, yielding
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\mathrm{cheb}}(\delta) \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2(1-\lambda_2)}} = O\Bigl( \sqrt{T_{\mathrm{rigid}}(\delta)} \Bigr),
\]
a square-root speedup over the basic power iteration.

[Theorem t:IntroGirsanov2 of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] In the setting of Assumptions~(ass:IntroSetting of the paper) and~(ass:QPPIntro of the paper), suppose further that~$\mssW$ is a diffusion with generator~$\mssL$.
Assume~$0<\phi^2<\infty$ is in the domain of the Dirichlet form of the measure representation~$\mu_\bullet$, i.e.\ of the solution to the free Dean--Kawasaki equation with singular drift~(equation eq:IntroSPDE of the paper).
Then, the Dean--Kawasaki-type equation
\begin{equation}
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu_t= \mathsf{div}(\sqrt{\mu_t}\, \xi)+\sum_{x\in \mu_t} \mssL'\delta_x \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t + \mathsf{div}\paren{\mu_t\, \mssd\frac{\delta \phi}{\delta\mu_t}(\mu_t)} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t
\end{equation}
admits a unique (analytically weak) solution~$\mu_\bullet^\phi$, which is the Girsanov transform of~$\mu_\bullet$ by weight~$\phi$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma l:time_regularity of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Fix $R,M,\mu>0$, and let $p,q\in (2,\infty)$ be such that (equation eq:condition_pq_subcritical_scaling_cutoff of the paper) holds.
For all $b\in (2,\infty)$ and $T\in (0,\infty)$, let $w_{{\rm cut}}^N$ be the unique global $(p,q)$-solution to (equation eq:navier_stokes_cutoff of the paper) provided by Lemma (l:global_cutoff of the paper) for some $u_0\in \mathcal{B}_{p,q}(M)$. 
Set 
\begin{equation}

\mathcal{M}^N(t)\stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}\sum_{k,\alpha} \theta_k^N \int_0^t (\sigma_{k,\alpha}\cdot \nabla) w_{{\rm cut}}^N\,\mathrm{d} W^{k,\alpha}_s.
\end{equation}
Then there exist constants $K_T,\kappa,\gamma_0,\gamma_1>0$ independent of $u_0\in \mathcal{B}_{p,q}(M)$ and $N\geq 1$ such that 
\begin{align}

{\mathbf E} [\|\mathcal{M}^N \|_{C^{\gamma_0}(0,T;H^{-\gamma_1})}^{b}]
&\leq K_T N^{-\kappa b} (1+\|u_0\|_{B^{1-2/p}_{q,p}}^{b}),\\

{\mathbf E} [\|w_{{\rm cut}}^N \|_{C^{\gamma_0}(0,T;H^{-\gamma_1})}^{b}]
&\leq K_T (1+\|u_0\|_{B^{1-2/p}_{q,p}}^{b}),
\end{align}
where $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ are additionally independent of $T>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniform-in-$N$ time regularity

body:
[Lemma lemma6 of arXiv:2411.11085, 'Universal constant order fluctuations for the cokernels of block triangular matrices'] Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $\mathcal{P}$ be the set of prime divisors of $|G|$. Let $\mathbf{M}$ be a $(\mathcal{P},\varepsilon)$-balanced $m\times n$ random matrix and $G_0$ be a subgroup of $G$. Furthermore, let $\mathbf{g}$ be a deterministic vector in $G^n$ such that $\langle \mathbf{g}\rangle\not\subseteq G_0$. Then for any $\mathbf{f}\in G^m$, we have
\[\mathbb{P}(\mathbf{f}+\mathbf{M}\mathbf{g}\in G_0^m)\le (1-\varepsilon)^m.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:tailrl-closed-form-weights of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] For every $i=1,\ldots,N$,
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{i}
\frac{r_{(k)}-r_{(k-1)}}{N-k+1}.

\end{equation}
Equivalently, all weights follow the recurrence
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\omega\bigl(r_{(i-1)}\bigr)
+
\frac{r_{(i)}-r_{(i-1)}}{N-i+1},
\qquad
\omega\bigl(r_{(0)}\bigr)=0.

\end{equation}
title: Closed-form empirical weights

body:
[Definition d:am-decbundle of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $\mu$   be a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the \emph{decomposability bundle} is a Borel map $T^{AM}_\mu: \mathbb{R}^n \to \Gr(\mathbb{R}^n)$ such that the following
		statements hold:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item Every Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is differentiable at $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with respect to the
			linear subspace $T_\mu^{AM}$, that is, there exists a linear function $df_x^{AM}: T^{AM}_\mu(x) \to \mathbb{R}$, such that
			\[ f(x+h) = f(x) + df_x^{AM}(h) + o(\lvert h\rvert)
			\quad \text{for } h \in T^{AM}_\mu(x). \]
			\item The previous statement is sharp:  there exists a Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$
			such that for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and every $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$ the derivative of $f$ at $x$ in the
			direction $v$ does not exist. More precisely, for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we have
			\[
			\liminf_{t \to 0} \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t} < \limsup_{t \to 0}  \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}, \quad \mbox{for all $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$}
			\]
		\end{enumerate}
title: Definition d:am-decbundle of arXiv:2510.13659

body:
[Lemma exp of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] The basis change formula expressing the elements of $({\mathbb A}^0)^\ast$ in terms of the elements of ${\mathbb A}^\ast$ in ${\mathbb R} {\langle}{\mathbb A}{\rangle}$ is obtained as
$$
	w^0=\sum_{(i_1, \ldots ,i_\ell)}\frac{1}{i_1!\cdots i_\ell!}(i_1, \ldots,\, i_\ell)\circ w.
$$
where $w^0=a_1^0\cdots a_n^0$. Here, the sum runs over all multi-indices $(i_1, \ldots , i_\ell)$ such that $i_1+ \cdots + i_\ell=|w|$ where $|w|$ denotes the length of the word $w$ and  
\begin{equation*}
	(i_1, \ldots,\, i_\ell)\circ w := 
		[ a_1,\ldots , a_{i_1}]
		[ a_{i_1+1}, \ldots , a_{i_1+i_2}]\cdots
		[ a_{i_1+\cdots+i_{\ell-1}+1}, \ldots , a_{n}]
\end{equation*}
is the concatenation of the repeated bracket product of the letters in each subword as indicated. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Consider the Bessel and free Bessel laws, depending on parameters $s\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ and $t>0$, which are the following compound Poisson/free Poisson laws,
$$b^s_t=p_{t\varepsilon_s}\quad,\quad 
\beta^s_t=\pi_{t\varepsilon_s}$$
with $\varepsilon_s$ being the uniform measure on the $s$-th roots of unity. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item At $s=1$ we recover the Poisson laws $p_t,\pi_t$.

\item At $s=2$ we recover the real Bessel laws $b_t,\beta_t$.

\item At $s=\infty$ we have the complex Bessel laws $B_t,\mathfrak B_t$.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary cor:stein of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] For \emph{any} $\theta$, not only a minimiser, define the free score discrepancy
$\mathcal S_{t}(\theta):=\tau\big[(\widehat\xi_{t}-\xi_{\mu_{t}}(X_{t}))^{2}\big]$,
the free (Fisher-divergence-type) analogue of a Stein discrepancy between the learned
and true conjugate variable at time $t$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal S_{t}(\theta)=\frac{1}{v_{t}^{2}}\Big(\mathcal L_{t}(\theta)-c_{t}\Big),
  \qquad
  \mathcal L_{t}(\theta):=\tau\Big[\big(g_{\theta}(X_{t},t)-\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}X_{0}
  \big)^{2}\Big],
\end{equation}
with $c_{t}$ as in (equation eq:bias-variance of the paper), exactly -- with no approximation and no
constant to be estimated. Consequently $\mathcal L_{t}(\theta)-c_{t}\ge0$ always, with
equality iff $\mathcal S_{t}(\theta)=0$.

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] Let $N\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a domain. Suppose that for some open set $U$,
	\[
	\partial N\cap U=\Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2,
	\]
	where $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ are smooth faces whose intersection
	$\Gamma=\Sigma_1\cap\Sigma_2$ is compact and smooth. Assume that the faces
	meet transversely along $\Gamma$ and that $N$ lies locally on their inner
	sides. With respect to the outward normals of $N$, suppose
	\[
	H_{\Sigma_1}\geq0,
	\qquad
	H_{\Sigma_2}\geq0
	\]
	near $\Gamma$. Then, for every neighborhood $V\Subset U$ of $\Gamma$,
	there exists a domain $\widetilde N$ differing from $N$ only inside $V$.
	Its boundary is smooth near $\Gamma$ and satisfies
	\[
	\widetilde N\triangle N\Subset V,
	\qquad
	\partial\widetilde N=\partial N
	\quad\text{outside }V,
	\qquad
	H_{\partial\widetilde N}\geq0
	\quad\text{on the modified part}.
	\]

body:
[Prop best of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $(M^4,g)$ be a smooth compact oriented Riemannian manifold,
let $\mathfrak c$ be a spin$^c$ structure on $M$, and let 
$c_1^+= [c_1(L)]^+$ denote the self-dual part of the harmonic $2$-form 
representing the first Chern class $c_1(L)$ of $\mathfrak c$. 
If   there is a  solution of the unperturbed Seiberg-Witten equations ((drc of the paper)--(sd of the paper)) 
on $M$ for $g$ and  ${\mathfrak c}$, then the scalar curvature 
$s$ of $g$ satisfies 
$$
\int_{M}s^{2}d\mu_{g} \geq \int_{M}s_-^{2}d\mu_{g} \geq 32\pi^{2} [c_{1}^{+}]^{2} 
$$
where $s_-:=\min (s,0)$ at each point. Moreover, when $c_1^+\neq 0$,  equality can only  occur if  $g$
is a K\"ahler metric of constant {negative} scalar curvature whose 
 complex structure $J$ induces the spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak{c}$ on $M$.

[Proposition 111 (Finite-dimensional rough/finite-variation stability) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Fix $p\in(2,3)$ and $1<\nu<p/(p-1)$.  Let $V_0$ be bounded globally
Lipschitz.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item If $V\in\operatorname{Lip}^\rho$ for some $\rho>p$, the solution map of
\[
 \dd Z=V_0(Z)\,\dd t+V(Z)\,\dd\mathbf z
\]
is locally Lipschitz on bounded geometric $p$-rough-path balls for
$d_{p\text{-var}}^{\rm hom}$.
\item If $V\in\operatorname{Lip}^{\rho+1}$ for some $\rho>p$, the solution map
of
\[
 \dd Z=V_0(Z)\,\dd t+V(Z)\,\dd\mathbf z
 -\frac12\langle\mathcal W_V(Z),\dd q\rangle_{\rm tr}
\]
is locally Lipschitz on bounded sets for
\[
 d_{p\text{-var}}^{\rm hom}(\mathbf z,\widetilde{\mathbf z})
 +\|q-\widetilde q\|_{\nu\text{-var};\mathcal S_1}.
\]
Both solution maps are causal under terminal restriction and obey the usual
subinterval-restriction and concatenation laws.  They do not commute with
stopping of $(\mathbf z,q)$ alone when $V_0\ne0$; exact stop preservation is
recovered by adjoining the finite-variation clock channel $\ell_t=t$, with
its canonical Young augmentation, and stopping $(\ell,\mathbf z,q)$
simultaneously.  More precisely,
for every driver radius $R$ and compact initial set $K\subset\R^m$, there is
$C_{R,K}$ such that solutions $Z,\widetilde Z$ starting in $K$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \|Z-\widetilde Z\|_\infty
 \le C_{R,K}\left(
 d_{p\text{-var}}^{\rm hom}(\mathbf z,\widetilde{\mathbf z})
 +\|q-\widetilde q\|_{\nu\text{-var};\mathcal S_1}
 +|Z_0-\widetilde Z_0|\right),
\end{equation}
whenever the two rough drivers and the two finite-variation drivers have
radius at most $R$.  In part~\textup{(i)}, the $q$-term is omitted.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lm:3.7.howard.newman of arXiv:2411.02046, 'Speed of Convergence and Moderate Deviations of FPP on Random Geometric Graphs'] For any~$d \ge 2$ and~$\uppsi \in (0,1/4)$, there exists~$c_\uppsi > 0$ such that the following holds. Let~$\{q_1,q_2,\ldots\}$ be a finite or infinite sequence of elements of $\mathbb R^d$ so that there exists~$k^* \in \mathbb N$ such that the following three properties hold: first,
    \[
    \|q_{i+1}-q_i\|\le \|q_i\|^{3/4} \text{ for all }i \ge k^*;
    \]
    second, 
    \[
    \|q_i\| \ge 3^{1/\uppsi} \text{ for all }i \ge k^*;
    \]
    and third,
    \[\mathrm{dist}(q_i,\overline{o q_j})\leq \|q_j\|^{1-\uppsi} \ \ \text{ for all $i,j$ with $j \ge k^*$ and ~$i \le j$}.\]
    Then, for all~$i,j$ with~$j > i \ge k^*$, we have
    \begin{equation*} 
        \uptheta(q_i,q_j) \le c_\uppsi~\|q_i\|^{-\uppsi}.
    \end{equation*}

[Theorem 5 (Finite-\(r\) annular Fourier decay on fixed arcs) of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] Let \(0<s<1\).  Let \(U\ge0\) satisfy \(\mathbb E U=1\), and assume that there
exist \(r>1\) and \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
    \mathbb E[U^r]<\infty
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    2^{1-r}\mathbb E[U^r]\le 2^{-r(s+\delta)}.
\]
Let \(\widetilde\nu\) denote the almost sure weak limit of the dyadic scalar
Mandelbrot cascade on \([0,1]\) generated by \(U\).  Let
\(\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^2\) be a fixed nondegenerate \(C^2\) embedded arc,
and set \(\nu_\gamma=\gamma_\#\widetilde\nu\).  Then there exist constants
\(C_\gamma<\infty\), \(c_\gamma>0\), and \(\eta>0\), depending only on
\(s,r,\delta\), the law of \(U\), and the fixed arc \(\gamma\), such that, for
every integer \(n\ge1\),
\[
\mathbb P
\left(
    \sup_{2^n\le|\xi|\le2^{n+1}}
    |\widehat{\nu_\gamma}(\xi)|
    >
    C_\gamma 2^{-sn/2}
\right)
\le
C_\gamma\exp(-c_\gamma2^{\eta n})
+
C_\gamma2^{-c_\gamma n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
    |\widehat{\nu_\gamma}(\xi)|
    =
    O(|\xi|^{-s/2})
    \qquad
    (|\xi|\to\infty)
\]
almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-\(r\) annular Fourier decay on fixed arcs

body: [Lemma implication-of-uniform-lipschitz of arXiv:2608.12056, 'Deviation inequalities for U-processes of growing order, with applications to half-space d'] Let $X_1, X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. copies of a random variable $X \in \mathbb R$ with absolutely continuous distribution. Assume that $\mathbb E X= 0$ and $\mathrm{var}(X) = 1$. Define $Y_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{j=1}^n X_j$, and let the density of $Y_n$ be denoted $f_n$. If $f_n$ is Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz constant $L$ uniformly for all $n \geq n_0$, then $f_n(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)$ uniformly over all $x \in \mathbb R$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$, where $\phi$ is the density of the standard normal law. Consequently, $f_n$ is also uniformly bounded.
title: Lemma implication-of-uniform-lipschitz of arXiv:2608.12056

body: In mathematics, a presentation is one method of specifying a group. A presentation of a group G comprises a set S of generators—so that every element of the group can be written as a product of powers of some of these generators—and a set R of relations among those generators. We then say G has presentation $$\langle S\mid R\rangle .$$

body: Certificate (campaign status: audited-pass): For every n >= 4 an independent set U of C_n of size ceil(n/3) exists with all cyclic gaps of length 2 or 3: n = 3k -> |U| = k, gaps 3,...,3; n = 3k+1 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,2,3,...,3; n = 3k+2 -> |U| = k+1, gaps 2,3,...,3. The residuals L_u = A+B_u = e_0+e_u are linearly independent because the e_u coordinate occurs only in L_u. With F_empty = -A, F_{i} = B_i, F_{i,i+1} = C_i one has F_{u} - F_empty = L_u and F_{u,v} - F_{v} = L_u, so every clique form is congruent mod span{L_u} to the form obtained by deleting its U-vertices. Deleting an independent U removes exactly 2|U| cycle edges. Notes: Proves feasibility in ALL THREE congruence classes mod 3, not only 3 | n. All gaps >= 2 (independence) AND <= 3 (domination) are both load-bearing -- see coverage_check_enforces_dominating_gaps.

body:
[Corollary cor:subcritical of arXiv:2608.30831, 'Sharp discrete Hardy constants in dimensions three and four\\ and strict upper bounds from'] For $N=3,4$, let $h_N$ be the supersolution in Lemma~(lem:N3 of the paper) or
Lemma~(lem:N4 of the paper), respectively, and define
\begin{equation}
 V_N(n):=\frac{(-\Delta_{\!d} h_N)(n)}{h_N(n)}-\frac{A_N}{|n|^2},
 \qquad n\in X_N.
\end{equation}
Then $V_N(n)>0$ for every $n\in X_N$, and
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_N[u]-A_N\mathcal D_N[u]
 \ge\sum_{n\in X_N}V_N(n)|u(n)|^2
\end{equation}
for every finitely supported $u$ with $u(0)=0$.
Thus the form on the left is subcritical, although $C(N)=A_N$.
In particular, $A_N|n|^{-2}$ is not a pointwise optimal Hardy weight.

[Proposition 4 (Abatangelo--Jarohs--Salda\~na) of arXiv:2609.00703, 'Ellipsoidal Positivity Sets for Fractional Obstacle Problems with Quadratic Forcing'] There exists a constant \(\kappa_{n,s}>0\) depending only on \(n\) and \(s\) such that,
for \(x\in E_B\),
\[
(-\Delta)^s\psi_B(x)
=
c_B-\langle A_Bx,x\rangle,
\]
where
\begin{equation}
c_B
=
\kappa_{n,s}
\int_{\partial E_B}\mu_{B,s}(d\theta)
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
A_B
=
\kappa_{n,s}
\left[
B\int_{\partial E_B}\mu_{B,s}(d\theta)
+
2s
\int_{\partial E_B}
(B\theta)\otimes(B\theta)\,
\mu_{B,s}(d\theta)
\right].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:crossconst of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] The deterministic cross-compensator of $V^{T,2}$ converges to
$\gamma_{12}\int_0^t L_{12}$ with $\gamma_{12}=m_1/(m_2\lambda_1)$.
The cross-martingale
\[
\mathcal C_t^T=\kappa_T^2\int_0^{Tt}\Psi_T^{12}(Tt-s)dM_s^{T,1}
\]
satisfies
\[
\mathbb{E}[(\mathcal C_t^T)^2]\to
(\gamma_{12}\nu_1)^2\int_0^t L_{12}(t-u)^2b_1(u)\,du.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\Cov(V_t^1,V_t^2)\to
\gamma_{12}\nu_1^2\int_0^t K_1L_{12}\,b_1
=\frac1{m_2\lambda_1^2}\int_0^t K_1L_{12}\,b_1 .
\]

body: A family $\Pi$ of probability measures on a metric space is tight if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a compact $K$ with $\mu(K)>1-\varepsilon$ for all $\mu\in\Pi$; by Prokhorov's theorem a tight family is relatively compact for weak convergence, and on a Polish space the converse holds.

body:
[Definition def:delta_close of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,4)$ and let $h$ be a whole-plane GFF with values modulo a global multiple of $2\pi\chi$. Let $D$ be a bounded open set containing $0$, let $\delta > 0$ and define $D_\delta = \{z \in \mathbf{C} \colon d(z, D) < \delta\}$. For $\theta \in \mathbf{R}$ let $\eta_{\theta}$ be the flow line of $h$ starting from $0$ with angle $\theta$ and for any set $A$ let $\tau_\theta(A) = \inf\{t \geq 0\colon \eta_\theta(t) \notin A\}$.
For $\theta \neq 0$, $\eta_0$ and $\eta_\theta$ are said to be \emph{$\delta$-close until $\eta_0$ exits $D$} if the following conditions hold. For all $t \in (0, \tau_0(D)]$ there exist $t_1, t_2, t'_1, t'_2$ where $0 < t_1 < t < t_2 < \tau_0(D_\delta)$ and $0 < t'_1 < t'_2 < \tau_\theta(D_\delta)$ such that for each $j = 1,2$, $\eta_0(t_j) = \eta_\theta(t'_j)$ and at this point $\eta_\theta$ hits $\eta_0$ on the \emph{left} side of $\eta_0$  (if $\theta > 0$) with angle gap $\theta$ (as defined in [ms2017ig4]). Furthermore, for any $s \in [t_1, t_2]$ and $s' \in [t'_1, t'_2]$, we have $|\eta_0(s) - \eta_\theta(s')| < \delta$. If $\theta < 0$, we replace `left side' by `right side' above.
title: Definition def:delta_close of arXiv:2411.13133

\]

body:
[Lemma lem:absolute_continuity of arXiv:2505.10256, 'Stochastic Oscillators out of equilibrium:\\ scaling limits and correlation estimates'] Assume $\kappa\ge 1$ and assume the condition in (thm:fourth-moment_bound of the paper).   
Let $Q^v_m$ (resp. $Q^e_m$) be any limiting point of the sequence $\{Q^{v,N}_m\}_{N\in\mathbb N}$ (resp. $\{Q^{e,N}_m\}_{N\in\mathbb N}$) as $N\to\infty$. 
Then, for any $t\in [0,T]$, all limiting points are concentrated on trajectories that are absolute continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure, i.e., 
\begin{equation*} 
Q^\sigma_m \Big( \pi^\sigma:
\pi^\sigma_t(du) = \sigma(t,u)du \text{ for some } \sigma(t,u) \Big) = 1
\end{equation*}
for each $\sigma\in \{v,e\}$.
title: Lemma lem:absolute_continuity of arXiv:2505.10256

body:
Let Omega be an open subset of R^n. A second-order operator in divergence form is Lu = -sum_{i,j} D_i(a^{ij}(x) D_j u) + sum_i b^i(x) D_i u + c(x) u, written Lu = -div(A grad u) + b.grad u + c u, where A = (a^{ij}) is a real n x n matrix-valued measurable function on Omega (not necessarily symmetric, not necessarily continuous) and b = (b^i), c are real measurable functions. L is uniformly elliptic with constants 0 < lambda <= Lambda if for a.e. x in Omega and all xi, eta in R^n: A(x)xi.xi >= lambda|xi|^2 and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta|; one normally also assumes b, c in L^infinity(Omega). Only the symmetric part of A enters the ellipticity condition. Sign convention: with the leading minus sign, L = -Laplacian when A = I, b = 0, c = 0, so a subsolution (Lu <= 0) generalizes a subharmonic function, and the favorable sign of the zeroth-order coefficient is c >= 0. The ratio Lambda/lambda is the ellipticity ratio; the constants in the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory depend only on n and Lambda/lambda. For u in H^1_loc the expression Lu is defined only weakly (in the sense of distributions); no differentiability of A is required.
Omega is an open subset of R^n
a^{ij}, b^i, c are real measurable functions on Omega
lambda|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi.xi and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta| for a.e. x and all xi, eta, with 0 < lambda <= Lambda
b, c in L^infinity(Omega)
title: Uniformly Elliptic Operator in Divergence Form

[Lemma lem:sq_of_PSD_matrices of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $\bm{N}_1,\bm{N}_2$ be symmetric positive semi-definite matrices. Define $\bm{N}_3\coloneqq\bm{N}_1+\bm{N}_2$ and, for $i\in\{1,3\}$, let $\bm{M}_i$ be symmetric positive semi-definite matrices satisfying $\bm{M}_i^2=\bm{N}_i$. Then $\bm{M}_3-\bm{M}_1$ is positive semi-definite and
\[
\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}\big((\bm{M}_3-\bm{M}_1)^2\big)}
\leqslant\mathrm{tr}(\bm{M}_3-\bm{M}_1).
\]

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix $\alpha$ and suppose that $\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)$ holds.
Then
\[
\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{norm}}_\alpha(x)\ge 1-\delta,
\]
and for every $\beta\neq\alpha$,
\[
\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{norm}}_\beta(x)
\le
\frac{|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|+\rho}{L_\beta}.
\]
In particular, if
\[
|S_\alpha\cap S_\beta|+\rho<(1-\delta)L_\beta,
\]
then
\[
\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{norm}}_\alpha(x)>
\mathrm{score}^{\mathrm{norm}}_\beta(x).
\]

[Proposition 1 (Deterministic score separation) of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix a target concept $\alpha$. On the event $\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)$, one has
	for every competitor $\beta\neq\alpha$,
	\begin{equation}
	H_\alpha(x)-H_\beta(x)
	\ge ((1-\delta)L-t_*^{(\alpha)})-\rho.
	\end{equation}

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2609.02175, '2609.02175'] Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary.
	We say that $M$ admits a strictly convex foliation if there exist
	$T>0$ and a smooth function
	\[
	\rho:M\longrightarrow [0,+\infty)
	\]
	such that, for every $t\in[0,T)$, the level set
	\[
	\Sigma_t=\rho^{-1}(t)
	\]
	is a strictly convex hypersurface, $d\rho\neq0$ on $\Sigma_t$,
	$\Sigma_0=\partial M$, and
	\[
	M\setminus\bigcup_{0\leq t<T}\Sigma_t
	\]
	has empty interior.

body: In differential geometry, the Ricci curvature tensor, named after Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro, measures how a curved space locally differs from flat space by tracking how nearby geodesics spread apart or converge. Formally, it is a symmetric rank-two tensor obtained by taking a trace of the Riemann curvature tensor of a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian metric. In Riemannian geometry, the Ricci curvature in a given tangent direction may be interpreted as an average of the sectional curvatures of planes containing that direction. A further trace of the Ricci curvature yields the scalar curvature.
title: Ricci curvature

[Corollary cor:polytope-tolerant-testing of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Let $r\geq1$ and let $0\leq\eps_1<\eps_2<1$.
	Put
	\[
		\Delta := \eps_2-\eps_1
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		k := \alpha(r,\Delta/4)\,.
	\]
	There is a black-box query algorithm which makes $k^{\poly(\log k,1/\Delta)} = 2^{\poly(r,1/\Delta)}$ queries to an unknown target function $f:\R^n\to\zo$, and with probability at least $9/10$ has the following guarantee:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item If $\mathrm{OPT}_r(f)\leq \eps_1$, then it outputs ``accept.''
		\item If $\mathrm{OPT}_r(f)\geq \eps_2$, then it outputs ``reject.''

body:
Fix a finite alphabet Sigma, block length n, message u, and a keyed randomized code with key K and encoder output X in Sigma^n. Suppose its decoding failure is at most a for every randomized channel C, acting on the input word alone, such that d_H(x,C(x))<=p*n almost surely for every x in Sigma^n. Let E be another randomized channel Sigma^n->Sigma^n, independent of K except through its input, and suppose P(d_H(X,E(X))>p*n)<=delta under the key, encoder and channel randomness. Then the decoding failure under E is at most a+delta. In particular robustness persists if a and delta are negligible in the security parameter. If the robustness premise is restricted to efficiently sampleable channels, also assume E and the budget comparison are polynomial-time computable; the clipping preserves that property.
Robustness to every almost-sure p-substitution-bounded channel in the relevant class.
E sees the word and its own randomness, with no additional secret-key side information.
The high-probability budget is averaged over the same key/encoder/channel experiment as the decoding guarantee.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume that conditions \textbf{(A)} and \textbf{(B)} hold. Let the tail exponent satisfy $\alpha \in (2, \frac{6}{3-2r}]$ and the sequence of inverse temperatures chosen as $\beta_N = \beta l(N^{3/2})^{-1}$. When the scaling $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$ , then the normalized fluctuation of the log-partition function converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian distribution:
$$
    \frac{1}{\beta_N N^{H/2}} \left( \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{p'} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \right)  \stackrel{D}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_H^2),
$$
where \(p'\) is any fixed integer satisfying
\[
        1\le p'<\alpha,
        \qquad\text{and}\quad
        \frac{N\beta_N^{p'+1}}{\beta_NN^{H/2}}\longrightarrow0 ~\text{as}~N\to\infty.
\]
The variance $\sigma_H^2$ is given by the integral:
$$
    \sigma_H^2 = 2H(2H-1) \int_0^1 \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \rho(t,x)\rho(t,y)|x-y|^{2H-2} \,dx \,dy \,dt.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
