[Introthm 3 (The Metropolis--Hastings algorithm) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $\XX,\XXA,\lambda,p,\pi$ be as in Theorem \ref{thm:posdens}. Let the proposal be the
Markov kernel $Q(A \mid x) = \int_{A} q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)$, given by an
$\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable map $q : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ with
$\int_{\XX} q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$ for every $x \in \XX$, and let $T$ be the
Metropolis--Hastings kernel
\[
  T(A \mid x) := \int_{A} a(y \mid x)\,q(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) + r(x)\,\ind_{A}(x),
  \qquad
  a(y \mid x) := \min\Bigl\{ 1,\ \frac{p(y)\,q(x \mid y)}{p(x)\,q(y \mid x)} \Bigr\},
\]
with $r(x)$ the resulting total rejection probability. If
\[
  q(y \mid x) > 0 \qquad\text{for every } (x,y) \in \XX\times\XX ,
\]
then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$ and
$\sup_{A \in \XXA}| (T^{n}\circ\mu)(A) - \pi(A) | \to 0$ for every initial
distribution $\mu$ on $(\XX,\XXA)$. No invariance hypothesis is needed: for the
Metropolis--Hastings kernel it is automatic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Metropolis--Hastings algorithm

body:
[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2608.13358, 'Extreme points of sets of probability measures and $\phi$-divergences'] Let $q\in\cP$, $H$ be an affine set of signed measures with finite variation, and
\[
\cM:=\{p\in\cP_q\cap H\mid p\approx q\}.
\]
Then, every extreme point of $\cM$ is an extreme point of $\cP_q\cap H$.

[Definition Weak isomorphism of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Two fibered probability measures \(\mu,\bar{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1])\) are said to be
	\emph{weakly isomorphic} if there exist two measure-preserving maps (not necessarily bijective) 
	\(\varphi,\psi \in \bar{S}_{[0,1]}\) such that \(\mu^{\varphi}=\bar{\mu}^{\psi}\).
title: Weak isomorphism

[Definition Cover of arXiv:2608.22044, 'Structured Learning on Mapper Representations'] Let $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^d$.
A collection of sets
\[
\mathcal{U}=\{U_1,\dots,U_K\}
\]
is a \emph{cover} of $Y$ if $
Y\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{K}U_k$.

[Cor identify-finite of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] Let $M_1, M_2$ be compact Riemannian manifolds that are not isometric, with metrics $d_1$ and $d_2$. 
    Then after possibly switching the roles of $M_1$ and $M_2$, there is some finite collection of points $x_1,\ldots,x_K \in M_1$ along with a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$ so that for all  $y_1,\ldots,y_K \in M_2$ we have $$\sum_{i,j} \left|d_1(x_i,x_j) - d_2(y_i,y_j)\right| \geq \varepsilon\,.$$

[Corollary 17 (Index as eigenvalue winding) of arXiv:2608.30991, 'A block-Toeplitz approach to the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on self-similar'] Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:fredholm-index}, let $\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_L$ be the closed contours traced out in $\mathbb{C}$ by the eigenvalues of $\kappa^{(M)}_\alpha(\theta)$, counted with multiplicity, as $\theta$ traverses $[-\pi,\pi]$. Then
	\[
	\operatorname{ind}(\lambda I-\widetilde K^*_\Gamma)
	=-\sum_{k=1}^{L}\operatorname{wind}_\lambda\Gamma_k ,
	\]
	the winding numbers being taken about $\lambda$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition def:regular of arXiv:2411.03512, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of Sublinear Expectation System and Applications'] A sublinear expectation space $(\Omega, \mathcal{H}, \hat{\mathbb{E}})$ is called regular if for each sequence $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ in $\mathcal{H}$ with $X_i \downarrow 0$ as $i \to \infty$, one has $\lim_{i\to\infty}\hat{\mathbb{E}}[X_i]=0$.
title: Definition def:regular of arXiv:2411.03512

body:
[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.31145, 'Gauge-compatible tensors on statistical manifolds: splitting and submanifold geometry'] Let $(M,g,\nabla,\nabla^{*})$ be a statistical manifold, with $\nabla$ and $\nabla^{*}$ written as in \eqref{eq:dual-connections}. A $(1,1)$-tensor field $\Theta$ satisfies the gauge equation if and only if
\begin{equation}
(\nabla_X^{g}\Theta)Y
+
K_X(\Theta Y)
+
\Theta K_XY
=
0.
\end{equation}
In particular, if
\[
\nabla^{g}\Theta=0,
\]
then the gauge equation is equivalent to
\begin{equation}
K_X\Theta=-\Theta K_X
\end{equation}
for every $X\in\Gamma(TM)$.

[Lemma lem:blocks_somewhere of arXiv:2607.08914, 'Linear spreading speed in non-monotone population models'] There exist $\Cl{c:bsbig},  \Cl{c:bstilde} \in (0,\infty)$
  such that for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and any $\zeta \in E^\mathbb{Z}$ which is non-zero
  only at the origin,
  \begin{equation*}
    \bar{\mathbb{P}}_{\zeta}\big( D_{\Cr{c:nwalb}\sqrt{n}}(0, \eta_n)
      \leq \Cr{c:bstilde} n \big)
    \geq 1 - \Cr{c:bsbig} e^{-\Cr{c:nwasmall} \sqrt n},
  \end{equation*}
  where the constants $\Cr{c:nwasmall}, \Cr{c:nwalb}$ come from
  Lemma~(lem:neverwalkalone of the paper).

[Thm restate of limiting profile of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Let $c\in\mathbb{R}$ be an absolute constant. Let $(n_N)_{N\ge 1},(m_N)_{N\ge 1}$ and $(l_N)_{N\ge 1}$ be sequences of positive integers, such that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $m_N,l_N\ge 2$ for all $N\ge 1$, and $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}l_N=\infty$.
\item $n_N=m_Nl_N$ for all $N\ge 1$.
\end{enumerate}
For all $N\ge 1$, let $t_N=\frac{n_N}{2}(\log n_N-\frac 12\log l_N+c)$. Let $\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N}$ be defined as in (defi: Pnk and its convolution of the paper), and let $\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_{n_N}}$ be defined as in (defi: quotient of space of the paper). Then, we have
$$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}d_{TV}(\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_{n_N}})=2\Phi\left(\frac{\exp(-c)}{2}\right)-1$$
when $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}m_N=\infty$, and 
$$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}d_{TV}(\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_{n_N}})=2\Phi\left(\sqrt{1-\frac 1m}\frac{\exp(-c)}{2}\right)-1$$
when $m_N=m\ge 2$ is fixed. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm restate of limiting profile of arXiv:2604.23890

[Dfn of arXiv:2603.13873, '{Solvability of BSDEs with possibly unbounded stochastic coefficients \\ on a general weig'] A continuous function $u:\bar {G}\rightarrow{\mathbb R}^k$ is a viscosity sub-solution (super-solution) of PDE (equation PDE-1 of the paper) if for any $1\leq i\leq k$ and any function $\phi\in C^2(\bar {G};{\mathbb R})$, it holds that
$$
\begin{array}{c}
\mathcal{\bar L}\phi(x_0)+g_i(x_0,u(x_0),(\nabla\phi\sigma)(x_0))\geq 0\ (\leq 0), \ x_0\in G;\\
\max\{\mathcal{\bar L}\phi(x_0)+g_i(x_0,u(x_0),(\nabla\phi\sigma)(x_0)),
h_i(x_0)-u_i(x_0)\}\geq 0, \ x_0\in \partial G\\
(\min\{\mathcal{\bar L}\phi(x_0)+g_i(x_0,u(x_0),(\nabla\phi\sigma)(x_0)),
h_i(x_0)-u_i(x_0)\}\leq 0, \ x_0\in \partial G),
\end{array}
$$
as long as $u_i-\phi$ has a local maximum (minimum) at point $x_0\in \bar {G}$. A continuous function $u$ is a viscosity solution of PDE (equation PDE-1 of the paper) if it is both a viscosity sub-solution and a viscosity super-solution.

body: [Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] Let \(S\in\ssreg_{\le n}\). Its \emph{face poset} \(P_{S} \) is \(\bigsqcup_{p=0}^n S_p\) with \( \sigma \leq \tau\) if and only if \( \sigma \) is obtained from \( \tau \) by applying a sequence of face maps. The \emph{Hasse diagram} \(\mathcal H(S)\) is the directed graph whose vertices are the elements of \(P_{S}\), with an arrow \( \sigma \rightarrow \tau \) whenever \( \sigma \) is a codimension-one face of \(\tau\).

 \|\mathcal C_k\|_{L^2(\Omega;\mathfrak{so}(n))}

In particular, the first shell has squared energy $O(n)$ for fixed $c$.
This assertion is denoted $\mathsf{MS}_{\mathrm{intact}}$.

       \begin{equation}
           \tau^{\xi,+}_{(x_0,s)}(r)<\tau^{\xi,-}_{(y_0,s)}(r), \qquad \forall r\geq s.
       \end{equation}
       \end{enumerate}

DRAFT source scope, not an existence theorem. Lewin (2022), Section VI.B, describes the predicted intermediate hexatic phase for two-dimensional classical Riesz-type particle systems through fast translational correlations and slow sixfold bond-orientational correlations. The discussion includes short-range exponents s>2 and separate numerical Jellium cases s=0 and s=1. The review does not fix one exponent, Gibbs specification, microscopic orientational observable, nonempty parameter interval, or quantified rates as a complete theorem. A proof attempt must state those choices and prove simultaneous behavior for an actual thermodynamic state.
This summarizes a predicted phase and its scope; current openness is not certified by the 2022 review.
No existence or novelty claim is made.
title: P0321 hexatic phase: primary source distinguishes positional and sixfold order

Then there exist constants $C=C(K_0)>0$ and $C'=C'(K_0)>0$ such that the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For any $x\in H_0$ and $y\in H_{KN}$ we have ${\mathbb P}[x\to y]\geq 1-C (1-\theta)$.
\item[(ii)] Let $h\in(0,1)$ be such that $\tfrac{h}{2}\ln\tfrac{1}{1-\theta}
> (1-h)\ln 3$. Then for any $x\in H_0$
\[ 
{\mathbb P}[\xi_{KN}^x \text{ is $(1-h)$-good}]
\geq 1 - C\exp\big(-\tfrac{1}{2}
\ln\tfrac{1}{9(1-\theta)}\big)
-C'N^2 \exp\big((1-h)N\ln 3-\tfrac{hN}{2}
\ln\tfrac{1}{1-\theta}\big).
\]
\item[(iii)] 

For any $B\subset H_0$ with $|B|\geq N/2$,
we have
\[
{\mathbb P}[\xi_{KN}^B \text{ is $(1-h)$-good}]
\geq 1 - 2C'N^2 \exp\big((1-h)N\ln 3-\tfrac{hN}{2}
\ln\tfrac{1}{1-\theta}\big).
\]

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Own-work draft, claim w733-T363-013 v2, proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. Let x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4) have labels+1. Train both hidden/output weights of a bias-free two-layer ReLU network by continuous gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss. Exactly k>=1 live neurons have w_j=(u_j,y_j), v_j>0 and min_j y_j(0)>4 sqrt(sum_j u_j(0)^2); every remaining neuron is strictly dead on both points, with arbitrary output. These activation sets and positive live outputs persist, the loss tends to zero, and the entire normalized parameter direction converges to a vertical KKT family of normalized margin1/8. Its unit-margin representative is v_j=y_j=r_j>0, u_j=0, sum r_j^2=4, with all other parameters zero. For k<m this representative is not a local minimum of parameter norm subject to the two unit-margin constraints. For k=m only the direction/margin conclusion is asserted. Under iid hidden/output N(0,sigma^2) coordinates, any sigma>0, put p=atan(1/4)/pi and h_k=2^(-k) E[(1-Phi(4R))^k] for a chi_k radius R and standard Gaussian CDF Phi. The exact probability that exactly k neurons satisfy the collective live condition and all others are dead is binom(m,k) h_k p^(m-k). Summing k=1..m-1 gives a sufficient nonlocally-optimal bad-KKT family probability at widths2..6. The k=1 event is the source's known one-live family; multiple-live terms are an additional classified subcone here. This does not classify every initialization with the same activation labels or give the full Gaussian basin probability. No kink solution selection is used; all finite-time trajectories lie in smooth activation regions.
two given positive-labelled inputs, no biases, fully trained hidden/output weights
continuous summed exponential or logistic gradient flow
strict collective barrier with k positive-output both-active neurons and all others dead
k<m for failure of local optimality; iid isotropic Gaussian coordinates only for event probability

## Statement and scope
Use x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels +1, f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j dot x), no biases, with both layers trained by gradient flow for the sum of exponential or logistic losses. Exactly k neurons have v_j>0 and w_j=(u_j,y_j) satisfying

    min_j y_j(0) > 4 sqrt(sum_j u_j(0)^2).                 (H)

Every other neuron is strictly dead on both points; its output is arbitrary. The sum in (H) is over the k live neurons. For any k>=1, these activation patterns persist, loss tends to zero, and the parameter direction converges to a vertical, margin-1/8 KKT family. When k<=m-1, the unit-margin representative is not a local minimum of squared parameter norm. The multiple-live case k>=2 extends the source's one-live-neuron sufficient event; it does NOT classify every initialization with the same activation pattern. It does not assert a full Gaussian basin probability.

## 1. Barrier and existence
While the activation sets persist let a_i=-ell'(f_i)>0, A=a1+a2, d tau/dt=A, and g=(a1-a2)/A. Set b_x=sum v_j u_j, b_y=sum v_j y_j. Then f1=b_y/4+b_x and f2=b_y/4-b_x. The derivative magnitude a(f) is strictly decreasing for both losses, so b_x*g<=0 and |g|<=1. In the tau clock:

    u_j'=v_j*g,  y_j'=v_j/4,  v_j'=u_j*g+y_j/4.

For U=sum u_j^2, U'=2 b_x*g<=0. Write M=sqrt(U(0)). As long as the sector and positive outputs persist, y_j increases, and v_j'>=y_j/4-|u_j|>=y_j(0)/4-M>0. Thus v_j stays positive, y_j>=y_j(0)>4M>=4|u_j|. A first-exit argument closes the strict invariant region: no finite-time exit is possible. Dead neurons remain constant since their ReLU values and derivatives vanish at the two data points.

The physical-time vector field grows at most linearly in parameters: all live contributions are positive, hence f_i>0 and a_i<=1. Consequently the solution exists for all physical times. The tau clock is unbounded: if tau had a finite limit, the displayed linear-coefficient system (|g|<=1) would keep parameters bounded, hence f_i bounded and A bounded away from zero, contradicting bounded tau as t tends to infinity. All these arguments take place strictly inside smooth activation regions and invoke no convention at a ReLU kink.

## 2. Direction and margin
Let s_j=v_j+y_j and d_j=v_j-y_j. Their equations are

    s_j'=s_j/4+u_j*g,  d_j'=-d_j/4+u_j*g.

Since |u_j*g|<=M, e^(-tau/4)s_j has an integrable derivative and converges to c_j. Moreover c_j>=s_j(0)-4M>0. The variation-of-constants formula gives |d_j(tau)|<=|d_j(0)|+4M, while |u_j|<=M. Thus

    e^(-tau/4) v_j -> c_j/2,  e^(-tau/4) y_j -> c_j/2,
    e^(-tau/4) u_j -> 0.

All dead parameters become zero after normalization. With N the total squared parameter norm and C=sum c_j^2>0, N/e^(tau/2)->C/2, b_y/e^(tau/2)->C/4, and b_x/e^(tau/2)->0. Therefore f_i/N->1/8 and f_i->infinity. In particular the entire parameter direction converges, not merely its margin. Its unit-margin representative has live v_j=y_j=r_j>0, u_j=0, sum r_j^2=4; dead neurons are zero. Both margins equal 1 and N=8.

## 3. KKT and strict local suboptimality
For minimizing N/2 under f_i>=1, multipliers lambda1=lambda2=2 certify KKT stationarity: at each live neuron the vertical and output derivatives of 2f1+2f2 are r_j and r_j, respectively, and the horizontal derivatives cancel. At a zero neuron the output-hidden product ReLU has derivative zero at the origin, so its first-order stationarity equation holds as well. Constraints are active and multipliers positive.

For k<=m-1 select a zero neuron and one live coefficient r>0. Put a=||x1||=sqrt(17)/4. For delta>0 small, change the selected live parameters to

    v=r, u=-delta/(2r), y=r-2delta/r.

It remains active on both points if delta<r^2/4. Its prediction changes are (-delta,0). At the zero neuron introduce w=t*x1/a and v=t, where t=sqrt(delta/a)>0. Since x1 dot x2=-15/16<0, this adds (delta,0). Both constraints therefore remain exactly equal to one. The total squared norm change is

    Delta N = (-4+2/a)*delta + (17/4)*delta^2/r^2.

Here 2/a<4 because sqrt(17)>2. For sufficiently small delta the change is strictly negative; all perturbations tend to zero with delta. This proves failure of local optimality. For k=m there is no spare zero neuron and this local argument is NOT claimed, though the margin/direction conclusions still hold.

For comparison a feasible network at this width can use x1-only and x2-only directions: two neurons w_i=s*x_i/a, v_i=s with s=1/sqrt(a). Each point has margin one and squared norm 4/a=16/sqrt(17)<8. Its normalized margin is sqrt(17)/16>1/8. This is only a witness of suboptimality; no global optimality proof is needed here.

## 4. Exact Gaussian event probability
Let all hidden and output coordinates be independent N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0. Write p=atan(1/4)/pi, the hidden dead-sector probability. For a specified set of k live neurons, the probability of (H) and all positive outputs is

    h_k = 2^(-k) E[ (1-Phi(4 R))^k ],  R~chi_k,
        = 2^(-k)/(2^(k/2-1) Gamma(k/2))
          integral_0^infinity r^(k-1) exp(-r^2/2) [1-Phi(4r)]^k dr.

Indeed, after dividing by sigma the k horizontal coordinates are independent standard Gaussians; conditionally on their radius R each vertical coordinate must exceed 4R, independently; output signs contribute 2^(-k). For k>=1 this integral is strictly positive. The exact probability of exactly k barrier-live neurons and all others dead, with arbitrary placements, is

    P_{m,k} = binom(m,k) h_k p^(m-k).

These placement events, and the events for different k, are disjoint since live and dead sectors are disjoint. For widths2..6 the sufficient non-local-minimum bad-family probability is sum_{k=1}^{m-1} P_{m,k}. The k=1 term is the already known source family, since h_1=p/2. The additional terms k=2..m-1 (ten width/k pairs for m=3..6) are the new part of this slice. For widths2..6 the coefficient rows multiplying h_k p^(m-k) are respectively [2], [3,3], [4,6,4], [5,10,10,5], [6,15,20,15,6]. These are exact event masses, not certified numerical approximations to h_k and not total bad-basin probabilities. The cone condition is scale-invariant, so these formulas apply in particular to sigma=1e-6.

## Source, verification, and remaining gap
Primary source: Vardi, Shamir and Srebro, On Margin Maximization in Linear and ReLU Networks, arXiv:2110.02732v4, Theorem3.2 and AppendixC.3 (two-point counterexample). Its case is taken as ground, not claimed new. This note supplies a self-contained sufficient multiple-live-neuron extension. Full activation-pattern classification, all mixed-sector interactions, and a total Gaussian bad-basin probability remain open. Independent reviewer PASS is required; no audit or novelty certification is claimed. The most delicate step for review is closing the all-neuron barrier using U'=2 b_x*g and then passing to the normalized parameter direction.

scripts/collective_barrier_checks.py passed exact symbolic checks of the ODE balance, collective energy derivative, KKT equations, and perturbation identities, plus exact rational feasible descent examples. The Gaussian integral quadrature reproduces h1=p/2 as a numerical sanity check; all quadrature entries remain estimates, not rigorous bounds. Ten new multiple-live cases (m=3..6, k=2..m-1) were integrated using the full exponential-loss gradient ODE at scale1e-6. All accepted nodes preserved sectors and positive outputs; final margins differed from1/8 by at most3.68e-15. These structured interior probes are not conditional Gaussian samples and do not estimate event frequency. The proof, rather than node sampling, supplies continuous invariance. No logistic numerical simulations were run.

Lean was attempted for only the denominator-cleared perturbation identity in collective_descent_identity.lean. The helper returned RUNTIME_UNVERIFIED after48.899 seconds with no compiler exit code. [Theorema Mixed Gaussian--jump comparison of arXiv:2510.18106, 'Law equivalence for Ornstein--Uhlenbeck dynamics\\ driven by L\'evy noise'] Let $A$ and $\widetilde A$ generate $C_0$-semigroups. Suppose that the Gaussian Ornstein--Uhlenbeck law generated by $A$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the one generated by $\widetilde A$, and that the jump--drift discrepancy
\[
        \int_0^t(S-\widetilde S)(t-s)\,dZ_s
        +\int_0^t(S-\widetilde S)(t-s)b\,ds
\]
belongs, conditionally on the jump path, to the Cameron--Martin space of the $\widetilde A$-Gaussian channel. Then
\[
        \mathcal{L}(X^A)\ll \mathcal{L}(X^{\widetilde A})
        \quad\hbox{on }D([0,T];H).
\]
If the two Gaussian Ornstein--Uhlenbeck laws are equivalent, then the two full L\'evy-driven laws are equivalent. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mixed Gaussian--jump comparison

In any tensor-triangulated category $\mathcal{T}$, the Bousfield lattice $\operatorname{BLat}(\mathcal{T})$ is a complete lattice satisfying the infinite distributive law: $\langle E \rangle \wedge \bigvee_{i \in I} \langle F_i \rangle = \bigvee_{i \in I} (\langle E \rangle \wedge \langle F_i \rangle)$, where $\wedge$ is given by $\otimes$ and $\bigvee$ is given by coproducts.
\mathcal{T} is a closed symmetric monoidal category with coproducts
Tensor product commutes with coproducts

[Corollary cor:bipartite of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Fix $\theta\in(0,1]$. Let $G^{(n)}$ be a sequence of bipartite graphs on $n$ vertices satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for the same $\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$. Let $\mathsf{x}_\mathrm{alt} = \mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}^{(n)}$ denote the alternating condition on $G^{(n)}$ as in (eq:alternatingbipartite of the paper). Then, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, the binary noisy voter model on $G^{(n)}$ with noise $\theta$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}}(\varepsilon) = \frac{1+o(1)}{\min\{4-2\theta,4\theta\}}\log n\,,
\end{equation}
where the $o(1)$-term is $ O\big(\log^{-\upalpha/2} n\big)
$ with a constant depending on $\varepsilon,\theta,\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$ (but not on $G^{(n)}$).
Furthermore, if $\mathsf{x}_0=\mathsf{x}_0^{(n)}$ is any arbitrary sequence of initial conditions, we have
\[
\liminf_{n \to \infty}\frac{t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_0}(\varepsilon)}{t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}}(\varepsilon)} \geq 1\,,
\]
thus $\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}$ is the asymptotically fastest initial condition on $G^{(n)}$. In particular, for Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}_n$ (the case $G^{(n)}=\mathbb{Z}_n$) at any inverse temperature $\beta>0$, the alternating initial condition $\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}$ is the asymptotically fastest initial condition. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:bipartite of arXiv:2507.16188

body:
[Theorem t:joint.sum.max.star of arXiv:2601.12677, 'Stable and Fréchet limit theorem for subgraph functionals in the hyperbolic random geometr'] $(i)$ If $\frac{1}{2} (k-1)<\alpha< k-1$, then as $n\to\infty$, 
\begin{align}
&\left( \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n\cdot\,]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) - [N_n\cdot\,]  \mathbb{E} [\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_1)] \bigg), \ \frac{1}{a_{k,n}}\bigvee_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot \,]} \mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i)\right)  \Rightarrow (S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot),\, Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot)),   
\end{align}
in the space $D\big([0,1], {\mathbb R} \times [0,\infty)\big)$ of right-continuous functions from $[0,1]$ to ${\mathbb R}\times [0,\infty)$ with left limits. The weak limit in (equation e:weak.conv.join.sum.max.star of the paper) is defined by the hybrid characteristic–distribution function
\begin{equation}  
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{ivS_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t)} {\mathbf 1} \{ Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t) \le z \} \big] = t\int_0^z e^{ivy} g(v,y)^t e^{-ty^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}} \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif y),  \  \ v\in {\mathbb R},\,  z\ge 0,  
\end{equation}
where
$$
g(v,y) := \exp \Big\{ \int_0^\infty \big( (e^{ivx}-1){\mathbf 1} \{ x<y \} -ivx \big) \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif x)\Big\}, 
$$
and $\mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a Radon measure on $(0,\infty]$ satisfying $\mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}\big((y,\infty]\big)=y^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}$ for $y>0$. \\
Marginally, $S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a zero-mean $2\alpha/(k-1)$-stable L\'evy process whose characteristic function is given by (equation e:chf.first.comp.zero.mean.stable of the paper) below. Furthermore, $Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is an extremal $2\alpha/(k-1)$-Fr\'echet process; that is, for $0\equiv t_0<t_1<\cdots <t_m<\infty$ and $z_i\ge0$, $i=1,\dots,m$, 
$$
\mathbb{P}\big( Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t_i)\le z_i, \, i=1,\dots,m \big)=\exp \Big\{ -\sum_{j=1}^m (t_j-t_{j-1}) (z_j \wedge \cdots \wedge z_m)^{-2\alpha/(k-1)} \Big\}. 
$$
$(ii)$ If $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<\frac{1}{2} (k-1)$, then as $n\to\infty$, 
$$
\left( \frac{1}{a_{k,n}}  \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot\, ]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i), \ \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \bigvee_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot \,]} \mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) \right)  \Rightarrow (\widetilde{S}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot), Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot)), \ \ \text{in } D\big( [0,1], [0,\infty)^2\big), 
$$
where the weak limit is defined by 
\begin{equation}  
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{iv\widetilde{S}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t)} {\mathbf 1} \{ Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t) \le z \} \big] = t\int_0^z e^{ivy} \, \widetilde{g}(v,y)^t e^{-ty^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}} \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif y),  \ \ \ v\in {\mathbb R},\,  z\ge 0,  
\end{equation}
with 
$$
\widetilde{g}(v,y) := \exp \Big\{ \int_0^y (e^{ivx}-1) \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif x)\Big\}. 
$$
Marginally, $\widetilde S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a $2\alpha/(k-1)$-stable subordinator (i.e., a stable L\'evy process with increasing paths) with its characteristic function given by (equation e:chf.first.comp.zero.stable.subordinator of the paper) below. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

A(Tx) A(x). The Oseledets multiplicative ergodic theorem states there exist real numbers lambda_1 > ... > lambda_r and, for almost every x, a filtration R^d = V_1(x) > ... > V_r(x) > V_{r+1}(x) = {0} with A(x) V_i(x) = V_i(Tx), such that for v in V_i(x) minus V_{i+1}(x), (1/n) log ||A_n(x) v|| -> lambda_i as n -> infinity. The lambda_i are the Lyapunov exponents. Due to Valery Oseledets.

Then the  sequence $(\overline{\gamma}_m)_{m}$ in Theorem (t:DeGiorgiNashMoser of the paper) can be taken constant whenever the stochastic flow of diffeomorphisms $\xi$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\biggl(
\sup_{t\in [0,T],x\in \mathbb{T}^d} | (D\xi_t(x))^{-1}|\biggr)\biggl/ \biggl( \inf_{t\in [0,T],x\in \mathbb{T}^d} \frac{1}{ |D\xi_t(x)| } \biggr)  \,\le \, C, 
\end{equation}
almost surely for some deterministic constant $C<\infty$. The latter applies in particular in the following cases.
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm(1)}]
   \item 
   {\rm(Constant noise coefficients)} For each $n\in {\mathbb N}$,  $b_n(t,\omega, x)$ depends only on $(t,\omega)$.
    \item  {\rm (Commuting flows)}  For some $N\in {\mathbb N}$ we have $b_n = 0$ for all $n>N$, while for  $k\ne n\le N$ it holds:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item  The commutator  
$[b_k,b_n]$ vanishes.
    \item Each $b_n(t,x,\omega) = b_n(x)$  depends only on space.
        \item For $\phi_t^n(x)$ being the solution to  $
         \dot{\phi}_t^n(x) \,=\, -b_n(\phi_t^n(x))$ starting from $ \phi_0^n(x)\,=\, x$,
        we have 
        \begin{equation}
        \biggl(
        \sup_{t\in [0,\infty),x\in \mathbb{T}^d} | (D\phi_t^n (x))^{-1}|\biggr)\biggl/ \biggl( \inf_{t\in [0,\infty),x\in \mathbb{T}^d} \frac{1}{ |D\phi_{t}^n(x)| } \biggr)  \,<\,\infty.
        \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 21 (Dense-discrepancy phase diagram) of arXiv:2608.26693, '2608.26693'] Assume the conditions of Assumption~\ref{ass:spectral-bounds} and equal unit masses.  Let
\[
\mu_{i,p}=\N(m_{i,p},\Sigma_{i,p}),\qquad i=0,1,
\]
and suppose
\[
\tau_p=\bar\tau p^\alpha,
\qquad \bar\tau>0,\quad \alpha>0,
\]
with
\[
w_p:=\frac1pW_2^2(\mu_{0,p},\mu_{1,p})\to w>0.
\]
Then the normalized action converges to the balanced discrepancy,
\[
\frac{\Acal_{*,p}}p\to w
\]
and the optimal transported mass satisfies
\begin{equation}
M_{*,p}\longrightarrow
\begin{cases}
0,&0<\alpha<1,\\[0.5ex]
\exp\{-w/(2\bar\tau)\},&\alpha=1,\\[0.5ex]
1,&\alpha>1.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem:ad_frame_comp_strat of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Assume (ass:standing of the paper)~(ass:standing:chart of the paper). One can choose \(C^{r}\) maps
  \begin{equation*}
    \mathbf{S}: \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{out}}\to \mathbb R^{d\times(m-c)},\quad
    \mathbf{C}: \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{out}}\to \mathbb R^{d\times c},\quad
    \mathbf{N}: \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{out}}\to \mathbb R^{d\times k},\quad
    \mathbf{L}: \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{out}}\to \mathsf{GL}(m),
  \end{equation*}
  such that, for every \(x=\varphi(\theta)\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{out}}\), the following properties hold.
  \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=0pt]
    \item The columns of \(\mathbf{S}(x)\),  \(\mathbf{C}(x)\) and \( \mathbf{N}(x)\) form an orthonormal basis of
    \(\mathcal T_x\mathcal{S}\), \(\mathcal T_x\mathcal{M}\cap(\mathcal T_x\mathcal{S})^\perp\) and \(\mathcal
    N_x\mathcal{M}=(\mathcal T_x\mathcal{M})^\perp\), respectively.

    \item With \(\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{M}}(x)=[\,\mathbf{S}(x)\ \mathbf{C}(x)\,] \in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) and \(
    \mathbf{Q}(x)=[\,\mathbf{S}(x)\ \mathbf{C}(x)\ \mathbf{N}(x)\,] \in\mathsf O(d)\), the matrix \(\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{ch}}(x) =
    \mathrm{D}_\xi \Phi(\theta,0)\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) satisfies
    \(\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{ch}}(x)=\mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{M}}(x)\mathbf{L}(x)\).

    \item The inward tangent cone is \(\mathcal T_x^+\mathcal{M} = \mathbf{Q}_{\mathcal{M}}(x)\mathbf{L}(x) \mathbb H_c^m\).
    \item The matrix field \(\mathbf{L}\) satisfies: \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{out}}}
    \bigl(\|\mathbf{L}(x)\|+\|\mathbf{L}(x)^{-1}\| \bigr)<\infty\).
  \end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:IPS:noise:contraction of arXiv:2605.16904, 'Positive-rate PCA and IPS with stationary Bernoulli measures are rapidly forgetful \footno'] Let $(\Theta_J)_{J\Subset\mathbb{Z}^d}$ be the family of asynchronous updating kernels associated with memoryless noise
	with error rate~$1$ and replacement distribution~$q$,
	and let $\lambda=\lambda_q$ be the Bernoulli measure with marginal~$q$.
	Then,
	\begin{equation}
		D_J(\mu\Theta_J\relto\lambda)
		\leq
			\Big(1-\frac{1}{\abs{J}}\Big) D_J(\mu\relto\lambda)
	\end{equation}
	for every probability measure~$\mu$ and every finite set $J\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d$.

[Lemma lemma1519 of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Let $X=(\xi_1,\cdots,\xi_N)\in\mathbb{C}^N$ have independent coordinates and each $\xi_i$ has a Lebesgue density $f_i$ satisfying $\|f_i\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{C})}\leq K$.
     Consider $U:\mathbb{C}^N\to\mathbb{C}^r$ an isometry onto its image: $UU^*=I_{\mathbb{C}^r}$. Then $UX$ has a planar density $P_U$ on $\mathbb{C}^r$ satisfying 
     $$
\|P_U\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{C}^r)}\leq (eK)^r.
     $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (A_j,B_j), j=1,2,..., be pairs of sigma-fields such that the joined fields A_j join B_j are mutually independent over j. Then rho(join_{j>=1}A_j,join_{j>=1}B_j)=sup_{j>=1}rho(A_j,B_j). The same conclusion holds for finitely many pairs. Independence of the joined pairs is required; independence just within or across individual coordinates is not a substitute. Rho is maximal L2 correlation over all measurable functions of the respective fields. Source: Basic Properties of Strong Mixing Conditions. A Survey and Some Open Questions, Theorem 5.1(b) and attribution paragraph, journal p.126 (PDF p.20).

[Corollary cor:periodic-marked-winding-bridge-limit of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] Assume \(d>2\) and let \(N_L/V_L\to\rho>\rho_{\mathrm c}\). 
Then the finite-volume periodic marked Feynman cycle process
\(\Xi_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{per}}\)  converges to the marked Gamma bridge of total
mass $\rho-\rho_{\mathrm c}$ with length-dependent mark measure \(\eta_x\) given by
(equation eq:periodic-limiting-eta of the paper).  More precisely, before conditioning on the
total macroscopic mass, the limiting tilted Poisson intensity is
$ du\,e^{-s x}dx/x\,\eta_x(dm)$,
and conditioning the total mass to be $\rho-\rho_{\mathrm c}$ gives the canonical marked bridge.
The resulting bridge law is independent of the auxiliary tilt parameter \(s\).

Let
$ \bigl(X_{L,i},U_{L,i},R_{L,i},Y_{L,i},\zeta_{L,i}\bigr)_{i\ge1}$
be the atoms of \(\Xi_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{per}}\) ranked by decreasing
macroscopic length.  Then, for every fixed \(m\ge1\),
\[
  \bigl(X_{L,i},U_{L,i},R_{L,i},Y_{L,i},\zeta_{L,i}\bigr)_{1\le i\le m}
  \Longrightarrow
  \bigl(X_i,U_i,R_i,Y_i,\zeta_i\bigr)_{1\le i\le m}.
\]
The limiting ranked lengths satisfy
$ (X_i)_{i\ge1}
  \sim
  (\rho-\rho_c)\,{\rm PD}(0,1)$.
Conditionally on \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\), the marks are independent and, for each
\(i\),
\[
  R_i\sim\mathsf H_{\mathbb T^d},
  \qquad
  Y_i\sim N(0,2\beta X_iI_d),
  \qquad
  \zeta_i\sim \sqrt{2\beta X_i}\,B^{\mathrm{br}}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Periodic marked winding--bridge limit

body: [Definition defepsbalanced of arXiv:2607.06952, 'Universality for cokernels of partially random integral matrices'] Let $X$ be a random vector valued in $V$ (with entries not necessarily independent). Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and $\tau \subset [n]$ and $A \in \GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/a\mathbb{Z})$. We say that $X$ is \emph{$(\varepsilon,\tau, A)$-balanced} if $\tilde{X} = AX$ has independent entries and \[\tau \supseteq \{i: \tilde{X}_i \text{ is not }\varepsilon\text{-balanced} \}.\]

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2604.24664, 'Absolute continuity of Rosenblatt measures'] Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and $f: [0, T] \to \Rbb$. The \emph{left} and \emph{right Riemann--Liouville fractional derivatives of $f$ of order $\alpha$} are defined by
	\begin{align*}
		(I^{-\alpha}_{0+} f)(x) &= \frac{1}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)} \frac{\d{}}{\d{x}} \int_0^x (x-y)^{-\alpha} f(y) \d{y},
		\\
		(I^{-\alpha}_{T-} f)(x') &= \frac{1}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)} \frac{\d{}}{\d{x'}} \int_{x'}^{T} (y-x')^{-\alpha} f(y) \d{y},
	\end{align*}
	for almost all $x,x' \in [0, T]$.
title: Definition 3 of arXiv:2604.24664

[Definition eqn: val-def of arXiv:2604.08462, 'Convergence of $k$-point functions in\\ high dimensional percolation'] Fix $v,w_1\ldots, w_k\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $S$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $\{0,\ldots, r\}$, with $r\ge k$. We assume the leaves (i.e. vertices of degree 1) are labeled by $\{0,\ldots, k\}$. 

We let $I(S)=\{k+1,\ldots, r\}$ denote the non-leaf (internal) vertices.
A map 
\[\psi: V(S)=\{0,\ldots,r\}\rightarrow \mathbb{Z}^d\]
is \emph{admissible} if $\psi(0)=v$ and $\psi(i)=w_i$ for $0\le i \le k$. Note that we do not require $\psi$ to be injective.

We define the \emph{valuation} of $S$ by
\begin{equation}

\mathrm{val}(S)=\sum_{\psi \text{ admissible }}\prod_{e=\{x,y\}\in E(S)}\tau\big(\psi(x),\psi(y)\big).
\end{equation}
title: Definition eqn: val-def of arXiv:2604.08462

We also recall that $\mathtt{Ht} \colon\mathbb{T}^{0}_{\! c} \! \to \!  \mathbb{R}_+$  stands for the height of compact $\mathbb{R}$-trees. Then $R_b $ under $ \texttt Q_{\xi,c}(\, \cdot \, | \, \mathtt{Ht} \! > \!  b )$ (resp.~under 
$\texttt P_{\! \xi, c, \varrho}$) is a GW($\xi^*\! , c^*$)-tree (resp.~a GW($\xi^*\! , c^*\! , \varrho^*$)-forest) where for all $s\! \in \!  [0, 1]$, 
\begin{equation}

c^*\!\!  :=\! c (1\! -\! \varphi'_{\xi} (\alpha)), \; \varphi_{\xi^*} \! (s) \! = \!  s+ \frac{\varphi_\xi (\alpha + (1\! -\! \alpha) s) \! -\! \alpha \! -\! (1\! -\! \alpha) s }{(1\! -\! \alpha)(1\! -\! \varphi'_{\xi} (\alpha))}, \; \varphi_{\varrho^*}\!  (s) \! = \!  \varphi_{\varrho} ( \alpha + (1\! -\! \alpha) s).

[Proposition prop:chi2 of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Under the pseudo-wave map the semigroup acts by
$\psi_{\pi_t}=D^{-1}T_tD\,\psi_{\pi_0}=e^{\Lambda t(A-\mathrm{I})}\psi_{\pi_0}$ with
$A=A^{T}$, so $T_t$ is self-adjoint in $L^{2}(1/\nu)$. The stationary law maps to
the unit vector $\psi_\nu=\sqrt\nu$, and the $\chi^{2}$ divergence is the
corresponding squared distance to it,

\begin{equation}
\chi^{2}(p\,\|\,\nu)=\sum_i\frac{(p_i-\nu_i)^{2}}{\nu_i}=\|\psi_p-\psi_\nu\|^{2}.

\end{equation}

Consequently, with $\gamma$ the spectral gap of the chain,
$\chi^{2}(\pi_t\,\|\,\nu)\le e^{-2\gamma t}\,\chi^{2}(\pi_0\,\|\,\nu)$.

[Proposition 43 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] Let $\nu$ be a supercritical offspring distribution whose mean is denoted by $\ttm_\nu$. 
 Let $\ttb\ino (2, \infty)$. We assume that $\sum_{k\in \bbN} k^{\ttb}\nu(k) \leko \infty$.
Let $(\bT, \boo)$ be an invariant GW($\nu$)-tree as in Definition \ref{definvRW}. 
Let the r.v.s $U_x, S_x$, $x\ino \bT$, be as in (\ref{welldefcoo}) and (\ref{defSx}). 
Let $\overline{X}_n \eqo (\bT, X_n)$, $n\ino \bbN$, be a $\mathtt m_\nu$-biased RW on $\bT$ such that $X_0 \eqo \boo$. 
We denote by $\ccF_n$ the $\sigma$-field generated by 
$(\overline{X}_k)_{0\leq k\leq n}$. Let $r_n , s_n\ino \bbN$, $n\ino \bbN$ be such that $\frac{1}{n}r_n \! \to \! r\ino \bbR_+ $ and $ \frac{1}{n}s_n \! \to \! s \ino \bbR_+$. Recall from (\ref{vutchi}) the definition of $\sigma_\nu$. 
Then for all $\lambda\ino \bbR$, 
\begin{equation}

\textrm{$\bP$-a.s.~} \quad \lim_{n\to \infty}\bE \Big[ \exp \big( i\tfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{n}} \big( S_{X_{r_n+s_n}} \! \! -\! S_{X_{r_n}}\big) \big) \Big| \ccF_{r_n} \Big]\eqo  e^{-\frac{_1}{^2} s\sigma^2_\nu \lambda^2}\; . 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For the centered unit-variance Gaussian wave on T_3 with eigenvalue -2sqrt(2), let p_prime_s be the probability that a fixed s-vertex simple path is exactly a component of the induced subgraph of negative wave values: all path values are negative and all adjacent off-path values positive. Let phi and Phi be the standard normal density and CDF. For R,S>=0 define g_0(R,S)=2Phi(sqrt(2)S+R/2)-1 and g_k(R,S)=integral_0^infinity phi(Y+sqrt(2)S+R/2)g_{k-1}(S,Y)dY for k>=1. For every s>=2 and 0<=m<=s-2, p_prime_s=integral_0^infinity integral_0^infinity D(R,S)g_m(R,S)g_{s-2-m}(S,R)dR dS, where D(R,S)=exp[-3(R^2+S^2)/8-(sqrt(2)/2)RS]/(8pi). The isolated-vertex probability is p_1=1/2-(3/(4pi))arccos(5/6). All kernels and functions are nonnegative. Positive rectangle lower sums may omit tails and further odd-path terms while retaining a lower inequality. The product of the two functions in the component integral is justified by the Gaussian Markov property conditional on the shared edge values, rather than an assumption of independent branches without conditioning.

\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem Informal; bounded-disorder coexistence of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:intro-coexistence}
For every \(p\ge3\), there is a symmetric, compactly supported law
\(\mu\) with a \(C^\infty\) density, matching the standard Gaussian moments through
order \(2p\), for which the following hold simultaneously.  Every fixed
admissible incoherent-frame regularization has expectation asymptotic to
its Gaussian counterpart, whereas for some compact interval
\(B\subset(0,\infty)\),
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_N^J(B)
 >
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_N^G(B).
\]
The count on the left is unregularized and unrestricted in space.  The
same dichotomy holds in the standard symmetric-coordinate model. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Informal; bounded-disorder coexistence

[Defi Def:Stratum of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] For a weighted polyhedron $(X,\lambda)$, let 
     $$O^n(X,\lambda):=\{x\in X\,|\, \lambda(x)=n\} \subseteq X,\ n\in \mathrm{Im}(\lambda).$$
      We call $O^n(X,\lambda)$ a \emph{stratum} of $(X,\lambda)$.
So $X$ is the disjoint union of all its strata:
 $$X = \bigcup_{n\in \mathrm{Im}(\lambda)} O^n(X,\lambda).$$

[Co restricted-isometry of arXiv:2608.13154, 'Extreme principal minors of Wishart and deformed GOE matrices'] Let $k\geq 1$ be fixed. Suppose that $p/\log n\to\beta\in\left( 0,\infty\right)$ and that (equation regularity conds of the paper) holds. Then
\[
    \delta_k \left( \bm X/\sqrt p \right)
    \stackrel{\mathbb P}{\to}
    \Delta_{k,\beta,\mu}
    :=\sup_{\bm Q\in\Gamma_{k,\beta,\mu}}
    \|\bm Q-\bm I_k\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
If $\mu=N(0,1)$ and $\lambda_{k,\beta}>1$ is the unique solution of
\[
    \lambda_{k,\beta}-\log\lambda_{k,\beta}-1=\frac{2k}{\beta},
\]
then
\[
    \Delta_{k,\beta,\mu}=\lambda_{k,\beta}-1.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed $\delta\in(0,1)$,
\[
\mathbb P\left(\delta_k\left(\bm X/\sqrt p\right)\leq\delta\right)
\to
\begin{cases}
1, & \displaystyle \beta>\frac{2k}{\delta-\log\left( 1+\delta\right)},\\[2mm]
0, & \displaystyle \beta<\frac{2k}{\delta-\log\left( 1+\delta\right)}.
\end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Restricted isometry threshold

[Lem I-prop of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] The following hold for any $\omega\in\Omega_0$, $\theta\in\Theta^\omega$, and $x_0,s_0,t\in\mathbb{R}$.

\begin{enumerate} [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}] \itemsep=1pt 
\item $-\infty<I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t)\le I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(t)<\infty$.
\item $W^{\theta-}(y,t;x_0,s_0)<W^{\theta+}(y,t;x_0,s_0)$ for all $y>I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(t)$.
\item $W^{\theta-}(y,t;x_0,s_0)>W^{\theta+}(y,t;x_0,s_0)$ for all $y<I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t)$.
\item $W^{\theta-}(y,t;x_0,s_0)=W^{\theta+}(y,t;x_0,s_0)$ for all $y\in[I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t),I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(t)]$.
\item $I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(s_0)\le x_0\le I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(s_0)$.
\item $W^{\theta-}(I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(t),t;y,t)>W^{\theta+}(I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(t),t;y,t)$ for all $y>I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(t)$.
\item $W^{\theta-}(I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t),t;y,t)<W^{\theta+}(I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t),t;y,t)$ for all $y<I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t)$.
\item $W^{\theta-}(I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t),t;y,t)=W^{\theta+}(I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t),t;y,t)$ for all $y\in[I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta-}(t),I_{(x_0,s_0)}^{\theta+}(t)]$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lem I-prop of arXiv:2604.12963

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, A necessary and sufficient condition for convergence of the quantile process in L^p(0,1) (October 2026), proves that for 1 <= p < infinity the empirical quantile process sqrt(n)(Q_n - Q) converges in distribution in L^p(0,1) if and only if the quantile function Q is locally absolutely continuous on (0,1) and the integral of q(t)^p [t(1-t)]^{p/2} dt over (0,1) is finite, where q = Q'. The limit is -qB, with B a Brownian bridge. No density is assumed and atoms are allowed. The case p = 1 is due to Beare and Kaji (arXiv:2502.01254); for p > 1 this answers Problem 2 in Section 7 of the survey of del Barrio, Gonzalez-Sanz, Loubes and Rodriguez-Vitores (arXiv:2505.19104). Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/quantile-process-lp (commit 4f78b53fc32e). Not refereed.
title: A necessary and sufficient condition for convergence of the empirical quantile process in L^p(0,1) (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/quantile-process-lp)

[Definition def:graph_event_E_reg of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Let $K^{\mathcal{E}}$ be a large constant. Define $\mathcal{E}$ to be the collection of graphs $H$ on the vertex set $[n]$ which satisfy the following inequalities (where $A$ denotes the adjacency matrix of $H$):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item  For $k\in \{1, 2\}$ and any distinct $s_1, \dots, s_k\in [n]$ we have
    \[\sum_{1\leq i\leq n} |A_{s_1i}-p|\cdots |A_{s_ki}-p|\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}p^k n, \quad \text{ which implies}\quad
    \sum_{1\leq i\leq n} |\lambda_{s_1i}\cdots \lambda_{s_ki}| \leq O(K^{\mathcal{E}} z_p^k p^k n).\]

    \item  For $k\in \{1, 2\}$, any interval $I\subseteq [n]$ and any distinct $s_1, \dots, s_k\in [n]$ we have
    \[\Big|\!\sum_{i\in I} (A_{s_1i}-p)\cdots (A_{s_ki}-p)\Big|\!\leq\! K^{\mathcal{E}}\sqrt{p^k n\log n}, \text{ which implies } \Big|\!\sum_{i\in I} \!\!\lambda_{s_1i}\cdots \lambda_{s_ki}\Big|\!\leq \!O(K^{\mathcal{E}}z_p^k \sqrt{p^k n\log n}).\]

    \item  We have $\|A-pJ\|_{op}\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}\sqrt{np}$. If the $n\times n$ matrix $\Lambda$ is defined by $\Lambda_{ij}=\lambda_{ij}$, this also implies $\|\Lambda\|_{op}\leq O(K^{\mathcal{E}}z_p\sqrt{np})$.

    \item  For any $s\in [n]$ we have \[\sum_{s<i<j\leq n}\big|(A_{si}-p)(A_{sj}-p)(A_{ij}-p)\big|\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}p^3 n^2, \text{which implies} \sum_{s<i<j\leq n}\big|\lambda_{si}\lambda_{sj}\lambda_{ij}\big|\leq O(K^{\mathcal{E}}n^2p^3z_p^3).\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:graph_event_E_reg of arXiv:2607.22480

Let psi_X be the cumulant generating function of a random variable X. The Cramer transform, in the one-sided convention used for upper-tail (Chernoff) bounds, is psi_X^*(t) = sup_{lambda >= 0} (lambda * t - psi_X(lambda)). For t >= E X it equals the Fenchel-Legendre dual (convex conjugate) sup over all real lambda of (lambda * t - psi_X(lambda)), which is Cramer's rate function; for t < E X the one-sided transform is 0, while the conjugate is in general positive (for a standard normal X the conjugate is t^2/2 for every t).
psi_X is the cumulant generating function of X
E|X| < infinity, so that E X is defined (used only in comparing the one-sided and two-sided transforms)

[Lemma 49 of arXiv:2606.15425, 'Well-posedness of stochastic parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities and applicat'] Let $\sigma$ be a stopping time,
and denote by $(\mathcal F^\sigma_t)_{t \geq 0} \coloneqq (\mathcal F_{\sigma+t})_{t \geq 0}$ the corresponding shifted 
filtration. Let $G \colon \Omega \times \R_{\geq0} \rightarrow E$ denote an $(\mathcal F^\sigma_t)_{t \geq 0}$-progressively measurable process with values in a topological vector space $E$ and let $\tau(\sigma) \geq 0$ denote a stopping time w.r.t. $(\mathcal F^\sigma_t)_{t \geq 0}$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item The process $\widetilde G_t \coloneqq \mathds1_{\{t \geq \sigma\}} G_{(t-\sigma)_+}$ is $\mathcal F_t$-progressively measurable and
    \item $\sigma + \tau(\sigma)$ is an $\mathcal F_t$-stopping time.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 8 (Overlap bound) of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix $\alpha$ and let $S_\alpha,S_\beta$ be independent uniform $L$-subsets of
	$\{1,\dots,M\}$. For any $t\in\{0,\dots,L-1\}$,
	\[
	\mathbb P\bigl(|S_\beta\cap S_\alpha|\ge t+1\bigr)
	\le
	\binom{L}{t+1}\left(\frac{L}{M}\right)^{t+1}.
	\]
	Consequently,
	\[
	\mathbb P\Bigl(\max_{\beta\neq\alpha}|S_\beta\cap S_\alpha|\ge t+1\Bigr)
	\le
	P\,\binom{L}{t+1}\left(\frac{L}{M}\right)^{t+1}.
	\]

body:
[Lemma lem.mathcalY of arXiv:2605.11785, 'Regularization of a mean-field SDE by an additive common noise: the conditional expectatio'] For any $\mu_0\in \mathcal P_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, there exists a unique Borel measurable map $\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}: [0,T]\times \mathbb{R}^d\times  {\mathcal C}\to \mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for any $(t,x,\bm{x})\in [0,T]\times \mathbb{R}^d\times {\mathcal C}$, 
$$
\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(t,x, {\bm{x}}) = x-\overline \mu_0+\int_0^t  b(\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(s,x, {\bm{x}})+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)ds - \int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} b(\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(s,y, {\bm{x}})+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)\mu_0(dy)ds. 
$$
In addition, $\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}$ is nonanticipating in the sense that 
$$
\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(t,x, {\bm{x}}) = \mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(t,x, {\bm{x}}(\cdot \wedge t))
$$
and the map $(x,\mu_0)\to \mathcal Y^{\mu_0}(t,x,\bm{x})$ is Lipschitz continuous on $\mathbb{R}^d\times \mathcal P_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, uniformly with respect to $t\in [0,T]$ and $\bm{x} \in {\mathcal C}$. Last, if $(y^1_t,\cdots,y^N_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ solves 
\begin{equation}
   \forall t\in[0,T],\;y^i_t=x^i_0-\frac 1N\sum_{j=1}^Nx^j_0+\int_0^t  b(y^i_s+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)ds - \int_0^t\frac 1N\sum_{j=1}^Nb(y^j_s+{\bm{x}}_s, {\bm{x}}_s)ds,\;i\in\{1,\cdots,N\},
\end{equation}
then 
$$
(y^1_t,\cdots,y^N_t)_{t\in[0,T]}=(\mathcal Y^{m^N_{\vec{x}_0}}(t,x^1_0, {\bm{x}}),\cdots,\mathcal Y^{m^N_{\vec{x}_0}}(t,x^N_0, {\bm{x}}))_{t\in[0,T]},
$$ 
where we recall the notation $m^N_{\vec{x}_0}=\frac 1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{x^i_0}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem.mathcalY of arXiv:2605.11785

    Assume that $\pi$ satisfies~(equation eq:lsi of the paper) with constant $1/\alpha$, $-\beta I \preceq \nabla^2 V \preceq \beta I$, $\gamma = \sqrt{32\beta}$, and $\kappa \coloneqq \beta/\alpha$.

    Then, for all $\varepsilon \in (0, \widetilde O(1 \wedge \sqrt{\mathfrak{L}(\bs \mu)})]$ and $h = \widetilde{\Theta}(\frac{\varepsilon^{2/3}}{(1+C_{\chi^2})^{1/3}\,\beta^{1/2} \kappa^{1/3} d^{1/3} \log^{1/3}(\mathfrak{L}(\bs\mu)/\varepsilon^2)})$, we have $\mathsf{TV}(\bs\mu\hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}^{N-1}\hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}' \mathbin{\|} \bs\pi) \leqslant \varepsilon$ provided that

[Definition of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] An intersections of $K$ halfspaces with $\gamma$ margin with respect to a (possibly infinite) collection of vectors $\mathcal X$ contained in the unit ball is specified by vectors $w_1,\ldots,w_k$ in the unit ball $B$. These vectors must satisfy the requirement that $\mathcal X \subset B_+ \cup B_-$, where the region $B_+$ is defined by
\[ B_+ = \{ x \in B: \forall i \in [k], \langle w_i, x \rangle \ge 0 \} \]
and similarly the region containing negative examples is
\[ B_- = \{ x \in B : \exists i \in [k], \langle w_i, x \rangle \le -\gamma \}. \]

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\|f_{n}g_{n}\|_{1}}{\|f_{n}\|_{p}\|g_{n}\|_{q}}=1,
$$
then 
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\left\|\frac{|f_{n}|^{p}}{\|f_{n}\|_p^{p}}-\frac{|g_{n}|^{q}}{\|g_{n}\|_q^{q}}\right\|_1=0.
$$

A dyadic block contains at most O(log m) expected tagged visits, uniformly in n, so its contribution is O(log m*m^(p-1)); this is summable over dyadic scales. For p>1, the same block estimate yields an upper bound O(n^p log n), while the root alone supplies n^p. Check: The dyadic sum is a convergent geometric series when p<1 and is dominated by its largest block when p>1. For complex alpha, absolute tail control uses Re(alpha); this is a bound on expectations, not a complex distributional limit. [Proposition 20 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Let $\varepsilon>0$, let $A, B$ be two bounded self-adjoint operators
on a separable Hilbert space, and $\Pi$ be a projection let ${\rm C}>0$. 
Define for $t\in\R$, 
\[
\mathcal U_t(A) : =  e^{it(\Pi A\Pi)} - \Pi e^{it A}\Pi  . 
\]
Suppose that the following conditions hold:
\[
1)\quad \|\Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le {\rm C}\, ,
\qquad
2)\quad \|[A,B]\| \le \varepsilon\, ,
\qquad
3)\quad
\| \Pi(A-B) (1-\Pi) \|_{\rm tr} \le \varepsilon \, ,
\]
\begin{equation} 
4)\quad \| \Pi B(1-\Pi)  (A-B) \|_{\rm tr}\leq \varepsilon\,,  \qquad  \|(A-B)\Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le \varepsilon   \, .
\end{equation}
Then,  for any $t\in\R$, 
\[
\|\mathcal U_t(A)- \mathcal U_t(B)\|_{\tr}  \leq  \varepsilon |t| (1+ |t|+{\rm C}t^2 )  .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (e_1, e_2, e_3, ...) be a finite or countable orthonormal sequence in an inner product space H. Then for every x in H, the sum over n of |<x, e_n>|^2 converges and satisfies sum over n of |<x, e_n>|^2 <= ||x||^2. (More generally, for an arbitrary orthonormal family {e_i : i in I}, at most countably many coefficients <x, e_i> are nonzero and the same bound holds for the sum over all of them.)

[Theorem 1 (Exact reduction to \texorpdfstring{$L_p$}{Lp}) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] Let \(\mu\) be a probability mass function on \(\{0,1,\dots,n\}\), and define
\[
\widetilde Q_{\mu,p}:=\sum_{u=0}^{n}\mu(n-u)\,\widetilde Q_{n-u,p},
\qquad
S_\mu(\ell):=\sum_{u=0}^{\ell}\mu(n-u)\,u!\,p^u.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\widetilde Q_{\mu,p}(x)}{U(x)}=S_\mu(L_p(x))
\qquad(x\in G_{n,p}),
\]
and, for every \(\Phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) for which the sums are finite,
\[
\sum_{x\in G_{n,p}}U(x)\,
\Phi\!\left(\frac{\widetilde Q_{\mu,p}(x)}{U(x)}\right)
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{n}U\{L_p=\ell\}\,\Phi\!\bigl(S_\mu(\ell)\bigr).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sep(\widetilde Q_{\mu,p},U)=
\begin{cases}
1-\mu(n)-\mu(n-1), & p=1,\\[4pt]
1-\mu(n), & p\ge2,
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
\left\|\frac{\widetilde Q_{\mu,p}(\cdot)}{U(\cdot)}-1\right\|_{L^\infty(U)}
=S_\mu(n)-1
=\sum_{u=0}^{n}\mu(n-u)\,u!\,p^u-1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact reduction to \texorpdfstring{$L_p$}{Lp}

[Theorem thm:vrjp-on-G-r-pos-rec of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] Let $G=(\Lambda,E)$ be a connected undirected graph without self-loops
  and take $l,r\in{\mathbb N}_0$ with $l\le r$.
  Let $(X,T)$ be vrjp in exchangeable time scale on the subdivided graph $G_r$ with
  starting point $\rho\in\Lambda$ and random weights $W_e>0$, $e\in E_r$, with
  respect to some probability measure with corresponding expectation ${\mathbb E}$. Its restriction
  $(X^{\Lambda_l\neq},T^{\Lambda_l\neq})$ to $\Lambda_l$
  with self-loops removed is again a mixture of vrjps on $G_l$ with random
  weights denoted by $W^{(l)}=(W_e^{(l)})_{e\in E_l}$. If the family $W=(W_e)_{e\in E_r}$ is
  independent or i.i.d., then so is the family $W^{(l)}$. Given $W$, the conditional
  law of $W^{(l)}$ can be described in terms of the restriction
  $\beta_{\Lambda_r\setminus\Lambda_l}$ of a $\nu_{\Lambda_r}^W$-distributed
  random field $\beta$. 
  For any finite subgraph $\tilde G$ of $G$ and the corresponding subdivision
  $\tilde G_l=(\tilde\Lambda_l,\tilde E_l)$, the restriction of $W^{(l)}$ to
  $\tilde E_l$ equals $W^{\tilde\Lambda_l}$ given in (equation def:W-J of the paper) with $J=\tilde\Lambda_l$
  and $I=\tilde\Lambda_r\setminus\tilde\Lambda_l$, and
  fulfills the recursion equations described in 
  Lemma (le:aux-W-l-1 of the paper), below. In particular, one has 
  \begin{align}
    
    &P_\rho^{W,\Lambda_r}((X^{\Lambda_l\neq},T^{\Lambda_l\neq})\in\cdot)=\int_{{\mathbb R}^{\Lambda_r}}
      P_\rho^{W^{(l)\neq}(\beta),\Lambda_l}((X,T)\in\cdot)\,
      \nu_{\Lambda_r}^W(d\beta).
  \end{align}
  Assume that the vertex degree of $G$ is bounded by $d$. Moreover, assume
  that the weights $W_e$, $e\in E_r$, are i.i.d.\ and satisfy
  ${\mathbb E}[W_e^\alpha]\le{c_1} 2^{\alpha(r-l)}$ for some $\alpha\in (0,\tfrac14]$
  with the 
  constant ${c_1}(d,\alpha)$ from Fact (fact:sabot-tarres-recurrence of the paper). 
  Then, the process $X^{\Lambda_l\neq}$ is a mixture of positive recurrent
  reversible Markov chains. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Vrjp on subdivided graphs

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2605.28473, 'The BKT transition and surface tension differentiability'] Consider the measure $\BM_{\Gamma,\beta}$.
    Then the following properties hold.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \textbf{Intermediate value theorem.}
            For $\BM_{\Gamma,\beta}$-almost every configuration,
            the following property holds true.
            Let $h$ denote a height function (defined either by choosing a root vertex or
            by imposing boundary conditions).
            If $\gamma\subset\bar\Gamma$ is any continuous path connecting two points
            $x,y\in\bar\Gamma$,
            and if $k\in\Z$ is any integer between $h(x)$ and $h(y)$,
            then there exists a point $z\in\gamma$ such that $h(z)=k$.
        \item \textbf{Markov property.}
            Let $h$ denote a height function (defined either by choosing a root vertex or
            by imposing boundary conditions).
            Then for any closed set $A\subset\bar\Gamma$ with $\partial\Gamma\subset A$
            and with $\Gamma\setminus A$ a finite union of continuum domains, the
            conditional law of $h$ on $\Gamma\setminus A$, given $h|_A$, is
            \begin{equation}
                \bigotimes_{\Gamma'\in\calC(\Gamma\setminus
                A)}\frac1{Z_{\Gamma',\beta}^{h|_{\partial
                \Gamma'}}}\BM_{\Gamma',\beta}^{h|_{\partial \Gamma'}}.
            \end{equation}
    \end{itemize}

[Defi defCBDI of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] \
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item  We call $\mathrm{CBDI}$ any $[0,\infty]$-valued càdlàg Markov process $\big(X, (\mathbb{P}_x)_{x\in [0,\infty]}\big)$, solution to the following martingale problem $\mathrm{MP}\big(\mathcal{X},\mathrm{C}^2_c((0,\infty))\big)$:
\[\forall x\in (0,\infty), \ f\in \mathrm{C}^2_c((0,\infty)), \quad \left(f(X_t)-\int_0^{t}\mathcal{X}f(X_s)\mathrm{d} s,\ t\geq 0 \right) \text{ is a } \mathbb{P}_x\text{ - martingale}.\]
\item  We call minimal and denote by $X^{\mathrm{m}}$, any $\mathrm{CBDI}$ process  whose boundaries $\{0,\infty\}$ are absorbing, namely: 
\[\forall x\in [0,\infty], \ \mathbb{P}_x-\text{a.s.}\  X^{\mathrm{m}}_t=\begin{cases} 0 &\text{ if } t\geq \sigma_0^{-} \text{ and }  \sigma_0^{-}<\sigma_\infty^{+}, \\
\infty  &\text{ if } t\geq \sigma_\infty^{+} \text{ and }  \sigma_\infty^{+}<\sigma_0^{-}.
\end{cases}
\]
\item  For $\Delta\in \{0,\infty\}$, we say that a process $\big(X^{\mathrm{e}\Delta},(\mathbb{P}_x)_{x\in [0,\infty]}\big)$ is a $\mathrm{CBDI}$ extended at $\Delta$, if it is a $[0,\infty]$-valued  Markov process, which once stopped at the boundary $\Delta$, has the same law as the minimal process: namely, if one sets  $\zeta^{\Delta}:=\inf\big\{t\geq 0: X_{t-} \text{ or } X_t =\Delta\big\}$, then one has
\[\forall x\in [0,\infty]\setminus \{\Delta\}, \ \  (X^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_{t\wedge \zeta^{\Delta}},t\geq 0)\overset{\mathrm{law}}{=}(X^{\mathrm{m}}_t,t\geq 0)\ \text{ under } \mathbb{P}_x.\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[-]The process $X^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}$ is said furthermore to be a continuous extension if its boundary $\Delta$ is continuous in the sense of Definition~(def:boundary of the paper)-(def:continuous of the paper). 
\item[-] It is a Fellerian extension of $X^{\mathrm{m}}$ if  its semigroup $(P^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ satisfies for any $f\in \mathsf{C}([0,\infty])$,
    $P^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_tf(x) \underset{t\rightarrow 0+}{\rightarrow} f(x),\ x\in [0,\infty]$ 	and $P^{\mathrm{e}\Delta}_tf \in \mathsf{C}([0,\infty])$.
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
title: Defi defCBDI of arXiv:2605.06488

[Theorem thm:list-robustification of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Let $s\ge1$, put $r=b+s$ and $t=\lfloor(n+b)/r\rfloor$, and perform the same
padding and random partition. Run an ordinary learner independently on each
group and output the pointwise list of its $r$ predictions. If the base
learner has population risk at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least
$1/2$ on a clean group, then the resulting list has risk greater than
$\varepsilon$ with probability at most $2^{-s}$. Consequently, if
$d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=d$, taking $s=\lceil\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil$ gives list size
$b+O(\log(1/\delta))$ using
$O((d/\varepsilon)(b+\log(1/\delta)))$ clean examples.

[Cor fixedfactor of arXiv:2607.00311, 'Thermal Concentration and Poisson--Dirichlet Edge Statistics for Random-Lattice Gibbs Ense'] Let $L_n$ be distributed according to $\mu_n$ on $\mathbb X_n$.
Let $\gamma>1$ and let $0<c<1$.
Define the primitive Gibbs mass of the $\gamma$--approximate shortest-vector window by
$$
\Pi_{n,c}^{\lambda}(\gamma,L)=
\frac{
\sum_{\bm u\in L_{\operatorname{prim}}^\sharp,\ \|\bm u\|\le\gamma\lambda_1(L)}
 g_{n,c}(\tau_n(\bm u))}
{B_{n,c}(L)}.
$$
Then
$$
\Pi_{n,c}^{\lambda}(\gamma,L_n)\to0
$$
in probability if $c<\gamma^{-2}$, while
$$
\Pi_{n,c}^{\lambda}(\gamma,L_n)\to1
$$
in probability if $c>\gamma^{-2}$ and $c<1$.
This probability is taken with respect to the primitive Gibbs ensemble; the shortest length 
$\lambda_1(L)$ is the usual shortest length of the full lattice, but the sampling measure is primitive.

body:
[Theorem flux phi of arXiv:2411.10296, 'Parking on a random rooted binary tree'] Let $T$ be a GW tree with offspring distribution $\nu$. Consider the parking process of cars arriving independently at each vertex of $T$ according to the distribution $\gamma$. If $\mu \leq 1$ and $\sigma^2$ respectively are the mean and variance of $\gamma$, and if $\Sigma^2$ is the variance of the critical (mean 1) offspring distribution $\nu$, we let
    \begin{equation}
        \Phi \coloneq (1-\mu)^2-\Sigma^2(\sigma^2+\mu^2-\mu).
    \end{equation}
    We then have
    \[
        \phi(T_n) \quad \begin{cases}
    \text{converges in distribution} & \Phi>0 \\ \rightarrow\infty, 
    \text{ but is } o_\mathds{P}(n) & \Phi=0 \\ \approx cn & \Phi<0
    \end{cases} \quad \text{ as } n \rightarrow \infty
    \]
    where $\phi$ is defined as the flux of the parking process on the tree, i.e. the number of cars leaving the tree through the root and $c=c(\gamma,\nu) \in (0,\mu)$ is a deterministic number. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Curien and Hénard \cite{flux}

body:
Let U ⊂ C be open and F a family of holomorphic functions on U. F is normal (in the finite sense) if every sequence in F has a subsequence converging uniformly on every compact subset of U; the limit is then automatically holomorphic, and it need not belong to F. F is normal in the extended sense if every sequence in F has a subsequence which, on each connected component of U, either converges uniformly on compact subsets to a holomorphic function or tends to ∞ uniformly on compact subsets (equivalently, the reciprocals tend to 0 uniformly on compact subsets). For families of meromorphic functions, normality means that every sequence has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets with respect to the chordal metric of the Riemann sphere; restricted to holomorphic families this coincides with the extended sense, because a spherical limit of zero-free reciprocals is, by Hurwitz's theorem, either holomorphic or identically ∞ on each component. Normality is a local property: F is normal on U if and only if every point of U has a neighborhood on which F is normal. Normality asserts the existence of convergent subsequences only; it does not assert convergence of the family itself, and the limit function may leave the family (for instance the limit of injective functions may be constant).
U ⊂ C is open
all members of the family are holomorphic (respectively meromorphic) on the same open set U

[Definition def.optimal_se of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n) \in (0,1]^n$.
    A sequence of

body:
[Proposition 14 (Filtered BCH and the initial ancestry symbol) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let \(A:V\to V\) be linear and write \(L(A)\) for its functorial action
on \(L\).  Then
\[
 L(A)\gamma_r(D)\subseteq\gamma_r(D),
 \qquad
 [\gamma_r(D),\gamma_s(D)]\subseteq\gamma_{r+s}(D).
\]
Consequently every truncation in ordinary tensor degree is nilpotent and
filtered for
\(F_0L=L\), \(F_rL=L\cap J^r=\gamma_r(D)\).  It therefore defines BCH
laws on the ordinary-degree completions of \({\operatorname{gr}}_FL\) and of the extended
Rees Lie algebra
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_F(L):=
 \sum_{r\geq0}F_rL\,z^{-r}\mathbf k[z]
 \subseteq L[z,z^{-1}],
 \qquad
 \mathcal R_F(L)/z\mathcal R_F(L)\cong{\operatorname{gr}}_FL,
 
\end{equation}
Reduction modulo \(z\) records the associated-graded deformation.  If
\(x\in F_rL\setminus F_{r+1}L\),
its full initial symbol is the nonzero class
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{in}^{\mathrm{full}}_F(x)
 :=x+F_{r+1}L\in{\mathfrak L}_r(Q).
 
\end{equation}
Thus filtration order cannot decrease under linear transport (with the
value \(+\infty\) if the transported element vanishes), and
\begin{equation}
 \nu_F([x,y])\geq\nu_F(x)+\nu_F(y)
 
\end{equation}
for nonzero \(x,y\), with the convention \(\nu_F(0)=+\infty\).  Exact
valuation is preserved
by transport precisely when the induced associated-graded map does not kill
the initial symbol; injectivity of that map on the containing graded layer
is sufficient.  Likewise,
equality holds in \eqref{cc:eq-valuation-superadditive} precisely when
the associated-graded bracket of the two initial symbols is nonzero.
Otherwise transport,
bracketing, cancellation in a sum, or a BCH component may raise the order
or annihilate the element.  A full Rees lift of a causal logarithm requires
a Rees jet or a splitting and is not supplied canonically by the filtration.

In the ordinary-degree completion, exponentiation identifies the special
fibre with
\begin{equation}
 \exp\!\left(V_{\mathrm{ab}}\ltimes_\rho\widehat{{\mathfrak L}}(Q)\right).
 
\end{equation}
Here
\(\widehat{{\mathfrak L}}(Q)=\prod_{n\geq1}{\mathfrak L}(Q)_n\) denotes completion in
ordinary tensor degree.
Moreover, the associated-graded bracket induces
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak b_{a,b}:G^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,a}(V)\otimes
 G^{\mathrm{full}}_{m,b}(V)
 \longrightarrow G^{\mathrm{full}}_{n+m,a+b}(V),
 \qquad \mathfrak b_{a,b}([x],[y])=[x,y],
 
\end{equation}
and this is the mixed quadratic symbol of BCH:
\begin{equation}
 \left.\partial_s\partial_t\right|_{s=t=0}
 {\operatorname{BCH}}(sx,ty)=\tfrac12[x,y].
 
\end{equation}
If the three layers in \eqref{cc:eq-ancestry-bracket} are finite
dimensional, duality gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak b_{a,b}^{\vee}:E^{\mathrm{full}}_{n+m,a+b}(V)
 \longrightarrow E^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,a}(V)\otimes
 E^{\mathrm{full}}_{m,b}(V).
 
\end{equation}

[Lem switch_k of arXiv:2604.07183, 'Stopping on the last success with unknown odds: asymptotic minimax optimality of the plug-'] Let~$k\ge2$ and~$n\ge k$, write~$t_k:=n-k+1$ for the first time of the oracle
window associated with~$m(p)=k$, and let $\pi$ be a (possibly randomized)
\mbox{$p$-blind} rule, with corresponding stopping time
$\tau_n^\pi=\tau_n^\pi(X_1,\ldots,X_n,U)$, where the auxiliary random
variable~$U$ realizes the possible internal randomization. Then,

(i) for any $p\in(\frac{1}{k+1},\frac1k)$,
$$
V_n(p)-W_n^\pi(p)
\ge
k(1-p)^{k-2}\Bigl(\frac1k-p\Bigr)
\,\mathbb P_p[X_{t_k}=1,\tau_n^\pi\geq t_k+1];
$$

(ii) for any $p\in(\frac1k,\frac{1}{k-1})$,
$$
V_n(p)-W_n^\pi(p)
\ge
k(1-p)^{k-2}\Bigl(p-\frac1k\Bigr)
\,\mathbb P_p[X_{t_k}=1,\tau_n^\pi=t_k]
.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem switch_k of arXiv:2604.07183

body: An element a of an extension field L of K is algebraic over K if it is a root of some nonzero polynomial in K[x]; its minimal polynomial is the monic generator of the ideal of polynomials vanishing at a. The extension L/K is algebraic if every element of L is algebraic over K. A finite extension (finite degree [L:K]) is algebraic; conversely a finitely generated algebraic extension is finite.
title: Algebraic Extension

body:
Let a Galton-Watson tree have iid offspring nu>=2 almost surely, finite mean m>1, and lambda in (0,m). Give each child weight 1 and the parent weight lambda, with an artificial reflecting parent above the root. Let beta(x) be the quenched probability of never hitting x's parent from x, and let beta_i, i>=0, be iid copies of the root beta, independent of nu. Then the deterministic speed is E[(nu-lambda) beta_0/(lambda-1+sum_{i=0}^nu beta_i)] divided by E[(nu+lambda) beta_0/(lambda-1+sum_{i=0}^nu beta_i)]. The conductance law obeys beta=S/(lambda+S), S=sum_{i=1}^nu beta_i. This is the no-leaf, minimum-offspring-at-least-two specialization of Aidekon, arXiv:1111.4313v4, Theorem 1.1; all conductances and the displayed denominators are positive. The source theorem treats a broader positive-speed regime, which is deliberately not included in this card.

finite mean m>1
0<lambda<m
parent weight lambda, each child weight 1

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Any family of commuting normal operators $T_i\in B(H)$ can be jointly diagonalized,
$$T_i=U^*M_{f_i}U$$
with $U:H\to L^2(X)$ being a unitary operator from $H$ to a certain $L^2$ space associated to $\{T_i\}$, with $f_i:X\to\mathbb C$ being certain functions, once again associated to $T_i$, and with
$$M_{f_i}(g)=f_ig$$
being the usual multiplication operator by $f_i$, on the Hilbert space $L^2(X)$.

[Proposition prop: inner product relation of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] Let \( x_1, x_2, x_3 \in {\mathbb{S}^{n-1} } \) be such that \( \left\langle{x_1, x_2}\right\rangle = \left\langle{x_1, x_3}\right\rangle = c \) and \( \left\langle{x_2, x_3}\right\rangle = r \). For \( i = 2, 3 \), we can write
\[
x_i = c x_1 + \sqrt{1 - c^2} y_i,
\]
where \( y_i = \frac{x_i - c x_1}{\|x_i - c x_1\|_2} \) satisfies \( \left\langle{y_i, x_1}\right\rangle = 0 \) and
\[
\left\langle{y_2, y_3}\right\rangle = f_c(r),
\]
with \( f_c(r) = \frac{r - c^2}{1 - c^2} \).

[Prop 48 of arXiv:2603.00353, 'Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups'] Let $n\ge3$ and let $\Gamma=([n],w)$ be a hypergraph with non-negative weights supported on subsets of size $n-1$. For every $k\in\Z_{\ge1}$ consider the $n\times n$ matrix\marginpar{$M_k$}
    \[
        M_k\defi \left(\sum_{x\in[n]}c_x\right)I_n-\begin{pmatrix}
            c_1& &&\\
            &c_2&&\\
            &&\ddots&\\
            &&&c_n
        \end{pmatrix} 
        \left(I_n+\frac{(-1)^k}{\binom{n+k-2}{k}}\left(J_n-I_n\right)\right).
    \]
    Then the spectrum of $\L(\Gamma,\rho_{(k,0,\ldots,0,-k)})$ consists of the eigenvalues of $M_k$ together with copies of $\sum c_x$.

[Prop 17 of arXiv:2604.13387, 'Multiradial Schramm-Loewner evolution: \\ Infinite-time large deviations and transience'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,8/3]$ and $n \ge 2$. 
There exists a constant $C_n(\kappa) \in (0,\infty)$ depending only on $\kappa$ and $n$ such that for 
$\vee > 2n + 2\log(4) +  \frac{\log(n)}{2}$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\Pr^\kappa [ \xescapeevent{j}{\u}{\vee} ]  \le C_n(\kappa) \, \exp\Big(\tfrac{(\u-\vee)(8-\kappa)}{2\kappa}\Big) , \qquad
0 < \u < \vee - \tfrac{\log(n)}{2}  - \log(4) - n - 1 
, \; j \in \{1,\ldots,n\}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    There exists $L > 0$ so that the following is true. Let $\{e_{i}\}_{i\leq n}$ be a $1$-unconditional sequence in a Banach space $(X, \norm{\cdot})$, and let $S = \mathbb{E}\left[\norm{\sum_{i=1}^{n}g_{i}e_{i}} \right],$ where $\{g_{i}\}_{i \leq n}$ are independent standard Gaussian random variables. [Lemma key_lemma_delocalized_eigenvector of arXiv:2504.00512, 'Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model at the edge'] Take $z=E+\mathrm{i} \eta\in \mathbf D\left({\tau}\right)$ with $E=\gamma_k\in \qa{E^{-},E^+}$ and $\eta\sim N^{-2/3+\varepsilon_L}k^{-1/3}$ for a small constant $\varepsilon_L>0$ (recall that we assume $k\in[\![{1,DN/2}]\!]$). Under the assumptions of (mix of the paper), there exists a constant $c_L>0$ (depending on $\varepsilon_L,\delta_A,\varepsilon_A$) such that 
\begin{equation}
\max_{z_1,z_2\in\{z,\overline z\}}\max_{a,b\in [\![{D}]\!]}\left|\left(\mathbb{E} L_{(1,2)}- K_{(1,2)}\right)_{ab}\right|
=\mathrm{O}\pa{N^{-1-c_L}\eta^{-2}} .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma key_lemma_delocalized_eigenvector of arXiv:2504.00512

[Lemma lem:two_locally_large_clusters of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] Suppose that $d=3\alpha$ and that the modified hydrodynamic condition does not hold. For each $\eta>0$ there exists a positive constant $c_1$ such that if $M_r\geq \eta r^{2\alpha}$ then
\[
  \mathbb E_{\beta,r}\left[ \sum_{y\in B_r} \mathbbm{1}(0\nleftrightarrow y) |K_y| \mathbbm{1}\!\left(|K \cap B_{2r}| \geq  c_1 r^{2\alpha} \right)\right] \geq c_1 r^{3\alpha}.
\]
title: Lemma lem:two_locally_large_clusters of arXiv:2508.18809

[Theorem 44 of arXiv:2609.02826, '2609.02826'] Let $S$ be a connected Dedekind scheme with generic point $\generic$, and
let $N$ be a proper flat finitely presented group algebraic space over $S$
whose generic fibre is an abelian variety.  Then $N$ is a commutative
projective group scheme.  The global \Neron{} model $A$ of $N_\generic$ is an
abelian scheme, and the generic identity extends to a finite normalization
map
\[
  u:A\longrightarrow N.
\]
For every $S$-ample invertible sheaf $\cL$ on $N$, the polarization
construction gives an exact sequence
\[
  0\longrightarrow F_\cL\longrightarrow N
  \xrightarrow{q_\cL}A^\vee\longrightarrow0
\]
with $F_\cL$ finite locally free.

[Lemma lem:wasser_converg of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $\bm{X}$ be a L\'evy process and $\bm{Z}$ be a standard normal random vector with $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^2]<\infty$. 
Then, for any $q \in [1,2]$, the limit $\lim_{t \to \infty}\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}_t/\sqrt{t},\bm{Z})=0$ is equivalent to $\bm{X}_t/\sqrt{t} \xrightarrow{d} \bm{Z}$ as $t \to \infty$.

[Lemma lemma2-1 of arXiv:2609.00627, 'Global well-posedness of radially symmetric strong solutions to two-dimensional compressib'] Let $\Omega$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Then,  for any $ q>2$, there is a positive constant $C_q$ depending on $q$ and $\Omega$, such that for any functions $\boldsymbol{u}:\Omega\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^2$ with $ \boldsymbol{u}\cdot\boldsymbol{n}|_{\partial \Omega}=0\text{ or } \int_{\Omega} u_i dx=0, i=1,2$, and $\nabla\boldsymbol{u}\in L^{\frac{2q}{q+2}}(\Omega)$, we have
	\begin{equation}
		{\Vert \boldsymbol{u} \Vert}_{L^q(\Omega)} \le C_q{\Vert \nabla \boldsymbol{u} \Vert}_{L^{\frac{2q}{q+2}}(\Omega)}  . 
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2605.21005, 'Double-transform Tauberian method\\ for precise large deviations'] Let $(f_\lambda(s))_{\lambda> 0}$ be a family of functions where $f_\lambda:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ for each $\lambda> 0$.  Let $(s_\lambda)_{\lambda> 0}$ be such that $s_\lambda \to 0$ as $\lambda\to 0$. The following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item 
$ \displaystyle
\lim_{\lambda\to 0} \sup_{0<s\leq s_\lambda} f_\lambda(s)=0.
$
\item For any $(\tilde s_\lambda)_{\lambda> 0}$ such that $\tilde s_\lambda\leq s_\lambda$ for all $\lambda> 0$, we have
$ \displaystyle
\lim_{\lambda\to 0}f_\lambda(\tilde s_\lambda)=0.
$
\end{enumerate}

In the normalized common-Hessian RR model f_i=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y, fix n>=2, deterministic x0!=0,y0, and zero-sum linear terms with mean squares s1>=0,s2>0. The globally minimized expected final-epoch error is asymptotic to (x0^2/2)*exp(-4*T/kappa_T). Every global minimizing constant-step sequence satisfies T*(eta_T-2/kappa_T)->0.
