 Xold=P/(sqrt(V)+rho)-X,
 Pold=((1-b)Xold-P)/b,
 Vold=(V-(1-d)Xold^2)/d.                                  (7)
As long as a backward state has X>=X_w>a, P>=cX and 0<=V<a^2,
sqrt(V)+rho<c/2. Thus
 Xold>2P/c-X>=P/c>=X,
 Pold>=c Xold,
 Vold<=V.
For the momentum inequality use 1-b-bc=c: Pold>=cXold is equivalent
to cXold>=P. If Vold remains nonnegative these conditions propagate.
With L=X_w^2 and the initial witness variance V_w<L, one also has
 V_(-j)<=L+d^(-j)(V_w-L).                                 (8)
The right side becomes strictly negative at some finite j. Thus w has
NO sufficiently long backward history with nonnegative variances.
The inverse in (7) remains continuous at V=0 because rho>0; a zero
intermediate variance does not evade the strict-negative conclusion
at the next step. Equations (5)-(8) are algebraic inequalities; exact
checks are in scripts/check_backward_cone.py, not floating-point bounds.

Fix this rho and let k be one finite length excluded by (8). This k
may depend on rho; uniform k as rho->0 is unnecessary. Near w and clocks0,
let A_k be the set of augmented states with a physical k-step backward
history, meaning every recovered variance is nonnegative. Restrict clocks
so dividing them by b^k,d^k still leaves them strictly below1. For the
corrected inverse, first recover alpha_old=alpha/b,sigma_old=sigma/d,
undo R on X,M, then use
 Xold=-X-M/[(1-alpha_old)(sqrt(V/(1-sigma_old))+rho)],
 Mold=(-M-(1-b)Xold)/b,
 Vold=(V-(1-d)Xold^2)/d.                                  (9)
These inverses are unique and continuous on the closed nonnegative-
variance domain, including V=0. The set A_k is closed locally: if a
sequence of such histories has convergent output states, recursively
applying (9) makes all k preceding states converge with nonnegative
variances. Denominators stay nonzero by rho>0 and the clock restriction.
Since w is not in A_k, it has an open neighborhood disjoint from A_k.

The selected point on W_(alpha,sigma) with X=X_w varies analytically
with the clocks and tends to w as they vanish. Hence for all sufficiently
small positive clocks this fiber contains a point outside A_k. At time
n the actual clocks are alpha_n=b^(n+1),sigma_n=d^(n+1). For every
sufficiently large n>=k, this selected point cannot lie on Gamma_n,
the finite image of the standard initial line: every state in Gamma_n
has its actual n-step physical history, in particular a k-step one.
The same witness construction at the negative phase follows by reflection.

	\end{equation}

		\d_t \eta + \div_x (\eta \Bi) + \d_z \eta = 0.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

		positive number $\lambda >0$.
		In particular, 
		if \( \phi_{\mathcal{E}}(1) = 1 \), then \( {\mathcal{E}} = L_1({\mathcal M}, \tau)_h   \) with equality of norms.

body: The Ising model, named after the physicists Ernst Ising and Wilhelm Lenz, is a mathematical model of ferromagnetism in statistical mechanics. The model consists of discrete variables that represent magnetic dipole moments of atomic "spins" that can be in one of two states. The spins are arranged in a graph, usually a lattice, allowing each spin to interact with its neighbors. Neighboring spins that agree have a lower energy than those that disagree; the system tends to the lowest energy but heat disturbs this tendency, thus creating the possibility of different structural phases. The two-dimensional square-lattice Ising model is one of the simplest statistical models to show a phase transition. Though it is a highly simplified model of a magnetic material, the Ising model can still provide qualitative and sometimes quantitative results applicable to real physical systems, and in general, it can be seen as a specialization of Stanley's n-vector model for n = 1.
title: Ising model

[Lemma 2 (The transference principle) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] For $m\in\N$, let $(X_1,\mu_{X_1}),\dots, (X_m,\mu_{X_m})$ be Polish measure spaces. Let $c \colon X_1 \times\cdots \times X_m \to (-\infty,\infty)$ be a continuous cost function. Fix $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m \in (0,1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1$.

Consider collections, for $i=1,\dots,m$, $\mathcal{C}_{X_i}$ of $\mu_{X_i}$-measurable subsets of $X_i$. Let $a,b\in \R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ be such that for all non-empty $A_i\in \mathcal{C}_{X_i}$, $\sup_{\substack{x_i\in A_i \\ 1\leq i \leq m}} -c(x_1,\dots,x_m) \in [a,b]$ and consider a continuous, non-decreasing function $F \colon (a,b]\to [0,\infty)$ satisfying $F(a^+)=0$.

Then, the following are equivalent:\begin{enumerate}
    \item For every non-empty $A_1\in \mathcal{C}_{X_1},\dots,A_m\in\mathcal{C}_{X_m}$, one has
    \[
\prod_{i=1}^m\mu_{X_i}(A_i)^{\lambda_i} \leq F\left(\sup_{\substack{x_i\in A_i \\ 1\leq i \leq m}} -c(x_1,\dots,x_m) \right).
\]
\item For every $(m+1)$-tuple of measurable functions $f_1 \in \mathcal{F}(\mathcal{C}_{X_1}),\dots, f_m\in \mathcal{F}\left(\mathcal{C}_{X_m}\right)$ and $\Omega \colon (a,b]  \to [0,\infty)$, where $\Omega$ is non-increasing, that satisfy
\begin{align*}
\prod_{i=1}^mf_i(x_i)^{\lambda_i} &\leq \Omega(-c(x_1,\dots,x_m)) \text{ for all } 
\\
&(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in X_1\times\cdots\times  X_m, \text{ with } -c(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in (a,b],
\end{align*}
one has
\[
\prod_{i=1}^m\left(\int_{X_i} f_i(x) d\mu_{X_i}(x) \right)^{{\lambda_i}} \leq \int_{a}^b \Omega(r) dF(r).
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The transference principle

body: In computability theory, the halting problem is the decision problem of, given an arbitrary computer program and an input, determining whether said program will eventually finish running and halt, or will continue to run forever. Alan Turing proved in 1937 that the halting problem is undecidable, meaning that no general algorithm exists that can correctly solve the problem for all possible program–input pairs. The problem comes up often in discussions of computability since it demonstrates that some functions are mathematically definable but not computable.
title: Halting problem

body: [Lemma 9 of arXiv:2512.02538, 'On the spectral geometry of Liouville quantum gravity'] Almost surely, $\mathbf{G}$ is a nonnegative operator on $L^2 (\mu_\ph)$. That is, almost surely, for all $f \in L^2 ( \mu_\ph)$ we have $\langle f, \mathbf{G}f \rangle_{L^2(\mu_\ph)} \ge 0$. In particular all the eigenvalues $\bmu_n $ of $\mathbf{G}$ are nonnegative. Furthermore, $\ker (\mathbf{G}) = 0$ a.s., thus $\bmu_n >0$ for all $n\ge 0$, a.s.

[Lemma lem:arrangement of arXiv:2608.28004, 'Hausdorff Dimension of the Set of Extreme Points\\ of a Random Countable Stable Zonotope'] Let \(\mathcal D\subset\mathbb R^N\) be convex and let
\(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m\) be affine functions on \(\mathbb R^N\). The partition of
\(\mathcal D\) into nonempty level sets of the vector-valued map
\[
    t\longmapsto\bigl(\1_{\{\ell_1(t)>0\}},\ldots,
    \1_{\{\ell_m(t)>0\}}\bigr)
\]
has at most \(C_N(m+1)^N\) members. We call these sets \emph{sign strata};
the count includes strata contained in the hyperplanes
\(\{\ell_j=0\}\) themselves. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: number of sign strata

body: In mathematics, an elliptic curve is a smooth, projective, algebraic curve of genus one, on which there is a specified point O. An elliptic curve is defined over a field K and describes points in K^{2}, the Cartesian product of K with itself. If the field's characteristic is different from 2 and 3, then the curve can be described as a plane algebraic curve which consists of solutions (x, y) for: $$y^{2}=x^{3}+ax+b$$

[Theorem 43 of arXiv:2609.03736, '2609.03736'] For this specialization, write
\[
 u_N=u(\eta_N,\gamma_N),\qquad v_N=v(\eta_N,\gamma_N).
\]
Then
\begin{align}
 u_N&=\frac1N\cot\frac{\pi}{2N},
 \\
 v_N&=\frac1N\csc\frac{\pi}{2N},
 \\
 \mathcal J(G_N,P_N)&=\frac1{2N}\cot\frac{\pi}{4N}.
 
\end{align}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal J(G_N,P_N)\uparrow\frac2\pi,
 \qquad
 \frac2\pi-\mathcal J(G_N,P_N)
 =\frac{\pi}{24N^2}+O(N^{-4}).
 
\end{equation}

body:
[Corollary 3 (Finite-window rate form) of arXiv:2604.07750, 'A finite-sample Borel--Cantelli inequality under $m$-dependence'] Let $(A_k)_{k\geq1}$ be an $m$-dependent sequence of events and let
\(\phi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\) be a non-decreasing function with
\[
  \sum_{k=1}^{\phi(n)} \mathbb{P}(A_k)\ge n
  \qquad\text{for all } n\ge 1.
\]
Then for every integer $N\ge1$ and all $i\ge0$,
\[
  \mathbb{P}\Bigl( \bigcup_{k=i+1}^{\phi(i+N)} A_k \Bigr)
  \ge 1 - \exp\Bigl(-\frac{N}{m+1}\Bigr).
\]

body:
[Lem 117 (temporal smoothing of budget constraint) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Analogously to \eqref{e:budget.constraint.Ising.plus.coarse} and the bound from Lemma~\ref{l:sp.smooth.budget}, with high probability we have 
	\begin{align*}
	\breve{C}^N(t)
	- \frac{\bar{W}^N(t)^2}{\alpha} 
	\le
	\bigg(\frac{\trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2 \TMAX_N \tep^{1/2}
	+ 3\epsilon^\circ
	\end{align*}
for all $t\in[q_*,1]$. Additionally, with $J^N\equiv J(p^N,\tep,\lambda)$ as  defined by \eqref{e:bad.times.J}, we have
	\[
	\Big|\breve{C}^N(t)
	-\bar{C}^N(t)
	\Big|
	\le \bigg(\frac{ \trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2
	\lambda^{1/2}
	\]
for all $t\in[q_*,1] \setminus J^N$.

\begin{proof}
We continue to use the abbreviations introduced above. The function $\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}$ is convex on the expanded domain $\{(b,v,u) : v \ge u^2-2\bar{\lambda}\}$. Recall $\tGam^N\equiv(\tbbb,\tvvv,\tuuu)^N$
and $\TGam^N\equiv(\Tbbb,\Tvvv,\Tuuu)^N$: we have from Lemma~\ref{l:t.smooth.domain} that
(with high probability)
 $\TGam^N(t,y)$ lies in the expanded domain for all $(t,y)\in[q_*,1]\times \R$, while
$\tGam^N(t,y)$ lies in the expanded domain for all $(t,y)\in ([q_*,1]\setminus J^N)\times \R$. Lemma~\ref{l:t.smooth.domain} implies, for $(t,y)\in ([q_*,1]\setminus J^N)\times \R$,
	\[
	\bigg|
	\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}
	\Big( \tGam^N(t,y)\Big)
	-\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}
	\Big( \TGam^N(t,y)\Big)
	\bigg|
	\le
	\bigg(\frac{ \trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2
	\lambda^{1/2}\,.
	\]
Integrating with respect to $\overline{\varrho_{\vY,N,t}*\sphi(y)}\,dy$ proves the second conclusion. For all $(t,y)\in[q_*,1]\times\R$, we can bound
	\begin{align*}
	& \Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}
	\Big(\TGam^N(t,y)\Big)
	=
	\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}\bigg( \tE \Big[\sGam(t-\sss,y)\Big]\bigg) \\
	&\qquad\le \tE\bigg[
	\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}\Big( \sGam(t-\sss,y)\Big)\bigg]
	= \int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}( \sGam(s,y) )\,ds\,.
	\end{align*}
Integrating with respect to $\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)\,dy$ gives
	\begin{align*}
	&\breve{C}^N(t)
	=
	\int_{\R} \Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}\Big(\TGam^N(t,y)\Big)
	\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)\,dy
	\le
	\int_{\R}
	\bigg[
	 \int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}( \sGam(s,y) )\,ds\bigg]
	\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)\,dy \\
	&\qquad=
	\int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\bigg[\int_{\R}
	\Cost_{2\bar{\lambda}}( \sGam(s,y) )
	\overline{\varrho_s*\sphi(y)} \,dy\bigg]\,ds
	+O\bigg[ \bigg(\frac{\trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2 \TMAX_N
	\tep^{1/2}\bigg]\\
	&\qquad=
	\int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\tilde{C}^N(s)\,ds
	+O\bigg[ \bigg(\frac{\trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2 \TMAX_N
	\tep^{1/2}\bigg]
	\,,
	\end{align*}
where the error estimate uses the bounds on $\sGam=(\sbbb,\svvv,\suuu)$ proved in Lemma~\ref{l:sp.smooth.reg}, along with the regularity of the map $t\mapsto \overline{\varrho_s*\sphi}$ proved in Lemma~\ref{l:sp.smooth.cty}. 
 Similarly, note that
	\[
	S_t(w)
	\equiv
	\bigg( \int_{\R} w(y)^{1/2} \varsigma_t*\sphi(y)\,dy\bigg)^2
	\]
is a concave function. It follows that
	\begin{align*}
	&\bar{W}^N(t)^2 
	=\bigg(\int_{\R} \twww(t,y)^{1/2} \varsigma_t*\sphi(y)\,dy\bigg)^2
	= S_t\bigg(\tE\Big[ \swww(t-\sss,\cdot)\Big]\bigg)
	\ge \tE\bigg[ S_t\Big( \swww(t-\sss,\cdot)\Big)\bigg]\\
	&\qquad= \int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\bigg( \int_{\R} \swww(s,y)^{1/2} 
		\varsigma_t*\sphi(y)\,dy\bigg)^2\,ds\\
	&\qquad=
	\int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\bigg( \int_{\R} \swww(s,y)^{1/2} 
		\varsigma_s*\sphi(y)\,dy\bigg)^2
	\,ds
	+
	O\bigg[ \bigg(\frac{\trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2 \TMAX_N \tep^{1/2}\bigg]
	\\
	&\qquad=
	\int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\tilde{W}^N(s)^2\,ds
	+
	O\bigg[ \bigg(\frac{\trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2 \TMAX_N \tep^{1/2}\bigg]
	\end{align*}
where the error estimate again follows from Lemmas \ref{l:sp.smooth.reg} and \ref{l:sp.smooth.cty}. The claim then follows by combining with
Lemma~\ref{l:sp.smooth.budget}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The estimator, per output coordinate: form the error covariance of the ensemble members in the per-sample relative metric (case weights $1/\|y_i\|^2$), replace its sample eigenvalues by the Ledoit-Peche nonlinear-shrinkage values (floored at a small fraction of the bulk level), and take the long-only minimum-variance weights $\arg\min_w w^T \Xi w$ subject to $w \ge 0$, $\mathbf{1}^T w = 1$, with the intercept closing the weighted mean error. Nothing in it is cross-validated. Measured on the EMIT lookup-table pool (seed 101, 23 members, 932 calibration rows): on the two components where regularisation matters it is the best estimator found - Y2 $0.1126$ against least squares $0.1292$ ($+12.9$ percent) and against the pool's cross-validated best heuristic $0.1186$ ($+5.1$ percent), Y4 $1.7559$ against $1.8981$ / $1.8340$ ($+7.5$ / $+4.3$ percent) - and it beats the same cleaned estimator with a cross-validated shrink toward the pooled simplex weights ($0.1141$ / $1.7716$) on both; on the easy component (Y1, where shrinking had nothing to give) it is within 3 percent. It keeps 7 to 11 of the 23 members active. The reading: the residual gain that the pool's heuristic obtained by interpolating toward the pooled simplex weights was the nonnegativity constraint, which by Jagannathan-Ma is an implicit shrinkage of the covariance with a data-determined amount; combined with the objective correction (the relative metric) and the spectral cleaning (nonlinear shrinkage), every ingredient of the heuristic is now a derived step. Three cells of one seed at the time of writing; the seventy-cell population test on both corpora was running.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare the invasion cluster two-point function with the IIC two-point function and locate the difference. Result: The IIC two-point function P_IIC(x in cluster) is asymptotic to A' |x|^{-(d-4)} in high dimensions (from the lace expansion of the IIC, Hofstad-Jarai), and the invasion percolation cluster is expected to have the same decay exponent because the invasion cluster near infinity looks like a critical cluster with a slightly supercritical 'ponds' structure at scales below the current pond size. The source notes that the IIC and IPC have different scaling limits on the tree (Angel-Goodman-den Hollander-Slade), so the constants A and A' differ and the exponent may agree. A rigorous bound: since the invasion cluster contains the IIC-like structure... no inclusion holds in either direction. The ponds structure: invasion percolation on Z^d invades the cluster of the origin at level p_c + eps_k where eps_k decreases to 0 along the pond sequence; the probability that x at distance r is invaded is roughly the probability that x lies in the p_c + eps(r) cluster of the origin restricted to the ball of radius r, with eps(r) the level at scale r; in high dimensions eps(r) ~ r^{-2} (mean-field correlation length exponent 1/2), and P_{p_c + r^{-2}}(0 <-> x, |x| = r) is of order r^{-(d-2)} times the number of extra connections... a computation via the slightly supercritical two-point function gives P(x in IPC) ~ r^{-(d-2)} x (number of vertices at distance about r in the cluster)/... I could not make this precise; the mean-field prediction of the exponent d-4 comes from the IIC analogy. Not resolved; the reduction is to a slightly supercritical two-point function estimate at p_c + r^{-2} with matching constants, which is a Problem 11.1-type supercritical quantity. Obstruction: Requires slightly supercritical two-point asymptotics with constants (C0065-type input).
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0085-two-point-function-of-high-dimensional-invasion-percolation
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved
title: Attempt on Two-point function of high-dimensional invasion percolation

[Proposition prop:5.4 of arXiv:2607.06785, 'On the smallest singular value of the product of random and deterministic matrices'] Let \(A\) be an \(n\times n\) random matrix with i.i.d.\ \(\mathcal N(0,1)\)
entries, and let \(M\) be a fixed invertible \(n\times n\) matrix. Then there
exist absolute constants \(c_{{\color{blue}5.4}},\varepsilon_{{\color{blue}5.4}}>0\) such that for
every \(n\geqslant2\) and every \(0\leqslant\varepsilon\leqslant \varepsilon_{{\color{blue}5.4}}\),
\[
  \mathbb{P}\!\left(
    s_{\min}(MA)\leqslant \frac{\varepsilon}{\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}}
  \right)
  \geqslant c_{{\color{blue}5.4}}\varepsilon.
\]

    \sum_{n\geq 1} n^{a_4} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( 1 \wedge e^{-a_1(v-a_2n)} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright) e^{-a_3un^\kappa}

    \]

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] \label[lemma]{induction}
    Let $\mathcal{O}, L, \Delta$
    be as in the statement
    of (decomposition of the paper), and
    assume $L \ge (\Delta + 1)4Q\rho r|\log r| + 2r$,
    $r$ satisfies
    (equation r small enough of the paper), and
    the event $A_{Q,\rho}(r)$ holds.
    To reduce clutter, 
    write $K = 4Q \rho r|\log r|$.

    Suppose we are given $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{O}$,
    $z \in Z_1(\mathring{G}^n_M(r))$,
    and $\sigma \in C_2(M)$
    such that the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\partial \sigma = z$.
        \item For any $x \in |\sigma|$,
        there exists
        $V \in \mathcal{O} \setminus \mathcal{D}$
        such that 
        \[
            \bar{B}(x, L - d(x)K)
            \subseteq V,
        \]
        where we define
        \[
            d(x) := 
            \sup \left\{ m : 
            \begin{array}{c}
            \exists U_1,...,U_m \in \mathcal{D} \mbox{ distinct, } x_1,...,x_m, x_{m+1}\in M \\
            \mbox{
            with } x_{m+1}=x, \mbox{ such that for all } 1 \le i \le m, \\
            x_i \in U_i
            \mbox{ and }
            d_M(x_i, x_{i+1}) \le K 
            \end{array}
            \right\}.
        \]
    \end{enumerate}

    Then, for any $W \in \mathcal{O} \setminus \mathcal{D}$,
    there exist
    $z' \in Z_1(\mathring{G}^n_M(r))$ and
    $\sigma' \in C_2(M)$
    such that,
    setting 
    \[
        \mathcal{D}' = \mathcal{D} \cup \{W\},
    \]
    we have:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $|z - z'| \subseteq W$.
        \item $\partial \sigma' = z'$.
        \item For any $x \in |\sigma'|$,
        there exists
        $V' \in \mathcal{O} \setminus \mathcal{D'}$
        such that 
        \[
            \bar{B}(x, L - d'(x)K)
            \subseteq V',
        \]
        where we define
        \[
            d'(x) := 
            \sup \left\{ m : 
            \begin{array}{c}
            \exists U_1,...,U_m \in \mathcal{D'} \mbox{ distinct, } x_1,...,x_m, x_{m+1}\in M \\
            \mbox{
            with } x_{m+1}=x, \mbox{ such that for all } 1 \le i \le m, \\
            x_i \in U_i
            \mbox{ and }
            d_M(x_i, x_{i+1}) \le K
            \end{array}
            \right\}.
        \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in t'

Let A be a nonempty subset of a finite set B. Then sum over X inside B with X union A = B of (-1)^|X| = 0, so a uniformly random subset X of B, conditioned on X union A = B, has E[(-1)^|X|] = 0. If instead each element of B is put in X independently with probability p in (0, 1], then P(X union A = B) = p^|B minus A| > 0 and E[(-1)^|X| | X union A = B] = (-1)^|B minus A| (1 - 2p)^|A|, which is 0 only at p = 1/2.

[Lemma lem:newGibbs of arXiv:2607.06813, 'Mixing of Glauber Dynamics on High Overlap Gibbs Measures'] Let $X,X'$ be iid draws from the quadratic Gibbs measure $\nu_{J, h}$ (as defined in~(equation eq:Gibbs of the paper)). Define $Z=X-X'$, the disagreement set $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq \{i: X_i \neq X_i'\}$, and $Z_\mathcal{D}$ as the restriction of $Z$ to the coordinates in $\mathcal{D}$.
 It holds that the random variable $\frac12 Z_\mathcal{D} \mid \mathcal{D}$ is distributed according to a Gibbs measure of the form~(equation eq:Gibbs of the paper) with interaction matrix $2J_{\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{D}}$ and zero external field.

body: [Definition def:local-limit of arXiv:2605.01444, 'From second moments to pairwise negative correlation: \\applications to minimal and unifor'] Let $(G_n)_{n\;\geqslant\;1}$ be a sequence of locally finite, connected graphs (possibly random). Choose $\rho_n$ uniformly from $V(G_n)$, independently of each other. We say a random element $(G,\rho)\in \mathcal{G}_\bullet$ is the \textbf{local limit} of $(G_n)_{n\;\geqslant\;1}$ if for every integer $r>0$, the rooted balls $(B_{G_n}(\rho_n,r),\rho_n)$ converge in distribution to $(B_G(\rho,r),\rho)$.
title: Definition def:local-limit of arXiv:2605.01444

    \begin{enumerate}

[Lem convolution-sup-bounds of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Fix $2 \leq r < \infty$ and $\mathcal{B} \coloneqq L^r$. For all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, $\epsilon \in (0,1/2)$, $p > \epsilon^{-1}$, $T > 0$ the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item For $y \in L^p([0,T]; \mathcal{B}_{\alpha - 1 + \epsilon})$,
        $$[0,T] \ni t \mapsto (S*y)_t \in \mathcal{B}_\alpha$$
        is continuous and
        $$
        \sup_{t \leq T} \|(S * y)_t\|^p_\alpha \lesssim \int_0^T \|y_t\|^p_{\alpha - 1 + \epsilon} dt \,.$$
        \item For $Z \in L^p(\Omega \times [0,T];\gamma(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{B}_{\alpha - 1/2 + \epsilon}))$,
        $$[0,T] \ni t \mapsto (S\diamond Z)_t \in \mathcal{B}_\alpha$$
        is continuous and
        $$\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t \leq T} \|(S \diamond Z)_t\|^p_\alpha \Big] \lesssim \mathbb{E}\Big[\int_0^T \|Z_t\|^p_{\gamma(\mathcal{U},\mathcal{B}_{\alpha - 1/2 + \epsilon})} dt\Big] \,.$$
    \end{enumerate}
    In the above, the constants in $\lesssim$'s do not depend on $x,y,Z$, and the dependence on $T$ is uniform over bounded subsets of $(0,\infty)$.

			= p_\alpha(t-s,y-x)-\int_{s}^{ t}\E_{s,x}\left[b(r,X_r)\cdot\nabla_y  p_\alpha(t-r,y-X_r)\right]d r.
		\end{align} 
Similarly, for the Euler scheme $X^h$ evolving according to \eqref{scheme-interpo_LP}, the conditional distribution of $X_t^h$  given $X_{t_k}^h=x$ with $k\in \llbracket 0,n-1\rrbracket ,\ t\in (t_k,T] $ admits a density $\Gamma^h(t_k,x,t,\cdot) $ which again enjoys a Duhamel type representation: for all $y\in \R^d $,
		\begin{align}
			\Gamma^h(t_k,x,t,y)
			= p_\alpha(t-t_k,y-x)-\int_{t_k}^{ t}\E_{t_k,x}\left[b_h(U_{\lfloor r/h\rfloor},X^h_{\tau_r^h})\cdot\nabla  p_\alpha(t-r,y-X^h_r)\right]d  r.
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Duhamel representation and density estimates for the SDE and the Euler scheme

body: [Defn def-fwdtree of arXiv:2607.25567, 'Random Trees in Hyperbolic FPP'] Consider FPP on $\Gamma$ with passage times satisfying that $\rho$ has no atoms. For $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega\in \Omega$, the union of random geodesics $$F(1,\omega):=\bigcup_{g \in G} [1,g]_\omega $$ is a tree, which we refer to as the  \emph{forward random geodesic tree}, or simply the forward tree,  of the FPP on $\Gamma$ with base point $1$. Forward random tree with base point $g\in G$ is defined similarly.

Independent review pending. Let G be a countable connected locally finite graph with p_c(G)>0 and sample iid Bernoulli bond percolation at p_c(G). Almost surely every infinite open component C, regarded as a fixed graph after conditioning on the sampled field, has quenched bond threshold p_c(C)=1. For rational r<1, independent r-thinning of the sampled open bonds is unconditionally iid bond percolation at p_c(G)r<p_c(G), so its probability of any infinite component is zero. Conditioning, then intersecting over rational r and using monotonicity, proves simultaneous failure of percolation below r=1 on every C. Infinitude of C alone therefore supplies no robustness under thinning.
G countable, connected and locally finite
p_c(G)>0
Independent bond retention and independent subsequent thinning
title: Draft thinning fact: surviving critical components have threshold one

[Defn def:poisson-dirichlet of arXiv:2601.09537, 'Gene genealogies in haploid populations evolving according to sweepstakes reproduction'] Let $0 < \alpha < 1$ be fixed,  write
$x := (x_1, x_2, \ldots)$ for $x \in \Delta_{+}$ (recall
~(equation eq:simplex of the paper)), and $(x,x) := \sum_{j=1}^\infty x_j^2$. Let
$F_\alpha$ be a probability measure on $\Delta_{+}$ associated with
the Poisson-Dirichlet$(\alpha,0)$-distribution, and $\Xi_\alpha$ a
measure on $\Delta_{+}$ given by
\begin{displaymath}
\Xi_\alpha({\rm d}x) =   (x,x)F_\alpha( {\rm d}x)
\end{displaymath}
A Poisson-Dirichlet$(\alpha,0)$-coalescent is a discrete-time
$\Xi$-coalescent with $\Xi$-measure $\Xi_\alpha$ and no atom at zero.
The transition probability of merging blocks in $r$ groups of size
$k_{1}, \ldots, k_{r} \ge 2$ with current number of blocks
$b \ge k_{1} + \cdots + k_{r}$ and $s = b - k_{1} - \cdots - k_{r}$ is
(recall~(equation eq:1 of the paper) in Definition~(def:notation of the paper)),
\begin{equation}

p_{b; k_{1}, \ldots, k_{r}; s} =  \frac{\alpha^{r+s-1}(r+s-1)! }{(b-1)!}\prod_{i=1}^{r} {(k_{i}-1 - \alpha)}_{k_{i}-1}
\end{equation}
so that $p_{2;2;0} = 1-\alpha$.
title: \citep{schweinsberg03}; The Poisson-Dirichlet$(\alpha,0)$-coalescent

body:
[Df 7 of arXiv:2511.18861, 'Correlation Decay for Maximum Weight Matchings on Sparse Graphs'] Let $G$ be a finite graph with fixed (non-random) edge weights $(w_e)_{e \in E(G)}$, and let $M$ be a matching.  
An augmenting path for $M$ is a finite self-avoiding path or cycle  
\[
P = e_1 \sim e_2 \sim \cdots \sim e_n
\]
where $e \sim e'$ means that the edges are adjacent in $G$ (and, if $P$ is a cycle, we also have $e_n \sim e_1$), such that the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The edges of $P$ alternate between those in $M$ and those not in $M$.  In particular, if $P$ is a cycle, then $n$ must be even.
    \item Writing $e_i = (x_{i-1}, x_i)$ for $i = 1, \ldots, n$, if $P$ is not a cycle and if $e_1$ (respectively $e_n$) is not in $M$, then $x_0$ (respectively $x_n$) is unmatched in $M$.
    \item The edge weights on $P$ satisfy
    \[
        \sum_{e \in P \cap M} w_e \;<\; \sum_{e \in P \cap M^c} w_e.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2511.18861

body:
[Theorem eq:abstract-pressure-bridge of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:conditional-transfer}
For all sufficiently large \(N\), suppose
\(\widehat Q_{N,L}\) and
\(\widehat P_{N,L}(\varepsilon,\eta)\) are finite for every
\(\varepsilon,\eta>0\).  Suppose also that there exist \(\Phi\in\mathbb R\) and a
function \(F\) on \((0,\infty)^2\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \widehat P_{N,L}(\varepsilon,\eta)\longrightarrow F(\varepsilon,\eta)
 \quad\text{for every fixed }\varepsilon,\eta>0,
 \qquad
 F(\varepsilon,\eta)\longrightarrow\Phi
 \quad\text{as }(\varepsilon,\eta)\to(0,0).
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{align}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\widehat Q_{N,L}
 &\le\Phi+\delta_{L,\mathrm{dr}}^{J,\mathrm{up}}(V),
 \\
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\widehat Q_{N,L}
 &\ge\Phi-\delta_{L,\mathrm{dr}}^{J,\mathrm{low}}(V).
 
\end{align}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 &\le
 \max\{\Phi+\delta_{L,\mathrm{dr}}^{J,\mathrm{up}}(V),
            \overline\Lambda_L^J(V)\},\\
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 &\ge
 \max\{\Phi-\delta_{L,\mathrm{dr}}^{J,\mathrm{low}}(V),
            \underline\Lambda_L^J(V)\}.
 
\end{align}
If both de-regularization defects vanish, then
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\widehat{\mathscr C}_{N,L}^J(V)=\Phi
\end{equation}
and the exact identities
\begin{align}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 &=\max\{\Phi,\overline\Lambda_L^J(V)\},
 \\
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 &=\max\{\Phi,\underline\Lambda_L^J(V)\}
 
\end{align}
hold.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)=\Phi
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \overline\Lambda_L^J(V)\le\Phi.
\end{equation}

A concrete sufficient condition for (equation eq:abstract-pressure-bridge of the paper)
is that, for any fixed \(L>0\), the disorder array and \(V\) satisfy the
hypotheses of (thm:bulk-universality of the paper) with \(m=2\).
Indeed, (equation eq:point-Haar-zero-cost of the paper) is automatic.  In this concrete
case,
\[
 \Phi=\Phi_p^{\rm bulk}(V)
 =\sup_{u\in\mathbb R}\{\theta_p(u)-V(u)\}.
\]
When the two de-regularization defects vanish,
(equation eq:exact-universality-iff-localized-defect of the paper) therefore gives a
criterion for the localized branch that is both necessary and sufficient. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

s\in S:

\right\},

then $S^{\mathrm{good}}\cap S^{\mathrm{ind}}$ is nonempty.

[Theorem 60 (singularity models of the two-nut case) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Let $\big(\widehat{M}$, $g (t)\big)$ be as in Theorem \ref{thm:twonut_typeI}, rescaled at the Type I rate as in \S\ref{sec:limits}. According to the first singular time, the pointed Cheeger--Gromov limits are:

\emph{(i) Fiber collapse}, $T = T_F'' < \min_{k \geq 3} \{ T_k^0, T_k^\ell \}$: with arbitrary base points,

\[
\big( \mathbb{CP}^{m_0 + m_\ell + 1} \times \mathbb{C}^{n''} , \; g_{FS} (t) \oplus g_{\mathbb{C}^{n''}} \big) \,, \qquad n'' \;=\; \sum_{k \geq 3} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} N_k \,,
\]

the shrinking Fubini--Study soliton on the fiber times a static flat factor.

\emph{(ii) Contraction at $Q_0$}, $T = \min_{k \geq 3} \{ T_k^0 \} < \min \big\{ T_F'', \min_{k \geq 3} \{ T_k^\ell \} \big\}$: let $\mathcal{I}_0 := \{ k \geq 3 : T_k^0 = T \}$; then $0 < ( m_0 + 1 )\, q_k < p_k$ for every $k \in \mathcal{I}_0$, and with base points on $Q_0$ the limit is

\[
\big( \operatorname{Tot} ( E_{\mathcal{I}_0} ) \times \mathbb{C}^{n''} , \; g_E (t) \oplus g_{\mathbb{C}^{n''}} \big) \,, \qquad E_{\mathcal{I}_0} \;=\; \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_0}^{\oplus ( m_0 + 1 )} \,, \quad c_1 ( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_0} ) \;=\; - \sum_{k \in \mathcal{I}_0} q_k\, a_k \,,
\]
where $E_{\mathcal{I}_0}$ is the restriction of the normal bundle $\mathcal{N}_{Q_0}$ to $\prod_{k \in \mathcal{I}_0} N_k$, $g_E (t)$ is the Dancer--Wang shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton of ansatz form \cite[Theorem 3.36]{DW2011}, and $n'' = m_\ell + \sum_{k \geq 3, \, k \not\in \mathcal{I}_0} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} N_k$: the $\mathbb{CP}^{m_\ell}$-factor of $Q_0$ does not contract, and flattens into $\mathbb{C}^{m_\ell}$.

\emph{(iii) Contraction at $Q_\ell$}: the mirror of (ii) under $( s, q_k, m_0 ) \leftrightarrow ( \ell - s, - q_k, m_\ell )$, with $\mathcal{I}_\infty := \{ k \geq 3 : T_k^\ell = T \}$, $0 < - ( m_\ell + 1 )\, q_k < p_k$ for every $k \in \mathcal{I}_\infty$, and limit $\operatorname{Tot} \big( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_\infty}^{\oplus ( m_\ell + 1 )} \big) \times \mathbb{C}^{n''}$, where $\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_\infty}^{\oplus ( m_\ell + 1 )}$ is the restriction of $\mathcal{N}_{Q_\ell}$ to $\prod_{k \in \mathcal{I}_\infty} N_k$, $c_1 ( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_\infty} ) = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{I}_\infty} q_k\, a_k$, and $n'' = m_0 + \sum_{k \geq 3, \, k \not\in \mathcal{I}_\infty} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} N_k$.

\emph{(iv) Borderline}, $T = T_F'' = \min_{k \geq 3} \{ T_k^0, T_k^\ell \}$: let $\mathcal{I} := \{ k \geq 3 : T_k^0 = T \} = \{ k \geq 3 : T_k^\ell = T \}$; then $- \frac{p_k}{m_\ell + 1} < q_k < \frac{p_k}{m_0 + 1}$ for every $k \in \mathcal{I}$, and with arbitrary base points the limit is $\widehat{Z} \times \mathbb{C}^{n''}$, where

\[
\widehat{Z} \;:=\; \widehat{M} \Big|_{\prod_{k \in \mathcal{I}} N_k} \;=\; \mathbb{P} \big( \mathcal{O}^{\oplus ( m_0 + 1 )} \oplus \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}}^{\oplus ( m_\ell + 1 )} \big) \,, \qquad c_1 ( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}} ) \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{I}} q_k\, a_k \,,
\]
carrying its unique compact shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton of ansatz form (uniqueness by Tian--Zhu \cite{TZhu}), and $n'' = \sum_{k \geq 3, \, k \not\in \mathcal{I}} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} N_k$. When $\mathcal{I} = \{ 3, \cdots, r \}$, we have $\widehat{Z} = \widehat{M}$ and the flow is the Fano canonical-class case.

The transductive covariance-penalty criterion of the label-free blend selects by the cross-validated relative squared loss, while the pools score by the mean per-row ratio. On the benchmark corpora the two orderings part on pkanrtm (24,000 calibration rows, a near-zero-target tail): the squared-loss criterion picks the simplex, the worst vertex, on every cell. The same criterion written in the score's own metric, R_1(w) = mean_i sqrt(max(r_i + delta(w), 0)), repairs it. Measured 2026-09-06: P39 (a) REFUTED: the ratio-metric blend vs the best vertex on pkanrtm = -0.93 (within 0.3); (b) REFUTED: vs the registered blend on the other corpora = advection -0.02, darcy +0.40, burgers -1.74 (within 0.2); (c) HELD: it beats least squares on 48 of 55 cells (87 pct); falsifier (worse than the registered blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus, or worse than the best vertex on pkanrtm by more than 1.0) TRIGGERED. On the pools the blend was built on (EMIT, OCO-2, both splits): P40 (a) HELD: the R_1 blend vs the registered blend = B-emit +0.48, B-oco +0.14, C-emit +1.52, C-oco +0.16 (within 0.2); (b) HELD: wins over least squares R_1 vs registered = B-emit 38/39, B-oco 30/30, C-emit 40/36, C-oco 30/30 (at least the registered count less three); (c) REFUTED: the two selections coincide on B-emit 3 of 40, B-oco 0 of 30, C-emit 0 of 40, C-oco 0 of 30 cells (at least half); falsifier (R_1 worse than the registered blend by more than 0.3 on either corpus on either split) not triggered.
the score is the mean per-row ratio ||e|| / max(||y||, floor); the criterion's cross-validated loss is the mean squared ratio; the transductive variance shift delta(w) = V_ev(w) - V_cal(w) is estimated by the pairs bootstrap of the fitted predictor at both row sets
measured on the benchmark corpora (advection, Darcy at four betas, Burgers at four viscosities, pkanrtm and pkanrtm-lowfi) with the three vertices simplex / least squares / pool heuristic and the 0.1 barycentric grid; the EMIT / OCO-2 check is P40

Write rho_i = ||f(x_i) - y_i|| / m_i for the per-row ratio. Then S = mean rho_i and Q = mean rho_i^2 = (mean rho_i)^2 + var(rho_i). Two estimators f and g with the same S can differ in Q by the difference of their ratio variances, and an estimator with the smaller Q can have the larger S whenever its ratios are less dispersed but larger on average - the ordering by Q is the ordering by S only when the ratio dispersion is comparable across candidates. On a corpus whose ratios have a heavy right tail (near-floor rows, where a fixed absolute error is a ratio of hundreds), the dispersion term dominates Q and the candidates are ordered by their tails, not by their mean ratio. The ratio criterion R_1(w) = mean_i sqrt(max(r_i + delta(w), 0)), with r_i the out-of-fold relative squared residual of candidate w at calibration row i and delta(w) the variance shift of the scored rows over the calibration rows, is an estimate of S under the same transductive correction, since E||e|| ~ sqrt(bias^2 + variance) row by row; it reduces to the cross-validated score when delta = 0 and to the same ordering as Q when the ratios are homoscedastic across candidates.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:74049dd47b3566659f1d55542a1e0edbcd532dc51b187848342b35a7f4329631","revision_digest":"sha256:78ede5727d3ca5ff1b9ac9270c2fa52c0f165ec6857efe2847021006a1c90698","source_id":"measurement of 2026-09-05/06 (ens_rmt_bench3.py, analyze_bench3.py); RMT_ENSEMBLE_THEORY.md 6ao / 6ap","source_revision":"as-read-2026-09-05","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Lemma Pro: tail of arXiv:2411.04778, 'Coupling between Brownian motion and random walks on the infinite percolation cluster'] There exists $C:=C(d)>0$, such that for every point $x,y \in \mathscr{C}_\infty$, we have
		\[
		p^\omega(t, x, y) \leqslant \begin{cases}C \exp \left(-\frac{\mathsf{d}(x,y)^{2}}{C t}\right) & \text { if }\mathsf{d}(x,y)\leqslant t,  \\ C \exp \left(-\frac{\mathsf{d}(x,y)}{C}\left(1+\ln \frac{\mathsf{d}(x,y)}{t}\right)\right) & \text { if }\mathsf{d}(x,y)>t.\end{cases}
		\]
		Here, $\mathsf{d}(x,y)$ denotes the chemical distance on $\mathscr{C}_\infty$, i.e., minimum length of the open paths connecting $x$ and $y$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Carne--Varopoulos bound

[Lemma 39 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Consider the IMFIS process on $(G,F,R,\b)$ with $G=(V,E)$ $2$-uniform. Assume $\ell$ is fixed, and let $\alpha\to\infty$. Then
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item $\begin{aligned}[t]
				|V|=n_{\alpha}=(1+O(\alpha^{-1}))\tfrac{\ell}{2}\alpha^2,
			\end{aligned}$
			\item $\begin{aligned}[t]
				|F|\leq\alpha F_{\max}\leq\alpha M,
			\end{aligned}$
			\item $\begin{aligned}[t]
				|R^*(U)|\leq|U|R_{\max}^{(a)}\leq|U|M,\ \forall U\subset V.
			\end{aligned}$
		\end{enumerate}

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2604.11691, 'Asymptotic behavior of spatio-temporal point processes of exceedances'] Let $\{\bm X_{t}, \, t \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ be a multivariate strictly stationary regularly varying time series with tail process $\{\bm Y_{t}, \, t \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ such that Condition \ref{con_1} and Condition \ref{con_2} hold. In addition, let $N_n(u)$ be the sequence of point processes given in \eqref{N_n} with $u>0$ satisfying the bound in Equation \eqref{eq:risk-bound}.
Then, $N_n(u)$ converges weakly to a point process $N(u)$ on 
$[0,1] \times \mathcal{X}_u$ which has the same distribution as the superposition of a random number of independent and identical copies of cluster processes, i.e.,
\begin{align} 
N(u)=_d{}\sum_{i=1}^{T} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \delta_{(V_i,s,\bm Z_{ij})} ~\mathds{1}\{r^{(s)}(Z_{ij}) >u\},
\end{align}
where $T$ is a Poisson random variable with mean $\theta$
and $$\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \bigg(\sum_{j=-\infty}^{\infty} \delta_{(V_i,s, \bm Z_{ij})}\bigg)_{i=1}^{\infty}$$ are i.i.d.~copies of the process $C$ defined in \eqref{C} and independent of $T$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, especially group theory, two elements $a$ and $b$ of a group are conjugate if there is an element $g$ in the group such that $b=gag^{-1}.$ This is an equivalence relation whose equivalence classes are called conjugacy classes. In other words, each conjugacy class is closed under the maps $a\mapsto gag^{-1},$ with $g$ an element of the group.

[Corollary cor:holder of arXiv:2509.04155, 'An Approach to Sub-Gaussian Heat Kernel Estimates via Analysis on Metric Spaces'] Let $\delta > 0$ and assume that the strongly local regular Dirichlet form $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ on $L^2(X,\mu)$ satisfies (eq:PI(Dir) of the paper).
    Let $x \in X$ and $R > 0$ and assume that $\xi \in \mathcal{F}$, not necessarily continuous, satisfies $0 \leq \xi \leq 1$ $\mu$-almost everywhere and the energy upper bounds (eq:CE(Dir) of the paper) for the open ball $B(x,R)$.
    Then the precise representative $\tilde{\xi}$ satisfies the global Hölder regularity
    \[
        \abs{\tilde{\xi}(y) - \tilde{\xi}(z)} \leq C\left(\frac{d(y,z)}{R}\right)^{\delta/2} \text{ for all } y,z \in X.
    \]
    This result is quantitative in the sense that $C$ depends only on $\delta$, the constants associated to $\Psi$ in (equation eq:Psi of the paper), the constants in (eq:CE(Dir) of the paper), (eq:PI(Dir) of the paper) and (equation eq:muDoubling of the paper).

[Proposition 32 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\bf G$ be a real reductive group and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Suppose that $\Gamma_{\mu}$ is Zariski dense in $G$ and that $\mu$ admits a finite exponential moment \eqref{Exponential-moment}.
Then, for any $\varphi \in C^0(\wt B)$, we have, uniformly in $\wt b \in \wt B$,  
\begin{align*}
 P_{\mu}^n \varphi (\wt b) - Q \varphi \big((\ell_0^{\mu})^n \theta(\wt b) \big) \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  0. 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 32 of arXiv:2607.19873

[Lemma lem:C5 of arXiv:2509.23086, 'On Optimal Markovian Couplings of L\'evy Processes'] Let $\mu_n,\mu \in \Lambda_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Suppose \( \mu_n \xrightarrow{\Lambda} \mu \) and
	\begin{align}
		\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |x|^2\, d\mu_n(x) 
		= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |x|^2\, d\mu(x).
	\end{align}
	Then for every \( \varepsilon > 0 \), there exists \( R \ge 1 \) such that
	\[
	\sup_n \int_{|x| \ge R} |x|^2\, d\mu_n(x) \le \varepsilon.
	\]
	Moreover, for any continuous $\varphi$ with quadratic growth, $|\varphi(x)| \le C|x|^2$ for some $C \ge 0$, one has
	\begin{align*}
		\lim_{n\to\infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x)\, d\mu_n(x) 
		= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x)\, d\mu(x).
	\end{align*}

[Proposition Separating_Surface_Prop of arXiv:2603.28520, 'The Supercritical Loop O(1) and Random Current Models: Uniqueness and Mixing'] Let $q\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2},$ $G=(V,E)$ be a graph and let $E_1,E_3\subseteq E$ be disjoint. Denote $E_2:=E\setminus (E_1\cup E_3).$ Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item $E_1$ and $E_2$ are finite.
    \item The induced graph $G(E_2)$ is connected.
    \item Any path $(\gamma_j)_{1\leq j\leq n}$ in $G$ with $\gamma_1\in G(E_1)$ and $\gamma_n\in G(E_3)$ must have a $1<j<n$ with $\gamma_j\in G(E_2).$
\end{enumerate}
Then, $\pi_{G(E_1)}(\ker(\partial^G))=\pi_{G(E_1)}(\ker(\partial^{G(E_1\cup E_2)})).$ In particular, for any $A\in (\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})^{V(G(E_3))}$ with $\sum_v A_v=0$,
$$\operatorname{UD}^A_G[\eta|_{\mathcal{O}(E_1)} \in \cdot\;]=\operatorname{UD}_{G}[\eta|_{\mathcal{O}(E_1)} \in \cdot\;]=\operatorname{UD}_{G(E_1\cup E_2)}[\eta|_{\mathcal{O}(E_1)}\in\cdot\;].$$ Furthermore, for $\eta\sim \operatorname{UD}^A_G,$ the random variables $\eta|_{\mathcal{O}(E_1)}$ and $\eta|_{\mathcal{O}(E_3)}$ are independent.
title: Proposition Separating_Surface_Prop of arXiv:2603.28520

[Lemma lem:af-heavy-bins-empty of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. 
Fix a sufficiently small $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$.
Let $j$ be a sufficiently large integer. Fix an integer $\tau \ge 0$ and a tuple $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$. Let $E^+$ be a constant-escape process on $[j]$ with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time $\tau$, end-of-step arrival rate $\nu_j^\mathrm{lo}$, and $\overline{\mathrm{arr}}_{[j]}^{E^+}(\tau) = \overline{a}$. Let $d$, $\varpi$, and $\theta$ be real numbers with $d\ge 0$, $\varpi\ge 1$, and $0 \le \theta < 1/(64j^2)$. Suppose that $\overline{a}$ satisfies (Con(item:Con1 of the paper)) for $d$, (Con(item:Con3 of the paper)) for $(\varpi,\theta,\nu_j^\mathrm{lo})$, and (Con(item:Con4 of the paper)) for~$2$. 
Fix $t$ in the range 
$\max\{\varpi j^{12}, d j^3\} \le t-\tau \le (4/\lambda)^{2j}$
Then, 
with probability at least $1- 2j^{-3j+1}$,
for all $k \in [j]$ with $W_k \ge j^{10}$,

body:
[Dfn 101 (coordinate sum) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any measure $\rho$ on $[0,1]\times\R^d$, let $\bar{\rho}$ be the measure on $[0,1]\times\R$ that satisfies
	\[
	\int_{t,y} f\bigg(t, \sum_{i=1}^d y^i\bigg)
	\,\rho(dt\,dy)
	= \int_{t,x} f(t,x)
	\,\bar{\rho}(dt\,dx)\,,
	\]
where $t\in[0,1]$, $y\in\R^d$, and $x\in\R$.
As above, let $\vY$ be an $\R^d$-valued semimartingale with drift $\vD$ and covariation $\vQ$. We now consider the one-dimensional projections
	\[
	Y = \sum_{i=1}^d Y^i\,,\quad
	\sum_{i=1}^d D^i\,,\quad
	\sum_{i,j=1}^d Q^{ij}\,.
	\]
Then $Y$ is a (one-dimensional) semimartingale with drift $D$ and covariation $Q$. We hereafter abbreviate $\rho\equiv\rho_{\vY}$ for the occupation measure of $\vY$ defined in Definition~\ref{d:intro.cts.occ}.
Then the occupation measure of $Y$ is $\bar{\rho}$. The occupation measures associated to the drift and covariation of $Y$ are
	\[
	\sum_{i=1}^d
	\bar{\rho}_{D^i}\,,\quad
	\sum_{i,j=1}^d
	\bar{\rho}_{Q^{ij}}\,.	
	\]
Let $\hvY$ be as defined by Lemma~\ref{l:ideal.smoothed.occ.msr},
and let $\iY$ be the one-dimensional projection, so $\iY(t)=Y(t-\sss)+\mathfrak{x}$ where $(\sss,\mathfrak{x})\sim\bar{\varphi}$ (the density $\varphi$ integrated over $x^1 + \ldots + x^d=\mathfrak{x}$). It follows that $\iY$ has occupation measure $\overline{\rho*\varphi}=\bar{\rho}*\bar{\varphi}$. Similarly, the occupation measures associated to the drift and covariation of $\iY$ have densities
	\[
	\sum_{i=1}^d
	\overline{\rho_{D^i}*\varphi}
	\,,\quad
	\sum_{i,j=1}^d
	\overline{\rho_{Q^{ij}}
		*\varphi}\,.	
	\]
Then, analogously to \eqref{e:intro.occ.ratio.drift} and \eqref{e:intro.occ.ratio.qv}, we define (with $x$ now a scalar)
	\begin{align}
	
	B(t,x) 
	&\equiv
	\sum_{i=1}^D \frac{
	\overline{\rho_{D^i}*\varphi}(t,x)
	}
		{\overline{\rho*\varphi}(t,x)}\,,\\
	A(t,x)
	&\equiv
	\sum_{i,j=1}^D \frac{
	\overline{\rho_{Q^{ij}}*\varphi}(t,x)
	}
	{\overline{\rho*\varphi}(t,x)}\,.
	
	\end{align}
Let $\iX$ be the solution to the (one-dimensional) SDE
	\[
	d\iX(t)
	= B(t,\iX)\,dt
	+A(t,\iX)^{1/2}\,dW(t)\,,
	\]
where $W$ is a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion.
title: coordinate sum

body:
[Corollary Cor:PW_dabrRobin of arXiv:2609.02325, 'A Payne-Weinberger inequality\\for quantum dot Dirac operators'] Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded simply connected domain with $C^2$~boundary and let~$\delta_\Omega$ denote its isoperimetric deficit, as in (equation Eq:IsopDeficit of the paper).
    Then, for all $a>0$ there holds 
    \begin{equation} 
       |\Omega| \, \mu_\Omega \bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{|\Omega|}}  \bigg)
       - \pi \, \mu_\mathbb{D} \bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}  \bigg) 
       \leqslant 
       F \left(\sqrt{\mu_\mathbb{D} \big(\tfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}\big)} \right) \delta_\Omega( \delta_\Omega+2) +  G \left(\sqrt{\mu_\mathbb{D} \big(\tfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}\big)} \right) \delta_\Omega,
    \end{equation}
    where $F$ and $G$ are as in (equation Eq:def_FG of the paper). In particular,
    \begin{equation} 
        |\Omega| \, \mu_\Omega \bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{|\Omega|}}  \bigg)
        - \pi \, \mu_\mathbb{D} \bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}  \bigg) 
        \leqslant C_{\mathrm{PW}} \delta_\Omega( \delta_\Omega+2) + \pi j_{0,1} \delta_\Omega
    \end{equation}
    and the equality holds if and only if $\Omega$ is a disk. Here, $C_{\mathrm{PW}}>0$ is the constant in (equation Eq:PW_Dirichlet of the paper).
title: Corollary Cor:PW_dabrRobin of arXiv:2609.02325

[Lemma lem:truncation-coupling of arXiv:2608.26745, 'Moderate Deviations for the Largest Eigenvalue of a Randomly Deformed Gaussian Unitary Ens'] There are constants $c,C>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P(\widehat\lambda_N\ne\lambda_N)
 \le CN e^{-c\tau_N}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for
\[
 \upsilon_N\in
 \left\{a_N^{3/2},\,a_N^3,\,\alpha_N^2a_N^2\right\},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1{\upsilon_N}
 \log\mathbb P(\widehat\lambda_N\ne\lambda_N)=-\infty.
\end{equation}
In particular, at each of these speeds, the scaled variables
$\sqrt N(\widehat\lambda_N-R_N)/\alpha_N$ and $Z_N$ are exponentially
equivalent.

body: [Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.29736, '2608.29736'] A class $\alpha\in H^{1,1}_{\BC}(X,\mathbb{R})$ is \emph{modified K\"ahler} if it contains a K\"ahler current $T$ whose generic Lelong number along any prime divisor is zero. [Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.26001, 'The kernel of the Birman--Craggs--Johnson homomorphism'] Fix $g \geq 2$.  Set $H = \HH_1(\Sigma_g^1;\bbF_2) = \HH_1(\Sigma_g;\bbF_2)$.  We then
have commutative diagrams with exact rows
\[\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=tiny, row sep=small]
& \QK_g^1 \arrow{r} \arrow{d}{\sigma} & \QTorelli_g^1 \arrow{r} \arrow{d}{\sigma} & \wedge^3 H \arrow{r} \arrow{d}{\cong} & 1 \\
0 \arrow{r} & \BCJ_2(g) \arrow{r}                & \BCJ_3(g) \arrow{r}                      & \BCJ_3(g)/\BCJ_2(g) \arrow{r}             & 0
\end{tikzcd}
\enspace \text{and} \enspace
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=tiny, row sep=small]
& \QK_g  \arrow{r} \arrow{d}{\sigma} & \QTorelli_g \arrow{r} \arrow{d}{\sigma} & (\wedge^3 H)/H \arrow{r} \arrow{d}{\cong} & 1 \\
0 \arrow{r} & \BCJZ_2(g) \arrow{r}              & \BCJZ_3(g) \arrow{r}                   & \BCJZ_3(g)/\BCJZ_2(g) \arrow{r}               & 0.
\end{tikzcd}\]
In both diagrams, the first two vertical arrows are the induced BCJ homomorphisms.

[Theorem 40 (The one-dimensional Stokes tree) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(F\) be a tame Morse polynomial of degree \(m\) in one variable and
fix an admissible direction.  Denote by
\[
 E_0,\ldots,E_{m-1}
\]
the \(m\) decay sectors at infinity.  There is a canonical boundary
isomorphism
\begin{equation}
 \partial:
 H_1^{\mathrm{rd}}(F;\mathbb Z)
 \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }
 \widetilde H_0(\{E_0,\ldots,E_{m-1}\};\mathbb Z).
 
\end{equation}
If \(\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_{m-1}\) is a distinguished integral thimble
basis, join two vertices whenever the corresponding thimble has its two
ends in those sectors.  The resulting oriented graph \(T\) is a spanning
tree.

Let \(\gamma\) be an admissible contour directed from \(E_p\) to \(E_q\).
Then
\begin{equation}
 [\gamma]
 =
 \sum_{e\in[p,q]_T}
 \epsilon_e(p,q)[\Gamma_e],
 \qquad
 \epsilon_e(p,q)\in\{-1,1\},
 
\end{equation}
where \([p,q]_T\) is the unique path from \(p\) to \(q\), and the sign is
positive precisely when the orientation of \(e\) agrees with that path.
Thus the physical Betti row is obtained by a finite path search and all
of its entries belong to \(\{0,\pm1\}\).  If the contour lies on a Stokes
direction, the two lateral trees give the two lateral rows, related by
\eqref{eq:Betti-wall-crossing}.

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2608.31145, 'Gauge-compatible tensors on statistical manifolds: splitting and submanifold geometry'] Let $(M,g,\nabla,\nabla^{*},\Theta)$ be a $\Theta$-statistical manifold. Then
\[
R^{\nabla}(X,Y)\Theta Z
=
\Theta\,R^{\nabla^{*}}(X,Y)Z,
\]
for all $X,Y,Z\in\Gamma(TM)$.

If $\Theta$ is invertible, then
\[
R^{\nabla}(X,Y)
=
\Theta\circ R^{\nabla^{*}}(X,Y)\circ\Theta^{-1}.
\]

Moreover, for every piecewise smooth loop $\gamma$ based at $p$,
\[
\mathcal{P}^{\nabla}_{\gamma}\circ\Theta_p
=
\Theta_p\circ\mathcal{P}^{\nabla^{*}}_{\gamma}.
\]
Hence, if $\Theta_p$ is invertible,
\[
\operatorname{Hol}_{p}(\nabla)
=
\Theta_p\circ
\operatorname{Hol}_{p}(\nabla^{*})
\circ\Theta_p^{-1}.
\]

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces with COMPLEX scalars, and let 1 <= p_0, p_1, q_0, q_1 <= infinity. Let T be a LINEAR map from L^{p_0}(mu) + L^{p_1}(mu) into the measurable functions on Y such that ||T f||_{q_0} <= M_0 ||f||_{p_0} for all f in L^{p_0} and ||T f||_{q_1} <= M_1 ||f||_{p_1} for all f in L^{p_1}. For 0 < theta < 1 define 1/p = (1-theta)/p_0 + theta/p_1 and 1/q = (1-theta)/q_0 + theta/q_1. Then ||T f||_q <= M_0^{1-theta} M_1^{theta} ||f||_p for all f in L^p(mu). Equivalently, the operator norm of T on the interpolated pair is log-convex along the segment joining (1/p_0, 1/q_0) to (1/p_1, 1/q_1). It suffices to assume the two endpoint bounds on simple functions with support of finite measure, and then T extends uniquely to L^p for p < infinity.

[Proposition 29 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] There is an isomorphism of graded $S_n$-modules:
$$H^\ast(\mathsf{T}_\Gamma(n)) \cong \bigoplus_{\substack{0\leq b \leq a \\ a+b\leq n }} y_{(a,b)}\Sigma^{a+b+1}\Phi[n,(a,b)^\ast]$$
where 
$$
y_{(a,b)} = \begin{cases}
	
	\left\lfloor\ds\frac{a-b+2}{3} \right\rfloor -\delta_{b,0}	&	a \equiv_2 b \\  & \\
	
	0	&	a \not\equiv_2 b
\end{cases}
$$

[Proposition 169 (Fundamental spacetime energy--null-flux identities) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] \hfill
	
	\noindent \underline{\textbf{Wave equation spacetime energy--null-flux identity}}.
	Suppose that on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}$, the scalar function $f$ is the solution to the inhomogeneous covariant wave equation $\upmu \Box_{\gfour} f = \mathfrak{G}$. Then the following identity holds for $q \in [0,\infty)$:
	\begin{align}
		\begin{split} 
			& \ingoingfluxwave{q}[f](\ubar,u) + \outgoingfluxwave{q}[f](\ubar,u) + \frac{1}{2} \spacetimecoercive{q}[ \angrmD f](\ubar,u)   			+ \frac{q}{2} \newspacetimecoercive{q-1}\left[ \sqrt{\upmu + 2\ReciprocaluLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction \upmu} \, \nullangrmD f\right](\ubar,u) + 2 q \newspacetimecoercive{q-1}\left[ \newuL f\right](\ubar,u)  \\
			& = \ingoingfluxwave{q}[f](\leftubar,u) + \outgoingfluxwave{q}[f](\ubar,\moreinterestingu_1) - \int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}} \left\{ \Lunit f + 2 \upmu \Transport f \right\} \mathfrak{G} \, \weight^{q} \ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction \voldiamond  \\
			& \ \
			+ \int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}  
			{^{(\multipliervectorfield)}\mathfrak{B}}[f]\, \weight^{q} \ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction \voldiamond  + 2q \int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}  \MagnitueofinnerproductofnewLandnewuL  (\ToriTangentVectorfieldAssociatedToDoubleNullFolliations f )(\newuL f) (\newL \weight) \, \weight^{q-1} \voldiamond
		\end{split}
	\end{align}
	The error term ${^{(\multipliervectorfield)}\mathfrak{B}}[f]$ appearing 
	in the last integral on RHS\,\eqref{E:ENERGYNULLFLUXINTEGRALIDENTITIESWAVE}
	can be decomposed as follows: 
	\begin{align}  
		{^{(\multipliervectorfield)}\mathfrak{B}}[f] 
		& \eqdef \frac{1}{2} \left| \angrmD f\right|^2_{\gtorus} \mathbf{1}_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]} \setminus \smallneighborhoodofcreasearg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}}  +
		\sum_{i=1}^6 {^{(\multipliervectorfield)}\mathfrak{B}_{(i)}[f]},
	\end{align}
	where:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align}
			{^{(\multipliervectorfield)}\mathfrak{B}_{(1)}[f]} 
			& 
			\eqdef (\Lunit f)^2 
			\left\lbrace 
			- \frac{1}{2} \Lunit \upmu + \muX \upmu
			- 
			\frac{1}{2} \upmu \mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi 
			- 
			 \upmu^2 \mytr_{\gtorus} \angktan 
			- 
			 \mytr_{\gtorus} \angktrans
			\right\rbrace,  
			 
			\\
			{^{(\multipliervectorfield)}\mathfrak{B}_{(2)}[f]} 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			- (\Lunit f) (\muX f) 
			\left\lbrace  
			\mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi 
			+ 
			2 \upmu \mytr_{\gtorus} \angktan 
			+ 
			2 \mytr_{\gtorus} \angktrans 
			\right\rbrace, 
			 
			\\
			{^{(\multipliervectorfield)}\mathfrak{B}_{(3)}[f]} 
			& \eqdef  
			|\angrmD f|_{\gtorus}^2 
			\left\lbrace \muX \upmu + 2 \upmu  \Lunit \upmu +			+ 
			\frac{1}{2}
			\upmu \mytr_{\gtorus}\upchi 
			+ 
			\upmu^2 \mytr_{\gtorus} \angktan 
			+ 
			\upmu \mytr_{\gtorus} \angktrans

[Definition 17 (Choice of auxiliary exponents) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Set
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak m_*:=\min\Bigl\{&
 s_1-\tfrac14-\betastar,
 \tfrac12-\betastar-s_1-\kappa,
 s_2-\tfrac12-\betastar-\kappa,\\
 &1-s_2-\betagamma-2\kappa,
 s_1+\tfrac14-s_2,
 \kappa,
 \tfrac14-\betastar-\kappa,\\
 &\tfrac12-\betasum-2\betastar-\kappa,
 \sigma-2\betastar,
 s_1-\sigma,
 s_2-\sigma,\\
 &\tfrac14-\sigma,
 \tfrac12-\betasum-\kappa-\sigma
 \Bigr\}>0.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Choose a master loss $0<\varepsilon_0<\mathfrak m_*/100$.
Every disposable dyadic loss $\varepsilon$, $\delta$, or $\eta$ is chosen
below $\varepsilon_0/10$.  Let $C_{\mathrm{inc}}\ge1$ be the maximum of $1$ and the finitely many
coefficients multiplying $\theta$ in the frequency exponents of the increment
estimates.  After the dyadic losses are fixed, choose
\[
 0<\theta<\frac{\varepsilon_0}{10C_{\mathrm{inc}}}.
\]
Since $\betasum<1/4$ and $\beta_a<1/8$, this choice also gives
\[
 \theta<\frac12-\betasum,
 \qquad
 2\beta_a+\theta+\varepsilon<1
 \quad(a\in\mathfrak C)
\]
for every disposable loss $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0/10$.  Finally choose the
Gaussian moment exponent $p_0$ so that $p_0\theta>4$.  These choices are kept
fixed throughout the proof.

[Proposition mainestimate of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Consider a family of probability measures $(\mu_t)_{t>0}$ verifying  $M_\beta$ for some $\beta>0$. Let moreover $\varepsilon>0$. 
    \par There exists a constant $C_\beta$ such that for integers $n < m$ and $l$, and independent random variables $(X^j_u)_{\substack{1\leqslant j\leqslant l \\ 1\leqslant u \leqslant n  }}$ and $(Y^j_v)_{{\substack{1\leqslant j\leqslant l \\ 1\leqslant v \leqslant m-n  }}}$ such that 
\[\mathbb{P}(X^j_u\in \mathrm{d} g)= \mu_{s^j_u}(\mathrm{d} g) \text{ and } \mathbb{P}(Y^j_v\in \mathrm{d} g)= \mu_{t^j_v}(\mathrm{d} g), \]
 where 
 \[\max\Bigg (\max_{\substack{1\leqslant j\leqslant l \\ 1\leqslant u \leqslant n  }} s^j_u, \max_{{\substack{1\leqslant j\leqslant l \\ 1\leqslant v \leqslant m-n  }}} t^j_u\Bigg )\leqslant \varepsilon,\]
we have

\mathbb{E}\left[\left\vert \sum_{j=1}^l \log(X^j_1\cdots X^j_n Y^j_1\cdots Y^j_{m-n})-\log(X^j_1\cdots X^j_n)  \right\vert^{2\beta}\right] \leqslant C_\beta l^{\beta} \left( (m-n)^\beta \varepsilon^\beta +n^{2\beta-}\varepsilon^{2\beta}\right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a sequence of finite, possibly random, rooted graphs G_n, local weak (Benjamini-Schramm) convergence means that for every finite radius r, the distribution of the isomorphism class of the r-ball around the (uniformly, or otherwise canonically) chosen root converges weakly to that of a limiting, typically infinite, random rooted graph (G*, o). The objective method, due to Aldous and Steele, is the broader program of analyzing this limiting infinite object directly, such as a Poisson weighted infinite tree or a unimodular Galton-Watson tree, to compute limiting constants for combinatorial optimization functionals on the finite graphs, such as the minimum spanning tree constant or the limiting value in the random assignment problem, by solving a recursive distributional (fixed-point) equation on the infinite limit rather than working with finite-n computations directly. It does not by itself establish that a given sequence converges locally weakly, which typically must be separately verified via a subsequential compactness argument together with uniqueness of subsequential limits, and it does not directly give convergence of global, extensive functionals without an additional concentration or summation argument beyond the purely local statement. Typical failure: Assuming that local weak convergence of the underlying random graph automatically implies convergence of a global extensive functional, such as the total weight of a minimum spanning tree, at the same per-vertex limiting rate; local convergence controls only typical local neighborhoods, and passing to a global average requires an additional uniform-integrability or concentration argument, often the genuinely hard part of an objective-method proof, which is easy to overlook once the local limit has been identified. Canonical reference: Benjamini and Schramm, 2001, Electronic Journal of Probability; Aldous and Steele, 2004, in Probability on Discrete Structures, Springer; Aldous and Lyons, 2007, Electronic Journal of Probability.

for extensive functionals: an additional argument, such as subadditivity or concentration, to pass from the local limit to a law of large numbers for the global sum

body: In number theory, the Green–Tao theorem, proven by Ben Green and Terence Tao in 2004, states that the sequence of prime numbers contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. In other words, for every natural number , there exist arithmetic progressions of primes with terms. The proof is an extension of Szemerédi's theorem. The problem can be traced back to investigations of Lagrange and Waring from around 1770.

Let G be a finite undirected loopless multigraph on n vertices with positive edge weights w_e, L its weighted Laplacian, and t > 0. A spanning rooted forest is a spanning forest with one chosen root in each tree; its weight is t^|E(F)| prod_{e in F} w_e (so an unrooted forest with trees T_1, ..., T_k counts prod |T_i| times). Z(t) is the total weight of spanning rooted forests, and Q_t = (I + tL)^-1. Z(t) is a polynomial in t of degree n - c(G), where c(G) is the number of connected components, and its leading coefficient is prod over components C of |C| tau_w(C), with tau_w(C) the total weight of spanning trees of C.

body:
[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Fix a compact interval $\mathcal I\subset \R$.
For any $f\in \mathbf{M}$ satisfying \eqref{eq:TwistCondition}, there exists a coupling between the $\alpha_p$ and an iid sequence $Z_p \sim \cN^{\C}(0,1)$  
such that
the error function 
\[
  E_{N,0}(x) \coloneqq S_{N,0}(x) - G_{N,0}(x)  = \sum_{p\leq N} \frac{f(p)}{\sqrt{p}} (\alpha_p-Z_p) p^{-ix}
\]
converges almost surely in $L^{\infty}(\mathcal{I})$ to a random continuous function $E(x)$. Moreover, for each $\lambda\geq 0$, we have the exponential moment bound
\begin{align}
  \E\big[\exp\big(\lambda \sup_{N\geq 0} \|E_{N,0}\|_{L^\infty(\cI)}\big) \big]<\infty\,,
\end{align}
which in particular implies 
\begin{align}
  \E \big[\exp(\lambda\|E\|_{L^\infty(\cI)})\big] < \infty \,.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\eta, \eta' \in \Prob_1(\RR)$. Then the following statements hold:
	\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
		\item  $U_\eta$ is well-defined in $[0,1]$ and convex, with $U_\eta(0)=0$ and $U_\eta(1)=\mean(\eta)$.
		\item  The distribution $\eta$ is dominated in convex order by $\eta'$ if and only if 
		\[
			U_\eta(1) = U_{\eta'}(1), \qquad \text{and} \qquad U_\eta(p) \geq U_{\eta'}(p), \quad \text{for all } p \in (0,1).
		\]
		\item  The pair $(\eta, \eta')$ is irreducible if and only if 
		\[
			U_\eta(1) = U_{\eta'}(1), \qquad \text{and} \qquad U_\eta(p) > U_{\eta'}(p), \quad \text{for all } p \in (0,1).
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 6 of arXiv:2607.15872

[Theorem 131 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider a discrete ensemble satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic}, \ref{Assumptions_offcrit}, \ref{Assumptions_analyticity} and the additional Assumption~\ref{Assumptions_extra}. For $h,h_1,h_2 \in [H]$, we set
\begin{equation}

\begin{split}
W_{2;h_1,h_2}^{[0]}(z_1,z_2) & = \mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2), \\
W_{1; h}^{[1]}(z) & = \Op_{h}\Bigg[\bigg(\frac{q^{+,[1]}_{g}}{s_g^{\circ}}\bigg)_{g = 1}^H\,;\,\boldsymbol{0}\Bigg](z_1), \\
W_{1;h}^{[2]}(z) & = \Op_{h}\Bigg[\bigg(\frac{1}{s_g^{\circ}}\Big\{q^{+,[2]}_{g} + q_g^{-,[1]} \big\langle\bth_g \cdot \boldsymbol{W}_{1}^{[1]}\big\rangle + \frac{q_g^+}{2}\big\langle\bth_g\cdot \boldsymbol{W}_{1}^{[1]}\big\rangle^{2} \\
& \qquad\qquad + \frac{q_g^+}{2} \big\langle \bth_g(\bth_g - 1)\cdot \partial \boldsymbol{W}_{1}^{[1]}\big\rangle
+ \frac{q_g^+}{2} \big\langle \bth_g^{\otimes 2}\cdot \boldsymbol{\mathcal{F}}_{\bullet,\bullet}(*,*) \big\rangle \Big\}\bigg)_{g =
1}^H;\, \boldsymbol{0}\Bigg](z).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $z \in \amsmathbb{M}_{h}$ and $z_i \in \amsmathbb{M}_{h_i}$ for $i \in \{1,2\}$.

Then, for any $\eps >0$ and compact sets $\amsmathbb{K}_h \subset \amsmathbb C\setminus [\hat a^{\mathfrak m}_h,\hat b^{\mathfrak m}_h]$ indexed by $h \in [H]$, there exist a sequence of positive constants $(C_n)_{n \geq 1}$ depending only $\eps$, the compacts, and the constants in the assumptions, such that for any $n \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{> 0}$, $h_1,\ldots,h_n \in [H]$ and $z_i \in \amsmathbb{K}_{h_i}$ for $i \in [n]$, we have
\begin{align}
 \big|W_{1;h}(z) - W_{1;h}^{[1]}(z) - \N^{-1}W_{1;h}^{[2]}(z) \big| & \leq C_1\,\N^{-\frac{3}{2} + \varepsilon}, \\
 \max_{ l = 1,2} \big|W_{1;h}^{[l]}(z)\big| & \leq C_1, \\
 \big|W_{2;h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2) - W_{2;h_1,h_2}^{[0]}(z_1,z_2)\big| & \leq
C_2\,\N^{-\frac{1}{2} + \varepsilon}, \\
 \big|W_{2;h_1,h_2}^{[0]}(z_1,z_2)\big| & \leq C_2
\end{align}
and for $n \geq 3$
\begin{equation}
 \big|W_{n;h_1,\ldots,h_n}(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\big| \leq C_n\,\N^{-\frac{1}{2} + \varepsilon}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm: reformulated theorem of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] There exist constants $0<c,C<\infty$ such that the following holds. For all $n\ge1$, $s\ge1$ and $v\in R_{0,n\mathbf{e}_+}$ such that $|v|_1\leq n$, $\min\{v_1,v_2\}\ge C$ and $|v_2-v_1|\le s |v|_1^{2/3}$ we have

$$
{\mathbb{P}}\big(0, \mathbf{e}_1\in\pi(-v, n\mathbf{e}_+-v)\big) \leq C\Big(s^2 |v|_1^{-2/3} +\exp(-cs^3)\Big).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let (X, M) be a measurable space and let mu and nu be positive measures on M. One says that mu and nu are MUTUALLY SINGULAR, written mu perp nu, if there exists a set E in M with mu(E) = 0 and nu(X minus E) = 0; equivalently, X splits into two measurable pieces, one carrying all of nu and mu-null, the other carrying all of mu and nu-null. The relation is symmetric. For signed or complex measures the definition is applied to the total variations: mu perp nu means |mu| perp |nu|. Basic consequences: mu perp mu holds if and only if mu = 0; if nu is absolutely continuous with respect to mu (nu << mu) and nu perp mu, then nu = 0; if nu_1 perp mu and nu_2 perp mu then (nu_1 + nu_2) perp mu. CAUTIONS. (1) Mutual singularity is much stronger than 'nu is not absolutely continuous with respect to mu': a measure can fail to be absolutely continuous without being singular, and in general a measure splits into an absolutely continuous and a singular part (Lebesgue decomposition). (2) Singularity is a measure-theoretic, not a topological, smallness statement: the measure sum over n of 2^(-n) times the Dirac mass at the n-th rational is mutually singular with Lebesgue measure on R yet has full support, and the Cantor-Lebesgue measure is mutually singular with Lebesgue measure while being atomless. (3) The witness set E must be measurable; without that requirement the notion is vacuous or ill-posed. (4) Mutual singularity is not preserved by arbitrary uncountable sums of measures.
(X, M) is a measurable space
mu and nu are positive measures on M (for signed or complex measures the definition is applied to their total variations)
the separating set E is required to belong to M
title: Mutually singular measures

[Lemm 12 of arXiv:2609.01932, 'Essential dimension and faithful rank of finite $p$-gerbes'] Let $\cE$ be a vector bundle on a gerbe $\cG$, and put
$\band=\operatorname{Band}(\cG)$.  The local kernels
\[
\fN_x=\ker(\rho_{\cE,x})\triangleleft\underline{\Aut}(x)
\]
determine a normal subband $\band_{\cE}\subset\band$.  Moreover, $\cE$ is
faithful on geometric inertia if and only if $\band_{\cE}=1$.  If
$\fC\subset Z(\band)$ is a central subband, then the kernel of the
restricted action of $\fC$ on $\cE$ is $\band_{\cE}\cap\fC$.
We call $\band_{\cE}=\ker(\overline\rho_{\cE})$ the kernel subband of $\cE$.

body:
Let X,Y solve the synchronous Skorokhod equations in {|x|>=R}, R>0, with the same continuous driving path and inward-to-domain normal X/R or Y/R on the boundary. Write r=|X-Y| and let L_X,L_Y be their boundary regulators. Before r reaches zero, d log r = (1/(2R))(1-(|Y|^2-R^2)/r^2) dL_X + (1/(2R))(1-(|X|^2-R^2)/r^2) dL_Y. For reflected Brownian motions the same identity holds pathwise because the common Brownian increments cancel in X-Y. Thus coalescence at infinity is equivalent to this signed occupation functional tending to minus infinity. No sign or long-time behavior of that functional is proved here.

same continuous driving path
normal reflection into the exterior domain
boundary regulators supported on |X|=R or |Y|=R

body: [Proposition prop:pilot of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] Split a public pilot of $n_p=2m$ scores (disjoint from all calibration data): $\hat q_p$ is the conformal quantile of the first half, $N_W$ counts second-half scores in $W=[\hat q_p-h,\hat q_p+h]$ with $h\le\Delta/2$, and $\hat f_{\mathrm L}:=\max\{N_W,1\}/\big((1+c)\,2hm\big)$ for an accuracy $c\in(0,1)$. If $e_m(\delta_p/3)\le f_{\min}\Delta/2$ and $m\ge3\log(3/\delta_p)/(2c^{2}hf_{\min})$, then on a pilot event $\mathcal{G}_p$ of probability $\ge1-\delta_p$: $W\subseteq I$ and $\tfrac{1-c}{1+c}f_{\min}\le\hat f_{\mathrm L}\le f_{\max}$. Set $\beta:=2\hat\kappa B_n/(\hat f_{\mathrm L}\rho)$, $B_n$ as in Theorem~(thm:upper of the paper), with shared offset $u=\beta V$, $V\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1)$. For every pilot realization in $\mathcal{G}_p$, under Appendix~(app:upper of the paper)'s explicit side conditions ($\overline\beta_n\le\Delta/2$, tail $\le\rho/2$), two analysts satisfy $\mathbb{P}[\tau\ne\tau'\mid\mathcal{D}_p]\le\rho$; unconditionally $\mathbb{P}[\tau\ne\tau']\le\rho+\delta_p$, made exactly $\rho_\star$ by running the construction at $\rho_0=(\rho_\star-\delta_p)/(1-\delta_p)$ (for $0<\delta_p<\rho_\star$). Marginal coverage $\ge1-\alpha$ holds for \emph{every} pilot and offset realization, and the conditional band holds with rounding excess at most $\tfrac{2(1+c)}{1-c}\hat\kappa\kappa B_n/\rho$. A valid $\hat\kappa\ge\kappa$ remains the one input that cannot be certified from data, and $\hat\kappa=1.5$ was consistent with the target in every configuration of the safety study (Section~(sec:exp of the paper)). (Full statement and proof: Appendix~(app:upper of the paper).) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 33 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Let $\cX$ be a Banach space, and fix $x_0 \in \cX$, $r > 0$, $a \in \R$, and $T_0 > a$.
Suppose $f \colon [a,\infty) \times C_r(x_0) \to \cX$ is a continuous function such that for all $T > a$, there exists a $c_T < \infty$ such that
\[
\sup_{a \leq t \leq T} \norm{f(t,x) - f(t,y)}_{\cX} \leq c_T\norm{x-y}_{\cX} \qquad (x,y \in C_r(x_0)).
\]
Define
\[
M \coloneqq \sup_{(t,x) \in [a,T_0] \times C_r(x_0)} \norm{f(t,x)}_{\cX} < \infty.
\]
If $a < T < \min\left\{T_0,a + r/(2M)\right\}$ and $c \colon [a,T] \to C_{r/2}(x_0)$ is continuous, then there exists a continuous function $y \colon [a,T] \to C_r(x_0)$ such that
\begin{equation}
    y(t) = c(t) + \int_a^t f(s,y(s))\,\d s \qquad (a \leq t \leq T).
\end{equation}

body:
[Proposition prop:closed-graph-tikhonov of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] Let $F \in \mathbb{D}^{1,2}(H)$, $\mathcal{T} = DF \in L^2(\Omega; L_2(H_W, H))$, and $\gamma_F = \mathcal{T}\mathcal{T}^{*}$. Let $h \in H$ be a deterministic direction satisfying the range and moment conditions $h \in \operatorname{Ran}(\gamma_F)$ a.s.\ and $\gamma_F^{\dagger}h \in L^q(\Omega; H)$ for some $q \geq 2$, and consider the Tikhonov-regularised covering fields
\[
  u_h^{(\varepsilon)} \;:=\; \mathcal{T}^{*}\,(\gamma_F + \varepsilon I)^{-1}\,h, \qquad u_h \;:=\; \mathcal{T}^{*}\,\gamma_F^{\dagger}\,h, \qquad \varepsilon > 0,
\]
and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}, leftmargin=2.2em, itemsep=2pt]
 \item At each fixed $\varepsilon$ the field lies in the domain of the divergence: $u_h^{(\varepsilon)} \in \mathbb{D}^{1,2}(H_W) \subset \operatorname{Dom}(\delta_U)$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.
 \item The main term converges: $u_h^{(\varepsilon)} \to u_h$ in $L^2(\Omega; H_W)$ as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$.
 \item The correction term converges as well, since the family $\{\delta_U(u_h^{(\varepsilon)})\}_{\varepsilon > 0}$ is Cauchy in $L^2(\Omega)$ as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $u_h \in \operatorname{Dom}(\delta_U)$, and
\begin{equation}
  \delta_U(u_h) \;=\; \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\,\delta_U(u_h^{(\varepsilon)}) \qquad \text{in } L^2(\Omega).
\end{equation}

[Proposition tighten_multicurve of arXiv:2506.02611, '\textbf{The tight length spectrum of large-genus random hyperbolic surfaces with many cusp'] Let $X \in \mathcal{M}_{g,n+p}(\mathbf{L},\mathbf{K})$ and $\Gamma=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k)$ be a multicurve on $\Sigma_{g,n+p}$ whose curves are simple and pairwise disjoint and not freely homotopic in $\Sigma_{g,n}$ to each other, to a boundary or to a point. For each $i=1,\ldots, k$, there exists a closed geodesic $\gamma_i' \in [\gamma_i]_{g,n}$ of minimal length. Then the multicurve $\Gamma' = \{\gamma_1',\ldots,\gamma_k'\}$ consists of simple and pairwise disjoint curves.
    Furthermore, $\Gamma'$ is tight or $X$ contains two simple closed geodesics of equal length that are not boundaries.

\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(
\frac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k} X_i \le x
\,\Big|\, k\le M_\infty
\right)
\le \exp\bigl\{-I_{\vartheta_E}(x)\,k\bigr\},
\end{equation}

[Prop 4 of arXiv:2609.03188, 'Some generalizations of Oort's conjecture'] Let $\tau\in \Omega$.

Then $$X_w(\tau)=\bigsqcup_{j\in \J_\tau/\J_\tau\cap P_J} jY(w),$$
where $Y(w)=\{xI\in P_J/I\mid x^{-1}\tau \sigma(x)\in IwI\}$ is a {\it classical Deligne--Lusztig variety} in the flag variety $P_J/I$.
In particular, each $jY(w)$ is an irreducible component.

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The free cumulants $\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3,\ldots$ appear as a modification of the moments $M_1,M_2,M_3,\ldots\,$, and uniquely determine $\mu$. We have
$$\kappa_1=M_1$$
$$\kappa_2=-M_1^2+M_2$$
$$\kappa_3=2M_1^3-3M_1M_2+M_3$$
$$\kappa_4=-5M_1^4+10M_1^2M_2-2M_2^2-4M_1M_3+M_4$$
$$\vdots$$
in one sense, and in the other sense we have
$$M_1=\kappa_1$$
$$M_2=\kappa_1^2+\kappa_2$$
$$M_3=\kappa_1^3+3\kappa_1\kappa_2+\kappa_3$$
$$M_4=\kappa_1^4+6\kappa_1^2\kappa_2+2\kappa_2^2+4\kappa_1\kappa_3+\kappa_4$$
$$\vdots$$
with in both cases the correspondence being polynomial, with integer coefficients.

[Lemma 23 (Matrix exponential bounds) of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:exp_bounds}
For any \(H\in\mathbb{C}^{m \times m}\), \(\|e^H\|_{\op} \le e^{\|H\|_{\op}}\).
For any \(A,B\in\mathbb{C}^{m \times m}\),
\[
\|e^{A}-e^{B}\|_{\op}\le e^{\max\{\|A\|_{\op},\|B\|_{\op}\}}\ \|A-B\|_{\op}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\|e^{A}-e^{B}\|_{\mathrm F}\le e^{\max\{\|A\|_{\op},\|B\|_{\op}\}}\ \|A-B\|_{\mathrm F}.
\]

[Lemma lem: Concentration of spin overlaps under tp extr. of arXiv:2411.10271, '$A$-localized states for clock models on trees and their extremal decomposition into glass'] There exists a sequence of spacings $r=(r_i)_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$, in general depending on the model parameter, such that for any thinned branch $(\Lambda_n^r)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ with $\sum^\infty_{n=1}\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n^r|}<\infty$, the following holds. For $\mu_A$-almost every $\omega\in \Omega$, for $\pi(\cdot|\omega)$-almost every realization of $\sigma$, we have 
     \begin{equation}
         \limsup_{n\uparrow \infty}\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n^r|}\bigg|\sum_{v\in \Lambda^r_n}\bigg(\mathds{1}_{\sigma_v\neq \omega_v}-\pi(\sigma_v \neq \omega_v|\omega)\bigg)\bigg|=0.
     \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem backgeodlargedev of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] For every $\delta \in (0, \frac{1}{2})$, there exist constants $c, C, r_0 >0$ such that for all $\lambda \in (\delta, 1-\delta)$, $r \geq r_0$ and all $s \in [0, r^{1/3}]$
\[
{\mathbb{P}} \Big(\pi(\lambda; -\infty, 0)\cap H_{- \lfloor r \mathbf{u}_{\lambda} \rfloor}   \subseteq \big[ - \lfloor r \mathbf{u}_{\lambda} \rfloor - s r^{2/3} \mathbf{e}_1 , - \lfloor r \mathbf{u}_{\lambda} \rfloor + s r^{2/3} \mathbf{e}_1 \big]  \Big)
\geq 1 - C \exp(-c s^3).
\]

body:
PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Exact critical tanh two-input Gram chain: given current Gram [[q,c sqrt(qr)],[c sqrt(qr),r]], draw n iid centered Gaussian pairs (Ai,Bi) with that Gram and set Qnew=mean tanh(Ai)^2, Rnew=mean tanh(Bi)^2, Cnew=mean tanh(Ai)tanh(Bi). Write D=1-C/sqrt(QR), S=Q+R, V=Q^2+R^2, F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2, and delta=1-E[tanh(Ai)tanh(Bi)]/sqrt(F(q)F(r)). Probability norms and expectations are over the exact chain.  Initialize Q0=R0=s in (0,1], c0 in [-1,1], D0=1-c0; H_L=sum_(j=1)^L 1/j. Let K,Lambda be the finite uniform C010/C015 raw angular moment constants: conditional absolute bias <=K delta/n, raw squared error <=K delta^2/n, raw fourth error <=Lambda^4 delta^4/n^2. Put M=12K+3Lambda^4 and B_T=8650752 s exp(210+(639/2)T). For integer n>=27648 and L<=Tn, ||D_L exp(96 S_L)||_2 <=exp(192+MT/4) D0[1+61 B_T L H_L/n]. In particular for fixed 0<eps<1 and L<=n^(1-eps), this is at most C_eps D0, where Bstar=8650752 exp(1059/2) and C_eps=exp(192+M/4)[1+61 Bstar(1+1/(e eps))]. This is an amplitude estimate, not an angular approximation-error or complete Tensor Programs rate.
Fresh iid Gaussian rows and layers; zero bias, variance1/n, exactly tanh; deterministic equal initial variances s<=1. Uses C010,C011,C014,C015 v1 unaudited, plus audited C002 v2 and C004 v1. Universal K,Lambda are the current-state bias/MSE/fourth-noise constants.
Only C002 v2 and C004 v1 among these inputs have reviewer PASS; new dependencies remain unaudited.
