body:
[Thm 4 of arXiv:2609.02331, 'Metastability of Interacting Stochastic Systems with Countably Many Metastable States: Bey'] Suppose that Assumptions \ref{assu:U} and \ref{assu:M}
are in force. Then, the diffusion process $\{X_{\epsilon}(t)\}_{t\ge0}$
is metastable in the following sense:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Mixing) The process satisfies the local mixing condition: For each
$n\in\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathfrak{m}_{n}$ is the attractor, i.e., for
any collection $(x_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon>0}$ in $\mathcal{E}^{n}$,
\[
\lim_{\epsilon\to0}\mathbb{Q}^{\epsilon}_{x_{\epsilon}}\left[\mathcal{H}_{\mathfrak{m}_{n}}>\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{E}\setminus\mathcal{E}^{n}}\right]=0.
\]
\item (Convergence in law) For any $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $(x_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon>0}$
in $\mathcal{E}^{n}$, the trace laws ${\bf Q}^{\epsilon}_{x_{\epsilon}}$
converge weakly to the limit law ${\bf Q}_{n}$ as $\epsilon\to0$.
\item (Delta-negligibility) The excursions outside $\mathcal{E}$ is negligible,
i.e. for each $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, $(x_{\epsilon})_{\epsilon>0}$ in
$\mathcal{E}^{n}$, and $T>0$,
\[
\lim_{\epsilon\to0}{\rm E}^{\mathbb{Q}^{\epsilon}_{x_{\epsilon}}}\left[\int^{T}_{0}{\bf 1}\left\{ X_{\epsilon}(t)\notin\mathcal{E}\right\} {\rm d}t\right]=0.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2609.02331

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2608.07042, 'Limit Points of Reflow with Minibatch Optimal Transport'] We call a set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d$ $N$-cyclically monotone for $N\geq 2$ if it holds for all $(x^{(i)},y^{(i)})\in A$ and
$\tau\in\Sigma_N$ that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^N \|x^{(i)}-y^{(i)}\|^2\leq \sum_{i=1}^N \|x^{(i)}-y^{(\tau(i))}\|^2.
$$
Similarly, we call a transport plan $\gamma\in \mathcal P_2(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ $N$-cyclically monotone
if $\mathrm{supp}(\gamma)$ is $N$-cyclically monotone.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.07042, 'Limit Points of Reflow with Minibatch Optimal Transport'

[Proposition prop:mode of arXiv:2607.19844, 'Binomial probabilities at a fixed distance from the mode:\\ size-biasing and the complete '] The upper mode of $\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)$ is

	When $h=p$ (equivalently $(N+1)p\in\mathbb Z$), the lower adjacent point $\nu-1$ is also a mode.

[Definition 12 (Quantum triangles with  {possibly} thin vertices) of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Fix $W_1, W_2, W_3>0$. Let $I:=\{i\in\{1,2,3\}:W_i<\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\}$. Let $\tilde W_i = W_i$ if $i \not \in I$ and $\tilde W_i = \gamma^2 - W_i$ if $i \in I$. Sample $(S_0, (S_i)_{i \in I})$ from 
 \[\QT(\tilde W_1, \tilde W_2, \tilde W_3) \times \prod_{i\in I } (1-\frac{2W_i}{\gamma^2}) \Md_2(W_i).  \]
 Embed $S_0$ as $(\tilde D, \phi, \tilde a_1, \tilde a_2, \tilde a_3)$, for each $i \not \in I$ let $a_i = \tilde a_i$, and for each $i \in I$ embed $S_i$ as $(\tilde D_i, \phi, \tilde a_i, a_i)$ in such a way that the $\tilde D_i$ are disjoint and $\tilde D_i \cap \tilde D = \tilde a_i$. Let $D = \tilde D \cup \bigcup_{i \in I} \tilde D_i$ and let $\QT(W_1, W_2, W_3)$ be the law of $(D, \phi, a_1, a_2, a_3)/{\sim_\gamma}$.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try a direct cluster-expansion (Mayer-type) argument for the susceptibility at fixed p (2d) in the d -> infinity limit. Result: At p = lambda/(2d) the expected cluster size chi(p) has, for fixed lambda < 1, a convergent expansion as d -> infinity in powers of 1/d obtained by comparing the cluster to a branching process with Poisson(lambda) offspring and counting cycles: the first correction is the non-backtracking one: an exploration with s - 1 = 2d - 1 new neighbours per vertex has critical point 1/(s-1) = s^-1 + s^-2 + s^-3 + ..., which already gives a_1 = a_2 = 1 with s = 2d; the cycles of Z^d first change the expansion at order s^-3, where the 4-cycles move the coefficient from 1 to the known 7/2. This direct route reproduces a_1, a_2 by hand; a_3 = 7/2 is the first coefficient the cycles change, and getting it requires the 4-cycle corrections together with the self-avoidance of the exploration; I did not complete it. Existence of the expansion to all orders without the lace expansion would need a general theorem that the non-backtracking cycle corrections form an asymptotic series, which is a version of the lace expansion in disguise (the lace expansion IS the systematic bookkeeping of these corrections); a Mayer-type expansion at fixed lambda < 1 converges for the subcritical susceptibility, and p_c is then the divergence point of the series in lambda, whose location in powers of 1/d is obtained by inverting the series, which is a purely algebraic step if the expansion of chi is known to all orders with uniform error terms. So: an alternative derivation exists in principle via the convergent subcritical cluster expansion plus inversion, but the uniformity of the subcritical expansion up to lambda near 1 is exactly the difficult point. Computing a_4 by hand would require the next order of cycle corrections; not done. Obstruction: Uniformity of the subcritical cluster expansion up to the critical point; a_4 requires third-order cycle corrections.

[Thm thm-busemann-property of arXiv:2510.26123, 'Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations:\\ exact exponents and scaling limit'] Let ${\operatorname{XDP}} \in \{\operatorname{LDP} , \operatorname{SDP}\}$ and let $\mathcal X$ be the Busemann function as in Theorem~(thm-busemann of the paper). The following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),ref=(\roman*)]
\item  \textbf{Independent increments.} The increments $\{\mathcal X(k) - \mathcal X(k-1)\}_{k\in\mathbbm Z}$ are independent.
\item  \textbf{Stationary increments.} The increments $\{\mathcal X(k) - \mathcal X(k-1)\}_{k \geq 1}$ all have the same distribution, and the increments $\{\mathcal X(k) - \mathcal X(k-1)\}_{k \leq 0}$ all have the same distribution.
\item  \textbf{Bounds on the increments for $k\geq 1$.} In the LDP case, for $k\geq 1$ we have the bound $\mathcal X(k) - \mathcal X(k-1)  \leq -1$ . In the SDP case, for $k\geq 1$, we have the bound $\mathcal X(k) - \mathcal X(k-1) \geq -1$. 
\item  \textbf{Symmetry for $k\leq 0$.} For $k\leq 0$, we have $\mathcal X(k)-\mathcal X(k-1) \overset{d}{=} \mathcal X(k-1) - \mathcal X(k)$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2608.28245, 'I-FLOP: Fast Learning of Order and Parents from Interventional Data'] Fix $v\in V$ and $Z\subseteq V\setminus\{v\}$.
	Under Assumptions~\ref{assump:data-generating process}, \ref{assump:conservative intervention design}, and \ref{assump:env-proportions}, the pooled residual risk criterion $R(P) = \sigma^2_{v\mid P,\mathrm{pool}}$ has a unique sparsest minimizer $M_v^{\mathrm{pool}}(Z) = \operatorname{supp}(w_Z)$, where $w_Z = (\Sigma_{ZZ}^{\mathrm{pool}})^{-1}\Sigma_{Zv}^{\mathrm{pool}}$.
	Furthermore, for every candidate set $P\subseteq Z$ with $M_v^{\mathrm{pool}}(Z)\nsubseteq P$, there exists $u\in M_v^{\mathrm{pool}}(Z)\setminus P$ satisfying $\sigma^2_{v\mid P\cup\{u\},\mathrm{pool}} < \sigma^2_{v\mid P,\mathrm{pool}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $D$ be a long virtual knot diagram. 
For each classical crossing $c$ of $D$, either one of  ``we reach $c$ along overarc first" or ``we reach $c$ along underarc first" holds.

[Lemma lem:hill-scc of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] Under the conditions stated previously, if $i \in \overline{Z}$, then $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$, so that $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$ has one terminal SCC, which must include $u$.

\proof If $i = u$, then, by definition, $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$. If $i \not= u$, then $i \leadsto_G z$ for some $z \in Z$. By Definition~(def:hill of the paper).2 and 3, the last edge on any path from $i$ to $z$ in $G$ is rerouted to $u$ in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$, so that $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$, as claimed. The final assertion follows in consequence. \hfill \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem AnalyticStraightLine of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:\left[0,K\right]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$
be a continuous BV path with unit speed parametrisation. Let $s$ be a point at which
$\gamma$ is differentiable. Let $T\in(s,K]$ be chosen such that \[
\big|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}-\gamma'_{s}(t-s)\big|\leqslant\frac{1}{6}(t-s),\ \Big|\Big|\frac{\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}}{t-s}\Big|-1\Big|\leqslant\frac{1}{6}
\]for all $t\in(s,T]$ and
\[
\left|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}\right|<\left|\gamma_{T}-\gamma_{s}\right|
\]for all $t\in(s,T)$. Suppose that $\log S\left(\gamma\right)$ has infinite R.O.C. on
the interval $\left[s,T\right]$. Then the following two statements hold true.

\vspace{2mm}\noindent (i) One has
\[

\[
\int_{s}^{T}\Phi\left(d\gamma_{v}\right)=\int_{s}^{T}\Phi\left(dL_{v}\right).
\]

[Theorem theorem1 of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] Consider the  $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP), where in each run we keep \textbf{all} the new observed coupons. Let $T_{N,d}$ be the number of trials until all $N$ different types of coupons, which are uniformly distributed, are collected (at least once). Then,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb {E}\left[T_{N,d}\right]=\binom{N}{d} \sum_{k=1}^{N}\left(-1\right)^{k+1}\binom{N}{k}\Bigg(\binom{N}{d}-\binom{N-k}{d}\Bigg)^{-1}.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Express the escape probability through the branching-process representation for the one-cookie deterministic case. Result: In the deterministic environment with one cookie of strength p at each site (M = 1, delta = 2p - 1... transient iff delta > 1 which needs more than one cookie; take M = 2 cookies of strength p each, delta = 2(2p - 1) > 1 iff p > 3/4). The event of never returning to 0 after the first step: the walk must never come back, which in the branching-process picture (right excursions counted by the number of down-crossings of each edge) means the branching process with migration started from the edge (0,1) never produces a down-crossing of (0,1) into 0... the escape probability equals the probability that the total number of down-crossings of the edge (0,1) is zero, which is P(the branching process with migration started at 1 individual at level 1 has zero descendants at level 0) - not directly a standard extinction probability but a hitting probability of the time-reversed process. For the source's example [Zer05, Th. 18] the closed form exists; for general bounded stacks the escape probability is the solution of a finite-dimensional fixed-point equation obtained by conditioning on the first cookie stack at sites 1, 2, ...: define q_k = P(never return to 0 | walk currently at k, all cookies at sites >= k intact, cookies at sites < k in their post-visit states); the states of the sites already visited matter only through the remaining cookie counts, which for M bounded is a finite vector, and the walk's returns to 0 require descending through all visited sites; the escape probability then equals the probability of survival of a Markov chain on finite cookie-count vectors, computable numerically for given (M, p) but with no closed form in general. Recorded: reduction to a finite-state escape problem; closed form only in special cases. Obstruction: No closed form beyond special cases; the reduction gives a numerical procedure only.

[Lemma lem-expinteraction of arXiv:2604.14318, '\large The free energy of the interacting Bose gas:\\\medskip a variational description \\'] Suppose that the interaction potential $v$ satisfies Assumption (V). Recall that $W=W_R=[-R,R]^d$ and $W'=W_{R+M}\setminus W_R$. For any $M\in(0,\infty)$, there is a constant $C\in(0,\infty)$ (only depending on $d$, $\beta$, $v$ and $M$) such that, for any $R\in(0,\infty)$, and for any $ y, y_1,y_2\in W',x, x_1,x_2\in (W')^{\rm c}$,
\begin{eqnarray}
\mathbb{E}_{y,x}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({W'}})}}}\Big[\sum_{j_1,j_2=1}^{\ell(B)}\1_{\{j_1\not= j_2\}}V(B_{j_1},B_{j_2})\Big]
&\leq& C |y-x|,\\
\mathbb{E}_{y_1,x_1}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({W'}})}}}\otimes \mathbb{E}_{y_2,x_2}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({W'}})}}}\Big[\sum_{j_1=1}^{\ell(B^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({1}})}}})}\sum_{j_2=1}^{\ell(B^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({2}})}}})}V(B^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({1}})}}}_{j_1},B^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({2}})}}}_{j_2})\Big]
&\leq& C \Big(\big|[\underline y_1,\underline x_1]\cap [\underline x_2,\underline y_2]\big|+1\Big),\\
\mathbb{E}_{y,x}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({W'}})}}}\Big[\sum_{j_1=1}^{\ell(B)} V(B_{j_1},f)\Big]
&\leq& C g({\operatorname {dist}}(K_f,[y,x])),\qquad  f\in {\mathcal C }(W),
\end{eqnarray}
where $g$ is a function with $\lim_{r\to\infty}g(r)=0$, and we wrote $K_f$ for the $C_v$-neighbourhood of $ \{f(t)\colon t\in [0,\beta]\}$, where $C_v={\operatorname {supp}}\sup v$.

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2607.22374, 'Asymptotic properties of the heat equation driven by stochastic measure'] (Lemma 2.8~\cite{radbook})
Let $Z$ be an arbitrary set, and the function $q(z,x):
Z\times [j, j+1]\to\rr$ be such that all paths $q(z,\cdot)$ are continuous on $[j,j+1]$, $\aaa\subset(j,j+1]$ be a Borel set. Denote
\[
q_n(z,x)=\sum_{1\le k\le 2^n}q(z,{d}_{(k-1)n}^{(j)}){\bf 1}_{\Delta_{kn}^{(j)}}(x).
\]
Then the random function
\[
\eta(z)=\int_{\aaa}q(z, x)\,d\mu(x),\ z\in Z,
\]
has a version
\begin{equation}\begin{split}
\widetilde{\eta}(z)  = \int_{\aaa}q_0(z,x)\,d\mu(x)
+\sum_{n\ge 1}\Bigl(\int_{\aaa}q_n(z,x)\,d\mu(x)-\int_{\aaa}q_{n-1}(z,x)\,d\mu(x)\Bigr)
\end{split}
\end{equation}
such that for all $\beta>0$, $\omega\in\Omega$, $z\in Z$
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\widetilde{\eta}(z)| \le  |q(z,j)\mu(\aaa)|\\
  + \Bigl\{\sum_{n\ge 1}2^{n\beta}
\sum_{1\le k\le 2^{n}}|q(z,d_{kn}^{(j)})-q(z,d_{(k-1)n}^{(j)})|^2\Bigr\}^{1/2}\\
\times\Bigl\{\sum_{n\ge 1}2^{-n\beta}\sum_{1\le k\le 2^{n}}|\mu(\Delta_{kn}^{(j)}\cap\aaa)|^2\Bigr\}^{1/2}.
\end{split}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 3 of arXiv:2607.22374

body: [Prop of arXiv:2410.23859, 'Subcritical regimes in the Poisson Boolean percolation on Ahlfors regular spaces'] Let $s>0$. Let $(S, d)$ be an ultrametric space. Let $\mu$ be an $s$-Ahlfors regular measure on $S$ and $\rho$ be a probability measure on $(0, \infty)$. If $\int_0^\infty R^s \rho(dR) < \infty$, then $\sup_{x\in S}\mathbb{P}_\lambda(M(x) = \infty) = 0$ for all $\lambda \in (0, \infty)$. If $\int_0^\infty R^s \rho(dR) = \infty$, then $\mathbb{P}_\lambda(\mathscr{W} = S) = 1$ for $\lambda \in (0,\infty)$.

body:
[Prop alphgrndstateprop of arXiv:2411.00629, '\Large Transformation of Stochastic Recursions and Critical Phenomena in the Analysis of t'] Let $\alpha>1$. Consider the stochastic Picard ground state iterations $X_n(t)$ (equation X_n-eq of the paper) with constant 
ground states $X_0(t)\equiv \delta >0$. Denote $N_t=|\partial V(t)|$ as before.  Then, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $u_0\in[0,1]$ then 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $\delta\in(0,1)$, 
$$X_n\to\underline{X}=\begin{cases}
0 \ &\ \text{if}\ S<t\\
u_0^{N_t}, \ &\ \text{if}\ S\ge t.\end{cases}$$
In particular, the minimal solution $u(t) = \underline{u}(t)={\mathbb{E}}(\underline{X})$ is 
well-defined and $\underline{u}(t)\to0$ as $t\to\infty$.
\item[(ii)] For $\delta=1$, $$X_n\to\overline{X}=\begin{cases}
1 \ &\ \text{if}\ L<t\\
u_0^{N_t}, \ &\ \text{if}\ L\ge t.\end{cases}$$
In particular, $u(t) = \overline{u}(t)={\mathbb{E}}(\overline{X})$ is well-defined and $\overline{u}(t)\to1$ as $t\to\infty$ 
\item[(iii)] For $\delta >1$, the limit 
$$X_\infty(t) = \lim_{n\to\infty}X_n(t) = \begin{cases}
\infty \ &\ \text{if}\ S<t\\
u_0^{N_t}, \ &\ \text{if}\ S\ge t.\end{cases}$$
In particular,  ${\mathbb{E}}(X_\infty(t))=\infty$ for all $t>0$ 
\end{enumerate}
\item Suppose that $u_0>1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $\delta\in [0,1)$,
\[X_n\to\overline{X}=\begin{cases}
0 ,\ &\ \text{if}\ S<t\\
u_0^{N_t}, \ &\ \text{if}\ S\ge t.\end{cases}\]
In particular, for all $t>0$
$$\underline{u}(t) ={\mathbb{E}}(\underline{X}(t))
\ \begin{cases} <\infty, \ &\ \text{if}\ u_0<(2\alpha-1)/4,\\
                         =\infty, \ & \text{in finite time if}\  u_0>2\alpha-1,\\
                         \text{unknown} & \text{in other cases.}
                        \end{cases}
      $$
 If there is a locally integrable function $g$ such that $X_n\le g$ for all $n$, then
  $\underline{u}(t)={\mathbb{E}}\underline{X}(t)<\infty$.
\item[(ii)] For $\delta =1$, 
$$X_n(t)\to\overline{X}(t) =\begin{cases}
\infty & \text{on} \ [N_t=\infty]\\
u_0^{N_t} & \text{on} \ [N_t<\infty].
\end{cases}$$
In particular, if $\alpha\in(1,2)$, then $\mathbb{E}(\overline{X}(t)) = \infty$, and if $\alpha>2$ then 
$\overline{X}(t)\in\mathbb{R}$ is well-defined for all $t>0$, while
\[
\overline{u}(t) ={\mathbb{E}}(\overline{X}(t))
\ \begin{cases} <\infty, \ &\ \text{if}\ u_0<(2\alpha-1)/4-(6\alpha^2-15\alpha+4)/4(\alpha-1)(2\alpha-1),\\
                         =\infty, \ & \text{in finite time if}\  u_0>2\alpha-1\ \text{or}\ \alpha\in(0,2),\\
                         \text{unknown} & \text{in other cases}.
                        \end{cases}
\]
\item[(iii)] For $\delta>1$, 
$$X_n\to{X}_{\infty}=\begin{cases}
\infty \ &\ \text{if}\ S<t\\
u_0^{N_t} \ &\ \text{if}\  S\ge t.\end{cases}$$
$u(t) ={\mathbb{E}}({X}_\infty(t)) = \infty$ for all $t>0$.
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}

body: [Lem 2 (The limit of a martingale partition) of arXiv:2604.12853, 'Coupling Markov Chains \\with a Common Image Chain'] Let $I$ be a countable set and for each $i \in I$ let $(U_t^{(i)})_{t \ge 0}$ be a non-negative martingale, all with respect to the same filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on a common probability space. Suppose that $ \sum_{i \in I} U^{(i)}_t   \le 1$ a.s. for every $t \ge 0$. Then almost surely \[\sum_{i \in I} \lim_{t \to \infty} U^{(i)}_t = \lim_{t \to \infty} \sum_{i \in I} U_t^{(i)}.\]

	\[P=\alpha_1Q_1+\ldots+\alpha_nQ_n+\alpha_{n+1}Q_{n+1}.\]
	Moreover, the decomposition is unique.

[Proposition 2 (Classical scale in anchored local form) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] There exist absolute constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
c\,\Bigl(R_\ast+\inf_{\mu\in\Delta(T)}\Phi_{\mu,\ast}\Bigr)
\le
\mathbb E\sup_{x\in T}X_x
\le
C\,\Bigl(R_\ast+\inf_{\mu\in\Delta(T)}\Phi_{\mu,\ast}\Bigr).
\end{equation}
Moreover, since the process is centered and anchored,
\[
\mathbb E\sup_{x\in T}|X_x|
\asymp
\mathbb E\sup_{x\in T}X_x.
\]
Therefore
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\sup_{x\in T}|X_x|
\asymp
R_\ast+\inf_{\mu\in\Delta(T)}\Phi_{\mu,\ast}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Classical scale in anchored local form

body:
[campaign status: unreviewed - author-checked against the source's exact wording; verification unreviewed] For a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator the ITINERARY of a trajectory is the sequence of fixed-point neighbourhoods it visits; Rozikov (2009, p. 4) asks whether some trajectory has a periodic itinerary. CLAIM, in two halves. (i) YES at m = 3, by an example already in the literature: for the cyclic Volterra operator with a = b = c = 1, matrix A = [[0,1,-1],[-1,0,1],[1,-1,0]], whose leading 2x2 minor is 1 so the operator is transversal and whose fixed-point set - the three vertices and the centre - is finite, the itinerary of every non-fixed interior point is periodic, 1 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> ..., with sojourns 12, 51, 1073, ... growing geometrically by the heteroclinic-cycle mechanism of Ganikhodzhaev and Zanin (2004). (ii) NO in general: at m = 4, Ganikhodjaev and Zanin (arXiv:1205.3841, Theorem 5) show the trajectory moves along the routes 1-4-3-2-1, 1-4-2-1 or 1-4-3-1, and a simulated cyclic-type m = 4 map produces the MIXED itinerary 1,4,3,2,1,4,2,1 - so itineraries need not be periodic. THE SHARP OPEN QUESTION, which is what the source presumably meant: is every itinerary eventually periodic, or which matrices A force it? The 2012 route analysis is the starting point. A periodic ITINERARY is a symbol sequence, not a periodic ORBIT: periodic orbits are typically absent while periodic itineraries need not be.
transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator with a finite fixed-point set
the object asked for is a periodic ITINERARY, a symbol sequence, not a periodic orbit
m = 3 for the affirmative half; m = 4 for the negative half

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $a, \eta>0$, $k,d\in\mathbb N$, and $d\ge2$. There exists
a constant $C:=C(a,\eta,k,d)>0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every
log-concave measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$, and every polynomial mapping
$
f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\in\mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^k)
$
satisfying
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\mu}(f_j)\ge a
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}
\quad
\text{and}
\quad
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge \eta,
\]
one has
\[
\mu(f\in A)
\le
C\bigl(\lambda_k(A)\bigr)^{\frac{1}{k(d-1)+1}}
\]
for every Borel set $A\subset\mathbb R^k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.01516

Similarly, for $\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)$ and $\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0)$ as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.sym} and \eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.chaos}, we have
	\[\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)
	=\sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0))\,.\]

\begin{proof}
   By the definitions of these sets, we have
    \[
        \sym(\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha))
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip}}{=} 
        \sym\bigg(
            \bigcap_{\epsilon>0} \bigcup_{L>0}
            \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)
        \bigg)
        \subseteq 
        \bigcap_{\epsilon>0} \bigcup_{L>0}
        \sym\Big(\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)\Big)
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym}}{=} \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)\,.
    \]
Similarly, we have
	\begin{align*}
	&\sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0))
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.chaos}}{=}\sym\bigg(
	\bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L > 0} \cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\bigg)\\
	&\qquad\subseteq
	\bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L > 0} \sym\Big(\cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\Big)
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.sym}}{=}
	\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.
	\end{align*}
Therefore it suffices to show the reverse inclusions.

    Consider any $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$ and a sequence $\epsilon_n\downarrow0$.

        \bigg\} \le \epsilon_n\,.
    \]
This implies the existence of $\tilde{\mu}_{n,j} \in \sym^{-1}(\mu)$ such that
	\[
	\WERR(\cA_{n,j},\tilde{\mu}_{n,j})
	=\max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(
            \mu(\cA_{n,j}),
            \tilde{\mu}_{n,j}

        \bigg\} \le \epsilon_n\,.
	\]

    Then
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{n,j}),

    \]
    where the last inequality holds after omitting finitely many $j$'s.
    By passing to a subsequence of the $\epsilon_n$ we can ensure that as $n\to\infty$, $\tilde\mu^n$ converges in $\bbW_2$ to $\tilde\mu \in \sym^{-1}(\mu)$.
    Then
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{n,j}),\tilde \mu\Big) \le \tilde\epsilon_n \equiv 2\epsilon_n + \bbW_2(\tilde{\mu}_n, \tilde\mu)\,.
    \]
Recalling the definition \eqref{e:cM.Lip} of $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)$, it follows that

[Proposition 22 (Cross-regularity) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Assume \hyperref[ass:PJG]{\textup{(A1)}}--\hyperref[ass:D]{\textup{(A4)}}. There exist a constant \(C_{\mathrm{cross}}>0\) and a measurable function
\(b:\R^d\to[0,\infty)\) such that, for all \(x,y\in\R^d\) and all \(t\in(0,\lambda]\),
\[
  \KL\!\bigl(\delta_x \widehat P \,\big\|\, \delta_y P_t\bigr)
  \;\le\;
  \frac{C_{\mathrm{cross}}}{1-e^{-K't}}\,\|x-y\|^2
  \;+\;
  b(x)^2,
\]
where
\[
  b(x)^2 \le C\,\lambda^2\bigl(1+\|x\|^{2\ell+2}\bigr).
\]
In particular, taking \(t=\lambda\), one may take
\[
  c'=\frac{C_{\mathrm{cross}}}{\lambda}.
\]

[Proposition eq:sparse-profile-net-bound of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:sharp-profile-energy}
Suppose that the random field satisfies \(({\rm PT})_p\).
Put
\[
 \pi_N(a):=
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1)}
 \mathbb P\{\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert\ge a\}.
\]
Put
\[
 \mathcal S_{N,k}
 =\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
       \abs{\operatorname{supp}x}\le k\},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_p=\frac{p^{p+1}}{p!}.
\]
For \(1\le k\le N\), \(a>0\), and
\(0<\delta<\Lambda_p^{-1}\),
\begin{align}
 &\mathbb P\left\{
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal S_{N,k}}\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert\ge a
 \right\}\notag\\
 &\qquad\le
 \binom Nk\left(1+\frac2\delta\right)^k
 \pi_N\bigl((1-\Lambda_p\delta)a\bigr).
 
\end{align}
Consequently, if \(1\le k_N\le N\), \(k_N=o(N)\), and
\(a_N\to a>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb P\left\{
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal S_{N,k_N}}\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert
 \ge a_N\right\}
 \le-\frac{a^2}{2}.
\end{equation}
The same conclusions hold for the standard symmetric-coordinate model
whenever its field satisfies \(({\rm PT})_p\); the profile MGF and
orbit-coordinate joint bounds described above are sufficient.

body:
[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(Q_T\) be a Kac walk of length $T$, and let
	\(I\subseteq [d]\), \(|I|=m\), be fixed. Let \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and
	\(0<\eta<1/2\). Suppose
	\[
	T
	\ge
	10d\log\left(\frac{2d}\eta\right)
	\qquad \text{and}
	\qquad
	m
	\ge
	64\varepsilon^{-2}\log\left(\frac{8d}\eta\right).
	\]
	Then, with probability at least \(1-\eta\),
	\[
	\kappa_I(Q_T)
	\le
	1+\varepsilon
	\]
	and
	\[
	\norm{Q_T}_\infty
	\le
	3\sqrt{\frac{\log(d/\eta)}{d}}.
	\]

body:
[Proposition geoprop of arXiv:2412.08334, 'Maker-Breaker on Galton-Watson trees'] The probability of Breaker winning on an instantly revealed GW-tree with offspring distribution 
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
		\item $\xi\sim\mathrm{Geo}_{\mathbb{N}}(s)$, i.e.\ $p_k=s\,(1-s)^{k-1}$ for $k\geq 1$, equals
		\[p=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-4s}}{2\,(1-s)}\quad\text{and}\quad \bar{p}=\frac{1-2s-\sqrt{1-4s}}{2\,(1-s)}=p-\frac{s}{1-s}\]
		respectively (depending on who starts the game) for parameter $s\in(0,\frac14]$. Further it holds $p=\bar{p}=1$, for $s\in(\frac14,1]$.
		\item $\xi\sim\mathrm{Geo}_{\mathbb{N}_0}(s)$, i.e.\ $p_k=s\,(1-s)^{k}$ for $k\geq 0$, equals
		\[p=\frac{1+s-\sqrt{(1-s)\,(1-5s)}}{2\,(1-s)}\text{  and  }\  \bar{p}=\frac{1-s-\sqrt{(1-s)\,(1-5s)}}{2\,(1-s)}=p-q\]
		respectively (depending on who starts the game) for parameter $s\in(0,\frac15]$. Further it holds $p=\bar{p}=1$, for $s\in(\frac15,1]$.
	\end{enumerate}

body:
[Thm 16 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] For $\calX_n=(X_n,d^{X_n},\rho_{X_n},\mu_{X_n}),\;\calX=(X,d^X,\rho_X,\mu_X)\in\frK_{\bullet}(\tau)$,
the following conditions are equivalent to each other.
\begin{itemize}
  \item [$\mathrm{(i)}$]There exist a compact metric space $(M,d^M,\rho_M)$ and root-preserving isometric embeddings $f_n:X_n\to M,\;f:X\to M$
  such that $f_n(X_n)\to f(X)$ in the Hausdorff topology, and $\mu_{X_n}\circ f_n^{-1}\to \mu_{X}\circ f^{-1}$ weakly.  
  \item [$\mathrm{(ii)}$]There exist a compact metric space $(M,d^M)$ and isometric embeddings $f_n:X_n\to M,\;f:X\to M$
  such that $f_n(X_n)\to f(X)$ in the Hausdorff topology, $f_n(\rho_{X_n})\to f(\rho_X)$ in $M$,
  and $\mu_{X_n}\circ f_n^{-1}\to \mu_{X}\circ f^{-1}$ weakly.
  \item [$\mathrm{(iii)}$]$d^{\tau,\BL^{\kappa}}_{\frK_{\bullet}}(\calX_n,\calX)\to 0$
\end{itemize}
In particular, $d^{\tau,\BL^{\kappa}}_{\frK_{\bullet}}$ induces the rooted compact Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov topology.

[Definition of arXiv:2411.17104, 'Two-barriers-reflected BSDE with Rank-based Data'] A function $v(\cdot,\cdot) \in C([0,T]\times \Gamma^{n})$ is called a viscosity subsolution (respectively, supersolution) to ($(4 of the paper)$) on condition that it satisfies for any $ x\in \Gamma^{n}$
\[
g(x)\geq v(T,x)\;\;(respectively,\;g(x) \leq v(T,x)),
\]
and for any  $\varphi(\cdot,\cdot) \in  C^{1,2}_{b}([0,T] \times \Gamma^{n})$, whenever $(t,x)\in[0,T)\times \Gamma^{n}$ is a local maximum (respectively, minimum) of $v(\cdot,\cdot) - \varphi(\cdot,\cdot)$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\min\Big\{v(t,x)-L(t,x), \max\Big\{v(t,x)-U(t,x),\\
\qquad \qquad \qquad\quad\;\qquad-\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial t}(t,x)-
\mathcal{L}\varphi(t,x)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma \triangledown \varphi(t,x))  \Big\}\Big\} \leq 0,\;x \in \Pi^{n},\\
\min\left\{\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial x_{k+1}}(t,x)-\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial x_{k}}(t,x), \min\Big\{v(t,x)-L(t,x),\max\Big\{v(t,x)-U(t,x),\right.\\
\left.\left.\left.
\qquad \qquad  \qquad \quad  -\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial t}(t,x)-\mathcal{L}\varphi(t,x)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma \triangledown \varphi(t,x))  \right\}\right\} \right\} \leq 0,\; x \in F_{k},\;k=1,\cdots,n.
\end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray*}
(respectively,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\min\Big\{v(t,x)-L(t,x), \max\Big\{v(t,x)-U(t,x),\\
\qquad \qquad \qquad\quad\;\qquad-\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial t}(t,x)-
\mathcal{L}\varphi(t,x)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma \triangledown \varphi(t,x))  \Big\}\Big\}\geq 0,\; x \in \Pi^{n},\\
\max\Big\{\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial x_{k+1}}(t,x)-\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial x_{k}}(t,x), \min\Big\{v(t,x)-L(t,x), \max\Big\{v(t,x)-U(t,x),\\
\qquad \qquad \qquad\quad\;\qquad-\frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial t}(t,x)-
\mathcal{L}\varphi(t,x)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma \triangledown \varphi(t,x))  \Big\}\Big\}\Big\} \geq 0,\;x \in F_{k},\;k=1,\cdots,n.)
\end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray*}

In all, if a function $v(\cdot,\cdot)\in C([0,T]\times \Gamma^{n})$ is both a viscosity supersolution and subsolution, it is called a viscosity solution to ($(4 of the paper)$).

STATUS: proof (unaudited), own-work draft. Exact normal linear-stability classification of every finite fixed point of joint-head factored-attention GD at every eta>0: the stationary curve v=0,kq=p_bar has tangent multiplier 1 and normal multipliers 1-eta lambda_+/- with lambda_+/-=(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2(k^2+q^2)))/2. One normal direction is always repelling; the other attracts exactly when k^2+q^2<(4/eta^2-2A/eta)/B^2, is neutral at equality, and repels beyond. Every positive fixed step loses the attracting normal direction at sufficiently unbalanced factorizations.

# Target 1: exact normal stability of the factored GD stationary curve

Version 1, proof unaudited. This is a linearized stability classification;
it does not claim a nonlinear flip bifurcation or a full-space GD basin theorem.

Assume precisely the n-example factored model of claim 010:
0<a_i<b_i, b_i,kappa_i>0, logistic average loss of
v h_i(kq), h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), and simultaneous Euclidean GD
with any fixed eta>0. Let p_bar<0 be the unique mean root and define

 A=mean_i h_i(p_bar)^2/4>=0,
 B=mean_i h_i'(p_bar)/2>0.

All finite stationary points, equivalently all GD fixed points, form the
curve E={v=0,kq=p_bar}. At such a point write S=k^2+q^2>=2|p_bar|.
The GD Jacobian has tangent multiplier 1 and normal multipliers

 mu_-=1-eta lambda_-, mu_+=1-eta lambda_+,
 lambda_+/-=(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2 S))/2.

Here lambda_-<0<lambda_+, hence mu_->1 everywhere: no point of E is
linearly attracting in all normal directions. The other normal direction is

* strictly attracting in the linearization when eta lambda_+<2;
* neutral with multiplier -1 when eta lambda_+=2;
* strictly repelling with multiplier less than -1 when eta lambda_+>2.

Let
 J_eta=(4/eta^2-2A/eta)/B^2.

The first case is EXACTLY S<J_eta, the middle case exactly S=J_eta,
and the last exactly S>J_eta. Equivalently, with C=k^2-q^2,
S=sqrt(C^2+4p_bar^2): there is an attracting normal direction only if
J_eta>2|p_bar|, and then precisely at

 |C|<sqrt(J_eta^2-4p_bar^2).

Equality gives neutral normal points when J_eta>=2|p_bar|. If J_eta
is smaller than 2|p_bar|, every point is repelling in both normal directions.
In particular, for EVERY eta>0, sufficiently unbalanced factorizations on
E are normally repelling in both directions. There is no positive constant
step that preserves the flow's one attracting normal direction uniformly
along the entire stationary curve. This does NOT imply an open basin of
cycles or disprove a full-space almost-everywhere GD endpoint theorem.

## Proof

The fixed-point condition is gradient L=0, classified in proof 008.
Its loss Hessian at E is
 [[A,-Bq,-Bk],[-Bq,0,0],[-Bk,0,0]].
The tangent vector (0,k,-q) is in its kernel. In the orthonormal basis
e_v=(1,0,0), e_s=(0,q,k)/sqrt(S) of the normal plane, the Hessian is
 [[A,-B sqrt(S)],[-B sqrt(S),0]].
The quadratic characteristic polynomial is lambda^2-A lambda-B^2 S,
which yields lambda_+/- and their signs. The GD Jacobian is I-eta Hessian,
proving the multipliers and their linear classifications.

For equivalence with J_eta, consider the polynomial
f(z)=z^2-Az-B^2 S, whose positive zero is lambda_+ and negative zero
lambda_-. Since 2/eta>0, lambda_+<2/eta is equivalent to
f(2/eta)>0, or S<J_eta; equality and the reverse inequality follow likewise.
This avoids squaring a potentially negative expression 4/eta-A.
Finally S^2=C^2+4p_bar^2 by algebra, and S is unbounded along E by
taking k->infinity, q=p_bar/k. All asserted threshold statements follow.

## Scope of the obstruction

The obstruction is to a PARTICULAR transfer from flow to GD: retaining
one attracting normal direction uniformly on every imbalance leaf at fixed
step. It is not an obstruction to every possible discrete-time proof.
The imbalance leaves themselves are not invariant under GD:
C_+=(1-eta^2 v^2 G^2)C. Both facts must be accounted for in further work.
Normal multipliers on the unit circle require separate nonlinear analysis;
no attracting two-cycle is claimed. Scalar genuine self-attention embeddings
of this family are supplied in claim 008.
Coupled n>=2 scalar h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), 0<a_i<b_i, b_i,kappa_i>0; logistic average loss; simultaneous Euclidean GD. A=mean h_i(p_bar)^2/4, B=mean h_i'(p_bar)/2, mean h_i(p_bar)=0. Linear normal stability only.

body:
[Lemm 8 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (closeness in $d_{BL}$ implies closeness of mixed moments, bounded case)
Let $X_1,...X_4,X_1',...,X_4'$ be random variables such that
\[
d_{BL}\big( (X_1,...,X_4),\ (X_1',...,X_4') \big) \leq \alpha,
\]
where $\alpha \geq 0$. 
Assume that there exists $L \in [1,\infty)$ such that $|X_i|,|X_i'|\leq L$ for all $i=1,...4$. Then for all non-negative integers $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ with $q=p_1+p_2+p_3+p_4 > 0$ it is the case that
\[
| \E \Pi_{i=1}^4 X_i^{p_i} - \E \Pi_{i=1}^4 X_i'^{p_i}| \leq 2q L^q \alpha.
\]

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c819e091264a02754ed335e688dca669f4ee1204e8e498dcbcfd50e98e207424","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c8/c819e091264a02754ed335e688dca669f4ee1204e8e498dcbcfd50e98e207424.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:c820a93e6e753a86c21e6abbb36df00871ed0282d81fbeb0fdaa8fbebf442e9a","bundle_entry_key":"2605-23292-lemma-7-amainlemma","bundle_id":"population.tex-extract-s3_036","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"tex-extract-20260907/bundle_s3_036.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.arxiv.mathematics:arxiv-2605-23292-lemm-7-amainlemma","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Paper's own proof, opening: If $\alpha=0$, the distribution of $(X_1,\hdots,X_4)$ coincides with that of  $(X_1',\hdots,X_4')$ and the bound holds trivially. We thus assume henceforth $\alpha>0$. The goal is to control 
$| \E \Pi_{i=1}^4 X_i^{p_i} - \E \Pi_{i=1}^4 X_i'^{p_i}|$ via a judicious choice of a 
Lipschitz function on $\R^4$.

To this end, define $f: [-L,L]^4 \to \R$ by $f(s,t,u,v) = s^{p_1}t^{p_2}u^{p_3}v^{p_4}$ and observe that $f$ is continuous and hence Lipschitz on the bounded domain $[-L,L]^4$.

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: the Hoelder exponent satisfies 0 < alpha < 1 strictly, and the Lebesgue exponent satisfies 1 < p < infinity strictly. The reason is that the second derivatives of the Newtonian potential are given by a singular integral operator, which is bounded on C^{0,alpha} and on L^p only in the open ranges. Failure at alpha = 0 (continuous right-hand side does not give a C^2 solution): in the plane put u(x) = (x_1^2 - x_2^2) (log(1/r))^{1/2} for 0 < r = |x| < 1/2, u(0) = 0. A computation with u = p g, p = r^2 cos(2 theta) harmonic and g = (log(1/r))^{1/2}, using Laplacian(p g) = 4 p g'/r + p (g'' + g'/r), gives Laplacian u = -cos(2 theta) ( 2 (log(1/r))^{-1/2} + (1/4)(log(1/r))^{-3/2} ), which extends continuously by 0 at the origin, while D_{11}u = 2(log(1/r))^{1/2} + o(1) blows up. Since u is C^1 and C^infinity off the origin, it solves Laplacian u = f distributionally on the ball with f continuous; no C^2 solution of Laplacian v = f exists near 0, because v - u would be harmonic hence smooth. (Consistently, this f is continuous but not Dini continuous, and Dini continuity is the correct substitute hypothesis.) Failure at alpha = 1: with q = x_1^3 - 3 x_1 x_2^2 and g = log(1/r), the function u = q g has Laplacian u = -6 q/r^2 = -6 r cos(3 theta), which is Lipschitz, while D_{111}u = 6 log(1/r) + O(1) is unbounded, so u is not in C^{2,1}. Failure at p = infinity: u = (x_1^2 - x_2^2) log(1/r) has Laplacian u = -4 cos(2 theta) in L^infinity while D_{11}u = 2 log(1/r) + O(1) is not bounded, so Laplacian u in L^infinity does not give u in W^{2,infinity} = C^{1,1}; the correct endpoint statement is Laplacian u in L^infinity implies D^2 u in BMO. Failure at p = 1: let f_k = rho_{1/k} be standard mollifiers and u_k = Gamma convolved with f_k, so Laplacian u_k = f_k with ||f_k||_{L^1} = 1 and ||u_k||_{L^1(B_2)} bounded; on B_1 minus the origin D_{12}u_k converges pointwise to D_{12}Gamma, whose size is comparable to |x|^{-n} and hence not integrable near 0, so by Fatou ||D^2 u_k||_{L^1(B_1)} tends to infinity. No estimate of the form ||D^2u||_{L^1} <= C(||Laplacian u||_{L^1} + ||u||_{L^1}) can hold; the correct endpoint statements are weak-L^1 bounds and the Hardy space result Laplacian u in H^1 implies D^2u in L^1. Practical consequence: from f merely continuous (or bounded) one gets u in W^{2,p}_loc for every finite p and u in C^{1,alpha}_loc for every alpha < 1, but not, in general, u in C^2 - the first example above is exactly the obstruction (for particular right-hand sides, a smooth f say, the solution is of course C^2).
title: Pitfall: Schauder and Calderon-Zygmund Estimates Fail at the Endpoints (C^0, L^1, L^infinity)

For n servers, Poisson jobs of rate lambda*n/k routing to uniform k-subsets, and k tagged arrival streams observed exactly on [0,T], let H count tagged servers hit per job and beta=(lambda*n/k)*P(H>=2). Their joint path total variation from independent rate-lambda Poisson streams is at least 1-exp(-beta*T). If k tends to infinity with k=o(sqrt(n)), beta~lambda*k^3/(2*n). At k/n^(1/3)->c>0, the liminf is at least 1-exp(-lambda*T*c^3/2). Conversely k=o(n^(1/3)) gives path TV tending to zero by the delete-and-restore coupling. This proves a path-coupling obstruction, not a necessary threshold for a stationary queue vector at a single time.

Exact continuous arrival paths

body: Let (mu_eps) be probability measures on a topological space X satisfying a large deviation principle with good rate function I as eps -> 0+, and let phi: X -> R be bounded and continuous. Varadhan's lemma states that the limit as eps -> 0 of eps times the log of the integral over X of exp(phi(x)/eps) mu_eps(dx) equals sup_{x in X} (phi(x) - I(x)). The boundedness hypothesis on phi can be relaxed to a mild exponential tail (moment) condition. This is a Laplace-type asymptotic for LDP-obeying measures, generalizing Laplace's method for integrals. Due to S. R. S. Varadhan.
title: Varadhan's lemma

[Defi Def:W-cont-map of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] Suppose $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ are
   weighted polyhedra of the same type. 
   A \emph{W-continuous map} from $(X,\lambda)$ to 
   $(X',\lambda')$ is a continuous map $f: X\rightarrow X'$   which satisfies: for all $x\in X$,
   $$ \begin{cases}
   \lambda'(f(x)) \mid \lambda(x),  &  \text{if  $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ are of ascending type}; \\
   \lambda(x) \mid \lambda'(f(x)),  &  \text{if  $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ are of descending type}.
 \end{cases}  
   $$  
    We also denote such a map by $f: (X,\lambda)\rightarrow (X',\lambda')$ to indicate its W-continuity
    since the definition of $f$ depends on the type of the weighted polyhedra involved.
   Moreover, $f$ is called \emph{weight-preserving} if 
$\lambda'(f(x))=\lambda(x)$ for all $x\in X$.\vskip 0.1cm

We say that $(X,\lambda)$ is \emph{isomorphic} to $(X',\lambda')$ if there exists a weight-preserving homeomorphism from $(X,\lambda)$ to $(X',\lambda')$.

Consider binary classifiers obtained by thresholding the scalar output of feedforward ReLU networks with at most W scalar parameters, each encoded using at most B bits, where W,B are positive integers. Use the finite graph-description convention in the proof of Theorem 6.1: all edge endpoints can be indexed among U<=W named neurons, so the architecture is encoded by specifying the two endpoint indices for every parameter. No additional uncharged choice of input-coordinate names is allowed. Then the number of distinct classifiers is at most 2^{O(W B + W log(W+1))}, and their VC dimension is O(W B + W log(W+1)). For a fixed architecture the simpler bound VCdim <= W B follows. The variable-architecture term is the cost of describing the graph, not extra numerical precision.

[Definition 14 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] Let $(T, o) \ino \overline{\bbT}^\bullet$. Let $\lambda \ino (0, \infty)$ and let $p_{T, \lambda} (\cdot, \cdot)$ be the transition probabilities of $\lambda$-RWs on $T$ as defined in (\ref{deflambRW}).  
The transition kernel on $\obbT^\bullet\! $ 
of the $\lambda$-biased RW is then defined for all $\overline{x}\!:= \! (T,x) \ino \obbT^\bullet\! $ by 
\begin{equation}
 
\overline{\mathtt p}_{\lambda} ( \overline{x}, d\overline{x}^\prime  ) = \sum_{y\in T} p_{T, \lambda } (x, y) \delta_{(T, y)} ( d\overline{x}^\prime) \, .
\end{equation}
We then denote by $P_{T,o}$ the law of the $\lambda$-biased RW
on $(\obbT^\bullet\! )^\bbN$ (that is 
the space of the $\obbT^\bullet \! $-valued sequences equipped with the product topology, which makes it Polish) starting at $(T,o)$. 
Note that $P_{T,o}$ depends on $\lambda$ although it does not appear in the notation. \cq
title: Definition 14 of arXiv:2605.02430

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $\kappa>1$, and suppose $n,d\to\infty$ with $n/d^2\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
		\item If $\alpha<\alpha_\star(\kappa)$, then there are constants
		$0<m<M<\infty$, depending only on $\alpha$ and $\kappa$ such that with probability tending to one there exists
		$R\in\Ssym^d$ satisfying
		$$
			mI_d\preceq R\preceq MI_d,
			\qquad
			\Tr R=d,
			\qquad
			\mathcal A_{G,\kappa} R=0.
		$$

		\item We have $\Gamma_{G,\kappa}\pto e_\star(\alpha,\kappa)$. If $\alpha>\alpha_\star(\kappa)$, then $e_\star(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ and
		$\P(\Gamma_{G,\kappa}\ge c_0)\to1$ for some
		$c_0=c_0(\alpha,\kappa)>0$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 41 of arXiv:2609.02785, 'Characterization of Stanley-Reisner varieties by their automorphism group'] Let $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$ be fully exposed simplicial complexes on $[n]$ and $[n']$. If there is an isomorphism of ind-groups
$$
\theta\colon\Aut(X_\Delta)\longrightarrow\Aut(X_{\Delta'}),
$$
then $n=n'$ and there is a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ with $\sigma\cdot\Delta=\Delta'$. In particular $\Delta\cong\Delta'$ as abstract simplicial complexes and $X_\Delta\cong X_{\Delta'}$ as algebraic varieties.

(Decoupling lemma, Lemma 4.7) For random variables X, Y with independent copies X', Y' and any event E(X,Y): P(E(X,Y)) <= P(E(X,Y) and E(X',Y) and E(X,Y') and E(X',Y'))^{1/4}. Let z_1,...,z_n be i.i.d. with P(z_i = 0) = P(z_i = 1) = 1/2 and Q = sum_{1<=i,j<=n} c_ij z_i z_j. (Cor 4.4) If there is U with |U| >= m >= 2 such that each i in U has at least m indices j with |c_ij| >= 1, then P(Q in I) = O(m^{-1/8}) for every interval I of length 1, absolute constant. (Cor 4.5) If at least m indices i each have at least m indices j with c_ij != 0, then P(Q = 0) = O(m^{-1/8}). (Thm 1.3) A random symmetric matrix with i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) entries on and above the diagonal is singular with probability O(n^{-1/8+delta}) for every delta > 0.

[Lemma of arXiv:2411.01104, 'Gaussian universality of $p$-adic random matrix products via corners'] For any $\mu^{(1)}=(\mu_1^{(1)},\ldots,\mu_n^{(1)})\in\Sig_n$, let $m_{\mu^{(1)}}(x_1,\ldots x_n)=\sum_\alpha x^\alpha$, summed over all distinct permutations $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$ of $\mu^{(1)}$ (See Subsection 1.2 of [Macdonald]). Let $b_1>b_2>\ldots>b_n>0$. Then we have
$$\frac{d}{dx}m_{\mu^{(1)}}(xb_1,b_2,\ldots,b_n)\Big|_{x=1}\ge\ldots\ge\frac{d}{dx}m_{\mu^{(1)}}(b_1,b_2,\ldots,xb_n)\Big|_{x=1}.$$
Every equality holds if and only if $\mu_1^{(1)}=\ldots=\mu_n^{(1)}$.

        \mathbb{E} \left[ |Y_{s,t}|^2\right] \leq c_H |t-s|^{2H}, \qquad

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked] This is the proved attraction-domain extension of the partial answer to Problem 3.11 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A probability measure is unimodal if, for some mode m, it is an atom at m plus an absolutely continuous measure whose density is nondecreasing to the left of m and nonincreasing to the right. Write boxplus for additive free convolution, the distribution of a sum of freely independent self-adjoint variables with the indicated laws, and * for classical convolution of independent real variables. A law lambda is freely strongly unimodal when lambda boxplus nu is unimodal for every unimodal nu. Let lambda be a nondelta probability law on R and suppose there are b_n>0 and a_n in R such that the image of lambda^{boxplus n} under x -> x/b_n+a_n converges weakly to C_1, the Cauchy law with density 1/[pi(1+x^2)]. Here lambda^{boxplus n} is its n-fold additive free convolution. Then lambda is not freely strongly unimodal. For the proof, D_c(mu) denotes the image of mu under x -> c x; unimodal measures are preserved by positive dilations and translations and are closed under weak convergence. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The affine-scaled free convolution powers converge weakly to C_1.
Free convolution is weakly continuous, and unimodal measures are weakly closed.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a1737915bd7ecd47997eca407b7de25c549d8752d0032010323b6a0c32850e92","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a1/a1737915bd7ecd47997eca407b7de25c549d8752d0032010323b6a0c32850e92.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9d13417b75738e2fc15d10e3322f651494c6abbbfcb1c6c7d810fcc69a74ead5","bundle_entry_key":"hasebe-ueda-problem-3-11-cauchy-attraction-obstruction","bundle_id":"population.probability-campaign-results-20260914-001","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-prob1000-nodes-1010/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.free:hasebe-ueda-problem-3-11-cauchy-attraction-obstruction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Suppose $\lambda$ is freely strongly unimodal. Then so is $\lambda^{\boxplus n}$ for every $n$, by
induction: $\lambda^{\boxplus n}\boxplus\nu = \lambda\boxplus(\lambda^{\boxplus n-1}\boxplus \nu)$, and
the inner measure is unimodal by the inductive hypothesis. Let $\nu$ be unimodal with
$\nu\boxplus C_1$ not unimodal, which the Proposition provides.

Let $b_n>0$ and $a_n\in\mathbb{R}$ be such that $D_{1/b_n}(\lambda^{\boxplus n})$ shifted by $a_n$
converges weakly to $C_1$, which is what membership of the free domain of attraction means. Since
$D_{b_n}(\nu)$ is unimodal, the hypothesis makes $D_{b_n}(\nu)\boxplus\lambda^{\boxplus n}$ unimodal.
Dilations pass through free convolution, $D_c(\alpha\boxplus\beta) = D_c\alpha\boxplus D_c\beta$, so
applying $D_{1/b_n}$ and the shift leaves
$$\nu \boxplus \big(D_{1/b_n}(\lambda^{\boxplus n})\ \text{shifted by } a_n\big)$$
unimodal for every $n$. Free convolution is continuous in the weak topology and the unimodal measures are
weakly closed, so the limit $\nu\boxplus C_1$ is unimodal, contradicting the choice of $\nu$.

body:
[Theorem 24 (O'Neill's Formula) of arXiv:2609.03951, 'Generalized Semi-Riemannian Submersions and Foliations'] Let $\pi: (M,g) \to (B,\mathcal{D},h)$ be a generalized semi-Riemannian submersion such that $\mathcal{D}$ is an involutive distribution. Then
\[
K^h_{\pi(p)}(d\pi(X),d\pi(Y)) = K^g_p(X,Y) + \frac{3}{4}\mathbf{A}(X,Y)
\]
for each $p \in M$ and $X,Y \in \mathfrak{X}_b(M)$ such that $X(p),Y(p)$ are orthonormal vectors, where $K^h_{\pi(p)}$ and $K^g_{p}$ denote the sectional curvatures of $(L_{\pi(p)},h) \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{D}}$ and $(M,g)$, respectively.
title: O'Neill's Formula

$h^{(j)}(0)=0$ for $0\leq j<K$.  Define $Ih(z):=\int_0^z h(\zeta)\,d\zeta.$ Then
\[
 \|Ih\|_{H^\infty(\D;Y)}
 \leq \frac{1}{K+1}\|h\|_{H^\infty(\D;Y)}.
\]

The orthogonal components of the particle-number current, and the mixed parallel-orthogonal stress-tensor components, take the following form, for some scalar functions~$\Numb_\chi,U_\chi$:
\be
\vNumb_\chi^a = \Numb_\chi(s_\perp, s_\parallel, \xi_\perp, \xi_\parallel) u^a ,
\qquad
T_\chi^{am} = \frac{1}{2} U_\chi(s_\perp, s_\parallel, \xi_\perp, \xi_\parallel) u^a u^m , \qquad
a=0,1 , \quad m=2,3 .
\ee

body:
[Proposition 219 (The system of integral inequalities satisfied by the energy controlling quantities) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\varsigma_0$ be the constant featured in Lemma\,\ref{L:PRELIMINARYBELOWTOPORDERL2ESTIMATESFOREIKONALFUINCTIONQUANTITIES} (see also Remark\,\ref{R:SMALLNESSCONSTANTFORBELOWTOPORDERACOUSTICVARIABLES}). If $\varsigma_1 \in (0,1]$ is sufficiently small, then there exist constants
$C > 0$ and $C_* > 0$ 
that are \textbf{independent} of $\varsigma_0,\varsigma_1$ 
such that the following estimates hold
for $(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot) \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$: 

\medskip

\noindent \underline{\textbf{Top-order integral inequalities for $\mastercontroltop$}.}
We have the following estimates for the $L^2$-controlling quantity $\mastercontroltop(\ubar,u)$
defined in \eqref{E:MASTERCONTROLLINGQUANTITY}:
\begin{align}
		\begin{split}  
			\mastercontroltop(\ubar,u) &\le \boxed{2.81 + 5.18} \weakspacetimetransvelocitycontrol_N(\ubar,u)  + \boxed{2.33 + 1.01} \totalbulkcontrolprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar,u) \\
			& \ \ +  \boxed{1.02 + 2.07} \weakspacetimeangularvelocitycontrol_N(\ubar,u) +  \boxed{4.13}  \totalbulkcontrolpartialmodifiedchi(\ubar,u) \\
			& \ \  + \boxed{\frac{2}{3}} \totalfluxcontrolvelocity_N(\ubar,u) + \boxed{\frac{3}{4}(1.01)} \totalfluxcontrolpartialmodifiedchi(\ubar,u) \\
			& \ \ + \Errortoparg{N}(\ubar,u),
		\end{split}
	\end{align}\noindent where we define $\Errortoparg{N}(\ubar,u)$ to be any term that satisfies the following estimate,
in which the implicit constants are \textbf{independent} of $\varsigma_0,\varsigma_1 \in (0,1]$:
	\begin{align}
		\begin{split} 
			\left|\Errortoparg{N}(\ubar,u)\right| &  \lesssim  (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1}+\varsigma_1^{-1}) \initialsmalldoublenull^2  + (\mr \upalpha + \fundbootsmall + \varsigma_1) \totalfluxcontrolvelocity_N(\ubar,u) +  (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1} + \varsigma_1^{-1}) \int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} \totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar',u) \, \mathrm{d} \ubar' \\ 
			& \ \  + (1+ \varsigma_0^{-1} + \varsigma_1^{-1}) \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u  \totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar,u') \, \rmd u' + \varsigma_1 (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1})\strongangularcontrolvelocity_{N}(\ubar,u) \\
			& \ \ + \fundbootsmall (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1}) \strongangularcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar,u) +  (1 + \varsigma_1^{-1}) \int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} \frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{1/2}} \totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,N]}(\ubar',u) \, \mathrm{d} \ubar' \\
			& \ \ +   \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \left\{\fluxcontrolVort_{\le N}(\ubar,u')+ \fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\le N }(\ubar,u')\right\} \, \mathrm{d} u +   \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \left\{\fluxcontrolVortVort_{\le N}(\ubar,u')+ \fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\le N }(\ubar,u')\right\} \, \mathrm{d} u' \\	
			& \ \ + (1+\varsigma_1^{-1}) \fluxcontrolVort(\ubar,u) + (1+\varsigma_1^{-1}) \bulkcontrolVort(\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolVortVort_N(\ubar,u) +  \bulkcontrolDivGradEnt_N(\ubar,u)  \\
			& \ \  + (1 +\varsigma_1^{-1})  \int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} \frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{0.5}}\totalfluxcontrolprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar',u) \, \rmd \ubar'   +  (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1} +  \varsigma_1^{-1}) \int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar}  \totalfluxcontrolimprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar',u) \, \mathrm{d} \ubar' \\
			& \ \ +  \fundbootsmall \totalbulkcontrolimprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar,u) +   \fundbootsmall \totalbulkcontrolprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar,u) +(\mr \upalpha + \fundbootsmall) \totalbulkcontrolpartialmodifiedchi(\ubar,u) +  (\mr \upalpha + \fundbootsmall  + \varsigma_1)\weakspacetimeangularvelocitycontrol_N(\ubar,u) \\
			& \ \ + (1 + \varsigma_1^{-1}) \int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} \totalfluxcontrolpartialmodifiedchi(\ubar',u) \, \rmd \ubar'.
		\end{split}
	\end{align}
	
	
\medskip

\noindent \underline{\textbf{Below-top-order integral inequalities for $\velocityarray$}.}
Finally, if $2 \leq N \leq \Ntop$, 
then we have the following estimates for the $L^2$-controlling quantity $\totalcontrolwave_{[1,N-1]}$
defined by \eqref{E:VELOCITYFLUXANDSTRONGANGULARL2CONTROLLINGQUANTITY} and Def.\,\ref{D:SUMMEDL2CO (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Prover-written mathematical claim; independent review pending. Let 1<=p<=q and T in H^(tensor(p+q)) tensor W be symmetric in the first p positions. Let Q average the next q positions, P_q average the first q positions, delta=||T-QT||, and b=binom(q,p). Then ||T||<=b||P_qT||+(b+1)delta. The two original block projections commute, so the sharp two-block bound applies to QT. Without the second block symmetry, a zero-error recovery estimate fails: for p=1,q=2,H=R^2, T=(e0 tensor e1-e1 tensor e0) tensor e0 is nonzero but P_2T=0. The error coefficient b+1 is a valid bound whose optimality is not claimed.

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Put $V_+=\sup_\Omega V$ and $V_-=\inf_\Omega V$. Then $\Lambda_V^\Omega$ is concave, $\Lambda_V^\Omega(0)\ge0$ and
\[
|\Lambda_V^\Omega(\gamma_1)-\Lambda_V^\Omega(\gamma_2)|\le\|V\|_\infty|\gamma_1-\gamma_2|,
\qquad
\Lambda_V^\Omega(\gamma)=-\gamma V_\pm+o(|\gamma|)\quad(\gamma\to\pm\infty).
\]
Assume in addition that $\Omega$ is bounded, $q\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ and $V\in C(\overline\Omega)$. Then $\Lambda_V^\Omega$ and $\Lambda_D^\Omega$ are real analytic on $\R$ and $(0,\infty)$, respectively. With $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*=1$,
\[
(\Lambda_V^\Omega)'(\gamma)=-\int_\Omega V\phi_\gamma\phi_\gamma^*,\qquad
(\Lambda_D^\Omega)'(\alpha)=-d\int_\Omega\phi_\alpha^*(J*_\Omega\phi_\alpha-\phi_\alpha).
\]
Moreover,
\[
(\Lambda_V^\Omega)'(\gamma)=-V_\pm+o(1)\quad(\gamma\to\pm\infty),
\]
and $\Lambda_V^\Omega$ is strictly concave if $V$ is nonconstant. No sign is imposed in general on $(\Lambda_D^\Omega)'$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2604.00630, 'The contact process on a bipartite spatial network'] There exists~$c > 0$ such that the following holds. Let~$\lambda_1,\lambda_2 \in (0,1]$ and~$n \ge m \ge 2e/\lambda_2$. Let~$A$ be a set of leaves of~$S_n$ with~$|A|=m$. Let~$(\xi_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be the contact process on~$S_n$ where the centre has infection rate~$\lambda_1$ and the leaves have infection rate~$\lambda_2$, started from~$A$ infected. Then,
	\[
		\mathbb P \left(|\xi_1| \ge \lambda_1 n/(8e) \right) > 1 - e^{-cm} - e^{-c\lambda_2m} - e^{-c\lambda_1n}.
	\]

body: [Thm Thm1 of arXiv:2607.19037, 'Semiclassical analysis for Yang--Mills \\ random connections on compact surfaces'] Let $\Sigma$ a compact surface. Consider the case of the group $G=\mathsf{SU}(N)$. For $\alpha\in (\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{2}),p\geqslant 2,s<0,\ell<-1$, seen as a family of measures on $\mathcal{B}_{\mathsf{YM}}^{\alpha,p,s,\ell}$, $(A_{\Sigma,t\sigma})_{t>0}$ converges  to a measure supported on $\mathcal F$. Moreover, this limit coincides with our representative of the normalized Atiyah--Bott--Goldman symplectic volume measure on $\mathcal F$ of Proposition~(ABGMeasure of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition def:glauber-weak-poincare of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] We say $\pi$ on $\qty{\pm 1}^n$ satisfies a $(\CPoi,\eps)$-weak \Poincare inequality for Glauber dynamics if for all functions $f$,
    \[ \Var_{\pi}[f] \le \frac{1}{\CPoi} \cdot \calE(f,f) + \eps \cdot \osc(f)^2. \]
    Similarly, we say $\pi$ satisfies a $(\MLSI,\eps)$-weak modified log-Sobolev inequality if for all functions $f$, 
    \[ \Ent_{\pi}[f] \le \frac{1}{\MLSI} \cdot \calE(f,\log f) + \eps \cdot \osc(\sqrt{f})^2. \]
title: Weak Poincar\'{e} for the hypercube

body: [Lemma 93 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $\mu$ be an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-content, $C\in D_\mu$, and $V$ be a neighbourhood of $\mu(C)$ in $\mf A$. \[
 \mathfrak{d} = \sum_{e=1}^{\mathfrak e}\big(|r_e^{\textnormal{I}}-r_e^{\textnormal{II}}\bigr| + \sum_{h=1}^H \Big( \big(|\theta^{\textnormal{I}}_{h,h}- \theta^{\textnormal{II}}_{h,h}\bigr| + \big(|\hat{a}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{I}}-\hat{a}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{II}}\bigr| + \big(|\hat{b}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{I}}-\hat{b}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{II}}\bigr|\Big).
\]
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{Lemma_continuity_varyinf_ff} there exists $C>0$ (depending only on the constants in Assumptions \ref{Assumption_A_prime} and \ref{Assumption_B}) and two measures $\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\textnormal{I} \rightarrow \textnormal{II}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\textnormal{II} \rightarrow \textnormal{I}}$, such that:
\begin{align}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.31164, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality'] For every $2 \leq m < N$, there exist constants $\ve_{N,m}>0$ and $C_N<\infty$ with the following property.
For every $\Psi \in C^1(\bG(N,m) , (0,\infty) )$ with $\sup_{T \in \bG(N,m)} \|B_{\Psi}(T) - T \| < \ve_{N,m}$, every rectifiable $m$-varifold $V = v(M,\theta)$ in $\bR^N$ with finite total mass and finite first variation with respect to the anisotropy $\Psi$ satisfies
\[
\|V\| (\bR^N) \leq C_N \, \cH^m(M)^{\frac{1}{m}} \, |\delta_{\Psi} V|(\bR^N).
\]
In particular, if $\Theta^m(\|V\|,x) \geq \theta_0 > 0$ holds $\|V\|$-a.e.~$x$, then 
\[
\|V\|(\bR^N)^{\frac{m-1}{m}} \leq C_N \theta_0^{- \frac{1}{m}} |\delta_{\Psi} V|( \bR^N).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.31164

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2609.04143, 'The Geometry of Real Anisotropic Bohnenblust--Hille Constants'] Let $\mathbf q$ be a Bohnenblust--Hille exponent with $\sigma(\mathbf q)>0$. Then
\[
 2^{\frac{\sigma(\mathbf q)}{2}\left(1+(m-2)Y_1(\mathbf q)\right)}
 \le C_{\mathbf q}^{(m)}
 \le
 2^{\frac{\sigma(\mathbf q)}{2}\left(1+(m-2)\max\{Y_1(\mathbf q),1/2\}\right)}.
\]
In particular, if $Y_1(\mathbf q)<1/2$, then
\[
 2^{\frac{\sigma(\mathbf q)}{2}\left(1+(m-2)Y_1(\mathbf q)\right)}
 \le C_{\mathbf q}^{(m)}
 \le 2^{\sigma(\mathbf q)m/4}.
\]

Let S be a fair all-or-none selector on three terminals a,b,c, and let T be a three-arm star whose arms are mutually independent Bernoulli(1/sqrt(2)). Every pair connection probability is 1/2 in both S and T. Add identical deterministic exterior wiring joining a to c, and ask whether b is connected to that wired pair. The crossing probability is 1/2 for S and 1-1/(2sqrt(2)) for T, differing by (2-sqrt(2))/4>0. Equal terminal-pair marginals therefore do not suffice for an exact gadget transfer in arbitrary exterior connectivity events.
Three distinct labeled terminals.
The star arms are mutually independent with probability 1/sqrt(2).
The selector is one Bernoulli(1/2) hyperedge.
Exterior wiring a~c is deterministic and crossing means b connected to a or c.

[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2608.29972, '\bf Cram\'er transform, half-space depth and threshold phenomena for convex bodies'] Let $\mu$ be an $s$-concave probability measure supported on a convex body $K$. Then
$$\operatorname{Var}_\mu\bigl(-\log q_\mu\bigr)\leq\frac{C}{s^2},$$
where $C>0$ is an absolute constant.

In particular, if $\mu=\mu_K$ is the uniform probability measure on a convex body $K$, then
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\mu_K}\bigl(-\log q_K\bigr)\leq Cn^2.$$

$$H^\ast(\mathsf{gr}_1(\mathsf{FT}_\Gamma))(n)\cong \bigoplus_\lambda  \Sigma^{|\lambda|+2} p_\lambda\Phi[n,\lambda^\ast] $$

	$$
	p_{(a,b)} = \begin{cases}
		(a-2)/2	&	a\equiv_2 b\equiv_2 0 \text{ and } b=0\\
		(a-b)/2	&	a\equiv_2 b\equiv_2 0 \text{ and } b\neq 0 \\
		(a-b)/2+1	&	a\equiv_2 b \equiv_2 1 \\
		0	&	a \not\equiv_2 b
	\end{cases}
	$$

[Prp 19 (\cite{KT25}, Proposition 4.1.20) of arXiv:2608.30743, 'Perspectives on the Bott spectral sequence for Lie groupoids'] The following maps
    \[
     (\Gamma(G_0, \wedge^{p-q} \nu^* \otimes S^q (A^*_{\iso}) ))^G \rightarrow (\Gamma(G_0, \wedge^{p+1-q} \nu^* \otimes S^q (A^*_{\iso}) ))^G
    \]
    agree:
    \begin{enumerate}[a)]
        \item The map corresponding to the differential of the first page of the spectral sequence constructed from the filtration of the Bott-Shulman-Stasheff bicomplex by columns.
        \item The map induced by the exteriour covariant derivative on
        \[
        \Gamma(G_0, \wedge^{p-q} \nu^* \otimes S^q (A^*_{\iso}) )
        \]
        with respect to a connection on $A_{\iso}$ obtained by differentiating the restriction of a multiplicative Ehresmann connection to the isotropy groupoid.
        \item The map corresponding on $J^E G$-invariant forms to the component of the de-Rham differential retaining the $E$-vertical degree for any choice of multiplicative Ehresmann connection $E$.
    \end{enumerate}
    The map described this way is denoted by $\dCart$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Borel family of probability measures of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Given a measurable space \((\Omega,\mathcal{A})\) and a Polish space \(\mathcal{X}\), we say that a family \((\mu^{\omega})_{\omega \in \Omega}\subset \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\) is a Borel family of probability measures if the map
\[\omega \in \Omega\mapsto \mu^{\omega}(B) \in [0,1]\] is measurable for every Borel set \(B\subset \mathcal{X}\).

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2605.21424, 'A dice game, a multinomial walk, and the inverted Dirichlet distribution'] Let \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m>0\).
For every \(n\in\N_{\ge 1}\), let \(G_{1,n},\ldots,G_{m,n}\) be independent and let \(G_{k,n}\) have a \(\operatorname{Gamma}(\alpha_k n,1)\) distribution, \(k=1,\ldots,m\). Then 
\begin{align*}
\lim_{n\to \infty}\P\Big(\frac{G_{2,n}}{\alpha_2 n}>\frac{G_{1,n}}{\alpha_1 n}, \ldots , \frac{G_{m,n}}{\alpha_m n}>\frac{G_{1,n}}{\alpha_1 n}\Big)
&=\P\Big(\frac{Z_2}{\sqrt{\alpha_2 }}>\frac{Z_1}{\sqrt{\alpha_1 }}, \ldots , \frac{Z_m}{\sqrt{\alpha_m }}>\frac{Z_1}{\sqrt{\alpha_1 }}\Big),
\end{align*}
where \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent standard normal variables.
title: Proposition 17 of arXiv:2605.21424

[Proposition Lambdaprop of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] We keep the notation of Definition (Lambdadef of the paper). 
Let $\mu, \mu_n \! \in \!   \mathcal{M}_f^{\mathtt{era}}(T)$, $n\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$. Then the following holds true. 
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] $\Lambda_{\mathbf h, \mu}$-a.e.~$L_\infty\! = \!  \sup_{p\in \mathbb{N}} L_p$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] For all integers $p\! \geq \!   q$ and all 
$r\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$, $d_{\mathtt{Pro}}^{T}\! (  \mathtt{P}_{T_{\! \mu, h_p}} \mu, \mathtt{P}_{T_{\! \mu, h_q}} \mu ) \! \leq \!  r \! \vee \! 
\Lambda_{\mathbf h, \mu} (\{ L_p\! -\! L_q \! > \!  r \}) $. Furthermore if $\mu \! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f(T)$, then 
$d_{\mathtt{Pro}}^{T}( \mu, \mathtt{P}_{T_{\! \mu, h_p}} \mu) \! \leq \!  r \! \vee\!  \Lambda_{\mathbf h, \mu} (\{ L_\infty\! -\! L_p \! > \!  r \}) $. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] Let $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$. Let $\rho \! \in \!   \mathtt{t}\!\subseteq\! T$ be a compact subtree such that $h_p\! > \!  \mu (T^*\backslash \mathtt{t})$. We set $\nu \! = \!  \mathtt{P}_{\!\mathtt{t}} \mu $. Then, for all Borel subsets $B$ of $[0, \infty] \! \times \!  \mathbb{R}_+^{{p+1}}\! $, we get 
$|\Lambda^{{\! (p)}}_{ \mathbf h, \nu} (B)\! -\! \Lambda^{{\! (p)}}_{\mathbf h, \mu} (B)| \! \leq \!  \mu (T^*\backslash \mathtt{t})$.    

\smallskip

\item[$(iv)$] We suppose that $\mu_n \! \! \to \! \mu$ in the sense of mass erasure and we suppose that $h\! \mapsto \! T_{\! \mu, h}$ is $d_{\mathtt{Haus}}$-continuous at each $h_p$, $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$. Then the following holds.
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(iv\textrm{-}a)$] $\Lambda^{\! o}_{\mathbf h, \mu_n} \!\! \!  \! \to \! \Lambda^{\! o}_{\mathbf h, \mu}$ weakly on $\mathcal{M}_{\! f}({\boldsymbol{\ell}}^{\uparrow}(\mathbb{N}))$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iv\textrm{-}b)$] The measures  $(\Lambda_{\mathbf h, \mu_n})_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ are tight in  $\mathcal{M}_{\! f}({\boldsymbol{\ell}}_\bullet^{\uparrow}(\mathbb{N}))$ and if $\Lambda$ is a weak limit point, then $\Lambda^{\! o}\! = \!   \Lambda^{\! o}_{\mathbf h, \mu}$ and $\Lambda$-a.e.~$\sup_{p\in \mathbb{N}} L_p \! \leq \!  L_\infty$.   
\end{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(v)$]Let $\mu_n, \mu\! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_{\! f}(T)$ are such that $\mu_n \! \to \! \mu$ weakly in $\mathcal{M}_f(T)$. We suppose that $h\! \mapsto \! T_{\! \mu, h}$ is $d_{\mathtt{Haus}}$-continuous at each $h_p$, $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$. Then, $\Lambda_{\mathbf h, \mu_n} \! \!\! \to \! \Lambda_{\mathbf h, \mu}$ weakly on $\mathcal{M}_{\! f}({\boldsymbol{\ell}}_\bullet^{\uparrow}(\mathbb{N}))$. 
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorema 1 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\geq5$, be a closed, connected, oriented, locally conformally
flat Riemannian manifold with positive scalar curvature and infinite
fundamental group.  Then there exists an integer
$i\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1$ such that $\pi_i(M^n)\ne 0$, and its universal Riemannian cover $(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ has macroscopic dimension at most $\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor$.  
 
Let $M^n\cong\Omega/\Gamma$ be the Kleinian realization given by the
 developing map.  If, in addition,
$H_1(M^n;\mathbb{Z})=0$, then $\Gamma$ is
non-elementary.  Under these additional assumptions, if $\Gamma$ is
torsion-free, then the Hausdorff dimension of its limit set satisfies
\begin{equation}
        1\;<\;\dim_{\mathcal H}\!\bigl(\Lambda(\Gamma)\bigr)\;<\;\frac{n-2}{2}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorema 1 of arXiv:2609.02267

body:
[Defn of arXiv:2411.11408, 'Multidimensional specific relative entropy between continuous martingales'] We write $$F_l(X):=\frac{1}{2}(tr(X)-l-\log(\det X)),$$ for every symmetric positive definite matrix $X\in \mathbb{R}^{l \times l}$. Thus 
\begin{align*}
  H(\mathcal{N}_l(\mu, \Sigma_1)|\mathcal{N}_l(\mu, \Sigma_2))
  & = \textstyle  \frac{1}{2}\Big(tr(\Sigma_2^{-1}\Sigma_1)-l-\log( \frac{\det \Sigma_1}{\det \Sigma_2})\Big) \\
  &=\textstyle  \frac{1}{2}\Big(tr(\Sigma_1^{1/2}\Sigma_2^{-1}\Sigma_1^{1/2})-l-\log( \det (\Sigma_1^{1/2}\Sigma_2^{-1}\Sigma_1^{1/2}))\Big) \\
  &=F_l(\Sigma_1^{1/2}\Sigma_2^{-1}\Sigma_1^{1/2})\\
  &=F_l(\Sigma_2^{-1/2}\Sigma_1\Sigma_2^{-1/2}) .
    \end{align*}
    With some abuse of notation we still write $F(\Sigma_2^{-1}\Sigma_1)$ for the above number, even if $\Sigma_2^{-1}\Sigma_1$ need not be symmetric.

[Lemma lem:saturated-properties of arXiv:2504.19367, 'Reduced Random Walks in the Hyperbolic Plane\textinterrobang'] Let $a \leq b \leq c$ be real numbers, let $T \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, and let $f, g \colon T \to \mathbb{R}$ be functions. Let $\epsilon > 0$, and let $C$ be a real constant.
    \begin{lemenum}
        \item  If $\left\lvertf(b) - f(a)\right\rvert < \epsilon$, then $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, b]$.
        \item  If $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, b]$, then $f$ is $\epsilon'$-saturated on $[a, b]$ for all $\epsilon' > \epsilon$.
        \item  If $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, b]$, then $f + C$ is also $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, b]$.
        \item  If $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, b]$, then $Cf$ is $(\left\lvertC\right\rvert\epsilon)$-saturated on $[a, b]$.
        \item  If $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on both $[a, b]$ and $[b, c]$, then $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, c]$.
        \item  Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, and let $h \colon U \to T$ be a monotone (increasing or decreasing) function. If $f \circ h$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, b]$, then $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[h(a), h(b)]$.
        \item  Suppose that $f$ and $g$ are each either monotone increasing or monotone decreasing on $[a, b] \cap T$. Let $\epsilon, \epsilon' > 0$. If $f$ is $\epsilon$-saturated on $[a, b]$ and $g$ is $\epsilon'$-saturated on $[a, b]$, then $f + g$ is $(\epsilon + \epsilon')$-saturated on $[a, b]$.
    \end{lemenum}
title: Lemma lem:saturated-properties of arXiv:2504.19367

body: In probability theory and information theory, the mutual information (MI) of two random variables is a measure of the mutual dependence between the two variables. More specifically, it quantifies the "amount of information" obtained about one random variable by observing the other random variable. The concept of mutual information is intimately linked to that of entropy of a random variable, a fundamental notion in information theory that quantifies the expected "amount of information" held in a random variable.
title: Mutual information

body: An infinite cardinal \kappa is regular if its cofinality equals itself: \mathrm{cf}(\kappa) = \kappa. If \mathrm{cf}(\kappa) < \kappa, then \kappa is singular.
title: Regular Cardinal

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We have the following formulae,
$$\sin t=\sum_{l=0}^\infty(-1)^l\frac{t^{2l+1}}{(2l+1)!}\quad,\quad 
\cos t=\sum_{l=0}^\infty(-1)^l\frac{t^{2l}}{(2l)!}$$
as well as the following formulae,
$$e^t=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{t^k}{k!}\quad,\quad 
\log(1+t)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty(-1)^{k+1}\frac{t^k}{k}$$
as Taylor series, and in general as well, with $|t|<1$ needed for $\log$.

[Theorem 6 (Lagrangian well-posedness and transport for the PF-ODE) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Assume \textup{(E1)}, \textup{(D$_{\mathrm L}$)}, \textup{(I)} and \textup{(S)}, and let
$v(x,t)=f(x,t)-\tfrac12\sigma^2(t)\nabla\log p_t(x)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] $v$ satisfies conditions \textup{(R1)--(R3)} of Theorem \ref{thm:DL}, with
\[
  \big\|[\Div v(\cdot,t)]^-\big\|_\infty\le\big\|[\Div f(\cdot,t)]^-\big\|_\infty
  +\tfrac12\|\sigma\|^2_{L^\infty}\Lambda(t)=:\Theta_-(t)\in L^1(0,T).
\]
\item[\textup{(ii)}] The PF-ODE \eqref{eq:pfode} admits a regular Lagrangian flow $Z$, unique up to $\Leb$-null
sets, with compressibility constant $L=e^{\Theta_-}$, where 
$\Theta_-:=\int_0^T\Theta_-(t)\,\dd t$; 
\item[\textup{(iii)}] $Z(t,\cdot)_\#(p_0\Leb)=p_t\Leb$ for every $t\in[0,T]$; hence for
$Z_0\sim p_0$ and $Z_t:=Z(t,Z_0)$,
\[
  \Law(Z_t)=\Law(X_t),\qquad t\in[0,T].
\] 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 101 of arXiv:2411.08303, 'The discrepancy in min-max statistics between two random matrices with finite third moment'] Let $X$ and $X^{\prime}$ are $n \times m$ independent Gaussian matrices with mean zero, that is,  $\mathbb{E}[X_{i,j}]=\mathbb{E}[X_{i,j}^{\prime}]=0$. For $1 \leq i_1,i_2 \leq n$ and $1 \leq j_1,j_2 \leq m$, let $\sigma=\max\limits_{i_1,j_1,i_2,j_2}|\mathbb{E}[X_{i_1,j_1}X_{i_2,j_2}-X_{i_1,j_1}^{\prime}X_{i_2,j_2}^{\prime}]|$. There exist a constant $ C > 0 $ such that for all borel subset $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ we have $$\mathbb{P}(|\min_{1 \leq i \leq n}\max_{1 \leq j \leq m}X_{i,j}-\min_{1 \leq i \leq n}\max_{1 \leq j \leq m}X_{i,j}^{\prime}|>5\epsilon ) \leq C \frac{\log nm}{\tau^2}\sigma,$$ for all $\tau >0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited), claim w725-T329-002 v1. This is an optimization of a published upper-bound certificate, not an optimal-capacity theorem. In Vardi?Yehudai?Shamir Theorem 6.2 (arXiv:2110.03187v1 p.9), let n>=4, d,C be positive integers, and let x_i in R^d have norms <=r, pairwise distances >=delta>0, and labels in {1,...,C}; normalize r>=1 and delta<=1. Put h=log_2(d*n*C*r/delta)>0 and M=floor(sqrt(n)). Fix source constants A,K>0 such that for every integer 2<=s<=M the source certifies weight precision <=A*h*f(s) and depth <=K*e(s), where f(s)=s/sqrt(log_2 s) and e(s)=n*h/f(s). For a bit budget beta>0 define t=beta/(A*h), and call s certified if f(s)<=t. The certified set is nonempty exactly when t>=2; if nonempty it is {2,...,S}, with S the largest certified integer, and e(S) minimizes the displayed depth expression. If t>=f(M), then S=M and e(S)=n*h/f(M). If 2<=t<f(M), then n*h/t<=e(S)<(3/2)*n*h/t, equivalently A*n*h^2/beta<=e(S)<(3*A/2)*n*h^2/beta. The inequalities concern e(S), not the actual network depth; the actual theorem supplies an upper bound K*e(S). For beta=c*log_2 n, the exact certificate threshold is c>=2*A*h/log_2 n. With fixed feasible c and h=Theta(log n), the unsaturated expression is Theta(n log n), so the constant-width parameter guarantee is O(d+n log n). All source constants are unspecified. For n=4 only s=2 is legal, so every feasible budget is saturated. Independent review is pending; no Lean certification is claimed.

Let X take values in {-1, 1}^n, n >= 1, under any law, fix a coordinate i, and let X_i' be a replacement sign which, given X_{-i}, is independent of X_i; X^(i) is X with coordinate i replaced by X_i'. Put D_i u(x) = (u(x with x_i = 1) - u(x with x_i = -1))/2, m = E[X_i | X_{-i}] and m' = E[X_i' | X_{-i}]. For every real u on the cube, (1/2) E[(u(X) - u(X^(i)))^2] = E[(1 - m m') (D_i u(X))^2], with the weight 1 - m m' in [0, 2]. Hence (1/2) E[(u(X) - u(X^(i)))^2] = E[(D_i u(X))^2] for every u if and only if m m' = 0 almost surely: at each value of X_{-i} of positive probability, X_i or X_i' is conditionally fair, and the law of the other sign is then arbitrary (X_i' = 1 always is allowed when X_i is conditionally fair). If X_i' is a fresh draw from the conditional law of X_i (m' = m, the heat-bath step), the left side is E[Var(u(X) | X_{-i})] = E[(1 - m^2) (D_i u)^2]. Under the uniform law and for u with values +-1, E[(D_i u)^2] is the influence of coordinate i.
X a random element of {-1, 1}^n, n >= 1, under any law

[Proposition 1 (Integral formula along a McKean--Vlasov flow) of arXiv:2608.03412, 'A McKean--Vlasov semigroup and its application to a martingale representation problem'] Assume {\rm \Cref{assum:main,assum:G}}. Let $m,m'\in\Pc(\R^d)$, and let
$(U,U')$ be a coupling of $(m,m')$, independent of the noises. Then, for
every $s\in[t,T]$, $\P$-a.s.,
\[
\begin{aligned}
G(\mu^{t,m}_s)-G(\mu^{t,m'}_s)
&=
\int_0^1
\E\Big[
\nabla_x\delta_mG(\mu^\theta_s)(S^\theta_s)
\cdot J^\theta_s(U-U')
\,\Big|\,\Gc_s
\Big]\,\mathrm{d}\theta
+
\int_0^1
\E\Big[
\nabla_x\delta_mG(\mu^\theta_s)(\overline S^\theta_s)
\cdot \overline J^\theta_s(U-U')
\,\Big|\,\Gc_s
\Big]\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
\end{aligned}
\]

[Theorem 53 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let $k$ be a perfect field and $X$ a del Pezzo variety over $k$.
Then for every simple normal crossings divisor $D$ on $X$, the pair $(X,D)$ is log HT-split.
In particular, we have
\[
F_*\Omega^{\bullet}_X(\log D) \simeq \bigoplus_{i=0}^{\dim X} \Omega_X^i(\log D)[-i]
\]
and Akizuki--Nakano-type vanishing for $(X,D)$ as in \Cref{vanishing}.
