[Theorem 9 (Error bounds for the autoregressive classifiers) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Suppose Assumption~\ref{ass:gaussian_ar} holds and let \(T\geq2\). Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), define \(Q_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}X_t^2\), and set \(\lambda_{AR,\alpha}=2\sigma_{AR}^2T\sqrt{\log(4T/\alpha)\log(2/\alpha)}\). The exact classifier \(h_{AR,\alpha}(\bm X)=\mathbb I\{S_{AR}(\bm X)>\lambda_{AR,\alpha}\}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P\{h_{AR,\alpha}(\bm X)=1\mid Y=0\}\leq\alpha\). Suppose there exist \(q_T>0\) and \(\eta_T\in[0,1]\) such that \(\mathbb P(Q_T\geq q_T\mid Y=1)\geq1-\eta_T\) and \(q_T\geq2\lambda_{AR,\alpha}/\kappa_{AR}\). Then
\[
\mathbb P\{h_{AR,\alpha}(\bm X)=0\mid Y=1\}
\leq\eta_T+\exp\left\{-\frac{\kappa_{AR}^2q_T}{8\sigma_{AR}^2}\right\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{err}(h_{AR,\alpha})
\leq
\pi_0\alpha
+\pi_1\left[
\eta_T+\exp\left\{-\frac{\kappa_{AR}^2q_T}{8\sigma_{AR}^2}\right\}
\right].
\]

Now fix \(M>0\) and \(\epsilon_{AR}>0\), and suppose that \(\sup_{\bm x\in\mathcal X_M}\lvert f_{\epsilon_{AR},M}^{AR}(\bm x)-S_{AR}(\bm x)\rvert\leq\epsilon_{AR}\). Define $\overline h_{AR}(\bm X)=\mathbb I\left\{f_{\epsilon_{AR},M}^{AR}(\operatorname{clip}_M(\bm X))>\lambda_{AR,\alpha}+\epsilon_{AR}\right\}.$ If the same \(q_T\) and \(\eta_T\) satisfy the stronger condition \(q_T\geq2(\lambda_{AR,\alpha}+2\epsilon_{AR})/\kappa_{AR}\), then
\[
\operatorname{err}(\overline h_{AR})
\leq\pi_0\{\alpha+\tau_0(M)\}
+\pi_1\left[\eta_T+\exp\left\{-\frac{\kappa_{AR}^2q_T}{8\sigma_{AR}^2}\right\}+\tau_1(M)\right]
=:\mathfrak B_{AR}(\alpha,\epsilon_{AR},M).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Error bounds for the autoregressive classifiers

a $K\rtimes G$-set with action given by $(k,g)\cdot k':=k+g\cdot k'-d(g)$.

(2) $\tc(d)=\secat(\pi_d).$

body:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R$ be open and let $A(x,t)=(a^{ij}(x,t))_{i,j=1}^n$ be real measurable on $\Omega$. The operator $\mathcal H u=\partial_t u-\sum_{i,j}\partial_{x_i}(a^{ij}\partial_{x_j}u)$ is uniformly parabolic with ellipticity constants $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$ if for a.e. $(x,t)\in\Omega$ and all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^n$: $a^{ij}(x,t)\xi_i\xi_j\ge\lambda|\xi|^2$ and $|a^{ij}(x,t)\xi_j\eta_i|\le\Lambda|\xi||\eta|$. No smoothness or symmetry of $A$ is assumed unless stated. For a cylinder $Q=B\times(t_1,t_2)$ with $B$ a ball, $u$ is a (local) weak solution of $\mathcal H u=0$ in $Q$ if $u\in L^\infty(t_1,t_2;L^2(B))\cap L^2(t_1,t_2;H^1(B))$ and $\iint_Q\big(-u\,\varphi_t+a^{ij}\partial_j u\,\partial_i\varphi\big)\,dx\,dt=0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$; a weak subsolution (supersolution) satisfies $\le 0$ ($\ge 0$) for every nonnegative such $\varphi$. The constants in De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory, Moser's Harnack inequality and Aronson's bounds depend only on $n,\lambda,\Lambda$.
A measurable on Omega
lambda |xi|^2 <= a^{ij} xi_i xi_j a.e.
|a^{ij} xi_j eta_i| <= Lambda |xi||eta| a.e.
title: Uniformly Parabolic Operator in Divergence Form

Let a be the Z^2 simple-random-walk potential kernel, normalized by a(0)=0, harmonicity off zero and a(x)=(2/pi)log|x|+O(1). Put g=2/pi and alpha=2/sqrt(g). Let phi be the centered Gaussian field pinned to zero at the origin, with covariance E[phi_x phi_y]=a(x)+a(y)-a(x-y). Fix beta>0. On Z^2 give each nearest-neighbor edge {x,y} conductance c(x,y)=exp(beta(phi_x+phi_y)), and let X be the discrete-time walk with transition p_phi(x,y)=c(x,y)/sum_{z adjacent to x}c(x,z). Write P for the field law, P_phi^0 and E_phi^0 for the walk law and expectation from zero, and B(N)=[-N,N]^2 intersect Z^2. Put beta_c=sqrt(pi/2), and define psi(beta)=2+2(beta/beta_c)^2 for beta<=beta_c and psi(beta)=4 beta/beta_c for beta>=beta_c (the definitions agree at beta_c). For every delta>0, the random conditional probability P_phi^0(|X_T|>=T^(1/psi(beta)) exp[-(log T)^(1/2+delta)]) tends to one in probability with respect to P as the integer T tends to infinity. Euclidean norm may be used. This is the displacement lower bound complementary to Biskup Problem 16.12, and is not its requested upper bound. Source: Return probability and recurrence for the random walk driven by two-dimensional Gaussian free field, Theorem 1.3, eq.(1.6), p.2; proof Section 5.2, p.49; lecture Corollary 13.4, p.183.
Fixed beta>0 and delta>0
The discrete-time walk and exponent psi are defined above
Convergence is in probability over the field of the displayed quenched probability

[Theorem 29 (Stationary product limit) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] For each $\gamma\in\Gamma$,
\[
        t_{\mathrm d}^\gamma
        =t_{\mathrm{sus}}^\gamma
        =t_\infty^\gamma
        =t_c^\gamma,
\]
where $t_c^{\mathrm{os}}$ and $t_c^{\mathrm{iso}}$ are the critical values
of Theorems~\ref{thm:range-criticality} and
\ref{thm:isotropic-criticality}, respectively. If
\[
        F_N^\gamma
        =\bigl(F_{N,x}^\gamma\bigr)_{x\in\Lambda_N}
\]
has law $\pi_N^\gamma$, then, for every fixed collection of distinct sites
$x_1,\ldots,x_\ell\in\mathbb Z$,
\[
        \bigl(
        F_{N,x_1}^\gamma,\ldots,F_{N,x_\ell}^\gamma
        \bigr)
        \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{\mathrm d}
        \nu_{t_c^\gamma}^{\otimes\ell}.
\]
Equivalently, in the original uniform parametrisation, the limiting
fitnesses are independent and uniform on $[q_c^\gamma,1]$, where $q_c^\gamma:=1-e^{-t_c^\gamma}$.

In a finite Markov count model with marked events, a spatial advance may leave counts unchanged. Its contribution rate*(h(new)-h(old)) to Lh is zero, but its counting-process intensity still contributes to the advance reward compensator. In the reviewed two-slab FPP model, the front self event at (1,1) has rate one and advances one slab. An independent exact C=2 calculation gives mean cycle time883/57, advance1709/57, ratio883/1709; deleting that reward gives the different ratio883/1708. A bias certificate and cycle definition must retain the marked self event.
Marked event process distinguished from the count trajectory
Bounded finite-state bias; integrable regeneration time

[Theorem thm:main_result_asymptotic of arXiv:2609.02659, 'Dimension Dependent Correlation Gap Bounds under Restricted Independence'] [Asymptotically tight bound]
For any $n$, any nonnegative monotone submodular function $f: 2^{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_+$ and any $\mbox{\boldmath $x$} \in [0,1]^n$: 
$$\frac{f^{+}(\mbox{\boldmath $x$})}{f^{++}(\mbox{\boldmath $x$})} \leq \frac{e}{e-1}$$
Moreover, the bound is asymptotically attained when:
\begin{comment}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\roman*)]
 \item The monotone submodular function is $f(S)=g_m(S),\; \forall S \subseteq [n]$, a union coverage function with weights $w_H=1,\;\forall H \in \mathcal{H}_m$
 \item 
The feature family is $\mathcal{H}_m=\{H \in A_1\times A_2 \times ..A_{m-1}\times Q:
\; |A_r|=q,\; \forall i \in  M \setminus \{m\},\quad \ell_{m}=n-(m-1)\ell\}$ consisting of $m$-tuples where $m=m(n)\to\infty,\quad m=o(n)$
\item 
The marginal probabilities are identical with $x_i=\frac1m, \;\forall i \in [n]$
\end{enumerate}
\end{comment}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\roman*)]
\item
The ground set is partitioned into $m$ blocks as
$
N=A_1\cup A_2\cup\cdots\cup A_{m-1}\cup A_m,
$ where \newline
$$|A_r|=\ell=\left\lfloor\dfrac{n}{m}\right\rfloor,\; \forall r\in M \setminus \{m\},\quad
|A_m|=\ell_{m}=n-(m-1)\ell,$$
and the feature family is defined as
$
\mathcal H_m=A_1\times A_2\times\cdots\times A_{m-1}\times A_m$, 
consisting of all $m$-tuples obtained by selecting one element from each set of 
the partition.
\item
The asymptotic regime considers the number of partition blocks $m$ as a
function of $n$, denoted by $m=m(n)$, with both $n$ and $m(n)$ tending to
infinity and $m(n)$ growing sublinearly in $n$, \emph{i.e.},
\[
n\to\infty,\qquad m(n)\to\infty,\qquad m(n)=o(n).
\]
\item
The marginal probabilities are set to be identical with
$x_i=\frac1m,\; \forall i\in N$.
\item
The function $
f(S)$ is the coverage function $g_m(S)$ with unit feature weights $w_H=1$ for every $H\in\mathcal H_m$ and counts the number of features covered by at least one element of $S$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Prop boxsmash-qcof of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The functor $\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}}$ restricts to a homotopical functor
    \[
        \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}^\textup{qcof}_*
        \times
        \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}^\textup{qcof}_*\to
        \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}^\textup{qcof}_*
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        If $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-cofibrant, then we find $\alpha\colon G\to G_1$ and $\beta\colon G\to G_2$ together with cofibrant $X'\in\cat{$\bm{G_1}$-\textbf{\textup{L}}-Top}_*$ and $Y'\in\cat{$\bm{G_2}$-\textbf{\textup{L}}-Top}_*$ such that $X=\alpha^*X'$ and $Y=\beta^*Y'$. Then the based orthogonal $G$-space $X\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}} Y$ is the restriction of the based orthogonal $(G_1\times G_2)$-space $X'\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}} Y'$ along $(\alpha,\beta)\colon G\to G_1\times G_2$. As $X'\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}} Y'$ is cofibrant by Lemma~(lemma:boxsmash of the paper), we conclude that $X\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}} Y$ is quasi-cofibrant.

        Similarly, we deduce from Lemma~(lemma:box-product-bifun-general of the paper) that for $X$ and $Y$ as above the top horizontal map in the pushout square
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                X\vee Y\arrow[d]\arrow[r]\arrow[dr,"\ulcorner"{very near end},phantom] & X\boxtimes Y\arrow[d]\\
                1\arrow[r] & X\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}} Y
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        defining $X\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}} Y$ is a restriction of a $(G_1\times G_2)$-cofibration along $(\alpha,\beta)$, and hence in particular an h-cofibration. Thus, Lemma~(lemma:h-cof-compute-po of the paper) shows that this square is also a homotopy pushout. Given now $G$-global weak equivalences $f\colon X_1\to X_2$ and $g\colon Y_1\to Y_2$ of quasi-cofibrant based $G$-spaces, the map $f\boxtimes g$ is a $G$-global weak equivalence by Corollary~(cor:box-product-bifun of the paper), as is $f\vee g$ by Lemma~(lemma:coprod-well-based of the paper). We conclude that also the induced map on homotopy pushouts $f\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}} g$ is a $G$-global weak equivalence.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop boxsmash-qcof of arXiv:2608.28504

title: FPP chi=1/3 campaign, 2026-08-12 fire 93 (MONOTONICITY_PROBE_20260812.md): variance monotonicity Var(X_{n+1}) >= Var(X_n) for planar FPP reduces exactly to a signed-covariance statement via the identity Var(X_{n+1}) - Var(X_n) = Cov(X_{n+1} + X_n, Delta), Delta := X_{n+1} - X_n bounded by an O(1) triangle bound. FKG/Harris positive association is structurally inapplicable: Delta is not environment-monotone (two-route gadget, verified by construction - raising a weight on X_n's geodesics only makes Delta strictly fall). The known conditional proof of the MEAN's monotonicity (S_+ <= 2 S_- support condition, arXiv 1202.2665) works precisely because that condition kills the rerouting gadget, so the natural variance attack is conditional of the same shape. Status: open, obstruction named; genuinely separate from the wall-equivalent doubling sub-problem.

[Lemma 7 (Weighted local control and stationary lifting) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] The following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.3em]
\item The space $\mathfrak T_{J_{\mathrm{ps}}}$ is Banach and embeds
continuously into $\mathcal S'(\R^3)$.  Multiplication by a function in
$C_b^\infty$ is bounded on $\mathfrak T_{J_{\mathrm{ps}}}$.  Moreover, if a
convolution kernel $K$ satisfies
\[
 \int_{\R^3}\la x\ra^{2J_{\mathrm{ps}}+6}|K(x)|\dd x<\infty,
\]
then $f\mapsto K*f$ is bounded on $\mathfrak T_{J_{\mathrm{ps}}}$.  In
particular, the admissible multipliers $\pi_\Lambda$ are uniformly bounded on
this space.
\item If $r\ge-J_{\mathrm{ps}}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \|f\|_{\mathfrak T_{J_{\mathrm{ps}}}}
 \lesssim_r\|f\|_{H^r}.
\end{equation}
\item Let $Z$ be a spatially stationary random path.  If, for some
$p\ge2$ with $pJ_{\mathrm{ps}}>3$,
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb Z^3}
 \|\vartheta_zZ\|_{L^p(\Omega;C_TH^{-J_{\mathrm{ps}}})}<\infty,
\]
then $Z\in L^p(\Omega;C_T\mathfrak T_{J_{\mathrm{ps}}})$.
\item If $Z_n-Z$ is spatially stationary and the preceding local norm tends to
zero uniformly in $z$, then
$Z_n\to Z$ in $L^p(\Omega;C_T\mathfrak T_{J_{\mathrm{ps}}})$.
The same convergence holds almost surely whenever
\[
 \sum_n\sup_{z\in\mathbb Z^3}
 \|\vartheta_z(Z_n-Z)\|_{L^p(\Omega;C_TH^{-J_{\mathrm{ps}}})}^{p}<\infty.
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Definition def:gamma-mart of arXiv:2512.13200, 'Martingales on a Euclidean manifold with a boundary and reflected BSDEs in non-convex doma'] Let $f$ be an element of $\ensuremath{\mathscr{H}^{1}}$, and let $X$ be a continuous (Euclidean) semimartingale with values in $\bar{\mathcal{D}}$. Then, $X$ is a $\Gamma$-martingale on $\bar{\mathcal{D}}$ with the drift $f$ if $X=X_0-F+ K+M$, with $F=\int_0^\cdot f_s\,\mathrm{d} s$, with $M$ being an $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued local continuous martingale, and with $K$ being an $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued adapted continuous process such that
 $$K_t = \int_0^t k_s\mathrm{d} \!\text{Var}_s (K),$$
 where $(k_s)_{s \in [0,T]}$ is a progressively measurable process satisfying
 $$k_t \in \mathfrak{n}(X_t), \quad \text{for a.e. }  t \in [0,T].$$

The printed potential (121), Fong--Yang arXiv:2608.20638v2 p.55,

This prevents directly applying a theorem requiring a continuous Lyapunov
function to the both-supercritical active-curvature level set. It does
NOT refute the paper's potential growth inequality or its stated results.

Write b=9/10, c=(1-b)/(1+b)=1/19. The two branches, omitting their common
continuous term -Gamma(V), at the boundary have difference (upper minus
lower)

 J(y,z)= (y^2-b*z^2)/(1+b)-y^2/2+c*(y-z)^2/2
       = c*y^2-c*y*z+(c/2-b/(1+b))*z^2.

scalar coordinates (105): take e=1/10, d=999/1000,
V_t=(1-e)^2=81/100, y_(t-1)=1, mu_t=c, y_t=0. Recover

 mu_(t-1)=(c-(1-b))/b=-c,
 V_(t-1)=(81/100-(1-d))/d>0.

Then the raw moment updates give exactly mu_t,V_t, and the position
update y_t=y_(t-1)-w_t*mu_t/c gives zero at w_t=1. Varying V_t near
81/100 and setting mu_t=c/w_t keeps y_t=0 and y_(t-1)=1 while the
preceding variance and momentum vary continuously and stay physical.
Thus the upper and lower limits are limits of actual one-step histories,
not merely arbitrary pairs of consecutive positions.

The parameter e=1/10 corresponds to p=1 and lambda=190 in the original
normalization e=epsilon/(c eta lambda), so this is inside a supercritical
parameter range relevant to target1. It is not a claim about late-time
standard-initialization trajectories crossing this point.

Possible repairs require a new argument: an invariant-measure integral
can use a bounded measurable potential, but does not by itself classify
all omega-limit points or exclude heteroclinic pieces. Alternatively,
prove a continuous replacement potential or keep recurrence away from
the branch boundary. None of these repairs is supplied here.

\]
In particular, $\mathcal{C}_x^{\mathrm{bad}}(N)$ is finite almost surely.

Uniform forward-KL risk is at most comparator risk plus twice the stated covering/concentration bound and optimization error. Status: proof (unaudited), standard adaptation; no novelty claim. Complete constants and hypotheses are in the proof below.

# C006: prior-averaged Gaussian log-loss generalization

Claim T336-w727-C006 v1. Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: bound.
Target: none (reviewer-authorized generalization half of the T336 statement).
This is an explicit adaptation of standard covering and exponential-moment
arguments, not a claim of a new learning-theory principle or a new solver.
The hardest step is uniform concentration for the unbounded query loss.

## 1. Statistical statement

Let (W_i,Y_i), i=1,...,m, be independent identically distributed tasks, m>=1.
W contains the context and query features, including all information on which
the predictive is conditioned. Assume the conditional law is exactly

    Y | W ~ N(a(W), b(W)), |a(W)|<=M, 0<b(W)<=V,

where M>=0 and V>0 are fixed. The law of W is otherwise arbitrary. In
particular no independence between the query and context features is required.
For the GP application this conditional-law premise must be checked; it is
not inferred just from a marginal GP label law or an arbitrary feature-selection
mechanism. A fixed GP, exogenous input design, and rejection of tasks based only
on their context labels satisfy it. Conditioning on query labels would not.

Assume the token encoding of W is measurable. Let H be the family of clipped
transformer predictions described in Section 2,
with outputs mu_theta(W) in [-U,U] and v_theta(W) in [v0,v1], where
U>=0 and 0<v0<=v1 are fixed. Define the normalized negative log loss

    ell_theta(W,Y) = (1/2)log(v_theta/v0)
                    +(Y-mu_theta)^2/(2v_theta).

The usual Gaussian negative log density differs by the same constant
(1/2)log(2 pi v0) for every theta, so its ERM and excess risk are identical.
Let R(theta)=E ell_theta and Rhat(theta)=m^(-1) sum_i ell_theta(W_i,Y_i).
An approximate ERM satisfies Rhat(thetahat)<=inf_theta Rhat(theta)+xi,
with xi>=0. No efficient algorithm for finding it is asserted.

For gamma>0 and alpha in (0,1), use the explicit architecture quantities
P,Lambda from Section 2 and set

    q = max(1,ceil(2 Wmax Lambda/gamma)), J=(q+1)^P,
    D0=M+U,
    C=(1/2)log(v1/v0)+D0^2/v0, A=V/v0, K=4(C+A),
    u=log(4J/alpha), t=log(4m/alpha),
    T=M+sqrt(2V t),
    Q=1/(2v0)+(D0+sqrt(V))/v0+(D0^2+V)/v0^2,
    L_T=1/(2v0)+(T+U)/v0+(T+U)^2/(2v0^2),
    beta=4sqrt(2) K sqrt(u/m)+2K u/m,
    E_m=beta+gamma(Q+L_T).

Then, with probability at least 1-alpha, simultaneously for all theta,

    |R(theta)-Rhat(theta)| <= E_m,
    R(thetahat) <= inf_theta R(theta)+2E_m+xi.             (1)

Let P_W=N(a(W),b(W)) and h_theta=N(mu_theta(W),v_theta(W)). Subtracting
the integrable conditional Gaussian entropy gives equivalently

    E_W KL(P_W || h_thetahat(W))
       <= inf_theta E_W KL(P_W || h_theta(W))+2E_m+xi.   (2)

For (2), assume also b(W)>=b0>0, as in the noisy-GP application. This
makes the conditional entropy finite and justifies subtracting it. Without
that lower bound (1) still holds, but (2) is not asserted via subtraction
of potentially infinite entropies.

## 2. Explicit parameter entropy for normalized ReLU attention

Fix N tokens, token dimension D>=1, L>=0 residual attention layers, at
most H>=1 heads per layer, and a linear two-output readout. No trainable
tokenwise MLP, softmax, or layer normalization is included in this architecture.
Pad unused heads by zero matrices. There are

    P=3HLD^2+2D

trainable scalar entries, all in [-Wmax,Wmax], with Wmax>=1. The encoding
of W into tokens is fixed and has every scalar coordinate bounded in
absolute value by K0>=1. One layer is exactly

    h_i^+ = h_i + N^(-1) sum_heads sum_j
                    ReLU(<Q h_i,K h_j>) V h_j.

Optionally apply a fixed coordinatewise clip onto [-Kcap,Kcap] after each
attention layer, with Kcap>=K0. This is fixed tokenwise ReLU postprocessing,
not a trainable MLP or layer normalization. For this variant use K_l=Kcap
for every l in the recurrences below instead of the growing K recurrence.
Clipping is nonexpansive, so the same E recurrence remains valid.

The readout acts on one fixed token. Apply coordinatewise interval clipping
to its two outputs. This postprocessing uses fixed, nontrainable constants;
each scalar clip is representable by two ReLUs. Count P as the trainable
parameters, not as every fixed scalar in this postprocessing.

Define deterministic nonnegative recurrences

    K_{l+1}=K_l+H D^4 Wmax^3 K_l^3,       K_0=K0,
    E_0=0,
    E_{l+1}=(1+3H D^4 Wmax^3 K_l^2) E_l
                       +3H D^4 Wmax^2 K_l^3,
    Lambda=D Wmax E_L+D K_L > 0.

For any two parameter vectors theta,theta' in the cube at sup distance
rho, the outputs obey

    sup_W max(|mu_theta-mu_theta'|,|v_theta-v_theta'|)
        <= Lambda rho.                                  (3)

To verify this, use the sup norm across all tokens and coordinates. Each
transformed coordinate Qh has magnitude <=D Wmax K_l; each score has
magnitude <=D^3 Wmax^2 K_l^2; each Vh coordinate has magnitude
<=D Wmax K_l. The normalized sum cancels N and proves the K recurrence.

At fixed weights, changing inputs by d changes one head by at most
3D^4 Wmax^3 K_l^2 d: two terms differentiate the score and one term
the value; ReLU is 1-Lipschitz. At fixed inputs of size K_l, changing
matrix entries by rho changes a head by at most
3D^4 Wmax^2 K_l^3 rho, by the same three-term product split. Splitting
the joint change into these two changes and adding the residual proves
the E recurrence by induction. The readout change is bounded by
D Wmax E_L rho+D K_L rho. Clipping is 1-Lipschitz, proving (3).
These estimates compare actual heads directly, and require no independence
among tokens or between successive layers.

Divide [-Wmax,Wmax] into q equal intervals. There are q+1 grid values;
each parameter has a grid value within 2Wmax/q<=gamma/Lambda.
Thus the full grid has J elements and gives a gamma cover in the output
metric of (3). It is fixed before seeing the training tasks. In particular
log J <= P log(2+2Wmax Lambda/gamma) except when the max with 1 is active;
in that case q=1 and the same bound still holds since 2+2Wmax Lambda/gamma>=2.

## 3. A uniform exponential moment and finite-cover concentration

Write Z=(Y-a(W))/sqrt(b(W)). Its conditional law given W is standard
normal, hence Z is independent of W. For every theta,

    0 <= ell_theta <= C+A Z^2.

Indeed |Y-mu_theta|<=D0+sqrt(V)|Z| and (r+s)^2<=2r^2+2s^2.
Since C/K<=1/4 and A/K<=1/4, Gaussian integration yields

    E exp(ell_theta/K)
       <= exp(C/K)(1-2A/K)^(-1/2)
       <= exp(1/4)sqrt(2) < 2.                           (4)

The last inequality follows from log(2)>1/2 (integrate 1/x on [1,2]).
It follows from the nonnegative exponential series that
E ell_theta^k <= 2 k! K^k for every integer k>=1. For
X=ell_theta-E ell_theta, convexity gives

    E|X|^k <= 2^k E ell_theta^k <= 2^(k+1) k! K^k.

For |z|<1/(2K), the centered exponential series therefore gives

    log E exp(z X) <= 8K^2 z^2/(1-2K|z|).              (5)

Interchange of expectation and the series is justified by the absolute
moment series, which converges at these z. Independence across the m
tasks gives for their centered sum the same bound with 8mK^2 in
the numerator. Chernoff's inequality and (5) give each one-sided tail

    Pr(|Rhat(theta)-R(theta)| >
                  sqrt(32)K sqrt(u/m)+2K u/m) <= 2exp(-u).

For completeness, the generic bound log E exp(z S)<=v z^2/[2(1-cz)]
implies Pr(S>=sqrt(2vu)+cu)<=exp(-u): substitute
z=r/(1+cr), r=sqrt(2u/v), into the exponential Markov bound.
Here v=16mK^2, c=2K; apply it also to -S and divide by m.
No bounded-label assumption has been used.

A union bound on the J fixed grid predictors, with u=log(4J/alpha),
shows all their risk deviations are <=beta except on probability alpha/2.

## 4. From the grid to every parameter

For two clipped predictors within gamma in both output coordinates,
the elementary log derivative and a difference-of-squares split give

    |ell_theta(W,Y)-ell_theta'(W,Y)| <= gamma L(Y),
    L(Y)=1/(2v0)+(|Y|+U)/v0+(|Y|+U)^2/(2v0^2).       (6)

In detail, the log term costs gamma/(2v0). Hold v fixed and vary the
mean to get gamma(|Y|+U)/v0. Hold the new mean fixed and vary 1/v to
get gamma(|Y|+U)^2/(2v0^2). Both denominators use the common positive
floor v0. Thus E L(Y)<=Q: E|Y|<=M+sqrt(V) and
E(|Y|+U)^2<=2D0^2+2V.

The standard-normal exponential integral E exp(zZ)=exp(z^2/2), followed
by exponential Markov at z=x, gives Pr(|Z|>x)<=2exp(-x^2/2).
For t=log(4m/alpha), a union bound gives |Y_i|<=T for all i except
on probability alpha/2. On that event the empirical average of L(Y_i)
is at most L_T. Combine this event with the grid concentration event.
For each theta choose a grid point theta' satisfying (3). Insert
R(theta') and Rhat(theta') and use (6) to obtain the first line of (1).
The approximate-ERM inequality then gives the second line of (1).
The same event works for all approximate ERMs, without a union over
their potentially data-dependent choice. This proves (1) and (2).

## 5. GP comparator and scope

For the finite-rank noisy GP in C002, with supplied features bounded by R,
context length <=n and context labels bounded by B, one can use

    M=nR^2 B/s, V=s+R^2.

Take a desired comparator accuracy eps_c>0, U=M+sqrt(s eps_c),
v0=s, v1=V+s min(1/2,sqrt(eps_c)). C002's scalar error estimates
ensure its outputs lie in these intervals and its expected forward KL
is <=eps_c. Its padded encoding has K0=max(1,R,B,s), width D=7p+4,
at most H=5 heads and L=T_c+2 layers. The construction gives fixed
explicit matrices and readout. Choose Wmax at least 1 and their largest
absolute scalar entry; this is an explicitly computable maximum of the
finite matrices specified by C002 Section 4, independent of task data.
The class of Section 2 then contains that comparator, and (2) implies

    E_W KL(P_W || h_thetahat(W)) <= eps_c+2E_m+xi.        (7)

One may use the internally clipped variant with the explicit common cap

    Kcap=max(1,R,B,s,2nRB/s,2R/s,U,v1).

It preserves the C002 comparator exactly: its feature and query registers
are bounded by R; for every Chebyshev iteration j, |r_j(lambda)|<=1,
so the mean-solve iterates have norm <=2nRB/s and the variance-solve
iterates have norm <=2R/s. The previous-iterate registers have the same
bounds. Initialization, broadcast, constants, and final output registers
are covered by the other displayed terms. Thus clipping changes none
of its states. For this class the parameter Lipschitz recurrence uses a
constant Kcap, and log Lambda grows at most linearly with depth, avoiding
the very loose cubic growth of the unclipped K recurrence. The statistical
bound (7) is consequently explicit for a class containing the comparator
with either choice of internal clipping. All added clipping parameters
are fixed, so P still counts exactly the trainable entries.

For R=0 use a constant exact comparator instead of C002's formulas that
divide by R. The class can contain it by initializing a constant coordinate
and choosing a readout that outputs (0,s).

If training uses rejection to enforce bounded context labels, (7) concerns
the resulting conditioned task distribution. It is not silently a theorem
for the original unconditioned GP context law. With unconditioned contexts,
the C002 comparator guarantee and this bounded-input parameter cover do
not apply as stated. This is the precise remaining distributional scope
issue, separate from the unbounded Gaussian query labels handled above.

All constants here are explicit but loose. The parameter cube and finite
cover give a statistical ERM guarantee, not SGD convergence, efficient
enumeration of the cover, a finite-bit realization theorem for the original
solver, or a claim that Chebyshev depth beats Newton-type solvers.

## 6. Sources and status

Bai, Chen, Wang, Xiong and Mei, arXiv:2306.04637v2, Section 5.1,
PDF pages 14-15, define pretraining ERM for square loss and give Theorem 20.
That is the related parameter-entropy/ERM framework, not a citation for
the Gaussian log-loss bound above. Sections 2-4 provide its proof directly.
C002 v1 supplies the independently checked uniform-KL comparator.
This extension itself remains unaudited. No novelty is claimed.

[Theorem 82 (Trace-clock obstruction to compact capacity cores) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Assume that $H$ is infinite dimensional and let $(e_n)$ be an orthonormal
sequence.  Let $\mathbb P_n$ be the law on $\Omega_H$ of
\[
 X_t=W_t e_n,
\]
where $W$ is a standard real Brownian motion.  Then
$\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak S_{1,0}^{0,T}(H)$ for every $n$, and for every compact
$K\subset C_0([0,T];H)$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{n\ge1}\mathbb P_n(K^c)
 =c_{\mathfrak S_{1,0}^{0,T}(H)}(K^c)=1.
\end{equation}
Consequently the trace-clock class is not uniformly tight and admits no compact
capacity core.  Moreover, no $\Gamma\in\mathcal S_1(H)_+$ satisfies
\[
 e_n\otimes e_n\preceq\Gamma
 \qquad\text{for every }n.
\]

[Theorem 4 (Varying environment) of arXiv:2605.04048, 'Catastrophe--dispersion models in random and varying environments across generations'] Assume $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\ge0}$ is deterministic and $0<\mu_n<+\infty$ for all $n$.
Define
\[
\underline{\Lambda}=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{S_n}{n},\qquad
\overline{\Lambda}=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{S_n}{n}.
\]
\begin{itemize}
  \item[(a)] If $\overline{\Lambda}<0$, then $\p(Z_n\to0)=1$ (extinction).
  \item[(b)] If $\underline{\Lambda}>0$, then $\p(Z_n\to\infty)>0$ (survival with positive probability).
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For an m by n matrix A = (a_{ij}) and a p by q matrix B, the Kronecker product A tensor B is the (mp) by (nq) matrix written in m by n block form, whose (i,j) block, of size p by q, equals a_{ij} B, for i = 1,...,m and j = 1,...,n. The Kronecker product satisfies the mixed-product property (A tensor B)(C tensor D) = (AC) tensor (BD) whenever the ordinary products AC and BD are defined, and if A is n by n with eigenvalues lambda_1,...,lambda_n and B is m by m with eigenvalues mu_1,...,mu_m, then A tensor B is nm by nm with eigenvalues lambda_i mu_j for all i,j. By definition of median, P(A) >= 1/2. By convexity of f, for any x and any y in conv(A), f(x) - f(y) <= L * ||x - y||_2. \]

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] The divisible sandpile on $\Z^d$ starts from i.i.d.\ masses at each site, and, in each discrete time step, a site with mass above one keeps one unit and sends the excess equally to its neighbors. \citet*{LMPU} showed that at mean one this process explodes, with every site emitting infinite mass. We show that the mass emitted from a site by time $t$ is of order $t^{(4-d)/4}$ for $d\leq3$, of order $\log t$ for $d=4$, and a tail-dependent, divergent rate for $d\geq5$. We further show that the mass emitted, after diffusive rescaling, converges to a Brownian optimal-stopping value for $d\leq3$ and to tail-dependent, weighted membrane fields for $d\geq5$, while at the critical dimension $d=4$, after superdiffusive rescaling, it converges to the membrane model. Using these estimates, we prove that, for every $d\geq2$, the set of sites that topple contains an infinite component at some mean below one, hence it has a non-trivial percolation phase transition. This answers a variant of a question of \citet*{FMR}. The proof adapts ideas from the theory of level-set percolation of strongly correlated Gaussian fields.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02829: Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile

[Prop 3 (All-order block recursion) of arXiv:2608.30374, 'Compact and Infinite-Order Error Analysis\\ for Null-Space SVD Estimation'] For \(k\geq1\), let
\begin{align}
    \Lambda_k
      &=Q_0^TA_1V_{k-1}+Q_0^TA_2V_{k-2}
        -\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}(Q_0^TV_{k-j})\Lambda_j,
      \\
    V_k^{\perp}
      &=G\left(
          -A_1V_{k-1}-A_2V_{k-2}
          +\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}V_{k-j}\Lambda_j
        \right),
      \\
    \Gamma_k
      &=-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}V_j^TV_{k-j},
      \qquad
    V_k=V_k^{\perp}+Q_0\Gamma_k.
    
\end{align}
Then \(V^{[K]}(\sigma)=\sum_{k=0}^K\sigma^kV_k\) satisfies the invariant
subspace equation and orthonormality through order \(K\).  The sum defining
\(\Gamma_k\) is symmetric: transposition followed by the reindexing
\(j\leftrightarrow k-j\) leaves it unchanged.  Thus
\(Q_0^TV_k=\Gamma_k\) is symmetric, or equivalently
\(\operatorname{skew}(Q_0^TV_k)=0\); this choice fixes the otherwise
arbitrary internal rotation gauge. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: All-order block recursion

body: Every natural number is a sum of four integer squares: for all n >= 0 there exist integers a, b, c, d with n = a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2.

[Theorem isoperimetric of arXiv:2608.31043, 'Sharp constants for weak estimates of Riesz Potentials when $0<s<\min\{n,2\}$'] Let $0<s<\min\{2,n\}$ and let $E\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with measure satisfying $0<|E|<\infty$. If $B_R$ is a ball
such that $|B_R|=|E|$, then
$$\operatorname{Cap}_s(E)\geq \operatorname{Cap}_s(B_R).$$
Moreover,
$$\operatorname{Cap}_s(B_R)=\frac{\Gamma(n/2)}{\gamma_{n,s}\Gamma(s/2)\Gamma((n-s+2)/2)}R^{n-s}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Entezari, Sedghi, Saukh and Neyshabur, Theorem D.1 (=3.1): initialization-only, fixed-input and fixed-interpolation-parameter specialization. Let d>=1 and h>=2 be integers. Let U,U' in R^(h x d) have mutually independent entries uniform on [-1/sqrt(d),1/sqrt(d)]. Let v,v' in R^h have mutually independent entries uniform on [-1/sqrt(h),1/sqrt(h)], independent of U,U'. Define f(v,U;x)=sum_i v_i max(0,u_i dot x). For each fixed deterministic x with ||x||_2=sqrt(d), fixed deterministic alpha in [0,1], and delta in (0,1), with probability at least 1-delta there is a simultaneous row/coordinate permutation P of (U',v') for which |f(alpha v+(1-alpha)Pv',alpha U+(1-alpha)PU';x)-alpha f(v,U;x)-(1-alpha)f(v',U';x)| = O_d(h^(-1/(2d+4)) times logarithmic factors in h and delta^-1). P can be selected using U,U' alone. This is a random-initialization output-interpolation estimate for two-layer ReLU networks. No trained-SGD result, dimension-free rate, simultaneous bound over all inputs or interpolation parameters, or loss-barrier conclusion is asserted by this card.
Fixed d>=1 and h>=2; exact two-layer unnormalized output sum and ReLU activation.
All input weights iid uniform on [-1/sqrt(d),1/sqrt(d)]; all output weights iid uniform on [-1/sqrt(h),1/sqrt(h)]; independence between all four arrays.
Deterministic x with Euclidean norm sqrt(d), deterministic alpha in [0,1], and 0<delta<1, selected before the random weights.
Only initialization; no SGD training or simultaneous uniform input/interpolation claim.

Fix d>=1, h>=2, delta in (0,1), a deterministic x with ||x||_2=sqrt(d), and a deterministic interpolation parameter alpha in [0,1]. All coordinates of U,U' are independent uniforms on [-1/sqrt(d),1/sqrt(d)], and all coordinates of v,v' are independent uniforms on [-1/sqrt(h),1/sqrt(h)], independent of U,U'.     ||D x||_2^2 <= 4d(h/q^2+|I|).

The output interpolation residual is exactly

    E_alpha=alpha v dot r+(1-alpha)(Pv') dot r'.

Conditional Hoeffding and a union bound give, with conditional probability at least 1-delta/2,

    |E_alpha| <= 2alpha(1-alpha) sqrt((2/h)log(8/delta)) ||Dx||

    h^(-1/(2d+4)) sqrt(2d log(8/delta)
        [4+sqrt(log(8h^(d/(2d+4))/delta)/2)]).

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2605.07059, 'Modified ruin probability for a Cram{\'e}r-Lundberg model driven by a compound mixed Poiss'] Assume that $\ell_1<c/\mu$ and $G(\{\ell_1\})=0$. Suppose that there exist $\delta>0$, $B,C_1,D_1,R_1>0$, and $b>0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item$G$ has a density $g$ on $(\ell_1-\delta,\ell_1)$ and $g(\ell_1-z)\sim Bz^{b-1}$ as $z\downarrow0$;
\item the fixed-intensity theorem holds at $\ell=\ell_1$, with constant $C_{\ell_1}$, and for every $M>0$,
\[
\sup_{0\le v\le M}\left|\frac{\psi_{\rm cl}(u,\ell_1-v/(D_1u))}{C_1e^{-R_1u}e^{-v}}-1\right|\to0,
\]
\[
\sup_{0\le v\le M}\left|\frac{\psi_{\ell_1-v/(D_1u)}(u)}{\psi_{\rm cl}(u,\ell_1-v/(D_1u))}-C_{\ell_1}\right|\to0;
\]
\item the adjustment coefficient $R(\ell)$ exists on $(\ell_1-\delta,\ell_1]$, satisfies $R(\ell_1)=R_1$, is differentiable at $\ell_1$ with $R'(\ell_1)=-D_1$, and there is $\eta>0$ such that $R(\ell)\ge R_1+\eta$ for $\ell\le \ell_1-\delta$.
\end{enumerate}
If $\psi$ is continuous or monotone on $(-\infty,0)$, then
\[
\psi(u)\sim C_{\ell_1}\,\psi_{\rm cl}(u)\sim C_{\ell_1}\frac{BC_1\Gamma(b)}{(D_1u)^b}e^{-R_1u},\qquad u\to\infty.
\]

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Posterior cones and sharp reconstruction thresholds on finite-mean Galton-Watson trees (October 2026), proves that for symmetric ferromagnetic Potts broadcasting with three or four states on an observed Galton-Watson tree with any finite mean offspring d and 0 < lambda < 1, reconstruction holds exactly when d lambda^2 > 1; at equality the root cannot be reconstructed. No assumption on the offspring variance or tail is needed. The three-state argument uses an explicit invariant cone of posterior laws built from H = y - x^2/2, where x and y are the quadratic and cubic centred posterior invariants; its two global inequalities are certified by exact nonnegative polynomial coefficients (80,532 coefficients, produced by two independent integer programs). The four-state case combines the same argument with a posterior cone from earlier work, which the paper credits. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/posterior-cones-reconstruction (commit fc9659e64c43). Not refereed.
title: Sharp reconstruction threshold d lambda^2 > 1 for three- and four-state Potts broadcasting on finite-mean Galton-Watson trees, via posterior cones (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/posterior-cones-reconstruction)

[Lemm 22 of arXiv:2609.01932, 'Essential dimension and faithful rank of finite $p$-gerbes'] Assume that $\mu_p\subset k$ and that $\band$ has $p$-primary
descent.  There is a finite separable extension $M/k$ of $p$-power
degree with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item the band $\band_M$ is represented by a constant $p$-group $P$;
\item the gerbe $\cG_M$ is neutral; and
\item $M$ is a splitting field for $P$.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2609.02444, 'The Hasse norm principle for $A_4$-quartic extensions of global function fields'] An element \((u,\sigma) \in G\) lies in \(\Phi\) if and only if there exists \(w \in (\ZZ/2\ZZ)^\ell\) such that \(w + \sigma(w) = u\).

  \[ |\Phi| = \sum_{i = 1}^\ell 2^{\ell-i} s(\ell,i).\]

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] Let $U\subset \R^2$ be an open set, and let $F:U\to \R^2$
be a random field with almost surely $C^1$ sample paths. Fix $v\in \R^2$.
Assume that for every relatively compact open set $O \subset U$, there exist a
neighborhood $V$ of $v$ and a constant $C_O<\infty$ such that, for every
$y\in V$, 
\begin{equation*}
\int_O p_{F(x)}(y)\,dx \le C_O,

\end{equation*}
where $p_{F(x)}$ denotes the density of $F(x)$ on $\R^2$.
Then
\[
\P\bigl(\exists x\in O:\ F(x)=v,\ \det DF(x)=0\bigr)=0.
\]
In other words, with probability one, the level $v$ is not a
 critical value of $F$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 9 of arXiv:2605.17296

[Lemma lem:finite-dimensional-sparse-recurrence of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \(Z_n=(Z_{n,1},\ldots,Z_{n,N})\), \(n\ge3\), be centered Gaussian vectors in
\(\mathbb R^N\) such that
\(
    \operatorname{Cov}(Z_n)=I_N
\)
for every \(n\). Assume that there exist constants \(C<\infty\) and \(\theta>0\) such that, for
all \(3\le n\le m\),
\[
    \max_{1\le i,j\le N}
    \left|
        \operatorname{Cov}(Z_{n,i},Z_{m,j})
    \right|
    \le
    C\left(\frac{n}{m}\right)^\theta .
\]
Then for every \(a\in\mathbb R^N\) with \(|a|<1\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists
\(\gamma>1\) and a sparse sequence
\(
    n_k:=\lfloor \exp(k^\gamma)\rfloor
\)
such that, with
\(
    r_k:=(2\log\log n_k)^{1/2},
\)
one has
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        |Z_{n_k}-r_k a|<\varepsilon
        \ \text{\rm for infinitely many } k
    \right)=1.
\]

[Thmintro rigidityspherical of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Assume $\bm{s} = (s_1, \dots, s_n) \in \mathcal{Z}(\Phi)$ is a spherical multislope or a $\mathbb{T}^2$-type planar multislope. Then either 
    $$\left((s_1, +\infty) \times \dots \times (s_n, +\infty)\right) \cap \mathcal{Z}(\Phi) = \varnothing$$
    or 
    $$\left((-\infty, s_1) \times \dots \times (-\infty, s_n)\right) \cap \mathcal{Z}(\Phi) = \varnothing.$$
    If Dehn filling $(M,\Phi)$ along the rational components of $\bm{s}$ results in a suspension flow on $S^1\times S^2$ or $\mathbb{T}^2\times I$, then both of the quadrants above are empty. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Rigidity of spherical multislopes

body: Let 0 < u_min < u_max and eta > 0, and let (u,v) in C satisfy u_min <= u <= u_max with u/v at distance at least eta from each mu_i, 1 <= i <= n. Under these conditions the stirring vector fields have the full rank property (A.23) on X_{u,v} (Proposition A.3), so the generator of the fast motion (drift and stirring) is uniformly elliptic on X_{u,v}, and mu_{u,v} is a stationary distribution of it. Its transition density p_t(x,y) with respect to mu_{u,v} satisfies |p_t(x,y) - 1| <= c_2 exp(-c_3 t) for all t >= 1 and x, y in X_{u,v}, with positive constants c_2, c_3 depending only on (u_min, u_max, eta).

[Proposition Exterior differential of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] The operator~$\mssd$
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
\item is $\mssE$-bounded, viz.
\[
\mssE(f)\leq \left\lVert\mssd f\right\rVert_{\msH_{}}^2 \leq 2\, \mssE(f)\,\mathrm{,}\;\, \qquad f\in\msD(\mssE) \,\mathrm{;}\;\,
\]
\item extends to a non-relabeled derivation on~$\msD(\mssE)$, viz.
\[
\mssd(f_1f_2)= (\mssd f_1)f_2 + f_1 (\mssd f_2) \,\mathrm{,}\;\, \qquad f_1,f_2\in\msD(\mssE) \,\mathrm{;}\;\,
\]
\item is decomposable over the direct-integral representation~(equation eq:DirIntForms of the paper) and represented by a $\nu$-essentially unique measurable field~$x\mapsto \mssd_x$ of derivations
\[
\mssd_x(f_1f_2)= f_1(x)\, \mssd_x f_2+ f_2(x)\, \mssd_x f_1 \,\mathrm{,}\;\, \qquad f_1,f_2\in\msD(\mssE) \,\mathrm{.}
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
\sup_{\sum_{I\in \mathcal{A}(m)} a_I^2 = 1} 
\mathbb{P}\left(
\Big\|\sum_{I\in \mathcal{A}(m)} a_I B^I_t\Big\|_{\infty,[0,1]}<\varepsilon\,\middle|\, \mathcal{F}_0^W
\right)
\leqslant \varepsilon^p\ \Psi_{m,p}
\]for all $\varepsilon>0$.

body: [Definition def-QD of arXiv:2605.03385, 'Quantum Loewner evolution in quantum natural time: phases and Markov properties'] Let $\ell > 0$. Let $\mathrm{QD}(\ell)$ be the law of $(\mathbb{D}, \phi)/{\sim_\gamma}$ where the field is sampled from the weighted measure $\frac{\gamma}{2\pi(Q-\gamma)^2}\mathcal{A}_\phi(\mathbb{D})^{-1}\mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb{D}, \ell}^{(\gamma, 0)}(d\phi)$. A sample from $\mathrm{QD}(\ell)$ is called a $\gamma$-LQG disk with boundary length $\ell$.

[Lemma lem:irreg2 of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields and associated function space'] Assume that $(Z_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ random variables.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Almost surely, one has 
    $$
    \limsup_{n \to + \infty} \frac{|Z_n|}{ \sqrt{\log(n+2)}} < + \infty . 
    $$
    \item If the random variables $Z_n$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, are independent, then one has almost surely
    $$
    \limsup_{n \to + \infty} \frac{|Z_n|}{ \sqrt{\log(n+2)}} >0. 
    $$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] Let $(\mu^k)_{k\ge 1}\subset \mathcal P_1(\R)$ and $\mu \in \mathcal P_1(\R)$. Then
\[
W_1(\mu^k,\mu)\to0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P_{\mu^k}\to P_\mu\ \text{ pointwise on }\mathbb R\ \text{and}\ \ba(\mu^k)\to\ba(\mu),
\]
and equivalently with uniform convergence of $P_{\mu^k}$ on $\mathbb R$. In particular,
\[
\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\big|P_{\mu^k}(x)-P_\mu(x)\big|\le W_1(\mu^k,\mu).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 (Empirical path-law rate) of arXiv:2608.07879, 'Sharp Wasserstein Convergence Rates for Empirical Path Laws of It\^o Processes'] Let $\rho >p\ge1$. Under Assumption \ref{assum:regularity}, let
\begin{equation}
    \mu:=\Lc(X),
    \qquad
    \mu_N:=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{X_i},
\end{equation}
where $X_1,\dots,X_N$ are independent copies of $X$. Then there exists
$C=C\bigl(d,T,p,\rho,\E\Lambda_X^\rho\bigr)>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
    \E\big[\Wc_p(\mu_N,\mu)\big]
    \le
    C(\log N)^{-1/2},
    \qquad N\ge2.
\end{equation}
title: Empirical path-law rate

body:
A topological space X is normal (meaning every pair of disjoint closed subsets has disjoint open neighbourhoods) if and only if for every pair of disjoint closed subsets A, B of X there exists a continuous function f: X -> [0, 1] with f = 0 on A and f = 1 on B (Urysohn's lemma and its converse). No T1 axiom is needed for this equivalence under this definition of normality.
X is a topological space
normal means disjoint closed sets have disjoint open neighbourhoods; no T1 axiom is assumed

Normality, in the equivalent form 'whenever C is closed, O is open, and C is contained in O, there is an open U with C contained in U and the closure of U contained in O', is applied repeatedly to build open sets U_q indexed by the rational numbers q in (0,1) (dyadic rationals suffice) such that A is contained in every U_q, every closure of U_q avoids B, and q < r implies the closure of U_q is contained in U_r. One starts with A inside the open set X minus B and interpolates one new index at a time. Define f(x) = inf of the set of q with x in U_q, with f(x) = 1 when x belongs to no U_q. Then f = 0 on A and f = 1 on B. Continuity: f(x) < a holds exactly when x lies in some U_q with q < a, an open condition; f(x) > a holds exactly when x lies outside the closure of some U_q with q > a, again an open condition; preimages of subbasic intervals [0,a) and (a,1] are therefore open, so f is continuous. Conversely, if such an f exists for disjoint closed A and B, then f^{-1}([0, 1/2)) and f^{-1}((1/2, 1]) are disjoint open sets containing A and B, so X is normal. body: [Definition DefDLE of arXiv:2410.23899, 'Tightness for interlacing geometric random walk bridges'] Let $\Sigma \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $\llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket$ be a non-empty integer interval in $\mathbb{Z}$. Consider the set $Y$ of functions $f: \Sigma \times \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ such that $f(i, j+1) - f(i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ when $i \in \Sigma$ and $j \in\llbracket T_0, T_1 -1 \rrbracket$ and let $\mathcal{D}$ denote the discrete $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$. We call a function $g: \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ such that $f( j+1) - f(j) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ when $j \in\llbracket T_0, T_1 -1 \rrbracket$  an {\em increasing path} and elements in $Y$ {\em collections of increasing paths}. A $\Sigma$-{\em indexed geometric line ensemble $\mathfrak{L}$ on $\llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket$}  is a random variable defined on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{B}, \mathbb{P})$, taking values in $Y$ such that $\mathfrak{L}$ is a $(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{D})$-measurable function. Unless otherwise specified, we will assume that $T_0 \leq T_1$ are both integers, although the above definition makes sense if $T_0 = -\infty$, or $T_1 = \infty$, or both.
title: Definition DefDLE of arXiv:2410.23899

Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent centered random variables, each sub-Gaussian with variance proxy sigma_i^2. Let S_n = sum_{i=1}^n X_i and sigma^2 = sum_{i=1}^n sigma_i^2. Then for any t >= 0, P(S_n >= t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2 * sigma^2)) and P(|S_n| >= t) <= 2 * exp(-t^2 / (2 * sigma^2)).

[Thm 15 of arXiv:2608.30173, '2608.30173'] Suppose that $u_\infty>0$. There exist $\va_1\in(0,1)$ and $C>0$
such that, for every $\va\in(0,\va_1)$ and every
$
u\in\mathcal D\cap\V(u_\infty,\ell,\delta;\va)
$
satisfying
$
\|\mathcal R_u-r_\infty\|_{C^0(\Omega)}<\va
$
and
$
\int_\Omega u^{\frac{2n}{n-2}}\,\ud x=1,
$
we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
&Y_\Omega(u)-r_\infty\\
&\geq
-C\mathfrak G(u)-
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
C\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}
\lambda_k^{-\frac{n+2}{4}}
(\ln\lambda_k)^{\frac{n+2}{2n}}+C\sum_{i\neq j}
\Lambda_{i,j}^{\frac{n+2}{2(n-2)}}
\left(
\ln\Lambda_{i,j}^{-1}
\right)^{\frac{n+2}{2n}},
&n\geq6,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle
C\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{\frac{2-n}{2}}+C\sum_{i\neq j}\Lambda_{i,j},
&n=3,4,5,
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
Y_\Omega(u)-r_\infty
\leq
C\mathfrak G(u)^{1+\gamma}.
\]
If, in addition, $Y_\Omega(u)\geq r_\infty$, then
\be
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{-\frac{n-2}{2}}
+\bm\Lambda+\|w\|^2
\leq
C\mathfrak G(u)^{1+\gamma}.
\end{aligned}
\ee

[Theorem 28 (Coupling from the past) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Consider a Glauber dynamic $R$ for a measure $\mu$ on $S^V$.
    Suppose that $S$ is partially ordered and that $R$ is monotone.
    Suppose moreover $S$ has a largest element $\alpha^+$ and a smallest element $\alpha^-$.
    We also write $\alpha^\pm$ for the corresponding elements in $S^V$.
    Then for any fixed $\Pi\in\Omega$:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item For any bounded $B\subset V\times\R_{\leq 0}$, the map $R_{\Pi(B)}:S^V\to S^V$ is monotone,
        \item The element $R_{\Pi(\Lambda\times[-t,0])}(\alpha^+)$ is decreasing in $\Lambda$ and $t$,
        \item The element $R_{\Pi(\Lambda\times[-t,0])}(\alpha^-)$ is increasing in $\Lambda$ and $t$.
    \end{itemize}
    In particular, if
    \[R_{\Pi(\Lambda\times[-t,0])}(\alpha^+)_u=R_{\Pi(\Lambda\times[-t,0])}(\alpha^-)_u\]
    then this value will not change if we replace $\alpha^+$ by any other $\alpha\in S^V$,
    $\Lambda$ by any larger set, and $t$ by any larger time. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Coupling from the past

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2604.15191, 'Quantitative Stability of Many-Marginal Schr\"odinger Bridge'] Suppose $\mu(x)$ and $\nu(x)$ are probability density functions on $\mb T^d$. Assume there exist positive constants 

$m_\mu, m_\nu, M_\mu, M_\nu\in\mb R_+$ such that $\mu(x)\in[m_\mu, M_\mu]$ and $\nu(x)\in[m_\nu, M_\nu]$ hold for all $x\in\mb T^d$. 
Let $(\phi_\varepsilon, \psi_\varepsilon)$ be the Schr\"odinger potentials~\eqref{eqn: Schro_sys}.
Then, there exist positive constants $C_\nu$ and $C_\mu$ depending only on $m_\nu, M_\nu, d$ and $m_\mu, M_\mu, d$ respectively, such that for any functions $\chi,\eta\in \m C(\mb T^d)$, 
we have
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
\mb V_\mu(\chi) &\leq \Big(4\varepsilon + C_\nu e^{\frac{2R^2}{\alpha} + 8\pi^2 d} + \frac{8\osc(\chi)^2}{3\varepsilon}\Big)\big[\m I_{\mu, \nu}^\varepsilon[\phi_\varepsilon] - \m I_{\mu, \nu}^\varepsilon[\phi_\varepsilon + \chi]\big],\\
\mb V_\nu(\eta) &\leq \Big(4\varepsilon + C_\mu e^{\frac{2R^2}{\alpha} + 8\pi^2 d} + \frac{8\osc(\eta)^2}{3\varepsilon}\Big)\big[\overline{\m I}_{\mu, \nu}^\varepsilon[\psi_\varepsilon] - \overline{\m I}_{\mu, \nu}^\varepsilon[\psi_\varepsilon + \eta]\big].
\end{align}    
\end{subequations}

Here, $\osc(\chi) = \sup_x \chi(x) - \inf_x\chi(x)$ is the oscillation of $\chi$ on $\mb T^d$; $R$ 

and $\alpha$ are the  two universal positive constants introduced in Proposition~\ref{prop: 2norm_local_convex}.
\myqed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2609.01114, 'Unbalanced spectral Tur\'an problem for color-critical graphs with prescribed large maximu'] Fix $p\ge2$. The following claims hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item If a complete multipartite graph has positive part sizes $s_1,\ldots,s_p$, then its spectral radius is the unique positive solution of
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{i=1}^{p}\frac{s_i}{\lambda+s_i}=1 .
\end{equation}
\item For fixed $D$ and $p$, the graph $(n-D)K_1\vee K_{m_1,\ldots,m_p}$ with $\sum_{i=1}^{p} m_i= D$ has maximum spectral radius when $m_1,\ldots,m_p$ are as equal as possible, and equality occurs only for such a balanced choice, up to permutation of the parts.
\item For fixed $n$, define the function $f_{n,p}(D):=\rho(S_{n,D,p})$, where $\left\lceil\frac{p}{p+1}n\right\rceil\le D\le n-1$.

Then $f_{n,p}(D)$ is strictly decreasing in $D$.
\item Denote $\eta_p:=\frac{2p-1}{p(p-1)}$.

There are constants $\beta_p\in(0,(100p^2)^{-1}]$ and $C_p>0$ such that, uniformly for $(1-\beta_p)n\le D\le n$,
\begin{equation}
        \left|\rho(S_{n,D,p})-\rho(T(n,p))-\eta_p(n-D)\right|
        \le C_p\left(\frac{(n-D)^2}{n}+1\right).
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
        \rho(S_{n,D,p})-\rho(T(n,p))
        =\eta_p(n-D)+O_p((n-D)^2/n)+O_p(1).
\]
\item For fixed $D$ and $p$, define $g_{D,p}(N):=\rho(S_{N,D,p})$, where $N\geq D+1$.

Then $g_{D,p}(N)$ is strictly increasing in $N$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2609.01114

[Theorem thm:BiInt of arXiv:2505.09604, 'Exceptional force, uncountably many solutions in the KPZ fixed point'] With probability one the following holds for every $\xi\in\Xi$ 
    \begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
       \item  (Bi-infinite interfaces live on the set of splitting points) For each $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the map $\tau \mapsto \tau(t)$ is a bijection between the set $\mathcal{T}^{\xi,-}$ (resp. $\mathcal{T}^{\xi,+}$) and the set $\mathfrak S_{t,\xi}^L$ (resp. $\mathfrak S_{t,\xi}^R$). In particular, the associated paths in $\mathcal{T}^{\xi,-}$ live in the set $\mathfrak S_\xi^L$, and the associated paths in $\mathcal{T}^{\xi,+}$ live in the set $\mathfrak S_\xi^R$.
        \item (Left and right bi-infinite interfaces corresponding to the same eternal solution are the endpoints of an interval in $\mathfrak{I}^{t,\xi})$  Let $b$ be a $\xi$-eternal solution and let $\tau^- \in \mathcal{T}^{\xi,-},\tau^+ \in \mathcal{T}^{\xi,+}$ be the associated interfaces from the bijections in Theorem (thm:mr of the paper). Assume that $\tau^- \in \mathcal{T}^{\xi,-}$ and $\tau^+ \in \mathcal{T}^{\xi,+}$  (i.e., $\tau^-$ and $\tau^+$ are not $\nu_{-\infty}$ or $\nu_{+\infty}$). Then, for each $t \in \mathbb{R}$, there exists an index $\alpha \in \mathcal \mathcal{I}^{t,\xi}$ such that 
        \[
        \tau^-(t) = \mathfrak{a}^t_\alpha,\quad\text{and}\quad \tau^+(t) = \mathfrak{b}^t_\alpha.
        \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:BiInt of arXiv:2505.09604

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2608.26823, 'Evolutes, involutes and parallels of Legendre curves in hyperbolic and de Sitter 2-spaces '] Let $(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d):I\rightarrow\Delta_1$ be a spacelike Legendre curve  with curvature $(m_h,n_h) $. 	 
Suppose	that there exists $\varphi:I\rightarrow\R$ such that $m_h(t)\cosh\varphi(t)+ n_h(t)\sinh\varphi(t)=0$ for all $t\in I$. Let $\bmu_{HE}(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)= HE(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)\wedge \bnu_{HE}(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)$ and denote the moving frame of $HE(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)$ by $ (HE, \bnu_{HE},\bmu_{HE}  )(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d) $.  Then  
$$ (HE, \bnu_{HE},\bmu_{HE}  )^T(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)  =B_2(-\varphi)R( -\pi/2) ( \bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d,\bgamma_h^s  )^T . $$
That is,  $ (HE(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)(t), \bnu_{HE}(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)(t),\bmu_{HE}(\bgamma_h,\bgamma_h^d)(t) )$ is obtained by applying a rotation with   angle $ -\pi/2$ to  $ (\bgamma_h(t),\bgamma_h^d(t),\bgamma_h^s(t) )$, followed by a boost in the $(-\bgamma_h^d)$-direction with rapidity $-\varphi(t)$  for all $t\in I$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 12 of arXiv:2608.26823

body: An outer measure on a set X is a function mu* from all subsets of X to [0, infinity] with mu*(empty) = 0, monotonicity (A subset B implies mu*(A) <= mu*(B)), and countable subadditivity (mu* of a countable union <= sum of mu*). Outer measures are cheap to build (e.g. by covering with a distinguished class and summing a premeasure), but are generally not additive on all sets - additivity is recovered on the Caratheodory-measurable sets.
title: Outer Measure

[Definition 24 of arXiv:2605.31344, 'Subcritical sharpness for real-valued spin models'] A \textit{decision tree} on $\Lambda$ is a pair $T = (x_1, (\psi_t)_{2 \leq t \leq n})$, where $x_1 \in \Lambda \cup \overline{E}(\Lambda)$ and for $2 \leq t \leq n$, $\psi_t$ is a function that takes as input $x_{[t-1]}$ and  $(\sfa, \omega)_{x_{[t-1]}}$ and returns an element $x_t \in \Lambda \cup \overline{E}(\Lambda) \setminus \{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}\}$.
    \begin{itemize}
    \item
    We say that $T$ is \textit{admissible} if it reveals edges only after any endpoints in $\Lambda$ have been revealed, so that the resulting sequence $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ is in $\overrightarrow{\Lambda}$.
    \item
    For a function $f: \{0, 1\}^{\overline{E}(\Lambda)} \rightarrow [0,1]$, we define
    \[
    \tau_{f, T}(\sfa, \omega) = \min \{t \geq 1: \forall \omega' \in \{0, 1\}^{\overline{E}(\Lambda)}, \omega'_{x_{[t]}} = \omega_{x_{[t]}} \Rightarrow f(\omega') = f(\omega)\}.
    \]
    This is the first time at which the value of $f$ is determined by the decision tree $T$.
    \item
    For $X \in \Lambda \cup \overline{E}(\Lambda)$, we write $R_{f, T}(X)$ for the event that there exists $t \leq \tau_{f, T}(\sfa, \omega)$ such that $x_t = X$. For $xy \in \overline{E}(\Lambda)$, we define
    \begin{align*}
         \delta_{xy}(f, T) = \mu[R_{f,T}(xy)] + \frac{\mu[R_{f,T}(x)]}{\mu[C_x]} + \frac{\mu[R_{f,T}(y)]}{ \mu[C_y]},
    \end{align*}
    where $C_x = \{\omega_{xy} = 0 \ \forall \, y \sim x \}$ and we interpret $\frac{\mu[R_{f, T}(x)]}{\mu[C_x]}$ as $0$ if $x \notin \Lambda$.
    \end{itemize}
title: Definition 24 of arXiv:2605.31344

[Proposition prop:LehnerFormula of arXiv:2510.01021, '\Large Random Matrices, Intrinsic Freeness, and Sharp Non-Asymptotic Inequalities\relatedv'] [Lehner's formula~[LehnerFormula1999] (see also~[bandeira2023free])]

Let $A_0,A_1,\dots,A_n$ be self-adjoint matrices and $X_{\mathrm{free}}$ as in Definition~(def:Xfree of the paper):
\begin{equation}
\big\| X_{\mathrm{free}} \big\| = \max_{\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}} \inf_{Z\succeq 0} \lambda_{\max}\left(Z^{-1} + \varepsilon A_0 + \sum_{k=1}^n A_k Z A_k \right).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:LehnerFormula of arXiv:2510.01021

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2604.07697, 'Stochastic fractional heat equation with general rough noise'] Let $ \frac{3-\alpha}{4}<H<\frac 12$ and  $\lambda(x)=c_H(1+|x|^2)^{H-1}$ satisfy $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\lambda(x)dx=1$.  Assume that $\sigma(t,x,u)$ satisfies hypothesis (H1) and that the  initial datum $u_0$ belongs to $\mathcal{Z}_{\lambda,0}^p$ for some $p>\frac{2(\alpha+1)}{4H-3+\alpha}$.
  Then there exists a unique weak solution to \eqref{SFHE} whose sample paths lie in $\mathcal{C}([0,T]\times\mathbb{R})$ almost surely. Moreover, for any $0<\gamma<\frac{2H+\alpha-2}{2}-\frac{\alpha+1}{p}$, the process $u(\cdot,\cdot)$ is almost surely H\"older continuous on any compact subset  of $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}$, with  H\"older exponent $\frac{\gamma}{\alpha}$ in the temporal variable  and H\"older exponent $\gamma$ in the spatial variable. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:simplicity_CM of arXiv:2607.16911, 'Multipartite random graphs with given degrees: local limit, revisiting the giant, distance'] Assume the pair $(i,j)$ is $\rm GOOD$, $i,j\in [k]$.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item If $i=j$, $\liminf_{n \to \infty}\Prob{CM_n^{i,i}\textrm{ is simple}}=e^{-\phi_i/2-(\phi_i)^2/4}>0$.
        \item  If $i \neq j$, $\liminf_{n \to \infty}\Prob{CM_n^{i,j}\textrm{ is simple}}=e^{-\phi_{i,j}}>0$.
        \item The law of $CM_n^{i,i}$ conditionally on the event $\{CM_n^{(i,i)}\textrm{ is simple}\}$ is uniform on the set of all simple graphs on $\mathcal N^{(i)}$ with degree sequence $\mathbf d_i(n)$.
        \item The law of $CM_n^{i,j}$ conditionally on the event $\{CM_n^{(i,j)}\textrm{ is simple}\}$ is uniform on the set of all simple bipartite graphs on $\mathcal N^{(i)}\cup \mathcal N^{(j)}$ with bi-degree sequence $(\mathbf d_{(i,j)}(n),\mathbf d_{(j,i)}(n))$.
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Simplicity probability of configuration models

Method: Sharp constant-one comparisons of reversible mixing and stopping parameters structural calculation Result: The stopping half follows from Dynkin optional sampling. Let Lf=-lambda*f with lambda=1/tau2, mean_pi f=0, and choose x with f(x)=M=max f>0. For any integrable randomized stopping time U from x with X_U distributed as pi, E f(X_U)-f(x)=-lambda*E integral_0^U f(X_s)ds. Thus M=lambda*E integral f<=lambda*M*E U, giving E U>=tau2. The discrete-time proof replaces the integral by sum_(s<U)f(X_s). Check: Apply the identity first at U wedge n. The bounded function and integrability of U justify dominated convergence of the integral and of f(X_(U wedge n)). This avoids the false assertion that an exponential eigenfunction martingale is automatically uniformly integrable at U. Obstruction: The bound on tau1 by tau0 remains unresolved here. Worst-start total variation cannot be bounded solely by an unweighted spectral trace without controlling eigenfunction amplitudes. The source convention uses the continuized threshold and pairwise total variation, not the usual distance-to-pi threshold.

[Lemma 69 (Moment rates imply almost-sure convergence) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $B$ be a Banach space, let $X_N\in L^p(\Omega;B)$ for every
$p\ge2$, and suppose that, for some $C,\rho,\gamma>0$ and numbers
$\varepsilon_N\ge0$,
\begin{equation}

 \norm{X_N}_{L^p(\Omega;B)}
 \le C(p+\rho)^\gamma\varepsilon_N,
 \qquad p\ge2.
\end{equation}
Then, for $t\ge2$,
\[
 \Prob\!\left\{\norm{X_N}_B>
 eC(t+\rho)^\gamma\varepsilon_N\right\}\le e^{-t}.
\]
If
$\varepsilon_N(\log(N+1)+\rho)^\gamma\to0$, then $X_N\to0$
almost surely in $B$.

\[
\lambda_0:=\Lp(d_J\partial_{xx}+q(x)\partial_x+a(x),\R).
\]
At the critical scaling $m=2$,
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}\lim_{\sigma\to0}\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,2,(-L,L)})
=
\lim_{\sigma\to0}\lim_{L\to\infty}\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,2,(-L,L)})
=\lambda_0.
\]
More precisely, for every fixed $L$,
\[
\lim_{\sigma\to0}\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,2,(-L,L)})
=
\lambda_1^D(d_J\partial_{xx}+q(x)\partial_x+a(x),(-L,L)),
\]
whereas for every fixed $\sigma>0$,
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,2,(-L,L)})

\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:symmetric_components}
If a PMF $f$ has a symmetric component, then it is neither variance symmetrization resistant nor entropic symmetrization resistant. 

\begin{proof}
Let $f = g * h$ satisfy the assumption, where $g$ is symmetric and nondegenerate ($\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{\supp(g)} \ge 2$). 
For a PMF $\varphi$ define $\varphi_-$ by $\varphi_-(z) = \varphi(-z)$ everywhere. 
Note that $h * h_-$ is a symmetric PMF. 
Thus $f* h_- = g * (h * h_-)$ is symmetric (the convolution of two symmetric PMFs is symmetric) 
and $h_- \in \Sym(f)$. 
Since $g$ is nondegenerate, $h \ne f$ and $h_- \ne f_-$. 
Moreover, $\Var(h_-) = \Var(h)$ and $H(h_-) = H(h)$. 
Therefore we need only show that $\Var(h) \le \Var(f)$ and $H(h) \le H(f)$. 

For variance, taking independent $X \sim g$ and $Y \sim h$, we have $X+Y \sim f$ and
\[ \Var(f) = \Var(X+Y) = \Var(X) + \Var(Y) = \Var(g) + \Var(h) > \Var(h) . \] 
Noting that $h$ cannot be periodic, 
we apply strict concavity and translation-invariance of entropy: 
\[ 
H(f) 
= H(g * h) 
= H\bigg(\sum_{w \in \supp(g)} g(w)h(\cdot-w)\bigg) 
> \sum_{w \in \supp(g)} g(w) H(h(\cdot-w))

= H(h). \qedhere
\] 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 35 (Quartic Bessel connection) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let
\[
 \Phi_4(t)=\E\exp\!\left(\frac{it}{4}Z^4\right),
 \qquad
 z=\frac{i}{8t},
 \qquad
 A(t)=\frac1{2\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\frac it}\,e^z,
\]
where the square root is positive on \(t=i\tau\), \(\tau>0\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_4(t)=A(t)K_{1/4}(z).
 
\end{equation}
It satisfies
\begin{equation}
 16t^2\Phi_4''+(32t+4i)\Phi_4'+3\Phi_4=0,
 
\end{equation}
whose two formal exponential levels at \(t=0\) are \(0\) and
\(i/(4t)\).

On the ray \(z>0\), put \(\nu=1/4\) and define the two lateral
normalisations of the exponential solution by
\[
 \Phi_{\exp}^{+}
 =
 A(t)\,iK_\nu(e^{i\pi}z),
 \qquad
 \Phi_{\exp}^{-}
 =
 -A(t)\,iK_\nu(e^{-i\pi}z).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{\exp}^{+}-\Phi_{\exp}^{-}
 =
 i\sqrt2\,\Phi_4.
 
\end{equation}
Thus the switching rays are
\(\arg t=\pi/2\pmod\pi\), whereas the equal-magnitude rays are
\(\arg t=0\pmod\pi\).

The full quartic twisted module has Jacobi basis
\([1],[x],[x^2]\).  It splits into an even block of rank two and an odd
block of rank one.  The Gauss--Manin orbit of the real Gaussian cycle
detects the complete even block and annihilates the odd block.  For an odd rapid-decay cycle
\(\Omega\), its nonzero period
\[
 H_\Omega(t)
 =
 \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \int_\Omega x
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{itx^4}{4}\right)\dd x
\]
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 H_\Omega'
 =
 -\frac{i+2t}{4t^2}H_\Omega,
 \qquad
 H_\Omega(t)=C_\Omega t^{-1/2}e^{i/(4t)}.
 
\end{equation}

[Lemma 35 (Key properties of the tamed drift) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Assume that \hyperref[ass:PJG]{\textnormal{(A1)}}, \hyperref[ass:PLC]{\textnormal{(A2)}},
and \hyperref[ass:D]{\textnormal{(A4)}} hold.
Then for any $\theta,\bar\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and any $0<\lambda<1$, the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
\emph{Dissipativity.}
The tamed drift satisfies
\[
  \langle h_\lambda(\theta),\theta\rangle
  \ge
  a\|\theta\|^2 - b .
\]

\item
\emph{Growth control.}
The magnitude of $h_\lambda$ satisfies
\[
\|h_\lambda(\theta)\|
\le
2a\|\theta\| + 2L\,\lambda^{-1/2},
\qquad
\|h_\lambda(\theta)\|
\le
(2a+L)\bigl(1+\|\theta\|^{\ell+1}\bigr).
\]

\item
\emph{Lipschitz continuity.}
There exists a constant $L_0>0$, depending only on
$a,L,\ell$, such that
\[
\|h_\lambda(\theta)-h_\lambda(\bar\theta)\|
\le
L_0\,\lambda^{-1/2}\,\|\theta-\bar\theta\|,
\]
where
\[
L_0 := 2a + 4L + (\ell+1)(2L+a).
\]

\item
\emph{Taming error.}
The deviation between the original and tamed drifts satisfies
\[
  \|h(\theta)-h_\lambda(\theta)\|^2
  \le
  4\lambda^2 (L+a)^2
  \bigl(1+\|\theta\|^{\,6(\ell+1)}\bigr).
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 138 (Terminal generation versus terminal enhancement) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] The selected terminal map extends uniquely to a continuous map
\[
 \mathcal G_T:\overline{\mathscr T_0}
 \longrightarrow\mathscr W_{Q,\cP}^{1,2}
\]
if and only if $\mathcal G_T^0$ is Cauchy-continuous.  Equivalently, for every
$d_{\mathscr T}$-Cauchy sequence $(\xi_n)$, the first-jet sequence
\[
 \bigl((Y^{\xi_n},Z^{\xi_n})\bigr)_{n\ge1}
\]
is Cauchy in $d_{\mathscr W}$.  In particular, it is sufficient that a
nondecreasing
modulus $\omega$ with $\omega(0)=0$ and
$\lim_{r\downarrow0}\omega(r)=0$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 d_{\mathscr W}\bigl((Y^\xi,Z^\xi),(Y^\eta,Z^\eta)\bigr)
 \le \omega\bigl(d_{\mathscr T}(\xi,\eta)\bigr),
 \qquad \xi,\eta\in\mathscr T_0.
\end{equation}
If Cauchy continuity fails, the first-jet completion cannot be the graph of a single-valued
continuous map over the zero-order terminal completion.  This happens, in
particular, if one terminal Cauchy sequence has non-Cauchy continuation jets,
or if two equivalent terminal Cauchy sequences yield different stable
first-jet limits.  Relative to the declared terminal and first-jet response
program, any completion retaining all such response limits must then enhance
the terminal state by a first-order lift.

For every even N >= 2, the law on {-1,1}^N that puts mass 1/(2N) on each of the all-plus and all-minus vectors and spreads the remaining mass (N-1)/N uniformly over the vectors with exactly N/2 plus signs has Rademacher coordinates that are pairwise independent.
N is an even integer at least 2

[Proposition prop:minibatchOT of arXiv:2608.07042, 'Limit Points of Reflow with Minibatch Optimal Transport'] Let $\gamma\in \Gamma(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ and let $\gamma^{(N)}=\mathcal F_N(\gamma)$.
Then, the minibatch OT has the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] \textbf{Marginal Preservation:} It holds that $\gamma^{(N)}\in\Gamma(\mu_0,\mu_1)$.
\item[(ii)] \textbf{Reduced Transport Cost:} It holds $\int\|x-y\|^2\mathrm{d}\gamma^{(N)}(x,y)\leq \int\|x-y\|^2\mathrm{d}\gamma(x,y)$.
\item[(iii)] \textbf{Equality:} We have $\int\|x-y\|^2\mathrm{d}\gamma^{(N)}(x,y)= \int\|x-y\|^2\mathrm{d}\gamma(x,y)$ if and only if $\gamma$ is $N$-cyclically monotone.
\item[(iv)] \textbf{Continuous Cost:} The mapping $(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d),W_2)\to(\mathbb{R},|\cdot|)$ defined by $\gamma\mapsto \int\|x-y\|^2\mathrm{d}\mathcal F_N(\gamma)(x,y)$ is continuous.
\end{itemize}
title: Proposition prop:minibatchOT of arXiv:2608.07042

[Corollary cor:linear-infinite of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] When $\mathcal{A}(t, u) = -Au$ is linear with $A$ generating an analytic semigroup $S(t)$, and $\mathcal{B}(t, u) = Q^{1/2}$ is state-independent, then for every deterministic direction $h \in \operatorname{Ran}(\gamma_t)$ (the covariance $\gamma_t$ being deterministic here, so that clause~\textup{(ii)} of Assumption~(ass:nondeg of the paper) is automatic) the Bismut formula reduces to
\[
  \beta_h(u) = -\ip{u - S(t)x}{\gamma_t^{\dagger}h}_H,
\]
which is Theorem 4 of [mirafzali2025infinite].

Method: Kernel criteria for critical inhomogeneous random-graph universality structural reduction Result: L3 integrability of the principal eigenfunction does not itself give a spectral gap. Partition[0,1] into blocks of masses p_i tending to0, choose epsilon_i>0 tending to0, and let m=sum p_i epsilon_i. On blocks i,j set kappa=(1-epsilon_i)1{i=j}/p_i+epsilon_i epsilon_j/m. This symmetric positive kernel has row integral1, so its principal eigenfunction is the constant1 in L3. For the centered indicator of block i, the Rayleigh quotient tends to1 as epsilon_i tends to0. Check: The row integral is1-epsilon_i+epsilon_i=1. The Dirichlet energy of the block indicator is at most p_i epsilon_i, while its centered L2 norm squared is p_i(1-p_i). Thus the spectral gap is at most epsilon_i/(1-p_i), tending to0. Positivity of the kernel makes the constant eigenfunction unique up to scale. Obstruction: The example is an obstruction to using an unstated spectral-gap consequence of the conjectured criterion. It is not asserted to refute random-graph universality; the component scaling for this explicit kernel remains to be analyzed.

body: [Definition def: contraction along an edge of arXiv:2603.10738, 'Pairwise Negative Correlation for Uniform Spanning\\ Subgraphs of the Complete Graph'] Suppose $G=(V,E)$ is  a finite graph and $e\in E$ is an edge. The \textbf{contraction} $G/e$ is the graph obtained from $G$ by identifying  the endpoints of $e$ (and removing the resulting self-loops). Similarly, if $e,f$ are two edges of $G$, then $G/\{e,f\}$ is the graph obtained from $G$ by identifying all the endpoints of $e,f$. See Fig.~(fig: K_n contraction along an edge of the paper) for examples of $K_n/e$ and $K_n/\{e,f\}$.
title: Definition def: contraction along an edge of arXiv:2603.10738

[Prop lem: existence of tau of arXiv:2604.21663, 'Large deviations for non-irreducible Markov chains on Euclidean spaces'] Assumption~(hyp: pseudo uniformity with tau of the paper) is equivalent to:	
	\\Assumption {\rm (B')}. For all admissible compact sets $K\subseteq C$, there exist a constant $c'_K$ and an integer $\tau_K$ such that, for all $j\in \mathcal J_K$,
	\begin{equation}
		
		\rho^k(x_1,y)

	\end{equation}

body:
[Proposition prop-F Poisson pp class QL of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] Suppose that $(X, \mathscr{B}_X) $ is a non-empty measure space and 
\[
\mathfrak{A} = \bigl( \Omega, \mathscr{F}, \mathbb{P}, \mathbb{F} \bigr), \mbox{ with } \mathbb{F} = (\mathscr{F}_t)_{t\geq 0} ,
\]
is a filtered probability space. Assume that a  point process $p: \Omega \to \Pi_X$ (on $X$ defined on $\Omega$) is  an $\mathbb{F}$-Poisson   point process. Then the following two conditions are equivalent.
 \begin{trivlist}
 \item[(a)] The point process $p: \Omega \to \Pi_X$  is of class \textbf{(QL)}  (with respect to filtration $\mathbb{F}$).
 \item[(b)] For every $U\in \Gamma_p$, the function
\[(0,\infty) \ni t \mapsto \mathbb{E}\bigl[ {\eta}_p((0,t] \timesU)\bigr]
\]
is continuous.
\end{trivlist} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop-F Poisson pp class QL of arXiv:2505.24043

body: [Proposition 64 of arXiv:2609.03070, 'Variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices'] The $r$-$\sigma$-demicontinuity and $r$-$\sigma$-semicontinuity are inherited by $\sigma$-regular sublattices, for every $r\ge 1$. In particular, $\sigma$-semicontinuity, $\sigma$-demicontinuity and topological $\sigma$-semicontinuity pass down to $\sigma$-regular sublattices. $\sigma$-order continuity also passes down to $\sigma$-regular sublattices. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 64 of arXiv:2609.03070

body:
[Lemma lem:second_moment_differential_inequality of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] Let $G=(V,E,J)$ be a transitive weighted graph, let $o$ be a vertex of $G$ and let $K$ be the cluster of $o$ in Bernoulli-$\beta$ percolation. Then
\[
\frac{d}{d\beta} \mathbb E_\beta |K| \geq \min_{e\in E} \left[\frac{J_e}{e^{\beta J_e}-1}\right] 
 \left(\frac{\mathbb E_\beta|K|^2}{4\mathbb E_\beta|K|}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbb E_\beta|K|+\frac{1}{4}\right)
\]
for every $\beta<\beta_c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:second_moment_differential_inequality of arXiv:2508.18809

body:
[Prop ShaoZhang of arXiv:2604.07711, 'Central Limit Theorem for Random Partial\\ Sphere Coverings in High Dimensions'] Let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_N)$ be a vector of $N\geq 1$ i.i.d.\ $E$-valued random variables and $f:E^N\to\mathbb{R}$ be a measurable function which is symmetric under all permutation of its arguments. Let $V_N:=f(X_1,\ldots,X_N)$, and define
\[
W_N:=\frac{V_N-\mathbb{E}[V_N]}{\sqrt{\var(V_N)}}.
\]
Then
\[
d_K(W_N,\mathcal N(0,1))
\leq
12\, N^{1/2}\var(V_N)^{-1}
\left(
\sqrt{N\delta_1}+N\sqrt{\delta_2}+\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(\Delta_1 f(X))^4]}
\right),
\]
where
\[
\delta_1
:=
\sup_{Y,Z\in\mathcal C(X,X',\widetilde X)}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[
\mathbf 1\{\Delta_{1,2}f(Y)\neq 0\}\,(\Delta_1 f(Z))^4
\right]
\]
and
\[
\delta_2
:=
\sup_{Y,Y',Z\in\mathcal C(X,X',\widetilde X)}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[
\mathbf 1\{\Delta_{1,2}f(Y)\neq 0,\ \Delta_{1,3}f(Y')\neq 0\}\,(\Delta_2 f(Z))^4
\right].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop ShaoZhang of arXiv:2604.07711

body: Fubini's theorem gives the conditions under which a double integral can be computed as an iterated integral, i.e. by integrating in one variable at a time. Intuitively, just as the volume of a loaf of bread is the same whether one sums over standard slices or over long thin slices, the value of a double integral does not depend on the order of integration when the hypotheses of the theorem are satisfied. The theorem is named after Guido Fubini, who proved a general result in 1907; special cases were known earlier through results such as Cavalieri's principle, which was used by Leonhard Euler.
title: Fubini's theorem

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2606.15843, 'Long-time behaviour of DLRA for SDEs'] Suppose  Assumptions~(H1)--(H6) hold. Moreover, suppose Assumption~\ref{AS:relation1} holds. 
    Then, there exists a constant $C(b,\sigma)>0$ such that for any $r\in\{1,2,\cdots,d\}$,
		\begin{equation}
			\sup_{t\in[0,\infty)}\bb E[|X^{(r)}_t|^2]\le C(b,\sigma)\big(1+\bb E[|X^{(r)}_0|^2]\big).
		\end{equation}
		In particular, for $r=d$ we have 
		$
			\sup_{t\in[0,\infty)}\bb E[|X_t|^2]\le C(b,\sigma)\big(1+\bb E[|X_0|^2]\big)$.
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2606.15843

[Lemma 31 (Rational Tori Invariance) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $D$ be a derivation of the form $D= \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}$ where $f_i\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}(X)$ are nonzero rational functions, let $A_1,\ldots,A_n\in \mathbb{Q}$ be nonzero rational numbers. Then $D$ defines an algebraically integrable foliation if and only if
    $E=\sum_{i=1}^n A_if_i(x_i)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}$ does too.
title: Rational Tori Invariance

body:
[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2607.20646, 'The Independence-Preserving Property and Planar Web Geometry'] For each $T\in\{X,Y,U,V\}$, let $I_T$ be an open interval of $\R$.
    Let $\mu^0_T$ and $\mu_T$ be $\sigma$-finite Borel measures on $I_T$, both equivalent to Lebesgue measure. 
    Assume that the Radon--Nikodym derivative $\dd\mu_T/\!\dd\mu^0_T$ admits a positive continuous representative, and let $\varphi_T$ denote its logarithm.
    
    Let $F \colon I_X\times I_Y \to I_U\times I_V$, $F(x,y)=(u,v)$ be a real-analytic diffeomorphism, and assume that the planar $4$-web $\W_F=(x,y,u(x,y),v(x,y))$ on $I_X\times I_Y$ is nonsingular.
    
    Suppose that $F$ preserves the independence of $(\mu^0_X,\mu^0_Y,\mu^0_U,\mu^0_V)$.
    Then $F$ preserves the independence of $(\mu_X,\mu_Y,\mu_U,\mu_V)$ if and only if
    \begin{equation}
        (\varphi_X,\varphi_Y,-\varphi_U,-\varphi_V)\in\A(\W_F).
    \end{equation}
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2607.20646
