Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). After the optimism reading was refuted (P20), the gain was located row by row: the per-evaluation-row relative-score gain of the long-only stack over least squares against the bootstrap variance of the least-squares stack at that row. P22 (a) REFUTED at the pre-registered 0.2: the within-cell median Spearman between a row's gain and the least-squares variance load at that row is 0.13 over the 40 EMIT cells (positive in 36 of 40; 0.37 on Y2, 0.01 on Y1); (b) HELD on Y2, REFUTED as an every-group claim: the top-decile-load rows carry 47 pct of Y2's gain (a uniform spread gives 10) but only 11 pct on Y1 (20 on Y3, 32 on Y4); (c) HELD: across the 40 EMIT cells the gain rank-correlates 0.54 with the variance-load share of least squares' error, and 0.65 with the share the constraint removes (least squares minus nn1) - the between-cell statistic that optimism (P20) failed to be; (d) REFUTED as written: the OCO-2 top-decile share reaches 0.40 on sco2, but as the share of a gain of -0.55 pct it is the ratio of two near-zero numbers and does not test the clause; falsifier (within-cell correlation at or below zero) not triggered. Reading: where the gain is large (Y2, +18) it sits where least squares is uncertain - row-level rank correlation 0.37, 47 pct of the gain on the tenth of rows with the largest variance; where it is modest (+5 to +6) it is spread over the rows; between cells the variance-load share of least squares' error predicts the gain (0.54) and the variance the constraint removes predicts it better (0.65). The calibration and evaluation rows share the same target-norm distribution, so this is not a split shift; the gain leans toward the small-norm evaluation rows the reported metric weights most. Cell level: the variance the constraint removes (least squares' bootstrap variance share minus the long-only stack's) predicts the gain within every output group (Spearman 0.79, 0.87, 0.54, 0.43 on Y1-Y4; 0.69 across 40 cells with the group effect removed), while the L1 norm of the least-squares weights does not survive the group adjustment (0.02): the constraint pays what it saves in estimation variance at the rows it is scored on. Fresh-split replication (split C, SPLIT_SEED 11): P23 (a) REFUTED at the per-group 0.5, HELD in the aggregate: on split C the within-group Spearman between the gain and the variance removed is +0.59, +0.49, +0.64, +0.22 on Y1..Y4 and +0.74 across the 40 cells with the group effect removed (split B: +0.69); (b) REFUTED: the split-B variance-removed share predicts the split-C gain only on Y1 and Y2 (+0.72, +0.47; Y3 +0.09, Y4 -0.24; demeaned +0.17), and the split-B gain itself predicts the split-C gain only weakly (Y1 +0.82, Y4 +0.47, Y2 +0.15, Y3 -0.14); (c) HELD: the long-only stack beats least squares on 35 of 40 split-C cells (mean +9.59 against +8.83 on split B); falsifier (any group at or below 0.2, or the demeaned correlation at or below 0.3) not triggered. Fresh-split check of the calibration-side correlates (P32, the P20 driver on split C): P32 (a) HELD: on split C the between-cell Spearman of the gain with the least-squares L1 is +0.55 and with n_eff -0.44; (b) REFUTED: group-demeaned, L1 +0.29 and members kept +0.21; (c) HELD: the nn0 RMSE gain with the smallest relative eigenvalue +0.29 and with the condition number -0.31; falsifier (L1 above +0.3 after the group adjustment) not triggered. The gain off the tail (P36, the top tenth of evaluation rows by |gain| removed): P36 (a) HELD for the sign, REFUTED for the size: the trimmed gain is positive on 36 and 36 of 40 EMIT cells (splits B, C) but reads +7.67 and +8.30 against untrimmed +8.83 and +9.59 - the body keeps 87 pct of the gain, not less than half; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the trimmed gain is +0.25 against -0.18 untrimmed; (c) REFUTED: the smallest trimmed gain is on Y4, not Y1; falsifier (negative trimmed gain on EMIT) not triggered. Removing the two-sided tail leaves 87 pct of the EMIT gain: the constraint pays broadly across the rows, and the non-transfer between splits comes from the tails' noise, not from where the gain sits.

[Lemma 1 (Criteria for PRM convergence) of arXiv:2506.12632, 'Point process convergence of extremes in $K$-symmetric exclusion'] Let $\{\theta_t : t \ge 0\}$ be a sequence of point processes on $\R$ and $\mu$ a locally finite measure on $\R$. 
 The following are equivalent: 

	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]

	\item $\displaystyle \theta_t \underset{t\to\infty}{\Longrightarrow} \text{PRM}\,(\mu)$. 
	
	\item $\displaystyle \theta_t(B) \underset{t\to\infty}{\Longrightarrow} \text{Poisson}\,(\mu(B))$ for any $B \in \sU$. 
	
	\item $\displaystyle \theta_t(A_1) + \theta_t(A_2) + \cdots + \theta_t(A_m) \underset{t\to\infty}{\Longrightarrow} \text{Poisson}\,(\mu(A_1) + \mu(A_2) + \cdots + \mu(A_m))$ for any finite collection of disjoint, finite intervals $A_k = (a_k, b_k]$, $1 \le k \le m$. 	
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T232-w704-C016 v1. No independent PASS or established novelty/priority. Let finite m>=2,w>=2, rank-two M in R^(m-by-2), and SPD 2-by-2 Sigma define the asymmetric factor gradient flow. Suppose a balanced rank-one reference zbar(t) converges to a stationary endpoint zstar=(bstar;astar) with NONZERO PRODUCT bstar astar^T. Put Gstar=(bstar astar^T-M)Sigma and let v be the unit top eigenvector of Lstar=[[0,-Gstar],[-Gstar^T,0]]. At one sufficiently late FIXED entrance time, write actual flows U_epsilon=[z_epsilon,X_epsilon]. Assume uniformly for all small positive epsilon that ||z_epsilon(0)-zbar(0)||<=C0 epsilon, c0 epsilon<=||v^T X_epsilon(0)||_F<=c1 epsilon with fixed 0<c0<=c1, and ||(I-vv^T)X_epsilon(0)||_F<=h||v^T X_epsilon(0)||_F for a sufficiently narrow fixed cone aperture h. The reference future tail must be inside the chosen fixed local endpoint neighborhood. Then convergence alone permits thresholds delta_epsilon tending to zero and first-hit times t_epsilon tending to infinity with p(t_epsilon)=||v^T X_epsilon(t_epsilon)||_F=delta_epsilon, ||z_epsilon(t_epsilon)-zstar||<=D delta_epsilon^2, and ||X_epsilon(t_epsilon)||_F<=sqrt(1+h^2)delta_epsilon, for fixed D. For Z_epsilon=U_epsilon U_epsilon^T and Z1=zstar zstar^T, a fixed K>0 gives ||Z_epsilon(t_epsilon)-Z1||_F<=K delta_epsilon^2 and v^T Z_epsilon(t_epsilon)v>=delta_epsilon^2, hence strong relative Gram alignment at least 1/K. C015 supplies the strict active/dormant gap and the nonpositive dormant complement. No exponential reference rate or actual-family balance is needed. This does not prove the Gaussian active O(epsilon) entrance premise: C014's qualitative convergence alone is insufficient. It does not prove the complete rectangular second-step composition.

Choose a sufficiently late reference time as the fixed local time zero. Consider any actual width-w flow family U_epsilon=[z_epsilon,X_epsilon], with positive epsilon tending to zero, satisfying at this ONE fixed entrance time, with constants independent of epsilon,
 ||z_epsilon(0)-zbar(0)||<=C0 epsilon,
 c0 epsilon<=||v^T X_epsilon(0)||_F<=c1 epsilon,  0<c0<=c1,
 ||(I-vv^T)X_epsilon(0)||_F<=h||v^T X_epsilon(0)||_F.
Here h>0 is a sufficiently narrow fixed aperture, and all entrance conditions hold for every sufficiently small epsilon. No independence of evolving factors, exponential reference convergence, or balance of the actual family is assumed.

Then there are first-threshold times t_epsilon tending to infinity and positive thresholds delta_epsilon tending to zero such that
 p(t_epsilon)=||v^T X_epsilon(t_epsilon)||_F=delta_epsilon,
 ||z_epsilon(t_epsilon)-zstar||<=D delta_epsilon^2,
 ||X_epsilon(t_epsilon)||_F<=sqrt(1+h^2)delta_epsilon.
With Z_epsilon=U_epsilon U_epsilon^T and Z1=zstar zstar^T, a fixed K>0 satisfies
 ||Z_epsilon(t_epsilon)-Z1||_F<=K delta_epsilon^2,
 v^T Z_epsilon(t_epsilon)v>=delta_epsilon^2.
Hence the liminf of their relative alignment ratio is at least 1/K>0. Constants may depend on fixed data, endpoint, reference and entrance constants; there is no uniform quantitative lower bound across data.

## 1. Rectangular spectral premises
C015 proves, under exactly the nonzero-product endpoint premise, rank(Gstar)=1, s>0, simple top s of Lstar, nonpositive complementary spectrum (one -s and m zeros), and v perpendicular to zstar. The full active derivative Jact=DF(zstar) is symmetric with top rate r satisfying 0<=r<s. Its added m-2 transverse active directions have eigenvalue -astar^T Sigma astar<0. Thus neither the dormant zero modes nor the additional active directions introduce a competing positive top rate.

Choose rplus in (r,s). Continuity makes the largest eigenvalue of DF at most rplus on a small convex active ball of radius R about zstar. Choose h>0 and then eta>0 small enough that
 eta(1+h)^2<h s,
 a=s-eta(1+h)>rplus,  b=s+eta(1+h).
These choices are possible since rplus<s. Fix active and dormant balls, of radii R and R_X, so the exact dormant generator differs from Lstar by at most eta throughout them. The generator difference is -H(P-Pstar), where P=z_b z_a^T+VW^T for X=(V;W). It is continuous and vanishes at (zstar,0). Shift the reference sufficiently late that its entire future tail lies in the active ball of radius R/4. The theorem assumes the uniform entrance hypotheses at that chosen time.

## 2. Dimension-independent cone and active comparison
Write Y=v^T X, Q_X=(I-vv^T)X, p=||Y||_F, q=||Q_X||_F. Up to first exit from the local balls, the exact equation X'=(Lstar+R(t))X has ||R(t)||op<=eta. For p>0,
 sp-eta(p+q)<=p'<=sp+eta(p+q).
The symmetric nonpositive complementary spectrum gives D^+q<=eta(p+q), including q=0 by the norm triangle inequality. At q=hp,
 D^+(q-hp)<=[eta(1+h)^2-hs]p<0.
Thus the cone q<=hp is invariant before exit. The initial p is positive, and p'>=ap preserves positivity. Inside the cone,
 ap<=p'<=bp,  ||X||_F^2<= (1+h^2)p^2.
This calculation uses only a nonpositive complement, not its dimension or absence of zeros.

The exact active equation is z'=F(z)-H(VW^T)z. On a fixed bounded active ball, ||H(VW^T)z||<=C||X||_F^2, for a fixed C. With E=||z-zbar||, symmetry of DF and integration along the segment between z,zbar give
 D^+E<=rplus E+C(1+h^2)p^2.
For u<=t, lower cone growth gives p(u)<=p(t)exp(-a(t-u)). Integration therefore yields
 E(t)<=C0 epsilon exp(rplus t)+C1 p(t)^2,
 C1=C(1+h^2)/(2a-rplus).
The denominator is strictly positive because a>rplus>=0. This uses the full active derivative; frozen dormant transport is not substituted for it.

## 3. A uniform cutoff for each fixed threshold
Set k=rplus/a<1 and C_H=max(1,C0 c0^(-k)). Choose delta0 in (0,1) so
 (1+C1)delta0^2<R/4,  sqrt(1+h^2)delta0<R_X/2.
For any fixed delta in (0,delta0], reference convergence supplies a finite t_delta>=0 such that ||zbar(t)-zstar||<=delta^2 for every t>=t_delta. Impose
 epsilon<=epsilon_ent,
 epsilon<=delta/(2c1),
 epsilon<=[delta^(2-k)/(2C_H)]^(1/(1-k)),
 epsilon<=delta exp(-b t_delta)/(2c1).
Here epsilon_ent is the fixed entrance cutoff. All four bounds are positive at fixed delta and hold for every smaller epsilon as well.

Before the first threshold p=delta or the first exit, lower growth gives the elapsed-time upper bound T_upper=log(delta/(c0 epsilon))/a: an interval without either event cannot extend past this value. Therefore its homogeneous active error is at most
 C0 epsilon exp(rplus T_upper)<=C_H delta^k epsilon^(1-k)<=delta^2/2.
Consequently E<=(C1+1/2)delta^2<R/4 and z remains within R/2 of zstar, while ||X||<R_X/2. There is a strict margin to both exit boundaries. Smooth local continuation in these bounded balls excludes exit first and, by the lower growth bound, ensures that the threshold is attained by T_upper.

Upper growth gives the stopping-time lower bound
 t_stop>=log(delta/(c1 epsilon))/b>=t_delta+log(2)/b.
Thus the reference endpoint error is at most delta^2 at this stop. Combining it with E yields
 ||z-zstar||<=D delta^2,  D=C1+3/2.
The Gram expansion gives
 ||zz^T+XX^T-zstar zstar^T||_F<=K delta^2,
 K=2||zstar||D+D^2 delta0^2+1+h^2.
Indeed the active difference is bounded by 2||zstar||||z-zstar||+||z-zstar||^2, and ||XX^T||_F<=||X||_F^2. Positivity gives v^T Z v=(v^T z)^2+||v^T X||^2>=delta^2. In particular K is fixed independently of delta and epsilon.

## 4. One diagonal selection; all smaller epsilon, not a subsequence only
Let delta_n=delta0 2^(-n), n>=1. Choose epsilon_n strictly below half of epsilon_(n-1) for n>1, delta_n^n/2, epsilon_ent/2, and half of each of the other three cutoffs in Section 3 evaluated at delta_n. Every epsilon_n is positive, epsilon_n strictly decreases to zero, and the delta_n stop is valid for EVERY epsilon<=epsilon_n.

For epsilon<=epsilon_1 set n(epsilon)=max{n>=1:epsilon<=epsilon_n}. This set is nonempty and finite because epsilon_n tends to zero. Its maximum tends to infinity as epsilon tends to zero. Choose the actual first delta_n(epsilon) stop and put delta_epsilon=delta_n(epsilon). All estimates above apply uniformly there, so delta_epsilon tends to zero and the claimed alignment follows. Moreover epsilon<delta_n^n implies
 t_stop>=[(n-1)log(1/delta_n)-log c1]/b,
which tends to infinity. This checks the index direction and the number n-1 explicitly.

The reference convergence modulus t_delta may be arbitrarily slow. It only shrinks positive epsilon cutoffs; no rate or interchange of growing-time limits is used. QED, subject to independent review.

## Remaining frontier obligations
This establishes conditional local arrival over the whole m-by-2 range if its proof and C015 are correct. It does NOT establish the entrance hypotheses for Gaussian initialization, a complete rectangular canonical escape or its forward endpoint. C014 supplies fixed-compact origin matching and ideal output confinement, not a growing-time comparison or an active O(epsilon) error estimate by itself. In particular normalized dormant convergence cannot be substituted for the active O(epsilon) entrance premise without a separate argument. That Gaussian handoff remains the hardest open link of the rectangular extension.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Use the Apollonian structure of the limit to predict the local statistics in each patch. Result: The Pegden-Smart limit is a piecewise-quadratic function whose Hessian takes values in the set Gamma of integer superharmonic matrices; inside a patch where the Hessian is a fixed matrix A in Gamma, the sandpile is (Levine-Pegden-Smart) a periodic pattern determined by A, so the height-j fraction in a patch converges to the frequency of height j in that periodic pattern, which is a computable rational number. Hence the refinement holds in the interior of every patch; the question reduces to the boundary set between patches (the Apollonian gasket of patch boundaries), which has Lebesgue measure zero in the limit but whose discrete neighbourhood might carry a positive fraction of sites at scale n if the boundary layers have width of order n^{alpha}, alpha > 0... the patches are of all sizes (Apollonian), and the total area of patches of diameter < eps tends to zero as eps -> 0 (the gasket has Hausdorff dimension < 2), so for any delta the fraction of sites within the small patches is < delta for eps small, and within large patches the convergence holds; therefore the height-j fraction converges PROVIDED the discrete configuration inside a large patch is exactly the periodic pattern except in a boundary layer of o(n) width, which is the content of the Levine-Pegden-Smart 'Apollonian structure in the abelian sandpile' theorem (they prove the patterns appear; the width of the transition layers is what I could not confirm from memory). Conditional resolution recorded: the height-fraction convergence follows from the patch-pattern theorem plus an o(n) transition-layer bound plus the measure-zero gasket; the identity-element scaling limit remains open beyond the Caracciolo-Paoletti-Sportiello special case. Key identity: Inside a patch with Hessian A the height-j frequency is the frequency of j in the A-pattern; the gasket of boundaries has area zero, so convergence reduces to o(n) transition layers. Obstruction: Transition-layer width between patches not confirmed; identity element limit open.

Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T: X -> X continuous. For n >= 1 define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max_{0 <= i <= n-1} d(T^i x, T^i y). A set E contained in X is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if d_n(x,y) > eps for all distinct x, y in E; let s_n(eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n, eps)-separated set. A set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if for every x in X there is y in F with d_n(x,y) <= eps; let r_n(eps) be the smallest cardinality of an (n, eps)-spanning set. Both are finite by compactness. THEOREM (Bowen, Dinaburg): h_top(T) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log s_n(eps) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log r_n(eps), and this common value coincides with the Adler-Konheim-McAndrew topological entropy defined through open covers. The limits in eps exist in [0, +infinity] because s_n(eps) and r_n(eps) are nonincreasing in eps, so the inner quantities are nonincreasing in eps. The two counts are comparable at shifted scales: r_n(eps) <= s_n(eps) <= r_n(eps/2). SHARP EDGES. (a) The order of the limits is not negotiable: for a FIXED eps the quantity limsup_n (1/n) log s_n(eps) is in general strictly smaller than h_top(T) (it is the 'entropy at scale eps'), and it is only after eps -> 0 that one gets the entropy. The single exception worth remembering is an expansive homeomorphism, where any eps below the expansive constant already gives the answer. (b) Compactness is used to make the counts finite and to make the value a topological invariant. Bowen's extension to a uniformly continuous map of a possibly non-compact metric space, taking the supremum of the above over compact subsets, defines a quantity h_d(T) that depends on the METRIC and not only on the topology: uniformly equivalent metrics give the same value, but merely topologically equivalent ones need not, so on non-compact spaces 'the topological entropy' is not well defined without naming the metric. (c) Separated and spanning counts measure ORBIT distinguishability over a finite time window; they say nothing by themselves about invariant measures. The link to measures is the variational principle, h_top(T) = sup over T-invariant Borel probabilities mu of h_mu(T), which is a separate theorem and is not proved by the counting argument below. (d) The definition uses only forward iterates 0, ..., n-1, and for a homeomorphism this already gives the entropy of T; the two-sided window max over |i| <= n gives the same number, not twice it.
(X,d) is a compact metric space
T: X -> X is continuous
for the non-compact extension, T is uniformly continuous and the entropy is taken as a supremum over compact subsets, and then depends on the uniform equivalence class of d

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine whether the Gaussian free field characterisation can be made asymptotically exact. Result: DLP show t_cov ≍ |E| (E max GFF)^2; the later result of Ding (2012, 'Asymptotics of cover times via Gaussian free fields: bounded-degree graphs and general trees') gives asymptotic equality t_cov ~ |E| (E max eta)^2 for bounded-degree graphs when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, and Zhai (2018) proved the asymptotic formula for general graphs under the same condition. Given the asymptotic formula, a (1+eps) approximation of t_cov reduces to a (1+eps) approximation of E max of a Gaussian vector with given covariance (the Green function), which is a deterministic computational problem: computing E max of a Gaussian vector to within 1+eps is not known to be in deterministic polynomial time in general (the majorizing-measure/generic-chaining bounds are only within constants; exact computation of Gaussian maxima expectations is #P-hard in some formulations). So the question reduces, for graphs with t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, to the deterministic approximability of E max of a Gaussian vector with a graph-Laplacian covariance; a positive answer would follow from a deterministic FPTAS for Gaussian expected maxima on such covariances, which is open; graphs with t_cov ≍ t_hit (e.g. cycles, where the cover time is dominated by hitting times) need a separate treatment and are the easier case since hitting times are computable exactly. Reduction recorded. Key identity: t_cov ~ |E| (E max GFF)^2 when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity (Ding; Zhai), so (1+eps)-approximation reduces to approximating a Gaussian expected maximum. Obstruction: No deterministic (1+eps) algorithm for Gaussian expected maxima with general covariance.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0116-deterministic-1-epsilon-approximation-of-the-cover-time
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

[Lemma 66 (Distribution, completeness, and the little core) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] With \(\phi_r\) as in \eqref{cc:eq-critical-profile}, for a compact operator \(T\), the quantity
\(\sup_Ns_N(T)/\phi_r(N)\) is equivalent, with constants depending only
on \(r\), to the least \(A>0\) for which

\begin{equation}
 d_T(u):=\#\{N:s_N(T)>u\}
 \leq C_r\frac Au
 \left(\log\left(e+\frac Au\right)\right)^{r-1},
 \qquad u>0.
 
\end{equation}

The space \(\mathfrak W^{[r]}\) is a complete symmetric quasi-Banach
ideal.  Its little subspace is closed and is exactly the
\(\mathfrak W^{[r]}\)-closure of the finite-rank operators.  Moreover,

\[
 \mathfrak W^{[r]}_0\subset\mathfrak W^{[r+1]}_0.
\]

For every fixed \(n\),
\(\mathfrak W_{\mathrm{mf}}^{[r]}(H^{\otimes n})\) is complete, and its
little subspace is precisely the closure of the finite-dimensional tensors
in the big multi-flattening quasi-norm.  Tensor-leg permutations are
isometries of both spaces.

[Corollary 27 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$, let $(X,\Delta)$ be log canonical near a closed point $x$ but not klt at $x$, and let $W:=W_x(X,\Delta)$ be positive-dimensional. Let $d:=\dim W$, $b:=b_x(X,\Delta)$, $a:=(d-b)/2$, and $c:=\edim\mathcal O_{W,x}-d$. If $c=0$, then $\mult_xW=1$. Assume that $c>0$, and let $s:=\left\lfloor\frac{(c+1)a}{c}\right\rfloor$. Then
$$
 \mult_xW\leq
 \left\lfloor
 \frac{1}{s+1-a}\binom{c+s+1}{c+1}
 \right\rfloor.
$$

[Prop P:temporal-est of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $n < n+r \le 2n \in \mathbb{N}$, and parameter $\alpha \ge 1/2 - n^{-1/6}$. For any $x, y_2\in \llbracket0, n/1000 \rrbracket$, denote $y_1 = \lfloor x + n(y_2-x)/(n + r) \rfloor$, and 
$u_1 = [x, 0; y_1, n]_\textsf{L}$, $u_2 = [x, 0; y_2, n + r]_\textsf{L}$.
Take any $\epsilon > 0$ satisfying the constraints:
\begin{equation}
	
	C_0 \max \left(\frac{|x-y_2|^2}{n^2}, ((1/2 - \alpha)\vee 0)^2\right) < \epsilon < C_* r^{-1/3},
\end{equation}
where $C_0>0$ is a universal constant, and $C_*>0$ is any large enough number. 
Then for a constant $c>0$ depending only on $C_*$, we have
$$
\mathbb{P}\left( \left|\bar X(u_1) - \bar X(u_2)\right| \ge \epsilon r \right) \le 2\exp\left(-c \epsilon^{3/2} r \right).
$$
title: Prop P:temporal-est of arXiv:2604.10020

DRAFT proof (unaudited), T318-C8 v1. Let a test input x have an arbitrary finite-dimensional Gaussian law, let A be PSD, V=xprime A x, q=EV, and f=xprime delta with deterministic delta conditional on the training environment; f and V need not be independent. Put R=Ef^2 and v=Var(V)<infinity. Then abs(E[(1+f^2)/(1+V)]-(1+R)/(1+q))<=sqrt(3v)(1+R), and abs(E log(1+V)-log(1+q))<=sqrt(v). This follows from the noncentral scalar Gaussian bound Ef^4<=3R^2 and the 1-Lipschitz reciprocal/log functions on nonnegative arguments. The ratio error is relative to 1+R, so a uniform lower risk bound can survive even when R is unbounded as a regularization parameter approaches zero: first require 1/(1+q)-sqrt(3v)>0, then insert a common lower bound on R. For any PSD covariance C, teacher w and fitted vector w_hat in a subspace S, the bound (w_hat-w)prime C(w_hat-w)>=wprime C^(1/2) P C^(1/2)w holds with P the orthogonal projection onto (C^(1/2)S)^perp. A Euclidean nullspace projection does not supply the same bound. These two facts yield C8 realized-teacher non-tightness of global likelihood-temperature minimizers in C7 offset-linear random features; that application requires all C7 assumptions and is not a probability-one escape claim. No novelty or independent-audit claim.
Finite-dimensional Gaussian test input, PSD quadratic denominator, scalar linear Gaussian numerator as stated; conditional training quantities fixed.
For the lower-risk substitution the relative coefficient must be positive; no independence of numerator/denominator.
Own-work proof draft (unaudited); C8 application retains all C7 model assumptions.

body: In mathematics, the multiplicative ergodic theorem, or Oseledets theorem provides the theoretical background for computation of Lyapunov exponents of a nonlinear dynamical system. It was proved by Valery Oseledets in 1965 and reported at the International Mathematical Congress in Moscow in 1966. A conceptually different proof of the multiplicative ergodic theorem was found by M. S. Raghunathan. The theorem has been extended to semisimple Lie groups by V. A. Kaimanovich and further generalized in the works of David Ruelle, Grigory Margulis, Anders Karlsson, and François Ledrappier.
title: Oseledets theorem

For any $R>0$, let $\{B_{r_j/5}(x_j)\}_{x_j\in S}\subset B_{3R}(0)$ be mutually disjoint
with $x_j\in B_R(0)$, and let
\[
\mu=\sum_j \omega_k r_j^k\delta_{x_j}.
\]
If for every $B_r(y)\subset B_{2R}(0)$ we have
\[
\int_{B_r(y)}\left(\int_0^r D_\mu^k(z,s)\frac{ds}{s}\right)\,d\mu(z) \leq \delta_R^2 r^k,
\]
then
\[
\mu(B_R(0))=\omega_k\sum_{i \in I}r_i^k\le C_R(n)R^k.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 12 (Hausdorff) of arXiv:2609.03653, 'The derived set of multiple star polylogarithms'] A sequence $\{x_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is completely monotone if and only if there is a finite nonnegative Borel measure $\mu$ on $[0,1]$ such that
\[
x_n=\int_{[0,1]}t^n\,d\mu(t),
\qquad n\geq 0.
\]
If $x_0=1$, then $\mu$ is a probability measure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (X_n)_{n=1}^\infty be independent real random variables, and fix c > 0. Define the truncated variables Y_n = X_n \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n| \le c\}}. Then the series \sum_{n=1}^\infty X_n converges almost surely if and only if all three of the following series converge: (1) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{P}(|X_n| > c) < \infty; (2) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{E}[Y_n] \text{ converges in } \mathbb{R}; (3) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \text{Var}(Y_n) < \infty.
(X_n) independent
c > 0 constant

[Corollary 3 (Maximal EPI on connected compact groups) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group,
equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. For any pair
of independent random 
variables $X,Y$ on $G$,
$$h(X+Y)\geq \max\big\{h(X),h(Y)\big\}.$$
Moreover, suppose that $G$ is connected and 
$\max{\{h(X),h(Y)\}} = h(Y) >-\infty$. Then we have
equality if and only if either $Y$ is uniformly distributed
on $G$ or $h(X)=-\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Maximal EPI on connected compact groups

\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
\]
Then, for every $f\in \mathcal{P}_d(\mathbb{R}^n)$, one has
\[
[f]_\infty
\le
2(8d^2(1+M))^d\|f\|_{L^1(\mu)}.
\]

[Lem 19 of arXiv:2609.03653, 'The derived set of multiple star polylogarithms'] Suppose that
\[
f(z)=\int_0^1\frac{\phi(t)dt}{1-tz},
\qquad
g(z)=c+\int_0^1\frac{\psi(t)dt}{1-tz},
\]
where $c\geq 0$, $f,g\in\mathfrak{T}$, $\phi,
\psi>0$ on $(0,1)$, and $\phi/\psi$ is nondecreasing.  If $c=0$, assume in addition that
\begin{equation}
\int_0^1\frac{\psi(t)}t\,dt<+\infty.
\end{equation}
Then $f/g\in\mathfrak{T}$.

body:
[Proposition 15 (Lossless-chart factorization) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $(\mathsf Z,Z)$ be a $\cP$-causal state.  Let
\[
 \mathcal O:\mathsf Z\to\mathsf R,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D:\mathsf R\to\mathsf Z
\]
be stable-causal maps between causal Polish spaces such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D\mathcal O=I_{\mathsf Z}.
\end{equation}
Then $\mathcal O$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed retract
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal O(\mathsf Z)=\operatorname{Fix}(\mathcal O\mathcal D)
 \subseteq\mathsf R.
\end{equation}
This retract is generated by the stable-causal idempotent
$\mathcal O\mathcal D$.
For a $\cP$-causal source state $(\mathsf S,S)$, a joint realization of the
chart is a stable-causal map $\Psi:\mathsf S\to\mathsf R$ satisfying
$\Psi(S)=\mathcal O(Z)$ $P$-almost surely for every $P\in\cP$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.5em]
\item Every joint realization yields the stable-causal factor
$\mathcal D\Psi:S\to Z$, and every stable-causal factor $R:S\to Z$ yields
the joint realization $\mathcal O R$.  Thus
\begin{equation}
 \Psi\longmapsto\mathcal D\Psi,
 \qquad
 R\longmapsto\mathcal O R
\end{equation}
are inverse after maps agreeing on the realized source state under every law
are identified.  In particular, the source realizes the lossless chart if and
only if $Z\preceqsc S$, and the factor is unique on the realized source.

\item Every stable-causal readout
$F:\mathsf Z\to\mathsf T$ factors through the chart on its image:
\begin{equation}
 F=(F\mathcal D)\mathcal O.
\end{equation}
The factor $F\mathcal D$ is unique on $\mathcal O(\mathsf Z)$.  If in addition
$\mathcal O\mathcal D=I_{\mathsf R}$, it is the unique factor on all of
$\mathsf R$.

\item Suppose a stable-causal map
$\pi:\mathsf Z\to\mathsf Y$ preserves the full chart in the sense that
$\mathcal O=\Psi\pi$ for a stable-causal
$\Psi:\mathsf Y\to\mathsf R$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 L:=\mathcal D\Psi
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 L\pi=I_{\mathsf Z}.
\end{equation}
Consequently $\pi$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed retract of $\mathsf Y$
generated by the stable-causal idempotent $P:=\pi L$, and
\[
 \pi(\mathsf Z)=\operatorname{Fix}(P).
\]
If $\pi$ is surjective, then $\pi$ is a stable-causal homeomorphism with
inverse $L$.
\end{enumerate}

body: [Question of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] There are also more ambitious questions. First, can we cover distributions $\xi$ with no density, such as the Bernoulli measure? Already for a single Bernoulli matrix $X^N$, its least singular value estimates rely on elaborate technical tools such as inverse Littlewood-Offord theorem [rudelson2008littlewood] and the obstruction to invertibility is arithmetic. But here for higher degree $\mathfrak{p}$, even with Gaussian entries, the obstruction to invertibility is structural rather than arithmetic, as one can read off from the proof in Section (section33 of the paper). If we further consider Bernoulli entries, one would need to overcome both arithmetic and structural obstructions simultaneously. Second, this paper only considers $P^N$ depending on $X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N$ but not their adjoints, and from a free probability viewpoint (see Section (section5.1 of the paper)) it is also interesting to study $P^N=\mathfrak{p}(X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N,(X_1^N)^*,\cdots,(X_n^N)^*)$. The current framework does not cover this model. (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Defn normal_LDC of arXiv:2411.10633, 'A Geometric Perspective on the Injective Norm of Sums of Random Tensors'] A code $\mathcal{C}: \{-1,1\}^n \rightarrow \{-1,1\}^d$ is $(q,\delta, \varepsilon)$-normally locally decodable if for each $i \in [n]$, there is a $q$-uniform hypergraph matching $\mathcal{H}_i$ on the set $[d]$ (a collection of vertex disjoint hyperedges, where every edge has $q$ vertices) with at least $\delta d$ hyperedges such that for every $C \in \mathcal{H}_i$, one has $\mathbb{P}_{b \sim \{\pm 1\}^n}(b_i = \prod_{v \in C} \mathcal{C}(b)_v) \geq \frac{1}{2} + \varepsilon$. 
In particular, for linear codes, one has $b_i = \prod_{v \in C} \mathcal{C}(b)_v$ with probability 1. We therefore call these linear  $(q,\delta)$-normally locally decodable codes.
title: Normal LDC

U^{*}_{n}TU_{n}=\bigoplus_{\left|w\right|=n}X_{w},\qquad n\geq0.
\end{equation}

[Prop apriori of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Let $\varepsilon>0$. There exist $R_{0}=R_{0}(\varepsilon)$ and $C=C(\varepsilon)$ such that for each $R \ge R_0$ there exists $p_0=p_0(\varepsilon,R)$ such that for all $p<p_0$, $k \geq 1$, and $n> R^k$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{P}\!\left(X_{R^{\kappa-k}}> \mathbf{q}_n\right)\leq CR^{-\!\left(\frac{3}{4}-\varepsilon\right)k}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Relaxation of linear-polymer coagulation and fragmentation structural calculation Result: The cluster-count coordinate K has exact rates K->K+1 at beta*(n-K) and K->K-1 at K*(K-1)/n. Its deterministic equilibrium density mu solves mu^2=beta*(1-mu), and linearizing the density drift gives restoring rate beta+2*mu=sqrt(beta^2+4*beta). At beta=b/n this is order n^-1/2. The source edge coupling has discrepancy killing rate at least beta+(K-1)/n, so it also suggests this scale once K is near sqrt(b*n). Check: For n=3 the partition states3,21,111 have rates3->21=2beta,21->3=2/3,21->111=beta,111->21=2. Direct characteristic-polynomial calculation gives gap[3beta+8/3-sqrt(beta^2+16/9)]/2. Thus finite-n small-beta behavior cannot simply be substituted for the joint n,beta_n limit. Obstruction: The required upgrade is a uniform exponential bound on the coupling survival functional E exp[-integral(beta+(K_u-1)/n)du], including atypically small K. Replacing K by its stationary mean inside the exponential has the wrong Jensen direction and is not a proof of the desired upper bound.

[Proposition of arXiv:2411.09621, 'Crossing bridges between percolation models and Bienaym\'e-Galton-Watson trees'] Consider the DaC model on an infinite tree $\mathbf{t}$ with parameters $p \in [0,1]$, $d=2$, and let $a_{\emptyset}$ be the probability of coloring a percolation cluster with the same color as the root. We have that
  \[
    \mathbb{P}_{p, d, a_{\emptyset}}^{\mathbf{t}}
    \left(  \widetilde{\mathbf{t}}_\emptyset \text{ has infinite size} \right) > 0
  \] 
  if and only if
  \[  \mathbf{P}_{\widetilde{p}}^{\mathbf{t}}
    \left( \mathcal{C}_{\emptyset} \text{ has infinite size} \right) >0,
  \]
  where $ \widetilde{p} = 1 - (1-p)(1 - a_{\emptyset})$, and $\mathcal{C}_{\emptyset}$ is the root cluster obtained by applying Bernoulli percolation with parameter $\widetilde{p}$ on $\mathbf{t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2411.09621, 'Crossing bridges between percolation models and Bienaym\'e-G'

body: [Thm 16 of arXiv:2506.09264, 'The bunkbed conjecture still holds for cactus graphs\\ and for graphs with certain biconne'] There is a smallest, finite set \(\mathcal{H} \neq \emptyset\) of graphs such that any given graph satisfies the strong bunkbed conjecture if and only if it contains no element of \(\mathcal{H}\) as a minor. In particular, with respect to the minor relation, \(\mathcal{H}\) consists exactly of the smallest counterexamples to the strong bunkbed conjecture \emph{(}up to graph isomorphism\emph{)} and every \(H \in \mathcal{H}\) is biconnected and contains a non-trivial subdivision of \(D\) as a minor.\vspace{6pt}

body:
[Proposition prop:multilevel_shifted_deriv of arXiv:2607.27810, 'Perturbed Beta Corners Process'] Let $N\ge2$, let $\mathsf{a}_1=\cdots=\mathsf{a}_{N-1}$ with
	$\mathsf{a}_N$ arbitrary, and set
	$\mathsf{c} \coloneqq \mathsf{a}_{N-1}-\mathsf{a}_N$.
	Let $P_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^{N}(x-z_j)$ be the top-row polynomial, and let
	$P_{N-1}$ be the monic polynomial of degree $N-1$ whose roots are the
	$N-1$ interlacing roots of $D_{\mathsf{c}} P_N$.
	Then, for each $k=1,\ldots,N-1$, the level-$k$ positions
	$\bar{\mathsf{y}}_1^k>\cdots>\bar{\mathsf{y}}_k^k$ of the deformed
	lattice are the roots of
	$\left(\frac{d}{dx}\right)^{N-1-k}P_{N-1}$.
	Equivalently, the levels $N-1,\ldots,1$ of the deformed lattice form the
	$\infty$-corners lattice of (def:deterministic_lattice of the paper) whose top
	row consists of the roots of $P_{N-1}$.
	For $\mathsf{c}=0$ we have $P_{N-1}=P_N'/N$, and the deformed lattice is
	the unperturbed one.

body: In algebra and number theory, Wilson's theorem states that a natural number n > 1 is a prime number if and only if the product of all the positive integers less than n is one less than a multiple of n. That is (using the notations of modular arithmetic), the factorial $(n-1)!=1\times 2\times 3\times \cdots \times (n-1)$ satisfies $$(n-1)!\ \equiv \;-1{\pmod {n}}$$

[Lemma lem:oneside of arXiv:2609.01745, 'The Directional Localization Game on Graphs'] Let $G$ be a graph, and let $(T, \mathcal{B})$ be a 
tree decomposition.  Let $a$ and $b$ be adjacent nodes in $T$ and let $S = B_a \cap B_b$. body:
Let (Omega,F,P) be a probability space, S:Omega->Omega a measurable measure-preserving transformation, and g:Omega->R a finite measurable function, not assumed integrable. If g-g composed with S is bounded below by an integrable real function, then g-g composed with S is integrable and its integral is zero. Equivalently it is enough that the negative part of this difference be integrable. Neither invertibility nor ergodicity of S is required. Source: Invariant Measures, Hausdorff Dimension and Dimension Drop of some Harmonic Measures on Galton-Watson Trees, Lemma 2.3, p.9, citing Lyons-Pemantle-Peres Lemma 6.2.

body:
[Theorem thm:limit of arXiv:2606.30475, 'Ancestries in random $d$-DAGs'] As $n\to\infty$, the number of ancestors of $i$ in $G_n$ satisfies the following:
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
  \item For $i=o\big(n^{(d-1)/d}\big)$, we have $n^{-1} a_i(n)\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\longrightarrow} 1$.
  \item For $i\sim \alpha n^{(d-1)/d}$ with $\alpha>0$, we have $n^{-1} a_i(n) \stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} \Xi_\alpha$, where $\Xi_\alpha$ is a random variable on $[0,1]$ with cumulative distribution function
  \begin{equation}
   \mathbb{P}(\Xi_\alpha\leq \gamma) = 1 - e^{-\frac{\alpha^d}{d-1}\big((1-\gamma)^{1-d}-1\big)}.
  \end{equation}
  Moreover, the convergence also holds for all moments.
  \item For $i=\omega\big(n^{(d-1)/d}\big)$ and $i=o(n)$, we have $(i/n)^d a_i(n)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} \mathsf{Exp}(1)$, where the convergence also holds for all moments.
  \item For $i\sim \beta n$ with $0<\beta \leq 1$, we have $a_i(n)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} \mathsf{Geo}(\beta^d)$, again with convergence of all moments.
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:limit of arXiv:2606.30475

[Lemma 53 (Scaled local hypoelliptic density lower bound) of arXiv:2607.20882, 'An Eyring--Kramers Law for the Hypoelliptic Third-Order\\ Langevin Diffusion'] There are $r_0,t_0>0$ such that for every $C_0<\infty$ there are
$c(C_0),c_0(C_0),\eps_0(C_0)>0$ such that, for $i\in\{m,s\}$,
$\eps<\eps_0(C_0)$, every $z\in B(x_i,C_0\sqrt\eps)$, and every Borel
$E\subset B(x_i,C_0\sqrt\eps)$,
\begin{equation}

\Pbb_z\left(Z_{t_0}^\eps\in E,\ t_0<\tau_{\partial B(x_i,r_0)}\right)
\ge c(C_0)\eps^{-3d/2}\operatorname{Leb}(E)-e^{-c_0/\eps}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for $\varrho\in(1/2,1]$,
\[
\inf_{z\in B(x_i,\eps^\varrho)}
\Pbb_z\left(
Z_{t_0}^\eps\in\mathsf A_\eps^i,
\ t_0<\tau_{\partial B(x_i,r_0)}
\right)
\ge c\eps^{3d/2}.
\]

[Thm Yaglom of arXiv:2608.13084, '\bf Branching random walk in random environment'] Under the Assumption (A1 of the paper), for any $x\in{\mathbb Z}^d$ and for ${\bf P}_p$-a.s. $\omega$,

 \frac{Z_n}{\{p\sigma_\circ^2+(1-p)\sigma_\bullet^2\}n/2}\le t
 \ \middle|\ Z_n>0\right)
 =F_{\mathrm{Exp}(1)}(t),\quad \forall t\in{\mathbb R},
\]
where
\[
 F_{\mathrm{Exp}(1)}(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&t<0,\\
 1-e^{-t},&t\ge0.
 \end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
R\in C(\Delta_T^2;B_\alpha)\  \text{\,and\,} \ \hat\delta R = h.
\]
Moreover, if $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and for every $0<\varepsilon<\gamma$, $$ \sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{\gamma-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon;\tau}<\infty,$$ then
$R\in E^{\gamma}(\Delta_T^2; B_\alpha)$ and for every $0<\varepsilon<\gamma$,
\begin{equation}

\|R\|_{\gamma-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon}
\le
\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}
\|r^\tau\|_{\gamma-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon;\tau}.
\end{equation}
Similarly, if 
$$\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{1,\log;\tau,\alpha}+\sup_{\tau\in[0,T]}\|r^\tau\|_{1-\varepsilon,\alpha+\varepsilon;\tau}<\infty$$
for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, then $R\in E_{\log}^{1}(\Delta_T^2; B_\alpha)$ and

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $d\in \N$ and $\alpha>0$. Let $\Omega:\R_+\to \R_+$ be a measurable function such that 
    \[
    0 < \int_{0}^{\infty}\Omega\left(t^\alpha\right)t^{d-1}\,dt < +\infty.
    \]
    Then, for every star body $L\subset \R^d$, it holds that
    \begin{equation}
    
    \vol[d](L) = \frac{1}{d} \frac{\int_{\R^d}\Omega\left(\|x\|_{L}^\alpha\right)\,dx}{\int_0^\infty \Omega\left(t^\alpha\right)t^{d-1}\,dt}.
    \end{equation}
title: Proposition 12 of arXiv:2609.01460

[Definition 9 (Asymptotically conformal contractions) of arXiv:2609.00571, '\textbf{Shape Optimization and Bernoulli Free Boundary Problems\\ for the Riemannian $p$-L'] Let $(\Psi_j)$ be a sequence of Riemannian contractions and let
$x_j$ be the associated contact points. We say that $(\Psi_j)$ is
\emph{asymptotically conformal at the contact points} if there exist
numbers $\mu_j\in(0,1)$, isometries
\[
P_j:T_{y_j}M\longrightarrow T_{x_j}M,
\]
and numbers $\varepsilon_j\downarrow0$ such that
\begin{equation}
\mu_j\longrightarrow1,
\qquad
\|d\Psi_j(y_j)-\mu_jP_j\|_g
\leq\varepsilon_j,

\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\|\nu_g(x_j)-P_j\nu_g(y_j)\|_g
\leq\varepsilon_j.

\end{equation}
title: Asymptotically conformal contractions

[Definition Driver--Sengupta measure of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $(\rho_t)_{t>0}$ be as above and let $\mathbb{G}$ be a finite graph on $\mathcal{S}$. 
The \emph{Driver--Sengupta measure} associated with $(\rho_t)_{t>0}$ and $\mathbb{G}$ is the probability measure on $G^{\mathbb{E}_+}$, denoted by $\mathrm{DS}(\rho,\mathbb{G})$, whose density with respect to the product Haar measure $\mathrm{d} g$ on $G^{\mathbb{E}_+}$ is given by
\[
\mathrm{d} \mathrm{DS}(\rho,\mathbb{G})\big((g_e)_{e \in \mathbb{E}_+}\big) 
 = \frac{1}{Z_{\rho,\mathbb{G}}}
   \prod_{F \in \mathbb{F}} \rho_{\sigma(F)}\big(\mathrm{Hol}(g,\partial F)\big)\, \mathrm{d} g.
\]
Here $\partial F$ is the oriented boundary of $F$, the time parameter $\sigma(F)>0$ is the area of $F$, and $Z_{\rho,\mathbb{G}}$ is the normalizing constant.
title: Driver--Sengupta measure

[Proposition prop:pq-small-rho of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] For fixed $q\ge2$,
\[
p_q(\rho)=\frac1q+c_q\rho+O_q(\rho^2),
\qquad
c_q=q^2(q-1)\left[
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\phi(x)^2\overline\Phi(x)^{q-2}\,dx
\right]^2.
\]
In particular, $c_2=1/\pi$, recovering the small-correlation expansion of
Sheppard's formula. Hence
\[
\Pr(\mathcal N_1=\widetilde{\mathcal N}_1)
=\frac1q+c_q\sqrt{\frac md}
+O_q\!\left(\frac md+\frac1{\sqrt m}+\frac1{\sqrt{d-m}}\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let d>=1, L>=m>0 and R>0. Let U:R^d->R be C1, have an everywhere-existing Hessian and globally L-Lipschitz gradient, with grad U(0)=0. Put Omega=R^d minus B(0,R). Assume V(x)=U(x)-(m/2)||x||_2^2 is convex on Omega in this precise sense: V(sum_j a_j x_j)<=sum_j a_j V(x_j) whenever a_j>=0, sum_j a_j=1, all x_j belong to Omega and their barycenter also belongs to Omega. Put mu(dx) proportional to exp(-U(x))dx and kappa=L/m. For epsilon in (0,1), initialize X_0~N(0,I_d/L). Run the unadjusted Langevin algorithm X_{k+1}=X_k-h grad U(X_k)+sqrt(2h)G_k with independent G_k~N(0,I_d), choosing h=c exp(-16 L R^2) kappa^{-1} L^{-1} epsilon^2/d for a sufficiently small positive absolute constant c. Then the number of iterations needed for total-variation distance to mu at most epsilon is at most ceil(C exp(32 L R^2) kappa^2 (d/epsilon^2) log(d/epsilon^2)) for an absolute C. The bound is polynomial in d only when its displayed parameter dependence is also polynomial.

[Thm t:thm_q of arXiv:2504.07255, 'A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme\\ for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Dri'] Let assumptions
$\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{Lip}_+}_A$,
$\mathbf{H}_{A_x,A_{xx}}$,
$\mathbf{H}_{a,b,c}^{\mathrm{Lip}_b}$, and
$\mathbf{H}_{\nu,p}$
 hold. Then, 
 for any $T\in[0,\infty)$ and $q\in (0,p)$ there is convergence
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\sup_{t\in[0, T]} \mathbf{E} \|X_t^n-X_t\|^q \leq_C h_n^{\bar \delta}(1+\|x\|^p),
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
with the convergence rate
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{p-q}{\chi}\wedge\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
In particular, if $\chi=0$, i.e., if the drift $A$ has bounded first derivatives, the convergence rate reduces to
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 11 of arXiv:2606.12820, 'Averaging principles for nonautonomous multiscale McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems'] For a matrix-valued map $h(\cdot,\cdot):\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n)\rightarrow\mR^{n \times d_1}$, we say $h\in C^{k,(2,2)}(\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n),\mR^{n \times d_1})$, if $h(x,\cdot)\in C^{(2,2)}(\cP_2(\mR^n),\mR^{n \times d_1})$ for any $x\in\mR^n$, $h(\cdot,\mu)\in C^k(\mR^n,\mR^{n \times d_1})$ for any $\mu\in\cP_2(\mR^n)$, and the derivatives
$$\p_x^ih(x,\mu),\quad \p_x^i\p_\mu h(x,\mu)(\tx),\quad\p_x^i\p_{\tx}\p_\mu h(x,\mu)(\tx),\quad 1\leq i\leq k,$$
$$\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx),\quad \p_{\tx}\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx),\quad \p_{\cx}\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx),\quad \p_{\cx}\p_{\tx}\p_\mu^2 h(x,\mu)(\tx,\cx)$$
are continuous at any $(x,\mu,\tx,\cx)$. We say $h\in C_b^{k,(2,2)}(\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n),\mR^{n \times d_1})$, if $h\in C^{k,(2,2)}(\mR^n\times\cP_2(\mR^n),\mR^{n \times d_1})$, and all the above derivatives are uniformly bounded w.r.t. $(x,\mu,\tx,\cx)$.

Tang, Chen and Liu, Beyond Quadratic Loss: The Stability Phase Diagram of Adam, arXiv2609.18314v1, Theorem3, treats L(x)=k|x|^n with k>0,n>2,1/2<beta1<1,0<beta2<1,v0>0,epsilon=0 and the imposed recurrence v_next=beta2*v. Conditional on attraction to either nonzero fixed point of the rescaled dynamics, the source concludes eventual absence of EoS-triggered spikes when beta1*beta2^(-n/(2*(n-2)))<1. Rescaling x_t=q^t*y_t with q=beta2^(1/(2*(n-2))) gives a second-order recurrence whose previous-position coefficient is beta1*beta2^(-n/(2*(n-2))). The imposed variance recurrence omits the ordinary squared-gradient addition. This theorem therefore does not cover n=2, positive epsilon, standard v0=0, or generic convergence to a quadratic unstable origin. Section3 Figure3(a) instead reports a numerical quadratic beta-boundary from finite trajectories, not a theorem about standard-initialization basin measure.

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2506.17109, 'Limit theorems under nonlinear expectations dominated by sublinear expectations'] Let a convex expectation $\mathbb{\tilde{E}}[\cdot]$ be
dominated by a sublinear expectation $\mathbb{\hat{E}}[\cdot]$ on
$(\Omega,\mathcal{H})$, and let $(X_{1},Y_{1})$ be a $2d$-dimensional random
vector satisfying
\begin{equation}
\lim_{N\rightarrow \infty}\mathbb{\hat{E}}\left[  (|X_{1}|^{2}-N)^{+}
+(|Y_{1}|-N)^{+}\right]  =0. 
\end{equation}
Then $\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}n\mathbb{\tilde{E}}\left[  \frac{1}{n}(\frac
{1}{2}\langle AX_{1},X_{1}\rangle+\langle p,Y_{1}\rangle)\right]  $ exists for
each $(A,p)\in \mathbb{S}_{d}\times \mathbb{R}^{d}$.
title: Proposition 13 of arXiv:2506.17109

body:
[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2608.31168, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality for surfaces in every codimension'] Consider a vector-valued Radon measure $\mathbf{A} \in \cM(\bR^2 ; \bR^{2 \times 2})$ with measure-valued row-wise divergence and concentrated on a Borel set $E \subset \bR^2$ of finite Lebesgue measure.
    Then,
    \[
    \Lambda_{2,\beta} ( \mathbf{A}) \leq C |E|^{\frac{1}{2}} ( |\mathbf{A}| + |\textup{Div} \, \mathbf{A}| )  + C \, |\textup{Div} \, \mathbf{A}| + \cN_2 ( \mathbf{A}) + 2 \, \cK_2( \mathbf{A})
    \]
    with the constant $\beta = \frac{4-\pi}{8}$.
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2608.31168

[Defn 9 (Likelihood ratio for i.i.d. prior) of arXiv:2605.07050, 'Universality of the fluctuations of the free energy in generalized Sherrington--Kirkpatric'] For an $N \times N$ Wigner matrix $W = (W_{ij})$ and a prior $\caX$, we define the likelihood ratio $\ol \caL (\SNR)$ by
\beq 
	\ol \caL (\SNR) = \E_\caX \left[ \prod_{i<j} \frac{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_i x_j)}{p(\sqrt{N} W_{ij})} \prod_k \frac{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk} - \sqrt{\SNR N} x_k^2)}{p_d(\sqrt{N} W_{kk})} \right].
\eeq
title: Likelihood ratio for i.i.d. prior

[Definition 1 (Non Uniform Exapnsions) of arXiv:2511.06414, 'Non-uniform Edgeworth expansions for weakly dependent random variables and their applicati'] We say that $W_n$ obeys the (non-stationary) Edgeworth expansion of order $r$ with power $s\geq 0$ if for every $x\in\bbR$,
$$
\cD_{r,n}(x):=\left|\bbP(W_n\leq x)-\Phi(x)-\varphi(x)\sum_{j=1}^{r}B_n^{-j}H_{j,n}(x)\right|\leq C_n(1+|x|)^{-s}B_n^{-r}
$$
where $C_n\to 0$
and  $H_{j,n}$ are polynomials with uniformly bounded coefficients and degrees not depending on $n$.

body:
[Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.02819, 'Adelic Points and Unramified Brauer Approximation for Classifying Stacks'] Let $\scX$ be an Artin stack of finite presentation over $\cO_{k,S}$.  We say
that $\scX$ is \emph{adelically liftable} if the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item The diagonal
\[ 
 \Delta_{\scX/\cO_{k,S}}:\scX\longrightarrow
 \scX\times_{\cO_{k,S}}\scX
\]
is representable by separated algebraic spaces of finite presentation.
\item There is a smooth surjective presentation
\[
 p:U\longrightarrow \scX
\]
where $U$ is a separated algebraic space of finite presentation over
$\cO_{k,S}$.
\item For every finite place $v\notin S$, the functor
\[
 U(\cO_v)\longrightarrow \scX(\cO_v)
\]
is essentially surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Such a presentation $p$ will be called an \emph{adelic lifting presentation}.
We say that a finite type Artin stack over $k$ is adelically liftable if it
admits an adelically liftable integral model after enlarging $S$.
title: Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.02819

body:
[Theorem 29 (Invertible thimble factor and selected-cycle rank) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Under the isolated-leading-part, tameness, Morse, and frame hypotheses of the
preceding paragraph, the period matrix
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}(P,t)
 =
 \left(
  \int_{\Gamma_\alpha}
  e^{F_{P,t}}\omega_\beta
 \right)_{1\leq\alpha,\beta\leq\mu}
 
\end{equation}
is holomorphic and invertible on \(\mathfrak C\).  If
\(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_N\) are selected rapid-decay cycles, set
\(C_{\mathrm{Betti}}\) to be their coordinate matrix in the integral
frame, as in \cref{def:physical-betti-matrix}.  Then the matrix of their periods
against a Jacobi normal-form frame is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{
 \Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}\,
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}\,
 B_{\mathrm{Jac}}.}
 
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{rank}\Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =
 \operatorname{rank}C_{\mathrm{Betti}}.
 
\end{equation}

Across a Stokes ray, if
\(\Gamma^+=S\Gamma^-\), then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^+
 =
 S\mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^-,
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^+
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^-S^{-1}.
\]
Hence \(\Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}\) and its rank are unchanged.  Confluence may
produce poles or ramification in the analytic period factors at the
boundary of \(\mathfrak C\), but never in the integral Betti matrix.
At a finite confluence the Morse basis itself ceases to exist; its two
lateral coordinate matrices remain integral and are related by
Picard--Lefschetz monodromy.

Owner campaign draft, proof (unaudited); standard finite-population identities, independent audit and novelty assessment pending. Let P0=P on R^d have finite second moment, n>=1, h>=0, and r=0. Each generation draws n conditionally iid samples from Pt and forms their equal-weight Gaussian KDE with covariance h^2 I_d; bandwidth is constant within a trajectory. Let a=1-1/n, v0=tr Cov(P), mt=mean(Pt), and vt=E tr Cov(Pt), using the KDE's divisor-n covariance. For t>=1, vt=a^t v0+n d h^2(1-a^t), and E|mt-m0|^2=v0(1-a^t)+d h^2[t-n(1-a^t)]. Thus expected second moment about m0 is v0+t d h^2, although fixed-h within-generation variance approaches n d h^2. At h=0 the mean martingale converges in L2 to random M_infinity and E W2^2(Pt,delta_M_infinity)=2a^t v0. For n tending to infinity and t_n/n tending to infinity, centered expected variance tends to zero if and only if n h_n^2 tends to zero; h_n tending to zero alone is insufficient. If n h_n^2 tends to finite lambda, vt_n tends to d lambda. Covariance calculations do not determine the complete positive-bandwidth limit distribution or keep the random mean near m0 for all times. Proof: C003 v2, T356/proofs/review/c003_v2.md.

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.05679, 'Small ball probabilities and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for Gaussian Volterra p'] \cite[Lemma 1.1, p. 138]{JM1978}
		Let $\{Z(t):\ t\ge0\}$ be a separable, centered, real-valued Gaussian process. Assume that 
		\[
		\mathbb E\left[\left(Z(t+h)-Z(t)\right)^2\right]\le \varphi(h)^2, \ \ \ t>0, \  h>0,
		\]
		for some continuous nondecreasing function $\varphi$ with $\varphi(0)=0$. 
         Then, for every integer $K_3>1$, all $t,x>0$, and every sequence of positive numbers ${\theta(p)}_{p\in\mathbb N}$, we have
\begin{align*}
& \mathbb{P}\left\{ \sup_{0\le s\le t}|Z(s)-Z(0)|>x\varphi(t)+\sum_{p=1}^{\infty} \theta(p)\varphi\left(tK_3^{-2^p} \right)  \right\} \\
&\le K_3^2 e^{-x^2/2}+\sum_{p=1}^{\infty} K_3^{2^{p+1}}e^{-\theta(p)^2/2}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.05679

[Defn $\delta$-thin of arXiv:2412.05746, 'Hyperbolicity, slimness, and minsize, on average'] \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item Given a geodesic metric space $(X,d)$ and $\delta \geq 0$, a geodesic triangle $\Delta(x,y,z)$ for $x,y,z \in X$ is $\delta$-thin if $d(x,v) = d(x,w) \leq \langle y,z \rangle_x$, then $d(v,w) \leq \delta$ holds for any points $v \in [x,y]$ and $w \in [x,z]$, and similar conditions hold for $y$ and $z$. We say $(X,d)$ is \emph{$\delta$-thin} if every geodesic triangle in $X$ is $\delta$-thin.
        \item Given a (connected) graph $G = (V,E)$ and $\delta \geq 0$,  a geodesic triangle $\Delta(x,y,z)$ for $x,y,z \in X$ is $\delta$-thin if $d(x,v) = d(x,w) \leq \langle y,z \rangle_x$, then $d(v,w) \leq \delta$ holds for any \textcolor{red}{vertices} $v \in [x,y]$ and $w \in [x,z]$, and similar conditions hold for $y$ and $z$. We say $G$ is \emph{$\delta$-thin} if every geodesic triangle in $X$ is $\delta$-thin.
    \end{enumerate}
title: $\delta$-thin

[Theorem 3 (Stationary-entry hitting) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $x_n$ be a sequence of initial states.  Assume
\[
        \pi_n(A_n)\to0,
        \qquad
        \mu_n\to0.
\]
Suppose there are integers $b_n,h_n,r_n\to\infty$ such that
\[
        h_n=o(b_n),\qquad b_n\mu_n\to0,
        \qquad \alpha_n(h_n)=o(b_n\mu_n),
\]
and such that the following two assumptions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(M\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item \textbf{Stationary one-block law.}  With
\[
        N_n^{(b)}:=\sum_{t=1}^{b_n}E_t,
\]
one has
\[
        \Pbb_{\pi_n}(N_n^{(b)}\ge1)=b_n\mu_n(1+o(1)).
\]
\item \textbf{Negligible initial burn-in.}  For this sequence $x_n$,
\[
        \Pbb_{x_n}(T_{A_n}\le r_n)=o(1),
        \qquad
        \|P_n^{r_n}(x_n,\cdot)-\pi_n\|_{\TV}=o(1),
        \qquad
        r_n\mu_n=o(1).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
        \mu_n T_{A_n}\Rightarrow \Exp(1)
\]
under $\Pbb_{x_n}$.

[Corollary Weak Simplex Conjecture of arXiv:2607.14087, 'Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution of the Weak Simplex Conjecture'] \label[corollary]{cor:wsc}
Let $m=d+1$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ be unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let the
message $I$ be uniform on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$.  Under the channel
\[
  Y=\lambda x_I+Z,
  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),\quad \lambda>0,
\]
the average probability of correct maximum-likelihood decoding is no larger
than for a regular simplex.  For every fixed $\lambda>0$, equality holds if
and only if the $x_i$ form a regular simplex.  Thus the regular simplex is the
unique maximizer up to rotation and relabeling. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Weak Simplex Conjecture

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2605.02713, '2605.02713'] Let $\beta>1$ and $f_n=\sum_{q=m}^p c_q  H_q(\cdot;\mathrm{Var} (\cdot))$. 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)] If $\sigma_n^2 \gg  (1 - \alpha_n^2)$ then
		$$\left( \hat{S}_{n,t}(f_n) \right)_{t\in[0,1]} \longrightarrow_{\mathcal{D}}  \bigg( t \, \frac{H_{p}(Z)}{\sqrt{p!}}  \bigg)_{t\in[0,1]} \hspace{1mm} \text{in} \; D[0,1]  \text{ as }n\rightarrow\infty;$$
		\item[(ii)] If $\sigma_n^2 \ll  (1 - \alpha_n^2)$ then

[Lemma lem:nonback of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j_0$ be a
sufficiently large integer.  
Let  
$\Psi_0$ be the initialising state with
$j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$ and $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$.  
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be  
the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$.   For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following statement holds  for
every $t >  \tau_0$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$ and 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} \in \{ \textup{refilling},\textup{stabilising}\}$, where
$j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.  
If
$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}
$ 
then 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item for all $t'$ in the range $t-1 \leq t' \leq \mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1)$, $j^{\Psi(t')} = j$,
\item for all $\hat{t}$ in  the range $t-1 \le \hat{t} < \mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1)$ with  $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\hat{t})} = \textup{stabilising}$,  
$\mathrm{trans}(\hat{t}) \leq \hat{t} + j^{\phi+72}$, 
\item 
If $\mathcal{M}_{[j-1]}^{\psi_{t-1}}(\tau^{\psi_{t-1}}) \leq 
2j^{44} 
$ then
for all 
$\hat{t}$ in the range $t-1 \le \hat{t} < \mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1)$
with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\hat{t})} = \textup{refilling}$,   
$\mathrm{trans}(\hat{t})  \leq \hat{t} + j^{\phi+{46}}$, and
\item 
If $\mathcal{M}_{[j-1]}^{\psi_{t-1}}(\tau^{\psi_{t-1}}) \leq 
2j^{44} 
$ then
$\mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1) \leq t-1 + j^{\phi+73}$. 
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem theorem4.50 of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Given two linear spaces $L,Y$ with $\dim L=\dim Y=r$, let $\Sigma\subset\operatorname{Hom}(L,Y)$ be an atomic full NC-Rank matrix space, which means that it satisfies
$$
\dim \Sigma(S)\geq\dim S,\quad\forall S\subset L.
$$and that more strongly, 
$$
0\neq S\subsetneq L\mapsto \dim\Sigma(S)\geq\dim (S)+1
.$$We consider its orthonormal complement space
$$
D:=\Sigma^\perp\subset\operatorname{Hom}(L,Y) 
$$where orthogonality is with respect to the Hilbert-Schmidt pairing. For a subspace $E\subset D$, we define 
$$
F:=\operatorname{span}_{T\in\Sigma}T^*E\subset\operatorname{End}(L).
$$Then there does not exist any nonzero subspace $E\subset D$ such that 
\begin{equation}
    \dim F=\dim E
\end{equation} and satisfies that the induced dual space 
$$ \mathcal{R}_E:=\operatorname{span}\{A\mapsto T^*A:T\in\Sigma
\}
\subset\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)
$$
is itself atomic, where the last statement means that 
\begin{equation}
    0\neq E_0\subsetneq E:\dim\operatorname{span}_{T\in\Sigma}T^*E_0\geq\dim E_0+1.
\end{equation}
Thus the square dual atoms do not occur. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Version 1, Target 1, kind bound; proofs (unaudited), 20 October 2026.

## C033: discrete-time semigroup subtraction

Let a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2), and A,B be the differential operators in C032.
One step of duration 1/n has P_n=I+A/n+B/n^2+O(n^(-5/2)) on positive
compacts. A diffusion step has exp(A/n)=I+A/n+A^2/(2n^2)+O(n^-3), for
sufficiently smooth local tests. Thus the local weak-error operator is

    C=B-A^2/2
     =(8u+a/5+b/u)D+(4u^2-3au/5)D^2.               (3)

This is an algebraic identity, not a global semigroup expansion at zero.
Direct differentiation gives

    A^2=(4u+2a)D+(14u^2+6au+a^2)D^2
                  +(8u^3+2au^2)D^3+u^4 D^4.

Subtracting half of this from C032's B proves (3); the third- and fourth-
derivative terms cancel exactly. Their inclusion before subtraction was
necessary. A global modified diffusion with this C is not asserted:
the drift b/u is singular and its second-order coefficient can be negative
near zero at finite n.

## C034: a rigorous logarithmic divergence of the limiting Duhamel functional

Use the reviewer-PASS C017 diffusion dU=(2U+a)ds+sqrt(2)U dW, U0=0,
and its semigroup P_s. Fix t>0 and f(u)=1-exp(-u). Define, for 0<epsilon<t,

    I_epsilon(t)=integral_epsilon^t E[(C P_(t-s)f)(U_s)] ds,
    D_t=(D P_t f)(0)=E[J_t exp(-U_t)],
    J_t=exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t).

Then 0<D_t<infinity, and there is a finite H_t such that

    I_epsilon(t)=(D_t/(2pi))log(1/epsilon)+H_t+O_t(sqrt(epsilon)). (4)

This statement concerns the specified cutoff integral for the limiting SDE.
It does not replace epsilon by 1/n inside a network weak-error theorem.

Proof of regularity. The solution from initial value u is U_v^u=U_v^0+uJ_v.
Consequently D^j P_v f(u)=E[J_v^j f^(j)(U_v^0+uJ_v)] for j>=1.
All these derivatives are bounded uniformly for 0<=v<=t, because Gaussian
exponentials J_v have every positive moment. Differentiation under expectation
is justified by these dominating moments. The time derivative of D P_v f
is bounded too: Af and (Af)' are bounded (polynomials times exp(-u)), and
the semigroup identity P_v f-f=integral_0^v P_r Af dr allows differentiation
in u. In particular, with h(s,u)=D P_(t-s) f(u),

    |h(s,u)-D_t|<=C_t(s+u), 0<=s<=t, u>=0.          (5)

The same bounded-derivative estimates apply to D^2 P_(t-s)f.

Proof of the entrance estimate. The explicit solution gives

    U_s=a integral_0^s exp((s-r)+sqrt(2)(W_s-W_r)) dr.

Let M_s=sup_(r<=s)|W_r| and H_s=s+2sqrt(2)M_s. Then
exp(-H_s)<=U_s/(as)<=exp(H_s). Brownian scaling and the Gaussian tail of
M_1 show, for each fixed t,

    E(1/U_s)<=C_t/s,
    E|1/U_s-1/(as)|<=C_t/sqrt(s), 0<s<=t.           (6)

For the second inequality use |1/(U_s/(as))-1|<=exp(H_s)-1 and
E(exp(H_s)-1)<=C_t sqrt(s). The moments of U_s of each fixed order are
O_t(s^j), by the same pathwise bound.

Equations (5)-(6) imply

    E[h(s,U_s)/U_s]=D_t/(as)+O_t(s^(-1/2))+O_t(1).

The nonsingular terms in C have bounded expectation near s=0, by the
derivative and U_s moment bounds. Therefore

    E[(C P_(t-s)f)(U_s)]= (b/a)D_t/s+O_t(s^(-1/2)). (7)

The difference between the integrand and (b/a)D_t/s is integrable at zero.
Integrating it proves (4), including its remainder. Finally b/a=1/(2pi).

## Consequence and the unpaid step

The natural candidate network leading correction for this bounded test is
(D_t/(2pi))log(n)/n, with a theta0-dependent constant/n at the next order.
This is a prediction, not proved network asymptotics. A proof still needs
uniform control while u approaches zero, a matching scale and remainder,
and the accumulated exact-to-regularized bounded-test comparison through
the entrance. A lower-cutoff contribution might alter or cancel a formal
coefficient unless controlled. C029's deterministic logarithmic offset is

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2607.27721, 'Asymptotic bias of the plug-in Shannon entropy estimator \\ under a regularly varying occu'] Let Assumption~\ref{ass:1} hold.
Then,
\[
|\biasPois(t)|
\sim t^{\alpha-1}L(t)C_\alpha
\]
as $t\to\infty$,
where
\begin{align*}
C_\alpha &\coloneqq \int_0^\infty y^{-\alpha}\psi(y)\,\dy,\\
\psi(y) &\coloneqq -\log y-1+\E\!\left[(P_y+1-y)\log(P_y+1)\right] \quad (y>0),
\end{align*}
with $P_y$ being a Poisson random variable with mean $y \,(>0)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2607.27721

body: [OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2609.03444 (question environment).] For a near-tight $n$-tuple let $q$ be the denominator of $\ML$. Theorem (thm:UC) gives $\max_iv_i<3q$ on $\UC$, and the ratio is below $1$ on $\UA$ and $\UB$; among all near-tight sextuples with speeds at most $110$ the largest ratio is $105/43$, and the largest ratio among the sporadic ones is $22/13$. Does $\max_iv_i<3q$ hold for every near-tight sextuple? More generally, Kravitz has pointed out that a bound $\max_iv_i\le C(n)\,q$ for all but finitely many near-tight $n$-tuples follows from [JainKravitz] whenever the Lonely Runner Conjecture holds for $n-1$ and $n-2$ speeds, the constant being a maximum over the finitely many critical subtori; the homogeneity argument in the proof of Theorem (thm:UC) is how such a constant is computed. Its value for other $n$, and whether the sporadic tuples respect it, are open. (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)

[Lem convex_fix_n of arXiv:2509.08659, 'Gap metrics for stationary point processes and quantitative convexity of the free energy'] Let $\varphi$ satisfy assumption (assumption0 of the paper) and assume that equation (equation eq:formula_hamiltonian of the paper) holds for any $n\in \IN$ and  $\mathsf{P}\in \mathcal P_{s,1}(\Gamma)$ with $\int \xi(\Lambda_1)^2\mathsf{P}(d\xi)<\infty$. Let $\mathsf{P}_i\in \mathcal P_{s,1}(\Gamma)$, $i=0,1$ with $\int \xi(\Lambda_1)^2\mathsf{P}_i(d\xi)<\infty$ and  $ \mathsf{Q}\in  \mathsf{Cpl}_{s,m}(\mathsf{P}_0,\mathsf{P}_1)$. 
    Set $\mathsf U:=\iota( \mathsf{Q})$ and  $\mathsf{P}_t:= \mathsf{gap}^{-1}\left((T_t)_{\#}\mathsf U\right)$.
    Then for $0\leq t\leq 1$ \begin{align}
        n^{-1}\int H_n(\xi) \mathsf{P}_{t}(d\xi)&\leq
        (1-t)n^{-1}\int H_n(\xi)\mathsf{P}_{0}(d\xi)+tn^{-1}\int H_n(\xi)\mathsf{P}_{1}(d\xi)\\
        &-\frac{(1-t)t}{2}\int \sum_{(0,0)\neq (x,y)\in \bar\xi\cap \Lambda_n^2} (x-y)^2\inf_{z\in [x,y]}f(\left\lvertz\right\rvert) \mathsf{Q}^0(d\bar\xi)\nonumber
    \end{align}

body:
[Lemma lm:Z_increment of arXiv:2605.09377, 'A factorization formula for the partition function in the semi-discrete parabolic Anderson'] Let $\beta$ be so small that Key Lemma~(lm:standard_arg of the paper) holds. Let $T > t > 0$. For $\mathbf{P}_{0,0}$-almost every realization of $\eta$ and for every sequence $\mathbf{t} = (t_1, t_2, \ldots)$ of positive numbers such that $t_i = s_i - s_{i-1}$, $1 \leq i \leq n_{T}$ and $t_{n_T + 1} \geq T - s_{n_T}$, one has 
$$   
\biggl \langle \biggl(e^{-\frac{\beta^2}{2} T} e^{\beta \mathcal{A}_0^T} - e^{-\frac{\beta^2}{2} t} e^{\beta \mathcal{A}_0^t} \biggr)^2 \biggr \rangle \\
\leq 3 \left(M \left(\mathbf{t} \right) - M_{n_{t}-1} \left(\mathbf{t} \right) \right) + 3 \left \langle \left(R^t \right)^2 \right \rangle,
$$
where $R^t$ is a random variable depending on $\eta$ and $(W^x)_{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d}$ that satisfies
\begin{equation}     
\lim_{t \to \infty} t^{\theta} \ \mathbf{E}_{0,0} \left \langle \left(R^t \right)^2 \right \rangle = 0, \quad \forall \theta \in \left(0, \tfrac{d}{2}\right). 
\end{equation}
title: Lemma lm:Z_increment of arXiv:2605.09377

body:
For the frog model on the rooted d-ary tree, d>=2, start one active frog at the root and independent Poisson(mu) sleeping frogs at every non-root vertex, with independent simple random walk paths. There is a critical density mu_c(d) in (0,infinity) separating almost sure transience for mu<mu_c(d) from almost sure recurrence for mu>mu_c(d). Johnson and Junge prove that, for all sufficiently large d, 0.24d <= mu_c(d) <= 2.28d. The sufficiently-large-d qualifier is essential; these constants do not settle the deterministic one-frog cases d=3 or d=4, and no assertion is made at mu=mu_c(d).
Integer d>=2; quantitative constants require sufficiently large d
Independent Poisson(mu) counts at non-root vertices
Independent simple random walks; one active root frog

[Theorem 1 (Noiseless optimality of the full model) of arXiv:2609.02790, 'Full-Model Optimality for Tunable Linear Generative Priors in Compressed Sensing'] Fix an invertible matrix \(G_n\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) with singular value
decomposition
\[
    G_n=U\Sigma V^\top,
    \ \Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n),
    \
\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_n>0,
\]
where \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are orthogonal.
For each \(k\in[n]\), define the rank-\(k\) linear generative model
\[
    \mathcal G_k:=U_k\Sigma_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times k},
    \qquad
    \Sigma_k:=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k),
\]
where \(U_k\) consists of the first \(k\) columns of \(U\).
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have i.i.d.\
\(\mathcal N(0,1)\) entries, where \(2\le m\le n\).
Let \(z^\star\sim\mathcal N(0,I_n)\) be independent of \(A\), and define
\[
    x^\star:=G_nz^\star,
    \qquad
    y:=Ax^\star .
\]
For each \(k\in[n]\), let \(\widehat x(k)\) be the reconstruction signal obtained
from the model \(\mathcal G_k\) according to the reconstruction rule
\eqref{eq0}, and let \(E(k)\) denote the expected reconstruction error
defined in \eqref{eq:recon err}.\footnote{The quantity \(E(k)\) is
interpreted as an extended-real-valued expectation. In particular,
\(E(m-1)=E(m)=+\infty\); see
Proposition~\ref{prop:boundary-divergence}.}
Then
\[
    E(n)\le E(k)
    \qquad\text{for every }k\in[n].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Noiseless optimality of the full model

[Definition 38 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Let $\UC$ denote the space of upper semi-continuous functions $f \colon \R \rightarrow \R \cup \{ -\infty\}$ such that for some $x\in \R$, $f(x)\neq -\infty$ and such that there exists some constants $m,C>0$ so that for all $x\in \R$
$f(x) \leq m |x| + C$. For any $\mathfrak{h}_0 \in \UC$ and $\mathcal{L}$ an independent (of $\mathfrak{h}_0$) full-space directed landscape, we define the \textbf{full-space KPZ fixed point} with initial data $\mathfrak{h}_0$ as the random function $(y,t) \mapsto \hfix(\mathfrak{h}_0;y,t)$, where
\begin{equation}
\hfix(\mathfrak{h}_0;y,t) := \sup_{x\in \R} \big(\mathfrak{h}_0(x) + \mathcal{L}(x,0;y,t)\big).
\end{equation} For multiple initial data this provides a coupling of full-space KPZ fixed points.
title: Definition 38 of arXiv:2607.18104

[Proposition Certificates: recovery and existence of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] (i) If \(\mathcal{A}\) is a degree-\(q\),
radius-\(r\) certificate, then
\(H_{T}\left( \mathcal{A} \right) \subseteq R_{q}(T,r)\); if
\(\mathcal{A}\) is full, then
\(H_{T}\left( \mathcal{A} \right) \subseteq R(T,r)\).

such that for every \(0 < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_{0}\)
and every intrinsic \(\varepsilon\)-net
\(\{ x_{1},\ldots,x_{N}\}\) of \(M\) with
\(N = N_{\varepsilon}(M)\), the family

\[\mathcal{A}_{\varepsilon} = \{ B_{M}\left( x_{1},\varepsilon \right),\ldots,B_{M}\left( x_{N},\varepsilon \right)\}\]

is a full homological certificate at every radius \(r\)
with
\(C_{low}\,\varepsilon \leq r \leq C_{up}\, \operatorname{reach}(M)\). In
particular, full certificates of size \(N_{\varepsilon}(M)\)
exist.

[Theo 5 (Feldman--H\'ajek) of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] \cite[Theorem 2.25]{DaPratoZabczyk2014}\\
Let~\(\nu_1\) and~\(\nu_2\) be two centered Gaussian measures over a Hilbert space $H$ with covariance operators~\(Q_1\) and~\(Q_2\). Then $\nu_1$ and $\nu_2$ are either mutually singular or mutually absolutely continuous with respect to each other. The latter happens if and only if 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item measures~\(\nu_1\) and~\(\nu_2\) have the same Cameron--Martin space $Q_1^{\mez}(H)=Q_2^{\mez}(H)=:H_0$;
    
    \item $Q_1^{-\mez}Q_2^{\mez}(Q_1^{-\mez}Q_2^{\mez})^* - \mathbf{1} \in \mathfrak{S}_2(\bar H_0)$. 
\end{enumerate}
In the first item, $Q_i^{\mez}(H)$ is the range of the operator $Q_i^{\mez}$, and in the last item, $\bar H_0$ stands for the completion of $H_0$ under the $H$ norm, and the adjoint is understood with respect to $H$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Feldman--H\'ajek

body:
[Proposition prop:c2-reg of arXiv:2509.23086, 'On Optimal Markovian Couplings of L\'evy Processes'] Let $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\in\mathcal{G}_2^\Lambda(\mathbb R^d)$ be L\'evy generators with mean vectors $m_\mathcal{A},m_\mathcal{B}$ and covariance matrices $Q_\mathcal{A},Q_\mathcal{B}$.  
	Define
	\[
	U(t,x,y) := (x-y+t(m_\mathcal{A}-m_\mathcal{B}))^\top(m_\mathcal{A}-m_\mathcal{B}),
	\]
	and let $\{T_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ be a Markovian coupling semigroup of $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{J}\in\Gamma(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$ be a Feller coupling generator.
	
	(i) It holds for all $t,h\ge 0$ and $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{2d}$:
	\begin{align*}
		\frac{h}{2}\,U(t,x,y)
		&\le (T_{t+h}c_2)(x,y)-(T_tc_2)(x,y) \\
		&\le h^2\big(|m_\mathcal{A}|^2+|m_\mathcal{B}|^2\big)
		+ h\big[\mathrm{tr}(Q_\mathcal{A}+Q_\mathcal{B})+U(t,x,y)\big].

	In particular, the map $t\mapsto (e^{t\mathcal{J}}c_2)(x,y)$ is locally Lipschitz. 
	
	(ii) One has $c_2\in C(\mathcal{J})$.
		
	(iii) If $\mathcal{J}$ itself is a L\'evy generator, then $c_2\in\bar D(\mathcal{J})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn Inner product on affine standard module of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $x, y \in V_{n,m}$ be two radial $(n,m)$-link states and $a,b \in \mathbb{C}$. Define the inner product $\langle x \mid y \rangle_{n,m}$ as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Reflect $x$ across a vertical axis (mirror image).
    \item Glue $x$ to $y$ vertically, forming a closed link diagram called $\mathcal{G}(\alpha, \beta)$.
    \item If all defects pair, and $m$ closed loops are formed, then
    \[
    \langle x \mid y \rangle_{n,m} := a^{n_a}b^{n_b}.
    \]
    where $n_a$ and $n_b$ denote the numbers of contractible and non-contractible loops formed in the diagram $\mathcal{G}(\alpha, \beta)$, and $a, b$ are loop weights.
    \item Otherwise, if any defects remain unpaired, then $\langle x \mid y \rangle_{n,m} := 0$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Inner product on affine standard module

[Definition Schwartz space \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] The \emph{Schwartz space} \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) is the space of all infinitely differentiable functions 
\[
  \varphi: \mathbb{R}^d \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{C}
\]
such that for every pair of multi-indices \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}_0^d\), the seminorm
\[
  p_{\alpha,\beta}(\varphi)
  \;=\;
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}
  \bigl\lvert x^\alpha\,D^\beta \varphi(x)\bigr\rvert
\]
is finite. Here \(x^\alpha = x_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots x_d^{\alpha_d}\) and 
\[
  D^\beta = \frac{\partial^{\beta_1}}{\partial x_1^{\beta_1}} \cdots \frac{\partial^{\beta_d}}{\partial x_d^{\beta_d}}.
\]
Equivalently, 
\[
  \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)
  \;=\;
  \Bigl\{
    \varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\;:\;\forall\,\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}_0^d,\;
    \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d} \lvert x^\alpha D^\beta \varphi(x)\rvert < \infty
  \Bigr\}.
\]
title: Schwartz space \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\)

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), C004 version 2; priority not established. Let d,m>=1, R0>=1 and Sigma be a positive semidefinite d by d matrix with trace(Sigma)<=1. Let nu be any law on pairs (a,w) with |a|<=R0 and Euclidean ||w||<=R0. For two independent iid size-m samples from nu, define rho((a,w),(b,v))=|a-b|+||Sigma^(1/2)(w-v)||. The expected minimum mean rho cost over neuron permutations is at most r_m=inf over positive integers k,q of [4R0/q+2R0/sqrt(k+1)+2sqrt(2)R0 sqrt(q^(k+1)/m)]. In particular it is O(R0 sqrt(log(log(m)+e)/log(m))) as m tends to infinity, with an absolute constant uniform in d, Sigma and nu. Singular Sigma is allowed; no inverse is used. body: For certain applications in linear algebra, it is useful to know properties of the probability distribution of the largest eigenvalue of a finite sum of random matrices. Suppose $\{\mathbf {X} _{k}\}$ is a finite sequence of random matrices. Analogous to the well-known Chernoff bound for sums of scalars, a bound on the following is sought for a given parameter t: $$\Pr \left\{\lambda _{\max }\left(\sum _{k}\mathbf {X} _{k}\right)\geq t\right\}$$

[Thm 5 (\cite{kannanKL2021}) of arXiv:2609.03268, 'Poincare Polynomials of Heavy-Light Hassett Spaces'] Fix $m\ge2$ and $n\ge 4$ and consider the weight vector $w=w_{m,n}:=(1^m, \epsilon^{n-m})$. 
            Let 
            $$R=\Z[x_I: I\subsetneq \{2,\ldots, n\};\ \{2,\ldots, m\}\cap I \neq \varnothing; \ |I|>1]$$ 
            be the polynomial ring over $\Z$ on $2^{n-1}-2^{n-m}-m$ variables. Then there is a quotient map $R\onto A(\DMumford{w})$. Furthermore, the kernel of this quotient map is the ideal generated by the following elements:
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item $x_I x_J$ for each pair $I,J$ such that $I\cap J\notin \{I,J, \varnothing\} $;
                \item For each $\{i,j\},\{k,l\}\in {\{2,\ldots, n\}\choose 2}$ with $i,k\le m$, 
                $$\sum_{I: \{i,j\}\subseteq I, \{k,l\}\not\subseteq I} x_I - \sum_{I: \{k,l\}\subseteq I, \{i,j\}\not\subseteq I} x_I.$$
            \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
