[Thm matchingmatsourbound of arXiv:2411.10633, 'A Geometric Perspective on the Injective Norm of Sums of Random Tensors'] Let $M_1, \ldots, M_n$ be matchings on $[d]$, the respective adjacency matrices be $A_1, \ldots, A_n \in \mathbb R^{d \times d}$, and $E \coloneqq M_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup M_n$. Define $\mu \in \mathbb R^n$ by $\mu_i \coloneqq \vertM_i\vert$ and $\Delta \in \mathbb R^d$ such that $\Delta_i$ is the degree of vertex $i$ in the multigraph $([d],E)$ (including multiplicities). For $p \geq 4$ and $g_1, \ldots, g_n$ being i.i.d. standard Gaussians, we have
    \begin{equation}
        d^{\frac1p -\frac12} \mathbb E \Big\|\sum_{k=1}^n g_k A_k \Big\|_{\mathcal{I}_p} \underset{p}{\lesssim} (\log d)\left\lVert\mu\right\rVert_1^{\frac14} \left\lVert\Delta \right\rVert_\infty^{\frac 1p} \left\lVert\mu\right\rVert_{\frac{2p-4}{p-4}}^{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{p}}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm matchingmatsourbound of arXiv:2411.10633

[Theorem thm4.4 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] Suppose $(g_1, g_2, g_3, \dots)$ is a sequence of positive
numbers such that $g_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$.
Then there exists a (real) strictly stationary, countable-state,
irreducible, aperiodic Markov chain 
$X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ which is reversible and has
the following properties: \hfil\break
(i) There exists a positive constant $C$ such that
$P(|X_0| \leq C) = 1$; \hfil\break
(ii) $\alpha(n) \leq \beta(n) << g_n \cdot n^{-1}$ as $n \to \infty$ 
(see Notations (nt2.1 of the paper));  \hfil\break
(iii) conclusions (iii) and (iv) in Theorem \ref {thm3.4} hold; and \hfil\break
(iv) defining ${\bf h}(n) := n^{-1} \textrm{\rm Var}(\sum_{k=1}^n X_k)$ for every $n \in \mathbb N$, one has that
\begin{align}

&{\bf h}(n)\ \leq\ g_n\ \ {\rm for\ every}\ n \in \mathbb N;\ \ \ {\rm and} \\

&{\rm for\ every}\ N \in \mathbb N,\ \ \ 
\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac {{\bf h}(N n)} {{\bf h}(n)}\ =\ N. 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm4.4 of arXiv:2508.12951

body:
[Corollary 27 (The two zones, geometrised) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] In the canonical realisation, for every $a$ and drift for which the
vertex condition \textup{(V)} holds --- in particular for $a=3,4$
by Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}, and for $5\le a\le8$ by the
numerical evidence of Remark~\ref{rem:walk-V-numeric} --- the
starting sites split into two consecutive zones about the
midpoint,
\[
\underbrace{+\ \cdots\ +}_{z<a/2}\quad
\underbrace{\bigl[\,0\,\bigr]_{a\ \mathrm{even}}}_{z=a/2}\quad
\underbrace{-\ \cdots\ -}_{z>a/2}\, ,
\]
where $\pm$ denotes the constant sign of
$\partial_\gamma C(e_z,\cdot)$. Two things must be distinguished.
That every orbit $\{z,a-z\}$ straddles the midpoint and contributes
exactly one site to each sign class is forced by the orbit
structure alone, and is independent of the parity of $a$. That the
class below the midpoint is the one labelled $+$, on the other
hand, is not: it depends on the orientation chosen for the
directors and on the global sign $\varepsilon$ of \textup{(V)}, and
is fixed here by the canonical orientation together with the sign
of the constant $-2q^{a}$ computed in
Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}. When $a$ is even the midpoint is
itself a site, the unique fixed point of $\sigma$, and it is
exactly reset-neutral; when $a$ is odd the value $a/2$ is not an integer, so no site is a
fixed point of $\sigma$, none is invariant, and the two index
ranges $z<a/2$ and $z>a/2$ exhaust the sites with no neutral index
between them. \textup{(}The ``zones'' are sets of integer sites
throughout, not regions of a continuum.\textup{)} This is the two-zone theorem
of Paper~I, obtained here as a corollary of the geometry: the two
zones are the two sides of the separatrix, the neutral site --- when
it exists --- is its intersection with the vertex set, and the
midpoint is fixed by the site involution $\sigma$, whose fixed
point it is, while the associated spherical reflection $R_L$ fixes
the separatrix pointwise; the two are distinct structures, kept
apart by Proposition~\ref{prop:three-involutions}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The two zones, geometrised

[Lemma lmm:smallest ev as corr of arXiv:2411.10311, 'Planar Novikov-Shubin invariant for adjacency matrices of structured directed dense random'] Let $a, c_1'$ be positive constants.
Let $D$ be an $n \times n$  random matrix with i.i.d. entries and finite variance and $M$ be an $n \times n$ deterministic matrix of spectral norm at most $n^{c_1'}$. Let $A$ be an $(N-n) \times (N-n)$ matrix, $B$ be an $(N-n)\times n$ matrix, and $C$ be an $n\times (N-n)$ matrix. Assume there exist $b''$ and an event occurring with probability $1-N^{-a}$ on which $A^{-1}$  has norm bounded by $N^{b''}$ and $\|B\|, \|C\|$ have norm $O(1)$. Furthermore, assume that $D$ is independent of $A$, $B$ and $C$.

With the definition 
\[
Y := \begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ C & D \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \mathcal{M}:= \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & M \end{pmatrix},
\]
 there are positive constants $b'$ and $c_2'$ (depending on $a$, $c_1'$ and $b''$) such that
\[ \mathbb{P}( \norm{( \mathcal{M}+Y)^{-1}} \ge N^{b'}) \leq c_2' N^{-a}.\]

[Proposition 14 (Transport kernels) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] For $0<p\le q$, define, for bounded measurable $h:\R\to\R$,
\[
K_{p,q}h(x)=\E h(V_{p,q}x),
\]
where $V_{p,q}$ has the unique factor law. Then $K_{p,q}$ is a Markov operator and
\[
\E h(X_p)=\E K_{p,q}h(X_q).
\]
Moreover, for $0<p\le q\le r$, the operators compose on test functions according to
\[
K_{q,r}(K_{p,q}h)=K_{p,r}h.
\]
The composition is evaluated using independent copies of the factor laws.

[Proposition prop:intrinsic-persistency of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {wijesekera_constructive_1990}}] 
  $\Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent for any f-model $\mathfrak{M}$.
  \begin{proof}
    Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ and take any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall only prove the cases with modal operators.

    Suppose that $x \leq x'$ and $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$,
    and take any $x'', y''$ such that $x' \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$.
    Here, $x \leq x' \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$ implies $x \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$ by $\leq$ being preorder,
    then $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$ implies $y'' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    Now suppose that $x \leq x'$ and $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$,
    and take any $x''$ such that $x' \leq x''$, then $x \leq x' \leq x''$ implies $x \leq x''$ by $\leq$ being preorder.
    Since $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, there is $y'' \sqsupset x''$ such that $y'' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A sequence (a_n) converges to L if for every epsilon > 0 there is N such that |a_n - L| < epsilon for all n >= N. The limit, when it exists, is unique. Convergent sequences are bounded; limits respect sums, products, quotients (nonzero denominator), and order (limits of a_n <= b_n satisfy lim a_n <= lim b_n).

[Definition def-point process of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] Suppose that $(X, \mathscr{B}_X) $ is a non-empty measure space  and
$\bigl( {\Omega}, {\mathscr{F}}, {\mathbb{P}} \bigr)$ is a probability space. A {random} point process (on $X$ and on $\bigl( {\Omega}, {\mathscr{F}}, {\mathbb{P}}  \bigr)$) is a map \[
p: \Omega \to \Pi_X
\]
which is ${\mathscr{F}}/\mathscr{B}(\Pi_X)$-measurable.
Hereafter, when there is no ambiguity we just say a point process instead of random point process.

If $p: \Omega \to \Pi_X$ is a point process, then
 we will write $p(t,\omega)$ for the value of $p(\omega)$ at $t \in D(p(\omega))$.
Moreover, see Definition (def-point function of the paper), when we will write $p(t,\omega)$ we will implicitly imply that $t\in \mathrm{Dom}(p(\omega))$.
title: Definition def-point process of arXiv:2505.24043

[Prop 15 of arXiv:2607.27932, '2607.27932'] For $\Psi_1$ and $\Psi_2$ as in~\eqref{GlobalPot}, define
\begin{equation}
	H_\varepsilon(\lambda):=\inf_{x,y\in \partial \mathbb{B}(\lambda;\varepsilon)}V(x,y)\,,
\end{equation}
and the threshold

\begin{equation}\varepsilon_c=\inf\left\{\varepsilon\le \varepsilon_0\,:\,\min\{M_{1,\varepsilon};M_{2,\varepsilon}\}>\inf_\lambda
H_\varepsilon(\lambda),\,\,i\neq j\in\{1,2\}\right\}\,.
\end{equation}
for 
\[
M_{1,\varepsilon}=\inf_{x\in\partial\mathbb B(\lambda_1;\varepsilon),y\in\mathbb R^d}V(x,y),\quad M_{2,\varepsilon}=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d,y\in\partial\mathbb B(\lambda_2;\varepsilon)}V(x,y).
\]
Let $C_\varepsilon(\sigma)$ be as in \eqref{near-collision-time-SS}, $\varepsilon\in(0,\varepsilon_c)$, $\underline
H_\varepsilon=\min H_\varepsilon$ and let $\mathcal M_\varepsilon$ be the set of minimizers of~$H_\varepsilon$. Then, for any
$\delta>0$,
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{\sigma\to0}\PP\left(\exp\left[\frac{2}{\sigma^2}\left(\underline
H_\varepsilon-\delta\right)\right]<{C}_\varepsilon(\sigma)<\exp\left[\frac{2}{\sigma^2}\left(\underline
H_\varepsilon+\delta\right)\right]\right)=1\,,
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{\sigma\to0}\PP\left(\inf_{\lambda_\varepsilon\in\mathcal M_\varepsilon}\max\bigg({\rm
dist}\big(X_{C_\varepsilon(\sigma)},\mathbb B(\lambda_\varepsilon;\varepsilon)\big),{\rm dist}\big(Y_{C_\varepsilon(\sigma)},\mathbb
B(\lambda_\varepsilon;\varepsilon)\big)\bigg)\ge \delta\right)=0\,.
\end{equation*}

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Let $a \in C^\infty(\TT^2)$. Then, there exists $C_r, C_{r,\delta}>0$ so that 
$$
\|a B\|_{\mathcal X} \leq C_r \|a \|_{L^\infty} \|B\|_{\mathcal X}+C_{r,\delta}\|\nabla a\|_{L^\infty}\|B\|_{\mathcal Y}.
$$
Furthermore, there holds the bound 
$$
\|aB\|_{\mathcal Y} \leq C_{r,\delta}\|a\|_{C^1}\|B\|_{\mathcal Y}.
$$

 we have

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $p \in S^m(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d)$. Let $U, V$ be two open sets of $\Rr^d$, $V$ being convex, and let $\chi : U \to V$ be a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying $\|\Jac \chi^{-1} - I_d\|_{L^{\infty}(V)} <1$. 
Let $\psi \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}_c(V)$ and $\rho \in \mathcal{C}_c^{\infty}(U)$ 
such that~\(\rho\) is equal to~\(1\) on a neighborhood of $\chi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp} \psi)$. If~\(f\) is compactly supported in~\(V\) set~\(C_\chi f\) the function corresponding to~\(f\circ \chi\) on~\(U\) and~\(0\) outside~\(U\). Operator~\(C_\chi\) is a bijection between functions compactly supported in~\(V\) and functions compactly supported in~\(U\).
Set 
\[
Q = \psi C_{\chi}^{-1} \rho \Op(p) \rho C_{\chi}\psi,
\]
and define $J(x,y)=\displaystyle\int_0^1 \Jac \chi^{-1}(tx+(1-t)y)^\top\mathrm{d}t$ for $x, y \in V$.

Then, there exists $q\in S^m(\Rr^d \times \Rr^d)$ such that $Q=\psi\Op(q)\psi$, and 
moreover, $q$ admits the following asymptotic expansion on a neighborhood of $\supp \psi$ included in~\(V\):
\begin{equation}
    
        q(x,\xi) \sim \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} \frac{\rho(\chi^{-1}(x))}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !} \partial_y^\alpha \left.\partial_{\xi}^\alpha \left(\rho(\chi^{-1}(y))p\left(\chi^{-1}(x),J(x,y)^{-1}\xi\right)\left\vert\frac{\det \Jac \chi^{-1} (y)}{\det J(x,y)}\right\vert\right)\right\vert_{y=x}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 11 of arXiv:2609.01105

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The circular measure $\varepsilon$ of a rooted bipartite graph $X$ is given by
$$d\varepsilon(q)=d\nu((q+q^{-1})^2)$$
where $\nu$ is the associated positive spectral measure.

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.03873, 'Minimal proximal definable flows over the $p$-adics'] Assume that $T$ is NIP. Let $X$ be a minimal proximal definable $G$-flow. Let $\mu\in \Prob(X)$ and $z\in X$. Then $\delta_z$, the Dirac measure for $z$, is in the weak-* closure of $G\mu$. 
Hence, $X$ is strongly proximal.

[Cor 17 of arXiv:2609.00739, '2609.00739'] Fix $x_0\in\R^2$ and $R>0$.  Let $a_j\in W^{1,\infty}(B_R(x_0))$ satisfy
\[
 a_-\leq a_j\leq a_+,
 \quad
 \frac{R\norm{\nabla a_j}_{L^\infty(B_R(x_0))}}{a_-}\leq\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Let $\frac{\eps_j}{R}\to0$, and let $u_j\in H^1(B_R(x_0);\R^k)$ be weak
solutions of
\[
 -\eps_j\Delta u_j+\frac{a_j}{\eps_j}\nabla V(u_j)=0
 \quad\text{in }B_R(x_0),
\]
with $\norm{u_j}_{L^\infty(B_R(x_0))}\leq L$.  Suppose
\[
 e_{\eps_j,a_j}(u_j)\dd x\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\nustar,
 \quad
 \frac{a_jV(u_j)}{\eps_j}\dd x
 \stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\zetastar
\]
on $B_R(x_0)$.  After reducing $\eta_0$ by a universal numerical factor,
the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=$(\theenumi)$]
\item If
$\nustar(\overline{B_r(x)})<\eta_0r$ and
$\overline{B_r(x)}\subset B_R(x_0)$, then
$\nustar\left(B_{\frac{r}{2}}(x)\right)=0$.
\item If $x\in\supp\nustar$ and
$\overline{B_r(x)}\subset B_R(x_0)$, then
\[
 \nustar(B_r(x))\geq\eta_0r.
\]
\item For every ball $B_r(x)$ with
$\overline{B_r(x)}\subset B_R(x_0)$,

body:
[Lemma 8 (the constant-field Fourier representation) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] With $(\tau,\xi)$ the spacetime Fourier variables, $\lambda$ as in
\eqref{eq:Bmult}, and $\tau_\pm=\tau\pm\lambda$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde{\mathcal Bf}=\mathrm i\lambda\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A^+f}=\mathrm i\tau_+\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A^-f}=\mathrm i\tau_-\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\Box f}=-\tau_+\tau_-\widetilde f .
\end{equation}
Consequently $D_\pm=-\mathrm i\mathcal A^\pm$ are commuting self-adjoint
operators on $L^2(dt dy)$ and, for every Borel function $\Phi$,
\begin{equation}
 \Phi(D_+,D_-)f
 :=\big(\Phi(\tau_+,\tau_-)\widetilde f\big)^\vee
\end{equation}
on its maximal domain.  Moreover
\[
 \mathrm e^{r\mathcal B}f(t,y)=f(t,y+r\Binf),
 \qquad
 \mathrm e^{r\mathcal A^\pm}f(t,y)=f(t+r,y\pm r\Binf),
\]
so these groups are isometries on every $L^p$ and unitary on $L^2$.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 [\Lambda^{\sreg},\mathcal B]=0
 \qquad(\sreg\in\Real),
\end{equation}
and all corresponding Fourier-multiplier commutators vanish.

[Theorem thm:stab of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let~$G = (V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, connected graph with
		degree bounded by~$d$, and let $(\sigma(v))_{v\in V}$ be i.i.d.\ random variables
		with $\mathbb{E}[\sigma(v)] = \mu \in [-\infty,1)$.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item If $\mathbb{E}[(\sigma(v)^+)^p] < \infty$ for some $p > 3$, then
			$\sup_{v \in V}\mathbb{E}[u_\infty(v)^q] < \infty$ for every $q\in[1,(p-1)/2)$; in particular $\mathbb{P}(\sigma \text{ stabilizes}) = 1$.
			\item If $|B(o,r)|\leq C r^{d_f}$ for some $o\in V$, some $C>0$, some $d_f\geq 1$, and all $r\geq 1$, and if $\mathbb{E}[(\sigma(v)^+)^p] < \infty$ for some $p > d_f$, then $\mathbb{P}(\sigma \text{ stabilizes}) = 1$.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2506.20789, 'Central limit theory for Peaks-over-Threshold partial sums of long memory linear time seri'] Let $\gamma\in (0,1)$. Then the following hold:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item
    For all $y,z\in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align}
    
    g_{\gamma}
    (z+y)
    \ \lesssim \
    g_\gamma(z)
    \cdot
    (1\lor |y|)^{1+\gamma}\,.
  \end{align}
  \item
    Let $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ with $a<b$. Then, for all $z\in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align}
    
    \int_a^b g_\gamma(z-w)\,\mathrm{d}w
    \ \lesssim \
    g_\gamma(z)
    \cdot
    ((b-a) \lor 1)^{1+\gamma}
    \,.
  \end{align}
  \end{enumerate}
  Here $\lesssim$ denotes inequality up to a constant $C_{\gamma}>0$ depending only on $\gamma$.

body:
[Thm 5 (Conditional one-point fluctuations on the boundaries) of arXiv:2608.20552, 'One-point fluctuations for exponential last passage percolation under upper-tail condition'] Set
\beq
	\mathbf v=(v_1,v_2):=(\sqrt{\slope \ac},-\sqrt{\bc}), \qquad 
	\mr c:=2(\slope \ac\bc)^{1/6}(\sqrt{\slope \ac}+\sqrt{\bc})^{-1/3}.
\eeq
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textnormal{(a)}]
Fix $(x,y)\in(1,\infty)^2$ on the lower boundary between $U_1$ and $U_2$, so that $\frac{y-1}{x-1}=\frac{1}{\slope}$, 
and fix $\ww\in\R$. Set $\delta_N:=\mr c\ww(y-1)^{2/3}N^{2/3}$. Then, for every $\rr\in\R$,
\beqq
	\lim_{N\to\infty}
	\prob\left[
		\frac{\LPP\left(\ac xN+v_1\delta_N,\bc yN+v_2\delta_N\right)-\mv(x,y)N}
		{\sdev(x,y)N^{1/3}}
		\le\rr
		\,\bigg|\,
		\LPP(\ac N,\bc N)>\lv N
	\right]
	=F_{\tn{BBP},\ww}(\rr+\ww^2).
\eeqq

\item[\textnormal{(b)}]
Fix $(x,y)\in(0,\infty)^2$ on the lower boundary between $U_2$ and $U_3$, so that $\frac{y}{x}=\frac{1}{\slope}$, 
and fix $\ww\in\R$. Set $\delta_N:=\mr c\ww y^{2/3}N^{2/3}$. Then, for every $\rr\in\R$,
\beqq
	\lim_{N\to\infty}
	\prob\left[
		\frac{\LPP\left(\ac xN-v_1\delta_N,\bc yN-v_2\delta_N\right)-\mv(x,y)N}
		{\sdev(x,y)N^{1/3}}
		\le\rr
		\,\bigg|\,
		\LPP(\ac N,\bc N)>\lv N
	\right]
	=F_{\tn{BBP},\ww}(\rr+\ww^2).
\eeqq

\item[\textnormal{(c)}]
The corresponding statements on the upper boundaries follow by symmetry under the simultaneous exchanges $\ac\leftrightarrow \bc$ and $x\leftrightarrow y$, with $\mathbf v$ replaced by $(-\sqrt{\ac},\sqrt{\slope \bc})$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conditional one-point fluctuations on the boundaries

body:
[Proposition lemma:frechet of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Suppose $F : L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ has continuous partial derivatives with respect to the standard
    basis $\{e_u\}_{u \in V}$, that is, for each $u \in V$ the $L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ function 
    \[
        \partial_u F(f) = \lim_{t \to 0} \frac{F(f + t e_u) - F(f)}{t}
    \]
    is continuous. Then $F$ is (Fréchet) $C^1$ and its gradient $\nabla F : L^2(V) \to L^2(V)$ is
    given by
    \[
        (\nabla F(f))(u) = |V| \cdot \partial_u F(f)
    \]
    for each $f \in L^2(V)$ and $u \in V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition lemma:frechet of arXiv:2505.02685

body:
[Thm Buslim of arXiv:2605.21366, 'The Martin boundary of the Directed Landscape'] The following holds on a full probability event.
Let $x_0,s_0\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $(r_n,z_n)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be a sequence such that $r_n\to\infty$ and $\mathcal L(\,\hspace{0.6pt}{\raisebox{1pt}{\scaleobj{0.6}{\bullet}}}\hspace{0.8pt}\,;z_n,r_n)-\mathcal L(x_0,s_0;z_n,r_n)$ converges uniformly on compacts to a function $\mathfrak h:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate} [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt 
\item There exists a $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $z_n/r_n\to\theta$ as $n\to\infty$. 
\item $\mathfrak h$ is an eternal solution, normalized to satisfy $\mathfrak h(x_0,s_0)=0$.
\item There exist $a_-,a_+\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ such that $a_-\vee a_+=0$ and 
\[\mathfrak h(x,s)=(W^{\theta-}(x,s;x_0,s_0)+a_-)\vee(W^{\theta+}(x,s;x_0,s_0)+a_+)\quad\text{for all $x,s\in\mathbb{R}$.}\]
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 8 (boundary quantities of the reflecting resolvent) of arXiv:2605.13648, 'Sticky CIR process with potential: invariant measure and exact sampling'] \label[lemma]{lemma-green-zero}
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item  The scale derivatives of $f_0(x) = M(a,b,z_x)$ and
  $f_\infty(x) = U(a,b,z_x)$ at the boundary satisfy
  \[
    \frac{df_0}{ds}(0^+) = 0,
    \qquad
    \frac{df_\infty}{ds}(0^+) = -|\mathcal{W}|.
  \]
  \item
  \(
    G_\alpha(0,0) = {U_0}/{|\mathcal{W}|},
    \)
    where $U_0 = U(a,b,0) = \frac{\Gamma(1-b)}{\Gamma(1+a-b)}$ and
    \begin{equation}
      |\mathcal{W}| = \lambda\beta\,\frac{\Gamma(b)}{\Gamma(a)}\,
      \Bigl(\tfrac{\lambda\beta}{2}\Bigr)^{-b}.
    \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}

[Thm 56 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Suppose $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{A}'$ are central  complex hyperplane arrangements. [Definition 4 (Disjoint testimony) of arXiv:2607.02272, 'The case of equality in BK'] Let \(A\) and \(B\) be two subsets of \(\Omega\).
  The disjoint testimony of \(A\) and \(B\) is the subset
  \(A\boxtimes B\) of \(A\times B\) consisting of the pairs \((x,y)\)
  admitting disjoint witnesses for \(A\) and \(B\), i.e.,
  \begin{multline}
    A\boxtimes B
    \,=\,
    \smash{\Big\{}\,(x,y)\in A\times B:\exists\,I,J\subset\unn,\quad
    I\cap J\,=\,\varnothing,
    \\
    I \text{ is a witness for } A \text{ in } x,\quad
    J \text{ is a witness for } B \text{ in } y
  \,\smash{\Big\}}\,.
  \end{multline}

body:
[Lemma lem:gaps-short of arXiv:2608.05123, 'A central limit theorem for the random assignment problem'] In the increasing ordering \(U_{(1)}<\cdots<U_{(n)}\),
\begin{equation}
 U_{(k+1)}-U_{(k)}=\frac{nE_k}{k(n-k)},\qquad
 E_k\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}{\rm Exp}(1),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 U_{(j)}=\sum_{k<j}\frac{E_k}{n-k}-\sum_{k\ge j}\frac{E_k}{k},
 \qquad
 \bar u_{j,n}:=\mathbb E U_{(j)}=\mathsf H_{j-1}-\mathsf H_{n-j}.
\end{equation}
Moreover
\[
 Z_n^{\rm gap}=\frac{n^{n-1}}{(n-1)!},\qquad
 \frac1n\sum_i\delta_{U_i}\Longrightarrow
 \ell(u)\,\mathrm d u,\quad
 \ell(u)=\frac{e^{-u}}{(1+e^{-u})^2},
\]
in \(W_2\), in probability.  If \(R=\osc U\), then
\begin{gather}
 R=O_{\mathbb P}(\log n),\qquad
 \mathbb E\sum_j(U_{(j)}-\bar u_{j,n})^2=2\mathsf H_{n-1},\\
 \mathbb E\left(\sum_j(U_{(j)}-\bar u_{j,n})^2\right)^2=O(\log^2n),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\left|\frac1n\sum_iU_i^2-\frac{\pi^2}{3}\right|
 =O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right).
\end{gather}
If \(\varpi_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{U_i}\) and
\(\bar\varpi_n=n^{-1}\sum_j\delta_{\bar u_{j,n}}\), then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E W_1(\varpi_n,\ell)^2=O(\log n/n),\qquad
 W_1(\bar\varpi_n,\ell)=O(\log n/n).
\end{equation}
For every fixed \(a,b,M\), there are \(A,C<\infty\), depending only
on \(a,b,M\), such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\bigl[n^a(1+R)^b\1_{\{R>A\log n\}}\bigr]\le Cn^{-M}.
\end{equation}

body: Every convex body K in R^n contains a unique ellipsoid E of maximal volume, and K is contained in the n-fold dilation of E about its center (sqrt(n)-fold when K is centrally symmetric). John's characterization: E is the unit ball exactly when there are contact points and positive weights forming an isotropic decomposition of the identity. The theorem bounds how far any norm is from a Euclidean one (Banach-Mazur distance at most sqrt(n)) and drives algorithmic rounding of convex bodies.
title: John Ellipsoid

[Df Join of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Two topological $(k-1)$-spheres $S$ and $S'$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ are said to be \emph{joined with width at most $w$}, denoted by $S\approx_wS'$, if there exists an open $k$-tube of width at most $w$ whose initial sphere is $S$ and terminal sphere is $S'$.
  We say that $S$ is \emph{joined to infinity with width at most $w$}, and write $S\approx_w\infty$, if there exists an infinite open $k$-tube of width at most $w$ whose initial sphere is $S$.
  Furthermore, if there exits some $w>0$ such that $S\approx_w\infty$, then we simply say that $S$ is \emph{joined to infinity}, and denote this by $S\approx\infty$.
title: Join

[Corollary C:elpp-result of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $\alpha>0$ and the field $X$ from Section (sssec:constru of the paper).
Let $W:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be an array of independent random variables, such that for each $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{1\}$,
$$
W(1, j) \sim \operatorname{Exp}(\alpha), \qquad W(i, j) \sim \operatorname{Exp}(1).
$$
Then for each $(1,1)\le (n,m)\in\mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge}$, we have
$$
\max_{0 \le i \le m - 1}X(1, 1; n + i, m - i) \stackrel{d}{=} W(1, 1; n, m).
$$
title: Corollary C:elpp-result of arXiv:2604.10020

[Lemma 28 of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] The conditional covariance matrix
  \begin{equation*}
    K_\tau ( t, s )
    =
    R ( \tau + t, \tau + s ) 
    - R ( \tau + t, \tau ) \, \Sigma^{-1} (\tau ) \, R ( \tau, \tau + s )
  \end{equation*}
  admits the following asymptotic formula:
  \begin{equation*}
    K_\tau ( t, s )
    =
    S_{\alpha,V}(t)+S_{\alpha,V}(-s)-S_{\alpha,V}(t-s)
    + o ( \tau^\beta + (\tau + t)^\beta + (\tau +s)^\beta + t^\alpha + s^\alpha + |t-s|^\alpha )
  \end{equation*}
  as \( \tau, t, s \to 0^+ \). In particular, for \(t\ge s\ge0\) the leading
  term is
  \[
    Vt^\alpha+V^\top s^\alpha-V(t-s)^\alpha .
  \]

[Prop 25 of arXiv:2607.28578, 'On two differing geometric descriptions of the passage from microscopy to macroscopy in Ma'] Let $G_{\eta}\colon\R^r\to\Vspace_{\eta}$ be given by $G_{\eta}e_j=\psi_j^{\eta}$, where $\Vspace_{\eta}$ is a Hilbert velocity space. Then
	\[
		\langle\beta,\gamma\rangle_{*,\eta}=\langle G_{\eta}\beta,G_{\eta}\gamma\rangle_{\Vspace_{\eta}}
	\]
	is positive semidefinite, and $G_{\eta}$ is an isometric isomorphism from $\R^r/\Ker G_{\eta}$ onto its finite dimensional closed range. If the family is minimal and the fields satisfy \eqref{statistic-stein-equation-eq}, then $G_{\eta}$ is injective. The minimum-$\Vspace_{\eta}$ right inverse gives a canonical cometric amongst the chosen velocity class; adding vertical fields changes the particles and the cometric without changing the model density evolution.

body:
[Theorem 1 (Averaged macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(d\ge 3\), let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, and let \(p_{d,n}\) denote its law. Assume
    \[
    d>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(\lambda>0\), and let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). Assume
    \[
    \lambda>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\), that is, the pairing model conditioned on simplicity. Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho.
    \]
    If
    \[
    \rho>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr),
    \]
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Averaged macroscopic-loop bounds

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.01362, '{Double cluster swapping for spin models: \\Pfaffian relations and sharpness}'] Let $P$ belong the class $\Ec$. Then, there exists $\beta_c \in (0,\infty]$ such that
	\begin{itemize}
		\item (Disordered phase) if $\beta < \beta_c$, then there is finite susceptibility $\chi(\beta) < \infty$. Moreover, if $J$ is finite-range then there exists $c = c(\beta) > 0$ such that
			\[
			\left< \vp_o \vp_x \right>_{\beta}^+ \leq \exp( - c \, d(0,x)).
			\] 
		\item (Ordered phase) there is $c > 0$ such that for all $\beta \geq \beta_c$, the susceptibility is infinite and
			\begin{equation}
			\left< \vp_o \right>_{\beta}^+ \geq c  \,\frac{\beta - \beta_c}{\beta}.
			\end{equation} 
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Consequently at L=floor(nt) its scaled reciprocal has a log(n)/(2pi n) correction plus a theta0-dependent constant and a fractional-layer term. This is not a finite-width stochastic mean expansion. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:924aa3cf967d37728017e8c0560d49a1b5c6c3d64d97286887a8cf4fc7ab7f9f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/92/924aa3cf967d37728017e8c0560d49a1b5c6c3d64d97286887a8cf4fc7ab7f9f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:452ba6bbe8bae42609897f9aa18612c97d80ca3354c8d48f003d294369bc6451","bundle_entry_key":"deterministic-log-offset","bundle_id":"population.t244-rate-diagnostics-011","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-deterministic-log-offset","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C028-C029: the mean observable and the deterministic entrance offset

20 October 2026. Target 1. These are rate diagnostics, not a finite-width
network weak-error theorem. Both statements require independent review.

## C028: the raw finite-width mean cannot have the proposed expansion

For every width n>=2 and finite positive depth L, the exact Gaussian ReLU
chain with initial angle in (0,pi) has

    E[1/(n theta_L); all layers nondegenerate] = infinity.

Here nondegenerate means neither vector is extinct and their angle is
strictly positive. The assertion follows directly from reviewer-PASS C003:
conditional on any nondegenerate previous state, the next reciprocal angle
has infinite expectation even on nondegenerate next states. The probability
of nondegenerate survival through each finite number of layers is positive
(restrict to open Gaussian-row sets giving two positive, nonproportional
output coordinates). Tonelli's theorem therefore propagates C003 to any
positive depth. Assigning a bounded cemetery value does not repair this
continuous near-collinearity divergence. Conditioning the entire finite path
on nondegeneracy also leaves the mean infinite, since its conditioning event
has positive probability and its unnormalized reciprocal integral is infinite.

Consequently an identity E U_n(t)=E U_t+c(t)/n+o(1/n), for the raw network
reciprocal at floor(nt)>=1, is false as stated. Each finite Monte Carlo sample
has a finite average, which can approximate the central part of the law, but
not this infinite expectation. A finite observable must be specified, for
example min(U_n,R) at fixed R, or the explicitly regularized good-event chain.
For fixed R the diffusion reference is E min(U_t,R), not E U_t. No uniform
error allowing R->infinity after a rate expansion has yet been proved.

## C029: deterministic ReLU offset contains log(depth), not just a constant

Let theta_(l+1)=F(theta_l) be the infinite-width ReLU angle recursion,
with fixed theta_0 in (0,pi), where

    cos F(theta)=[sin(theta)+(pi-theta)cos(theta)]/pi.

Put r_l=1/theta_l, a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2). There is a finite constant
C(theta_0), depending on the entire initial deterministic orbit, such that

    r_l = a l + (1/(2pi)) log l + C(theta_0)
                   + O_theta0(log(l)/l),  l->infinity.             (D)

The fixed offset is therefore not exactly 1/theta_0, and the correction
cannot consist solely of an initial constant number of layers.

Proof. The cosine equation and Taylor's theorem give

    F(theta)=theta-a theta^2-(a^2/2)theta^3+O(theta^4),
    1/F(theta)-1/theta=a+(3a^2/2)theta+O(theta^2)
                      =a+b theta+O(theta^2).                      (E)

To justify the expansion despite the derivative of arccos at one, use
F=2 arcsin(sqrt((1-cos F)/2)). Factoring theta^2 in 1-cos F leaves a
positive analytic factor near zero; the remaining square root and arcsin
have convergent Taylor expansions there. The positive branch gives (E).

The strict inequality 0<F(theta)<theta implies theta_l decreases to zero.
Thus r_l increases to infinity, and (E) implies

    r_(l+1)-r_l=a+b/r_l+O(r_l^(-2)).

The increments tend to a, so r_l/l->a by averaging the increments. In
particular r_l is bounded above and below by positive multiples of l for
large l. Summing the O(1/l) correction gives r_l=al+O(log l). Now define
H_l=r_l-al-(b/a)log l for l>=1. Then

    H_(l+1)-H_l
       =b/r_l-(b/a)log(1+1/l)+O(r_l^(-2))
       =O(log(l)/l^2).

This is absolutely summable. Hence H_l converges to C(theta_0), with
tail O(log(l)/l). Since b/a=1/(2pi), this proves (D).

For L=floor(nt), fixed t>0, (D) yields the precise deterministic expansion

    r_L/n = a t + [log n/(2pi)+log t/(2pi)+C(theta_0)
                     -a {nt}]/n + O_theta0,t(log n/n^2).           (F)

The fractional-part term is essential unless nt is integral. This is a
theorem for the deterministic map, not for the finite-width chain: its
leading a t differs from the stochastic mean a(exp(2t)-1)/2. In particular,
one may not simply add (F) to that stochastic mean and call it a network
rate. The singular b/(nu) term suggested by (E) is a warning that matching
the entrance to a higher-order compact generator can create log(n)/n terms.
Showing their coefficient, cancellation, or absence for a specified bounded
network observable is still open in this note.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:3d7df9f2e51673034c933127493e891f934b33deb918593bd355f53d6e87ca80","revision_digest":"sha256:89b76734d3eecc1aa1a1e6461d2ae719c0a7a31d2a3401415dfd3abc343dfc91","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C029:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma le:good_scales_merging_multiple of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $D$ with some bounded boundary values. For any $b>0$ and $q \in (0,1)$ there exist $M,p>0$ so that the following is true. 
Let $z \in D$ and $r>0$ such that $B(z,r) \subseteq D$. Let $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$ be as defined in Section~(se:gff of the paper) with the same boundary values as $\widetilde{h}$ above (after scaling and translation). Let $G_{z,r}$ be the event that
\begin{itemize}
 \item the scale $(z,r)$ is $M$-good for $h$, and
 \item the event $G$ above occurs for the (scaled and translated) field $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$ let $E$ be the event that the fraction of $1 \leq j \leq k$ so that $G_{z,2^{-j}r}$ occurs is at least $q$. Then $\mathbf{P}[E^c] = O(e^{-bk})$.

[Proposition prop:sym_tilted_explicit of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $\mathcal{L}_S = p_{\textrm{s}}^{-1}\nabla\cdot(p_{\textrm{s}} D\nabla)$ and $\mathcal{L}_A = v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot\nabla$
be the symmetric and antisymmetric parts of the Markov generator
from Eq.~(equation eq:markov_gen_decomposition of the paper).
For $f \in
D(\mathcal{L})$, the tilted generator for \emph{density observables} has symmetric and
antisymmetric parts, 
\begin{align}
  \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_k^\rho f= \mathcal{L}_S f + kV f,
  \qquad
  \widehat{\mathcal{L}}_k^\rho f= \mathcal{L}_A f,
  
\end{align}
and the tilted generator for \emph{current observables} decomposes as
\begin{align}
  \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_k^J f
  & = \mathcal{L}_S f + k(v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U) f + k^2(U\cdot DU)f\nonumber\\
  
  \widehat{\mathcal{L}}_k^J f
  &= \mathcal{L}_A f + 2k(DU)\cdot\nabla f + kp_{\textrm{s}}^{-1}\nabla\cdot(p_{\textrm{s}} DU) f,  
  
\end{align}
where $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_k^A = \tfrac12\bigl[\mathcal{L}_k^A + (\mathcal{L}_k^A)^\dagger\bigr]$
and $\widehat{\mathcal{L}}_k^A = \tfrac12\bigl[\mathcal{L}_k^A - (\mathcal{L}_k^A)^\dagger\bigr]$
denote the symmetric and antisymmetric parts in $L^2(\mu)$ for $A \in \{\rho, J\}$
from Definition~(def:sym_tilted of the paper).

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of an amenable group $\Gamma$
    admitting a finite-index left-orderable subgroup $H$, with
    $n=[\Gamma:H]$. Consider Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter $p\in(
    0,1)$, an exhaustive F{\o}lner sequence $(A_{r})$, and let $\mathcal{A}$
    be its orbit under $\Gamma$. Then there exists an $H$-fundamental set of
    edges $\tilde E\subset E$ such that, if the stationary $\mathcal{A}$-functional
    $F$ stabilizes in sequence and satisfies a finite moment condition on $\tilde
    E$, then:
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item $\displaystyle \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{1}{|A_{r}|}\Var_{p}\!\bigl
        (F(A_{r})\bigr)=\sigma^{2}$;

      \item $\displaystyle |A_{r}|^{-1/2}\bigl(F(A_{r})-\E_{p}[F(A_{r})]\bigr
        )\ \overset{d}{\Longrightarrow}\ \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})$,
    \end{enumerate}
    where
    \[
      \sigma^{2}= \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{e\in\tilde E}\E_{p}\!\left[\E_{p}\!\left
      [D_{e}^{\infty}\,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_{e}\right]^{2}\right].
    \]
    Here $D_{e}^{\infty}$ is the limit in probability of $D_{e}(\omega,xA_{r}
    ):=F(\omega,xA_{r})-F(\omega^{e},xA_{r})$ as $r\to\infty$ (the limit
    does not depend on $x$), and $\mathcal{F}_{e}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra
    generated by the edges preceding or equal to $e$ in an $H$-invariant total order on
    $E$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.07579

[Lem 17 of arXiv:2608.21090, 'Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process conditioned to have restricted $L_2$-norm'] Fix $r>0$ and $z_0\in\C$. Let $f$ be holomorphic on $B_{r'}(z_0)$ for some $r'>r$. Then
    \[f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{f^{(k)}(z_0)}{k\,!}(z-z_0)^k\]
    for all $z\in B_r(z_0)$ and
    \[\left|f(z)-\sum_{k=0}^n \frac{f^{(k)}(z_0)}{k\,!}(z-z_0)^k\right|\leq \max_{\abs z'-z_0\abs=r}\abs f(z')\abs\frac{\abs z-z_0\abs^{n+1}}{r^{n+1}}\frac{1}{1-\frac{\abs z-z_0\abs}{r}}.\]

body:
[Lem construction:q_star of arXiv:2506.10623, 'Polynomial slowdown in an angle-dependent 2d branching Brownian motion'] Let $\alpha \in (0,2)$.
	For any $T \in (0,1)$ and $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2 \in (0,T/10)$ such that $\varepsilon_2 \leq (1-T)/10$, there exist functions $q^*,q_*\colon [0,T]\to [0,\infty)$ that satisfy the following:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $q_*,q^*$ are non-decreasing, Lipschitz continuous on $[0,T]$, and differentiable on $[0,T]$ except at finitely many points;
		
	    \item $q_*,q^*$ are constant on $[0,\varepsilon_1]$ and $[T-\varepsilon_2,T]$;
	    
	    \item For any $t\in [2\varepsilon_1, T-2\varepsilon_2]$, $q_*(t) = (1-t)^{-\alpha} = q^*(t)$;
	    
	    \item For any $t\in [0,T]$, $q_*(t)\leq (1-t)^{-\alpha} \leq q^*(t)$;
	    
	    \item For any $t \in [0,2\varepsilon_1]$,
	    \[
	    1 - 4 \varepsilon_1 \leq \frac{q_*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq \frac{q^*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq 1 + 3 \varepsilon_1.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any $t\in [T-2\varepsilon_2,T]$, 
	    \[
	    1- \frac{2 \varepsilon_2}{1-T} \leq \frac{q_*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq \frac{q^*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq 1 + \frac{5 \varepsilon_2}{1-T}.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any, $t\in [0,T]$, 
	    \[
	    \frac{1}{2} \leq \frac{q_*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq \frac{q^*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}}\leq 2.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any $t \in [0,T]$ and $q = q_*$ or $q^*$,
	    \[
	    \frac{q'(t)}{q(t)} \leq \frac{8}{(1-t)}.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any $t \in [0,T]$ and $q = q_*$ or $q^*$,
	    \[
	    \int_0^T \abs{(1-t)^{-2\alpha/(2+\alpha)} - q(t)^{2/(2+\alpha)}} \mathop{}\mathopen{}\mathrm{d} t
	    \leq 10 \varepsilon_1^2 + \frac{10 \varepsilon_2^2}{(1-T)^{\kappa+1}}.
	    \]
	\end{enumerate}

body:
For a graph with finite nonnegative edge weights, let T(x,y) be the infimum of the total weights of finite walks from x to y. An injective bigeodesic is a sequence (v_i) indexed by all integers, with distinct vertices and adjacent consecutive vertices, such that the weight of the segment from v_i to v_j equals T(v_i,v_j) for every i<j.
Graph with finite nonnegative edge weights

[Lemma capacity_bound of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] For any $K \subset \subset V$ we have 
	\begin{equation}
		
		(1 - \rho(G)) \cdot |K| \leq
		\mathrm{cap}(K) \leq
		|K|,
	\end{equation}
	where recall that $\rho(G)$ denotes the spectral radius of the graph. In particular, by (equation eq:relation_of_spectral_radius_and_Cheeger_constant of the paper), on a nonamenable graph $G$ the capacity and the cardinality of a finite vertex set are comparable. [Propn 3 of arXiv:2606.13487, 'Branching-Selection Particle Systems and Inverse First Passage Problems'] Let $(\mu_t^N)_{t\geq 0}$ be the measure-valued process describing the $(\omega,f,\Lambda,N)$-BBM process, and define $b^N(t):=\inf\{x:\Lambda\langle \mu_t^N,\omega(\cdot-x)\rangle\geq f(t)\}$. Then for any bounded $\omega$ and any test function $\phi(x,t)\in \C{BC}^{2,1}(\B{R}\times [0,\infty),\B{R})$ we have
    \begin{align}  \langle \mu_t^N,\phi(\cdot,t)\rangle = \langle \rho^N, \phi(\cdot,0)\rangle &+ \int_0^t \langle \mu_s^N, \frac12 \phi_{xx}(\cdot,s) + \phi_t(\cdot,s)+f(s)\phi(\cdot,s)\rangle \\
    &- \frac{f(s)\langle \mu_s^N,\phi(\cdot,s)\omega(\cdot-b^N(s))}{\langle \mu_s^N,\omega(\cdot-b^N(s))\rangle} ds
    \nonumber + M_t^{N,W} + M_t^{N,b},
    \end{align}
    where $M^{N,W}_t$ is a continuous local martingale and $M^{N,b}_t$ is a local martingale, with $\B{E}[[M^{N,W}]_t],\B{E}[[M^{N,b}]_t]\to 0$ as $N\to\infty$ for fixed $t\geq 0$.

[Lemma 3 (Specialized maxima) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Fix $c\in[K]$ and $\zeta,\tau\in\{\pm1\}$. On the one-cluster feasible branch,
write
\[
    f(b)
    :=
    -\frac{\tau\zeta}{K\sqrt6}
    b\varphi(b)
    \left(1-\frac{b^2}{R^2}\right)^{3/2},
    \qquad |b|<R,
\]
and let
\[
    I:=\{b\in(-R,R):f(b)>0\}.
\]
Then $I$ is a connected open interval. For all sufficiently large $R$, $f$
has a unique critical point $b^\star\in I$, which is a strict local maximum
and satisfies
\[
    b^\star=-\tau\zeta+O(R^{-2}).
\]
The corresponding direction
\[
    \omega^\star
    =
    \tau\sqrt{1-\frac{(b^\star)^2}{R^2}}\,v_c
    +
    \frac{b^\star}{R^2}\mu_c
\]
is a strict local maximum of $\Psi_\zeta$ and obeys
\[
    \omega^\star
    =
    \tau v_c
    -
    \frac{\tau\zeta}{R^2}\mu_c
    +
    O(R^{-2}).
\]

[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] We define the fibered Wasserstein space of order \(p,q \in [1,\infty)\) as 
	\[
		\mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1]) := \left\{\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1]) : \int_{0}^{1}W_p(\mu^{\xi},\delta_{x_0})^q d\xi < \infty\right\},
	\]
	where \(x_0\) is an arbitrary fixed point in \(\mathcal{X}\). For any \(\mu,\bar{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1])\), we define the distance 
	\[
		d_{W_p,q}(\mu,\bar{\mu}) := \left( \int_{0}^{1} W_p(\mu^{\xi},\bar{\mu}^{\xi})^q d\xi \right)^{1/q}.
	\]

body:
[Lem lemma:delta-map of arXiv:2411.11676, 'Surface sums for lattice Yang--Mills in the large-$N$ limit'] Let $s = (\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_n) \in \mathcal{S}_o$ be a non-null string, and let $\delta = \delta(s)$. For each positive splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, we have that there is some $1 \leq h_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - h_{s'}, h_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto h_{s'}$ on the domain $\mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$ can be chosen to be injective. 

Similarly, for each negative splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, either 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - 2, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n),\qquad \Big(\delta(s') \leq (\delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n)\quad  \text{if}\quad \delta_1 = 2\Big),$$ 
or there is some $1 \leq g_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that  
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - g_{s'}, g_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto g_{s'}$ (whose domain is a suitable subset of $\mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$) can be taken as injective.
title: Lem lemma:delta-map of arXiv:2411.11676

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Fix $\theta\in(0,1]$ and $q\geq2$. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for some $\mathfrak{c}_0>0$ and $\upalpha\in(0,1)$, and let $\mathsf{x}_0$ be an arbitrary initial condition. Then the $q$-state noisy voter model on $G$  
and noise probability $\theta$ started from $\mathsf{x}_0$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_0}(\varepsilon) = (1+

o(1)
)\max\Big\{T_{\mathsf{x}_0}, \frac{1}{4\theta}\log n\Big\}\,,
\end{equation}
where the $o(1)$-term is $ O\big(\log^{-\upalpha/2} n\big)
$ with a constant 

depending on $\varepsilon,\theta,q,\mathfrak{c}_0,\upalpha$ (but not $G$ or $\mathsf{x}_0$).

In particular, for any sequence of connected graphs $G^{(n)}$ with $n$ vertices satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for the same $\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$, and any sequence of initial conditions $\mathsf{x}_0^{(n)}$, the $q$-state noisy voter model on $G^{(n)}$ with noise probability $\theta$ has cutoff at $\max\{T_{\mathsf{x}_0^{(n)}}, \frac{1}{4\theta}\log n\}$. [Definition 4 (Convex order and irreducibility) of arXiv:2607.15872, 'Existence of $q$-Bass martingales in the semidiscrete setting'] Let $\mu,\nu\in\Prob_1(\RR)$. We say that $\mu$ is dominated by $\nu$ in
convex order, and write $\mu\preceq_c \nu$, if
\[
	\int_{\RR}\varphi\,d\mu
	\leq
	\int_{\RR}\varphi\,d\nu
\]
for every convex function $\varphi:\RR\to\RR$ such that both integrals are
well-defined.

For $\rho\in\Prob_1(\RR)$, define its potential function by
\[
	C_\rho(x):=\int_{\RR}(y-x)^+\,\rho(dy),
	\qquad x\in\RR.
\]
We say that the pair $(\mu,\nu)$ is
irreducible if $\mu \preceq_c \nu$ and the set
\[
	I:=\{x\in\RR:C_\mu(x)<C_\nu(x)\}
\]
is an interval and satisfies $\mu(I)=1$.
title: Convex order and irreducibility
Corollary 2-l13 of arXiv:2412.04015

body:
[Theorem supercritical case JW of arXiv:2607.00731, 'Sharp Asymptotics for the Largest Component in the Subcritical Regime of Preferential Atta'] Assume that $\alpha=\alpha(n)\to a\in(0,\infty]$. Let $m_c=\frac{\alpha n}{2(\alpha+1)}$, suppose that $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(n)>0$ satisfies $\varepsilon=o(1), \varepsilon^3 n\to\infty .$ Then, for $m=\lfloor m_c(1+\varepsilon)\rfloor,$ we have
\[
L_1(G^\alpha_{n,m})
=
\frac{2}{1+2/a}\,\varepsilon n\,(1+o_p(1)),
\]
with the convention $1/\infty=0$.

In particular, if $\alpha=\alpha(n)\to\infty$ and
$\alpha\varepsilon\to\infty$, then, for $m=\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2}(1+\varepsilon)\right\rfloor,$
we have
\[
    L_1(G^\alpha_{n,m})
    =
    2\varepsilon n\,(1+o_p(1)).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Janson--Warnke \cite{JansonWarnke2021Preferential}

body:
[Theorem thm:torus of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] Let $\a_2, \ldots, \a_K : {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be differentiable functions with bounded derivatives, where $K \geq 2$ is an integer independent of $N$, and fix $y_0 > 0$. Let
	\[ \phi(\underline x, y) = \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y)\, f_k^N(\underline x) \]
be the corresponding test function on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _n^d \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $, and let $\varphi(\underline x, y) \coloneqq \phi(\underline x, y/a_N)$ on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _n^d \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} $. Then with $T = N \lfloor y_0 a_N \rfloor$,
	\[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{N a_N}} \langle \! \langle D_T,\, \varphi \rangle \! \rangle
	\Rightarrow \ensuremath{\mathcal N}\!\left(0\,, \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y_0)^2\, \frac{1 - e^{-2\g_k y_0}}{2\g_k} \right) \]
as $n \to \infty$, where $\g_k \coloneqq \lim_{n\to\infty} a_N \sqrt{2(1 - \l_k(N))}$.

body:
[Theorem thm:house of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] Let $(H^N_0,H^N_1)$ be as in Definition~(defHN of the paper).
    Then, conditional on the event of fixation $\{\mathcal T_1^N < \infty\}$, for $i\in\{0,1\}$, 
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[I.1)] the rescaled sequence of fixation times
        $\sigma_{\rm fix}^N:=\frac{\mathcal T_1^N}{ \varphi_N^{-1}\log N}$ converges, as $N \to \infty$, in probability to~$\frac{2(1-b)}{a}$,
      \item[I.2)] for any $\varepsilon >0$,  the sequence $H_i^N$ converges as $N\to \infty$ in probability to $h_i$, with respect to the uniform distance when restricted to the set $D^\varepsilon_i$ defined as
  \begin{equation}
  D_1^\varepsilon:= \mathbb{R}\setminus [0, \varepsilon), \qquad D_0^\varepsilon:= \mathbb{R} \setminus\left(\tfrac{2(1-b)}a-\varepsilon, \tfrac{2(1-b)}a+\varepsilon \right),  
  \end{equation}
     \item[I.3)] in the case $b=0$ the uniform convergence in probability of $H_i^N$ to $h_i$  holds on $\mathbb{R}$,
     \medskip
     \item[II)] the sequence $(H_i^N)$, viewed as random elements of $\mathcal D$,
       converges, as $N\to \infty$ in probability to~$h_i$. Hereby, $\mathcal D$ is equipped with the Skorokhod $M_1$~topology.
     \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:house of arXiv:2605.10617

[Lemma 5 ({\cite[Lemma 3.1) of arXiv:2608.28528, 'Strong solutions of SDEs with critical discontinuities in diffusion coefficients'] {RZ}}]

Let $U \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded smooth domain. Let $\{F_n=F_n(x,\omega)\}$ be a sequence of random fields in $L^2(U \times \Omega, dx \times \mathbf{P})$. 
Assume that
\begin{align}
 
& \quad \qquad \mathbf{E}\int_U \big(|F_n(x)|^2+|\nabla_x F_n(x)|^2 \big)dx   \leq K \\
 
&\qquad \qquad \mathbf{E} \int_{U} \int_0^T |D_s F_n(x)|^2 \, ds \, dx  \leq K, \\
 
&\mathbf{E} \int_{U} \int_0^T \int_0^T \frac{|D_s F_n(x) - D_{s'} F_n(x)|^2}{|s - s'|^{1 + 2\beta}} \, ds \, ds' \, dx  \leq K
\end{align}
for some $\beta>0$ and $K<\infty$ independent of $n$.
Then the sequence $\{F_n\}$ is relatively compact in $L^2(U \times \Omega)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:edges of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let $w_{ij}=p_ip_jd_{ij}$. Then $\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}=1$,
$\sum_{i<j,\,t_i\ne t_j}w_{ij}B_{ij}=0$, and
\[
  \sum_{\substack{i<j\\ t_i\ne t_j}}w_{ij}\Wnorm{B_{ij}}^2
  \;=\;2E-2\sum_{G}\Bigl(P_G\!\!\sum_{i\in G}p_i|z_i|^2
      -\Bigl|\sum_{i\in G}p_iz_i\Bigr|^2\Bigr)\ \le\ 2E ,
\]
where $G$ ranges over the classes of equal direction and
$P_G=\sum_{i\in G}p_i$. In particular some valid pair has
$\Wnorm{B_{ij}}^2\le2E$.

		\[
			\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{\log \mathbb{P}_\lambda(\mathcal{L}(r,1))}{\log r}\le \zeta.

			\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{\log \mathbb{P}_{\lambda}\big(B(r)\xleftrightarrow[]{}B(2r)^{\textsf{c}}\big)}{\log r}\leq \zeta \vee \xi.

body:
[Lemma lem:singulargap of arXiv:2505.12187, 'Speeding up quantum Markov processes through lifting'] Given an ergodic QMS generator $\mathcal{L}$ with an invariant state $\sigma \in \mathcal{D}_+(\mathcal{M})$, let $s(\mathcal{L})$ be the singular value gap of $\mathcal{L}$, $C \ge 1$ and $\nu > 0$ be constants in exponential convergence (equation ex:expdecay of the paper), and  let $t_{\rm rel}$ be the relaxation time (equation eq:trelax of the paper). Then, it holds that 
\begin{align*}
\nu \le (1 + \log C) s(\mathcal{L})\,,\quad
    t_{\rm rel} \ge  \frac{1}{2 s(\mathcal{L})}\,.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:fromfilling of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] The initial setting is defined as follows:
Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$ such that,
for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$.
Let $j_0$ be a sufficiently large positive integer
where all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Fix an initialising high-level state $\Psi_0$  with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).  
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, 
 send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and birth rate~$\lambda$  (Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)).
For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Fix $t>\tau_0$, 
 and fix a tuple  
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} = \textup{filling}$, 
$\tau^{\psi_{t-1}} = t-1$, and $z_j^{\psi_{t-1}} = 0$ where $j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.
Consider the evolution of~$V$, conditioned on
$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}$.

Define the following quantities, sets, and stopping times.
\[
\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} = \min\{t'  \geq t \colon \textup{type}^{\Psi(t')} = \textup{failure} \mbox{ or }j^{\Psi(t')} = j+1\}.\]
Let $O_0 = t-1$. For all positive integers $x$, let
\begin{align*}
I_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > O_{x-1} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via (R(item:R2 of the paper))(ii) from $j$-filling to $j$-refilling
} \}).\\
O_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > I_{x} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via  (R(item:R6 of the paper))(i) from $j$-stabilising to $j$-filling
} \}).
\end{align*}
Let 
\begin{align*} 
A &= \lceil 4(4 j)^{\phi} W_j\rceil.\\
\mathrm{Ready} &  
= \{ T'\geq t-1 \colon  
\mbox{ $\Psi(T')$ is a $j$-filling state,  
$T' + j^{24} \leq t+A$, and
$
F_j^{\Psi(T')}(T'+1) \ge \mu_j^{\overline{\gamma}} $ }
\}. 
\\
t_{\mathrm{min}} &= \min(\{t+A\} \cup \mathrm{Ready}).
\end{align*}
title: Definition def:fromfilling of arXiv:2602.21315

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.19065, 'Boundedly exchangeable graphs'] An adjacency measure on $S$ is a simple measure $\xi$ on $S^2\times\{0,1\}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item there is a simple measure $\nu$ on $S$ with $\xi(C\times\{0,1\}) = \nu^{\otimes 2}(C)$ for every $C \in \Bcal(S)^{\otimes 2}$,
    \item $(\theta \otimes \mathrm{id})\,\xi = \xi$, where $\theta(x,y)=(y,x)$ and $\mathrm{id}$ denotes the identity function on $\{0,1\}$.
\end{enumerate}
For $B\in\mathcal{B}(S)$, the $B$-restriction of $\xi$ is the adjacency measure $\xi\vert_{B \times B \times \{0,1\}}$, which we denote by $\xi\vert_B$ for brevity.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.19065

[Theorem thm:determinacy of arXiv:2605.02104, '\textbf{Chart-Generated Probability Geometry\\and Kolmogorov Expectations}'] Let $G$ be a probability coordinate chart on $I$ and let $X$ and $Y$ be
$I$-valued random variables. If
\[
\mathbb{E}\bigl((G(X))^{r}\bigr) \;=\; \mathbb{E}\bigl((G(Y))^{r}\bigr)
\qquad\text{for all } r\ge 1,
\]
then $X$ and $Y$ have the same law. Equivalently, the sequence of initial
Kolmogorov moments $\{M_{r}^{(G)}(X)\}_{r\ge1}$ determines the law of $X$
on $I$.

[Theorem thm:main_CPMRE of arXiv:2606.10257, 'Downward conditional monotonicity gives survival and extinction for contact processes in r'] Consider the CPMRE described above with increasing infection rate vector $\beta=(\beta_0,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{k-1})$, decreasing recovery rate vector $\mu=(\mu_0,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_{k-1})$, 
	and irreducible, monotone environmental process with generator matrix $T$. Let the initial environmental distribution at each site be arbitrary.	
	\begin{longlist}
		\setlength{\itemindent}{28pt}

		\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}

		$\frac{\beta^*}{\max_j\mu_j}>\lambda_c$, 
		then the CPMRE survives (strongly).
		\item If the permutation-reversed MMPP with $\widehat\mu,\widehat{T}$ is DCM and 
		$\frac{\max_j\beta_j}{\mu^*}\leq\lambda_c$,

[Theorem 15 (Lattice Fourier CLT) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] For every $\theta\in E_Y$ with $2\theta\neq0$ and every
$h_1,\ldots,h_m\in C_c^\infty(\bR^d;\bC)$, there is an $H^m$-valued complex Gaussian random element with mean zero
\[
    G_\theta
    =\bigl(G_\theta(h_1),\ldots,G_\theta(h_m)\bigr)
\]
such that
\begin{equation}

    \bigl(V_R(h_1,\theta),\ldots,V_R(h_m,\theta)\bigr)
    \dto G_\theta
    \qquad\text{in }H^m.
\end{equation}
Its covariance is determined by
\begin{equation}

    \E\!\left[
      \langle G_\theta(h_a),u\rangle_H
      \overline{\langle G_\theta(h_b),v\rangle_H}
    \right]
    =\left(\int_{\bR^d}h_a\overline{h_b}\right)
      \langle\mathcal F_Y(\theta)v,u\rangle_H,
\end{equation}
for $u,v\in H$ and $1\leq a,b\leq m$, and
\begin{equation}

    \E\!\left[
      \langle G_\theta(h_a),u\rangle_H
      \langle G_\theta(h_b),v\rangle_H
    \right]=0
\end{equation}
for all such $a,b,u,v$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Rouche's theorem: Let C be a simple closed contour (one without self-intersections) such that C together with its interior is contained in a region on which the complex-valued functions f and g are holomorphic. If |g(z)| < |f(z)| for every z on C, then f and f + g have the same number of zeros in the interior of C, each zero counted with its multiplicity. (The hypothesis forces f, and hence f + g, to have no zeros on C itself.)

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2603.28226, '2603.28226'] In the setting of Proposition~\ref{prop:global-joint-sharpness}, take $\beta=1$. Then every decomposition
\[
 f=g+h+k,
 \qquad 0\le k\le\lambda,
\]
satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P\Bigl(\sup_{n\ge1}|\mathbb E_n[g]|>0\Bigr)=1
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 \Bigl\|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|\mathbb E_n[h]-\mathbb E_{n-1}[h]|\Bigr\|_1
 \ge2(1-p)\|f\|_1.
\]
Consequently, no pair of constants $c_1<1$ and $c_2<2$ can simultaneously replace the coefficients in Theorem~\ref{thm:stein-gundy}\textup{(a)--(b)} under the same condition $0\le k\le\lambda$.

body:
[Prop cocycles into Aut(N) reduce to lattice stabiliser of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $N$ be a nilpotent Lie group of the form $\mathbb{Z}^d \ltimes N_0$ with $d \geq 3$ and $N_0$ connected simply connected, and let $\Gamma \subset N$ be a lattice and $H \subset \Gamma$ be a subgroup. Let $\Delta \subset \Aut(N)$ be a subgroup such that $\delta(H) = H$ and $\delta(\Gamma)$ is commensurable with $\Gamma$ for every $\delta \in \Delta$. Let $(X, \nu)$ be an ergodic $\SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$-system and $\alpha: \SL_d(\mathbb{Z}) \times X \to \Delta$ be a map satisfying the cocycle equation modulo inner automorphisms of $H$ in $\Delta$.

    Then there exist a finite group extension $\pi: \tilde{X} \to X$, a lattice $\Gamma' \subset N$ containing $H$ and a measurable map $\phi: \tilde{X} \rightarrow \Delta$ such that 
    $$ \phi(\gamma\cdot\tilde{x}) \alpha(\gamma,  \pi(\tilde{x})) \phi(\tilde{x})$$ belongs to $\{\delta \in \Delta : \delta(\Gamma') = \Gamma'\}$ for all $\gamma \in \SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$  and almost all $\tilde{x} \in \tilde{X}$.
title: Prop cocycles into Aut(N) reduce to lattice stabiliser of arXiv:2605.16921

[Dfn 38 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] Let $\phi:\A \to \rmM_k$ and $\psi:\A \to \rmM_\ell$ be completely positive.  A \textbf{joining} of them is a completely positive map $\theta:\A\to \rmM_{k+\ell}$ such that
\[\theta(a)[K] = \phi(a) \qquad \hbox{and} \qquad \theta(a)[L] = \psi(a) \qquad (a \in \A).\]
In particular, the \textbf{diagonal joining} is defined by
\[\rm{diag}(\phi,\psi)(a) := \left[\begin{array}{cc} \phi(a) & 0\\ 0 & \psi(a)\end{array}\right] \qquad (a \in \A).\]

Joinings of more than two completely positive maps are defined similarly.  If $\phi$ is a positive functional and $k$ is a positive integer, then we write $\phi\otimes I_k$ for the diagonal joining of $k$ copies of $\phi$.
title: Definition 38 of arXiv:2507.08909

[Proposition \cite{Trinh-Trinh-Jacobi} of arXiv:2412.01015, 'Classical beta ensembles and related eigenvalues processes at high temperature and the Mar'] Assume that the initial measure $\mu_0^{(N)}$ converges weakly to a probability measure $\mu_0$. Then the following hold.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[\rm (i)] For each $n = 1, 2,\dots,$ the sequence of moment processes $S_n^{(N)}(t) = \bra{\mu_t^{(N)}, x^n}$ converges in probability as random elements in $C([0, T])$ to a deterministic limit $m_n(t)$, which is defined inductively as the solution to the following initial value ODE
		\begin{align*}
			&m_n'(t) = -n(2c+a+b+n+1) m_n(t) + n(a+n)m_{n-1}(t)\\
			&\qquad\qquad + cn \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}m_i(t) m_{n-1-i}(t) - cn \sum_{j=1}^{n-1} m_j(t) m_{n-j}(t),\\
			&m_n(0) = \lim_{N\to \infty} \bra{\mu_0^{(N)}, x^n}, \quad (n \ge 1).
		\end{align*}
Here $m_0(t) \equiv 1$.

		\item[\rm(ii)] For any $t \ge 0$, let $\mu_t$ be the unique probability measure with moments $\{m_n(t)\}$. Then the sequence $\mu_t^{(N)}$ converges in probability to $(\mu_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ as random elements in the space of continuous maps from $[0,T]$ to the space of probability measures on $[0,1]$ endowed with the uniform topology.
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{Trinh-Trinh-Jacobi}

[Theorem 3 (=Theorem \ref{invtpoly}) of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group of rank $n$, $S$ a torus subgroup of dimension being $n-1$, $T$ a maximal torus of $G$ containing $S$, $\mu\in \chi(T)$ a primitive character of $T$ such that $S=\text{ker }\mu$, $L$ a primitive weight in the weight lattice $\mathfrak{t}^*_\mathbb{Z}$ corresponding to $\mu$ after exponentiation, and $W$ the Weyl group of $G$. Define
	\[\Phi_L:=\left(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}} wL\right)^{n(L)}\in \text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W,\]
	where $W_{[L]}$ is the stabilizer of $[L]:=\{\pm L\}\in \mathfrak{t}^*/\{\pm 1\}$, $n(L)=1$ or 2 depending on whether $\displaystyle\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL$ is $W$-invariant or $W$-anti-invariant, i.e. 
	\[\displaystyle w'(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL)=\text{sgn}(w')\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL\text{ for all }w'\in W.\] 
	Then $(G, S)$ is isotropy formal if and only if $\Phi_L\notin (f_1, \cdots, f_n)^2$, where $f_1, \cdots, f_n$ are the fundamental $W$-invariant homogeneous polynomials on $\mathfrak{t}$, i.e. $\text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W=\mathbb{R}[f_1, \cdots, f_n]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: =Theorem \ref{invtpoly}

body:
[Theorem thm2.7 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] {\rm (Cuny and Lin)}.
 
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a real strictly stationary, 
{\bf reversible} Markov chain that satisfies $\alpha$-mixing with 
$\alpha_X(n) \to 0$ at least exponentially fast as $n \to \infty$.  
Suppose
$h: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$  is a Borel function such that
\begin{equation}
\label {eq2.71}
0\ <\ E[\, [h(X_0)]^2]\ <\ \infty \indent  {\rm and} \indent E[h(X_0)]\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}
Then $\sigma^2 := E[\, [h(X_0)]^2] + 2 \cdot \sum_{k=1}^\infty E[h(X_0) \cdot h(X_k)]$
exists in $(0, \infty)$, with the sum converging absolutely (in fact with the summands
decaying at least exponentially fast); and
$n^{-1} \textrm{\rm Var}(\sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)) \to \sigma^2$ as $n \to \infty$.
Further, $(1/(n^{1/2}\sigma)) \sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k) \to N(0,1)$ in distribution as $n \to \infty$.  

   Thus, letting $\sigma_n(h) := \|\sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)\|_2$ for each $n \in \mathbb N$, 
one has that $[\sigma_n(h)]^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)$ converges in distribution
to $N(0,1)$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm2.7 of arXiv:2508.12951

The deterministic Rosenzweig-MacArthur predator-prey model is the planar autonomous dynamical system for prey density N >= 0 and predator density P >= 0 given by dN/dt = r*N*(1 - N/K) - (s*N*P)/(1 + s*tau*N) and dP/dt = -c*P + d*(s*N*P)/(1 + s*tau*N), where r > 0 is the intrinsic prey growth rate, K > 0 is the prey carrying capacity, s > 0 is the predator search rate, tau > 0 is the prey handling time, c > 0 is the predator mortality rate, and d > 0 is the conversion efficiency. In nondimensionalized coordinates, the system takes the form dN/dt = N*(1 - N/k) - (m*N*P)/(1 + N) and dP/dt = -c*P + (m*N*P)/(1 + N), where k > 0, m > 0, and c > 0.
Prey density N >= 0 and predator density P >= 0
Parameters r, K, s, tau, c, d are strictly positive constants
title: Deterministic Rosenzweig-MacArthur Predator-Prey Model

body:
[Proposition p:IntfDist of arXiv:2505.09604, 'Exceptional force, uncountably many solutions in the KPZ fixed point'] The following holds on the event $\Omega_1$: Let $\xi \in \mathbb{R}, (x_0,s) \in \mathbb{R}^2, t>s$, and assume that
        \[
        \tau_{(x_0,s)}^{\xi,-}(r) < \tau_{(x_0,s)}^{\xi,+}(r)\qquad \text{for all }r \in (s,t].
        \]
       Then, letting $\tau_t^{{\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}} = \tau_{(x_0,s)}^{\xi,{\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(t)$ for ${\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}} \in \{-,+\}$, we have
        \begin{align}
        g_{(\tau_t^-,t)}^{\xi+,R}|_{[s,t]}&=g_{(\tau_t^-,t)}^{\xi-,R}|_{[s,t]},\\
        g_{(\tau_t^+,t)}^{\xi+,L}|_{[s,t]}&=g_{(\tau_t^+,t)}^{\xi-,L}|_{[s,t]}, \qquad\text{and} \\
         g^{\xi+,R}_{(\tau_t^-,t)}(s)&=g^{\xi-,L}_{(\tau_t^+,t)}(s) = x_0.
        \end{align}
title: Proposition p:IntfDist of arXiv:2505.09604

[Definition of arXiv:2607.14332, '\textbf{ Dimers, filters, and $q$-deformed real numbers}'] Let $x>0$ be irrational, and write
\[ x = [c_1;c_2,c_3,\dots] := c_1+\frac{1}{c_2+\frac{1}{c_3+\cdots}} \]
with $c_1\ge0$ and $c_i\ge1$ for $i>1$.
Let $S_x$ be the infinite snake graph that read from right to left
consists of $c_1$ downward (leftward) steps, followed by $c_2$ upward steps,
followed by $c_3$ downward steps, followed by $c_4$ upward steps,
followed by $c_5$ downward steps, and so on.

body:
[Theorem 45 of arXiv:2609.02819, 'Adelic Points and Unramified Brauer Approximation for Classifying Stacks'] Let
\[
 (A_v)_{v\notin S}\in B\PGL_n(\bA_k^S)
\]
be an adelic family of degree-$n$ central simple algebras.  It is the
localization away from $S$ of a degree-$n$ central simple algebra over $k$ if
and only if
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{v\notin S}\inv_v(A_v)\in I_S(n).
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 B\PGL_n(k)\longrightarrow B\PGL_n(\bA_k^S)
 \quad\text{is surjective}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 I_S(n)=\frac1n\bZ/\bZ.
\end{equation}
After the computation of the unramified Brauer group in
Corollary~\ref{cor:characterfree-Brun-BG}, the same criterion governs strong
approximation with respect to $\Brun(B\PGL_n)$.

[Theorem th.Liggett of arXiv:2604.24743, 'The impact of disorder and non-convex interactions on delocalisation of height functions'] For any $d\geq 1$, any $k\geq 1$ and any $p\in (0,1)$, there exists 
$\bar p=\bar p(d,k, p) < 1$ such that the following hold. For any subset $\Lambda \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}^d}$, if $\{X_i\}_{i\in \Lambda}$ is a $k$-dependent field of Bernoulli variables satisfying $\Bb\mathbb{P}{X_i=1}\geq \bar p$, for each $ i \in \Lambda$, then if $\{Y_i\}_{i\in \Lambda}$ is an i.i.d field of Bernoulli variables with parameter $p$, one has 
\begin{align*}
\{X_i\}_{i\in \Lambda}  \text{ Stoch. dominates } \{Y_i\}_{i\in \Lambda}\,.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 0.0 from \cite{liggett1997domination}

body:
[Definition 1 (Fourier, energy and correlation dimensions) of arXiv:2606.08703, '2606.08703'] Let \(\nu\) be a nonzero finite Borel measure on \(\R^m\).  The Fourier
dimension of \(\nu\) is
\begin{equation}
\dimF(\nu)
=
\sup\bigl\{0\le s\le m:
|\wh\nu(\xi)|=O(|\xi|^{-s/2}) \text{ as } |\xi|\to\infty
\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
The energy dimension of \(\nu\) is
\[
\dimE(\nu)=
\sup\biggl\{0<s<m:
\iint |x-y|^{-s}\,d\nu(x)d\nu(y)<\infty
\biggr\}.
\]

For the dyadic interval grid on \([0,1]\), let \(\mathcal D_n\) denote the
family of dyadic intervals of length \(2^{-n}\).  The corresponding correlation
dimension is
\begin{equation}
        \dimtwo(\nu)
        =
        \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{-\log_2\sum_{I\in\mathcal D_n}\nu(I)^2}{n}.
\end{equation}
For the \(b\)-adic cube grid on \([0,1]^d\), let
\(\mathcal D_n^{b,d}\) denote the family of \(b\)-adic cubes of side length
\(b^{-n}\).  The corresponding correlation dimension is
\begin{equation}
        \dimtwo(\nu)
        =
        \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{-\log_2\sum_{Q\in\mathcal D_n^{b,d}}\nu(Q)^2}
        {n\log_2 b}.
\end{equation}
title: Fourier, energy and correlation dimensions

body:
[Definition $\gamma$-Fat-Shattering Dimension of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $X$ be a set, let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{X}$, and fix $\gamma>0$. A finite set $\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subseteq X$ is said to be $\gamma$-\emph{fat shattered} by $\mathcal{F}$ if there are $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in\mathbb{R}$ such that: for every $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m)\in\{-1,1\}^m$, there is an  $f_\sigma\in\mathcal{F}$ satisfying
\[
    \sigma_j(f_\sigma(x_j)-t_j)\ge\gamma
\]
for every $j\in[m]_+$. The $\gamma$-fat-shattering dimension $ \operatorname{fat}_{\gamma}$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is the largest such $m$.
title: $\gamma$-Fat-Shattering Dimension

body:
[Definition eq:rho_definition of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{def:berger_good}
    For $i \geq 1$, for $s$ as in \thref{def:renormalisation_scheme}, and for $c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}$ as in \thref{prop:tile_and_cell_volume_bounds}, let
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \rho_0 
        = 
        \theta 
        c_G
        /
        2^{2d + 1},
        \quad
        \rho_i 
        =
        1
        /
        \left(
            c_{\mathrm{vor}}{} 
            (i+s)^{2d}
        \right).
    \end{equation}
    
    Let $((\Tile{i}{j})_{j \geq 0})_{i \geq 0}$ be the renormalisation scheme in \thref{def:renormalisation_scheme}, and consider the associated sequence of cells $((\Cell{i}{j})_{j \geq 0})_{i \geq 0}$. 
    
    We say that a level-$0$ cell $\Cell{0}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if it contains a cluster $\goodcluster{0}{j}$ satisfying
    
    \begin{equation}
        
        \# (\goodcluster{0}{j} \cap B(\netvertex{0}{j},r_0/4))
        \geq 
        \rho_0
        r_0^d. 
    \end{equation}
    
    We call the cluster $\goodcluster{0}{j}$ the \textbf{good cluster} and we call the set $\goodsize{0}{j} = \goodcluster{0}{j} \cap B(\netvertex{0}{j},r_0/4)$ the \textbf{semi-cluster}. 
    
    For $i \geq 1$, we say that a level-$i$ cell $\Cell{i}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if at least a $\rho_i$ proportion of its \level{i{-}1} subcells are good, and  their good clusters are connected to each other inside $\mathrm{Cell}_{i,j}$ to form the cluster $\goodcluster{i}{j}$. 
    
    We call the cluster $\goodcluster{i}{j}$ the \textbf{good cluster} and we call the set $\goodsize{i}{j} = \goodcluster{i}{j} \cap \Tile{i}{j}$ the \textbf{semi-cluster}. 
    
    When the good cluster is not unique, we choose one arbitrarily.
title: Definition eq:rho_definition of arXiv:2607.18011

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, paired; one n = 60 draw per cell). The long-only stack ($\\|w\\|_1 = 1$) against the same estimator under a gross-exposure constraint $\\|w\\|_1 \\le c$ for $c \\in \\{1.5, 2\\}$ and the unconstrained sum-to-one form, all on the raw relative-metric error covariance (the cleaner is irrelevant inside the constraint). At full calibration the best finite $c$ gains $+1.00$ percent on EMIT and $+0.12$ on OCO-2 over $c = 1$ ($c = 2$: $-1.45$ / $-0.11$; $c = 1$ within one percent of the best on 29 of 40 and 30 of 30 cells). At $n = 60$ calibration rows $c = 1.5$ reads $-7.07$ / $-4.22$, $c = 2$ $-10.16$ / $-6.39$ and the unconstrained form $-63.8$ / $-18886.9$ against $c = 1$ - the $c^2$ growth of the excess-risk bound seen directly, with the unconstrained plug-in's collapse at the end of the ladder. Reading: a modest relaxation buys a little at full calibration and costs at small n, so long-only is the right default and the exposure cap is a tuning knob with a cross-validated price

[Proposition 10 (Submultiplicative pressure principle) of arXiv:2607.07014, '2607.07014'] Let \((C_n)_{n\ge1}\) be random variables such that
\begin{enumerate}
	\item \(1\le C_n\le B^n\) almost surely for a deterministic constant \(B\ge1\), and
	\item for every \(n,\ell\ge1\), there exists a random variable \(C_\ell'\) with the same law as \(C_\ell\), independent of \(C_n\), and satisfying \(C_{n+\ell}\le C_nC_\ell'\) almost surely. 
\end{enumerate}
	 Then for every \(q\in\mathbb R\), the limit \(\Lambda_C(q):=\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[C_n^q]\) exists. For \(q\ge0\), one has \(\Lambda_C(q)=\inf_{n\ge1} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[C_n^q]\), while for \(q<0\), one has \(\Lambda_C(q)=\sup_{n\ge1} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[C_n^q]\). Moreover, \(\Lambda_C\) is finite and convex on \(\mathbb R\), and \(\min\{0,q\log B\}\le\Lambda_C(q)\le\max\{0,q\log B\}\). If \(I_{C,+}(x):=\sup_{q\ge0}\{qx-\Lambda_C(q)\}\) and \(I_{C,-}(x):=\sup_{q\le0}\{qx-\Lambda_C(q)\}\), then, for every \(x\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb P(Y_n\ge x)\le -I_{C,+}(x)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb P(Y_n\le x)\le -I_{C,-}(x),
\]
where \(Y_n:=n^{-1}\log C_n\).

[Lemma LOP of arXiv:2605.16963, 'Stochastic Euler Equations with Pseudo-differential Noise: Continuous and Discontinuous Pe'] Let $r,r_{1},r_{2}\in \mathbb R$, $\mathscr{p}\in \mathbf S^{r}$,
		$\mathscr{p}_{1}\in \mathbf S^{r_{1}},\mathscr{p}_{2}\in \mathbf S^{r_{2}}$,
		and let ${\mathrm{OP}}$ be given in (equation OP define of the paper). The following results hold:
		
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{\textbf {(\arabic{enumi})}},leftmargin=0.79cm]\setlength\itemsep{0.2em} 
			\item
			
			\textup{\textbf{(Continuity of ${\normalfont{\mathrm{OP}}}$)}} For any $q,s\in \mathbb R$,
			${\mathrm{OP}}: \mathbf S^{s}\to {\rm OP}\mathbf S^s$ is one-to-one  and ${\mathrm{OP}}: \mathbf S^{s}\to \mathscr L(H^{q+s};H^{q})$ is bounded. More precisely, there
			are $\widetilde \beta ,\widetilde \alpha \in \mathbb N_{0}^{d}$ and a constant
			$C=C(s,q)>0$ such that
			\begin{align*}
				\|{\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p})\|_{\mathscr L(H^{q+s};H^{q})}\leq C(s,q)|\mathscr{p}|^{\widetilde \beta ,\widetilde \alpha ; s},
			\end{align*}
			where $|\cdot|^{\widetilde \beta ,\widetilde \alpha ; s}$ is the seminorm given in (equation OPS+seminorms of the paper).
			
			\item
			\textup{\textbf{(Adjoint)}} There is a symbol $\widetilde{\mathscr{p}}\in \mathbf S^{r}$ such that
			$$\big({\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p})\big)^{*}={\mathrm{OP}}(\widetilde{\mathscr{p}}),\quad 
			\widetilde{\mathscr{p}}\equiv \mathscr{p}\ \text{mod}\ \mathbf S^{r-1},$$
			and 
			\begin{equation*}
				\mathbf S^{r}\ni \mathscr{p}\mapsto \widetilde{\mathscr{p}}\in
				\mathbf S^{r}  \ \text{is continuous}.
			\end{equation*}
			
			
			\item 
			\textup{\textbf{(Composition)}} 
			There is a symbol denoted by $\mathscr{p}_{1}\#\mathscr{p}_{2}\in \mathbf S^{r_1+r_2}$ such that
			$${\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p}_1){\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p}_2)={\mathrm{OP}}(
			\mathscr{p}_{1}\#\mathscr{p}_{2}),\quad \mathscr{p}_{1}\#\mathscr{p}_{2}\equiv\mathscr{p}_{1}\mathscr{p}_{2} \ \text{mod}\ \mathbf S^{r_1+r_2-1},$$
			and  
			\begin{equation*}
				\mathbf S^{r_{1}}\times \mathbf S^{r_{2}}\ni (\mathscr{p}_{1},
				\mathscr{p}_{2})\mapsto \mathscr{p}_{1}\# \mathscr{p}_{2}\in
				\mathbf S^{r_{1}+r_{2}}\ \text{is bi-linear continuous},
			\end{equation*}
			
			
			\item 
			\textup{\textbf{(Commutator)}} If
			$\mathscr{p}_{1}\in \mathbf S^{r_{1}}$ and
			$\mathscr{p}_{2}\in \mathbf S^{r_{2}}$ are commuting matrices, then
			\begin{equation*}
				\big[{\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p}_{1}),{\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p}_{2})\big]\in {
					\mathrm{OP}}\mathbf S^{r_{1}+r_{2}-1}.
			\end{equation*}
		\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:LDP_wiener-chaos of arXiv:2511.22162, 'Landau Hamiltonian with Gaussian white noise potential and the asymptotics of its bottom o'] Fix a bounded open box $B$. As $\beta \to 0$, the law of $Q_\beta = (\mathrm{h}_\beta, \mathrm{Z}_\beta)$ induced on $\ccM(B)$ satisfies a LDP with rate $\beta^{2}$ and rate function $\cI$ given by
	\[\cI(q) = \frac12 \left\| \varphi \right\|_{L^2(B)}^2, \quad \text{for $q = (G\ast\varphi, -|\nabla G\ast\varphi|^2 - F\ast\varphi) \in \ccM$ with $\varphi \in L^2(B)$},\]
	and $\cI(q) = + \infty$ otherwise. More precisely, it means that for any open and closed set $O, F$ in $\ccM(B)$, one has the inequalities
	\begin{equs}
		\liminf_{\beta \to 0} \beta^{2} \log \P(Q_\beta \in O) &\geq -\inf_{q \in O} \cI(q),\\
		\limsup_{\beta \to 0} \beta^{2} \log \P(Q_\beta \in F) &\leq -\inf_{q \in F} \cI(q).
	\end{equs} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let A and B be self-adjoint operators on a complex Hilbert space H and suppose that A + B, defined on D(A) ∩ D(B), is essentially self-adjoint (for example self-adjoint) there; write C for its closure. Then for every t ∈ ℝ, e^{itC} = strong limit as n → ∞ of (e^{itA/n} e^{itB/n})^n, uniformly for t in compact intervals. If instead A and B are self-adjoint and bounded below, then e^{-t(A ∔ B)} = strong limit of (e^{-tA/n}e^{-tB/n})^n for t ≥ 0, where A ∔ B is the form sum, provided the form domains satisfy that Q(A) ∩ Q(B) is dense (Kato's theorem). For bounded operators no hypotheses beyond boundedness are needed: e^{A+B} = lim (e^{A/n}e^{B/n})^n. The hypothesis that A + B be essentially self-adjoint on D(A) ∩ D(B) is essential; the intersection can even be {0} for two self-adjoint operators, in which case the left-hand side is undefined while the right-hand side products still make sense.

body:
Of the six regular 4-polytopes only the 5-cell is locally projectively rigid (every 4-simplex is projectively equivalent to every other). The 8-cell and the 120-cell are simple and the 16-cell and the 600-cell are simplicial, so small moves of their facet hyperplanes or vertices keep the combinatorial type and their realization spaces are open sets of dimension 4 f_3 or 4 f_0, namely 32, 480, 32 and 480, all above dim PGL(5,R) = 24. The 24-cell has the expected local dimension 48 at its regular realization (Brysiewicz-Sinn, arXiv:2609.02818), also above 24. What arXiv:2609.02818 completes is the local-dimension program for regular 4-polytopes, not a rigidity classification.

Assumes: realizations in R^4 up to projective transformation
