For integers n>=2, let a_n=1/4 on even n and 1/3 on odd n. Set X_n=n^(a_n) Z for a symmetric random sign Z, and D_n=n^((1+a_n)/2). Define chi_a as the infimum of q with some alpha>0 such that sup_n E exp(alpha |X_n|/n^q)<infinity; define chi_b as the supremum of q with some N such that inf_{n>=N} Var(X_n)/n^(2q)>0. Define xi_a and xi_b in the same way using D_n for upper moments and E D_n for lower bounds. Then chi_a=1/3, chi_b=1/4, xi_a=2/3, xi_b=5/8. At every scale sqrt(Var(X_n))=D_n^2/n; both endpoint identities chi_a=2xi_a-1 and chi_b=2xi_b-1 hold, but the threshold gaps are 1/12 and 1/24. This refutes an abstract inference from scale balances to common strong exponents. These observables are NOT an iid FPP model; no FPP nonexistence or exponent theorem follows.
Abstract integer-indexed observables, not FPP passage times or geodesics
Upper bounds are uniform exponential moments; lower bounds allow a finite index cutoff
The odd and even subsequences are both unbounded
title: exact KPZ balances can coexist with unequal exponent thresholds

[Lemma lem:phi-psi of arXiv:2412.01015, 'Classical beta ensembles and related eigenvalues processes at high temperature and the Mar'] Let $\{h_n\}_{n \ge 0}$ and $\{p_n\}_{n \ge 0}$ be two sequences with $h_0 = p_0 = 1$. For $c>0$, let 
\[
	\phi(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(c)_n}{n!} h_n \frac{1}{z^{c+n}},  \quad
	\psi(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty{p_n} \frac{1}{z^{n+1}}
\]
be formal power series. Then the relation~(equation moment-MKR of the paper) is equivalent to the following relation of formal power series
\[
	\psi = -\frac1c \frac{\phi_z}{\phi}, \quad \text{or} \quad \phi_z = -c \phi \psi.
\]
Here $\phi_z$ denotes the formal derivative with respect to $z$,
\[
	\phi_z(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{-(c)_{n+1}}{n!} h_n \frac{1}{z^{c+n+1}}.
\]

For finite connected simple undirected graphs of order n let mu(G) be the second-smallest eigenvalue of the combinatorial Laplacian D-A. Fix an integer d>=3. Over graphs with minimum degree at least d, min mu(G)=(d-1+o(1))*pi^2/n^2. Over d-regular graphs, min mu(G)=(c_d+o(1))*pi^2/n^2, where c_d=d-1 for odd d and c_d=2*(d-2) for even d. The limit is n->infinity at fixed d, through nonempty admissible graph classes. For a d-regular graph the source's ordinary random-walk gap is mu(G)/d; these algebraic-connectivity constants are not already normalized random-walk gaps. Source: The maximum relaxation time of a random walk on regular graphs, Theorem 1.1, p.2; notation preceding it; proofs in Section 3.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try a direct cluster-expansion (Mayer-type) argument for the susceptibility at fixed p (2d) in the d -> infinity limit. Result: At p = lambda/(2d) the expected cluster size chi(p) has, for fixed lambda < 1, a convergent expansion as d -> infinity in powers of 1/d obtained by comparing the cluster to a branching process with Poisson(lambda) offspring and counting cycles: the first correction comes from the 4-cycles of Z^d (each pair of neighbours of a vertex shares a common neighbour with frequency ~ 1/(2d)), which gives the known a_2 = 1 through the shift of the effective branching ratio. This direct route reproduces a_1, a_2 by hand; a_3 = 7/2 requires the 6-cycle and the double-4-cycle corrections and the interplay with the self-avoidance of the exploration, and I did not complete it. Existence of the expansion to all orders without the lace expansion would need a general theorem that the non-backtracking cycle corrections form an asymptotic series, which is a version of the lace expansion in disguise (the lace expansion IS the systematic bookkeeping of these corrections); a Mayer-type expansion at fixed lambda < 1 converges for the subcritical susceptibility, and p_c is then the divergence point of the series in lambda, whose location in powers of 1/d is obtained by inverting the series, which is a purely algebraic step if the expansion of chi is known to all orders with uniform error terms. So: an alternative derivation exists in principle via the convergent subcritical cluster expansion plus inversion, but the uniformity of the subcritical expansion up to lambda near 1 is exactly the difficult point. Computing a_4 by hand would require the 8-cycle counts and the interactions of three 4-cycles; not done. Obstruction: Uniformity of the subcritical cluster expansion up to the critical point; a_4 requires third-order cycle corrections.

[Corollary COR714 of arXiv:2412.08886, 'On domination for (non-symmetric) Dirichlet forms'] Let $(\kappa,\theta)$ be a quasi-admissible pair with $\bar{\theta}(\cdot):=\theta(\cdot, \Gamma_{\kappa,\theta})$.  
A quasi-regular and local Dirichlet form $({\mathscr E},{\mathscr F})$ on $L^2(\overline{\Omega})$ is sandwiched between $(\mathbf{D},H^1_0(\Omega))$ and $({\mathscr E}^{\kappa,\theta},{\mathscr F}^{\kappa,\theta})$ if and only if there exists a quasi-admissible measure $\mu$ with the properties
\[
\begin{aligned}
	&\Gamma_{\mu}\subset \Gamma_{\kappa,\theta},\quad \mu\geq (\kappa+2\bar\theta)|_{\Gamma_{\mu}}
\end{aligned}\]
such that $({\mathscr E},{\mathscr F})=({\mathscr E}^\mu,{\mathscr F}^\mu)$,  as defined in (equation eq:73 of the paper).

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, A tree automaton with infinitely many rogue fixed points under every supercritical offspring law (October 2026), answers the question of Johnson, Podder and Skerman (Random Structures & Algorithms 56 (2020); arXiv:1808.03019, Section 6) whether a tree automaton with finitely many, but at least three, states can have infinitely many fixed points of its automaton distributional map. On states {a, b1, ..., bk}, a vertex takes state bi when exactly one of its children is in a state b and that child is in state bi, and state a otherwise. If the offspring law has generating function G and mean greater than one, the fixed points are the point mass at a and every law giving a the mass s* with G'(s*) = 1, a (k-1)-dimensional simplex (for Poisson offspring with mean lambda > 1, s* = 1 - (log lambda)/lambda); every point of the simplex is rogue. Under binary branching an example is implicit in Rozikov and Zada (arXiv:0712.3979, Theorem 2(iv)). Two states suffice when the offspring law has infinite mean; three are needed for Poisson offspring. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/automaton-fixed-simplex (commit fa1897f13cab). Not refereed.
title: Johnson-Podder-Skerman question answered: a tree automaton with finitely many states and infinitely many rogue fixed points under every supercritical offspring law (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/automaton-fixed-simplex)

body: [Thm 48 (Baues\textendash Buth) of arXiv:2608.26698, 'Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion '] There is a short exact sequence \[0 \rightarrow \mathrm{haut}(M | \dot{M}) \rightarrow \mathcal{I}^h(M) \xrightarrow{t} H_M^h \rightarrow 0.\] If $H_2(M)$ has no 3-torsion, then $\mathrm{haut}(M | \dot{M}) \cong {(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2g}$. If $H_2(M)$ has nontrivial 3-torsion, then $\mathrm{haut}(M | \dot{M}) \cong {(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2g} \oplus {(\mathbb{Z}/3)^{2s_1}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 42 (Uniqueness in law) of arXiv:2506.09637, 'Nonlinear Stochastic Filtering with Volterra Gaussian Noises'] We say that uniqueness in law holds for equation \eqref{sensor_equation} if the
following property is satisfied. Let
\[
    (Z,\mathbf I),\quad
    (\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in[0,T]},\mathbb P)
\]
and
\[
    (\widetilde Z,\widetilde{\mathbf I}),\quad
    (\widetilde\Omega,\widetilde{\mathcal F},
    (\widetilde{\mathcal F}_t)_{t\in[0,T]},\widetilde{\mathbb P})
\]
be two weak solutions of \eqref{sensor_equation}, possibly defined on different
probability spaces, with the same initial distribution. Then the laws of the
solution paths for the trace agree:
\(
    \mathcal L_{\mathbb P}(Z^{(0)})
    =
    \mathcal L_{\widetilde{\mathbb P}}(\widetilde Z^{(0)})
\)
as probability measures on the path space
\(
    C([0,T],\mathbb R^{d_Z}).
\)

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): Over R, sup_y Pr(sum_{i=1}^u c_i*eps_i = y) <= 2^{-u}*C(u, floor(u/2)) (tag 14). Over F_p the same inequality holds for nonzero coefficients when u < p - the finite-group Littlewood-Offord theorem in the no-wrap range (the F_p specialization of the optimal group inequality of Juskevicius-Semetulskis). In the application u <= r < p (15). Since p is odd the two targets b-1, b+1 are distinct, so applying (14) to each and taking a union bound gives <= 2^{1-u}*C(u, floor(u/2)) (16). body: In mathematics, the Cantor set is a self-similar set of points lying on a single line segment that has a number of unintuitive properties. It was discovered in 1874 by Henry John Stephen Smith and mentioned by German mathematician Georg Cantor in 1883. As it contrasts with a linear continuum, the Cantor set has been called the Cantor discontinuum.
title: Cantor set

[Theorem theorem7.4littlewoodchapter2 of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and fix $\alpha,\gamma\in(0,1)$, $B>0,\mu\in (0,2^{-15})$. We can find $c,R>0$ depending only on these constants so that the following holds. For $0\leq k\leq c\alpha n$ and $\epsilon\geq\exp(-c\alpha n)$, fix $v\in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ and orthogonal vectors $w_1,
\cdots,w_k\in\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$. Let $\zeta\in\Gamma_B$, $\zeta'$ be an independent copy of $\zeta$ and $Z_\mu$ a Bernoulli variable with mean $\mu$. Let $\widetilde{X}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a random vector with i.i.d. coordinates of law $(\zeta-\zeta')Z_\mu$. Then if $D_{\alpha,\gamma}(v)\geq 1/\epsilon$ then 
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P}_{\widetilde{X}}(|\langle\widetilde{X},v\rangle|\leq\epsilon\text{ and }\sum_{j=1}^k\langle \widetilde{X},w_j\rangle^2\leq ck)\leq R\epsilon\cdot e^{-ck}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theorem7.4littlewoodchapter2 of arXiv:2504.15992

[Definition 5 (Effective Rank) of arXiv:2606.25810, 'Spectral Collapse Under Geometric Alignment of Extreme Events'] Define the effective rank

\[
\operatorname{erank}(Q_n) = \frac{(\operatorname{tr} Q_n)^2}{\operatorname{tr}(Q_n^2)}.
\]

This quantity satisfies \(1 \le \operatorname{erank}(Q_n) \le n\). When \(\operatorname{erank}(Q_n) = 1\), the matrix has rank 1. When \(\operatorname{erank}(Q_n) = n\), the eigenvalues are all equal.
title: Effective Rank

body:
[Lemma l:subgaus.with.constant of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] Suppose $X$ is a real-valued random variable, mean zero, such that
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}] \le c \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{vt^2}{2}\bigg)
    \]
for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, with $c\ge1$ a constant. Then $X$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $v' \le 2cev$.
    
    
    
    

\begin{proof}
First note that for large $t$ a subgaussian bound holds, since
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}]
    \le \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{vt^2}{2} + \log c\bigg)
    \le \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg((1+M)\frac{vt^2}{2}\bigg)
    \]
as long as $|t|\ge h$, where $M>0$ is a parameter to be determined, and 
    \[h \equiv \bigg(\frac{2 \log c}{Mv}\bigg)^{1/2}\,.
    \]
We then consider $|t| \le h$.
For $a,y\in\mathbb{R}$ with $|a|\le1$, we can bound
    \[e^{ay}
    -1-ay
    \le a^2 \sum_{k\ge2}
    \frac{|y|^k}{k!}
    \le a^2 e^{|y|}
    \le a^2 (e^y + e^{-y})\,.
    \]
Since $\mathbb E [X]=0$, it follows that, for all $|t| \le h$,
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}]
    \le 1 + \frac{t^2}{h^2}\mathbb E[e^{hX} + e^{-hX}]
    \le
    1 + \frac{2}{h^2}
        { c} t^2 \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{vh^2}{2}\bigg)
    = 1 + v t^2 \frac{M  c}{\log c}
    \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{\log c}{M}\bigg)\,.
    \]
Taking $M=\log c$ gives
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}]
    \le 1 + {c} e vt^2 
    \le \mathop{\rm exp}({c} evt^2)
    \]
for all $|t| \le h$. Combining with the above bound for $|t| \ge h$ shows that $X$ is subgaussian with variance proxy
    \[v' \le 
    \max\{1+\log c, 2ce\} v = 2ce v\,,
    \]
proving the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l:subgaus.with.constant of arXiv:2607.02013

\]

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C014 v1; no specialist novelty asserted. Fix alpha>0 and 0<r<=1/10 independently of dimension d, m=ceil(alpha*d), independent real a_i~N(0,I_d), x_*=e1 and deterministic x=e1+r e2. For f(z)=sum_i[((a_i^T z)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2]/(4m), lambda_min(Hess f(x))<=-13*r^2*log(d)/(128*alpha) with probability tending to one. For each fixed C>sqrt(2), simultaneously max_i|a_i^T(x-x_*)|<=C*sqrt(log d)*||x-x_*|| with probability tending to one. Thus full-matrix positive curvature cannot follow uniformly from independent local initialization and initial relative incoherence at linear sample size. Proof outline: write a_i=(g_i,t_i,b_i) and w_i=3(g_i+r*t_i)^2-g_i^2. Select the first row with g_i in [r*sqrt(log d),1.25*r*sqrt(log d)] and t_i in [-1.25*sqrt(log d),-sqrt(log d)]. Each event has probability at least r*log(d)/(32*pi)*d^(-25*(1+r^2)/32), so a row exists with probability tending to one; its weight is at most -13*r^2*log(d)/16. Selection uses only the two signal-plane coordinates. In its independent tangent direction b_i/||b_i||, the selected contribution is negative order log(d), whereas all other contributions have conditional mean tending to 2+3*r^2 and variance tending to zero. A Gaussian maximum bound gives the initial incoherence statement. For eta=c/log d the GD derivative expands some direction by a fixed factor above one. This concerns sensitivity, not growth of the error toward the signal, and does not prove GD nonconvergence. It invalidates a uniform full-matrix positivity premise for these starts, not energy control restricted to actual trajectory directions. No distributional assertion about the sample-dependent escape-entry point is made.

[Defn 17 (Pfaffian point process) of arXiv:2512.02286, 'Pfaffian Transition Probability and Correlation Kernel of TASEP in Half-space'] Let $\mathcal{Z}$ be a set of points and let $\mu:2^\mathcal{Z}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a measure on the powerset $2^\mathcal{Z}$. This measure is called a \emph{Pfaffian point process} if there exists a matrix valued kernel $K:\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{Z}\to\mathbb{C}^{2\times 2}$ which is skew-symmetric, i.e. $K_{ij}(x,y)=-K_{ji}(y,x)$, given by
	\[K(x,y) = \left[\begin{array}{cc}
		K_{11}(x,y) & K_{12}(x,y) \\
		K_{21}(x,y) & K_{22}(x,y)
		\end{array}\right],\]
    such that correlation functions $\rho(z_1,\dotsc,z_m)\coloneqq\mu(\{A\in2^\mathcal{Z}\!:z_1,\dotsc,z_m\in A\})$ have the form  
	\begin{equation}
		
		\rho(z_1,\dots,z_m) = \pf\left[\begin{array}{cc}
			K_{11}(z_i,z_j) & K_{12}(z_i,z_j) \\
			K_{21}(z_i,z_j) & K_{22}(z_i,z_j)
		\end{array}\right]_{1\leq i,j\leq m}.
	\end{equation}
	for all finite subsets $\{z_1,\dots,z_m\}\subseteq\mathcal{Z}$.
    The kernel $K$ is known as the \emph{correlation kernel} of the process.
title: Pfaffian point process

[Lemma lem:good-degree-unified of arXiv:2607.00731, 'Sharp Asymptotics for the Largest Component in the Subcritical Regime of Preferential Atta'] There exist sequences $M_n\to\infty, \delta_n\downarrow0, \rho_n\downarrow0,$ constants $C_0<\infty$ and $\beta>0$, and sets $\mathcal D_n$ of degree sequences such that
\[
\mathbb P\bigl(d(G_{n,m}^{\alpha,\ast})\in\mathcal D_n\bigr)=1-o(1).
\]
Moreover, every $d_n\in\mathcal D_n$ satisfies 
\begin{align}
\max_{0\le k\le M_n}\Bigl|\pi_k(d_n)-\mathbb P(Y^{(n)}=k)\Bigr|&\le \delta_n,\\
\Bigl|\mu_j(d_n)-\mathbb E\bigl[(Y^{(n)})^j\bigr]\Bigr|&\le \rho_n\varepsilon \qquad (j=1,2,3),\\
\mu_4(d_n)&\le C_0,\\
\frac1n\sum_{v=1}^n d_{n,v}^r e^{\beta d_{n,v}}&\le C_0 \qquad (r=1,2,3,4).
\end{align}
Each such $d_n\in\mathcal D_n$ satisfies assumptions \textup{(1)}--\textup{(5)}
of Proposition~(prop:cp-upper of the paper) with limit law $D=Y$, and
\[
Q(d_n)=-\varepsilon+o(\varepsilon),
\]
$$R(d_n)=\frac{\alpha+2}{\alpha+1}+o(1).$$

Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: With remaining-work vector x, arrival rate lambda, and relative value V, the formal average-cost equation is g=m+lambda*E[V(x appended with S)-V(x)]-max_{sum b_i<=n} sum_i s(b_i)*partial_i V(x). Check: Between arrivals the residual of job i decreases at rate s(b_i), giving the minus sign. For linear speedup the maximization concentrates resources on the largest value gradient; this is consistent with a priority rule, not proof of which priority. Obstruction: The value gradients, boundary conditions at completion, recurrence assumptions and optimality verification remain unknown.

Let $\tau_0$ be a non-negative integer. Let $\Psi_0$ be the   initialising high-level state with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper) and let $\ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$  (Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-state-space of the paper)) be the  $\Psi_0$-closure (Definition~(def:hls-closed of the paper)) of~$\mathrm{hls}$. body: [Corollary 3.2 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] For $m,N\in\mathbb{N}$, for any permutations $\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2}\in\mathcal{P}([m])$, we have $\displaystyle N^{M(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\left|\left(\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{1}}\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{2}}\right)\left(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\right)\right|\leq N^{C(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})}.$ Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

[Proposition regularity of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields and associated function space'] Let $\alpha \in [0,1]$ be fixed. Assume that $\{X_{(x_1,x_2)}\}_{(x_1,x_2) \in \mathbb{R}^2}$ is a Gaussian stochastic field for which there exist some constants $\beta, c, R>0$ such that
  \[  \mathbb{E}[|\Delta  X_{(h_1,h_2);(x_1,x_2)}|^2] \leq c \left(\max\{|h_1|,|h_2| \}^{1-\alpha}\min\{|h_1|,|h_2| \}^{1+\alpha}\right)^{\beta}\]
  for all $(x_1,x_2)\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and $(h_1,h_2) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $|h_1| < R$ and $|h_2|<R$. Then, there exists a version $\{\widetilde{X}_{(x_1,x_2)}\}_{(x_1,x_2) \in \mathbb{R}^2}$ of $\{X_{(x_1,x_2)}\}_{(x_1,x_2) \in \mathbb{R}^2}$ for which, for all $\gamma \in [0,\frac{\beta}{2})$ and for every bounded intervals $I,J$ of $\mathbb{R}$, for all $\omega \in \Omega$, there exists a finite constant $C(\omega)>0$ such that
    \[

    \]
for every $x_1 \in I$, $x_2 \in J$ and $h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x_1+h_1 \in I$ and $x_2 + h_2 \in J$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let g be a norm on R^2 even in the first coordinate (every lattice-symmetric FPP limit-shape norm qualifies). Fix a transversal offset h and span length r, and for a dogleg from (0,0) through v = (h, j) to (0, r) consider F(j) := g((h, j)) + g((h, r-j)) (the second leg g((0,r) - v) = g((-h, r-j)) equals g((h, r-j)) by evenness). F is convex in j (a sum of compositions of g with affine maps) and satisfies F(r - j) = F(j), so it is symmetric about j = r/2 and therefore minimized there: F(j) >= F(r/2) for EVERY real j, including j < 0 and j > r. Consequence: any lower bound on the dogleg excess assumed only for the MIDPOINT-displaced point (the enclosing-ball statement as classically printed) extends free of charge to every longitudinal position at the same transversal offset - for axis-aligned spans, the 'displaced point arbitrary at its distance' reading is a theorem, not an added assumption. For tilted spans the reflection symmetry fails and the extension is genuinely false (measured deficits up to 4.5 percent at small tilts), so this reduction is exactly the boundary of what symmetry buys. Verified: zero violations over 80,000 fresh trials on four norms (weighted p-norms and a polygonal norm), worst ratio 1 + 2e-12; independently verified by its originating referee at zero violations over 5 norms x 3 scales x 5 offsets x 1401 positions.

body:
[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2511.00764, 'Further Developments on Stochastic Dominance for Convex\\ Combinations of Infinite-Mean Ra'] Let $Y_1, Y_2$ be iid random variables with distribution function $G$.

\begin{itemize}
 \item[{\rm (i)}] If $G$ is a $\mathcal{H}$-type distribution in tail beyond a point $c\in\R_{++}$, then
   $$
        \P\(\th_1 Y_1 +\th_2 Y_2 >x \) \ge \P\(\eta_1 Y_1+\eta_2 Y_2 > x \),\quad x\ge c,
   $$
   for $\bm \th, \bm\eta\in\Delta_2$ such that $\bm\th\prec_{\rm m} \bm\eta$.

 \item[{\rm (ii)}] If $G$ is a $\mathcal{H}^\ast$-type distribution in tail beyond a point $c\in\R_{++}$, then for $\bm \th\in\Delta_2$,
   $$
        \P\(\th_1 Y_1 +\th_2 Y_2 >x \) \ge \P\(Y_1>x \),\quad x\ge c.
   $$
\end{itemize}

[Definition ass:linear_mdp of arXiv:2609.00193, 'Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and'] For each step $h\in[H]$, there exist an unknown vector $\theta_h\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and an unknown vector of signed measures
$\mu_h=(\mu_h^{(1)},\ldots,\mu_h^{(d)})$ over $\mathcal{X}$ such that, for every $(x,a)\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{A}$ and every measurable set $\mathcal B\subseteq \mathcal X$,
\[
    r_h(x,a)=\langle \phi(x,a),\theta_h\rangle,
    \qquad
    \mathbb{P}_h(\mathcal B\mid x,a)=\langle \phi(x,a),\mu_h(\mathcal B)\rangle.
\]
Moreover, $\|\theta_h\|_2\le \sqrt d$ and $\|\mu_h(\mathcal X)\|\le \sqrt d$ for all $h\in[H]$.

[Lem 14 of arXiv:2608.15379, 'Stochastic Jacobi fields along discontinuous martingales on Riemannian submanifolds'] Let $(\cE,\cF)$ be a regular Dirichlet form on $L^2(E;\bdm)$ satisfying \thetag{C} for some vector field $\cH \in \mathfrak{X}(E)$. Let $\Phi_s$ be the local flow generated by $\cH$. Let $D$ be an open set and $D_1$ a relatively compact open set with $\overline{D_1}\subset D$. Fix $\delta>0$ and a compact set $K$ with $\overline{D_1} \subset K \subset D$ in such a way that
\[
\Phi_s(\overline{D_1})\subset K \ \text{for all}\ s\in [-\delta, \delta].
\]
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $s\in [-\delta, \delta]$, $\Phi_s^* \colon C_0^{\infty} (D_1) \to C_0^{\infty}(D)$ extends to an $\cE_1$-isometry from $\cF^{D_1}$ to $\cF^D$ and $s \mapsto \Phi_s^*\phi$ is $\cE_1$-continuous for $\phi \in \cF^{D_1}$ on $[-\frac{\delta}{2},\frac{\delta}{2}]$.
\item For $\phi \in \cF^{D_1}$ with $\cH \phi \in \cF^{D_1}$, there exists a sequence $\phi_k \in C_0^{\infty}(D)$ such that $\phi_k \to \phi$ and $\cH \phi_k \to \cH \phi$ as $k \to \infty$ in $\cE_1$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 1 (Independent atom-bounded entries) of arXiv:2606.25204, 'Exponential Rank Bounds for Random Matrices'] Fix \(b\in(0,1)\).  For each \(n\ge1\), let \(A=(A_{ij})\) be an
\(n\times n\) random matrix with independent real entries such that
\[
   \sup_{x\in\R}\PP\{A_{ij}=x\}\leq b<1
   \qquad (1\leq i,j\leq n).
\]
Then there exists \(c_{1.1}=c_{1.1}(b)>0\) such that for all \(n\ge1\) and
all \(1\leq k\leq n\),
\begin{equation}
   \PP\{\rank A\leq n-k\}\leq \exp(-c_{1.1}nk).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Conditional on other blocks and independent background, full auxiliary oracle has at most 2^a(n) fixed protected-variable-independent references, with a polynomial

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:64c777810b86414ca70d2d3c1a2be66c9a3cd6d556de82f8b6a0286e4e3a4117","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/64/64c777810b86414ca70d2d3c1a2be66c9a3cd6d556de82f8b6a0286e4e3a4117.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:58d0a1c13624564312f217a40a040ad33d187d5d06207c755edc8f37f97277ed","bundle_entry_key":"t410-w739-c008-v1","bundle_id":"population.t410-w739-background-obstructions-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"oracle computational complexity; weighted sampling; hidden witnesses; average-case inversion","draft":"w739/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:t410-w739-c008-v1","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Polynomial probes remove an independent fair witness background

C008 v1. Target 2. Kind: route-failure. Status: proof (unaudited).
This extends the C007 obstruction to a natural positive-background ensemble.
It does not construct the requested oracle, exclude exceptional oracles, or
claim novelty. The full common-oracle target remains OPEN.

## Ensemble and precise dependence assumptions

Use C006 v2 protected sets H_n of size h=2^floor(n/2), independent fair
bits b_y and uniform n^2-bit locations r_y, with M=2^(n^2). At y in H_n,
the witness table accepts exactly when b_y=1 and w=r_y. At each y outside
H_n, each witness answer is an independent fair bit, independently of ALL
protected variables. Blocks at different lengths are independent before the
auxiliary oracle is selected. H_n is fixed, not computed by the weight.

For each n, conditional on all other blocks AND this block's unprotected
background, the entire auxiliary oracle ranges over at most 2^a(n) reference
oracles fixed independently of the remaining protected variables. Here a(n)
is polynomial. The chosen reference may depend on those variables; union over
references rather than independence after selection is required, as in C006.
The total-reference condition concerns entire oracles, not single answers.

Then almost surely C003 A fails. More precisely, one uniform efficiently
weighted family below has the following property: every fixed uniform
polynomial-time oracle sampler approximates it within TV 1/(100L) at only
finitely many distinguished lengths. Countably many samplers can be chosen
after the oracle; this quantifier does not require an effective enumeration.

## An efficient filter and its simultaneous success event

For n>=2 take k=n^2 distinct fixed n^2-bit witnesses, the binary encodings of
0,...,k-1. Let G_n(y)=1 iff all these k witness queries at y return zero.
For a background input, Pr[G_n(y)=1]=2^(-k). By a union bound, the chance
that ANY background input passes is at most 2^n 2^(-n^2). For a protected
input with b_y=0, G_n(y)=1 always. A protected yes input fails the filter
only if r_y is one of the k probes. Consequently the probability ANY
protected yes input fails is at most h k/M. Using a bound without the
additional factor 1/2 is intentional.

Let D_n mean that no background input passes and every protected input
passes. Then

    Pr[not D_n] <= (2^n + h n^2) / 2^(n^2) = delta_n.       (1)

This bound is unconditional; we never condition the protected posterior
argument on D_n. For n>=4, n^2<=2^n and h<=2^n give
delta_n<=2^(-n^2+2n+1)<=2^(-n), a summable sequence. The inequality n^2<=2^n
starts at n=4 and is preserved since (n+1)^2<=2n^2 for n>=3. Also
n^2-3n-1>=0 for n>=4. Thus the filter succeeds at every sufficiently large
length almost surely, without assuming independence of D_n events.

## Weighted family and extraction without conditioning away hardness

At L(n)=1+n+n^2, n>=2, give dummy 0^L weight 1 and give word 1 y w
weight 4 iff G_n(y)=1 and the witness table accepts (y,w). All other
weights are zero; at nondistinguished lengths use just the dummy.
Evaluation takes k+1 oracle queries and polynomial time. Neither H_n nor
the random bits nor the auxiliary oracle's chosen reference is hardcoded.

On D_n this law is EXACTLY the C007 law supported on the dummy and the
protected yes witnesses. No approximate-normalizer argument is needed.
Let E_n denote that a fixed sampler S has TV error at most tau=1/(100L)
for this weight family. On each fixed oracle in E_n intersect D_n, the
coupon-and-TV extraction of C007 applies: run S independently
t=6h(n+2) times, verify both G_n and the witness predicate on every output,
and guess one precisely for observed verified protected witnesses. The
procedure need not recognize H_n to run; its output can be restricted to
the fixed protected coordinates when analyzing success. It has at most
floor(h/8) errors with probability at least 15/16. The s=0 case yields
the all-zero vector immediately. The C007 calculation uses only the
distribution on this fixed oracle, so this implication is valid on E_n
intersect D_n and assumes nothing about its probability or independence.

If each call of S makes at most q(n) witness queries, verification adds
at most k+1 per sample. Hence total direct witness queries are at most

    Q=6h(n+2)(q(n)+n^2+1).

For fixed sampler random tapes, fix all independent background information
and other blocks and apply the C006 posterior bound to each reference oracle.
The C007 Hamming-ball union bound gives unconditional learner success at
most

    2^(a(n)-h/4) (1+1/M)^Q <= 2^(a(n)-h/4) exp(Q/M).       (2)

Average over tapes and over the fixed independent background afterwards.
It would be invalid to assert the posterior factorization after conditioning
on E_n or D_n. Instead success conditional on each oracle in E_n intersect
D_n is at least 15/16, so (2) implies

    Pr[E_n] <= delta_n + (16/15) 2^(a(n)-h/4) exp(Q/M).     (3)

For any fixed polynomial q and a, the second term is summable: Q/M tends
to zero and a(n)<=h/8 eventually, so it is eventually bounded by a constant
times 2^(-h/8). The first term is summable by (1). Tail union bounds show
E_n happens infinitely often with probability zero. A countable union over
all uniform polynomial-time samplers preserves this conclusion. In
particular no such sampler works eventually at every distinguished length,
which contradicts C003 A for this explicit weight family. This proves the claim.

## Consequence and remaining construction

Adding independent fair background witnesses does not repair the small-total-
leakage protected-block construction. The weights themselves can filter it
away; uniformity of the weights and secrecy of H_n do not prevent this.
The conclusion is almost-sure for this ensemble, not universal over all
oracles. Other background distributions, larger dependent interfaces, and
exceptional oracles remain unexcluded. The unprotected background was fixed
independently of the protected variables, so C006 still supplies circuit
hardness under the stated leakage hypothesis; A is what fails here.

A promising next distinction is sparse unique-witness background: polynomial
zero probes then do not isolate the protected set. This is only a proposed
next route, not a construction satisfying A/B or a claim that no other filter
exists. The missing obligations are still weighted-mass stability under all
uniform oracle weight families and compatible final sampling/inversion

body: In mathematics, the Euler–Maclaurin formula is a formula for the difference between an integral and a closely related sum. It can be used to approximate integrals by finite sums, or conversely to evaluate finite sums and infinite series using integrals and the machinery of calculus. For example, many asymptotic expansions are derived from the formula, and Faulhaber's formula for the sum of powers is an immediate consequence.
title: Euler–Maclaurin formula

body: The Poincare conjecture states that every closed (compact, boundaryless) simply connected 3-dimensional topological manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere S^3; equivalently, S^3 is the only closed 3-manifold, up to homeomorphism, with trivial fundamental group. Posed by Henri Poincare in 1904, it was proved in 2002-2003 by Grigori Perelman, who established the stronger Geometrization conjecture of William Thurston using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow with surgery. The higher-dimensional generalized Poincare conjecture was proved earlier, for n >= 5 by Smale and for n = 4 by Freedman.
title: Poincare conjecture

[Defn 4 (Test curves and maximality) of arXiv:2609.03296, 'Nonuniqueness of Model Potentials and Weak Geodesic Rays'] A test curve is a family
\[
 (\psi_\tau)_{\tau\in\RR},
 \qquad
 \psi_\tau\in\PSH(X,\omega)\cup\{-\infty\},
\]
such that, for every \(x\in X\), the function
\(\tau\mapsto\psi_\tau(x)\) is upper semicontinuous, concave, and decreasing,
while \(\psi_\tau=0\) for all sufficiently negative \(\tau\) and
\(\psi_\tau\equiv-\infty\) for all sufficiently positive \(\tau\).
The test curve is maximal if every finite slice is a normalized model
potential:
\[
 P_\omega[\psi_\tau]=\psi_\tau
 \qquad\text{whenever }\psi_\tau\not\equiv-\infty.
\]
title: Test curves and maximality

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The measurable functions have the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f:X\to Y$ is measurable and $g:Y\to Z$ is continuous, $g\circ f$ is measurable.

\item If $f,g:X\to\mathbb R$ are both measurable and $h:\mathbb R^2\to Y$ is continuous, then the function $x\to h(f(x),g(x))$ is measurable. 

\item $f:X\to\mathbb C$ is measurable precisely when $Re(f),Im(f):X\to\mathbb R$ are measurable. In this case, the function $|f|:X\to\mathbb R$ is measurable too.

\item If $f,g:X\to\mathbb C$ are measurable, then so are $f+g,fg:X\to\mathbb C$. 
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma 2 (Path-event total-variation comparison) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $P$ be a Markov transition matrix on a finite state space, and let $\eta$ and $\zeta$ be two initial laws.  For any integer $b\ge0$, the laws on paths $(X(0),\ldots,X(b))$ generated from $\eta$ and $\zeta$ differ in total variation by at most $\|\eta-\zeta\|_{\TV}$.  Consequently, for every event $B$ measurable with respect to $(X(0),\ldots,X(b))$,
\[
        \left|\Pbb_\eta(B)-\Pbb_\zeta(B)\right|
        \le \|\eta-\zeta\|_{\TV}.
\]
In particular, if $B$ is the event that a block of length $b$ contains at least one new entry into $A_n$, then its probability from an initial law within $\varepsilon$ of stationarity differs from its stationary probability by at most $\varepsilon$.

[Cor 101 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] Let $I_1$, \dots, $I_r$ be finite index sets, and for each $i$ let $\bf{x}_i$ and $\bf{y}_i$ be two $I_i$-tuples such that $H(\bf{x}_i;\bf{y}_i)$ is nonempty.  Let $j \in \{1,2,\dots,r\}$ and let $z \in X$.  Then the kernel
\[\prod_{i<j}m(\,\cdot\mid \bf{x}_i;\bf{y}_i)\times m(\,\cdot\mid \bf{x}_j,z;\bf{y}_j,w)\times \prod_{i > j}m(\,\cdot\mid \bf{x}_i;\bf{y}_i) \qquad (w \in H(\bf{x}_j;\bf{y}_j)z)\]
is a disintegration of the measure
\[\prod_{i=1}^r m(\,\cdot \mid \bf{x}_i;\bf{y}_i)\]
over the map
\[(g_1,\dots,g_r)\mapsto g_jz.\]

h_l(\mathbb{Q}|\mathbb{B})\geq \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}} \Big[ \int_0^1 tr(G(s,X)) -l -\log(\det G(s,X) ) ds\Big].
\end{split}\end{equation}

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2608.22693, 'Uniformity of extremal behaviour along geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\gamma \in (0,2)$ and $\alpha \in [-2,2]$ and let $h$ be a whole-plane GFF. 
Then, with $\Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}, \Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{Euc}}, \Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{LQG}}, \chi, \chi', \alpha_{\mathrm{min}}$, and $\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}$ being as in Proposition \ref{prop:zero_one_law}, the following holds almost surely. For any $D_h$-geodesic $P\colon [0,T]\rightarrow \CC$ parametrised by $D_h$-length and any $[s,t]\subseteq (0,T)$, we have
\begin{enumerate}
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}(P\lvert_{[s,t]})\leq\Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}$,
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}(P\lvert_{[s,t)}\cap \cT_h^{\alpha})\leq \Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}_{\alpha}$ and $\dim_{\mathrm{LQG}}(P\lvert_{[s,t]}\cap \cT^\alpha_h)\leq\Delta^{\mathrm{LQG}}_{\alpha}$,
  \item 
  $\chi(P\lvert_{[s,t]})\geq\chi$ and $\chi'(P\lvert_{[s,t]})\leq\chi'$,
  \item 
  $\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}(P|_{[s,t]}) \leq \alpha_{\mathrm{max}}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{min}}(P|_{[s,t]}) \geq \alpha_{\mathrm{min}}$.
 \end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem 1 (Validity after discovery) of arXiv:2608.30916, 'Selection-Aware Stress Testing for Interactive Agents'] Condition on the discovery data $\mathcal F_{\Dcal}$. For a finite
predeclared family, suppose the confirmation cluster vectors
$H_k=(H_{k,m}:m\in\Jcal_0)$ are conditionally independent and
identically distributed. Let
$\widehat\Delta_m=F_m(N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N H_{k,m})$,
$\mu_m=\E(H_{1,m}\mid\mathcal F_{\Dcal})$, and
$\Delta_m=F_m(\mu_m)$, where $H_{k,m}$ contains every weighted
numerator and denominator, every selector input, and both sides of the
paired contrast. Assume bounded density ratios, denominators bounded
away from zero, continuously differentiable $F_m$ near $\mu_m$, finite
cluster second moments, a finite-dimensional Lindeberg condition,
conditional covariance converging to $\Sigma$, and positive limiting
variances for reported coordinates. Then
$\sqrt N(\widehat\Delta_m-\Delta_m:m\in\Jcal_0)$ is asymptotically
Gaussian, and the cluster Gaussian multiplier consistently
approximates its joint law. Pointwise intervals and signed
simultaneous bands have asymptotic conditional coverage, including for
a coordinate highlighted after inspecting the protected family. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Validity after discovery

body:
[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Fix $T>0$ and let $\eta_t$ be a random finite signed measure on $\R^d$ for each $t\in[0,T]$.
Assume that for every fixed test function $f\in C_b^2(\R^d)$, the real
process
\begin{equation*}
t\mapsto \langle \eta_t,f\rangle
\end{equation*}
is a continuous semimartingale admitting a decomposition
\begin{equation}

\langle \eta_t,f\rangle
=
\langle \eta_0,f\rangle + \int_0^t \langle \eta_s, \mathcal G_s f\rangle ds + M_t(f),
\end{equation}
where $(\mathcal G_s)_{s\in[0,T]}$ is a (possibly random, but progressively measurable) family of linear operators on $C_b^2(\R^d)$
and $M_t(f)$ is a continuous martingale.
\\~\\
Let $\psi \colon [0,T]\times\R^d\to\R$ be deterministic with $\psi\in
C^1\left([0,T];C_b^2(\R^d)\right)$, i.e., $t\mapsto
\psi_t=\psi(t,\cdot)$  is $C^1$ into $C_b^2$. Then, $\langle \eta_t,\psi_t\rangle$ is a continuous semimartingale and satisfies
\begin{equation}

d\langle \eta_t,\psi_t\rangle
=
\langle \eta_t,\partial_t\psi_t\rangle dt
+\langle \eta_t,\mathcal G_t\psi_t\rangle dt
+dM_t(\psi_t).
\end{equation}

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] Suppose that $J$ is a bipartite graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and no $\Delta$-regular connected components.
  Suppose further that $J$ has a bipartition $V(J) = A \cup B$ such that $\deg a = \Delta$ for every $a \in A$.
  Then, the characteristic function of $B$ is the unique largest fractional independent set of $J$.

body:
Let f ∈ C^2(R) with f''(s) > 0 for all s, and let u_l, u_r ∈ R with initial datum u0(x) = u_l for x < 0 and u0(x) = u_r for x > 0. The unique Kruzhkov entropy solution of u_t + f(u)_x = 0 is: (a) if u_l > u_r (shock): u(x,t) = u_l for x < σ t and u(x,t) = u_r for x > σ t, with σ = ( f(u_l) - f(u_r) ) / ( u_l - u_r ); this jump satisfies the Lax inequalities f'(u_l) > σ > f'(u_r); (b) if u_l < u_r (rarefaction wave): u(x,t) = u_l for x ≤ f'(u_l) t, u(x,t) = (f')^{-1}( x/t ) for f'(u_l) t ≤ x ≤ f'(u_r) t, u(x,t) = u_r for x ≥ f'(u_r) t; this function is continuous on t > 0 and Lipschitz away from t = 0. (c) if u_l = u_r the solution is constant. For Burgers' equation f(u) = u^2/2 these read: shock speed (u_l+u_r)/2 when u_l > u_r, and the rarefaction u = x/t between the lines x = u_l t and x = u_r t when u_l < u_r. Both solutions are self-similar: u(x,t) = U(x/t).
f ∈ C^2 with f'' > 0 everywhere (genuine nonlinearity); for nonconvex f the Riemann solution is a composite of shocks and rarefactions given by the convex/concave hull construction
initial datum exactly the two-state Riemann datum
entropy (Kruzhkov / Oleinik) admissibility is what excludes the nonphysical expansion shock when u_l < u_r

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] When playing with a biased coin, your winning law is
$$b_p=(1-p)\delta_0+p\delta_1$$
called Bernoulli law of parameter $p\in[0,1]$. When playing $n$ times, your winning law is
$$b_{np}=\sum_{s=0}^n\binom{n}{s}p^s(1-p)^{n-s}\delta_s$$
called binomial law of parameter $p\in[0,1]$. We have the formula $b_{np}=b_p^{*n}$.

Load-bearing hypothesis: a local regularity condition (Dini, Holder, bounded variation), not mere continuity. The evaluation functionals $f\mapsto S_Nf(0)$ on $C(\mathbb T)$ have norms equal to the Lebesgue constants $\|D_N\|_{L^1}=\frac4{\pi^2}\log N+O(1)\to\infty$, so by Banach-Steinhaus the set of continuous $f$ with $\sup_N|S_Nf(0)|=\infty$ is a dense $G_\delta$ in $C(\mathbb T)$; du Bois-Reymond (1873) gave the first explicit example. Kahane-Katznelson: for every set $E\subset\mathbb T$ of measure zero there is a continuous $f$ whose Fourier series diverges at every point of $E$. Kolmogorov (1926): there is $f\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ whose Fourier series diverges at every point. What is true: Carleson (1966) - $f\in L^2(\mathbb T)$ implies $S_Nf\to f$ a.e.; Hunt - the same for $L^p$, $p>1$; Riesz - $S_Nf\to f$ in $L^p$ for $1<p<\infty$, but this fails in $L^1$ and in the uniform norm; Fejer - $\sigma_Nf\to f$ uniformly for continuous $f$. Also note convergence in norm does not repair the pointwise picture near a jump: for a function with a jump $J$, the partial sums overshoot by $\big(\frac1\pi\int_0^\pi\frac{\sin t}{t}dt-\frac12\big)J\approx0.0895\,J$ on each side (Gibbs phenomenon), so $\|S_Nf-f\|_\infty$ does not tend to 0 even though $\|S_Nf-f\|_2\to0$.

[2 4 of arXiv:2607.12303, 'Marginal Stationary Distributions and Convergence Rates of Higher Order Markov Chains'] {\rm \cite{HanXu26}}
Suppose that  $\{X_t \}_{t=1}^{\infty}$ is  an $(m-1)$th order Markov chain on the state space $S$ with a transition tensor $\cal P$. If the chain is regular, then there exists 
$\pi \in \mathbb R^n$ satisfying $\pi_i > 0$ for each $i \in S$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n \pi_i = 1$ such that 
\be

\lim_{k \to \infty} p^{(k)}_{ii_2\ldots i_m}=\pi_i, \ \ \ \  \forall i_2, \ldots, i_m \in S.
\ee 
Moreover, 
\be

\lim_{t \to \infty} \xi_{i}^{(t)} = \lim_{t \rightarrow \infty}\Pr(X_t=i)=\pi_i, \ \ \ \  \forall i \in S,
\ee
regardless of the initial probability distributions of $(X_{m-1}, \ldots, X_1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 47 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] For every $\kappa>1$, the solution in
	\eqref{eq:shifted-omega-eqn} exists and is
	unique for every $\zeta\in\R$. The map
	$\zeta\mapsto\chi_\kappa(\zeta)$ is nondecreasing and is strictly
	increasing wherever it is positive. Moreover:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
		\item For every $\alpha>0$, there is a unique
		$\omega_{\alpha,\kappa}<\sqrt2$ satisfying
		\begin{equation}
			\mathcal E_\kappa(\omega_{\alpha,\kappa})=\alpha.
		\end{equation}
		Define $\zeta_{\alpha,\kappa}
		:=c_\kappa m(\omega_{\alpha,\kappa})-\omega_{\alpha,\kappa}$.
		Then $\chi_\kappa(\zeta_{\alpha,\kappa})=\alpha$ and
		\begin{equation}
			\zeta_{\alpha,\kappa}>0
			\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
			\alpha>\alpha_\star(\kappa).
		\end{equation}
		
		\item For every $\zeta\in\R$,
		$$
		\sup_{\substack{f\in L^2(\nu),\ f\ge0\\f\not\equiv0}}
		\frac{\left(\int(x+\zeta)f(x)\,d\nu(x)\right)_+^2}
		{\int f(x)^2\,d\nu(x)
			+c_\kappa\left(\int f\,d\nu\right)^2}
		=\chi_\kappa(\zeta).
		$$
		In particular, $\alpha_\star(\kappa)=\chi_\kappa(0)$.
		
		\item For all $\kappa > 1$ we have
		$0\le\alpha_\star(\kappa)\le1/2$, with
		$\alpha_\star(\kappa)\to0$ as $\kappa\to\infty$ and
		$\alpha_\star(\kappa)\to1/2$ as $\kappa\to 1$.
	\end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition proppoubelle of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] For all $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N} $ let $\xi_p$, $c_p$, $\phi_p$, $\Lambda^{\!(p)}\! = \! (\Lambda^{{\! (p)}}_{n})_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$, $\varrho_p$ and 
$\Lambda_{\varnothing}^{\!(p)}\! = \! (\Lambda^{{\! (p)}}_{\varnothing, n})_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ be as in Definition (meaGWregedef of the paper). Further suppose that $\xi_p$ is proper for all $p\in\mathbb{N}$. 
We assume that, as $p \!\rightarrow \! \infty$,
\begin{compactenum}
\smallskip
\item[$(a)\!$] $F_{\xi_p,c_p,\Lambda^{{\! (p)}} } \!\!  \rightarrow \! F$ pointwise on $[0,1]\! \times\! \mathbb{R}_+$, for 
a limit $F\! \not \equiv\!  0 $ that is continuous at the point $(1,0)$;
\smallskip
\item[$(b)\!$] $\phi_p \! \rightarrow\! \phi$ pointwise on $\mathbb{R}_+$, for a limit $\phi$ that is continuous in a neighbourhood of $0$;
\smallskip
\item[$(c)\!$] $F^\varnothing_{\!\! \varrho_p,\Lambda^{{\! (p)}}_{\varnothing, \cdot} } \!\! \rightarrow \! F^\varnothing$
pointwise on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}_+$, for a limit $F^\varnothing$ that is continuous at the point $(1,0)$.
\smallskip
\end{compactenum}
Then there are admissible GW parameters $(\xi,c,\phi,\Lambda ,\varrho,\Lambda_{\varnothing})$ as in Definition (meaGWregedef of the paper) such that 
the convergence $P_{\! \! \xi_p ,c_p,\phi_p,\Lambda^{{\! (p)}} \!\! ,\, \varrho_p,\Lambda^{{\! (p)}}_\varnothing }$ $\! \rightarrow \! 
P_{ \xi,c,\phi,\Lambda ,\varrho,\Lambda_{\varnothing}}$ holds  weakly
in $(\mathbb{T}_{\! c}^1,{\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GHP}})$. 

Moreover, the same result holds true for unmeasured GW forests: If $c_p\varphi_{\xi_p} \! \to \! F$  pointwise on $[0,1]$ with $F\! \not \equiv\!  0 $ continuous at the point $1$, and if $\varphi_{\varrho_p} \! \to \! f$ pointwise on $[0,1]$ with $f$ continuous at the point $1$, then 
there are admissible GW parameters $(\xi,c,\varrho)$ as in Definition (meaGWregedef of the paper) such that the convergence 
$\texttt P_{ \xi_p ,c_p, \varrho_p}$ $\! \rightarrow \! 
\texttt P_{ \xi,c, \varrho}$ holds  weakly
in $(\mathbb{T}_{\! c}^0,{\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GH}})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let X = (X_t)_{t in [0, T]} be a cadlag stochastic process belonging to D^{1, 2} at each time t. Define the running supremum M_T = sup_{0 <= t <= T} X_t. If for a countable dense sequence (t_k)_{k >= 1} in [0, T] the finite approximations F_n = max_{1 <= k <= n} X_{t_k} satisfy sup_{n >= 1} ||D F_n||_{L^2} < infinity, then M_T belongs to D^{1, 2}. Furthermore, D_t^{(1)} M_T = D_t^{(1)} X_tau * 1_{[0, tau]}(t), where tau = inf{t in [0, T] : X_t = M_T} is the first time the process attains its supremum, and D_{t, z}^{(2)} M_T = sup_{0 <= s <= T} (X_s + J_{t, z} 1_{t < s}) - M_T.
X_t in D^{1, 2} for all t in [0, T]
sup_n ||D F_n|| < infinity

body:
[Corollary 22 of arXiv:2607.28578, 'On two differing geometric descriptions of the passage from microscopy to macroscopy in Ma'] Let $u_{\rho}=\grad\log(\rho/\pi)$. The Wasserstein and Stein entropy law tangents agree at $\rho$ if and only if
	\[
		\Mop_{\rho}u_{\rho}=u_{\rho}.
	\]
	They determine the same unparametrised entropy trajectory on a region if $\Mop_{\rho}u_{\rho}=a(\rho)u_{\rho}$ for a positive function $a$. Their instantaneous entropy dissipations agree if and only if
	\begin{equation}
		\langle u_{\rho},\Mop_{\rho}u_{\rho}\rangle_{L^2(\rho)}=\|u_{\rho}\|_{L^2(\rho)}^2.
	\end{equation}
	Equality in \eqref{entropy-dissipation-comparison-eq} need not imply equality of the law tangents.

body: [Definition 3 (Scalar quantizer) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] A $b$-bit scalar quantizer is a map $Q:\R\to\mathcal C=\{c_1,\dots,c_L\}$, $L=2^b$, defined by decision boundaries $-\infty=b_0<b_1<\cdots<b_L=+\infty$ and reproduction points $c_i$, with $Q(x)=c_i$ for $x\in(b_{i-1},b_i]$. It factors into an \emph{encoder} $\alpha:\R\to\{1,\dots,L\}$ storing the index ($b$ bits) and a \emph{decoder} $\beta$ mapping indices to $\mathcal C$. Its distortion is $D=\E[(X-Q(X))^2]$.
title: Scalar quantizer

body:
[Lemma 14 (Explicit log-annular mollifier) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty((0,1))$ satisfy
\[
  \varphi\ge0,\qquad \int_0^1\varphi(r)\dd r=1.
\]
For $\delta\ge2$, $\eps\in(0,1)$, put $L_\delta:=\log\delta$. For $y\ne0$, define
\[
  r_{\delta,\eps}(y):=\frac{\log(\eps/|y|)}{L_\delta}
\]
and
\begin{equation}
  \psi_{\delta,\eps}(y)
  :=\frac{1}{2L_\delta |y|}\,\varphi\!\left(r_{\delta,\eps}(y)\right),
  \qquad y\ne0,
\end{equation}
while setting $\psi_{\delta,\eps}(0)=0$. Then
\[
  \psi_{\delta,\eps}\in C_c^\infty(\R),\qquad
  \psi_{\delta,\eps}\ge0,
  \qquad
  \int_\R\psi_{\delta,\eps}(y)\dd y=1,
\]
and
\[
  \supp\psi_{\delta,\eps}\subset\{y:\eps/\delta<|y|<\eps\}.
\]
Moreover, there exists a constant $C_\varphi>0$, independent of $\delta$ and $\eps$, such that
\begin{align}
  \|\psi_{\delta,\eps}\|_\infty
  &\le C_\varphi\frac{\delta}{\eps\log\delta}, \\
  \|\psi_{\delta,\eps}'\|_\infty
  &\le C_\varphi\frac{\delta^2}{\eps^2\log\delta}, \\
  \|\psi_{\delta,\eps}''\|_\infty
  &\le C_\varphi\frac{\delta^3}{\eps^3\log\delta}. 
\end{align}
Finally,
\begin{equation}
  0\le \psi_{\delta,\eps}(y)
  \le \frac{C_\varphi}{|y|\log\delta},
  \qquad \eps/\delta<|y|<\eps.
\end{equation}

[Proposition 22 (Abstract polynomial cutoff technique) of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Let \(d\) be a discrepancy satisfying \eqref{eq:target-comparison}.
Let $A,B,c>0$ and $L \ge 0$.  Suppose that
$a_N\in(0,1]$ and $b_N\in[0,1]$, with $a_N,b_N\to0$, and
\begin{align}
    \E d(\mu_t^N,\mu_t)&\le A\{a_Ne^{Lt}+b_N\},
      \\
    \E d(\mu_t^N,\pi)&\le B\{e^{-ct}+b_N\},
      \\
    d(\mu_t,\pi)&\le Be^{-ct}.
      
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{t\ge0}\E d(\mu_t^N,\mu_t)
    \le C_{\mathrm{cut}}\{a_N^{c/(L+c)}+b_N\},
\end{equation}
where $C_{\mathrm{cut}}$ depends only on $A,B$, and
$C_{\mathrm{tar}}$.  For $d=\KSD_\pi$ or $d=W_2$, the constant in
\eqref{eq:target-comparison} can be taken to be $1$; for $d=W_2^2$, it can
be taken to be $2$.

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] Let $I$ denote a uniformly random independent set in $\Qp$ and let $\hat{I}$ denote the output of $\AS$,
given that $\AS$ does not fail.
Let $S$ denote the random subset of $\cE$ given by $I \cap \cE$, conditioned on $I \cap \cE \in \Sep$.
Let $\hat{S}$ denote the random subset of $\cE$ given in step \ref{step:fail2_shatconstruct} of $\AS$, conditioned on choosing
$\cH = \cE$ in step \ref{step:hpick} (and on $\AS$ not failing).
If $\TVbin{S}{\hat{S}} \pto 0$ and the analogous statement holds for $\cO$, then $\TVbin{I}{\hat{I}} \pto 0$ as well.

body:
[Prop Prop_finite N formula of arXiv:2608.23156, 'Disc counting statistics of the real Ginibre ensemble'] Let $N=2n$ be a positive even integer and let $R\in[0,\infty]$. For $t,u \in \mathbb{R}$, define 
\begin{align}
  \mathbf{A}_N(t;R)
    &:=
    (e^{2t}-1)\mathbf{M}_N(R)
    -
    (e^{2t}-e^t)\mathbf{E}_{N,1}(R),  
   \\
      \mathbf{B}_N(u;R)
    &:=
    (e^{2u}-1)
    \Big(
        \mathbf{L}_N(R)
        -
        \mathbf{M}_N(R)
        -
        \mathbf{E}_{N,2}(R)
    \Big). 
\end{align}  
Then we have
    \begin{align} 
        \mathbb{E}\Big[e^{t \mathcal{N}_N^{\rm r}(R) + u \mathcal{N}_N^{\rm c}(R)}\Big] = \det \Big[ \mathrm{Id}_n + \mathbf{A}_N(t;R) + \mathbf{B}_N(u;R) \Big].
    \end{align}
Consequently, for nonnegative integers $p$ and $q$ with $p+q\geq1$, we have 
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{split} 
    \kappa_{p,q}
        \bigl(
            \mathcal{N}_N^{\rm r}(R),
            \mathcal{N}_N^{\rm c}(R)
        \bigr)
    &=    p!\,q!\,[t^p u^q] \operatorname{Tr}\log \Big[ \mathrm{Id}_{n} + \mathbf{A}_N(t;R) + \mathbf{B}_N(u;R) \Big]. 
        \end{split}
    \end{equation}
Here, $[t^pu^q]f(t,u)$ denotes the coefficient of $t^pu^q$
in the Taylor expansion of $f$ about $(t,u)=(0,0)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textbf{Finite-$N$ representation of joint cumulants}

[Theorem thm:coordinate-naturality of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Consider two reference models satisfying
Assumption~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper), and denote their reference processes
by $X^{(1)}$ and $X^{(2)}$.  Suppose that there are mutually inverse
maps $\Phi,\Psi$, jointly continuous on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$, such that, for
every $t>0$, $\Phi_t$ is a global $C^2$ spatial diffeomorphism with inverse
$\Psi_t$, and
$
 \Phi,\Psi\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}((0,T]\times\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)
$
in the positive-strip sense.  Assume
$x_{0,2}=\Phi_0(x_{0,1})$ and
\begin{align}
 a_2(t,\Phi_t(x))
 &=D_x\Phi_t(x)a_1(t,x)D_x\Phi_t(x)^\top,
 \\
 b_2(t,\Phi_t(x))
 &=\partial_t\Phi_t(x)+D_x\Phi_t(x)b_1(t,x)
   +\tfrac12a_1(t,x):D_x^2\Phi_t(x).
 \notag
\end{align}
Define the source and Hessian maps by
\begin{equation}
 (\mathsf J_0F)(t,\cdot)=F(t,\cdot)\circ\Psi_t,\qquad
 (\mathsf J_2H)(t,\cdot)=(D_x\Psi_t)^\top
   (H(t,\cdot)\circ\Psi_t)D_x\Psi_t.
 
\end{equation}
Then, for every interval $I$ and regular weight $w$, these maps are unitary
on the corresponding source and Hessian-matrix spaces.  In addition,
$
 (\Phi_t)_\#\mu_t^{(1)}=\mu_t^{(2)},\,
 S_I^{(2)}\mathsf J_0=\mathsf J_0S_I^{(1)}.
$
Moreover, the optimal constants agree:
\begin{equation}
 C_{w,I}(X^{(1)})=C_{w,I}(X^{(2)})\quad\text{in }[0,\infty].
 
\end{equation}
If this common value is finite, the bounded realizations satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf T_{w,I}^{(2)}\mathsf J_0=\mathsf J_2\mathsf T_{w,I}^{(1)}.
 
\end{equation}
title: Theorem thm:coordinate-naturality of arXiv:2608.16119

body: [Lemma 40 (Extremality of the Delaunay graph) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group and $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space. Let $Y$ be a Poisson point process on $X$ with intensity $c \, {\rm vol}_X$ for some $c>0$. Let $Y_0=Y \cup \{o\}$ and let ${\rm Vor}(Y_0)$ be the associated Voronoi diagram. Let $\mathcal G$ denote the Delaunay graph associated to ${\rm Vor}(Y_0)$, and let $\rho$ be the vertex of $\mathcal G$ corresponding to the cell of the origin. Then the law of $(\mathcal G,\rho)$ is an extremal unimodular probability measure.

[Lem 91 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] The defining polynomials of $X$ can be written as
\[
\begin{split}
\msF_1 &= t s + w f_2 + f_6, \\
\msF_2 &= t^2 z + t g_5 + w^2 + g_8,
\end{split}
\]
where $f_i \in \mbC [x, y, z]$ and $g_i \in \mbC [x, y, z, s]$.
Moreover, we have $f_6 (0, y, z) \ne 0$ and either $s^2 y \in g_8$ or $s^2 z \in g_8$.

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] For a set $S \sse \cH$ and a dimer $\fd$, we write $\fd \sim S$ if $\fd$ shares a neighbor with a vertex in $S$.
Note that this includes the case where $S$ contains a vertex of $\fd$ itself.
Now for $S \sse \cH$, define
\begin{equation}
    \Adj(S) \coloneqq \sum_{\fd \sim S} \phi_\fd.
\end{equation}
For future reference, we also define $\tAdj(S)$ in the same way but with $\phi_\fd$ replaced by $\fphi_\fd$.
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2511.07350

[Theorem thmIP of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] We keep the previous notation, we assume $\mathbf{A1}$--$\mathbf{A5}$ and we recall that $\mathbf m_p$ is viewed as a $\mathbb{T}_{\! c}$-valued r.v.~when it is convenient. Then the following holds true. 
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] $\mathbf m_p \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}^*\! , {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] $\mathbf m_p \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$ iff $\psi$ is of Type C. In particular, if $\psi$ is of Type B, $(\mathbf m_p)_{p\in \mathbb{N}}$ cannot converge in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] The laws of $(\mathbf m_p)_{p\in \mathbb{N}}$ are tight on $(\mathbb{T}^1_{\! c}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GHP}})$ iff ((Greydiscr of the paper)) holds true. In this case ((Grey of the paper)) holds true, ${\bf P} (\mathbf m \! \in \!  \mathbb{T}_{\! c})\! = \!  1$ and $\mathbf m_p \! \to \! \Phi_1 (\mathbf m)$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}^1_{\! c}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GHP}})$. \smallskip
\end{compactenum}
Moreover, the convergence in law $\mathbf m_p \! \to \! \mathbf m$ holds jointly with the convergence in law in $\mathbb{R}_+$ of the total masses $\langle \mathbf m_p\rangle$ to $\langle \mathbf m \rangle$, and $\langle \mathbf m \rangle$ is furthermore distributed as the total population $\int_0^\infty \! Z^{x_0}_s ds$. If $\psi$ is of Type C in $(ii)$ (resp.~if ((Greydiscr of the paper)) is satisfied as in $(iii)$), the convergence $\mathbf m_p \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$ (resp.~in law in $(\mathbb{T}^{1}_{\! c}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GHP}})$) holds jointly with $({\boldsymbol{\lambda}}_{\mathbf m_p} ([0, s]))_{s\in \mathbb{R}_+}  \!\!\!\!  \longrightarrow \! \!({\boldsymbol{\lambda}}_{\mathbf m} ([0, s]))_{s\in \mathbb{R}_+}\!\! \! \overset{{\textrm{(law)}}}{=} \!\! (\int_0^s \! Z^{x_0}_r dr)_{s\in \mathbb{R}_+} $ in law in $\mathbf C (\mathbb{R}_+, \mathbb{R})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 71 (Universal and minimax spectral depth) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Fix the stable natural exact-layer family
\[
 G^{\mathrm{Schur}}_{\lambda,n,r}(-):
 H\longmapsto
 {\mathbf S}_{\lambda}H_{\mathbb C}\otimes
 \operatorname{gr}^{\mathrm{anc}}_rM_{\lambda,n},
 \qquad r\geq1,
\]
assume that its stable multiplicity space is nonzero, and fix the
adapted projector \(P_{\lambda,r}\).  This is a polynomial-functor
type: evaluating it on a particular Hilbert space is not part of the
spectral-depth datum.  Its ancestry depth is
\(d_{\mathrm{anc}}(G^{\mathrm{Schur}}_{\lambda,n,r})=r\).  Its
universal critical spectral depth
\(d_{\mathrm{sp}}^{(\beta)}(G^{\mathrm{Schur}}_{\lambda,n,r})\) is the
least \(q\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}\) for which a constant
\(C_{G,P,\beta}\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|P_{\lambda,r}L_n(s,t)\|_{\mathfrak W_{\mathrm{mf}}^{[q]}(n)}
 \leq C_{G,P,\beta}\omega(s,t)^{n\beta}
 
\end{equation}
for every \(T\), every member of
\(\mathfrak C_{\beta}^{\mathrm{crit}}(T)\), and every \(s<t\).
The constant is uniform over the natural family, in particular
independent of the ambient Hilbert-space dimension.

An integer grade \(q\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}\) is called minimax sharp if
there are \(T_G,N_G,c_G,p_G>0\) and one fixed nontrivial cut
\(S_G\subset[n]\), chosen for the natural family before the spectral
window, with the following property.  For every \(L\geq N_G\) there is
a finite-dimensional random realization and an event \(G_L\) of
probability at least \(p_G\) on
which the realization belongs to
\(\mathfrak C_{\beta}^{\mathrm{crit}}(T_G)\) and
\begin{equation}
 s_N\!\left(
 \operatorname{Mat}_{S_G}
 (P_{\lambda,r}L_n(0,T_G))
 \right)
 \geq c_G\phi_q(N),
 \qquad N_G\leq N\leq L.
 
\end{equation}
All constants and algebraic data are independent of the ambient
dimension; only the finite block dimensions may depend on \(L\).  In particular,
minimax sharpness is not the assertion that every realization, or every
flattening of one realization, is extremal.
title: Universal and minimax spectral depth

body:
For every integer n >= 1 there is a prime p with n < p <= 2n. Conjectured by Bertrand (1845, verified to 3 million), proved by Chebyshev (1852); the proof below is Erdos's (1932), from the prime factorisation of the central binomial coefficient. Refinements: for n >= 25 there is a prime in (n, 6n/5) (Nagura); the prime number theorem gives a prime in (n, (1 + eps) n) for every eps > 0 and n large; Ramanujan primes generalise the statement to k primes in (n/2, n].
n a positive integer
the elementary product bound prod_{p <= x} p < 4^x is used for real x >= 2 (Erdos)

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C001 v1. Let d>=2, a_i iid N(0,I_d), x_* a deterministic unit vector, and f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2. For every 0<delta<1, with probability at least 1-2delta, lambda_max(Hess f(x_*)) <= 4 log(2m/delta) [8+16d log(5)/m+16 log(1/delta)/m]. For fixed alpha>=1, m=ceil(alpha d), delta=d^-2, this is O_alpha(log d). This bound is at the solution, not on a constant-radius ball. It follows from H_* <= (2 max_i (a_i^T x_*)^2/m) A^T A, a union bound on scalar Gaussian tails, and a 1/2-net bound on ||A||. No independence between the maximum projection and the design matrix is assumed.
fixed deterministic unit signal
independent real standard Gaussian rows
loss normalized by 1/(4m)
title: Draft: Phase retrieval Hessian upper bound at proportional Gaussian sample size

[Defn boundarysignature of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\Sigma \subset M$ be a compact planar surface with $\partial \Sigma \subset \partial M$. Define
\begin{align*}
    b_{nd}(\Sigma) &\coloneqq \text{the number of nondegeneracy boundary components of } \Sigma, \\
    b_{-\infty}(\Sigma) &\coloneqq \text{the number of $-\infty$ degeneracy boundary components of } \Sigma, \\
    b_{+\infty}(\Sigma) &\coloneqq \text{the number of $+\infty$ degeneracy boundary components of } \Sigma.
\end{align*}
We also define the \textbf{degeneracy signature} of $\Sigma$,
$$\bm{b}(\Sigma) \coloneqq \big(b_{nd}(\Sigma), b_{-\infty}(\Sigma), b_{+\infty}(\Sigma)\big).$$
title: Defn boundarysignature of arXiv:2608.30031

[Definition 18 of arXiv:2604.13454, 'Invariant and periodic measures in classical spin systems on infinite lattices with highly'] A function $h:\Omega_{Spin}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is called a finite-dimensional cylinder function, if there exists $m,l\in \mathbb{N}$, a finite subset $\Lambda_m\subset\mathbb{Z}^+$ and $g:\mathbb{R}^{l\Lambda_m}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ such that $h(\omega)=g(\Pi_{\Lambda_m}\omega(t_1),\cdots,\Pi_{\Lambda_m}\omega(t_l))$. Moreover, if $g$ is bounded and Lipschitz i.e. there is a  constant $L>0$ such that 
    	$$
    	|g(z) - g(\tilde{z})| \leq L\|z - \tilde{z}\|_{\mathbb{R}^{l\Lambda_m}} \ \forall z, \tilde{z} \in \mathbb{R}^{l\Lambda_m},
    	$$
    	we say that $h$ is cylindrically bounded and  Lipschitz, such functions $h$ form a function space denoted as $C_{b,lip}^{Cly}(\Omega_{Spin})$.
title: Definition 18 of arXiv:2604.13454

[Defn pleat of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] A representation $\rho:\pi_1(S)\to \mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ is said to be \emph{n-pleated along
$\lambda$} if there exists a $\rho$--equivariant map
\[
\xi:\partial\widetilde{\lambda}\to \mathcal{F}(\mathbb{C}^n),
\]
called the \emph{$\lambda$--limit map}, satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item (\emph{$\lambda$--transversality}) For every leaf of $\widetilde{\lambda}$
  with endpoints $x,y\in\partial\widetilde{\lambda}$, the pair of flags
  $\xi(x),\xi(y)$ is transverse, i.e. is in general position. 

  \item (\emph{$\lambda$--hyperconvexity}) For every complementary ideal triangle
  (plaque) of $\widetilde{\lambda}$ with vertices $x,y,z$, the triple
  $\xi(x),\xi(y),\xi(z)$ is in general position.

  \item (\emph{$\lambda$--Anosov property}) The limit map $\xi$ induces associated $\mathbb{C}^n$-bundles over $T^1\lambda \subset T^1S$, and the dynamics of the lift of the geodesic flow there is Anosov.
\end{enumerate}
title: $n$-pleated representation

[Theorem thm:Darboux of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Let $K$ be dressing compatible with $(\Psi, \Phi)$, with resolvent $R(u) = (I - zK(u))^{-1}$.  Define the dressed observable and dressed
waves by
\[
\mathcal{M}(u) \vcentcolon= I + z\Phi(u)R(u)\Psi(u),
\]
\[
\widehat\Psi(u) \vcentcolon= R(u)\Psi(u), \qquad
\widehat\Phi(u) \vcentcolon= \Phi(u)R(T^{-1}u).
\]
Then $\mathcal{M}(u)$ is invertible for every
$u \in \mathcal{V}$. The dressed waves
$\widehat\Psi, \widehat\Phi$ satisfy the
linear system (equation eq:Linear-Psi-3 of the paper) and adjoint linear
system (equation eq:Linear-Phi-Prob of the paper) respectively, with data
$(\mathcal{M}_i, \Lambda_i)$:
\begin{align*}
\widehat\Psi(S_i u)
&= \widehat\Psi(Tu)\mathcal{M}_i(u)
- \widehat\Psi(u)\Lambda_i(u), \\
\widehat\Phi(Tu)
&= \mathcal{M}_i(u)\widehat\Phi(S_i u)
- \Lambda_i(Tu)\widehat\Phi(TS_i u),
\end{align*}
for $i \in \mathbb{N}$, where the dressed edge weights are given by
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{M}_i(u) \vcentcolon=
\mathcal{M}(Tu)^{-1}C_i(u)\mathcal{M}(S_i u),
\end{equation}
and $\widehat K(u) \vcentcolon= K(u)R(u)$ is dressing compatible
with $(\widehat\Psi, \widehat\Phi)$.
Moreover, the pair $(\mathcal{M}_i, \Lambda_i)$ satisfies
the diamond equations
(equation eq:diamond-C-ij of the paper)--(equation eq:diamond-mixed-ij of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:Darboux of arXiv:2608.02772

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] Let $\mu\cvd \nu \in \Pc_r(\R)$ with $r\geq 1$. Assume that  $C:\R \times\Pc_r(\R) \to \R$ is  measurable, continuous and convex in the second argument and  there exists  $K>0$ so that 
$$
\forall (x,p) \in \R \times \Pc_r(\R), \ |C(x,p)| \leq K \left( 1 + |x|^r  + \int_{\R} |y|^r  p (dy) \right).
$$
Then  $\pi \in \Pi_S(\mu, \nu)$ is supermartingale $C$-monotone w.r.t. some $\Gamma$ if and only if $\pi$ is optimal for (WSOT).

body: [Theorem inversetheorem of arXiv:2507.05417, 'Invertibility for non-Hermitian and symmetric random band matrices with sublinear bandwidt'] Let $\mu\in(0,\frac{1}{4}]$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$, $p$ a prime number and $v\in\mathbb{F}_p^d$. Write $D=\frac{2}{\mu}\log \rho_\mu(v)^{-1}$. Suppose that $|v|\geq D$ and $\rho_\mu(v)\geq \frac{2}{p}$. Then we can find $T\subset[d]$ with $|T|\leq D$ such that, if we denote $w=v_T$, then $v_i\in N_\mu(w)$ for all but at most $D$ values of $i\in[n]$. Moreover, we have the following cardinality upper bound: $$|N_\mu(w)|\leq \frac{256}{\rho_\mu(v)}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemme decompok of arXiv:2603.21634, 'Individual-based stochastic model with unbounded growth, birth and death rates: a tightnes'] Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^{+} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+})$, and $F \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}([0,R_\mathrm{in}] \times \mathbb{R})$. Under Assumptions~(hyp:probamortel of the paper) and (hyp:poidsomega of the paper), we have almost surely, for all $K \in \mathbb{N}^{*}$, $t \geq 0$,
\begin{align*}
F(R^{K}_{t},\langle \mu^{K}_{t}, \varphi_{t} \rangle) = & \hspace{0.1 cm} F(R_{0},\langle \mu^{K}_{0}, \varphi_{0} \rangle) \\
    & + \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}} \rho(\mu^{K}_{s},R^{K}_{s}) \partial_{1}F(R^{K}_{s},\langle \mu^{K}_{s}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \\
    & \hspace{5cm} + \langle \mu^{K}_{s}, \Phi_{s}(R^{K}_{s},.) \rangle \partial_{2} F(R^{K}_{s},\langle \mu^{K}_{s}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \mathrm{d}s \\
    & + \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}}\int_{\mathcal{U} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+} } \mathbb{1}_{\{u \in V^{K}_{s-} \}} \mathbb{1}_{\{h \leq b\left(\xi^{u,K}_{s-}\right)\}} \\
    & \hspace{3 cm}  \bigg( F(R^{K}_{s},\langle \mu^{K}_{s-}+\frac{1}{K} \left( \delta_{x_{0}} + \delta_{\xi^{u,K}_{s-}-x_{0}}-\delta_{\xi^{u,K}_{s-}} \right), \varphi_{s} \rangle) \\
    & \hspace{6 cm}- F(R^{K}_{s}, \langle \mu^{K}_{s-}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \bigg) \mathcal{N}(\mathrm{d}s,\mathrm{d}u,\mathrm{d}h) &
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
     \hspace{3cm}& +
    \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathcal{U} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+} } \mathbb{1}_{\{u \in V^{K}_{s-} \}} \mathbb{1}_{\{h \leq d(\xi^{u,K}_{s-})\}} }\bigg( F(R^{K}_{s},\langle \mu^{K}_{s-}-\frac{1}{K}\delta_{\xi^{u,K}_{s-}}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \\
    & \hspace{6cm}- F(R^{K}_{s}, \langle \mu^{K}_{s-}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \bigg) \mathcal{N}'(\mathrm{d}s,\mathrm{d}u,\mathrm{d}h),

with $\Phi$ associated to $\varphi$ as in (equation eq:Phidef of the paper).

[Cor 10 of arXiv:2609.02342, '2609.02342'] Let \(G\) be a rooted directed tree without leaves. Let
	\(\rho=(\rho_i)_{i\in I}\) be a \(1\)-admissible weight such that the left
	translation semigroup \((T_t)_{t\geq0}\) is a strongly continuous semigroup on
	\(L^1_\rho(L(G))\). 
	For a finite nonempty set \(K\subset I\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and
	\(0<\alpha<1\), define
	\[
	\mathcal N_1(K,\varepsilon,\alpha)
	=
	\Biggl\{
	t\geq0:
	\inf_{\substack{E\subset[0,1)\\ m(E)>\alpha}}
	\int_E
	\sum_{i\in K}
	\inf_{j\in M_{n(t,s)}(i)}
	\rho_j(t+s-n(t,s))
	\,ds
	<\varepsilon
	\Biggr\}.
	\]
	Then the following assertions are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\renewcommand{\labelenumi}{\textnormal{(\roman{enumi})}}
		\item \((T_t)_{t\geq0}\) is \(\mathcal F\)-transitive on
		\(L^1_\rho(L(G))\);
		\item for every finite nonempty set \(K\subset I\), every
		\(\varepsilon>0\), and every \(0<\alpha<1\), one has
		\[
		\mathcal N_1(K,\varepsilon,\alpha)\in\mathcal F .
		\]
		\item \((T_t)_{t\geq0}\) is topologically \(\mathcal F\)-recurrent on $L^1_\rho(L(G))$.
	\end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem 24 (Echo decay beats volume growth: unconditional front decoupling) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Assume bounded degrees, the saturated regime with margin $\delta$, the dissipative condition $\kappa<1$ of \eqref{eq:kappa}, and $\kappa\,\rho(M)<1$. Then Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red} holds: there is a constant $C=C(\kappa,\alpha_{\min},\mu_0,\Delta_{\max})$ such that for the cascade on $G_n$,
\[
\dTV\Big(\mathcal L\big(\text{cluster}\big),\ \mathcal L\big(\mathrm{GW}(M)\big)\Big)\le C\,\frac{\varepsilon(\delta)}{(1-\kappa\rho(M))^2(1-\rho(M))}+\eta_n,
\]
with $\eta_n\to0$ as $G_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BS}}T$, in the subcritical regime $\rho(M)<1$. Consequently all results of Sections \ref{sec:spectral}--\ref{sec:stab} hold unconditionally, as statements about the SDE, on the open parameter region
\[
\mathcal R:=\{\kappa<1\}\cap\{\text{saturation margin $\delta$ large}\}\cap\{\rho(M)<1\},
\]
in the iterated limit $n\to\infty$ then $\delta\to\infty$. At criticality the bound degrades: conditionally on $\{|S|=n\}$ the total-variation error is $\le C\,n\,\varepsilon(\delta)/(1-\kappa)$, so the critical limit theorems (Theorems \ref{thm:32} and \ref{thm:crt}) hold unconditionally along any joint limit $\delta_n\to\infty$ with $n\,\varepsilon(\delta_n)\to0$.

  \end{equation}

[Proposition prop:comonadtower of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $F:\cC\leftrightarrows\cD:G$ be an adjunction of stable $\infty$-categories with unit $\eta$ completed to a cofiber sequence $S\xrightarrow{\tau}1_{\cC}\xrightarrow{\eta}GF$ and let $\tau^n\coloneqq \tau\circ(\tau S)\circ\cdots \circ  (\tau S^{n-1})$ as before (but dual).
Suppose there is a coherent diagram of stable $\infty$-categories and functors
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\cC \arrow[d,swap,"F"]\arrow[dr,swap]\arrow[drr,swap]\arrow[drrr]\arrow[drrrrr,"P_n"] \\
\cD & \cC_1 \arrow[l,"Q_0"] & \cC_2 \arrow[l,"Q_1"] & \cC_3 \arrow[l,"Q_2"] & \ldots\arrow[l] & \arrow[l] \cC_n & \ldots\arrow[l]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
which is a limit cone with apex $\cC$, i.e.\ $\cC\simeq\lim \cC_n$.
Suppose further that $P_n(\tau^{n+1})=0$ and all $\cC_n$ are idempotent complete.
Then $F$ is comonadic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition allpinningsgiveboundedexternalfields of arXiv:2607.06813, 'Mixing of Glauber Dynamics on High Overlap Gibbs Measures'] Let $C\geq 0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$. Let $J\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ symmetric such that $\|J\|\leq C$, and $h\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Consider the quadratic Gibbs measure
       \[
    \nu(x) \propto \exp\left(\frac{1}2x^\top J x + h^\top x\right).
        \]
Let $\mathcal{P}\subset [n]$ be a set of pinning coordinates of size $|\mathcal{P}|\leq (1-\delta)n$ and $\tau_\mathcal{P}\in\{\pm1\}^{\mathcal{P}}$ be the pinned values. Let $\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{P}^c$ and $m=|\mathcal{S}|$. The probability measure of $x_{\mathcal{S}}\Bigm|x_{\mathcal{P}}=\tau_\mathcal{P}$ is a quadratic Gibbs measure on $\{\pm1\}^{\mathcal{S}}$ of the form 
       \[
    \nu(x) \propto \exp\left(\frac{1}2x_{\mathcal{S}}^\top J_{\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}} x_{\mathcal{S}} + h_{\mathcal{S}}^\top x_{\mathcal{S}}+v^
    \top x_{\mathcal{S}}\right),
        \]
with $\|v\|\leq C\sqrt{\frac{1-\delta}{\delta}}\sqrt{m}$.

[Proposition 27 of arXiv:2608.12291, 'When should one stop the most exciting game?\\ {\tiny Sequential Inference for win-marting'] The value function $V_T$ satisfies
\begin{align}
    (\partial_t+\mathcal{L})V_T(t,x)=-c(t),\qquad &(t,x)\in\mathcal{C}_T,\\
    V_T(t,x)=g(x),\qquad &(t,x)\in\mathcal{D}_T,
\end{align}
for any $T\leq\infty$.

body:
[Prop 8 of arXiv:2607.06745, 'Regularization and asymptotic behaviour of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck evolution operators in infin'] Take $\left\{ \mu_{t}\mid t\in\mathbb{R}\right\} $
as in $\text{\eqref{def misura inv}}$. For each $s<t$, and $p\in[1,+\infty)$,
the operator $P_{s,t}:C_{b}\left(X\right)\to C_{b}\left(X\right)$
has a bounded extension:
\[
P_{s,t}^{p}:L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)\to L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right).
\]

Analogously the operator $\overrightarrow{P_{s,t}}:C_{b}\left(X;X\right)\to C_{b}\left(X;X\right)$
has a bounded extension:
\[
\overrightarrow{P_{s,t}^{p}}:L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t};X\right)\to L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s};X\right).
\]

Both these extended operators are contractions. Relations $\text{\eqref{eq: muinv}}$
and $\eqref{eq: muinv vettoriale}$ also hold for $P_{s,t}=P_{s,t}^{p}$
with $\varphi\in L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)$ and $\overrightarrow{P_{s,t}}=\overrightarrow{P_{s,t}^{p}}$
with $\Phi\in L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t};X\right)$, respectively.
title: Prop 8 of arXiv:2607.06745

body:
[Definition def:walkbridge of arXiv:2411.12149, 'Airy limit for $\beta$-additions through Dunkl operators'] For $H_{1},H_{2}\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, $L\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$, $N\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$, $\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ is the set of walk bridges of length $L$  from $H_{1}$ to $H_{2}$. 
    $\mathcal{W}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ is the set of walk bridges $W(t)$ of length $L$ from $H_{1}$ to $H_{2}$, such that $W(t)\ge0$ for all $t$ in its domain.
    
    For each element in $\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ or $\mathcal{W}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$, by viewing the increments of $W(t)$ as i.i.d. random variables with distribution $\mu(N)$, defined in Eqn.~((eq_rvx of the paper)), we assign a weight to each walk bridge as $$\text{weight}(W)=\prod_{l=-1}^{\infty}[P_{l}(N)V_{N}(z_{c}(N))]^{\# t:\ W(t)-W(t-)=l}.$$

    Let $$|\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)|=\sum_{W\in \mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)}\text{weight}(W)$$
     be the \emph{partition function} of $\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$. The partition function of $\mathcal{W}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ is defined similarly.
title: Definition def:walkbridge of arXiv:2411.12149

\E{ |\Lambda_{(x_1,U)}F|^3 } &= \mathcal{O}\left(\beta^{3\alpha}\right).
\end{align*}

\norm{m'_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}}_{L^\infty(\mathbb R)}\leq
\norm{m'_\varsigma}_{L^\infty(\mathbb R)}.
\]
\item[(ii)]

For every $\varsigma\geq1$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ 
it holds
that 
\[
  \frac{1}{m_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}(r)}\le \frac{1}{\varepsilon^\varsigma} \quad \forall\, r \in \mathbb{R}.
\]
\item [(iii)]
 
For every $\varsigma\geq1$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$
it holds that $\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\in C^2(\mathbb R)$
is strictly convex, 
$\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}'$ is monotone increasing and $\frac{1}{\varepsilon^\varsigma}$-Lipschitz continuous,
with $\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}'(0)=0$, 
$m_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}''\equiv1$,
and 
\[
  \frac1{\norm{m_\varsigma}_{L^\infty(\mathbb R)}+1}\leq\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}''(r)\leq \frac1{\varepsilon^\varsigma}
  \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\]
\item [(iv)]

For every $\varsigma>1$, there exist $C_\varsigma, c_\varsigma>0$
such that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
it holds that 
\[
c_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma-1, \varepsilon}''(r)\leq 
|\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'(r)| 
\le C_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma-1, \varepsilon}''(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\]
\item [(v)]

For every $\varsigma\geq1$, there exist $C_\varsigma, c_\varsigma>0$
such that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
it holds that 
\begin{alignat*}{2}
c_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r) &\leq 
|\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'(r)| &&\le C_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R,\\
c_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+2, \varepsilon}(r) &\leq 
\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}''(r) &&\le C_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+2, \varepsilon}(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R,\\
c_\varsigma\Psi''_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r) &\leq 
|\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'''(r)| &&\le 
C_\varsigma\Psi''_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\end{alignat*}
\item [(viii)]

For every $\varsigma, \zeta \ge 1$, $\varsigma\le\zeta$,
there exists $C_{\varsigma,\zeta}>0$ such that,
for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, it holds that
\[
\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}(r)\leq C_{\varsigma,\zeta}
\Psi_\zeta(r) \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R, \qquad
\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}''(r)\leq C_{\varsigma,\zeta}
\Psi_\zeta''(r) \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\]
\item [(ix)]

For every $\varsigma, \zeta \geq 1$ with $\varsigma+\zeta>2$,
there is $K_{\varsigma,\zeta}>0$ such that,
for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, it holds 
    \[
    \Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'(r)
    \Psi_{\zeta, \varepsilon}'(r)
    \geq K_{\varsigma,\zeta}
    \Psi_{\varsigma+\zeta-2, \varepsilon}''(r) - K_{\varsigma,\zeta}^{-1} \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
    \]
   \end{itemize}

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] When flipping a coin, and with our winning function being
$$f:\big\{{\rm heads},\,{\rm tails}\big\}\to\mathbb R\quad,\quad f({\rm heads})=a\quad,\quad f({\rm tails})=b$$
with $a,b\in\mathbb R$, what we can expect to win, on average, is the quantity
$$E(f)=ap+b(1-p)$$
in the case of a biased coin. For a normal coin, this reads $E(f)=(a+b)/2$.
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

body:
[Def 11 of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Given a metric  space $(X,d)$ and two subsets $A,B \subset X$, the \emph{Hausdorff distance} between them (denoted $d_H(A,B)$) is defined to be
\[    \max\{  \sup \{  \inf \{ d(a,b) \, \vert \, b \in B \} \, \vert \, a \in A \} ,    \sup \{  \inf \{ d(a,b) \, \vert \, a \in A \} \, \vert \, b \in B \}      \} .         \]
We say that a sequence of subsets $A_i \subset X$ \emph{converges in the Hausdorff topology} to a subset $A \subset X$ if $d_H(A_i , A) \to 0$ as $i \to \infty$.
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.30990
